dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work specifically on Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level: the calculator-free paper, the technology paper and the exploration. Each profile names the components they work on rather than the subject in general. The free trial session produces a marked script and two named target question types, which is the baseline every later comparison is measured against.

intro.heading: The problem with a maths lesson that went well
paragraphs: Almost every maths tutorial feels successful at the end. The student follows the worked example, nods at the right moments, completes the practice question with a prompt or two, and leaves with the sense that the topic is sorted. Three weeks later the same question appears on a mock paper in a slightly different form and the method is gone. This is not a failure of the tutor's explanation. It is a failure of the evidence: nothing in that session tested whether the method had been learnt rather than followed.

That distinction is the whole of this page. Lesson-time success is the cheapest and least informative evidence available, and it is what most families are shown. The evidence that actually predicts an Analysis and Approaches SL grade has three properties: it is delayed, so recall is being tested rather than imitation; it is unprompted, so the student has to choose the method rather than apply the one just demonstrated; and it is disguised, so the skill has to be recognised inside a question that does not announce which topic it belongs to.

Delivery, stated plainly before anything else. IB Gram provides tuition in Dubai as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. For a maths page this is less of a compromise than parents expect, because the format is better suited to evidence: written working is photographed or written on a shared surface, annotation sits on the document, and the markscheme reference stays attached to the mark. A visiting tutor leaves with the explanation in the air and nothing on file.

Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is a particularly good course to apply this to, because its published assessment structure is clean. Two written papers, one sat without a calculator and one with technology permitted, carrying the bulk of the grade between them, plus the mathematical exploration worth a fifth of it. A student can be competent at the content of all five syllabus topics and still sit in the middle of the grade range because of how marks are collected under time pressure, and that gap is exactly what delayed, unprompted, disguised evidence exposes.

Dubai adds its own layer. This is the densest private-school market in the country, inspected annually by the regulator on a six-band scale, and the pacing of a Diploma maths class varies enormously between schools. A student in a strong cohort can be taught at the pace of the fastest third and arrive at the exploration still shaky on calculus. None of that shows up in a report grade, and all of it shows up in a marked script.

What follows is a hierarchy of evidence, a delayed-recall protocol you can run yourself, the four disguises an AA SL skill arrives in, what a properly annotated script looks like, how the exploration version history works, and the three different numbers a Dubai school will give you about the same child. The last section says when the evidence means the tutoring should end.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Four routes sit around an Analysis and Approaches SL candidate in Dubai, and the evidence a parent should ask for differs across them. Knowing which one your child is on prevents the most common mistake, which is reading a criterion-referenced grade as if it were a percentage.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1 to 7, plus up to three points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination. Mathematics is compulsory, which is why Analysis and Approaches SL is one of the most widely sat courses in any Dubai cohort and why its tutoring market is the busiest.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit in schools whose internal assessment deadlines are set by their own coordinator, often several weeks earlier than families assume. Those dates govern when exploration evidence has to exist, so a plan is built from the coordinator's sheet rather than from a generic programme calendar.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
programmes.description: Two written papers, one without a calculator and one with technology permitted, plus the mathematical exploration. The course covers number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. The published weighting puts the exploration at a fifth of the final grade.
programmes.countryNote: In most Dubai schools this is the default maths course for students who are not heading into engineering or pure mathematics but need a recognised quantitative qualification. That makes the cohort wide in ability, and the class pace a compromise that leaves distinct gaps in individual students.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
programmes.description: The same subject family with greater depth and an additional paper of extended problem-solving. Relevant here because a meaningful number of Dubai students begin at Higher Level and move down, and the evidence trail should make that decision on marks rather than on how hard the course feels.
programmes.countryNote: A route change has a deadline set by the school rather than the board, so the window for moving is narrower than families expect. Two dated marked scripts on comparable question types are the evidence a coordinator will take seriously in that conversation.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D on an eight-point achievement scale rather than as percentages. Students arriving into Analysis and Approaches SL from MYP 5 are comfortable with criterion-referenced work and often unpractised at timed papers marked against a markscheme.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run a full continuum from the Primary Years Programme through to the Diploma, so a student may never have sat an externally marked timed paper before DP1. The first marked script in that case is a diagnosis of exam behaviour as much as of mathematics.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Analysis and Approaches SL is five topics and one piece of coursework. Below, each is described by the evidence that shows the skill has actually transferred, because transfer rather than exposure is what a grade measures.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms and the binomial expansion. Transfer looks like a student recognising a geometric structure inside a word problem about depreciation without being told the topic. Doing a bare sequence question correctly proves only that they were on the right page.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, quadratics and rational functions. The transfer test is a sketch question with no instruction naming the transformation. Students who can answer when told to translate often cannot read the transformation out of an equation three weeks later.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Triangle rules, radians, trigonometric identities and equations. Transfer shows up when a trigonometric identity is needed inside a calculus question rather than in a section headed trigonometry, which is where most SL candidates lose the marks.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability rules, discrete and normal distributions. The marks lost are usually not statistical: they are unstated conditions and results given without interpretation. A transfer test asks for a conclusion in context, which many students never practise.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and optimisation. The single richest source of disguised questions in the course, because a rate of change can arrive dressed as a volume, a cost or a velocity. Fluency at bare differentiation is weak evidence of anything here.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique, no calculator
subjects.description: A separate skill from the mathematics. Exact values, surd and fraction handling, and writing the step that earns the method mark. Evidence of improvement is the appearance of intermediate lines in the working, which is countable on a script without any mathematical judgement.

subjects.name: Paper 2 technique, technology permitted
subjects.description: Knowing which tool to reach for and recording enough on paper to earn method credit anyway. The recurring loss is a correct screen result with nothing written down, which scores a fraction of the same answer supported by stated reasoning.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Coursework carrying a fifth of the grade, assessed against lettered criteria. The evidence is a dated version history: the student's own drafts with criterion-referenced comments attached, which demonstrates both development and sole authorship.

subjects.name: Physics and Economics as paired subjects
subjects.description: Included because disguised mathematics appears here first. A student losing kinematics marks in Physics is usually telling you something about their calculus transfer, and that cross-subject signal often arrives weeks before the maths teacher sees it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Relevant where a student chooses a mathematics-based Extended Essay. The same authorship rule applies as to the exploration: criterion-referenced questioning, a dated draft trail, and every sentence written by the candidate.

sections.heading: What an IB DP Math AA SL tutor in Dubai should actually be able to prove
paragraphs: Start with the direct answer, because the search deserves one. A tutor for Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level in Dubai can show you four kinds of evidence, and they are not equally worth having. The weakest is the one most commonly offered, which is a report that the session went well and the student understood the topic. The strongest is an unprompted attempt at a disguised question several weeks after the teaching, marked against the published markscheme.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is an India-only service. For this subject the format is an advantage rather than a concession, because the evidence protocol depends on written work moving between sessions and being annotated on the document. Working is written on a shared surface or photographed and marked up, the markscheme reference stays beside the mark, and the file accumulates. A visiting tutor leaves the explanation in the room and the notebook with the student.

The reason this matters more in mathematics than in most subjects is that mathematical understanding is unusually easy to simulate. A student who has just watched a method can reproduce it for twenty minutes without having learnt anything durable, and both the student and the tutor will experience that as success. Every parent who has heard that a topic is now fine and then seen the mock result knows this effect without having a name for it.

So ask for the strong evidence from the start, and treat the weak kind as a courtesy rather than a report. The table below ranks the four types by what they genuinely establish and how easily each can be produced without any learning having occurred.

sections.heading: The delayed-recall protocol, and how to run it yourself
paragraphs: This costs nothing and any parent can administer it, including one who has never studied calculus. It is the single most useful thing in this page.

When a tutor reports that a topic has been covered, write the topic and the date on a sheet. Do nothing for three weeks. Then ask the tutor to set two questions on that topic inside a mixed set, without telling your child which topics are represented, and to mark the result against the published markscheme. The condition that makes it work is the mixing: a question labelled with its topic tests retrieval from a known shelf, and a question in a mixed set tests whether the student can find the shelf at all, which is what a real paper demands.

Interpret the outcome in three bands. Full marks on both means the teaching transferred and the topic can be left alone. Correct method with lost method marks means the mathematics is secure and the mark collection is not, which is a procedural fix of a few weeks. No method selected at all means the topic was followed rather than learnt, and it needs re-teaching with spaced revisiting rather than another explanation.

Run this on rotation across the five Analysis and Approaches SL topics and by the middle of DP2 you have something no report can give you: a map of which topics are durable and which are theatre. Most families discover that one topic they believed was finished is the weakest thing on the list, and that another they worried about has been solid for months. Both discoveries save money.

One caveat worth stating. A delayed attempt that goes badly is information, not a failure of the tutor, and treating it as the latter is how families end up with tutors who only ever report good news. The whole value of the protocol is that it is allowed to produce bad results.

sections.heading: The four disguises an Analysis and Approaches SL skill arrives in
paragraphs: Paper questions rarely announce their topic. A calculus mark can arrive inside a question about the volume of a container, the cost of production or the velocity of a particle, and a student who can differentiate on request may not recognise that differentiation is what is being asked for. This is the most common reason a competent Standard Level student sits in the middle of the grade range.

The mechanism is simple. Classroom practice is almost always topic-blocked: a chapter on trigonometry, an exercise set on trigonometry, a test on trigonometry. Blocked practice produces rapid apparent progress and poor transfer, which is a well-established effect and one that an exam-shaped assessment punishes precisely. Interleaved practice feels harder and slower to the student, produces worse homework scores in the short term, and transfers far better.

Which means a tutor doing the comfortable thing — working through the current chapter at the current pace — is producing exactly the kind of practice that will not survive a mixed paper. The useful session structure keeps a quarter of the time for questions from topics covered weeks earlier, deliberately out of order, and that quarter is where the evidence comes from.

sections.heading: What a properly annotated Standard Level script looks like
paragraphs: A marked script is only evidence if the marking is legible to somebody who is not a mathematician. A page of ticks and a total at the bottom is a score, not an analysis, and it cannot support any of the comparisons this page recommends.

Three things have to be visible. First, where each mark was awarded or lost, written next to the line it refers to rather than summarised at the end. Second, which markscheme the marker applied, named specifically enough that you could find it: the board, the paper and the series. Third, the category of each loss, because the category is what determines the fix. A mark lost because the method was never written down needs a habit. A mark lost because an identity was not known needs re-teaching. A mark lost because the question asked for an exact value and received a decimal needs neither, only attention.

The reason to insist on the third item is that it makes the next comparison possible. If the first script shows eleven marks lost to working not written down, then the only question about the second script is whether that number has fallen. That is a conversation a parent can hold with confidence in any subject, and it removes the need to evaluate the mathematics itself.

There is one annotation habit worth asking for explicitly in Standard Level maths: marking the questions the student skipped or abandoned, and in what order they attempted the paper. Timing failures look identical to knowledge failures on a total, and they are a completely different problem. A student who left eight marks of accessible calculus untouched at the end of Paper 2 has a pacing issue, and no amount of calculus teaching will touch it.
bullets: Marks annotated beside the line, not summarised at the foot of the page
The markscheme named by board, paper and series
Every loss categorised: method, knowledge, instruction or accuracy
Skipped and abandoned questions marked, with the attempt order noted
The same categories used on the next script, so the counts are comparable

sections.heading: The exploration as a version history with one author
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration carries a fifth of the Standard Level grade and is assessed against lettered criteria, which makes it the most valuable single artefact in the subject and the most sensitive to how support is given.

The evidence model is a version history. Each draft the student produces is saved with the date it was written, and each set of comments is saved with the date it was returned. Over a term this produces a sequence that shows how the thinking developed, and it does two jobs at once: it tells a parent whether anything is actually happening, and it demonstrates that the work is the candidate's own if a coordinator ever asks.

The boundary is not negotiable and it is easy to state. The student selects the topic, does the mathematics, writes the commentary and types every sentence. The supervisor asks questions and names criteria. Which criterion is this section trying to satisfy. The mathematics is correct but the reflection does not say why this approach was chosen. This notation is inconsistent between pages. Those comments work precisely because the student has to write the improvement, and anything that supplies the improvement instead is malpractice under IB rules with the consequence falling on the candidate.

There is a provider in this market selling completed internal assessments outright. A Dubai family buying one is purchasing a finding against their own child, potentially across the whole Diploma rather than one subject grade, and no price makes that a reasonable trade.

Practically, keep the version history yourself rather than leaving the only copy with a tutor. If the tutor changes mid-process, a dated sequence of drafts means the new supervisor begins from where the work actually is. Published subject guides and criteria are referenced and linked from the official sources rather than redistributed, which is also how you can tell whether a provider treats board material correctly.

sections.heading: Three numbers a Dubai school gives you, and what each one is for
paragraphs: Families routinely compare numbers that are not comparable, and in Dubai this happens more than most places because schools report differently and parents compare across schools in the same conversation.

The report grade is a teacher's judgement of current performance against the 1 to 7 scale, usually based on classwork and internal tests, and it moves for reasons that include effort and attendance. The mock grade is a snapshot of performance on one paper on one day, converted using a boundary set the school has chosen, often last year's. The predicted grade is a formal judgement submitted by the school about what the candidate will achieve, and it is the one universities see.

None of them is a measurement of the thing a tutor can change. What a tutor can change is marks collected by question type, and that is a fourth number nobody publishes. This is why the comparison recommended throughout this page is type-level and not grade-level: a student can gain nine marks on calculus questions, which is real and valuable, while the reported grade stays at a 5 because the boundary did not move with them.

The practical consequence is a different question to ask the school. Rather than why is the grade still a 5, ask which components the grade was calculated from and which of them was weakest. A maths department will answer that readily, and the answer tells a tutor where to aim. Grade boundaries are the board's business on results day and nobody can predict them; marks by type are the only variable in a family's control.

A note on what this page deliberately does not state. No IB examination or results date appears anywhere on it, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no session date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. Dubai schools sit the May session; the dates that actually bind your child are the coordinator's internal deadlines, and those come from the school.

sections.heading: The Dubai cohort effect on a Standard Level maths grade
paragraphs: Dubai is the densest private-school market in the country, and the regulator inspects schools annually on a six-band scale running from the highest rating down to the weakest. Those reports describe a school, and a parent reading one should be careful about what it implies for an individual maths class.

The sector context is worth having. Dubai's private schools served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. Enrolment rose 6 per cent during 2025-26, six new schools opened in that year, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven more, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. The regulator also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

What all that means for an Analysis and Approaches SL student is competition for pace. In a strong cohort the class moves at the speed the top third can sustain, and a student in the middle accumulates small unfinished topics that never trigger an intervention because nothing is failing. By the exploration, those gaps have compounded. This is the single most common profile among Dubai students who come to tutoring with a report grade of 5 and no obvious problem.

Two timetable realities also shape when evidence can be produced. The mandatory UAE subjects sit alongside the licensed curriculum: federal rules require Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of curriculum, and the Dubai regulator's guidance specifies separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, calculates instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, and advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Those lessons occupy the school day that a maths-heavy student might otherwise use for consolidation.

The second is the calendar: mock weeks, school trips and the shortened school day during Ramadan all compress what a student can realistically produce. A delayed-recall attempt scheduled into a mock week is not evidence of anything, so the protocol moves around the school year rather than running regardless of it.

sections.heading: How written mathematics gets marked over live video
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how a subject that lives on paper works on a screen, and the answer is specific enough to be checked.

Working is produced in one of two ways. Either the student writes on paper and photographs the page, which is then annotated on screen during the session, or the student writes directly on a shared surface the tutor can see live. The first is better for timed papers because it preserves normal exam conditions. The second is better for teaching, because the tutor sees the hesitation and the crossing-out rather than only the finished product, which is where a diagnosis actually comes from.

For the full timed papers, the sequence is the one a school would use. The student sits the paper under time, photographs or scans it, and sends it before the session. The marking happens outside the session, because an hour spent watching a tutor mark is an hour not spent teaching. The session then opens with the annotated script on screen and the comparison to the previous attempt already prepared.

On equipment, the honest list is short. A device with a camera, a reliable connection, paper and a pen. A graphics tablet helps a tutor demonstrate but is not needed by the student, and it is worth being sceptical of any requirement that converts into a purchase. Calculator work for the technology paper is done on the student's own model, because the model matters and practising on a different one builds the wrong reflexes.

On the file itself: session notes, marked scripts and the exploration version history are records about a child, and a family should know what is kept, why, and how to have it removed. The UAE's personal data protection law frames that expectation, and the sensible practice is the same regardless: the family holds copies, the purpose is stated, and nothing about a child's school or grades is collected without a reason that can be explained in one sentence.

sections.heading: When the evidence says the tutoring is finished
paragraphs: The protocol in this page has an endpoint, and a provider that never mentions it is not using the evidence for your benefit.

The finishing condition is specific: the student passes delayed, unprompted attempts across all five topics, collects method marks reliably on Paper 1, finishes Paper 2 in time, and can mark their own work against a published markscheme and tell you which question types they are weak on. At that point they have the skill the tutoring was bought to install, and the right move is a session a fortnight through the final term and then nothing.

There are also two failure conditions, and both are reasons to change something rather than to buy more hours. The first is six weeks of flat type-level counts on the targets that were set, which means the diagnosis was wrong or the match is wrong. The second is a student producing nothing between sessions, which means the constraint is time and motivation rather than teaching. Neither responds to a longer or more expensive session, and a provider recommending one in those circumstances is selling rather than advising.

On availability, the honest position: Standard Level Analysis and Approaches is the best-covered maths course in this set, so a specialist is usually available within days across most slots. Where it gets tight is the busiest weekday evening hour in term time, and there are weeks when the right specialist is not free in it. The options then are a different time, an adjacent specialist who can start now, or a date. What is not on offer is a generalist described as a Standard Level specialist, because that produces exactly the file of pleasant sessions and flat marks this page exists to prevent.

One last suggestion, free of charge. Before contacting anyone, run the delayed-recall test yourself on one topic your child's school reported as covered a month ago. Whatever the result, you will be able to describe the problem in a sentence that gets you matched to the right person first time.

process.title: Send one marked script and the topic log
process.description: A recent marked paper plus a list of which topics the school has covered and roughly when. Between them they let a first session start with a real diagnosis instead of a conversation, and they are what make the delayed-recall protocol possible from week one rather than week five.

process.title: Use the trial to produce a baseline
process.description: A working session over live video, booked without card details and scheduled around the school day. It produces a marked piece of work with the markscheme named, a count of losses by category, and two target question types written down. That count is the number every later comparison is measured against.

process.title: Agree the interleaving rule
process.description: A quarter of every session is spent on questions from topics covered weeks earlier, out of order and unlabelled. It makes homework scores look worse in the short term and transfer better in the long term, so it is worth agreeing explicitly rather than discovering by surprise.

process.title: Book the exploration block against the school's date
process.description: Get the coordinator's submission deadline and scope the block to it. Each session ends with the student holding a question to answer in writing, and the dated version history records what came back. The block closes when the work is submitted rather than renewing by default.

process.title: Review at six weeks on the counts
process.description: Two dated marked attempts, compared by loss category and by question type. Three honest outcomes: continue, change the diagnosis or the tutor, or stop because the student now self-marks. Fixing the date before the first paid session is what makes it a decision rather than a progress chat.

whyPoints.title: Progress tested after a delay, not during the lesson
whyPoints.description: Any competent tutorial produces a student who can do it now. The evidence that predicts a grade is an unprompted attempt three weeks later inside a mixed set. Building that into the schedule is the difference between a file of pleasant sessions and a file that tells you something.

whyPoints.title: Interleaved practice even though it looks worse
whyPoints.description: A quarter of each session on older topics out of order, because blocked practice flatters short-term performance and fails on a mixed paper. Agreeing this up front matters, since the first few weeks of interleaved work produce lower scores than a parent expects.

whyPoints.title: Every loss categorised so the counts are comparable
whyPoints.description: Method, knowledge, instruction or accuracy, marked beside the line it refers to, with the markscheme named by board, paper and series. A parent who cannot do the mathematics can still read whether eleven method losses became four.

whyPoints.title: The exploration kept as a dated version history
whyPoints.description: The student's own drafts with dates, criterion-referenced comments, and no replacement text at any point. It shows a parent that work is happening and demonstrates sole authorship if a coordinator asks. The family keeps the copies rather than the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Matched on component rather than proximity
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 technique, Paper 2 technology use and exploration supervision are three different jobs. Live video means the person matched is the one who does your child's job repeatedly, anywhere in the network, rather than the Standard Level generalist nearest your area of Dubai.

whyPoints.title: A stated finishing condition
whyPoints.description: Delayed attempts passing across all five topics, method marks collected reliably, Paper 2 finished in time, and the student able to self-mark. At that point the correct advice is to stop, and a provider unwilling to describe that point is not using the evidence on your behalf.

faqs.question: What evidence should we have after a month of AA SL tutoring?
faqs.answer: Two dated marked scripts, the markscheme named on both, a count of losses by category on each, and at least one unprompted attempt at a topic taught three weeks earlier inside a mixed set. If an exploration is live, add the dated draft and the criterion-referenced comments. What should not be the main item is a weekly report saying the sessions are going well, because that is the normal output of any competent lesson and it tells you nothing about retention. The categories matter most: eleven method losses falling to four is a measurement anybody can read.

faqs.question: How are the marks split between the two AA SL papers and the exploration?
faqs.answer: The published Standard Level structure is two written papers carrying the bulk of the grade between them, one sat without a calculator and one with technology permitted, plus the mathematical exploration at a fifth of the total. Check the exact weightings against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator, since the guide is the authoritative document and this page does not reproduce board material. The practical consequence is that a student who ignores the exploration has capped their grade before sitting a paper, and that is a surprisingly common pattern in a busy Diploma year.

faqs.question: Which AA SL paper should the first month of evidence come from?
faqs.answer: The calculator-free paper, almost always. It is where written argument earns the marks, so it exposes the gap between knowing the mathematics and collecting the marks more sharply than the technology paper does. A student who loses marks there while answering correctly has a procedural problem that is fast to fix and highly visible on a second script. Start with the technology paper only if the school report or a mock points specifically at timing or at calculator technique, in which case the pacing evidence matters more than the method evidence.

faqs.question: How do we tell a method-mark problem from a topic my child has not learnt?
faqs.answer: Read the script rather than the total. A method problem looks like correct answers with missing intermediate lines, or a right result with no stated reasoning. A knowledge problem looks like a blank, a false start, or a method borrowed from a different topic. The two need completely different responses: the first is a habit that can change within a few weeks of deliberate practice, the second needs re-teaching followed by spaced revisiting. Ask for every loss to be categorised on the script, because the category is the only thing that tells you which fix applies.

faqs.question: Which parts of the AA SL syllabus show up most often in our marked scripts?
faqs.answer: Calculus and functions dominate the recoverable losses, not because they are the hardest content but because they appear most often in disguise. A rate of change arrives as a volume, a cost or a velocity, and a student who can differentiate on request does not always recognise that differentiation is the request. Trigonometric identities come second, usually needed inside an integration question rather than in a section labelled trigonometry. Statistics losses are typically interpretive: a correct figure with no conclusion in context, which is a writing habit rather than a mathematical gap.

faqs.question: How many marks is the AA SL exploration worth, and against which criteria?
faqs.answer: It carries a fifth of the Standard Level grade and is assessed against lettered criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. For exact mark allocations, work from the current subject guide through your child's coordinator rather than from any third-party summary, including this one. What matters for a parent is the shape of the support: criterion-referenced questioning on the student's own work, a dated version history, and a submission date taken from the school's internal calendar rather than from the board's.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately write on an AA SL exploration draft?
faqs.answer: Questions and criterion pointers. Which criterion is this section trying to satisfy. The mathematics is correct but the reflection never says why this approach was chosen. The notation changes between pages three and five. Each of those forces the student to produce the improvement themselves, which is both the rule and the only version that leaves them better at the subject. What a tutor must never do is supply replacement sentences or restructure the work for the candidate. One provider in this market sells completed internal assessments outright, and buying one risks a malpractice finding against the student.

faqs.question: How often should the exploration version history be updated?
faqs.answer: Every time a draft moves in either direction. The student's file gets a date when they write it; the comments get a date when they come back. Over a term that produces four or five pairs, which is enough to show development without becoming a filing exercise. Keep the copies yourself rather than leaving the only set with a tutor, for two reasons: if the supervisor changes, the new one starts from where the work actually is, and if a coordinator ever queries authorship, the dated sequence is the answer rather than an assurance.

faqs.question: Does a higher raw mark always mean a better AA SL grade?
faqs.answer: No, and this is where families most often feel misled. Grade boundaries are set by the board for each series and move with paper difficulty, so a raw mark does not convert permanently into a grade. A student can gain nine marks on calculus questions, which is real and worth having, while the reported grade stays at a 5 because the threshold did not move with them. This is exactly why the comparison recommended here is at question-type level. Nobody can predict boundaries, and anybody converting marks into grades with confidence is guessing.

faqs.question: What is the difference between my child's mock grade and their predicted grade?
faqs.answer: The mock grade is performance on one paper on one day, converted with a boundary set the school chose, often from a previous series. The predicted grade is a formal judgement the school submits about what the candidate will achieve, and it is the number universities see. They are produced by different processes and routinely differ. Neither measures the thing a tutor can change, which is marks collected by question type. The more useful question to ask the school is which components the grade was calculated from and which of them was weakest.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark written working over video?
faqs.answer: Two ways, used for different purposes. For timed papers the student writes on paper under exam conditions, photographs or scans the script and sends it before the session; marking happens outside the session so the hour is spent teaching rather than watching. For teaching, the student writes on a shared surface the tutor sees live, which matters because the hesitation and the crossing-out are where a diagnosis comes from. The annotated script is then kept on file with the markscheme reference beside each mark, which is more than a visiting tutor usually leaves behind.

faqs.question: Is an IB DP Math AA SL tutor in Dubai available for home visits?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition across the UAE is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For this subject the format suits the evidence rather than compromising it, because written work moves between sessions and gets annotated on the document. It also widens the choice: instead of the Standard Level generalist nearest your part of Dubai, the match is somebody who works on the calculator-free paper or on exploration supervision repeatedly. Nothing in the hour pays for a drive across the city.

faqs.question: How do KHDA inspection reports help us read our child's maths grade?
faqs.answer: They describe a school, not a class, so use them for context rather than diagnosis. The regulator inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale, and a strong rating tells you the provision is good; it does not tell you whether your child's maths set is moving at a pace they can sustain. The more informative question for a maths department is which components the current grade was built from. In a strong cohort the commonest profile is a student who fails nothing, triggers no intervention and quietly accumulates unfinished topics.

faqs.question: Will mock weeks and Ramadan interrupt the evidence trail?
faqs.answer: They change its timing, which is why the protocol follows the school calendar rather than ignoring it. A delayed-recall attempt scheduled inside a mock week measures exhaustion rather than retention and should be moved. During Ramadan the shortened school day shifts when a student can concentrate, and sessions move accordingly, often later in the evening. The practical approach is to agree in advance which weeks are for evidence and which are for consolidation, so a gap in the file is a planned gap rather than a silent one.

faqs.question: When has AA SL tutoring done its job?
faqs.answer: When the student passes delayed, unprompted attempts across all five topics, collects method marks reliably on the calculator-free paper, finishes the technology paper inside the time, and can mark their own work against a published markscheme and name their weak question types. At that point the skill the tutoring was bought to install belongs to them, and the right shape is a session a fortnight through the final term and then nothing. A tutoring arrangement with no stated finishing condition was never a plan, and any provider unwilling to name one is not using the evidence on your behalf.

faqs.question: What happens if no AA SL specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, with options rather than a holding message. Standard Level Analysis and Approaches is the best-covered maths course in this set, so a match is usually available within days across most of the week. The pressure point is the busiest weekday evening hour in term time, where there are weeks when the right person is not free. The alternatives offered are a different time, an adjacent specialist who can start immediately, or a date. A generalist presented as a Standard Level specialist is the outcome this whole approach exists to avoid.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.closingHeading: Test one topic before you hire anyone
dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.closingBody: Pick a topic your child's Dubai school reported as covered about a month ago. Ask for two questions on it inside a mixed set, with no labels, and have the result marked against the published markscheme. Whatever comes back, you will know more about your child's Analysis and Approaches SL position than any report has told you, and you will be able to describe the problem in one sentence. Then book a free trial session over live video and send that script with it. The plan that comes back will name two question types and a review date rather than a number of hours.

intro.heading: The course Dubai students choose for the wrong reason and then need help with
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level has an image problem in this city, and it works in both directions. Students pick it believing it is the lighter of the two Higher Level mathematics courses, then meet a syllabus containing material that has no counterpart in Analysis and Approaches at all. Other students avoid it believing it is less rigorous, and discover during university applications that a number of quantitative degrees accept it perfectly well. Both groups end up searching for a tutor, and both need the same first thing: an honest account of what the course actually contains.

Here is that account. AI HL is examined by three papers and an exploration, with the same weightings as its sister course: Paper 1 and Paper 2 at 110 marks and 30 per cent each over two hours, Paper 3 at 55 marks and 20 per cent over one hour, and the twenty-mark exploration carrying the final fifth. A graphic display calculator is assumed in every paper, including Paper 1. The guide's recommended hours run to 240, of which roughly 210 cover examined content, and the largest single block, around 52 hours, sits in statistics and probability.

What makes the course demanding is not algebraic difficulty. It is breadth of unfamiliar machinery. A Higher Level Applications candidate is expected to handle Voronoi diagrams and toxic-waste-dump problems, adjacency and transition matrices, minimum spanning trees and the Chinese postman problem, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, complex numbers in exponential form for alternating-current modelling, chi-squared and t-tests, non-linear regression with coefficients of determination, and numerical methods including Euler's and Simpson's rules. A capable mathematics tutor who has only ever taught Analysis and Approaches will not have taught most of that list.

This is the reason delivery matters on this page. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubai address; home visits are something we run only in India. For AI HL that trade is close to decisive. The number of tutors in any single Dubai community who have genuinely taught graph theory and Markov chains for examination is very small, and restricting your shortlist to those who can arrive by half past five generally means accepting a tutor who is learning the syllabus alongside your child.

Dubai's own numbers explain how a student ends up isolated inside a large market. KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils in 227 private schools in 2024-25, teaching seventeen curricula, with the IB accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment, and seven further schools are opening for 2026-27 including three International Baccalaureate schools adding to a total of 16,846 new places. Inside that scale, a given school may enter four or five candidates for AI HL in a year. Those four or five students share one teacher, one scheme of work and one timetable, and if the gap is in matrices, nobody in the room has spare capacity to close it.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Applications and Interpretation rewards students who can interpret, model and justify, and those are habits built long before the Diploma. Here is what each programme contributes, and what Dubai parents should watch for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: AI HL counts as one of the three Higher Level subjects in a full Diploma. The 240 recommended hours are distributed differently from Analysis and Approaches: statistics and probability takes around 52, geometry and trigonometry around 46, functions around 42, calculus around 41 and number and algebra around 29. Breadth, rather than depth in one strand, is what the examination tests.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates overwhelmingly sit the May session. The IB publishes session windows and results dates and revises them, so take your dates from the school's Diploma coordinator rather than from any tutoring site. Internal deadlines for the exploration typically fall a term earlier than external ones, and those are the dates a tutoring plan should work backwards from.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is the direct ancestor of Applications and Interpretation. Students who score well on criterion D and less well on criterion A are frequently better suited to AI than to AA, and that signal sits in school reports two years before the choice is made. Very few families are shown it in those terms.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools teach the MYP straight into the Diploma, which means the route decision between the two mathematics courses is often made on teacher recommendation alone, with no external examination evidence either way. Asking for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the overall MYP grade is the most useful question a parent can put to the school.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP builds mathematics through inquiry across transdisciplinary themes, with data handling and measurement appearing early and often. Those strands matter unusually much for a future Applications student, because interpreting a data set and justifying a conclusion from it is the examined skill at the far end of the route.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA inspects annually and comments on attainment and progress separately in each subject. A primary report noting strength in data handling and weakness in number fluency describes a profile that will suit Applications and Interpretation later, which is worth filing away rather than acting on immediately.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: AI HL students in Dubai most often pair the course with the subjects below. Each entry names the component that usually decides the grade, since that is what a tutoring block has to target.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Three papers plus the exploration, with a calculator assumed throughout. The HL-only content carries the course: eigenvalues, Markov chains, graph theory algorithms, complex numbers in exponential form, hypothesis testing and numerical methods including Euler's and Simpson's rules.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Two 90-minute papers of 80 marks each plus the exploration, and no Paper 3. Statistics and probability dominates the hours. Students dropping from HL to SL lose the matrix and graph-theory content entirely, which is a substantial reduction rather than a trim.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with a non-calculator Paper 1 and a Paper 3 built on proof and pure problem-solving at Higher Level. A student considering a switch should understand that the two courses overlap less than their shared name suggests, particularly in the HL-only material.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The most natural partner to AI HL. HL adds a quantitative paper that draws on exactly the data-handling and interpretation skills the maths course examines. Three internally assessed commentaries on published articles complete the assessment, each with its own word limit and deadline.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Investment appraisal, break-even analysis and ratio interpretation sit close to AI content. The research project at Higher Level is the component most often underestimated, and AI students handle its quantitative side well while losing marks on the strategic evaluation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Graph and tree structures appear in both this course and AI HL, which is an overlap worth exploiting deliberately. Paper 2 and the solution-development internal assessment carry the practical weight; written extended responses on ethics and system design are the usual mark leak.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Statistical treatment of fieldwork data in the internal assessment is where AI HL students have an edge they rarely use. The written papers reward precise case-study detail and command-term discipline, neither of which is a mathematical skill.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the 2023 syllabus, Paper 1B is entirely data analysis, which suits an Applications student. The algebraic manipulation in Paper 2 can be harder for AI candidates than for AA candidates, and that gap is worth naming early rather than discovering in DP2.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Higher Level psychology includes research methodology and inferential statistics. An AI HL student already understands hypothesis testing and should be converting that into marks here; where they are not, the cause is usually the terminology of the discipline rather than the statistics.

sections.heading: What an AI HL home tutor search in Dubai is actually trying to solve
paragraphs: Specialist IB mathematics tuition in Dubai is published at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, and for Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level the scarce commodity is syllabus coverage rather than teaching skill. IB Gram supplies this as one-to-one tuition over live video to every community in the emirate. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and in-home work is a service we run only in India, which we state before any discussion of money.

The home-tutoring question still deserves answering properly. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is widely available at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with monthly packages around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, and for some students it is the right choice. A child who will not work without an adult in the room, a household where devices are shared and unreliable, a learner who finds screens genuinely difficult: each of those is a reason to pay the travel premium rather than fight it.

An AI HL candidate rarely fits that description. The problem is usually that nobody has taught them how to build an adjacency matrix from a weighted graph, or what an eigenvalue is doing inside a Markov chain, or how to choose between a chi-squared test for independence and one for goodness of fit. Those are specific pieces of a specific syllabus. A tutor is either carrying them or not, and geography has nothing to do with it.

There is a scheduling argument too, which families notice later. Because our tutors do not travel, a slot at 20:00 on a weeknight costs nobody an hour of driving afterwards, and the two or three weeks around Ramadan can shift to post-Iftar timings without renegotiating the arrangement. For a Higher Level student carrying six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the mandatory UAE subjects, that flexibility is often what keeps a weekly session from quietly lapsing in February.

sections.heading: What is in AI HL that is not in Analysis and Approaches at all
paragraphs: This is the section most families tell us they could not find anywhere else, so it is set out as a list of content rather than as a comparison of difficulty. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level contains substantial strands that have no counterpart in Analysis and Approaches at either level, and a tutor who has not taught them cannot teach them from a textbook on Sunday evening.

In geometry and trigonometry: Voronoi diagrams and their use in nearest-neighbour and toxic-waste-dump problems. In number and algebra: adjacency matrices, transition matrices, matrix multiplication, inverses, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and complex numbers written in exponential form for modelling alternating current and phase. In graph theory, which is examined as its own strand: walks, trails and cycles, minimum spanning trees via Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem, and the travelling salesman problem with upper and lower bounds.

In statistics and probability, the largest topic by hours: non-linear regression with coefficients of determination, chi-squared tests for independence and goodness of fit, the t-test, Spearman's rank correlation, transition matrices applied to long-run steady states, and the Poisson distribution. In calculus: slope fields, Euler's method for differential equations, coupled systems solved with eigenvalues, phase portraits, and numerical integration using the trapezoidal and Simpson's rules.

Set against that, the content Applications omits is real and worth knowing. There is no proof by induction, no implicit differentiation, no integration by substitution or by parts in the Analysis sense, and no complex-number work of the algebraic kind that Analysis examines. The honest summary is that Applications trades algebraic manipulation for breadth of applied technique, and that a student who finds unfamiliar machinery intimidating will not find this the easier course.

sections.heading: A calculator in every paper changes what the examiner is looking for
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation assumes a graphic display calculator in all three papers, including Paper 1. That single structural fact reshapes what preparation means. There is no paper on which algebraic fluency alone earns marks, and no paper on which the device cannot be used. What the papers test instead is whether the student can select the right tool, operate it correctly, and then explain the result in the language of the question.

The first consequence is that the calculator becomes examinable equipment rather than a convenience, and the student must know their own model. Entering a chi-squared test, reading the degrees of freedom, running a non-linear regression and extracting the coefficient of determination, setting up a transition matrix and raising it to a power: these are menu-level skills that differ between models, and a student who borrowed a sibling's calculator a week before the examination will lose marks to navigation rather than to mathematics.

The second consequence is that written justification carries more weight than students expect. A correct number produced by a device, with no indication of what was entered or why that test was appropriate, frequently scores less than half the available marks. Mark schemes award for stating hypotheses, for identifying the test, for giving the p-value and for drawing a conclusion in context. The arithmetic is the cheap part, and students who treat the answer as the destination routinely lose three or four marks on a six-mark question.

The third consequence is about sanity-checking. Because every answer comes from a device, an input error produces a plausible-looking output and nothing in the student's experience flags it. We teach an estimate-first habit: a rough expectation written down before the calculator is touched, so that a probability of 1.4 or a steady state that does not sum to one is caught by the student rather than by the examiner. It costs ten seconds a question and it is the single most reliable mark-saver in this course.

sections.heading: AI HL Paper 3: two questions, one hour, twenty per cent
paragraphs: Paper 3 at Higher Level is 55 marks in sixty minutes and contains two compulsory extended-response questions. In Applications and Interpretation those questions are modelling investigations: a context is introduced, usually with data, and the student is walked through a sequence of parts that build on one another, often ending somewhere the student has never been asked to go before. Twenty per cent of the final grade sits in this hour.

The paper's difficulty is structural rather than technical. Nothing appears on Paper 3 that is absent from the syllabus, which is why covering content again does not raise the mark. What raises it is the willingness to keep going when part (d) introduces a twist, and the discipline of answering earlier parts fully, since later parts frequently depend on a value or a model produced earlier. A student who guesses at part (b) and moves on has often forfeited parts (c) and (d) as well.

The commonest failure we record is a clean collapse at the point where the question asks for a comment rather than a calculation. "Explain why this model is unsuitable for large values of t" is worth marks and requires a sentence about the mathematics, not about the context in general. Students trained to produce numbers freeze at these parts, leave them blank, and then run out of time on the second question because the first took too long.

The training for this is specific and it starts early. From the first term, a Paper 3 question goes into every second session, under timed conditions, marked, and then examined for one thing: where did the student stop, and was it because they could not do the mathematics or because they did not believe they could? Those two causes look identical on a blank page and need opposite responses. Leaving Paper 3 until the revision term is the most common planning error in this course.

sections.heading: Switching between the two maths courses, and what the switch costs in hours
paragraphs: Route changes are common in Dubai and are usually discussed too late. A student who moves from Analysis and Approaches HL to Applications and Interpretation HL does not simply drop difficult content; they acquire a different set of unfamiliar content, and most of it sits in strands the Analysis syllabus never touches. Graph theory, matrices and eigenvalues, hypothesis testing and numerical methods have to be built from nothing, and that is a defined block of work rather than a tidy-up.

Moving the other way is harder in a different place. A student going from Applications to Analysis at Higher Level inherits a non-calculator Paper 1 they have never sat, plus proof, implicit differentiation and the integration techniques Applications omits. In our experience the non-calculator paper is the shock, not the new content: two years of calculator-permitted practice leaves algebraic fluency untested, and it takes longer to rebuild than a topic does.

The timing of a switch is set by the school and by IB registration, not by a tutor, and a family should raise it with the Diploma coordinator as soon as it is being considered. What we can do is scope the work honestly before the decision is made: which strands are missing, roughly how many hours each takes to build to examination standard, and whether that is feasible in the weeks remaining. A switch agreed in October of DP1 is a different proposition from one attempted in DP2.

They should be read as a planning range rather than a promise, because a student's starting point changes everything. What they are good for is testing whether a proposed switch is realistic before the registration form is signed.

sections.heading: The exploration when the data is real
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation explorations tend to use real data, and that is both the course's advantage and its characteristic trap. The exploration is marked out of twenty against five criteria, with twelve to twenty pages recommended, and criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six of those marks and asks for mathematics commensurate with Higher Level. For an AI HL candidate that usually means a statistical test properly chosen and properly interpreted, or a model fitted and then criticised, rather than a large data set described at length.

The trap is gathering data first and looking for a question afterwards. A student who collects eight hundred rows of something interesting and then tries to find mathematics to apply to it produces an exploration that scores badly on personal engagement and reflection while containing a great deal of work. The order matters: a question that can be answered, then the data needed to answer it, then the mathematics, then the reflection on what the mathematics missed.

Criterion D, reflection, is worth three marks and is where real-data explorations can win easily. Data gathered by a student has limitations that are concrete and discussable: a small sample, a biased collection method, a confounding variable noticed too late. Writing about those honestly scores better than pretending the investigation was clean. Criterion C, personal engagement, also worth three, is satisfied far more convincingly by data the student collected than by a downloaded file.

The limits on tutor involvement here are firm and worth stating in full. The exploration must be entirely the student's own work. A tutor may interrogate a research question until it is specific enough to answer, read a submitted draft, comment against each criterion, point out where a statistical test does not support the claim being made, and explain what a criterion rewards. A tutor may not supply text, rework paragraphs, choose the data or provide analysis for insertion. Providers in this market sell finished coursework; the malpractice consequence falls on the candidate alone.

What you receive in exchange is a record. Every fortnight: the marked work annotated in mark-scheme wording, a strand log showing which of the HL-only topics have been pre-tested, taught and post-tested, the Paper 3 stopping points in sequence, and one line naming the current working mark and the component it came from. sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what a Dubai parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the regulator approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, not only inspection outcomes.

Private tutoring is a separate matter from school regulation, and it is permitted rather than unregulated. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than most parents assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you. A parent engaging any in-person tutor in the UAE can simply ask to see the permit.

One more boundary is worth stating because it affects a popular arrangement. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as the regulator's exact wording, and verify it against the current policy before relying on it. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation HL easier than Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: It is different rather than easier, and students who choose it expecting a gentler course are the ones who most often need help. Applications drops proof, implicit differentiation and the Analysis integration techniques, and adds strands with no AA counterpart at all: graph theory, matrices and eigenvalues, chi-squared and t-tests, non-linear regression, slope fields and numerical methods. The algebra is lighter and the breadth of unfamiliar machinery is greater. A student who finds new techniques intimidating will not find this the softer option.

faqs.question: What exactly is in AI HL that my child would never meet in AA?
faqs.answer: Voronoi diagrams and nearest-neighbour problems. Adjacency and transition matrices, matrix inverses and determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Graph theory as an examined strand, including minimum spanning trees by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem and the travelling salesman problem with bounds. Chi-squared tests for independence and goodness of fit, the t-test and Spearman's rank correlation. Complex numbers in exponential form for alternating-current modelling. Slope fields, Euler's method, coupled systems and Simpson's rule. None of that appears in Analysis and Approaches at either level.

faqs.question: Why does AI HL need ninety-minute sessions rather than sixty?
faqs.answer: Because the questions are long. A single Paper 3 modelling investigation can take a student twenty-five minutes before any discussion of it begins, and a graph-theory question with a real network or a matrix question with a transition model is not a ten-minute exercise. Sixty-minute sessions on this course tend to stop in the middle of a problem, which is the least useful place to stop. Ninety minutes also usually prices lower per hour, because the tutor's scheduling overhead spreads further.

faqs.question: Does the AI HL tutor come to our home in Dubai, or is it all online?
faqs.answer: All online. Sessions run live over video, one-to-one, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Parents search for "home tutor" and the page uses the phrase honestly, but on this course the trade is unusually clear: the tutors who have taught eigenvalues and spanning trees for examination are few, and limiting the shortlist to those who can drive to your community by 17:30 generally means accepting someone learning the syllabus as they go.

faqs.question: How is Paper 3 different in Applications from Paper 3 in Analysis?
faqs.answer: Both are one hour, 55 marks, two compulsory extended-response questions and twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade. The Analysis version is pure problem-solving, developing an unfamiliar mathematical idea in stages. The Applications version is modelling: a real context is introduced, usually with data, and the student builds or fits a model and then extends, criticises or recommends. The Applications paper asks for written comment on the mathematics more often, and students trained only to produce numbers lose marks at exactly those parts.

faqs.question: My son enters the right test on his calculator and still loses marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the number is the cheap part. Mark schemes for a statistical test award marks for stating the hypotheses, naming the test, giving the degrees of freedom or the p-value, and drawing a conclusion in the context of the question. A student who writes only the p-value and a verdict typically collects fewer than half the available marks, even with everything correct. The fix is a written template per test type, practised until it is automatic, and it usually recovers three to four marks per question.

faqs.question: What do UAE universities think of AI HL for engineering or finance?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements are set by individual universities and faculties and are revised, so the only reliable source is each university's admissions page for the year of entry. The broad pattern is that engineering and physics programmes more often specify Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, while business, finance, economics, geography and many computer science routes accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level without difficulty. Check the named course rather than relying on a general claim from any tutoring provider, including this one.

faqs.question: Can my daughter switch from AA HL to AI HL now, and what would she need to catch up?
faqs.answer: The school and IB registration timetable decide whether a switch is possible, so raise it with the Diploma coordinator immediately. On the workload, the switch is not a reduction: graph theory, matrices and eigenvalues, hypothesis testing and numerical methods all have to be built from nothing, which in one-to-one work typically takes somewhere between twenty-five and forty hours depending on her starting point. We will scope it honestly before the decision rather than afterwards, including when the answer is that there is not enough time left.

faqs.question: How should an Applications exploration use real data without losing marks?
faqs.answer: Question first, data second. Students who gather a large data set and then search for mathematics to apply to it score badly on personal engagement and reflection despite doing a great deal of work. A workable research question, then the minimum data needed to answer it, then a properly chosen statistical test or fitted model, then honest reflection on the sample's limitations. Criterion D is worth three of the twenty marks and real-data explorations can win it easily, because their limitations are concrete and genuinely worth discussing.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to do with an AI HL exploration draft?
faqs.answer: Read it, comment against the five criteria, question the research question until it is answerable, point out where a test does not support the claim being made, and explain what each criterion rewards. What a tutor must not do is supply text, rework the student's paragraphs, choose the data set or hand over analysis for insertion. The exploration must be entirely the student's own work under IB academic-honesty rules. Some providers in this market sell completed coursework outright, and the malpractice consequence of that falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: How much does Applications and Interpretation HL tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for IB specialists in Dubai run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above, with Unitors advertising IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table extending past AED 450 for examination-year specialists. In-home visits are quoted from about AED 180 to AED 500 with travel embedded, and monthly in-home packages around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those are market figures. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, since the number depends on components, hours and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Which calculator should my child be using, and does the model matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more on this course than on any other Diploma subject, because a graphic display calculator is assumed in all three papers. The school will specify an approved model and the student should use that same device for every practice session, not a sibling's different one. Menu paths for a chi-squared test, a non-linear regression or a matrix power differ between models, and marks lost to navigation under time pressure are indistinguishable from marks lost to not knowing the mathematics. Check the model during the free trial.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time listed on the ministry's own service page. Registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18 are all eligible. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Nobody is free at 18:00 for AI HL. What are the realistic alternatives?
faqs.answer: You will be told that before paying, which is not standard practice in this market. The alternatives are a different hour in the same week, often 16:30 or 20:00, which open up more readily; a wait of a week or two for a named specialist to free a slot; or a tutor outside the Gulf time zone whose availability is stated plainly so you can judge whether the hour works for your household. What we will not do is fill the slot with a general maths tutor and leave you to discover the gap in matrices.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during study leave or move during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Both, and online delivery is what makes it straightforward. Ramadan shortens the school day in Dubai and reshapes family evenings, so sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar slots for that period and then return to the usual time. Study leave and the examination weeks themselves are usually the right moment to pause rather than push, and that pause works better agreed in advance than cancelled week by week. Family travel is handled the same way: the lesson follows the student rather than the address.

intro.heading: What progress in AI HL looks like on paper, week by week
paragraphs: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level runs to 240 teaching hours and is assessed by three papers and one exploration. Paper 1 and Paper 2 each last two hours, carry 110 marks and take 30% of the grade. Paper 3 lasts one hour, carries 55 marks, takes 20%, and consists of two compulsory extended-response problem-solving questions. The exploration takes the final 20%, marked out of 20. Every one of those components produces something you can read, and this page is about reading it.

Most parents judge tutoring by whether their child seems more confident. That is the least reliable signal available. A student who has been taught a technique in a session will feel better about it that evening and still lose the same four marks three weeks later under timed conditions. The signal worth tracking is narrower: a script, with marks on it, dated, with the mark type named beside each loss, and a second script two weeks later showing whether the same loss recurred.

AI HL generates unusually good evidence because technology is permitted in every paper. When the calculator is not the variable, the remaining variables are interpretation, modelling choice and the written justification, and all three are visible in the student's own handwriting. A tutor who returns a marked AI HL script can tell you whether a mark was lost because the model was wrong, because the answer was correct but never stated in context, or because the student rounded at the wrong point of the calculation.

Paper 3 deserves a paragraph of its own, because it is the component Dubai families most often discover late. It is a single hour of two long investigations that build on each other, where part (a) feeds part (f) and an early error propagates. School mock papers frequently omit it or shorten it, so a student can reach February of DP2 with no full-length Paper 3 attempt on record. Asking a tutor for one marked Paper 3 script is the fastest way to find out where the real risk sits, and it costs one session rather than a term.

The rest of this page describes the evidence in order: the four-week trail, the Paper 3 script, how to read mark types on a markscheme, the dated version history behind the exploration, what a grade rise actually requires in raw marks, and the reporting file we keep and will delete on request. Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and the comparison table in the seventh section explains why the evidence a family ends up holding tends to be better, more complete and more portable without one.
