A tutor working without sight of those is working on description rather than data, which is why the first session asks for the most recent marked paper rather than a list of topics.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools publish their own mock windows and their own internal coursework deadlines, and those dates differ between schools a few kilometres apart. The practical effect for an AI HL family is that the first genuinely comparable piece of evidence often arrives in the first term of DP2, when a full mock finally exists. Before that, the usable evidence is whatever the subject teacher has marked, which is why we ask for it in the first message rather than the fourth week.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria, not papers, so the evidence is criterion-referenced and qualitative. That makes it harder to compare with Diploma marks and easier to misread. A student achieving a 7 in MYP 5 against criterion A may still be weak at the sustained multi-step work Paper 3 demands. The useful evidence at this stage is a timed, unseen multi-step question marked honestly, which is what a diagnostic session produces.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB continuum schools run large MYP cohorts in Al Barsha, Nad Al Sheba and Mirdif, and the AI or AA decision is usually taken in MYP 5. Families who ask for one piece of evidence at that point, a marked unseen problem rather than a report comment, make a better-informed choice. AI HL suits a student who reasons well with data and context; it is not the easier course, and 52 hours of statistics is not a soft option.

programmes.name: IGCSE to AI HL bridge
programmes.description: An IGCSE Extended maths grade is a poor predictor of AI HL performance on its own, because IGCSE rewards executing a known procedure while AI HL rewards choosing a model and justifying it. The bridging evidence worth collecting is a single AI-style modelling question: given data and a context, build something defensible and write a sentence explaining what the answer means. Students who can do that in Year 11 need far fewer paid hours in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is predominantly British by enrolment, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of private school students, so most AI HL students in the emirate come from IGCSE rather than MYP. Summer bridging work between Year 11 and DP1 is common here and produces its own evidence: four marked modelling questions, done in August, tell a family more about readiness for Higher Level than a Year 11 report does.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: AI HL is the subject in the URL, and the grid below places it among the Diploma subjects Dubai families most often support alongside it. Each entry is written around the evidence that subject generates, because that is what a parent can actually inspect.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: HL adds Paper 3 and ninety guide hours over SL. The evidence to ask for is a marked full-length Paper 3, because it is the component schools most often leave out of mocks and the one where early errors propagate through a whole question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA Paper 1 is sat without technology, so the evidence looks different: manual algebra and exact values in the student's own hand. Families comparing the two courses should ask to see a marked script from each before committing to a switch.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1B is a data-analysis section, so Physics produces evidence that overlaps directly with AI HL: gradients, uncertainties and conclusions written in context. A single marked Paper 1B often explains a maths problem and a physics problem at once.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation chains are the evidence here, and they fail in identifiable places. A marked question on moles and concentration shows whether the student loses marks on chemistry or on arithmetic discipline, which is a question worth answering before paying for either subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The statistical content, standard deviation, error bars and correlation, is shared ground with AI HL. Extended-response answers need reading closely rather than scanning, so marking turnaround is the practical constraint on how much evidence a week can produce.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal commentaries plus a quantitative HL paper make this a document-heavy subject. The dated draft history of a commentary is strong evidence of genuine authorship, and the quantitative paper rewards exactly the habits AI HL is trying to build.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study responses are the evidence, and they improve visibly once structure is taught. Progress here is easier to see week to week than in mathematics, which makes it a useful second subject when a family wants an early signal.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution component produces its own artefacts, including a dated development record. Pseudocode discipline sits close to AI HL reasoning, and a student who writes clear pseudocode usually writes clearer mathematical justification too.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Data interpretation and systems diagrams generate evidence quickly, and the subject's quantitative questions reward the same contextual writing AI HL demands. A common pairing for Dubai students who want a second data-led subject without a third mathematics-heavy one.

The notes below describe what each community does to a weekly slot and to the turnaround on marked work, because both affect how much evidence a term actually produces.

regions.note: A dense DP population and a short school walk, so an early evening slot is easy to hold. Marked work usually comes back fastest here simply because sessions start on time and run their full hour.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Tower living with mixed school destinations across Sheikh Zayed Road. Families here often hold a later slot, which means written work is set for a weekend return rather than a midweek one.

regions.note: An early school finish makes a 4pm slot genuinely available, and that is the slot where a full timed Paper 3 attempt fits inside one session without running into dinner.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Served by established IB continuum schools with their own internal exploration deadlines. Those school deadlines, rather than the exam session, are what the version history of a draft gets planned around here.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: A newer corridor with growing Diploma cohorts, which means mock timetables are still settling. We ask for the published school calendar in the first week rather than assuming last year's dates apply.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: An eastern family district with a long crossing to the western school corridor. Online delivery is what makes a fixed weekly slot survivable here, and a surviving slot is what produces a continuous evidence trail.

regions.note: Next to Academic City, with a large student population and evening slots that fill early. Booking the slot in the first week of term is the difference between twelve marked scripts in a term and seven.

schoolClusters.note: Several Diploma cohorts within a few kilometres, which means mock papers and internal deadlines in this corridor are comparable between schools. Students we support here most often ask for Paper 3 technique and for help reading their own mock feedback.

schoolClusters.note: A wider spread of IB continuum and Diploma schools from Meydan and Nad Al Sheba through to Deira and Dubai Festival City. modes.title: A diagnostic session built on an existing script
modes.description: One hour spent marking and interrogating a paper the student has already sat. The output is a written list of the marks lost, sorted by mark type rather than by topic, and an estimate of how many sessions each one needs. It is the cheapest piece of real evidence available, and it tells you whether the problem is method, accuracy or reading the question.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with marking between sessions
modes.description: A fixed Gulf Standard Time slot each week, work set after every session, and that work returned marked before the next one. Over a Dubai term this produces about a dozen dated scripts, which is enough to see whether a specific loss recurs. The pattern across those scripts is the evidence; any single script is noise.

modes.description: Three or four sessions built entirely around full-length Paper 3 attempts under exam conditions, marked and reviewed. Because Paper 3 questions escalate within themselves, the evidence it produces is different from anything Paper 1 or Paper 2 generates: it shows whether a student can hold a thread across six parts of one problem.

sections.heading: The four-week evidence trail: what should exist, and when
paragraphs: Four weeks of weekly AI HL support should leave four dated artefacts behind. Week one produces a written diagnosis built on an existing script. Week two produces the first piece of work set and marked. Week three produces the first repeat test of the original weakness. Week four produces a short pattern note saying whether the weakness has moved. If any of those four is missing, the question to ask is not whether your child is enjoying the sessions.

The trail matters because mathematics improvement is not linear and feels like nothing for the first fortnight. A student rebuilding how they set up a model will temporarily get slower and may score lower, and without dated evidence that looks like failure rather than reconstruction. With the scripts in front of you, it is visible as a method change: fewer marks on the first attempt, the same marks regained two weeks later, and then marks appearing that were never there before.

What should be in each note is specific and short. The topic, the component it belongs to, the marks available, the marks scored, the mark type lost, and the single thing set as follow-up. Notes longer than that tend to be padding, and notes shorter than that are not evidence. We write them in plain language rather than in assessment vocabulary, because a note a parent cannot read is a note that gets filed and never used.

Missing evidence has honest explanations. A session lost to a school trip, a week where the student had three internal deadlines, or a deliberate decision to spend two sessions teaching rather than testing are all legitimate. What is not legitimate is four weeks of pleasant sessions with nothing written down, and a family being asked to renew on the strength of a feeling. The table sets out what to expect and what to do if it is absent.

sections.heading: Paper 3 is the Higher Level script you should ask to see marked
paragraphs: Paper 3 is one hour, 55 marks and 20% of the AI HL grade, made up of two compulsory extended-response problem-solving questions. Technology is required throughout. Its structure is what makes it different: each question unfolds across several parts that depend on earlier answers, so a modelling choice made in part (b) can cost marks in parts (d), (e) and (f) even when every subsequent step is executed correctly. No other component in AI HL punishes an early decision that way.

The practical consequence for Dubai families is that Paper 3 is under-evidenced. School mocks often use a shortened version or omit it, because marking two long investigations for a whole cohort is expensive in teacher time. A student can therefore arrive in February of DP2 having never completed a full-length Paper 3 under timed conditions. The first full attempt is almost always a shock, and it is far better experienced in a session in November than in an examination hall in May.

A marked Paper 3 script is also the most informative single document a tutor can produce about an AI HL student. It shows whether they can read a long stem, whether they define variables before using them, whether they notice that part (e) is asking them to validate the model they built in part (b), and whether they write a conclusion in the context of the question rather than as a bare number. Those four habits are worth more than any amount of topic revision.

Ask for the attempt, the markscheme-aligned marking and the propagation trace: which later marks were lost because of which earlier decision. A tutor who can produce that for one paper can produce it for the rest. One who returns a percentage and a verbal summary has not done the work that makes the evidence useful.

sections.heading: Reading a markscheme: method marks, accuracy marks and follow-through
paragraphs: A mark on an IB mathematics markscheme is not a generic point. Method marks reward a correct approach even when the arithmetic fails afterwards. Accuracy marks reward a correct value, usually to three significant figures unless the question says otherwise. Reasoning marks reward a justification written in words. Follow-through allows a correct method applied to an earlier wrong answer to still earn credit. A student who does not know which type they are losing cannot fix the loss, and neither can a tutor working from a percentage.

This distinction changes what a session should do. A student losing method marks needs to be taught a technique. A student losing accuracy marks while keeping every method mark does not need teaching at all; they need discipline around rounding, units and transcription, and that is fixed by habit rather than by explanation. Buying teaching hours for an accuracy problem is one of the commonest wasted spends in the Dubai tutoring market, and the marked script is what exposes it.

Follow-through is the rule that most changes how a parent should read a low mark. A student can make one error in part (a) and still collect most of the marks in later parts, provided their working is visible. The corollary is brutal: a student who writes down only final answers forfeits both the method marks and the follow-through. On Paper 3, where parts chain together, invisible working can turn a single slip into a double-figure loss.

We write the mark type beside each loss on anything we return, and the six-week pattern note counts them. Four weeks of accuracy losses and no method losses is a very different brief from the reverse, and the two briefs need different tutors, different work and a different number of hours. That is the whole argument for evidence over impression.

sections.heading: The exploration at Higher Level: a dated version history, one author
paragraphs: The AI HL exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, with six of the twenty marks on the last of those. It carries the same 20% weight as Paper 3. The IB recommends a piece of roughly twelve to twenty pages. The evidence that it is genuinely the student's own is a dated version history, and that history is also the best protection either of you has if authorship is ever questioned.

Practically, that means keeping versions rather than overwriting one file. A first version with the topic and the data source. A second with the mathematics attempted and the gaps visible. A third after feedback, where the changes are the student's response to questions rather than text supplied to them. Dubai schools run their own internal deadlines and their own authenticity conversations, and a student who can walk a coordinator through three dated versions is in a different position from one who cannot.

The boundary on paid support is firm and we state it the same way everywhere. A tutor may teach a technique on a different example, ask what a symbol means, say where a reader loses the thread, and ask what would change the result. The student makes every choice and types every word of what is submitted. Any provider offering a finished document for a fee is selling academic malpractice, and the consequence under IB rules falls on the candidate, not the seller.

At Higher Level the commonest failure is not dishonesty but ambition. A student picks a topic requiring mathematics beyond the course, spends six weeks on it and produces something that scores poorly against criterion E because the mathematics is unsupported rather than wrong. One session testing topic viability against the AI HL toolkit in the first fortnight prevents most of that, and it produces a written note recording what was ruled out and why.

sections.heading: Raw marks against grade boundaries: what a grade rise actually requires
paragraphs: A grade in IB mathematics is produced by adding weighted component scores and comparing the total against boundaries set for that examination session. The boundaries are not fixed in advance and are not ours to publish; grade-boundary tables are the IB's material, and a tutoring page reproducing them would be both a copyright problem and a disservice, because a boundary from one session does not transfer cleanly to the next. What a family can work with instead is raw marks and the weighting arithmetic.

That arithmetic is worth doing once in front of the scripts. A student scoring consistently on Paper 1 and Paper 2 but leaving Paper 3 largely unattempted is carrying a 20% component at a fraction of its value, and recovering even half of that component moves the total more than a general improvement across the two long papers would. Conversely, a student losing a scatter of accuracy marks across all three papers has no single fix, and the honest answer is that the gain will be smaller and slower.

This is also where we decline to make a promise. Nobody can commit to a particular grade, because the total depends on components we do not mark and boundaries nobody knows in advance. Any provider promising a particular score in advance is describing something they do not control. What a tutor can commit to is the process: marked work every week, a count of mark types lost, and an honest statement at six weeks about whether the pattern is moving.

What progress looks like in the numbers, then, is this: the same mark type appearing less often across successive dated scripts, and a previously unattempted component starting to score. Those two movements are visible weeks before a school report reflects them, which is exactly why the evidence trail is worth more to a parent than a predicted grade.

sections.heading: The statistics half of AI HL, where the evidence usually points
paragraphs: Statistics and probability takes 52 of the 240 guide hours at AI HL, more than any other topic, with geometry and trigonometry at 46, functions at 42, calculus at 41 and number and algebra at 29. The weighting surprises students who chose AI expecting a lighter course than Analysis and Approaches. It is not lighter; it is differently heavy, and the weight sits on interpretation of data rather than on manipulation of symbols.

In the marked scripts, the losses concentrate in identifiable places. Choosing the wrong statistical test or regression model for the data given. Quoting a correlation coefficient without saying what it means for the situation described. Treating a p-value as a verdict rather than as evidence. Confusing the conditions under which a normal model applies. Each of those produces a distinctive pattern of lost reasoning and context marks, and each is fixable in two or three sessions once named.

The Higher Level additions are where Paper 3 draws much of its material: more demanding probability, matrices and graph theory applied to real contexts, and modelling that has to be validated rather than merely constructed. A student who can build a model but never checks it against the data will lose marks consistently in the back half of a Paper 3 question, and that is the single most common HL-specific pattern we see in Dubai scripts.

The practical sequence is to test statistics first in any diagnostic session, because it is the largest block and the one most likely to be generating losses. If the diagnostic shows statistics is secure and calculus is not, the plan changes accordingly. The point of leading with evidence rather than a standard syllabus tour is precisely so that the plan can be wrong in week one and corrected in week two.

sections.heading: Why the evidence is better from an online specialist than a nearby generalist
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen where tutor and student write on the same page, timed to Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school day. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and no sentence on this site should suggest otherwise to a family in this emirate.

The case for that is about the evidence rather than convenience. The International Baccalaureate accounts for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for UK curricula, which means AI HL specialists are thin on the ground in any single community. Requiring a tutor to be within a tolerable drive of your villa reduces the pool to whoever is nearby and available, and the person who is nearby is often a general maths tutor rather than someone who has marked Paper 3 scripts to a markscheme.

Online delivery also improves the artefacts themselves. Work is shared as a file rather than carried in a bag, so a marked script exists in two places and can be read by a parent in another country. The shared screen leaves a written record of the session's working. Nothing is lost to a dropped folder or a forgotten exercise book, and a tutor who moves house or changes city does not end the arrangement mid-course.

The honest counterweight is that a student who will not sit still for a video lesson is not served by one, and we say so at the trial rather than afterwards. The trial exists for exactly that question. sections.heading: The reporting file: what we write down, what we keep, and how to delete it
paragraphs: Everything described on this page creates records about a child: marked scripts, session notes, a school name, a year group and a set of grades. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs that, and the honest position is to tell you what exists rather than bury it in a policy page. We keep the session notes, the marked work and the enquiry details. We do not collect a child's photograph, their full school timetable or their medical information, because none of those are needed to teach mathematics.

Deletion is a request, not a negotiation. Ask and the file goes, including the marked scripts, and we confirm when it has. The one thing we will do first is offer to send you copies, because a family that has paid for a term of marking usually wants the scripts even after they stop the lessons. Several providers in this market treat accumulated student work as their own asset; it is the student's.

The other half of honest reporting is what we refuse to publish. No satisfaction percentage, no median tutor score, no claim about what proportion of students improved, because we cannot show you the sample, the date or the method behind any of those numbers. Pages in this search carry all three, and in some cases two contradictory versions on the same page. A statistic without its sample size and its method is decoration.

What a session note will say is narrow and checkable: the date, the component, the topic, the marks available, the marks scored, the mark types lost and the single piece of follow-up work. What it will never say is that your child is on track for a particular grade. That claim depends on components nobody in this arrangement marks, and a tutor who makes it is telling you something they cannot know.

process.title: Send one marked paper, not a summary
process.description: A photograph of a recent AI HL script with marks on it is the single most useful thing you can send. It shows whether the losses are method, accuracy or context, which is information no description of a child's confidence can carry. Add the school and the year group and the brief is complete.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, free, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. Your child works with the tutor we actually propose. The trial produces its own first artefact: a short written note on what the session found, which you keep whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Agree what gets marked and when
process.description: Before the second session we state in writing what work will be set, how it comes back, and the turnaround. Marking is inside the fee rather than billed separately, because a tutor charging for marking time has a quiet reason to set very little of it.

process.title: Run the weekly slot and collect the scripts
process.description: A fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, work set after each session and returned marked before the next. Over a Dubai term that produces around a dozen dated scripts. Keep them in one folder; the pattern across them is the evidence, and any single script on its own is noise.

process.title: Hold the six-week review properly
process.description: Six weeks in, we put the scripts on the table and make one of three decisions: continue, change the component the hours target, or stop because the pattern has resolved. Stopping is a real outcome and we will recommend it when the evidence supports it rather than letting a slot roll on.

whyPoints.title: Mark types written beside every loss
whyPoints.description: Returned work says whether a mark went on method, accuracy, reasoning or context. That distinction decides whether the next session teaches something or builds a checking habit, and the two are not interchangeable. A percentage tells you neither.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 attempted in full before February
whyPoints.description: The hour-long Higher Level paper is the component Dubai school mocks most often shorten or omit. We schedule a full-length timed attempt early, because the first complete Paper 3 is always instructive and much better experienced in a session than in an exam hall.

whyPoints.title: A dated note after every single session
whyPoints.description: Short, plain and specific: date, component, topic, marks available, marks scored, mark types lost, follow-up set. Long notes are padding. A note you cannot read in thirty seconds is a note that gets filed and never used again.

whyPoints.title: A review at six weeks where stopping is allowed
whyPoints.description: The default in this market is renewal. The default here is a conversation with the scripts in front of both of us, and one of the three legitimate outcomes is that the problem is fixed and the weekly slot should end.

whyPoints.title: No numbers we cannot show you the method for
whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentage, no improvement rate, no median tutor score. Pages in this search publish all three without a sample size or a date, and some publish two different versions of the same figure. We would rather publish nothing than that.

whyPoints.title: The work belongs to the student
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts and session notes are yours. Ask for them and they are sent; ask for deletion and the file goes, with copies offered first. Several providers treat accumulated student work as a retention tool, which is the wrong way round.

faqs.question: What should we see after four weeks of AI HL tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four dated artefacts. A written diagnosis from week one built on a real script, the first set work returned marked, a timed repeat of the original weakness in week three, and a short pattern note in week four saying whether the same mark type is still being lost. Marks may not have moved yet, and in a genuine method rebuild they sometimes dip first. What matters is that the four documents exist and that the pattern note is specific. Four pleasant sessions with nothing written down is not progress you can verify.

faqs.question: How do we know a marked AI HL script was marked properly?
faqs.answer: Look for mark types rather than a total. A properly marked script shows where a method mark was awarded despite a wrong final answer, where an accuracy mark was lost to premature rounding, and where follow-through credit carried an error forward. It should also trace propagation on Paper 3: which later marks fell because of which earlier decision. A script returned as a percentage with a comment has not been marked in any useful sense, and you cannot plan the next session from it.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 evidence look like for an AI HL student?
faqs.answer: A full-length attempt, one hour, timed and uninterrupted, on two compulsory extended-response questions worth 55 marks between them. Marked, it should show whether the student defined variables before using them, whether they validated the model they built earlier in the question, and whether each answer ends with a sentence in the context given. Because the parts chain together, the marking should name the one decision that cost the most marks downstream. That single document is usually more informative than a term of topic quizzes.

faqs.question: Can we see the markscheme the tutor used on our child's paper?
faqs.answer: You can see the marking on your child's script, including the mark type beside each loss, and we will explain the reasoning in plain language. We do not send you IB markschemes, past papers or grade-boundary tables, because those are the IB's material and redistributing them is a copyright matter rather than a service. Schools have legitimate access through their coordinators. What we provide is our marking of your child's own work, which is the part you are actually paying for.

faqs.question: How many drafts of the exploration can a tutor comment on?
faqs.answer: Follow your school's stated policy, because the school sets the internal process and runs the authenticity conversation. The IB model is a limited round of feedback on a single version, with the student responding to questions rather than receiving replacement text. Practically, we recommend keeping three dated versions: one with topic and data source, one with the mathematics attempted, and one after feedback. Every choice and every word is the student's. A tutor who offers to supply paragraphs is offering malpractice, and the candidate carries the consequence.

faqs.question: Does a rise in raw marks always mean a rise in the AI HL grade?
faqs.answer: No. The grade comes from weighted component totals compared against boundaries set for that session, and those boundaries are not published in advance. A rise of a few raw marks spread thinly across three papers may not cross a boundary, while recovering half of an unattempted Paper 3, worth 20% of the grade, moves the total considerably. That is why the plan targets a component rather than a general improvement, and why nobody should promise you a specific grade in exchange for a specific number of hours.

faqs.question: What does a weekly AI HL session note actually contain?
faqs.answer: The date, the component covered, the topic, the marks available, the marks scored, the mark types lost and one piece of follow-up work. Nothing else. It is written so a parent can read it in half a minute, because a note in assessment vocabulary gets filed and never used. It deliberately avoids any statement about which grade your child is heading for, since a tutor marks only part of the course and cannot know how the rest will score.

faqs.question: How do you tell a calculator mistake from a method mistake in AI HL?
faqs.answer: The written working shows it. Because technology is permitted in all three AI HL papers, a wrong answer with correct visible method points at the machine or at the input: a degree-radian setting, a mistyped value, a regression run on the wrong column. A wrong answer with no working, or with working that sets up the wrong model, points at method. The two need different remedies, and that is why we insist every line is written down even when the student can see the answer.

faqs.question: Our school report says working at a 5. What does that tell us?
faqs.answer: Less than it appears to. A school grade is a teacher's judgement against that cohort and that scheme of work, often before a full set of components has been assessed, and schools in Dubai differ in how conservatively they predict. It tells you roughly where your child sits in their class. It does not tell you which mark types are being lost, whether Paper 3 has been attempted in full, or whether the exploration is viable. Those three answers come from scripts, not from a report line.

faqs.question: When should we stop AI HL tutoring?
faqs.answer: When the pattern note shows the original loss has stopped recurring across three or four successive dated scripts and no new pattern has replaced it. That is a real outcome and we will say so at the six-week review rather than let a weekly slot continue by default. Some families then keep a reduced arrangement for mock windows only, which is sensible. What we try to avoid is the arrangement that runs for two years because nobody ever scheduled the conversation about ending it.

faqs.question: Does the tutor talk to my child's AI HL teacher in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Only if you arrange it and the school agrees; the relationship is between you and the school, and we do not approach a teacher independently. What works better in practice is that you pass on the school's published mock dates, internal exploration deadlines and any written feedback, and we plan against those. Most of the useful information flows that way anyway. Where a school runs its own support clinic, we will say plainly when that free session covers what we would otherwise charge for.

faqs.question: How is my child's AI HL data stored and how do we delete it?
faqs.answer: We hold the enquiry details, the session notes and the marked work, under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. We do not collect photographs, a full school timetable or medical information, because teaching mathematics does not require them. Ask for deletion and the file is removed and you are told when; we offer to send you copies of the marked scripts first, because a family that paid for a term of marking should keep the output. The work is the student's, not ours.

faqs.question: What evidence should we ask for before paying for a second term of AI HL?
faqs.answer: Four things. The dated scripts from the first term in one place. A count of mark types lost, first month against last. One full-length timed Paper 3 attempt, marked with the propagation traced. And a written statement of what the next term targets, naming a component rather than the subject. If a provider cannot assemble that in an afternoon, the first term has not produced evidence, and a second term is unlikely to produce any either.

faqs.question: Is six weeks long enough to see AI HL progress before the May session?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is long enough to see whether a method has changed, which is a different question from whether a grade has. Expect three or four dated scripts, a visible shift in the mark types being lost, and a clear answer on whether Paper 3 is attemptable in full. If the aim is one narrow repair, a rounding habit or one statistical model, six weeks is often sufficient. If several components are weak at once, six weeks will tell you which to prioritise rather than fix them all.

faqs.question: Do you keep the marked AI HL papers, or do we?
faqs.answer: Both, by design. The marked file is sent to you and a copy stays with the tutor so the next session starts from the last one rather than from memory. If you change tutor inside the network, the folder moves with the student, which is one practical advantage of work that exists as files rather than in an exercise book. If you leave entirely, ask and we send everything and then delete our copy. Nothing about the arrangement depends on us holding your child's work.

intro.heading: The costly decisions in Applications and Interpretation HL are not hourly
paragraphs: Families comparing tutors for Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level usually start by collecting hourly rates. It is the wrong first move, because in this particular course three other decisions each carry a larger price tag than the difference between a good rate and an excellent one. Whether the student is in the right maths course at all. How many hours the Higher Level investigation paper absorbs before anyone budgets for it. And whether the person being paid can actually teach the statistics content, which is the half of this syllabus that general maths tutors handle worst.

Delivery, first. IB Gram provides tuition in Dubai as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. On a cost page this is a line item rather than a disclaimer. Published rate data in this market puts in-home visiting work above the equivalent online rate, and the gap is travel. In Dubai an approach drive across the city at six in the evening is not short, and somebody pays for it whether the invoice itemises it or not.

The second structural point about this course is supply. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is sat by fewer students than Analysis and Approaches, and the subset of tutors who are genuinely comfortable with hypothesis testing, regression analysis, graph theory and matrices is smaller still. That pushes the band upward for reasons of scarcity rather than difficulty, which matters because scarcity pricing responds to flexibility. A family able to use a weekend morning gets a better match at the same number than a family insisting on the busiest weekday hour in term time.

Third, and most expensive of all, is the route question. A meaningful number of Dubai students choose Applications because it is described to them as the lighter option, discover that the Higher Level version is not light, and then face a decision with a deadline attached. Moving course mid-programme costs catch-up hours, and staying in the wrong one costs two years of inefficient support. Either way the cost of the decision dwarfs the cost of the hour, and it is settled by evidence rather than by preference.

So this page prices by component rather than by week. What Paper 1 and Paper 2 technique absorb. What the Higher Level investigation paper absorbs, which is more than families expect. What the exploration absorbs when the data is real rather than textbook. What a route change absorbs. And what each of those is worth buying at the top of the market rather than the middle.

All dirham figures here are published market anchors with the publisher named. Nothing on this page is an IB Gram price list, because the honest number depends on the components involved and the weeks remaining, and it is given after a free trial session rather than before one.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Three maths routes and one preceding programme sit around an Applications and Interpretation HL candidate in Dubai, and the price of support differs sharply between them. Most of the money families waste is spent in the wrong one of these four boxes.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
programmes.description: Three written papers, with technology permitted throughout, plus the mathematical exploration. The Higher Level content reaches into graph theory, matrices, complex numbers in applied contexts, hypothesis testing, regression and numerical methods, and the third paper sets extended investigations rather than short questions.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this course is often chosen by students heading for business, economics, data or design pathways. The pricing consequence is that specialist availability is thinner than for Analysis and Approaches, so the rate band reflects supply, and timing flexibility is worth more here than negotiation.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
programmes.description: Two papers rather than three, with the same applied flavour and a lower content ceiling. Relevant on a cost page because the single biggest saving available to some families is recognising that the Standard Level version was always the right course, which removes the third paper from the budget entirely.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai school's internal deadline for a level change is usually earlier than families expect, and it is set by the coordinator rather than the board. Two dated marked scripts on comparable question types are the evidence that conversation needs.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
programmes.description: The pure and theoretical route, with a calculator-free paper and an emphasis on proof and formal technique. Included because switching between the two Higher Level courses is one of the most expensive moves a Diploma student can make, and because some destinations expect this route specifically.
programmes.countryNote: University prerequisite expectations differ by destination and by course, and they change. Any claim about which UAE or overseas institution requires which maths route should be verified on that institution's own admissions page before it influences a decision, because an out-of-date requirement is an expensive thing to inherit.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D on an eight-point scale. Students arriving into Applications HL from MYP 5 often have strong applied and investigative habits and limited experience of timed papers, which affects which components need funding first and therefore the shape of the budget.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the full continuum, so a student may reach Higher Level maths having never sat an externally marked timed paper. The cheapest early spend in that case is on examination behaviour rather than on content.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Applications and Interpretation HL is best costed strand by strand, because the hours each one absorbs vary by a factor of several and so does the kind of tutor who can teach it. Below, each strand is described by where the hours actually go.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: The largest cost centre in the course. Hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, distributions and the interpretation of all of it. Hours here are expensive because the pool of maths tutors genuinely comfortable with inference is small, and because interpretation marks need writing practice as well as calculation.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Including logarithmic and exponential scales, approximation and error, and complex numbers in applied form. Cheap to support in isolation and frequently the first thing a generalist reaches for, which is why it is also the most commonly over-funded strand on this syllabus.

subjects.name: Functions and modelling
subjects.description: Fitting models to data, piecewise and composite models, and judging which model suits which situation. The marks lost are usually judgement marks rather than algebra marks, so sessions that only drill manipulation buy very little here.

subjects.name: Geometry, graph theory and matrices
subjects.description: Voronoi diagrams, adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees, transformations with matrices. Unfamiliar to most tutors trained on a traditional syllabus, which makes it the strand where a specialist most clearly outperforms a generalist and where the rate premium is justified.

subjects.name: Calculus and numerical methods
subjects.description: Including differential equations, slope fields and numerical approaches. Hours absorbed here depend heavily on how well the student handles technology, because the marks reward using the right tool and recording enough reasoning on paper to earn credit anyway.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique
subjects.description: Short-response work across the syllabus with technology permitted. The recurring loss is a correct screen result with no stated reasoning, which scores a fraction of the same answer supported by working. A cheap and fast fix, and a good first purchase.

subjects.name: Paper 2 technique
subjects.description: Extended-response work where context and interpretation carry marks alongside the calculation. Students who answer numerically and stop lose marks they had already earned, which is a writing habit rather than a mathematical gap.

subjects.name: Paper 3 investigations
subjects.description: Higher Level only: extended investigative problems that build across parts, where an early error propagates. The most hours-hungry component in the course and the one most budgets omit, because it does not map onto any chapter of the textbook.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Coursework assessed against lettered criteria. For Applications candidates it usually involves real data, which adds sourcing, cleaning and justification work before any mathematics happens. Priced as a scoped block against the school's submission date rather than as weekly hours.

subjects.name: Economics, Business Management and Computer Science
subjects.description: Listed because the applied mathematics in these subjects overlaps with Applications HL, and a student struggling with regression in one is usually struggling with it in both. Supporting the shared skill once is cheaper than funding two subjects separately.

sections.heading: What drives the Applications HL number in Dubai
paragraphs: Take the published anchors first so there is something concrete to reason from. At the low end of this market, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is university-student territory. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tuition at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 with home tutors reaching AED 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are the market's own numbers, attributed to whoever published them.

Within that range, five things move an Applications HL quote, and they are not equally negotiable. Format is the largest and the most controllable: a visiting hour carries a Dubai approach drive inside it, and choosing live video removes the component rather than discounting it. Component is second: Paper 3 work and exploration supervision sit above general content teaching everywhere in this market, and reasonably so.

Third is supply, which is the Applications-specific factor. Fewer students sit this course than Analysis and Approaches, and the proportion of maths tutors who are fluent in hypothesis testing, regression, graph theory and matrices is smaller again. Scarcity pricing does not respond to haggling; it responds to flexibility, which is why the same specialist is easier to secure at 20:00 or on a weekend morning than at the busiest hour of a term-time weekday.

Fourth is session length. Ninety minutes costs more per sitting than sixty and usually costs less per unit of ground covered in this course, because an investigative question cannot be set, attempted and reviewed inside an hour with anything useful left over. Fifth is timing in the year: availability thins as a session approaches, so arranging a mock-period block early is cheaper than arranging it late, even when the sessions themselves start later.

sections.heading: Cost by component, not by week
paragraphs: A weekly commitment is the wrong unit for this course, because the components absorb very different amounts of time and only some of them reward a specialist rate. Pricing by component also makes a budget finite, which a weekly arrangement never is.

Paper 1 technique is the cheapest and fastest purchase on the list. The characteristic Applications loss is a correct answer from the calculator with nothing written down, and teaching a student to record the stated reasoning alongside the result recovers marks on questions they were already getting right. A short block, mid-market rate, visible on the next script.

Paper 2 is a writing problem more than a maths problem. Interpretation and context carry marks, and students who produce a number and stop lose credit already earned. Again a short block rather than a term, and again not a job that needs the top of the market.

Paper 3 is the expensive one and the one most budgets omit entirely. Higher Level investigations build across parts, so an early error propagates and a student who has never practised the format loses marks structurally rather than mathematically. This is where a specialist earns the premium, because recognising how these questions are constructed is a specific skill. The exploration is the other place a premium is justified, and for Applications candidates it carries hidden hours: finding a defensible dataset, cleaning it, and justifying its use before any analysis begins.

The strands differ too. Statistics and the graph theory and matrices material are where a generalist most often improvises, and improvisation is the most expensive teaching there is because it has to be repeated. Number and algebra is where generalists are comfortable, which is why it tends to be over-funded relative to what it costs the grade.

sections.heading: The price of the route decision
paragraphs: This is the most expensive thing on the page and the one families least often price. Applications and Interpretation is sometimes described to Dubai students as the lighter maths option, and at Higher Level that description is misleading. A student who chose it on that basis can end up in the most demanding version of the course they were trying to avoid.

Three scenarios recur. First, a student in Applications HL who should be in Applications SL: the content ceiling and the third paper are the problem rather than the subject, and moving removes an entire component from the budget. Second, a student in Analysis HL who would be better served by Applications HL, usually someone strong with data and context and weak at formal proof. Third, a student in Applications HL who needs Analysis for a destination course, which is the only one of the three where delay is genuinely costly.

Each move has a deadline set by the school rather than the board, and in most Dubai schools it is earlier than families assume. That turns the decision into a cost question with a clock on it. Catch-up hours after a switch are real: moving between the two Higher Level courses means covering content the new course assumes and unlearning habits the old one rewarded, and it is the largest block of hours in any of these scenarios.

The evidence a coordinator will take seriously is two dated marked scripts on comparable question types, with the losses categorised. Not a parent's impression and not a tutor's opinion. That evidence costs a trial session and one marked paper to produce, which makes it the cheapest piece of decision-making available in the whole programme.

One caution on destinations. University prerequisite expectations vary by institution and by course and they change between admissions cycles. Any statement about which route a particular UAE or overseas university expects should be read on that institution's own admissions page before money or a decision rests on it, and no page should be trusted to have kept up, including this one.

sections.heading: The statistics half, and why a generalist costs more
paragraphs: If one paragraph on this page saves a Dubai family money it should be this one. The statistics and inference content in Applications HL is the part of the syllabus where general maths tutors are weakest, and paying somebody to learn it alongside your child is the most expensive form of tutoring available.

The content itself is specific: hypothesis testing with its stated conditions and conclusions, regression and correlation with the interpretation marks that go with them, distributions, and the judgement about which test or model suits which situation. It is not hard content for somebody who has worked with it. It is unfamiliar content for a tutor whose own training was in pure mathematics, and unfamiliarity shows up as hours.

The symptom is recognisable. Sessions on statistics that stay at the level of pressing the right calculator buttons, with the conditions unstated and the conclusion left as a number. A student taught that way produces correct figures and loses the interpretation marks, which are a substantial share of what these questions carry. Then the same ground is covered again later, at the same rate, because nothing durable was installed the first time.

The test is cheap to run. Ask a prospective tutor what conditions a hypothesis test requires before it can be applied, and what a stated conclusion has to include to earn full credit. Somebody who works with this content answers immediately and in specifics. Somebody who does not will answer about procedures. That question costs nothing and routinely saves a term of inefficient hours.

The same logic applies to graph theory and matrices, which appear on this syllabus and on very few traditional ones. A tutor who has never taught a minimum spanning tree or an adjacency matrix in an examination context will be reading ahead, and you will be paying for the reading.

sections.heading: What an Applications HL quote should itemise
paragraphs: A quote in this market is usually a single number per hour, which hides the things that actually determine what you pay across a term. Four questions turn that number into something comparable.

First, what the hour includes. Is marking inside the paid time or outside it. If a ninety-minute session contains thirty minutes of the tutor marking in silence, the real teaching rate is higher than quoted. Second, what happens to a session cancelled because a Dubai school moved a mock week or an exam-leave date, which happens every year and is a reasonable thing to have an answer for.

Third, whether materials are charged. Published syllabus documents, past papers, markschemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, should be referenced and linked from the official sources rather than redistributed, and should certainly not appear as a line item on an invoice. A provider charging for board material is charging for something they should not be supplying.

Fourth, the tax and invoicing position. This page does not state the UAE treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that would require a citation from the tax authority. What a family should do is ask two direct questions: is the quoted figure inclusive of VAT, and do you hold a tax registration number. A provider who answers both plainly has told you something useful about the operation, and one who cannot has told you more.

On free trials, the only honest version states the conditions next to the word: the length, who is eligible, and whether card details are needed to book. A trial that produces a marked piece of work and a scoped plan is worth taking. A trial that is a sales call with a maths flavour is not, and the difference is visible from what you are holding afterwards.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the Dubai context
paragraphs: A rate in isolation feels large. Set against the rest of a Dubai education budget it is usually a small line, and families make better decisions with the scale in front of them.

The anchor is fees, and they have been held. The regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. The sector itself is large and growing: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, seventeen different curricula, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. Enrolment rose 6 per cent during 2025-26, six new schools opened that year, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven more, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

Against an annual international school fee, a scoped Paper 3 block or an exploration block is a modest fraction, and each attaches to a specific component of the grade. Where the arithmetic turns bad is an open weekly commitment across two years on a course the student should have left, which is why the route section sits above this one.

There is also a set of costs outside tutoring that belong in the same spreadsheet. Enquiries upon results, remarks and retake entries carry board fees. A retake means a second preparation period as well as a second entry. The correct calculator model, replaced if a school changes its requirement. University admissions tests and application fees, which land in the same months as the heaviest tutoring spend. And Ministry equivalency, which is a Ministry process rather than something a tutoring service performs, arranges or guarantees, and which should be confirmed through the official channel.

One honest note on what this page will not do. It will not state an IB examination or results date, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no session date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Dubai schools sit the May session, and the dates that bind your child are the coordinator's internal deadlines.

sections.heading: What to do before paying anybody
paragraphs: Three things cost nothing, take an evening, and change what you end up buying. Families who do them spend less and spend it better.

First, get the component picture from the school. Ask the maths department which components the current grade was built from and which was weakest. A department will answer that readily. It converts a grade of 4 into something actionable, and it often reveals that the problem is the investigation paper rather than the content, which changes the whole plan.

Second, read one marked script with a pen. Label every lost mark as method, knowledge, instruction or accuracy. A script dominated by method and instruction losses is a cheap, fast fix and does not need the top of the market. A script dominated by knowledge losses in the statistics strand needs a specialist and a longer block. Those are two completely different budgets, and the script tells you which you are in.

Third, settle the route question with evidence rather than feeling. If there is any doubt about whether Higher Level Applications is the right course, produce two dated marked scripts and take them to the coordinator before the school's change window closes. The worst outcome in this course is two years of competent support propping up the wrong choice, and that outcome is entirely avoidable in the autumn.

Then, when you do buy, buy a component with a finish line. A Paper 3 block before mocks. An exploration block against the submission date. A short Paper 1 and Paper 2 technique block. Each of those ends, which is what keeps a budget finite and what lets you judge whether the money worked.

On availability, the honest position for this course: Applications at Higher Level is thinner on specialists than Analysis, and the busiest term-time evening hour sometimes has nobody suitable free. What you will be offered then is a different time, an adjacent specialist who can begin now, or a date. Paying a specialist rate for a generalist who is reading ahead is the single most expensive mistake available here, and it is the one this page is written to prevent.

faqs.question: What should we budget for AI HL across the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Budget by component rather than by month. A short technique block for Papers 1 and 2, a substantial Paper 3 block in the run-up to mocks, an exploration block scoped to the school's submission date, and a statistics block if the marked scripts point there. Published anchors give the scale: Unitors advertises IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate puts specialist work at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those blocks together are a smaller total than an open weekly commitment across twenty-four months, and unlike it they end.

faqs.question: Why do AI HL rates sit above AA SL rates in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Mostly supply, not difficulty. Fewer students sit Applications at Higher Level than Analysis at Standard Level, and the proportion of maths tutors genuinely fluent in hypothesis testing, regression, graph theory and matrices is smaller still. Thin supply lifts the band. The useful consequence is that scarcity pricing responds to flexibility rather than negotiation: the same specialist is far easier to secure for a weekend morning or a 20:00 start than for the busiest ninety minutes of a term-time weekday, at the same quoted rate.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 support charged separately, and should it be?
faqs.answer: It should be scoped separately, which usually means a block rather than a different rate. The Higher Level investigation paper is the component most budgets omit, because it does not correspond to a textbook chapter and nothing in the school's scheme of work announces it. Investigations build across parts, so an early error propagates and a student who has never practised the format loses marks structurally. Buying it as a defined block before mocks is both cheaper and more effective than discovering the gap in the mock results and buying panic hours in the spring.

faqs.question: What does it cost to switch into AI HL in the middle of DP1?
faqs.answer: In hours, a lot: the applied strands that Analysis does not cover, plus unlearning habits the previous course rewarded. In money, it is the largest single block most families in this situation buy. The deciding factor is usually not cost but the deadline, because the change window is set by the school's coordinator and is often earlier than parents expect. Produce two dated marked scripts with the losses categorised and take them to the coordinator early. A switch decided in the autumn costs a fraction of one decided in the spring.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to stay in AA HL and get help, or move to AI HL?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the marked scripts show, and the question should not be answered on feel. If losses are concentrated in formal proof and calculator-free technique while the student handles data and context well, moving may remove the problem rather than treating it. If losses are spread across all topics, the course is not the issue and a switch buys new content to learn as well as the old gap. The cheap move is to produce the evidence first, because it costs a trial session and settles a decision worth a year of support.

faqs.question: How many hours does the AI HL exploration absorb when the data is real?
faqs.answer: More than families budget, because the mathematics is only the second half. An Applications exploration usually involves a real dataset, and finding one that is defensible, cleaning it, and justifying its use takes sessions before any analysis happens. Scope the block to the coordinator's submission date rather than buying weekly hours, since an unscoped arrangement expands to fill the time available. The hours are worth buying at specialist level because the criteria are where marks are won, and a supervisor who knows them saves several drafts of drift.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy software or data for an Applications exploration?
faqs.answer: Generally no. Publicly available datasets and a spreadsheet handle the overwhelming majority of Applications explorations, and the student's own graphical calculator covers the rest. Be sceptical of any requirement that converts into a purchase, and be more sceptical of an offer to supply a dataset and an analysis together, which starts to look like supplying the work. What a supervisor can legitimately do is question whether a dataset is defensible and whether its limitations have been acknowledged, both of which carry marks.

faqs.question: Which AI HL topics are the most expensive to fix late?
faqs.answer: The statistics and inference strand, and graph theory and matrices. Both for the same reason: they are unfamiliar to many tutors trained on a traditional syllabus, so a late start means paying somebody to get fluent while your child waits. Statistics is also interpretation-heavy, and interpretation is a writing habit that needs weeks rather than a session. Number and algebra is the opposite case, cheap and fast, which is why it tends to be over-funded. The marked script tells you which category you are actually in.

faqs.question: Does a statistics specialist cost more than a general maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Often slightly, and in this course it is usually the cheaper option in total. A generalist working through hypothesis testing for the first time teaches calculator procedure, leaves the conditions unstated and the conclusion as a number, and the same ground gets covered again later at the same rate. Content paid for twice is the most expensive outcome available. Test it with one question before hiring: what conditions does a hypothesis test require, and what must a conclusion state to earn full credit. The answer separates fluency from familiarity immediately.

faqs.question: What should an AI HL quote itemise before we pay it?
faqs.answer: Four things. Whether marking happens inside or outside the paid session, because marking inside can consume a third of the teaching you bought. What happens to sessions when a Dubai school moves a mock week, which happens every year. Whether any materials are charged, noting that board documents should be referenced and linked rather than redistributed or invoiced. And the tax position: ask directly whether the figure includes VAT and whether a tax registration number is held. Plain answers to all four make two quotes comparable for the first time.

faqs.question: Is a group AI HL class cheaper, and does it work for Paper 3?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student, and a reasonable format for content delivery when everyone in the group is at a similar point in the same strand. It works poorly for the investigation paper, because the skill there is an individual's own approach to an unfamiliar multi-part problem and the useful feedback is on that individual's choices. A workable compromise is a shared session on the statistics content plus a short individual block on Paper 3 technique, which keeps the per-student cost down without blunting the part that needs one-to-one attention.

faqs.question: What does an in-home AI HL visit in Dubai add to the price?
faqs.answer: Published data puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 with home tutors reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the gap is travel. In Dubai that is a slow evening crossing rather than a long distance, but the effect on the hour is identical. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; tuition here is one-to-one over live video, and home tutoring is an India-only service. For a thin-supply course the format also widens the pool, which matters more than the saving.

faqs.question: What tax and invoicing questions should we ask before paying?
faqs.answer: Two, and ask them of every provider you compare. Is the quoted figure inclusive of VAT, and do you hold a tax registration number. This page does not state the UAE treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that would require a citation from the tax authority, and nor should any other page. What a family is entitled to is clarity about the number they are being asked to pay. A provider who answers both plainly has told you something about their operation, and one who deflects has told you more.

faqs.question: Does the calculator model change what we spend?
faqs.answer: It can, in two ways. Technology is permitted throughout this course, so fluency on the specific model the school requires is part of the subject rather than an extra, and practising on a different model builds reflexes the examination will punish. If a school changes its required model mid-course, that is a real cost. The other way is less legitimate: be wary of any tutoring arrangement that requires a hardware purchase. A device with a camera, paper, a pen and the student's own calculator covers everything needed for live-video sessions.

faqs.question: What can we do for nothing before paying for AI HL support?
faqs.answer: Three things, in one evening. Ask the maths department which components the current grade was built from and which was weakest, which converts a grade into something actionable. Read one marked script with a pen, labelling every loss as method, knowledge, instruction or accuracy. And if there is any doubt about the route, produce two dated marked scripts and take them to the coordinator before the change window closes. Those three steps routinely change what a family ends up buying, and they cost attention rather than money.

faqs.question: When does the next AI HL dirham stop buying anything?
faqs.answer: At three recognisable points. When a scoped block has shown up on the next marked script, because the skill now belongs to the student and renewing buys nothing. When nothing is produced between sessions, because the constraint is the student's week rather than teaching and no rate solves that. And when the student can mark their own work against a published markscheme, finish each paper in time and name their weak question types, at which point a session a fortnight through the final term and then nothing is the correct shape.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Price the decisions, then the hours
dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.closingBody: The families who spend least on Applications and Interpretation HL in Dubai are not the ones who found the lowest rate. They are the ones who settled the route question in the autumn with two marked scripts, scoped a Paper 3 block before mocks, booked the exploration block against the school's own submission date, and asked one hypothesis-testing question before hiring anyone for the statistics strand. Send a marked script and the coordinator's deadline sheet, take a free trial session over live video, and the plan that comes back will name components and session counts rather than a monthly figure.

intro.heading: The course that looks like the safe choice and then asks for something different
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is the most chosen mathematics course in many Dubai Diploma cohorts, and it is chosen for the wrong reason more often than any other. Students take it because it has a reputation for being the gentlest of the four. What they find is a course where a graphic display calculator is assumed in both papers, where roughly a third of the teaching hours sit in statistics and probability, and where a large share of the marks depend on explaining what a number means rather than on producing it.

The structure is straightforward and worth stating plainly, because many families have never seen it written down. There are two written papers, each 80 marks over ninety minutes, each carrying 40 per cent of the final grade. The exploration is marked out of twenty and carries the remaining 20 per cent. There is no Paper 3 at Standard Level. The guide recommends 150 teaching hours, of which about 120 cover examined content: around 36 in statistics and probability, 31 in functions, 19 in calculus, 18 in geometry and trigonometry and 16 in number and algebra.

That distribution is the key to how the course behaves. A student weak in statistics is weak in the largest part of the examination, and statistics is also the most quickly recoverable content in the Diploma, because much of it is procedural once the right calculator routine and the right written template are known. A student weak in functions and modelling has a slower problem, because interpreting and justifying a model is a judgement skill that develops over months rather than weeks. Those two profiles need completely different tutoring plans, and a single mock percentage cannot tell them apart.

Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubai address, and in-home tuition is something we run only in India. For this course the honest argument is availability rather than scarcity: AI SL candidates outnumber every other Diploma maths group in most Dubai schools, which means demand is concentrated in the same two early-evening hours across the whole city. Removing travel from the arrangement is what makes a 16:30 or a 20:00 session possible at all.

Dubai's market context matters for a different reason here. KHDA counted 387,441 pupils in 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the IB at 7 per cent of enrolment, and confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Against a school fee that is holding flat, a tutoring decision is easier to size honestly, and the right question becomes how few hours will fix the specific problem rather than how many hours a family can absorb.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Applications and Interpretation rewards interpretation and justification, and those skills are visible years before a student reaches Standard Level maths. Here is what each programme contributes and what to watch for in Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: AI SL satisfies the Diploma's mathematics requirement and is frequently taken at Standard Level alongside two or three Higher Level subjects elsewhere. The 150 recommended hours include around thirty notionally reserved for the exploration, leaving roughly 120 for examined content across the five topics.
programmes.countryNote: Almost all Dubai candidates sit the May session. Session windows, upload deadlines and results dates are set and revised by the IB, so take them from your school's Diploma coordinator rather than from any tutoring site. In practice the dates that govern a tutoring plan are the school's own internal exploration deadlines, which usually sit a full term earlier.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics assesses four criteria, and criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is the direct forerunner of this course. A student who writes confidently about what a result means, even when the arithmetic is shaky, is well suited to Applications and should be told so rather than steered towards Analysis by default.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai's continuum schools the choice between the two mathematics routes is often made on teacher recommendation with no external examination evidence on either side. Asking the school for the criterion-level MYP breakdown rather than the overall grade is the single most useful question available to a parent in Year 11.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Data handling, measurement and pattern appear early in the PYP and are the strands that matter most for a future Applications student. The course at the far end of the route is largely about reading data and justifying a conclusion from it, which begins as a primary-school habit rather than a secondary-school technique.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA inspects Dubai schools annually and reports attainment and progress separately by subject. A primary report showing good attainment but only acceptable progress in mathematics is the earliest reliable signal a parent receives, and it describes the teaching group the child is actually in rather than the school's headline band.

dubai/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: AI SL rarely arrives alone in an enquiry. These are the subjects Dubai families most often book alongside it, with the component that tends to decide each grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Two 80-mark papers plus the exploration, calculator assumed throughout. Financial mathematics, Voronoi diagrams, correlation and regression, the chi-squared test and the trapezoidal rule are the strands where marks are won and lost at this level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Adds a one-hour Paper 3 of 55 marks, plus matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, coupled differential equations and Euler's method. A student considering the move up should understand that Paper 3 is a trained skill rather than extra content, and takes time to build.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route at Standard Level, with a non-calculator Paper 1. Students who find Applications statistics tedious but enjoy algebraic manipulation are sometimes in the wrong course, and a marked paper from each is the cheapest way to settle the question.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Break-even analysis, investment appraisal and ratio interpretation sit close to the financial mathematics in AI SL. The marks usually lost are in strategic evaluation against a named business context rather than in any calculation, which is a writing problem rather than a numeracy one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internally assessed commentaries on published articles, plus written papers with diagram work. AI SL students handle the quantitative questions comfortably and lose marks on precise definitions and on correctly labelled diagrams, which reward drill rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Fieldwork data in the internal assessment needs statistical treatment, and AI SL students have the tools to do it properly. Written papers reward specific case-study detail and command-term discipline, so the maths advantage does not carry across to the examination papers.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A transdisciplinary course with substantial data interpretation, which suits this profile well. The internal investigation is where AI SL students can distinguish themselves, provided the statistical treatment matches the data rather than being added for show.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Higher Level psychology includes research methodology and inferential statistics, which overlap directly with the AI SL statistics strand. Students who do not connect the two tend to lose marks on study evaluation, where the statistical weakness of a named study is the point being tested.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Listening, reading, writing and speaking components with a productive-skills emphasis. Listed here because Dubai families frequently pair a maths booking with a language one, and because the individual oral is the component most commonly left too late to rehearse properly.

paragraphs: Qualified online subject tutors in Dubai publish rates from roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and IB specialists from about AED 200 to AED 450.
