We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; in-home work is a service we run only in India. That is said before money is discussed, because two providers in this market route Emirates enquiries overseas without saying so.

The in-home question is a fair one and this page answers it rather than deflecting. A tutor physically present removes the option of a quiet refusal to work, supplies social pressure that some teenagers genuinely respond to, and makes a lesson visible to a parent in the next room. Those are real benefits. Market rates for in-home one-to-one in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel embedded, and monthly packages of about AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits are commonly advertised.

What the premium does not buy is subject match. On this course the three things that most often need fixing are a written template for statistical tests, fluency with the financial mathematics routines, and the habit of explaining what a model means in one sentence. Each of those is specific, each is teachable in a handful of sessions, and none of them depends on the tutor being in the room. A generalist who travels well can still be the wrong person for a chi-squared question.

The scheduling effect is what families comment on by week four. A tutor who does not drive can hold 16:30 on a Monday and 20:00 on a Wednesday without renegotiating, can shift to post-Iftar slots for Ramadan and then shift back, and does not lose the marking hour to traffic. For a Diploma student already carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the mandatory UAE subjects, a session that can move is a session that survives.

sections.heading: Where the AI SL hours actually sit, and what that means for a plan
paragraphs: The Applications and Interpretation guide distributes its Standard Level hours unevenly, and reading that distribution is how a tutoring plan gets built in the right order. Statistics and probability takes the largest share at around 36 hours. Functions follows at around 31. Calculus has roughly 19, geometry and trigonometry roughly 18, and number and algebra roughly 16, with a further thirty notionally reserved for the exploration.

Number and algebra carries the fewest hours and includes the strand students most often arrive unable to do: financial mathematics. Compound interest with varying compounding periods, annuities, amortisation and loan repayment schedules are examined content, they appear in both papers, and they are almost entirely procedural. A student who cannot do them is losing marks that could be recovered inside three sessions, which makes this the highest-yield place to start for most new enquiries on this course.

Functions is the strand that behaves least like the others. Modelling with an appropriate function family, transformations, and the written justification of a model choice are judgement skills. They improve slowly and they cannot be drilled in a fortnight, which is why a student whose weakness is here needs a longer block and an earlier start. Telling the difference between a functions problem and a statistics problem is most of what the first two weeks of diagnosis is for.

Calculus at this level is narrower than many parents expect: introductory differentiation, tangents and normals, increasing and decreasing behaviour, optimisation, and the trapezoidal rule for area. There is no integration by substitution and no implicit differentiation. The marks lost here are usually about reading which quantity a question wants rather than about technique, and that is a comprehension drill rather than a mathematics one.

sections.heading: Financial mathematics: the strand nobody revises until it is too late
paragraphs: Compound interest, annuities and amortisation sit inside AI SL's number and algebra topic, and they are the clearest example of examined content that students ignore because it does not feel like mathematics. The questions are not conceptually hard. They require knowing which calculator application handles a loan repayment, which sign convention the device expects for payments and balances, and how to read the output back into the units the question asked for.

The marks are won and lost in small, specific places. Interest compounded quarterly when the rate is quoted annually. A payment entered as positive when the device expects it negative, producing a plausible answer with the wrong sign. An amortisation question asking for the outstanding balance after a stated number of years rather than the total paid. Each of these is a one-line error that costs two or three marks, and each is eliminated by practice on the student's own calculator rather than by explanation.

This strand is also where the course earns its name. A question asking whether a particular loan arrangement is better value than another is asking for a comparison and a justification, not just two numbers. Mark schemes award for the conclusion stated in context, and students who produce both figures and then stop lose the final mark on a question they had effectively completed. A written template handles this, and it is three lines long.

The practical reason we start here with many new students is that the return on time is high and visible. A student who could not do amortisation in week one and can do it reliably by week three has moved a measurable number of marks, which changes the atmosphere around a tutoring arrangement that was begun reluctantly. Starting with the slowest strand in a course is defensible pedagogically and often fatal to a teenager's willingness to continue.

sections.heading: A third of the course is statistics, and most of its marks are in the writing
paragraphs: Statistics and probability is the largest strand in AI SL at roughly 36 guide hours, and it is the part of the course where students most reliably underperform relative to their understanding. The reason is consistent: they treat the statistical result as the answer. Mark schemes do not. A chi-squared test for independence is marked for the hypotheses, the test named, the degrees of freedom or the p-value, the comparison against the significance level, and a conclusion expressed in the context of the original question.

A student who writes a p-value and "so they are independent" typically collects fewer than half the available marks with every number correct. The correction is a template per test type, learned to the point of automation: what to state before the calculator, what to record from it, and what sentence to write after. We drill three templates at this level, for the chi-squared test for independence, the chi-squared goodness-of-fit test and the t-test, and they transfer directly into the exploration.

Regression and correlation behave the same way. Pearson's correlation coefficient quoted without comment on strength and direction, a regression line used to predict far outside the data range without noting that extrapolation is unreliable, a coefficient of determination reported and not interpreted: all of these are available marks left on the table. These are not difficult points. They are habits, and habits respond to repetition rather than to a better explanation.

Sampling and data presentation round out the strand and are examined more carefully than students expect. Knowing why a convenience sample limits a conclusion, identifying an outlier by the stated rule rather than by eye, and choosing a presentation that suits the data type are all mark-bearing. They also matter in the exploration, which is one reason why a block of work on statistics pays twice in this course.

sections.heading: Was Applications and Interpretation the right choice? An honest decision table
paragraphs: A substantial minority of the AI SL enquiries we take are really route questions in disguise. The student is coping, the grade is a 4 or a 5, and the parent wants to know whether the problem is the course rather than the effort. That is a legitimate question and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales response, because the honest answer is sometimes that no tutor is needed, and sometimes that a different course would have suited better but switching now would cost more than it gains.

The signals are reasonably reliable. A student who enjoys the statistics and the financial questions and stalls at modelling and justification is in the right course and needs writing work rather than mathematics. A student who finds the statistics tedious, prefers algebraic manipulation and resents being asked to interpret is often better suited to Analysis and Approaches, though by DP2 that observation is usually academic. A student who is coping with everything and scoring a 5 because of pacing and presentation needs four sessions, not a year.

Switching is governed by the school and by IB registration, never by a tutor, and a family considering it should raise it with the Diploma coordinator immediately rather than after a term of deliberation. What we can do is scope it: moving from AI SL to AA SL means acquiring a non-calculator paper that has never been sat, which is usually the real obstacle rather than the new content. Moving from AI SL up to AI HL means the HL-only strands plus Paper 3 technique, which is a substantial piece of work.

The table below is the version of this conversation we have most often. It is a planning aid rather than a diagnosis, and the marked evidence from a first block will always tell you more than any table can. What it is useful for is deciding which question to ask the school, which is frequently the step families skip.

sections.heading: The exploration at AI SL: twenty marks from a question you can answer
paragraphs: The exploration is worth twenty per cent of the final grade, is marked out of twenty against five criteria, and runs to a recommended twelve to twenty pages. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks and asks for mathematics commensurate with the level studied, which for a Standard Level Applications candidate means a statistical test chosen properly and interpreted properly, or a model fitted and then criticised. It does not mean reaching for Higher Level techniques.

The characteristic failure on this course is data without a question. A student collects a large and genuinely interesting data set, then looks for mathematics to apply to it, and ends up with an exploration containing a great deal of work and very little personal engagement or reflection. The order that works is the reverse: a question narrow enough to answer, then the minimum data needed to answer it, then the test or model, then honest commentary on what the analysis could not show.

Criterion D, reflection, is worth three marks and is the cheapest available improvement in this course. Most drafts contain no reflection until a concluding paragraph. Examiners expect it throughout: what the result meant, what the sample could not support, what a different approach would have produced. Criterion C, personal engagement, also worth three, is far easier to earn with data the student gathered themselves than with a downloaded file, which is the single most practical piece of advice available at the planning stage.

The boundaries on tutor involvement are fixed and we put them in writing. The exploration must be entirely the student's own work. A tutor may interrogate a research question until it is answerable, read a submitted draft, comment against each criterion, note where a statistical test does not support the claim being made, and explain what each criterion rewards. A tutor may not supply sentences, rework paragraphs, choose the data or hand over analysis for insertion. Providers in this market sell completed coursework outright, and the malpractice consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: What AI SL tuition costs in Dubai, and what a travelling tutor adds
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars. The table below gives the AED position for Standard Level Applications tuition in Dubai, with the source of each band. These are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list. Our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson, and a quote afterwards reflects how many strands are in play and how many weeks remain before the session.

Standard Level prices below Higher Level in this market because the pool of capable tutors is larger, and on this course that is particularly true: a competent mathematics teacher can teach AI SL content, whereas AI HL requires graph theory, matrices and eigenvalues that many have never taught. A family being quoted a Higher Level rate for Standard Level work is entitled to ask what the premium buys, and to expect a specific answer.

A travelling tutor adds roughly AED 50 to AED 200 an hour over an equivalent online session here, and that addition is travel rather than quality. It is money well spent in particular circumstances: a younger student who will not work without supervision, a household where the only device is shared, a learner for whom a screen is a genuine barrier. For a sixteen-year-old who needs three sessions of amortisation drill on their own calculator, it is not.

On sizing the decision, Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run from roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for examination-year specialist support. Set against KHDA's confirmation on 22 May 2026 that Dubai school fees would not rise for 2026-27, a short, targeted block is usually a better use of a family's budget than an open-ended weekly commitment.

sections.heading: The fortnightly scorecard, and the limits of what any tutor can promise
paragraphs: Evidence on this course takes the form of a strand scorecard, because AI SL marks are lost in identifiable places. Five rows, one per topic, each with a date, a score out of a stated total, and a retest score when one exists. Alongside it: the marked work annotated in mark-scheme wording, and one line naming which paper is currently weaker and why. It fits on a screen and a parent who has never studied the course can read it.

What the scorecard deliberately excludes is encouragement. "Working well" and "improving steadily" cannot be checked a month later and are therefore worthless as management information. A row that reads "statistics, 9 March, 12 out of 25; retest 23 March, 19 out of 25" can be checked, and so can a row that has not moved in six weeks. The second kind of row is the useful one, because it prompts a change rather than a continuation.

The scorecard also records what was not attempted. Three missed question sets in a row is information about the timetable or the arrangement rather than about the student's character, and the right response is often to move the slot or shorten the sessions. February is the usual pressure point in Dubai, when internal assessment deadlines across several subjects land in the same fortnight and a maths question set is the first thing to be dropped.

No tutor can promise a grade, and anybody in this market who offers one should be treated with real scepticism. What can be promised is that the evidence is dated and in front of you, and that an arrangement which is not working becomes visible within six weeks rather than in August. At the end of a block the student sits a second full paper under the conditions of the first, and those two scripts side by side are the only honest measure available.

sections.heading: Equivalency, permits and the things a Dubai parent can verify directly
paragraphs: Two administrative questions come up on nearly every Standard Level maths enquiry, and both have published answers that no competitor page in our research covers. The first is Ministry of Education equivalency. For British-curriculum students the rule is specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test, and English proficiency is evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section.

For the IB there is no points threshold we are prepared to publish, because the source we read does not state one and we have not read a figure on the Ministry's own site. One ranking competitor already publishes a wrong IGCSE subject count, and inheriting an error of that kind across a set of pages would be worse than declining to answer. Check the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority. Equivalency is a Ministry process; no tutor performs it, guarantees it, or is required for it.

The second question is the permit. Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the ministry's app, website or e-services. Teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18 may apply, and anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

A parent can verify all of this directly, which is the point of setting it out. Ask any in-person tutor to show the permit. Read the regulator's own school listing rather than a provider's claim about a school. And treat any phrase that attaches a regulator's name to the word "approved" and then to a tutor as a prompt for harder questions: KHDA licenses schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, and IB Gram holds neither, nor any accreditation from ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board.

process.title: Send the course, the school and the last marked paper
process.description: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, the school, the year group, and the most recent marked work if any exists. A percentage on its own is hard to act on. A script with the lost marks visible tells a tutor in ten minutes what a conversation takes three sessions to uncover.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a named specialist
process.description: A working session rather than a presentation. The student attempts questions from a strand they dislike, and you see how a wrong answer is handled. This is also where the calculator model is checked, since the menu paths for a chi-squared test or an amortisation calculation differ between devices.

process.title: Score the five strands
process.description: Short timed tests across number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, in the first fortnight. Scores and dates go on the scorecard. This is what stops the common pattern in which a tutor teaches whatever last week's homework happened to contain.

process.title: Start with the fastest strand, not the weakest
process.description: On this course the financial mathematics and the statistical templates usually return marks fastest, and a visible gain in three weeks changes a reluctant student's attitude to the arrangement. The slower work on modelling and justification runs alongside, where it has the term it needs rather than a fortnight.

process.title: Retest, then review against the baseline
process.description: Each taught strand is retested with comparable questions, not the same ones. At the end of the block a second full paper is sat under the conditions of the first. If the marks moved, the next block builds on it; if they did not, we change the tutor, the format or the level and say which.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course, not to the subject
whyPoints.description: There are four Diploma mathematics courses and "IB maths tutor" usually means a tutor who has taught one of them. We match on Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level specifically, because the financial mathematics, the Voronoi work and the statistical testing are not content an Analysis tutor has necessarily ever taught.

whyPoints.title: Written templates for every statistical test
whyPoints.description: Most marks lost in this course's largest strand are lost in the writing, not the calculation. We drill a three-line template for each test type: what to state before touching the calculator, what to record from it, and what sentence follows. It transfers straight into the exploration, so the work pays twice.

whyPoints.title: The student's own calculator, every session
whyPoints.description: Both AI SL papers assume a graphic display calculator, and menu paths differ between models. Practising on a sibling's device or a classroom spare means losing marks to navigation under time pressure, which is indistinguishable in a results sheet from not knowing the mathematics. The model is checked in the trial lesson.

whyPoints.title: A scorecard a non-mathematician can audit
whyPoints.description: Five strands, dated scores, retests beside them. You do not need to follow the mathematics to see that a strand has not moved in six weeks, and that is exactly the question we want a parent to be able to ask. Encouragement is not management information and does not appear in the record.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when fewer hours are enough
whyPoints.description: A student scoring a 5 with no content gap usually needs four to six sessions on pacing and mark-scheme habits, not a year of weekly tuition. Saying so costs us revenue and is the reason the diagnosis comes before the quote rather than after it. The same applies when the honest answer is a route conversation with the school.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated before any payment
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram operates no home visits in the UAE and keeps no office in the Emirates. If the hour you want is unavailable, you are told with the alternatives named, rather than being matched with whoever happens to be free that evening.

faqs.question: Is AI SL the easiest of the four Diploma maths courses?
faqs.answer: It is the least algebraically demanding, which is not the same thing. Both papers assume a graphic display calculator, roughly a third of the guide's hours sit in statistics and probability, and a large share of the marks depend on explaining what a result means rather than on producing it. Students who chose it to avoid writing are often disappointed. The course suits a student who reads data confidently and can justify a conclusion in a sentence, and it frustrates one who wants mathematics to be only calculation.

faqs.question: Is there any non-calculator paper in Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: No. A graphic display calculator is assumed in both Standard Level papers, and in all three at Higher Level. That is the single biggest structural difference from Analysis and Approaches, where Paper 1 permits no calculator at all. The consequence is that the device becomes examinable equipment: knowing your own model's menu paths for a chi-squared test, a regression or an amortisation calculation is part of the preparation, and a student practising on a borrowed calculator will lose marks to navigation rather than to mathematics.

faqs.question: Does the tutor come to our villa in Dubai, or do lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: Online, over live video, one-to-one, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address, and in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. Families search for "home tutor" so the page uses the phrase, but the delivery model is stated before money is discussed. On this course the gain is mostly scheduling: AI SL is the largest maths group in most Dubai Diploma cohorts, demand crowds into the same two early-evening hours, and removing travel is what makes a 16:30 or a 20:00 slot possible.

faqs.question: My daughter cannot do the compound interest and loan questions at all. Is that fixable quickly?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the first thing we would work on. Financial mathematics in this course is procedural: compound interest with different compounding periods, annuities, amortisation and outstanding balances. The errors are specific and repeatable, such as a quarterly rate applied as an annual one, or a payment entered with the wrong sign so the output looks plausible and is not. Three sessions of drill on her own calculator, plus a three-line written template for the comparison questions, typically moves a measurable number of marks.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on statistics questions he gets right?
faqs.answer: Because the number is the smallest part of the mark. A chi-squared test for independence is marked for stating both hypotheses, naming the test, giving the degrees of freedom or p-value, comparing against the significance level and concluding in the context of the question. A p-value plus a verdict usually scores under half. The same applies to a correlation coefficient quoted without comment on strength and direction, or a regression prediction made outside the data range with no note that extrapolation is unreliable.

faqs.question: How much does Standard Level Applications tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with IB specialists advertised from AED 200 and examination-year specialists to AED 450 and above in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table. In-home visits are quoted from about AED 180 to AED 500 with travel embedded, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions are commonly advertised. Standard Level typically prices below Higher Level because more tutors can teach it. IB Gram quotes after a free trial.

faqs.question: Should my child have taken Analysis and Approaches instead?
faqs.answer: The signal worth reading is which part of the course they resent. A student who enjoys the statistics and the financial questions and struggles only with model justification is in the right course and needs writing work. A student who finds the statistics tedious and prefers algebraic manipulation may have suited Analysis better, though by DP2 that is usually academic. Switching is controlled by the school and IB registration, so raise it with the Diploma coordinator rather than deliberating for a term. The real obstacle in that direction is the non-calculator paper.

faqs.question: What is a Voronoi diagram and why is it in a maths syllabus?
faqs.answer: A Voronoi diagram divides a plane into regions according to which of several given points is nearest, and it is examined in Applications and Interpretation because it models genuine decisions: where to site a facility, which service area a location falls into, where the furthest point from all existing sites lies. Questions typically ask for perpendicular bisectors, the identification of a region, or the solution of a toxic-waste-dump problem. The content is self-contained, which makes it one of the quickest strands to secure once a student sits down with it.

faqs.question: How long is the exploration and what does it have to contain at SL?
faqs.answer: The IB recommends twelve to twenty pages, and the exploration is marked out of twenty against five criteria: presentation worth four, mathematical communication worth four, personal engagement worth three, reflection worth three, and use of mathematics worth six. Criterion E asks for mathematics commensurate with the level studied, so Standard Level mathematics used well scores better than Higher Level mathematics handled badly. The commonest failure on this course is collecting data first and looking for a question afterwards, which costs marks on engagement and reflection.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read my son's exploration draft, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: A tutor may read a submitted draft, comment against each of the five criteria, question the research question until it is answerable, point out where a statistical test does not support the claim being made, and explain what each criterion rewards. A tutor may not supply sentences, rework paragraphs, choose the data set or hand over analysis to be inserted. The exploration must be entirely the student's own work under IB academic-honesty rules. Our tutors keep a written note of the advice given, which is useful if the school asks what support was received.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the papers. What should we prioritise?
faqs.answer: The strands that return marks fastest, in this order: written templates for the statistical tests, the financial mathematics routines on the student's own calculator, then timed half-papers to fix pacing at roughly one mark a minute. Eight weeks is not enough to build modelling judgement from nothing, and a plan that pretends otherwise wastes the time available. A baseline paper in week one shows how many marks are genuinely recoverable. If that number is twenty or more the block is worth running, and if it is five we will say so.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools do your Standard Level Applications students come from?
faqs.answer: From across the emirate: large Diploma cohorts at Deira International School, GEMS Wellington International School, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and Raffles World Academy, and continuum schools including Uptown School, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, Dwight School Dubai and Fairgreen International School. KHDA recorded 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment. Those schools are named as market context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with or endorsement from any of them.

faqs.question: What English and maths scores does the Ministry want for the American track?
faqs.answer: For the American curriculum track, the published requirement is at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test, with English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Those figures come from reporting on the Ministry's clarification of equivalency requirements. For the IB there is no points threshold we will publish without reading it on moe.gov.ae, and no tutoring is required for equivalency in any case.

faqs.question: Do two short sessions a week work better than one long one for this course?
faqs.answer: For many students on this course, yes. Statistics and financial mathematics are built from routines that need repeating rather than explaining twice, so two forty-five minute sessions often outperform one ninety-minute block. Shorter sessions also survive February better, when internal assessment deadlines across several subjects collide and a long weekly commitment is the first thing to be cancelled. Students whose weakness is modelling judgement usually do better with the longer format, because that work needs room to develop within a session.

faqs.question: If nobody is free in our slot, what actually happens?
faqs.answer: You are told before any payment, with the options named. Early-evening hours in Gulf Standard Time fill first across the whole city, so the alternatives are usually a different hour the same week, a short wait for a named tutor to free a slot, or a specialist in another time zone whose availability is stated plainly so you can judge whether it suits your household. None of the competitor pages we researched discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number.

intro.heading: The documents an AI SL family should end up holding
paragraphs: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is 150 teaching hours, assessed by two papers of ninety minutes each, worth 80 marks and 40% apiece, plus one exploration marked out of 20 and worth the remaining fifth of the grade. There is no third paper at Standard Level. Technology is permitted in both papers, which matters more than it sounds: it means the calculator is never the excuse, and every lost mark can be traced to a decision visible in the student's own working.

Parents are usually sold a feeling and then asked to renew on the strength of it. A better arrangement produces documents. After a term of weekly AI SL support, a family should be holding about a dozen dated scripts, a topic error log showing which mistakes recur and which have stopped, and one written review that says whether the weekly hour is still worth holding. None of that requires trust. All of it can be read in an evening, and all of it belongs to you rather than to the provider who produced it.

The error log is the part most providers skip and the part that does the work. Each entry records the date, the topic, the question, and the category of the mistake: wrong model chosen, right answer never interpreted, rounded too early, calculator in the wrong mode, or question misread. Within a month the log stops being a list and starts being a pattern, and the pattern tells you what the next six sessions should target. A log that gets shorter is the most honest progress signal this subject produces, and it arrives weeks before any school report says anything at all.

AI SL has a distinctive failure profile that the log exposes quickly. Statistics and probability takes 36 of the 150 guide hours, more than any other topic, and functions takes 31. The marks lost in those blocks are rarely about computation, because the technology handles that. They are lost on choosing a model that does not fit the data, on quoting a coefficient without saying what it means for the situation described, and on stopping at the number the calculator produced rather than answering the question asked.

What follows sets out the components and what each script reveals, the places AI SL marks leak, how an error log is read, what the gap from MYP or IGCSE actually measures, the authorship evidence behind the exploration, and the Ministry of Education equivalency paperwork these grades eventually feed into. Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that is an India-only service, and the reason it matters here is the record a session leaves behind.

sections.heading: Two ninety-minute papers, both with a calculator: what each script reveals
paragraphs: AI SL is assessed by Paper 1 and Paper 2, each ninety minutes, each 80 marks, each 40% of the final grade, with technology required in both. The exploration supplies the remaining 20%. There is no Paper 3 at Standard Level, which is the single most useful thing to establish before buying any support, because Higher Level material and Higher Level rates have a habit of attaching themselves to Standard Level students in this market.

Paper 1 is broadly short and structured, moving across the syllabus in smaller questions. Paper 2 runs longer questions that develop over several parts. Marked properly, they tell you different things. Paper 1 shows coverage: which of the five topic blocks are reliable and which collapse. Paper 2 shows stamina and interpretation: whether the student can carry a context through four parts and still answer the question that was asked at the end rather than the calculation they performed in the middle.

Because technology is allowed throughout, the arithmetic is rarely the fault. That makes AI SL unusually diagnosable. A wrong answer with clear working and a correct method points at the calculator, the mode it was in, or the data column selected. A right answer with no interpreting sentence points at the habit of stopping too early. A wrong model at the start of a long question points at topic knowledge. Three different problems, three different remedies, all visible on the page.

The table below is what we ask for when a family first makes contact, and it is also what a tutor should be able to produce from any script within twenty minutes. If a provider cannot tell you which component a mark came from and what the loss category was, they are not reading the paper; they are reading the total at the top of it.

sections.heading: Where AI SL marks leak, and how the leak shows up in writing
paragraphs: The commonest AI SL loss is a mark the student had already earned and then did not collect. They run the regression correctly, state the coefficient, and never write the sentence saying what it means for the shop, the population or the temperature in the question. The calculation is worth the method mark; the sentence is worth the context mark; and across a full paper, those uncollected sentences can add up to a double-figure total. Nothing about fixing it requires new mathematics.

The second leak is model choice. Given a scatter of data, a Standard Level student has to decide whether a linear fit is defensible, whether an exponential model suits the growth described, or whether the data should be treated as discrete. Choosing wrongly costs the marks that follow, because every subsequent calculation is executed on the wrong object. In the error log this appears as a cluster of entries in the functions and statistics blocks, which between them carry 67 of the 150 guide hours.

The third is rounding. Technology encourages a student to carry a displayed value forward, round to two decimal places midway, and then produce a final answer that misses the accuracy mark by a unit. The rule to train is simple and unglamorous: carry full precision through the working and round only at the end, to three significant figures unless the question specifies otherwise. That is a habit, not a concept, and habits respond to repetition rather than explanation.

The fourth is the calculator itself: degree and radian modes confused, a statistics list left populated from the previous question, a graph window that hides the root being asked for. These are the fastest losses to eliminate and the ones most likely to be dismissed as carelessness. They are not carelessness; they are an unpractised routine, and a tutor who watches the student operate their own model of calculator on a shared screen will see it in one session.

sections.heading: The topic error log, and how a parent reads one
paragraphs: An error log is one page per month with five columns: date, topic, question reference, error category and whether the category has recurred. It takes a tutor three minutes per session to maintain and it changes the conversation at review from impressions to counts. A category with six entries in September and one in November is the clearest statement of progress available in this subject, and it exists weeks before any school report reflects it.

The five AI SL blocks are unevenly weighted in the guide, and the log usually reflects that. Statistics and probability takes 36 hours, functions 31, calculus 19, geometry and trigonometry 18 and number and algebra 16, with 30 further hours for the toolkit and the exploration. A log dominated by statistics entries is normal rather than alarming. A log dominated by number and algebra entries suggests the problem predates the Diploma and the remedy is different and usually shorter.

Reading the log is a matter of counting categories rather than reading comments. If the top category is interpretation, the next sessions should be short, frequent and almost entirely about writing sentences. If it is model choice, they should be longer and built around data sets. If it is rounding and calculator handling, two sessions and a checking routine should close most of it, and a provider recommending a full term for that is overselling.

The log is also what makes a change of tutor survivable. Inside the network the log moves with the student, so a new tutor starts from thirty categorised entries rather than from a conversation. Families leaving entirely can take the log with them; it is their record, not a retention device, and we send it on request along with the marked scripts.

sections.heading: From MYP or IGCSE into AI SL: the gap, measured rather than described
paragraphs: Every Dubai family arriving at AI SL has a different gap to close, and the useful version of that statement is a table rather than a paragraph. A student from IGCSE Extended has procedural fluency and no practice at choosing a model. A student from MYP has criterion-based feedback and no experience of a timed ninety-minute paper. A student from a CBSE background usually has strong algebra and little exposure to writing conclusions in context. The remedies differ in content and in length.

Measuring the gap takes one session and one unseen question. Give the student data, a context and no instruction about method, and watch what happens. Do they sketch? Do they choose a model and say why? Do they answer the question asked? The answers place them precisely, and they also produce the first entries in the error log. That single hour is worth more than any readiness description a school or a provider can offer.

The transition that catches most Dubai families is the one nobody names: a student who was comfortable in Year 11 maths and has arrived in AI SL expecting the same subject with a new label. AI SL asks for interpretation in a way IGCSE rarely does, and the first reported DP1 grade in November is often the first time anyone notices. Two or three weeks of targeted work at that point is a far smaller intervention than the one required in DP2.

The right-hand column gives honest ranges rather than a single number, because the variable is the student rather than the curriculum they came from. Where a gap is wider than the table suggests, we say so at the trial, and where a student plainly needs no support at all we say that too. Telling a family they do not need to buy anything is the cheapest way to be trusted later.

sections.heading: The exploration at Standard Level, and what counts as proof of authorship
paragraphs: The AI SL exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, with six of those twenty marks on the last. It is worth 20% of the grade, the same as half a paper, and the IB recommends roughly twelve to twenty pages. Length is not rewarded. What is rewarded is a question worth asking, mathematics at the right level, and reflection that evaluates rather than recaps.

The authorship evidence is a dated version history. A first version carrying the research question and the data source. A second with the mathematics attempted and the gaps still visible. A third responding to questions rather than absorbing supplied text. Dubai schools run their own internal deadlines and their own authenticity conversations, and a student who can walk a coordinator through three dated versions is in a very different position from one who produces a single polished file.

The order matters more at Standard Level than families expect. A student who finds a data set first and then invents a question to fit it almost always scores poorly on personal engagement and reflection, because neither is genuine. A student who writes the question first and then goes looking for data has a document with a spine. One session spent on that sequence, before any mathematics is attempted, is the highest-value hour in the whole exploration process.

The boundary on paid support is the same wherever it appears on this site. A tutor may teach a technique on a separate example, ask what a symbol means, say where a reader loses the thread, and ask what would change the conclusion. The student makes every decision and types every word of the submitted file. Providers in this market sell completed documents for thousands of dirhams; under IB rules the consequence of that falls on the candidate, and it can end a diploma.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the paperwork these grades eventually feed
paragraphs: AI SL marks end up in a transcript, and that transcript eventually meets the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process if your child applies to a UAE university or needs their certificate attested. Almost nobody in this search mentions it. The British-track requirements have been published: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details in that are worth holding onto. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count, which corrects a figure one ranking competitor publishes. And for the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying.

For the IB specifically we publish no points threshold, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site and an unsourced number here would be repeated across thousands of pages. Verify the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before planning around it. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates; it is a government process with its own channel, and anyone implying otherwise is misrepresenting it.

The practical link back to AI SL is modest and real. Mathematics appears in every one of these routes, so a student with a secure Standard Level mathematics grade has fewer complications in the paperwork than one who has had to resit. That is a reason to take the subject seriously, not a reason to buy tutoring. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any page suggesting it is has invented an urgency that does not exist.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one in Dubai, and the record a session leaves behind
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen where tutor and student write on the same page, timed to Gulf Standard Time and fitted around a Dubai school day. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai. Those are a service we run only in India, and no sentence on this site should suggest otherwise to a family in this emirate.

The argument here is specifically about the record. Work exchanged as files exists in two places and can be read by a parent travelling or living elsewhere. A shared screen leaves the session's working behind rather than inside an exercise book. The error log is a document rather than a memory. None of that is available from an arrangement where feedback is given verbally at the door and the only artefact is whatever the student wrote down at the time.

There is a supply argument too. The International Baccalaureate accounts for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, against 37 per cent for UK curricula, so AI SL specialists are sparse in any single community. Making proximity a requirement narrows the choice to whoever is nearby and free, which in practice often means a general maths tutor rather than someone who has marked Standard Level scripts against a markscheme and knows where the context marks hide.

The honest limit is that a student who will not engage with a video lesson is not served by one. That is exactly what the free trial exists to test, and we would rather find out in the trial than in week five. Where the answer is no, we say so instead of selling a term and hoping the habit forms.

sections.heading: The six-week review, and three things we will not claim at it
paragraphs: Six weeks in, the review happens with the scripts and the log in front of both of us. It produces one of three decisions: continue with the same target, change the target because the log has moved, or stop because the categories have closed. Stopping is a real outcome and we will recommend it when the evidence supports it. The default in this market is a renewal nobody discussed, which is how families end up two years into an arrangement they cannot evaluate.

The first thing we will not say is that your child is on track for a particular grade. The grade comes from weighted components compared against boundaries set for that session, and a tutor who marks part of one subject cannot know how the rest will score. The second is any statistic about our own results. No satisfaction percentage, no proportion of students improved, no median tutor score, because we cannot show you the sample, the date or the method, and a figure without those is decoration.

The third is a claim about speed. Some error categories close in two sessions, particularly calculator handling and rounding. Others, model choice in particular, take a term because the student has to meet enough different data sets to build judgement. Any provider offering a fixed timescale for an unseen student is quoting a sales figure. The log is what replaces the promise: it either shortens or it does not, and you can see which within a month.

What we do commit to is narrow and checkable. A fixed weekly slot, work marked against the markscheme between sessions, every error categorised in the same log, a dated note after each session, and a review at six weeks where ending the arrangement is one of the three legitimate answers. If your school's own maths clinic covers what a session would cover, we will tell you that as well, because it is free and we are not.

process.title: Send a script and the school's calendar
process.description: A photograph of a marked AI SL paper and the school's published mock and coursework dates are enough to brief a tutor properly. The script shows the error categories; the calendar shows when the next real data point arrives. Together they fix what the first month should target.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, free, no card details taken, no obligation afterwards. Your child works with the tutor we actually propose, and the session produces page one of the error log, which you keep whether or not you continue. If the match is wrong, we change it or say we cannot.

process.title: Fix the slot before the term fills
process.description: The 4pm to 6pm window is the one that survives a Dubai school week, and it fills in the first fortnight of term. Booking it early is the difference between a dozen marked scripts in a term and seven, and the number of scripts is what makes the review meaningful.

process.title: Maintain the log every week
process.description: Work set after each session, returned marked before the next, and every error categorised in the same running log. It takes three minutes per session to keep and it is the document that turns a term of lessons into something you can actually evaluate.

process.title: Decide at six weeks with the log on the table
process.description: Continue, change the target, or stop. We bring the scripts and the counts; you make the call. A category that has gone from six entries to one is the clearest progress signal this subject produces, and it arrives well before a school report says anything.

whyPoints.title: An error log kept from session one
whyPoints.description: Date, topic, question, category, recurrence. Five columns, one page a month, three minutes a session. It converts a term of impressions into counts, and counts are the only thing a parent can genuinely check at a review.

whyPoints.title: Standard Level priced and planned as Standard Level
whyPoints.description: AI SL is 150 hours and two papers. There is no Paper 3 at this level. We write the level into the plan so nobody ends up preparing for a component their child will not sit, which is a common and expensive drift in this market.

whyPoints.title: Context marks treated as the main event
whyPoints.description: The most frequent AI SL loss is a sentence never written about a calculation already done correctly. Sessions drill the interpreting sentence until it is automatic, because it is the cheapest mark on the paper and the one most often left behind.

whyPoints.title: Marking inside the fee, not beside it
whyPoints.description: Written work comes back scored against the markscheme with no separate charge. A tutor billing for marking time has a quiet reason to set very little, and the marked script is the only shared evidence either of us has about whether the hours are working.

whyPoints.title: The log and the scripts are yours
whyPoints.description: Ask and we send them; ask for deletion and the file goes, with copies offered first, under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. Student work is not a retention tool, and treating it as one is the wrong way round.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on the exploration
whyPoints.description: We question the research question, teach technique on separate examples and read drafts against the criterion letters. Every decision and every word in the submitted file is the student's. Finished documents are sold in this market, and the candidate carries the risk.

faqs.question: What does week-one evidence look like for an AI SL student?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis built on work the school has already marked, and the first page of the error log. The log entries name the topic, the question and the category of each mistake: model choice, missing interpretation, premature rounding, calculator handling or a misread question. No marks will have moved after one session, and anyone claiming otherwise is selling you something. What should exist is a categorised list specific enough that you can see what the next five sessions will target and why.

faqs.question: Which AI SL topics leak the most marks in a Dubai cohort?
faqs.answer: Statistics and probability first, which is unsurprising since it takes 36 of the 150 guide hours, followed by functions at 31. The losses in both are rarely computational, because technology is permitted in every AI SL paper. They come from choosing a model the data does not support and from quoting a result without saying what it means in the situation described. Number and algebra entries appear less often, and when they dominate a log the underlying problem usually predates the Diploma.

faqs.question: How do we check that an AI SL tutor is marking to the current syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. How many marks is each AI SL paper worth, and what is each one's weighting? Is there a Paper 3 at Standard Level? How many marks is the exploration and across how many criteria? The answers are 80 marks and 40% each, no, and 20 marks across five criteria. A tutor who hesitates on any of those is working from the course they learned rather than the one your child is sitting, and the marking will reflect that.

faqs.question: My child uses the calculator for everything. Is that an AI SL problem?
faqs.answer: Not in itself, since technology is allowed in both AI SL papers and using it well is part of the course. It becomes a problem in two specific ways. First, a student who never sketches or estimates cannot tell when the machine has given them something absurd. Second, mode errors, stale statistics lists and badly chosen graph windows produce confident wrong answers. Both show up quickly when a tutor watches the student operate their own calculator model on a shared screen, and both are usually fixed inside two sessions.

faqs.question: What is the difference in evidence between AI SL and AA SL work?
faqs.answer: AA Paper 1 bans technology, so its evidence is manual algebra, exact values and differentiation done by hand, and the losses cluster around technique. AI allows technology throughout, so its evidence is model choice and interpretation, and the losses cluster around unwritten sentences and unjustified models. A family deciding between the two courses learns more from one marked script in each than from any syllabus comparison, because the two scripts fail in visibly different places.

faqs.question: How long does it take to see AI SL coursework improve?
faqs.answer: The exploration improves in steps rather than steadily, and the steps are tied to specific sessions. One session on the research question usually produces a visible structural change in the next version. One on criterion B notation cleans up a document quickly. Reflection, which carries three marks, is the slowest to shift because it depends on the student having something genuine to say about their own results. Expect a different document after each dated version rather than gradual weekly progress.

faqs.question: What does the six-week AI SL review meeting cover?
faqs.answer: The scripts, the log and one decision. We count how often each error category appeared in the first fortnight against the last, name what is closed and what is not, and then choose between continuing with the same target, changing the target, or stopping because the categories have resolved. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will recommend it when the counts support it. What the review will not produce is a predicted grade, because a tutor marking part of one subject cannot know how the rest will score.

faqs.question: Can an AI SL tutor help my child read their own markscheme?
faqs.answer: That is one of the more valuable things a session does. Students routinely look at a marked paper, see the total, and learn nothing from it. Teaching them to read why a method mark was awarded on a wrong answer, or why an accuracy mark was lost on a correct one, turns every future returned paper into free feedback. We do not redistribute IB markschemes or past papers, since that is the IB's material; we work from your child's own script and the marking on it.

faqs.question: How do we track AI SL progress between school reports in Dubai?
faqs.answer: With the log and the dated scripts, because Dubai school reports arrive two or three times a year and compress everything into a grade. Between reports, the countable things are how many entries each error category collected this month against last, and whether a previously unreliable topic block produced a clean script. Those move weeks before a report does. Ask for the counts rather than a summary, and ask for them at a fixed point in the term rather than when you happen to think of it.

faqs.question: What does a context sentence have to do with AI SL marks?
faqs.answer: It is often the mark itself. A question gives data about rainfall, sales or population; the student runs the correct calculation and writes down a number. The markscheme awards the method and the accuracy, then awards a further mark for stating what the number means for the rainfall, the sales or the population. Students who never write that sentence lose a steady trickle of marks across both papers while answering every question correctly. It is the cheapest repair available in this course.

faqs.question: My child moved from MYP maths into AI SL. What should we watch?
faqs.answer: Timed paper technique, which MYP does not train, and sustained accuracy across ninety minutes. MYP assessment is criterion-based and often untimed, so a student can have excellent investigation habits and no experience of working at pace with marks at stake. Watch the first timed mock closely: if coverage is fine but the last third of the paper is thin, the issue is pace rather than knowledge, and that is three to five weeks of targeted work rather than a term of teaching.

faqs.question: Does rounding really cost AI SL marks on Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Consistently. The pattern is a student who rounds a displayed value to two decimal places midway through a multi-step question, carries it forward, and produces a final answer that misses the accuracy mark. The method marks survive; the accuracy marks do not. The fix is a rule rather than a concept: carry full precision through the working and round only at the end, to three significant figures unless the question specifies otherwise. Two sessions and a checking routine usually close this category for good.

faqs.question: What proof should we ask for before switching AI SL tutors?
faqs.answer: The log and the scripts. A tutor who has been working properly can hand over a categorised list of thirty or so errors and a folder of dated marked papers, and a new tutor starts from that rather than from a conversation. If neither exists after a term, that is itself the answer about whether the arrangement was producing anything. Inside our network the log moves with the student; if you are leaving entirely, ask for it and the marked work, and it is sent.

faqs.question: Is an AI SL mock result a reliable predictor of anything?
faqs.answer: It is the most useful single data point a Dubai school generates, and it is still only one. A mock tells you how the student performs on a full-length timed paper against their own cohort, which no class test does. What it cannot tell you is where the grade will land, because mock papers vary in difficulty between schools and grade boundaries are set per session. Treat it as the best available diagnostic and the worst available prophecy, and mark it carefully rather than reading the percentage.

faqs.question: How many AI SL past papers should my child have marked by February?
faqs.answer: Enough to produce a pattern rather than a score, which in practice means at least four full-length timed attempts with the errors categorised, and ideally more across both papers. Quantity without marking is wasted effort: a student who has worked through ten papers unchecked has practised their mistakes ten times. Two papers marked properly and reviewed beat six papers completed and filed. Your school may provide the papers; we work from the attempt and the marking rather than redistributing board material.

intro.heading: The course that is assessed with a calculator in both hands
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is the only IB Diploma mathematics route where a graphic display calculator is permitted in every written component. That single fact changes what tuition has to do. A student who is fluent on paper but slow on the machine loses marks that have nothing to do with understanding: a regression line typed into the wrong menu, a normal probability entered as a lower bound when the question wanted an upper one, a solver result copied to two decimal places when the question asked for three significant figures. An online IB maths tutor in Dubai can see all of this directly, because the calculator screen is shared rather than described.

The second thing that shapes the course is where its hours sit. The published guide gives AI SL roughly 16 hours to number and algebra, 31 to functions, 18 to geometry and trigonometry, 36 to statistics and probability, and 19 to calculus, with about 30 further hours for the toolkit and the exploration. Statistics is the largest single block, and it is the one most Dubai students arrive at with the least prior practice, because neither IGCSE nor the MYP asks for chi-squared tests, Spearman's rank or regression with interpretation attached. Families often book help for calculus and discover the marks were leaking in topic four all along.

Third, AI SL rewards writing in a way that surprises students who chose it to avoid writing. A correct value earns the method mark; the interpretation sentence earns the rest. Papers ask what the gradient means in the context of a fuel-consumption model, whether a correlation coefficient justifies a prediction outside the data range, what a residual tells you about the fit. Students who answer with numbers alone cap out in the middle bands. Tuition that only re-teaches content will not move that; tuition that marks a student's own sentences against the mark scheme will.

Dubai adds its own constraints. KHDA oversees 227 private schools in the emirate, which between them enrolled 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment. A DP2 student in one of those schools is carrying six subjects, the core, mandatory Arabic or Islamic Education lessons on top, and a commute that can eat ninety minutes a day. The practical question for most families is not whether tuition helps but which ninety-minute slot in the week can carry it without costing sleep.

What follows is the detail: what the calculator audit finds, which function families the papers keep returning to, how the statistics strand is actually marked, whether AI SL satisfies the degree your child is aiming at, what the five exploration criteria are worth, what the Dubai market charges in AED, and what a tutor may and may not do with a draft. Nothing here is a promise about a grade. Every figure has a source or a caveat attached.

sections.heading: The calculator audit: what an AI SL script reveals in the first session
paragraphs: An IB DP math AI SL tutor in Dubai should be able to tell you within one session whether the problem is mathematics or machinery. The audit is simple. The student is given six questions of a kind that appear on both AI SL papers, told to use the calculator exactly as they would in the examination, and asked to narrate what they are doing while the screen is shared. Six questions is enough, because the faults repeat.

The pattern that shows up most often in Dubai classrooms is a student who knows what a chi-squared test is for and cannot reach it in under ninety seconds. Another is a student who finds a regression line correctly and then types the rounded gradient back into the model, losing accuracy marks on every subsequent part. A third is a student who uses the solver for an equation the question wanted solved analytically, which is permitted, and then cannot show enough working to earn the method marks. None of these is a gap in understanding, and none of them is fixed by re-teaching the topic.

The audit also tells a parent something a report card cannot: whether the calculator in the bag is the one the student can actually use. Dubai schools issue different models, and a student who revised on a borrowed machine over the summer will sit the paper on a different key layout. We note the model at the first session and work only on that model from then on, because the muscle memory is the point.

The output of the audit is a one-page note: the six questions, what the screen showed, which marks were lost and to what cause. It is deliberately boring. A parent should be able to read it, hand it to the school, and have the conversation at the next parents' evening with evidence rather than impressions.

sections.heading: Modelling at AI SL: the function families the papers keep returning to
paragraphs: AI SL modelling questions are not open-ended. They draw on a small set of function families, and a student who can recognise which family a context belongs to has already earned the first two marks. The families are linear, quadratic, exponential growth and decay, sinusoidal, and piecewise. Logistic and power models appear at Higher Level more often than at Standard Level, but an AI SL paper can still show a scatter of data and ask which of two models fits better.

Recognition is taught by context, not by formula. Population with a ceiling behaves differently from population without one. Cooling and radioactive decay share a shape. Tide heights, daylight hours and temperature over a year are sinusoidal; delivery charges and tax bands are piecewise. Dubai contexts come up often enough in school-written assessments that it is worth practising them deliberately: a metro fare structure is piecewise, a summer temperature curve is sinusoidal, and a property-value question is usually exponential with a stated rate.

The marks after recognition sit in two places. The first is parameter meaning: what the amplitude represents, why the vertical shift is there, what the base of the exponential says about the rate per unit time. The second is the limitation sentence. Every modelling question that asks for a prediction is also asking whether the prediction is safe, and a student who extrapolates to a year outside the data without saying so has lost a mark that costs nothing to earn.

Tutorial work on modelling is therefore split: twenty minutes on fitting with the calculator, twenty on writing the interpretation to a mark scheme, twenty on the limitation. Students who do only the first part continue to score in the middle of the paper no matter how many questions they attempt.

sections.heading: Statistics carries the most hours at AI SL, and most of its marks are in the writing
paragraphs: Thirty-six of the roughly 120 content hours in AI SL go to statistics and probability. That is more than calculus and functions receive individually, and it is the block where Dubai students most often arrive without prior exposure. Neither the IGCSE syllabuses commonly taught in Dubai nor MYP mathematics asks a student to run a chi-squared test, calculate Spearman's rank correlation, or decide whether a sample justifies a conclusion.

The technical content is manageable in a term. What takes longer is the discipline of writing the conclusion. A chi-squared question is worth little if the student reports the test statistic and stops. The mark scheme wants the hypotheses stated, the degrees of freedom shown, the comparison made against the critical value or the significance level, and a sentence that names the two variables and says whether the evidence supports independence. Students lose one or two marks per question on that sentence alone, across a paper where such questions are common.

Correlation is the other recurring trap. A student who reports a correlation coefficient of 0.87 and calls it strong has done the easy half. The marks sit in whether correlation licenses a causal statement, whether the data range supports the prediction being asked for, and whether an outlier is doing the work. Dubai school-based assessments frequently use local datasets, including rainfall, visitor numbers and fuel prices, where the outlier is obvious once a student is in the habit of looking.

Tutorial practice here is repetitive on purpose. Four questions a week, each written out in full, each marked against the published scheme, until the conclusion sentence is automatic. It is the least glamorous part of AI SL tuition and reliably the part that moves a grade.

sections.heading: Does Applications and Interpretation SL open the degree your child wants?
paragraphs: This is the question that brings most Dubai families to an AI SL page in DP1 rather than DP2, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. AI SL is a full IB Diploma mathematics course and satisfies the mathematics requirement of the Diploma itself. What it does not always satisfy is the mathematics prerequisite set by a specific university for a specific degree, and those prerequisites are published by the universities, not by the IB.

The pattern across published entry requirements is consistent enough to plan around. Engineering, physics, mathematics and most quantitative finance degrees in the United Kingdom typically ask for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a minority accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. Medicine and dentistry usually specify chemistry and biology rather than a mathematics level. Business, economics at many institutions, psychology, architecture, law and the humanities commonly accept either course at Standard Level. Universities inside the UAE publish their own requirements, and several accept an IB Diploma with any mathematics course alongside a subject-specific test.

The practical advice is to check three named universities and the exact degree title before the subject-change window closes in DP1, and to check the current year's requirement rather than a forum post. A requirement written for 2024 entry may have moved. Where a student discovers in DP2 that the target degree wants AA HL, the realistic routes are a different degree choice, a foundation year, or a mathematics module taken after school rather than a mid-course transfer, which is rarely feasible that late.

A tutor's job in that conversation is to be useful and not to sell. If a student is capable of AA SL and aiming at a degree that needs it, saying so in DP1 is worth more than two years of AI SL sessions. Separately, the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process for certificates has its own documented requirements, and no tutoring arrangement is required for it.

sections.heading: Criterion A to E on the exploration, and where a tutor must stop
paragraphs: The AI SL exploration is 20 marks and 20 per cent of the grade, assessed against five criteria. Criterion A, presentation, is worth 4. Criterion B, mathematical communication, is worth 4. Criterion C, personal engagement, is worth 3. Criterion D, reflection, is worth 3. Criterion E, use of mathematics, is worth 6. The guide recommends a length of about 12 to 20 pages. Those numbers are the whole reason the exploration is winnable: a student who reads the criteria before choosing a topic can plan for marks that most candidates lose by accident.

The commonest failure is not weak mathematics. It is a topic that leaves no room for reflection, or mathematics at a level the criteria cannot reward, or presentation that buries the reasoning under screenshots. Criterion E rewards mathematics commensurate with the course and used correctly; a student who runs a single regression and stops will cap low on E no matter how neatly the document is laid out. Equally, a student who imports university-level statistics they cannot explain gains nothing, because the criterion rewards understanding rather than ambition.

Where a tutor stops matters more than what a tutor covers. Under IB academic honesty rules the exploration must be the student's own work, and the school signs it off on that basis. A tutor may discuss how the criteria are read, give feedback on a draft the student has produced, point out that a section does not address reflection, and teach a technique the student then applies. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the dataset analysis, rewrite passages, or hand over prose. We keep a dated history of drafts received and comments given, so that if a school ever asks, the authorship record exists.

The practical sequence we use is: the student proposes three candidate questions, the tutor says which are answerable with AI SL mathematics and why, the student picks one, and feedback from then on is criterion-referenced only. That boundary is a selling point rather than a limitation. Essay mills in this market sell completed internal assessments; an IB student who submits one risks a malpractice finding and the loss of the Diploma.

sections.heading: The timetable squeeze: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: A Dubai Diploma student is not carrying six subjects and the core alone. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements that schools were told to implement by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a DP2 student, those lessons occupy periods that in another country would be study time, and that is the single biggest constraint on when an AI SL tutorial can sit.

The detail matters because the requirements are not uniform. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two things follow for a family planning tuition. First, the week has less slack than the subject count suggests, so the realistic question is which single 90-minute block is protected rather than how many sessions can be squeezed in. Second, Arabic itself is often the subject a DP student is quietly behind in, and an AI SL tutorial that eats the only Arabic revision slot has moved the problem rather than solved it.

We schedule around this by asking for the school timetable at the start, not the third week. Where a student needs support in both mathematics and Arabic, the sensible pattern is one long mathematics session and two short Arabic sessions rather than four equal blocks, because mathematics technique needs continuous time and language retention needs frequency.

sections.heading: What AI SL support costs in Dubai, and what each band includes
paragraphs: Published rates in the Dubai tutoring market, read in October 2026, fall into clear bands. University-student and budget online providers advertise from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online are commonly quoted between AED 150 and AED 300. In-home one-to-one visits, which include the tutor's travel, run around AED 180 to AED 500 depending on area and subject. IB and A-Level specialists sit at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named or examiner-branded tutors have been advertised as high as AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the same market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list. What the bands buy, though, is worth unpicking, because the hourly number hides most of the difference. A cheap hour is usually contact time only: no marking between sessions, no written note, no mark scheme work. A specialist hour at the top of the range usually includes a marked script returned before the lesson, which is where the diagnostic value sits. A family paying AED 150 for four sessions a month and a family paying AED 300 for two are often buying the same total teaching, and the second arrangement frequently moves a grade faster because the evidence trail exists.

The second variable specific to this emirate is travel. An in-home rate in Dubai carries the drive, and in practice that both raises the hourly figure and narrows the pool to tutors who happen to live within reach. For a course as specific as AI SL, that trade is poor value: a Dubai Marina family choosing by postcode is choosing from whoever can reach the Marina at 5pm, while the same family choosing online is choosing from every AI SL specialist available in the time zone.

On our own pricing, the honest position is that it depends on level, session length and how much marking sits between sessions, and that the first lesson is free with no card required. We publish the market bands so a parent can judge any quote, ours included, against something other than the next advertisement.
