sections.heading: Being human: the stimulus question nobody practises
paragraphs: Paper 1 opens on the compulsory core theme, Being human, and the question is stimulus-based. A short text, image or scenario is given, and the student must identify a philosophical issue arising from it and then argue about that issue. Two distinct operations are being tested, and students routinely perform only the second. An answer that argues brilliantly about a question the stimulus does not raise has already capped itself.

Identifying the issue is a skill with a procedure. Read the stimulus twice. Ask what is being assumed in it about personhood, identity, freedom, agency or the limits of the self. Name that assumption as a philosophical claim rather than as a topic. Then write the question the stimulus raises in one sentence, and check it is a question philosophy can argue about rather than one that needs a fact. A student who does this reliably has secured the first third of the marks before beginning the argument.

The content behind it matters too, and the core theme is often taught quickly because it is assumed to be intuitive. Personal identity over time, the relationship between mind and body, what makes a person rather than a human organism, freedom and determinism, and the social constitution of the self are all live here, and a student needs two or three positions on each with their standard objections. Not twenty. Two or three, known well enough to be used under time pressure.

Sessions work on this with unseen stimuli every few weeks, because the skill decays if it is not practised. Dubai students have an advantage worth exploiting: a city where several cultural traditions sit side by side makes questions about identity and the social self concrete rather than abstract, and an answer that uses a real observation precisely is stronger than one built from a textbook example. The trap is letting the observation become the answer instead of the illustration.
bullets: Identify the issue first, in one sentence, before arguing anything
Name the assumption in the stimulus as a philosophical claim
Hold two or three positions per core topic, with their standard objections
Practise on unseen stimuli regularly; the skill decays without it

sections.heading: The seven optional themes and where each one loses marks
paragraphs: Section B of Paper 1 is an essay on an optional theme, one at Standard Level and two at Higher Level, chosen by the school rather than the student. Each theme has a characteristic failure mode, and they are different enough that a tutor who has taught Ethics is not automatically useful for Philosophy of science. Matching on the theme rather than on the subject is therefore worth insisting on.

The pattern across all seven is the same underneath: the student answers the question they find interesting rather than the one on the paper, and substitutes their own view for an accurate account of the position being examined. Ethics essays describe what the student believes is right instead of what a named theory claims. Philosophy of science essays explain science. Aesthetics essays describe taste. Philosophy of religion essays argue a conclusion rather than evaluating an argument's structure.

Fixing it starts with a rule that sounds trivial and is not: write the strongest version of the position you intend to criticise before you criticise it, and make it strong enough that someone who holds it would recognise it. Examiners credit that explicitly, and students skip it because it feels like conceding ground. An essay that sets out a position fairly, raises the best objection to it, and then responds to that objection has performed the operation the subject exists to test.
The table below gives each theme's own trap. It is a diagnostic tool rather than a revision list: read down it with a marked essay in hand and the relevant row is usually obvious within a minute.

Analyse judgement and value, not individual works
Describing personal taste and calling it evaluation

sections.heading: Paper 2: arguing from the prescribed text, not about it
paragraphs: Paper 2 is one essay in one hour on one text that the school has chosen from the published list. It is worth a quarter of a Standard Level grade and a fifth of a Higher Level one, and it is the component most often left to private reading. The marks go to an essay that argues from the text, with accurate reference to what it actually says, in response to the question asked. They do not go to a summary of the author's thought or an account of their historical significance.

The commonest shape of a failed Paper 2 answer is recognisable immediately. It opens with context about the philosopher's life and period, moves to a general exposition of their main ideas, mentions the question in the final paragraph, and never quotes or closely paraphrases a specific passage. A student who has read the text once and relied on secondary summaries writes this essay almost inevitably, because they have no passages available to them under time pressure.

The fix is a passage bank. Fifteen to twenty short passages, located precisely, each tagged with the claim it supports and the objection it invites. Building one takes a few hours of close reading with guidance and transforms the paper from a memory exercise into a selection exercise. The difference under exam conditions is large: a student with a passage bank spends the first five minutes choosing evidence rather than trying to remember any.

Published editions, papers and markschemes are cited at their source rather than reproduced, which is both a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. What a tutor supplies is the method of reading and the questions to put to a passage. The reading itself has to be done by the student, and there is no version of this component that works without it.

sections.heading: Higher Level Paper 3: the unseen paper on doing philosophy
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit a third paper of 75 minutes, worth a fifth of the grade, presenting an unseen passage about the nature, method or value of philosophy itself. The task is to engage with the passage philosophically rather than to summarise it or to agree with it. Nothing else in the course asks for this, and that is precisely why it is the component Higher Level students are least prepared for.

What makes it difficult is the absence of a syllabus to revise. There is no content to learn, only an operation to practise: read a passage making claims about what philosophy is or does, identify the claims, test them, and arrive at a considered position that engages with what the passage actually argued. A student who has done five of these under time is in a completely different position from one who has read about them, and reading about them is what most do.

The second difficulty is tonal. Passages about philosophical method invite either deference or dismissal, and both are fatal. Deference produces an answer that restates the passage approvingly. Dismissal produces one that announces the author is wrong without engaging. The marks are in the middle, in an answer that takes the passage's claim seriously enough to find the real objection to it and then considers what the author might say in reply.

The practical plan is simple and unpopular: a Paper 3 attempt every three or four weeks from early in DP2, each one marked and discussed. Students resist because it feels less productive than covering optional-theme content. It is the highest-yield hour in the Higher Level course, because it is twenty per cent of the grade with almost no competition from anyone who has not practised it.
bullets: No content to revise; the paper tests an operation, not knowledge
Engage with the passage's claims rather than restating or dismissing them
Find the real objection, then consider the author's likely reply
One timed attempt every three or four weeks from early in DP2

sections.heading: The internal assessment: why the stimulus choice decides the grade
paragraphs: The internal assessment is a philosophical analysis of a non-philosophical stimulus, up to 2,000 words, worth a quarter of a Standard Level grade and a fifth of a Higher Level one. The stimulus can be a film, an advertisement, a photograph, a news item, a song, a scene from a novel. What it cannot be is a piece of philosophy, and what it should not be is something with a single obvious philosophical moral.

Stimulus choice sets the ceiling before any writing happens, and this is where most lost marks originate. A stimulus that plainly illustrates one issue gives the student nowhere to go: the analysis names the issue, restates it, and runs out of material at nine hundred words. A stimulus containing a genuine tension — something that pulls in two directions, or that assumes something the student can question — produces an analysis with somewhere to travel. Testing three candidates for that quality is an hour well spent.

The word budget is the second lever. Description of the stimulus should be as short as clarity allows, because description earns nothing. The analysis needs almost all of the 2,000 words: identifying the issue, setting out the relevant philosophical positions accurately, arguing, and handling the obvious objection. Students who write eight hundred words of elegant description about a film they love then compress the philosophy into the last page, and the mark reflects that split rather than the quality of the writing.

A tutor's role here is bounded and worth stating plainly. A tutor may help test whether a stimulus has depth, teach how to identify and narrow a philosophical issue, explain what the assessment criteria credit, and read one draft and give written feedback on where it falls short. A tutor does not supply analysis, provide paragraphs, or hand over text. The analysis is the student's own work from first word to last, and the candidate signs for that.
bullets: The stimulus must not itself be philosophy
Pick something with a real tension, not a single obvious moral
Keep description short; the 2,000 words are for analysis
Handle the obvious objection inside the piece rather than ignoring it
Test three candidate stimuli before committing to one

sections.heading: Seven ways Dubai Philosophy students lose marks, in order of frequency
paragraphs: Most students have one or two of these, not seven, and identifying which is the point of the first session. The list is ordered by how often it shows up in marked work from Dubai Diploma candidates, and every item is diagnosable from a single essay. None of them is about reading more.

First, answering an adjacent question: the student writes a strong response to a question slightly different from the one on the paper. Second, failing to state the position being criticised fairly, so the objection lands on a version nobody holds. Third, treating a technical term loosely — knowledge for belief, cause for correlation, right for good. Fourth, reaching a conclusion without handling the strongest objection to it, which is the difference between an argument and an opinion.

Fifth, writing about a philosopher rather than from a passage, which is the Paper 2 failure in its pure form. Sixth, running out of time: Philosophy students write long and plan little, and a 50 per cent paper with two essays at Higher Level punishes that harder than any other component. Seventh, a stimulus-based answer that reacts to the stimulus rather than identifying the philosophical issue in it, which costs marks on the core theme question every single session.

Each has a specific drill, and the drills are short. Underline the question's verb and its object before writing. Write the opposing position in two sentences first. Keep a one-page glossary of the theme's terms. Devote the penultimate paragraph to the best objection. Build a passage bank. Write a 40-second plan and hold a word budget. Write the issue in one sentence before arguing. A student who does the two that apply to them improves faster than one who revises everything.
bullets: Answering an adjacent question rather than the one set
Criticising a weak version of a position nobody actually holds
Using technical terms loosely while writing fluently
Concluding without handling the strongest objection
Writing about a philosopher instead of from a passage
Running out of time because nothing was planned or budgeted

sections.heading: Equivalency, mandatory UAE subjects and whether Philosophy counts
paragraphs: Dubai parents reasonably ask whether a subject like Philosophy affects university access and Ministry of Education equivalency. Two things are worth separating. For the British track, the published equivalency requirements are specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. For the IB, no points threshold should be taken from any tutoring website, including this one: verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

Nothing about equivalency requires tutoring, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. The useful action is to ask your school's university counsellor which specific requirements your child's intended destination sets, and to check the authority's own published page rather than a summary. One competitor page ranking for these searches states a subject count for IGCSE candidates in the UAE that does not match the published rule, which is a reminder to go to the source.

The second question is the mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the Diploma. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools able to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met.

For a Diploma Philosophy student the practical effect is timetable pressure rather than academic difficulty. Those lessons sit inside a week that already contains six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the creativity, activity and service requirement. A tutoring plan that ignores them produces a schedule a student cannot keep. IB Gram supports Arabic as a separate stream where a family needs it, and the only honest thing to say about equivalency is to describe it, cite the authority, and point you at the official channel.

Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from that count of five
Plus one A Level at E, or two AS Levels, for the British route

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and what to ask before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Philosophy is a subject where the line between teaching and producing work is easy to blur, because the product is argument and arguments are made in conversation. The boundary is still clear. A tutor may explain positions, take the opposing side, teach how to structure an argument, discuss a stimulus the student has chosen, explain the criteria and read one draft with written feedback. A tutor may not supply paragraphs, rewrite a draft into final form, or hand over anything for submission. One provider visible in this search sells completed assessed work; the consequence of using it falls on the candidate, not the seller.

Generative tools need naming in this subject more than most, because they produce plausible philosophical prose quickly. A student may use them to find reading or to check their own grammar. A student may not use them to produce sentences that go into an assessed piece. Dubai schools increasingly ask candidates to show a research process, and keeping a short log of where ideas came from makes that straightforward rather than stressful.

On the regulatory side, there is one question most parents never think to ask. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified.

Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or endorsement from any of those bodies, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and it occupies no office in the UAE. Any page telling you otherwise is one to leave.

process.title: Send one marked essay and the course outline
process.description: The outline shows which optional themes and which prescribed text the school has set. A marked essay shows which operation is failing. With both, the trial lesson starts on a named failure mode instead of a syllabus tour, which is the difference between a useful first hour and a pleasant one.

process.title: Get a diagnosis, in writing
process.description: After the first session you should have one or two named failure modes from the list on this page, with the evidence from your child's own writing attached. Seven general weaknesses is not a diagnosis. One specific operation, with the drill that fixes it, is.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session at no cost, no card, no package. Watch for whether the tutor argues back. Philosophy is learned through someone taking the opposing position competently, and a tutor who only explains positions is giving a lecture your child could read instead.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot and a writing cycle
process.description: A repeating hour in Gulf Standard Time around school, activities and prayer times, with Ramadan timings shifted so nothing sits across Iftar. One written argument goes back marked between every session, because this subject improves through marked writing rather than through discussion alone.

process.title: Re-diagnose at six weeks
process.description: The named failure mode should have closed, and a new one usually becomes visible underneath it. That is progress, not failure. If nothing has moved after six weeks of marked writing, the match or the plan changes, and that conversation is scheduled rather than left to you to raise.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before content
whyPoints.description: Most Philosophy students have one or two consistent failure modes, visible in a single marked essay. Sessions name them and drill the specific repair, rather than touring a syllabus the student has already read more of than the tutor has.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the theme and the text
whyPoints.description: Schools choose the optional themes and the prescribed text, and a tutor who has taught Ethics is not automatically useful for Philosophy of science or for Hume. Matching starts from your school's course outline, so no sessions are spent with a tutor reading the text for the first time.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 practised, not discussed
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level unseen paper is a fifth of the grade and has no content to revise. Timed attempts start early in DP2, each one marked, because students who have written five of these are in a different position from students who have read about them.

whyPoints.title: The stimulus is tested before it is used
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment's ceiling is set by the stimulus. Three candidates are tested for genuine philosophical tension before anything is written, which prevents the commonest version of this component: elegant description of something with one obvious moral.

whyPoints.title: Someone argues back
whyPoints.description: This subject is learned by having a competent opponent. A tutor who takes the opposing position, finds the real objection and makes the student answer it is doing the thing the examination rewards, and that only works one-to-one.

whyPoints.title: Online, one-to-one, said plainly
whyPoints.description: Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Philosophy is a small subject and matching on the actual text and theme requires a pool wider than one city's driving radius.

faqs.question: My child loves Philosophy and keeps getting 5s. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always one or two specific operations rather than a knowledge gap. The commonest are answering an adjacent question rather than the one set, and criticising a weak version of the position being examined. Both are visible in a single marked essay and both have short drills: underline the question's verb and object before writing, and write the opposing position in two fair sentences before raising any objection. Reading more philosophy does not help a student with either problem, which is why a first session should mark their own writing against the criteria rather than cover content.

faqs.question: What is the core theme in IB Philosophy and is it compulsory?
faqs.answer: The core theme is Being human and it is compulsory at both Standard and Higher Level. It covers personhood, identity, the self, freedom and the human condition, and it is examined through a stimulus-based question at the start of Paper 1. Two operations are tested: identifying a philosophical issue arising from the stimulus, and arguing about that issue. Students generally do the second well and skip the first, which caps the answer regardless of the argument's quality. Writing the issue in one sentence before arguing anything is the single most valuable habit on this paper.

faqs.question: How many optional themes does my child study in Philosophy?
faqs.answer: One at Standard Level and two at Higher Level, chosen by the school rather than the student, from seven: aesthetics, epistemology, ethics, philosophy and contemporary society, philosophy of religion, philosophy of science, and political philosophy. Each has a characteristic failure mode, which is why matching a tutor to the theme matters. Ethics essays substitute personal intuition for a named theory's claims. Philosophy of science essays explain science instead of its philosophy. Aesthetics essays describe taste. Check the school's course outline before engaging anyone, because these are genuinely different teaching jobs.

faqs.question: Which prescribed text will my child be examined on in Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Whichever one the school has chosen from the published list, which includes Plato's Republic, Descartes' Meditations, Hume's Enquiry, Mill's On Liberty, Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals, de Beauvoir's The Second Sex, the Tao Te Ching and Singer's The Life You Can Save among others. Ask the school directly, because Paper 2 is a full hour on that one text and a tutor needs to know it closely. The full list is in the subject guide, and your IB coordinator can confirm the school's choice in one message.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Paper 2 essay score poorly when they know the text?
faqs.answer: Because the paper credits arguing from the text with accurate reference, and knowing the text in general terms is not the same thing. The failing shape is recognisable: context about the philosopher's life, general exposition of their ideas, the question mentioned in the last paragraph, and no close reference to any specific passage. The repair is a passage bank of fifteen to twenty short passages, located precisely, each tagged with the claim it supports and the objection it invites. Under time pressure a student with that bank chooses evidence rather than trying to recall any.

faqs.question: What is Higher Level Paper 3 in Philosophy actually about?
faqs.answer: An unseen passage making claims about the nature, method or value of philosophy itself, answered in 75 minutes and worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade. There is no content to revise, which is what makes it difficult. The task is to identify the passage's claims, test them, and arrive at a considered position that engages with what was actually argued. Both deference and dismissal fail: restating the passage approvingly earns little, and announcing the author is wrong without engaging earns less. One timed attempt every three or four weeks from early in DP2 is the fix.

faqs.question: What can my child use as the stimulus for the Philosophy internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Anything that is not itself philosophy: a film, an advertisement, a photograph, a news item, a song, a scene from a novel. The choice sets the ceiling of the whole piece. A stimulus with one obvious philosophical moral leaves nowhere to go, and the analysis runs out of material at nine hundred words. A stimulus containing a genuine tension, or one that assumes something the student can question, produces an analysis with somewhere to travel. Testing three candidates for that quality before writing is the highest-value hour in the component.

faqs.question: How long is the Philosophy internal assessment and how should the words be split?
faqs.answer: Up to 2,000 words, worth 25% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level. Description of the stimulus should be as short as clarity allows, because description earns nothing, and the analysis needs almost all the budget: identifying the issue, setting out the relevant philosophical positions accurately, arguing, and handling the obvious objection inside the piece. The common split is eight hundred words of affectionate description of a favourite film followed by compressed philosophy, and the mark reflects the split rather than the quality of the prose.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Philosophy a lot more work than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is more work and differently distributed. Higher Level adds a second optional theme, extends Paper 1 from 105 to 150 minutes, and adds a fourth component, the unseen Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade. The weightings shift too: Paper 1 falls from 50% to 40%, and the prescribed text and internal assessment from 25% each to 20% each. A Standard Level student can concentrate most effort on one paper. A Higher Level student cannot, because the fourth component rehearses nothing the others teach.

faqs.question: Does Philosophy help or hurt a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the course and the institution, and the right person to ask is your school's university counsellor, who knows the specific requirements your child's destinations set. What can be said generally is that Philosophy develops the written argument that law, politics and humanities courses assess, and that no subject choice substitutes for meeting a published entry requirement. For Ministry of Education equivalency, check the authority's own page rather than any summary. No tutoring site, including this one, should be the source of a points threshold.

faqs.question: What are the UAE equivalency rules for an IGCSE and A Level student?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. For the IB there is no figure that should be taken from a tutoring page; verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, and any site implying it is has invented urgency about a regulatory process.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic and Islamic Education in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student the practical consequence is timetable pressure, which any tutoring plan has to respect.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Philosophy internal assessment legitimately?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a boundary worth stating. A tutor may test whether a stimulus has real philosophical depth, teach how to identify and narrow an issue, explain what the assessment criteria credit, take the opposing position in discussion, and read one draft and give written feedback on where it falls short. A tutor may not supply paragraphs, rewrite a draft into final form or hand over text. The analysis must be the student's own work from first word to last, and the candidate signs an authorship declaration they should be able to sign honestly.

faqs.question: My child is the only Philosophy student in their Dubai school. Can tutoring replace a class?
faqs.answer: It can replace the part that matters most. Philosophy is normally learned by arguing with people who disagree competently, and a single-candidate cohort has nobody to supply that. One-to-one teaching substitutes directly, because the method is dialogue rather than exposition and a tutor can take the opposing side on demand. What it cannot replicate is the range of views a seminar produces, so sessions compensate by presenting positions the student would not have reached alone. Small and single-candidate groups are common in Dubai, where Philosophy runs in a minority of Diploma schools.

faqs.question: Does a Philosophy tutor in Dubai need a permit, and should I ask?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and asking is routine rather than rude. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a separate educational services permit from KHDA.

intro.heading: Why Philosophy quotes in Dubai vary by a factor of ten
paragraphs: Ask five Dubai providers what IB Philosophy support costs and you will be quoted anything from AED 60 an hour to AED 650. Nothing about the subject explains that spread; what explains it is that the five are selling different things. At the bottom of the range the hour is content revision by a graduate who has read around the course. At the top it is a named specialist with examining experience whose scarcity, not whose syllabus coverage, sets the price. In between sits the band where most families actually transact.

Philosophy also costs more to tutor than most Group 3 subjects for one structural reason: almost nothing in it can be marked quickly. A Maths exploration can be checked in twenty minutes. A Philosophy essay on Nietzsche's account of moral genealogy cannot, because the grade turns on whether the argument has been reconstructed accurately and then tested, and reading for that takes as long as the student took to write it. Any quote that does not say whether essay marking happens inside or outside the paid hour is incomplete.

The third variable is the component mix. A Standard Level student who needs help with the core theme is buying ordinary teaching. A Higher Level student who needs the prescribed text paper, the unseen-text paper and supervision of the internal assessment is buying three distinct skills, and the third of those is project supervision rather than teaching. Providers who price all of that as one undifferentiated hour are either underpricing the supervision or overpricing the teaching, and it is worth asking which.

The fourth is timing, and it is the one families control. Rates in this market firm up as the exam window approaches because availability shrinks, and the hours themselves become less productive: a student six weeks out cannot absorb a new optional theme, so the money buys technique rather than knowledge. The same budget spent in DP1 buys both. Nothing in Philosophy tutoring is as expensive as starting it late. A family who buys fifteen hours across DP1 almost always ends up ahead of one who buys thirty in the final term, at half the outlay, and the difference is availability rather than effort.

Delivery for families in the Emirates is online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE at any price; that service exists only in India. For this subject the trade is almost entirely in your favour, because Philosophy specialists are rare in any single city and the text your child has been set may be one that only a handful of teachers in the region have taught to examination. Restricting the search to people who can also drive to your district by six in the evening is how families end up paying a premium for a tutor who has never taught their text.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme

Candidates also study a prescribed philosophical text and write an internal assessment analysing a non-philosophical stimulus. Higher Level adds a paper on unseen material about the nature of philosophical activity itself.

Before committing in Year 11, ask whether the course will definitely run, which optional themes the department teaches, and which prescribed text has been chosen, because that third answer determines how scarce and therefore how expensive a suitable tutor is.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: No MYP subject is philosophy, but the thinking-critically criterion in Individuals and Societies and the conceptual framing used across MYP subjects both rehearse the move the Diploma needs: separating a claim from the reasons offered for it. Students who have been marked on that arrive able to recognise an argument rather than an opinion.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students coming out of MYP into Philosophy usually need fewer paid hours than those arriving from an exam-led British Year 11, because they have already been assessed on conceptual thinking. Where they need help is speed: MYP assessment rarely runs against a clock, and Philosophy papers are unforgiving about time.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP contributes the disposition rather than any content: asking why, being asked for a reason, and being told that two classmates can disagree reasonably. The exhibition in the final PYP year is the first time most students have to defend a position they chose themselves in front of an audience.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large PYP sector and many of those schools sit on a campus that also runs the Diploma. For families planning a long stay in the emirate, the continuity matters less for content than for assessment literacy: students who have been inside IB marking since Year 3 need noticeably less of the technique coaching that paid hours otherwise go on.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Career-related Programme students take Diploma courses alongside a career-related study and a reflective project. Philosophy pairs well with the reflective project, which asks for an ethical dilemma to be examined, and that is close to the analytical work the Philosophy internal assessment requires.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is rare in Dubai, so a CP student taking Philosophy is often the only candidate in the school. Costs run higher for those students in practice, because there is no class to supply discussion and more of the dialectical work has to happen in paid one-to-one time rather than in a seminar room.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: What a Philosophy tutor needs to have taught depends on three choices the school made: the optional themes, the prescribed text, and whether the cohort is Higher or Standard Level. Those three narrow the pool of suitable tutors considerably, which is why they also move the price. Below is the full content map.

subjects.name: Core Theme: Being Human
subjects.description: Personhood, identity, the self, freedom, the mind and body, and what distinguishes human beings. Examined from a stimulus rather than a named question, which is why students who have only revised content freeze: the stimulus has to be read philosophically before anything can be written about it.

subjects.name: Optional Theme: Ethics
subjects.levels: Optional, SL one theme and HL two
subjects.description: Normative theories, metaethics, the status of moral claims and applied problems. The most commonly chosen theme in Dubai schools and the easiest to write badly, because students argue for positions instead of analysing the arguments that support them.

subjects.name: Optional Theme: Epistemology
subjects.levels: Optional, SL one theme and HL two
subjects.description: Knowledge, justification, scepticism, perception and testimony. Technically demanding and well rewarded: a student who can state and attack a justification condition precisely will score higher here than they would on a theme that invites opinion.

subjects.name: Optional Theme: Philosophy of Religion
subjects.levels: Optional, SL one theme and HL two
subjects.description: Concepts of the divine, arguments for and against the existence of God, religious experience and language, and the problem of evil. Requires careful handling of argument form: students who paraphrase an argument rather than reconstruct its premises cannot then evaluate it.

subjects.name: Optional Theme: Philosophy of Science
subjects.levels: Optional, SL one theme and HL two
subjects.description: Scientific method, demarcation, theory change, realism and the status of scientific knowledge. A strong pairing for students taking a Group 4 subject at Higher Level, who already have the examples and need the analytical vocabulary.

subjects.name: Optional Theme: Political Philosophy
subjects.levels: Optional, SL one theme and HL two
subjects.description: Authority, legitimacy, liberty, equality, justice and the grounds of political obligation. Candidates taking Global Politics alongside it must keep the writing conventions apart: this theme rewards conceptual analysis, not contemporary evidence.

subjects.name: Optional Theme: Aesthetics
subjects.levels: Optional, SL one theme and HL two
subjects.description: Art, beauty, judgement, representation and the value of aesthetic experience. Rarely chosen and therefore the hardest theme to find a tutor for, which is the clearest single example of how a school's syllabus choice moves what a family pays.

subjects.name: Optional Theme: Philosophy and Contemporary Society
subjects.levels: Optional, SL one theme and HL two
subjects.description: Philosophical questions raised by technology, work, gender, the environment and social organisation. Accessible and popular, with the usual risk: the contemporary material crowds out the philosophy and answers drift into commentary.

subjects.name: The Prescribed Text
subjects.description: One text studied in depth from the published list, which includes works such as Plato's Republic, Descartes' Meditations, Hume's Enquiry, Mill's On Liberty, Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morality, de Beauvoir's The Second Sex, Confucius' Analects and the Tao Te Ching among others. Examined by essay on that text alone.

subjects.name: HL Extension: the Nature of Philosophical Activity
subjects.description: An unseen passage about what philosophy is and how it is done, answered without prior knowledge of the passage. Students cannot revise content for it, only method, which is why it is the component most often left unpractised until the mocks expose it.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment: Philosophical Analysis of a Stimulus
subjects.description: An essay of roughly two thousand words that takes a deliberately non-philosophical stimulus, such as a film, an advertisement, a news item or an artwork, and extracts and examines a philosophical issue from it. Supervision here is project work rather than teaching, and should be priced as such.

subjects.name: Argument Reconstruction as a Trainable Skill
subjects.description: Setting out a philosopher's premises, identifying the inference, naming the hidden assumption, then attacking the weakest link. This single skill carries marks on all four components, and it is the one thing a Philosophy tutoring budget should be spent on first.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Where you live in Dubai changes the cost of tutoring in two concrete ways: how much of an in-home tutor's hour is paid travel, and how late a session has to start after the school run. Both show up on an invoice. These are the districts the enquiries come from most often.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Central, close to several Diploma schools, and therefore the band where in-home rates are least inflated by travel. Even here a tutor crossing from the other side of the city at six in the evening is charging for forty minutes of Sheikh Zayed Road inside the hourly rate.

regions.name: The Springs and The Lakes
regions.note: Established villa communities with a short run to the Meadows and Ranches schools. Sessions here typically start at five. Families in this band often already pay for two or three subjects, which is why the question they ask first is how few Philosophy hours will do the job.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Production City
regions.note: Peripheral and sparsely served, so an in-home tutor's quote here usually carries a visible travel premium or a two-hour minimum. The arithmetic that pushes these families online is simple: the same budget buys more teaching when none of it is spent on a car.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Garhoud
regions.note: Close to the older Deira-side schools with reasonable evening access. A band where group tuition centres are available and cheaper per head, which is worth comparing honestly: group provision works for content revision and not at all for the internal assessment.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Dense, well-connected and price-sensitive, with many families comparing a tuition centre's group rate against one-to-one. For a minority subject like Philosophy there is usually no group option at all, which changes the comparison before it starts.

regions.name: Town Square and Remraam
regions.note: Newer, more affordable communities a long way from the established Diploma schools, where the daily commute already consumes an hour. Sessions start late here, and the saving from online delivery is as much in time as in money.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: Recent high-rise development with a small, young school-age population and few nearby Diploma places, so students commute. Philosophy candidates in this band are often the only one in their year taking the subject, which removes any possibility of sharing a session.

regions.name: Meydan and Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: Villa and townhouse communities with good road access and families who tend to buy longer sessions less frequently. Ninety minutes once a week is the common shape here, and for essay-based subjects it is the better shape anyway.

schoolClusters.city: The large, long-established Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Bigger cohorts make a minority subject viable, so these are the schools where Philosophy is most likely to run every cycle. Ask the department which optional themes and which prescribed text they teach before you price any tutoring, because those two answers decide how scarce a suitable tutor is.

schoolClusters.city: Schools where the option depends on opt-in numbers
schoolClusters.note: At many Dubai Diploma schools a minority Group 3 subject runs only if enough students choose it, and the decision can come late in Year 11. Families here sometimes end up with a student taking Philosophy largely independently, which raises the number of paid hours required rather than the rate.

schoolClusters.city: Newer Diploma provision in the inland communities
schoolClusters.note: Recently opened schools often build their Group 3 offer around the staff they have, so the themes taught can change between cohorts. That instability is worth knowing about when budgeting across two years, because a change of teacher between DP1 and DP2 can mean a change of optional theme as well.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-online-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: These schools are named to describe the Dubai Diploma market this page addresses. Nothing here implies a partnership, endorsement or commercial relationship, and none is held.
dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three session shapes cover almost every Philosophy requirement, and they cost different amounts because they take different amounts of a tutor's unpaid time. Knowing which one you are buying is the easiest way to stop overpaying for the wrong thing.

modes.title: Weekly essay cycle, ninety minutes
modes.description: One longer session a week, with an essay written between sessions and read before the next. Ninety minutes is the right length for this subject because an argument cannot be reconstructed, attacked and rewritten inside an hour. Ask whether reading time is billed; where it is not, the hourly rate quoted is doing more work than it appears to.
bullets: An essay question set every session and answered to the real time limit
Marked against the published descriptors before the next session starts
One fault worked on at a time: reconstruction, objection, or judgement
Recording shared so the marking commentary can be rewatched in April

modes.title: Internal assessment supervision block
modes.description: Four to six sessions placed around the stimulus-based essay: testing whether the chosen stimulus actually yields a philosophical issue, settling which issue, choosing the philosophers to bring to it, then one round of criterion-referenced comments on the student's own draft. This is project supervision and it should appear as its own line on a quote.
bullets: Stimulus tested for philosophical yield before any drafting
The issue narrowed to one question the word count can actually hold
Philosophers chosen for relevance rather than for reputation
A single feedback round on the student's draft, with no text supplied

modes.title: Prescribed text intensive
modes.description: Six to eight sessions on the one text the school has set, working through its argument structure section by section rather than reading around it. The most cost-efficient block in the subject, because the examined content is finite and known in advance, and because the same reconstruction skill transfers to every other paper.
bullets: The text's argument mapped premise by premise, not summarised
Standard objections learned with their replies, not as a list
Past questions on the text answered to time from session three
Quotation discipline drilled, because unsupported claims lose marks here

modes.title: Unseen-text technique, Higher Level only
modes.description: Two to four sessions on the Higher Level paper, which presents unseen material about the nature of philosophical activity. No content can be revised, so the whole intervention is method: how to find the passage's claim, what to do in the first five minutes, and how to build an answer that engages rather than paraphrases.
bullets: A full unseen passage attempted cold in the first session
A reusable opening routine for the first five minutes
Paraphrase identified and eliminated from the student's answers
Timing rehearsed until the answer finishes rather than stops

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for Philosophy support, by provider model
paragraphs: Dubai publishes less tutoring pricing than almost any comparable market, and three of the best-ranked pages for IB tutoring in this city carry no figure at all. The table below assembles what providers do publish, with the band, who quotes in it, and what the hour includes. Every figure is a market rate read from the provider's own published material in October 2026, not an IB Gram price, and rates move.

Read it as a map of what you are buying rather than a league table. The lowest band is content revision and homework support, usually from a recent graduate, and for a subject where the grade turns on argument reconstruction it is poor value even when it is cheap. The middle band is the one most Dubai families transact in and is where a qualified subject tutor who can mark to the descriptors sits. The top band prices scarcity and reputation, which are real but are not the same as syllabus coverage.

One figure families should extract from any quote before paying is whether marking and reading happen inside or outside the billed hour. In Philosophy this is not a detail. An essay takes a tutor roughly as long to read properly as it took the student to write, and a provider quoting AED 200 an hour with marking included is charging less in real terms than one quoting AED 160 with marking billed separately. Ask the question in writing.

sections.heading: The six things that move a Philosophy quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Level comes first. A Higher Level candidate has two optional themes rather than one, plus the unseen-text paper, so the teachable surface is larger and the tutor pool smaller. Second is the prescribed text. A student set Plato or Mill can be matched easily; a student set a less commonly taught text on the list is looking for someone who has taken candidates through it to examination, and scarcity prices itself. Ask the school which text before you ask anyone what they charge.

Third is the optional themes, for the same reason: Ethics and Philosophy and Contemporary Society are widely taught, Aesthetics is not. Fourth is whether the internal assessment is in scope. Supervising a stimulus-based essay is project work spread over months, including reading a draft once and carefully, and it belongs on a quote as its own line rather than hidden in a weekly rate.

Fifth is timing. Availability tightens in the final two terms and the hours themselves do less, because a student six weeks from the papers cannot absorb a new theme and can only improve technique. Sixth is session length. Philosophy works badly in sixty-minute blocks and well in ninety, so compare quotes per session rather than per hour or you will conclude that the more expensive tutor is the cheaper one. None of these six is about the tutor being better. They are about what is being bought, and any provider who cannot explain which of the six is driving their number is quoting on instinct.
bullets: Higher Level means two optional themes and an extra paper, so a larger scope
A rarely taught prescribed text is the single biggest driver of scarcity
Internal assessment supervision is months of project work, not a weekly hour
Starting in the final term costs the same per hour and delivers less per hour

sections.heading: What the hours are buying: the four components
paragraphs: Philosophy is assessed through two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher, plus the internally assessed stimulus essay. The components are unusually independent of one another, which is good news for budgeting: a family can buy help with the prescribed text alone and leave the core theme to the school, and the two will not interfere. Few subjects allow that kind of targeted purchase, and it is worth exploiting rather than buying a blanket weekly arrangement that covers everything at once.

The weightings matter to where money goes. At Standard Level the first paper carries roughly half the grade, which makes the core theme and the single optional theme the obvious priority. At Higher Level that share falls and the two additional components take weight, so the hours have to be split more evenly, with the unseen-text paper usually the most neglected and therefore the best marginal buy. A Higher Level candidate who has never attempted that paper is typically two to four hours away from a reusable method, which is the cheapest band movement available anywhere in the subject.

Confirm the current weightings and durations against the subject guide your child's school holds rather than against any figure found online, including this one. Guides are revised, and the version that applies is the one the school registered for. Ask the coordinator for the assessment outline in writing at the start of DP1; it is a five-minute request that prevents a tutor planning towards the wrong paper for a year. The same outline names the command terms and the assessment objectives, which is what a tutor should be planning sessions from rather than a textbook contents page.

sections.heading: Hours to marks: what each common Philosophy fix costs
paragraphs: The most useful thing a tutoring quote can tell you is not the rate but the number of hours. Philosophy has a short list of recurring faults, each with a fairly predictable repair time, and once you know which fault your child has you can price the fix rather than buy an open-ended arrangement. A diagnostic essay identifies the fault in one session.

The repairs divide into cheap and expensive. Technique faults are cheap: a student who summarises instead of reconstructing, or who never states an objection, can be retrained in a handful of marked essays because the problem is a habit. Content gaps are mid-priced and predictable: an optional theme takes around eight to twelve hours to teach to an examinable standard. Project supervision is the expensive item, not per hour but in total, because it stretches across months.

The table costs each at the middle of the published Dubai band for a qualified online subject tutor, which the market puts at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. Those are market figures rather than ours, and they are there to let you sanity-check a quote rather than to set a price. What the table should make clear is that the cheapest intervention in this subject by a wide margin is fixing argument reconstruction early, because it pays on all four components at once. The costliest line is the one at the bottom of every column: a problem identified too late, where the hours are available and the time to use them is not.

sections.heading: The prescribed text: the cheapest marks in the subject
paragraphs: One component of Philosophy is fully knowable in advance. The school chooses a text from the published list, the examination asks an essay on that text, and the argument of a finished book does not change between sessions. A student who has mapped their text properly walks into that paper knowing roughly what can be asked of them, which is not true of any other component in the subject.

Mapping is the operative word, and it is different from reading. The product of a good prescribed-text block is a document in the student's own handwriting that sets out the text's major arguments premise by premise, names the standard objections to each, and records the author's own replies where the text makes them. Twenty pages of highlighted photocopy is not that. The map is what gets revised in April; the highlighting is not.

This is why the prescribed text is usually the best value block a Dubai family can buy, and why it is worth buying early. Six to eight sessions produces a map that serves the examination and, incidentally, teaches the reconstruction skill that lifts every other component. Starting it in the final term inverts the economics: the same hours then have to cover reading, mapping and timed practice at once, and something gets dropped. Ask the department in Year 11 or early DP1 which text has been chosen, and start the block in the first term rather than waiting for a mock result to prove it was needed.

sections.heading: The internal assessment: a stimulus that has to yield a real question
paragraphs: The internal assessment asks for roughly two thousand words examining a philosophical issue drawn from deliberately non-philosophical material: a film, a photograph, an advertisement, a song, a news report. Students choose the stimulus for interest and then discover it will not carry a question. A striking image that produces only the observation that identity is complicated has not yielded an issue; one that produces a specific question about whether personal identity survives a particular kind of change has.

That is where supervision earns its fee, and why this component should be priced separately from weekly teaching. The sequence is: test the stimulus for yield, settle one question narrow enough for two thousand words, choose two or three philosophers who speak to it directly rather than impressively, then read the student's own draft once against the criteria. Four to six sessions spread across months, not a block in the final fortnight.

The honesty boundary here is firm and worth stating before any money changes hands. A tutor may comment on one student-written draft, name a criterion that is not being met, point out that a premise is unsupported, or ask why a philosopher has been introduced. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the essay for the student, or hand back a version that only needs accepting. Ask any prospective tutor how they handle a draft and treat the word editing as a reason to look elsewhere. The stimulus essay is also the component where a late start is least recoverable, because the engagement with the material has to precede the analysis rather than be reconstructed from memory afterwards.

sections.heading: Where Dubai Philosophy candidates lose marks
paragraphs: The dominant fault is exposition without analysis. A student writes a clear, accurate account of what Mill argues and stops, because exposition feels like the work. The descriptors want the argument set out and then tested: a hidden premise named, an objection raised and answered, a judgement reached about whether the argument succeeds. Exposition alone sits in the middle bands however elegant it is, and the pattern is visible in a single marked essay.

Second is advocacy. Philosophy attracts students with strong views and the Ethics theme attracts them most. An essay that argues for a position reads as a position paper, and position papers are marked as such. The discipline to learn is that the question is almost never whether a view is right but whether the argument for it works, and students find that distinction genuinely difficult rather than merely unfamiliar.

Third is quotation discipline, which costs marks quietly. Claims about what a philosopher holds need textual support, and in the prescribed text paper especially an unsupported attribution is simply not credited. Fourth, and specific to Dubai cohorts, is pace: many candidates here write Philosophy essays at the length they write History essays and run out of time on the second question. Both are mechanical faults with mechanical fixes, which is the good news in a subject that otherwise resists quick repair. A single marked essay with the descriptors alongside it will usually show which two of these four a student has, and that is enough to price the work honestly.
bullets: Exposition without evaluation is the single commonest cause of a mid-band grade
Arguing for a view instead of testing the argument for it reads as advocacy
An attribution without textual support is not credited on the text paper
Essay length habits imported from History cause timing failures

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees and the 2026-27 freeze
paragraphs: Tutoring spend only makes sense against what a family is already paying. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate taking seven per cent of students against thirty-seven per cent for UK curricula. Diploma places sit at the upper end of the fee range in that market, and a Philosophy tutoring budget is a small increment on a large annual commitment.

The timing is also favourable. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For families planning two years of Diploma support, a frozen fee line makes the tutoring line easier to commit to and easier to compare against.

The sector is also expanding, which affects staffing and therefore the tutoring market. KHDA has reported that the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, following six openings in 2025-26 and a six per cent rise in enrolment. More Diploma places means more demand for a small pool of Philosophy specialists, which is a reason to book a scarce match early rather than a reason to pay more. The table below puts the tutoring numbers next to the fee line so the increment is visible rather than guessed at.
