sections.heading: In-home tuition, permits and what to check before you pay
paragraphs: IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at any price. Lessons for families in the Emirates are delivered live, one-to-one, over video, and the in-home service exists only in India. That is stated here rather than discovered after a deposit. The market figures above show what the alternative costs: published in-home bands run roughly AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with independents advertising higher, and a meaningful share of that hour pays for the drive rather than the teaching.

Whoever you hire, check the permit position. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. According to u.ae it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure you see quoted with scepticism.

Two further checks are worth making on a quote. First, ask whether the AED figure includes value added tax; we do not state the VAT treatment of tuition in the UAE on this page, because that depends on the provider's registration and on Federal Tax Authority rules rather than on anything a tutoring site can assert. Second, in Abu Dhabi specifically, press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so never engage a child's own teacher privately without checking the current policy.

process.title: Tell us the text and the themes, then ask the price
process.description: The useful first message names the prescribed text, the optional theme or themes, the level, and whether the internal assessment is in scope. Those four decide how scarce a suitable tutor is, and therefore what the honest rate is. A quote given before anyone knows which text your child was set is a guess dressed as a number.

process.title: A free diagnostic essay, marked in front of you
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing, is limited to one per student, and needs no card details. It is spent on one essay from a taught theme, marked against the published descriptors with the student watching, so you leave knowing which of the recurring faults you have and roughly how many hours it takes to repair. No sales pitch, and no package offered in the session.

process.title: Get the quote itemised before anything is booked
process.description: Weekly teaching, essay reading time, internal assessment supervision and any prescribed-text block should appear as separate lines with their own hour counts. That is the only form in which quotes from different providers can be compared, and it is also what stops supervision work being absorbed invisibly into a weekly rate.

process.title: Buy the block, not the year
process.description: Philosophy support works in blocks with a defined end: a prescribed text mapped, a theme made examinable, a reconstruction habit built, an internal assessment through its draft round. Each block has an hour count agreed in advance. Open-ended weekly arrangements are how families reach March having spent a great deal with nothing they can point at.

process.title: Review against marked work at each milestone
process.description: At the end of each block, at the mock session, and six weeks before the papers, the plan gets rebuilt from fresh marked evidence rather than from momentum. If the marks say the work is done, we say the work is done. A candidate reliably in the top bands with a submitted internal assessment does not need more hours.

process.title: Change tutor at no cost, no reason required
process.description: A different tutor costs nothing and needs no justification. In Philosophy the match is to a specific text and specific themes, so a mismatch is usually a matching error rather than a quality one, and it is cheaper to correct in week two than in month four. Any unused prepaid hours move with you.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED, published with their source and date
whyPoints.description: This page states the bands the Dubai market actually charges, names which provider publishes which figure, and dates the reading to October 2026. Three of the best-ranked IB tutoring pages for this city publish no price at all, and one of them asks the price in its own FAQ and declines to answer it.

whyPoints.title: Quotes itemised so they can be compared
whyPoints.description: Teaching, essay reading, prescribed-text work and internal assessment supervision are quoted separately with hour counts. A single blended hourly rate hides which of those you are actually buying, and in a subject where reading a draft takes as long as writing it, that distinction decides what the hour is worth.

whyPoints.title: Hours estimated against the specific fault
whyPoints.description: A diagnostic essay identifies which of the recurring Philosophy faults a student has, and each has a fairly predictable repair time. You get an hour count before you commit rather than an open invitation to keep booking, and the cheapest intervention is named first because it pays across all four components.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the prescribed text, not to the subject
whyPoints.description: Being set a less commonly taught text on the prescribed list narrows the pool of suitable tutors sharply. Online delivery is what makes that match findable at all, because the search runs across everyone who can teach your child at seven in the evening rather than everyone within driving distance of Al Safa.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment is the student's own work. One round of comments on one student-written draft, pointed at criteria, with no sentences supplied and no restructuring done on their behalf. Businesses in this market sell completed coursework at four-figure prices; the consequence of buying it falls on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: No outcome promised at any price
whyPoints.description: Nobody can sell a grade, and a provider quoting a premium rate alongside an implied result is selling the wrong thing. What is offered here is an hour count against a named fault, marked evidence of whether it is closing, and an honest recommendation to stop when the marks say the work is finished.

faqs.question: What does an IB Philosophy tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai span roughly AED 45 to 650 an hour, and the spread reflects different products rather than different quality of the same product. Budget online platforms publish from AED 33 to 65. A qualified subject tutor delivering online sits around AED 150 to 300, which is where most families transact. Specialist IB rates run from AED 200 to 450 and above, with one named provider publishing AED 650. Those are each provider's own published figures, read in October 2026, and they are market rates rather than ours. Ask any quote whether essay reading time is billed separately.

faqs.question: Why do some Dubai tutors quote Philosophy above Maths?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, both structural. First, marking time: a Maths exploration can be checked in twenty minutes, while a Philosophy essay takes a tutor about as long to read properly as the student took to write it, so a tutor who includes reading in the rate is doing more unpaid work per billed hour. Second, scarcity: there are far fewer Philosophy specialists than Maths specialists anywhere, and if your school has set a less commonly taught prescribed text the pool shrinks again. Neither reason has anything to do with the subject being harder.

faqs.question: Should we book sixty or ninety minutes for a Philosophy session?
faqs.answer: Ninety, for anything involving essays. Reconstructing an argument, raising an objection, and then rewriting a paragraph in response does not fit into sixty minutes, and sessions that try end with the rewriting set as homework the student will not do. The practical consequence for budgeting is that quotes should be compared per session rather than per hour: a tutor at AED 250 for ninety minutes is cheaper per unit of work than one at AED 200 for sixty. Short sessions do make sense for the Higher Level unseen paper, where the drilling is narrow.

faqs.question: How many Philosophy hours does a Dubai DP2 student actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which fault the student has, which is why the first session should diagnose rather than teach. Technique repairs are cheap: retraining a student who summarises instead of reconstructing takes four to six marked essays. Teaching an untaught optional theme to an examinable standard takes eight to twelve hours. Internal assessment supervision takes four to six hours spread across months. A typical DP2 family buys between fifteen and twenty-five hours in total. A student starting in the final six weeks can still improve technique, but cannot acquire a theme, and should be told so.

faqs.question: Does the quoted AED rate include essay marking between sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, because the answer changes the real price substantially. In Philosophy a full essay takes roughly as long to read and annotate as it took to write, so a tutor quoting AED 200 an hour with marking included may be better value than one quoting AED 150 with reading billed separately. Some providers include a fixed number of marked pieces per month; others bill reading time at the teaching rate. Neither is wrong, but comparing two quotes without knowing which model each uses produces a conclusion that is simply incorrect.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two Philosophy students in one session?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and for some work it is also better: two candidates arguing against each other about whether an objection succeeds is closer to how philosophy is actually done than one student explaining it to an adult. The limits are real though. The internal assessment cannot be supervised in a pair, because the stimulus, the question and the draft are individual. And for a minority subject in Dubai there is often no second candidate available at the same level with the same prescribed text, which ends the discussion before cost enters it.

faqs.question: What does supervising the Philosophy internal assessment add to the cost?
faqs.answer: Typically four to six hours spread over several months, which at published Dubai market rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour is roughly AED 600 to 1,800. The hours are not continuous and that is the point: one to test whether the chosen stimulus yields a philosophical issue at all, one to narrow the question, one or two on choosing philosophers who speak to it, and one to read the student's own draft against the criteria. This should appear as its own line on a quote rather than absorbed into a weekly rate, because it is project supervision rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Does a Philosophy tutor cost more in the final term before exams?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens and rates firm up, but the more important change is that the hours do less. Six weeks out, a student cannot absorb an optional theme they were never taught, so the money buys technique and timing rather than knowledge. The same budget spent in DP1 buys both, plus the prescribed text mapped properly and the internal assessment supervised while it can still be redirected. Families who treat tutoring as an exam-term purchase pay the same rate for a narrower product, which is the most common avoidable waste in this market.

faqs.question: Our budget is AED 200 an hour. What does that buy for IB Philosophy?
faqs.answer: At AED 200 you are inside the published band for a qualified subject tutor delivering online, which in this market runs roughly AED 150 to 300. That buys someone who knows the course, can mark essays against the descriptors, and can take a student through the prescribed text properly. What it will not reliably buy is a named specialist with examining experience on a rarely taught text, where published rates reach AED 450 and above. If your budget is fixed, spend it on the prescribed text block and argument reconstruction first, because those pay across every component.

faqs.question: Can we book a short block rather than commit to a whole term?
faqs.answer: That is the shape we prefer, and it is the shape families should ask every provider for. Philosophy support divides naturally into blocks with a defined end: a prescribed text mapped in six to eight hours, an optional theme made examinable in eight to twelve, a reconstruction habit built in four to six, an internal assessment supervised through its draft round. Each has an agreed hour count before it starts. Open-ended weekly billing is how a family reaches March having spent several thousand dirhams with nothing specific completed.

faqs.question: What is the prescribed text paper in IB Philosophy?
faqs.answer: An essay on a single philosophical text that the school chooses from a published list, studied in depth across the course. The list includes works such as Plato's Republic, Descartes' Meditations, Hume's Enquiry, Mill's On Liberty, Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morality, de Beauvoir's The Second Sex, Confucius' Analects and the Tao Te Ching, among others. It is the most knowable component in the subject, because the argument of a finished book does not change, which makes it the best-value block to buy early and the cheapest place to find marks.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Philosophy at Higher and Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level candidates study two optional themes instead of one and sit an additional paper on unseen material about the nature of philosophical activity itself. Both levels take the compulsory core theme, study a prescribed text, and write the internally assessed stimulus essay. Because the extra components take weight, the first paper carries a smaller share of a Higher Level grade than a Standard Level one. Confirm current weightings with your school's coordinator. For budgeting, Higher Level means a wider scope and a smaller pool of suitable tutors, both of which raise what a good match costs.

faqs.question: What is the Philosophy internal assessment actually about?
faqs.answer: It asks for roughly two thousand words that take a deliberately non-philosophical stimulus, such as a film, an advertisement, a photograph or a news item, and extract and examine a philosophical issue from it. The common failure is choosing a stimulus for interest rather than for yield: a striking image that produces only the thought that identity is complicated has not given the student a question. One that produces a specific, arguable question has. Testing the stimulus for yield before anything is drafted is the single most valuable supervision hour in the subject.

faqs.question: Why is my child's Philosophy essay marked down for summarising?
faqs.answer: Because exposition is not analysis, and the descriptors separate the two sharply. A clear, accurate account of what a philosopher argues sits in the middle bands however well written it is. The marks above that require the argument to be tested: a hidden premise named, an objection raised and answered, and a judgement reached about whether the argument actually succeeds. This is the commonest fault in the subject and also the cheapest to fix, usually four to six marked essays, because it is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

faqs.question: Is Philosophy a risky Group 3 choice for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: It is less predictable than Economics and less content-heavy than History, which cuts both ways. Students who enjoy precise argument often do better here than in a subject that rewards memorised case studies. Students who write fluently but dislike being told their conclusion was not earned find it uncomfortable. Two practical Dubai-specific risks are worth weighing: the option may not run if too few students opt in, and if it does run the prescribed text chosen determines how easy outside support will be to find. Ask the department both questions in Year 11.

faqs.question: How do I check a Dubai Philosophy tutor is permitted to charge for lessons?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation; u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years and that eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. In Abu Dhabi, additional professional-ethics rules restrict school staff from tutoring their own enrolled students.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-online-tutor.closingHeading: Get the hour count before you get the rate
dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-online-tutor.closingBody: The question worth asking a Philosophy tutor is not what they charge but how many hours the specific problem takes and what is included in each one. Send us the prescribed text your child was set, the optional themes, the level, and whether the internal assessment is in scope, and the free diagnostic lesson will give you a named fault, an hour count, and an itemised quote you can compare against anyone else's. One free lesson per student, no card details taken. Lessons run live and one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not visit homes in the Emirates.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Diploma Philosophy at Standard and Higher Level for students in Dubai schools and for candidates studying the subject without a timetabled class. Each one works from the student's own essays, the prescribed text their school has set, and the assessment objectives the examiner marks against.

intro.heading: Pricing a Philosophy tutor in a city that barely timetables the subject
paragraphs: Dubai is the densest private-school market in the UAE. The emirate's media office put the 2024-25 sector at 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of that enrolment. Philosophy is a Group 3 option inside those IB programmes, and only a minority of Dubai's Diploma schools put it on a timetable. That single fact reshapes the search. A parent typing 'IB DP philosophy tutor in Dubai' is not comparing twenty nearby candidates on price; they are usually trying to find out whether anyone in reach teaches the subject at all, and what the answer costs.

Scarcity is what moves the number here, not difficulty. The published rate pages in this market spread very wide. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 for budget online sessions. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level support at AED 200 to 450 and above, with in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are other providers' own figures, read in October 2026, and they are market context rather than an IB Gram price list.

Philosophy quotes sit toward the upper half of that spread for a reason a parent can check. The subject is assessed almost entirely through argued prose written under time pressure, which means the thing being bought is not an explanation of content but a marking relationship. A tutor who teaches Philosophy properly reads a timed essay, marks it against the published assessment objectives, writes an examiner-style comment on where the argument stopped doing work, and then teaches into that specific gap next session. That cycle takes unpaid reading time between lessons. Providers who price only the contact hour either absorb it or quietly stop doing it, and the second outcome is the one that shows in a predicted grade.

Four decisions change a Dubai family's two-year Philosophy bill far more than haggling over an hourly rate ever will. The first is the Group 3 choice itself, made in DP1 before anyone has written a philosophy essay. The second is Standard against Higher Level, because Higher Level adds an unseen paper on the practice of philosophy that almost nobody revises for and that therefore needs its own block of hours. The third is when the internal assessment stimulus gets chosen: a weak stimulus cannot be rescued late, and a late rescue is the single most expensive thing on this page. The fourth is whether the Extended Essay is also in Philosophy, which doubles the supervision load in the same term.

Delivery is online. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school week. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a subject with this few specialists, that is the point rather than a compromise: a Jumeirah or Mirdif family gets a Philosophy teacher who has marked the prescribed text their school set, instead of whichever generalist humanities tutor happens to be a twenty-minute drive away. A tutor here teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work, and never authors any part of an assessed submission.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.programmesIntro: Philosophy sits in Group 3 of the Diploma Programme, but the writing habits it rewards are built earlier and carried into the Diploma core. These are the three programme levels a Dubai family is usually dealing with when they contact us about Philosophy.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme does not teach Philosophy as a named subject, but it is where the argued essay is either learned or missed. Individuals and Societies criteria reward the use of evidence, the weighing of perspectives and a conclusion that follows from what came before. A student who has only ever been marked on describing a source arrives in DP1 able to summarise a philosopher and unable to argue against one, which is exactly the habit that caps a Diploma Philosophy mark at a 4 or a 5.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai IB schools run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11, and a sizeable group of British-curriculum schools run IGCSE instead before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. Either route can lead into Philosophy, but the IGCSE cohort usually arrives with stronger exam timing and weaker practice at holding two positions in tension. We work on the missing half rather than the half the school already built.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Philosophy
programmes.description: Diploma Philosophy is built around a compulsory core theme on what it is to be human, a set of optional themes the school chooses, a prescribed philosophical text, and an internal assessment built from a non-philosophical stimulus. Higher Level adds an unseen paper on the practice of philosophy itself. Confirm the current component structure, durations and weightings with your school's IB coordinator before planning hours against them, because the subject guide is revised on its own cycle.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical question is whether the school runs the subject with a specialist or with a willing humanities teacher covering it alongside History. Both exist in this emirate. Where a specialist is in post, outside help is usually a marking supplement. Where the subject is being covered rather than taught, the tutoring load is closer to a full teaching role, and the hours and therefore the cost roughly double.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and Philosophy overlap in vocabulary and diverge completely in what earns credit. Theory of Knowledge asks how knowledge claims are made and tested across areas of knowledge; Philosophy asks a student to construct and defend a position against the strongest objection available. Students who treat one as the other lose marks in both, and it is the most common cross-subject confusion we see in Dubai Diploma cohorts.
programmes.countryNote: An Extended Essay in Philosophy is a real option for a Dubai student and a demanding one, because the supervisor cannot supply the argument and the library resources available locally skew toward secondary commentary. Supervision through us is structured as questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts, with the school's registered supervisor remaining the person who signs the work off.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.subjectsIntro: Philosophy is rarely the only subject a Dubai family is thinking about. These are the related Diploma courses our tutors cover for the same students, with the specific demand each one makes.

subjects.name: Philosophy
subjects.description: Assessed through argued essays on the core theme, the optional themes and a prescribed text, plus an internal assessment built from a stimulus. Marks are lost on exposition that never becomes argument, and on objections raised and then not answered. Higher Level adds an unseen paper about the practice of philosophy.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The Group 3 subject Dubai students most often choose instead of Philosophy. It rewards study citation, research method critique and ethical evaluation. It is a heavier memory load and a lighter argument load, and the tutor pool in this emirate is noticeably deeper, which shows in the quotes families receive.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Shares Philosophy's demand for conceptual precision and adds a case-study burden. Students are marked on the use of political concepts such as sovereignty, legitimacy and power rather than on narrative. The Higher Level extension asks for an oral presentation of a case study, which rewards different practice from essay work.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The closest neighbour to Philosophy in writing style and the furthest in method. History marks the handling of evidence and historiography; Philosophy marks the handling of argument. Students who move between the two often import the wrong habit, writing philosophy essays that catalogue thinkers' views as if they were sources.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Frequently paired with Philosophy by Dubai students aiming at politics, philosophy and economics degrees. Diagram accuracy and definitional precision carry the marks, with a portfolio of internal assessment commentaries built from real news articles. The skills transfer less than families expect, so hours rarely substitute between the two.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: A newer Group 3 course that some Dubai schools added in place of Information Technology in a Global Society. It asks for inquiry into real digital contexts and rewards claim-and-evidence writing closer to Philosophy than to Psychology, which makes it a sensible fallback for a student who wanted Philosophy and could not get it timetabled.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The most heavily subscribed Group 3 option across Dubai Diploma cohorts, which is why it is the easiest to find help for. Tools, stakeholder analysis and a research project carry the assessment. Students considering it against Philosophy should compare the writing styles, because one rewards structure and the other rewards scrutiny.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Where a Philosophy student's close-reading skill either exists or does not. The guided textual analysis rewards attention to how a text makes its claim, which is the same move Paper 2 of Philosophy asks for on a prescribed philosophical text. We often run the two together for the same student.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A compulsory essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Marked on the quality of discussion of knowledge questions, not on philosophical sophistication. Philosophy students tend to over-argue it and lose marks for not addressing the prescribed title as written.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A four-thousand-word independent research essay in a chosen subject. In Philosophy it needs a question narrow enough to be argued rather than surveyed. Supervision is coaching and questioning on the student's own drafts; the argument and the prose remain entirely the student's.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so the area a family lives in does not change who is available to teach. It does change the school their child attends, the traffic that decides when a session can start, and how much of the subject the school is actually covering.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Served by one of the emirate's longest-running Diploma cohorts, where Group 3 provision is usually broad enough to include Philosophy with a subject specialist. Families here most often want marking volume and Higher Level unseen-paper practice rather than teaching from scratch.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills
regions.note: A dense cluster of IB and British schools within a few kilometres. Several run the Diploma with Philosophy as an option subject in alternate years depending on uptake, so a Year 12 student may find the course withdrawn before DP2. That is the scenario that pushes a family into full outside provision.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Older villa communities feeding a mix of Diploma and A Level schools. Afternoon traffic along Al Wasl and Jumeirah Beach Road routinely pushes a 16:00 start to 17:00 for anything requiring travel, which is one reason online slots fill first in this stretch.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lake Towers
regions.note: Apartment living, long commutes and a high share of expatriate Diploma students arriving mid-programme from other systems. Mid-year transfers into Philosophy are common here, and they need the core theme rebuilt quickly rather than revised.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: A large catchment of Indian-, British- and IB-curriculum schools where Group 3 choices tend toward Business Management and Economics. A Philosophy student in this area is often the only one in their year, which changes what tutoring has to replace.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several universities and a set of schools running the Diploma alongside other curricula. Students here frequently ask how a Philosophy grade reads to a UAE admissions office, because the campus is on their doorstep and the question is concrete.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Sports City
regions.note: Villa communities with long school runs and a heavy co-curricular load, so sessions here usually settle on weekend mornings or after 19:00 on weekdays. Essay marking between sessions matters more where contact hours are hard to schedule.

regions.name: Downtown, Business Bay and Al Quoz
regions.note: A mixed residential and studio district where Diploma students often combine Philosophy with Visual Arts or Film. The cross-subject work is useful: a student who can read an image closely usually reads a prescribed philosophical text better than one who cannot.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB World Schools running the full Diploma
schoolClusters.note: These schools run the Diploma Programme and are inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Group 3 provision varies between them year to year, and Philosophy is the option most often affected by uptake. Ask the coordinator directly whether the course will run to DP2 before choosing it.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools where Diploma students sit alongside other curricula
schoolClusters.note: Several Dubai schools run the Diploma next to a British or American track in the same building. Timetable pressure in these schools falls hardest on small option subjects, which is why a Philosophy student here is often studying with a teacher whose main subject is History or English.

dubai/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.modesIntro: Philosophy support is bought in blocks, not open-ended retainers, because the subject has a small number of discrete things that go wrong. These are the four blocks Dubai families actually book, and what each one is for.

modes.title: Weekly essay cycle
modes.description: The standard arrangement through DP1 and the first half of DP2. The student writes one timed essay a week on the core theme or an optional theme, the tutor marks it against the published assessment objectives before the next session, and the lesson is spent teaching into the specific failure the script shows. Progress is visible because the marked scripts accumulate in one place and can be read in sequence.

modes.title: Higher Level unseen-paper block
modes.description: A short intensive block aimed only at the Higher Level paper on the practice of philosophy. It is the component most Dubai students have done least practice on, because schools understandably spend their time on the themes and the prescribed text. Six to ten sessions on unseen extracts, with each one written under time and marked, usually moves this component more than any other single intervention.

modes.description: Booked when the stimulus is being chosen, which is the point at which the grade is largely decided. A stimulus that yields only one obvious philosophical question produces an essay with nowhere to go. Sessions interrogate the candidate's shortlist, test which stimulus supports a genuine problem, and then give feedback on the student's own drafts without touching the prose.

modes.title: Pre-session revision sprint
modes.description: A four to six week block in the term before the May session, built entirely around timed writing. The aim is throughput: more essays written under clock pressure than the school can realistically set and mark. Sessions are short, marking turnaround is fast, and the content work is restricted to the themes the student's own scripts keep failing on.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family is actually buying when they price Philosophy help
paragraphs: A Philosophy hour is not one product. It is four, and providers price them as if they were interchangeable, which is why two quotes for the same subject in the same emirate can differ by a factor of ten. Separating them is the single most useful thing a parent can do before paying anyone, because three of the four cost real time outside the lesson and the fourth does not.

The first purchase is teaching: someone explains the core theme, the optional themes the school has chosen, and the argumentative moves the subject expects. A capable graduate can do this. The second is marking: a timed essay is read, scored against the published assessment objectives, and returned with a comment that identifies where the argument stopped doing work. This requires someone who has marked the subject and it takes forty minutes per script that nobody sees. The third is prescribed-text work, which depends entirely on which text the school has set and cannot be delivered generically. The fourth is internal assessment supervision, which is mostly questioning and is bounded by IB academic-honesty rules.

Ask any prospective tutor which of the four their quoted rate covers. A rate that includes marking turnaround will be higher per hour and lower per mark gained. A rate that covers contact time only is cheaper and leaves the most valuable work undone, because in a subject assessed through argued prose the marked script is the teaching material. The table below sets out the four purchases, what each looks like when it is being done properly, and the question that tests whether it is included.
bullets: Teaching the themes: explainable by a strong graduate, cheapest of the four
Marking timed essays: the component that actually moves a grade

sections.heading: Group 3 in Dubai: the choice that sets the two-year bill
paragraphs: The biggest number in a Dubai Philosophy budget is fixed in DP1, before a single essay is written, by the Group 3 choice. Tutor supply in this emirate is uneven across the group, and supply sets price far more firmly than content difficulty does. Business Management and Economics are taught in almost every Diploma school here and supported by a deep local tutoring market. Philosophy is taught in a minority of them and supported by very few people, so quotes for it cluster at the specialist end of the published bands rather than the mid band.

That is worth saying plainly because the usual explanation offered to parents, that Philosophy is harder, is not the real mechanism. A Psychology student carries a heavier recall load than a Philosophy student does. What Philosophy carries is a narrower pool of people who can mark it, and the published rate pages show what a narrow pool does to a price. Bestimate's Dubai table puts specialist IB support at AED 200 to 450 and above, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online; Philosophy sits in the first band and Business Management frequently in the second.

The switching cost matters too. A student who abandons Philosophy in the middle of DP1 has to rebuild a different Group 3 course from scratch while carrying five other subjects, and that rebuild is the most expensive tutoring any family on this page will buy. The practical conclusion is unglamorous: decide Group 3 with the real rates and the real provision in front of you, confirm with the coordinator that the course will actually run to DP2, and treat a mid-programme switch as a last resort rather than a correction.

sections.heading: Timed writing is the product, and it is the thing nobody practises enough
paragraphs: Diploma Philosophy is examined by essay under clock pressure. A student who understands the material and has written four essays in two years will be beaten by a student who understands it less well and has written forty. This is not a motivational point, it is an arithmetic one: the examinable skill is producing a structured argument against an unseen prompt inside a fixed number of minutes, and that skill only responds to repetition under the same constraint.

Dubai schools cannot generate that volume. A teacher with a Diploma class, a Middle Years timetable and internal assessment supervision cannot mark two essays per student per week, and should not be expected to. The gap between what the examination rewards and what a school can physically mark is the clearest honest case for outside help in this subject, and it is also the thing to buy first. Everything else, including content revision, is downstream of it.

Confirm the current paper structure, durations and weightings with your school's IB coordinator before you plan hours against them, because the subject guide is revised on its own cycle and no figure on a tutoring page should be treated as the source. What does not change is the practice requirement. A student aiming at the top bands needs planning time rehearsed to the minute, a default essay shape they can deploy without thinking, and the experience of having run out of time in a practice essay rather than in the real one.

The internal check we use is simple. By the February mock of DP2, a student should be able to plan an essay on an unfamiliar prompt in under eight minutes and name, unprompted, the strongest objection to their own position. A student who can do both is in a different band from a student who can do neither, and the difference was built by volume of marked writing rather than by additional reading.

sections.heading: Command terms and assessment objectives: where a Philosophy mark actually comes from
paragraphs: Most mid-band Philosophy scripts we read in Dubai are not wrong. They are off-task. The student has written a competent account of what two philosophers think and the prompt asked them to evaluate a claim, so the marks available for argument were never in play. Command terms are the mechanism by which an examiner decides which marks a script is even eligible for, and they are taught far less often than content is.

The fix is mechanical and quick, which makes it the best value work on this page. A student learns what each command term obliges them to produce, writes a paragraph that produces exactly that, and has it marked. Two or three sessions on command terms typically does more for a 4 or a 5 than a term of content revision, because the content was usually already there. What was missing was the obligation being met.

The table below lists the command terms that appear most often in Philosophy prompts, what the examiner is looking for behind each one, the shortfall we see most frequently in Dubai scripts, and what a session actually does about it. Use it as a checklist against your child's last returned essay: in most cases the mismatch between the verb in the question and the verb the script performed is visible in the first paragraph.

One caution. Command-term lists circulate widely online and not all of them match the current guide. Check the wording against the subject guide your school is teaching from, through the coordinator, rather than against a revision site.

sections.heading: When a Dubai school does not run Philosophy: the routes, priced honestly
paragraphs: A recurring message we get from Dubai parents reads roughly the same each time: our child wants Philosophy, the school does not offer it, what are our options? The honest answer is that the options are narrower than the internet suggests, and the narrowness is worth understanding before money is spent, because one of the routes families ask about most often is not available at all.

IB Diploma registration runs through an IB World School. Unlike Cambridge, which allows private candidates to enter through an approved examination centre, the Diploma is not something a student can sit independently alongside a school that does not teach it. Confirm the current position with your school's IB coordinator or the regional IB office before relying on any route, including this one. What that rules out in practice is the arrangement parents most often propose: keep the school place, buy the teaching privately, and enter the exam separately.

What remains is a short list. The student can take a Group 3 subject the school does run and read Philosophy seriously outside the Diploma, which costs little and earns nothing on the transcript. They can move to a Dubai school that timetables it, which is a school-fee decision rather than a tutoring one and sits inside a market where KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. They can ask whether the school will run the subject as a supported self-study option with an internal teacher of record, which some Dubai schools will do for a determined student and which is where private tutoring genuinely substitutes for a class. Or they can choose Philosophy as the Extended Essay subject, which gets the thinking without the timetable.

sections.heading: Writing philosophy in English when English is the second or third language
paragraphs: A large share of Dubai's Diploma cohort writes its examinations in English while speaking something else at home. In most subjects that shows up as slower reading. In Philosophy it shows up somewhere more awkward: the subject's marks depend on small logical connectives, and the words that carry them are exactly the ones that language learners use loosely. The difference between 'therefore', 'nevertheless', 'granted that' and 'in so far as' is the difference between an argument and a sequence of assertions, and an examiner reads the connective rather than the intention behind it.

This is coachable and it is not an English lesson. The work is a short, closed set of argumentative phrases, practised until they are automatic, paired with a habit of reading one's own paragraph and asking what each connective is claiming about the relationship between two sentences. Students who do this stop writing paragraphs that end weaker than they began. It takes a handful of sessions and it is often the fastest visible improvement in a returned script.

There is a scheduling dimension too. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction for each. For an Arabic-first student those lessons are additional contact hours in an already full Diploma week, and Philosophy tutoring has to be scheduled around them rather than on top of them. We plan the week with the school timetable in front of us for that reason.

One thing we do not do is rewrite prose. A tutor who smooths a student's sentences has taken ownership of the writing, which is both a disservice and an honesty problem. The feedback names the logical gap and leaves the repair to the student, every time.

sections.heading: What a Philosophy grade does for a university route, in the UAE and outside it
paragraphs: Parents ask whether Philosophy closes doors. The accurate answer distinguishes three different gates, and conflating them is what produces the bad advice circulating in Dubai parent groups. The first gate is the degree's own subject prerequisites. The second is the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process, which is about the certificate rather than the subject. The third is admissions judgement, which is about the whole application.

On prerequisites, Philosophy is not a substitute for a science or for Mathematics. A student aiming at medicine, engineering or most quantitative degrees needs the relevant subjects at the relevant level, and Philosophy neither helps nor hurts that requirement. For law, politics, international relations, economics with a philosophy component, and anything requiring an admissions essay or interview, it is a genuinely strong subject, because the thing it trains is the thing those processes test.

On equivalency, the published rules are specific for the British and American tracks and were reported in July 2026. A British-track applicant must show five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. An American-track applicant must show English proficiency at IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics. One ranking competitor publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five. No IB points threshold has been verified for this page, so none is published here. Check the current requirement on the Ministry's own channels before relying on it, and note that equivalency is a process families complete with the authority directly, not something a tutoring service performs on their behalf.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a subject where the work is the argument
paragraphs: In a subject assessed through prose, the line between help and malpractice is finer than in a subject assessed through calculation, and it is crossed more often by accident. A tutor who suggests a thesis has supplied the student's position. A tutor who reorders paragraphs has supplied the structure. Neither is dramatic, and both are a problem, because the internal assessment and the Extended Essay are submitted as the student's own work and the IB treats authorship seriously.

Our working rule is that a tutor may ask any question and may not supply any sentence. That rule survives contact with reality better than longer policies do. It means the tutor can ask what the strongest objection to a claim is, whether a stimulus actually generates a philosophical problem, where a paragraph stops arguing, and what a word in the prompt is doing. It means the tutor does not propose the thesis, does not draft or redraft the prose, does not restructure the student's document, and does not supply a reading that the student then cites without having read it.

There is a second honesty question specific to the present moment, which is generative text. A paragraph produced by a language model and then lightly edited is not the student's work, and in Philosophy it is unusually easy for a reader to notice, because such paragraphs are fluent and argumentatively inert. They state positions, balance them, and commit to nothing, which is exactly the profile of a mid-band script. Where a student has used any such tool, the school's own policy on acknowledgement applies and the coordinator is the person to ask.

The same restraint applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are the board's copyright and the school's to distribute. We reference them, cite the official source, and link out, which is also what the examination boards ask of anyone writing about their qualifications.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and how these lessons actually run
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service called Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the ministry's app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here.

Two further points are worth a Dubai parent's attention. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not hold such a permit and does not operate premises in the UAE, and no page of ours should be read as claiming regulator endorsement of any kind. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way. The practical implication for any emirate is that a family should not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by their own class teacher.

Delivery is online. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, screen-shared, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and recorded or summarised depending on the family's preference. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Philosophy that limitation costs a Dubai family nothing and gains them access to specialists who could never be inside commuting distance of Mirdif or Arabian Ranches at four in the afternoon.

If no Philosophy specialist is free in the slot you want, we say so rather than substituting a general humanities tutor and hoping. Where we can offer an adjacent specialist who can teach the essay method while you wait for the subject slot, we explain exactly what that person can and cannot cover. A free trial lesson comes first in every case, with no card required to book it.

That single document tells a specialist more than a conversation about aims does, because it shows whether the problem is content, command terms, timing or structure.

process.title: We confirm whether a specialist is genuinely free
process.description: Philosophy is a thin-supply subject in the UAE, so we check availability against the specific slot you need in Gulf Standard Time before promising anything. If nobody suitable is free, we tell you that and say when a slot is likely rather than offering a general humanities tutor as a silent substitute.

No card is required to book it, and nothing is charged if you decide not to continue. You see how the tutor marks, which is the part of the relationship that matters most in this subject.

The AED context on this page is market data from published sources; your own quote is set in the consultation rather than from a rate card.

process.title: Marked scripts accumulate where you can read them
process.description: Every timed essay comes back scored with a comment, and the scripts stay together in sequence. Parents who want evidence rather than reassurance read three consecutive essays and see whether the same fault keeps appearing. That is also how we decide when a block has done its work and should stop.

whyPoints.title: Rates on the page, with the source and the date
whyPoints.description: Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. We publish the AED bands other providers advertise, attribute them, and date them to October 2026, so a Dubai parent can see where a quote sits before they take a call.

whyPoints.title: A specialist, or an honest no
whyPoints.description: Philosophy has few Diploma-level teachers in this region. Where one is free for your slot we say so; where none is, we say that too. The alternative, quietly assigning a generalist and letting a parent find out in week three, is how this market earns its reputation.

whyPoints.title: Marking is the product, not an extra
whyPoints.description: A Philosophy grade moves when timed essays are written and marked in volume. Our blocks are built around that cycle rather than around contact hours, and the marked scripts are the deliverable a parent can actually inspect.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry or examination-board approval and claims none. Every figure on this page is attributed to the source it came from, and where a number could not be verified, including IB session dates, it is left out.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools actually timetable Diploma Philosophy?
faqs.answer: Fewer than parents expect. Philosophy is a Group 3 option, and in Dubai it tends to run in the larger, longer-established Diploma cohorts where a class of eight or ten students is viable, while smaller cohorts fill Group 3 with Business Management, Economics and Psychology. Provision also moves year to year with uptake, so a subject offered to Year 11 at options evening can be withdrawn before DP1 starts. Ask the IB coordinator two questions directly: is Philosophy running this year, and what is the minimum class size at which it would be withdrawn. Get the answer before you build a subject plan around it.

faqs.question: What should we budget for two years of Philosophy support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on whether the school teaches the subject. Where a specialist is in post and outside help is a marking supplement, one session a week through DP1 and DP2 at the published Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour puts the recurring cost in the AED 800 to 1,800 a month range, with heavier blocks before mocks. Where the school is covering rather than teaching the subject, two to three hours a week is realistic and the figure roughly doubles. Those bands are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list; your own quote comes from the consultation.

faqs.question: Is Philosophy a sensible Group 3 choice next to Psychology or Global Politics?
faqs.answer: It is sensible for a student who enjoys being argued with and risky for one who prefers material that can be learned. Philosophy rewards the construction and defence of a position; Psychology rewards accurate recall of studies and methodological critique; Global Politics rewards concepts applied to cases. The honest discriminator is not interest but writing. Ask your child to write four hundred words defending a claim they hold against the strongest objection they can find. If that is enjoyable, Philosophy will suit them. If it is miserable, Psychology is the better two-year investment and the local tutoring market is far deeper.

faqs.question: How many marked essays should come back each month?
faqs.answer: On a weekly block, four, one per session, each written under exam timing and returned scored with a comment before the next lesson. In a pre-session sprint, eight. Below about three a month the practice volume is too low to shift a grade, whatever the quality of the teaching, because the examinable skill is producing argument under time pressure and that only responds to repetition. If a provider cannot tell you how many scripts will come back marked per month, you are buying contact hours rather than progress, and in this subject those are not the same purchase.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IB Philosophy as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Diploma registration runs through an IB World School, which rules out the arrangement families most often propose: keep the current school place, buy the teaching privately, and enter the examination separately. This differs from Cambridge, where private candidates can enter through an approved examination centre. Confirm the current position with your school's IB coordinator or the regional IB office before planning around it, because the rules on registration and on anticipated and retake entries are the board's to state and not a tutoring site's. In practice, the workable routes are school-supported self-study with an internal teacher of record, or a school transfer.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Philosophy change the hourly rate we should expect?
faqs.answer: Not usually the rate, but almost always the hours. Higher Level adds a paper on the practice of philosophy worked from unseen material, and it is the component Dubai students have typically written least for, because schools reasonably spend their time on the themes and the prescribed text. Budget a separate block of six to ten sessions for it rather than assuming weekly lessons will absorb the extra demand. Confirm the current Higher Level component structure and weighting with your coordinator, since the subject guide is revised on its own cycle and no figure from a tutoring page should be treated as authoritative.

faqs.question: My son writes well in English but keeps scoring a 4 in Philosophy. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the essays are off-task rather than wrong. Fluent writers produce balanced accounts of what philosophers think, and the prompts ask for evaluation, discussion or justification, which oblige a judgement and a response to the strongest objection. The marks for argument are therefore never in play. Read his last script and check whether the final paragraph commits to anything. If it summarises, that is the problem, and it is a fast fix: two or three sessions on command terms and paragraph obligations typically moves a script more than a term of additional reading does.

faqs.question: How long before the May session is it still worth starting Philosophy help?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is enough to change timing, essay shape and command-term accuracy, which is a real improvement and the fastest available. It is not enough to repair a weak internal assessment, because that document will already be with the school. So the answer depends on which component is the problem. If the papers are the weakness, a short intensive sprint of two marked timed essays a week is worth starting late. If the internal assessment is the weakness and the school deadline has passed, say so at the consultation and we will plan around the papers instead of selling hours that cannot help.

faqs.question: What does the assessment objective wording actually oblige a student to do?
faqs.answer: It tells the examiner which marks a script is eligible for, which is why an off-task essay cannot reach the top bands however well written it is. In practice each prompt verb carries an obligation: evaluate requires a judgement with the counter-position addressed, analyse requires the load-bearing assumption identified, to what extent requires a calibrated answer rather than a yes or a no. We teach these as mechanical obligations first and nuance second, because the mechanical version is what recovers marks quickly. Check the current wording through your school's coordinator rather than from a revision website, as circulating lists are often out of date.

faqs.question: Can Philosophy be the Extended Essay subject, and what does supervision involve?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it suits students who want the subject without the timetable. The difficulty is the question: philosophy essays fail when the question is broad enough to survey rather than narrow enough to argue. Supervision through us is questioning and written feedback on the student's own drafts, never proposing the thesis or redrafting the prose, and your school's registered supervisor remains the person who signs the work off. Budget supervision across two terms rather than a burst near the deadline, since the expensive failure in this component is a question that cannot be argued and is only discovered late.

faqs.question: Does the subject my child picks affect UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is assessed on the certificate rather than on which Group 3 option was chosen. For the British track the reported rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects; the sourced figure is five. No verified IB points threshold exists for this page, so none is published. Check the current requirement on the Ministry's own channels, and note that equivalency is something families complete with the authority, not something a tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: Our daughter studies Arabic as a first language too. How does the week fit together?
faqs.answer: Carefully, and with the school timetable in front of us. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. For an Arabic-first student those are additional contact hours inside an already full Diploma week. We schedule Philosophy around them rather than on top of them, usually one later weekday slot plus a weekend morning, and we keep the written work to one timed essay a week so the load is predictable rather than variable.

faqs.question: What exactly can a Philosophy tutor do with the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Ask questions and give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor can interrogate a stimulus shortlist, test whether a candidate's question is arguable, point out where a paragraph stops doing argumentative work, and explain how the word allocation usually breaks down between stimulus analysis and the argument itself. A tutor cannot propose the thesis, cannot draft or redraft the prose, cannot restructure the document, and cannot supply a reading for the student to cite unread. Our rule is that a tutor may ask any question and may not supply any sentence. Ask any prospective tutor what they will refuse to do, and be wary if the answer is nothing.

faqs.question: Do online lessons work for a subject built on discussion?
faqs.answer: They work well, because the discussion in Diploma Philosophy is one-to-one rather than seminar-shaped. A shared screen with the student's own script on it is arguably better than a kitchen table: both parties annotate the same document, the marked version is saved rather than lost, and the tutor can pull up the prompt wording mid-argument. What online cannot replicate is the corridor conversation and the classroom of eight disagreeing peers. Where a Dubai student has no class at all, we partly compensate by running sessions as sustained argument rather than exposition, which is also what the examination rewards.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with Dubai students need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private lessons in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, the eligible categories include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18, and the application runs through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service for private tutor licensing. Those without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here. Ask any tutor directly, and ask a UAE-resident tutor to show their permit.

faqs.question: What happens if no Philosophy specialist is free at our preferred hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when a slot is likely rather than filling it quietly. Philosophy has a thin specialist pool across this region, so an honest wait of two or three weeks for the right person is a better outcome than a general humanities tutor assigned without comment. Where it helps, we will say what an adjacent specialist could usefully cover in the meantime, which is usually essay method, command terms and timing rather than the prescribed text. Nothing is charged while you wait, and the free trial lesson still comes first when the slot opens.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The specialists below teach Higher Level physics on the current syllabus: the five themes with their additional Higher Level content, the data-analysis questions in Paper 1B, the extended responses in Paper 2, and the scientific investigation marked against four criteria. Each profile names the courses and levels taught.

intro.heading: The physics course changed, and most tutoring advice has not caught up
paragraphs: Higher Level physics in the Diploma was restructured for first teaching in 2023 and first examinations in May 2025, and the change was not cosmetic. The options are gone. Paper 3 is gone. The course is now organised into five themes, each with additional Higher Level content layered on a shared core, and the assessment is two written papers plus the scientific investigation. Any tutor, revision guide or well-meaning relative still talking about choosing an option or preparing for Paper 3 is describing the previous course.

What replaced it is a tighter structure that concentrates risk. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent of the grade and comes in two parts: Paper 1A, which is multiple choice, and Paper 1B, which is built from data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and runs for two and a half hours at Higher Level, in short-answer and extended-response form. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent, is marked out of 24 against four criteria of six marks each, and is limited to 3,000 words.

The practical consequence is that two of the three components now examine experimental skill directly. Paper 1B asks students to read data, work with uncertainties, extract gradients with their units, and judge whether a conclusion is supported. The scientific investigation asks for the same skills in a longer form. A student who is strong on theory and weak on uncertainties used to lose a handful of marks; on the current syllabus that weakness touches well over a third of the available grade, which is why we test it in the first fortnight rather than the final term.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video with the student's working visible. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubai address; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Higher Level physics the trade is clear-cut. The number of people in any single Dubai community who teach HL physics on the current syllabus is small, and smaller again if the requirement is someone who can mark a data-analysis question properly. Limiting the shortlist to those who can drive to your villa by half past five generally means accepting a general science tutor instead.

Dubai's scale produces the isolation families describe. KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils in 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the IB at 7 per cent of enrolment, and seven new schools open for 2026-27 including three International Baccalaureate schools, adding 16,846 places. Even so, a given school may enter six or eight candidates for Higher Level physics in a year. One teacher, one scheme of work, one laboratory timetable. If the gap is in field theory or in propagating an uncertainty through a calculation, there is rarely anybody with spare capacity to close it.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level physics is built on habits formed in middle-years science and in whatever pre-Diploma course a student took. Here is what each programme contributes and the Dubai-specific thing to watch.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics at Higher Level is one of three HL subjects in a full Diploma, with 240 recommended hours against 150 at Standard Level. The guide sets aside an experimental programme of 60 hours at Higher Level, which includes the scientific investigation and the collaborative sciences project, so a substantial share of the course is time in a laboratory rather than at a desk.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sit the May session almost without exception. The IB publishes and occasionally revises session windows, upload deadlines and results dates, so take those from your school's Diploma coordinator rather than from any tutoring site. The dates that govern a tutoring plan are the school's internal deadlines for the investigation, which normally fall a term before anything external.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP sciences assess four criteria, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, is the direct ancestor of Paper 1B and of the scientific investigation. A student with strong criterion A marks and weak criterion C marks will arrive in Higher Level physics able to recall theory and unable to handle a data set, which is now a large share of the examination.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai continuum schools take students straight from MYP sciences into the Diploma with no external science examination in between. Asking the school for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the overall MYP grade is the most useful diagnostic a parent can obtain before DP1 begins, and almost nobody asks for it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP science is inquiry-led, with measurement, fair testing and recording what actually happened rather than what was expected appearing early. Those are the foundations of experimental physics, and a child who learns to write down an anomalous reading instead of quietly discarding it is practising the skill the scientific investigation rewards a decade later.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA inspects annually and comments on attainment and progress separately by subject. For a parent thinking long-term, the science progress judgement in a primary report describes the teaching group a child is actually in, which is more informative than the school's overall inspection band.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes with additional Higher Level content, examined through Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data analysis and a two-and-a-half-hour Paper 2, plus the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Marks are lost most consistently on uncertainties, on gradients quoted without units, and on command terms read as synonyms.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same five themes without the additional Higher Level content, with a shorter Paper 1 and a ninety-minute Paper 2, and the same scientific investigation requirement. A student moving down from Higher Level keeps the experimental programme and loses the extension content in each theme.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most common pairing. Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities all appear in physics, and students who treat the two subjects as separate lose physics marks to algebra they can demonstrably do. Paper 1 at Higher Level in maths permits no calculator, which is worth knowing when planning revision.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A calculator is assumed in every paper, and the statistics and data-handling content maps neatly onto Paper 1B in physics. The algebraic manipulation in physics Paper 2 is usually the harder adjustment for an Applications student, and naming that early prevents a slow surprise in DP2.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the 2023 science assessment model: Paper 1A, Paper 1B, Paper 2 and the same scientific investigation criteria. Energetics and kinetics overlap with thermal physics. A student doing both sciences can prepare the investigation skills once and spend the saving on content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Also on the 2023 model, with Paper 1B data analysis and the same four investigation criteria. The statistical treatment expected in biology data questions is heavier than in physics, which is useful experience for the physics investigation's evaluation criterion.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1, Paper 2 and a solution-development internal assessment. Physics students handle the logic and algorithmic content comfortably, and lose marks on the extended-response questions about system design, which reward structured writing rather than technical knowledge.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Shares an evidence-gathering and evaluation mindset with physics, and the internal assessment is substantial. Students taking both frequently underestimate how much coursework lands in the same term, which is a scheduling problem a tutoring plan has to work around.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece. A physics Extended Essay needs a question answerable with the equipment and data genuinely available, and the commonest failure is an ambitious topic with no feasible method, which is a problem best caught at the proposal stage rather than in the second term.

sections.heading: What a Higher Level physics home tutor search in Dubai is really asking
paragraphs: Specialist IB tuition in Dubai is published at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above, and Higher Level physics sits at the top of that band because the supply of tutors is genuinely thin. IB Gram delivers it as one-to-one tuition over live video to every community in the emirate. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. That is stated before money is discussed rather than buried in a footer.

The home-tutoring question still deserves a proper answer. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel embedded in the rate, and monthly packages of about AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits are widely advertised. For some students the premium is worth paying: a younger child who will not work unsupervised, a household where the only device is shared, a learner who finds a screen a genuine obstacle rather than an inconvenience.

A Higher Level physics candidate is rarely in that position. What they need is somebody who can look at a graph with error bars and say why the gradient has been quoted without units, or explain what the additional Higher Level content in the fields theme is actually asking, or mark an extended response against the command term it used rather than against the facts it contained. Those are syllabus-specific capabilities. A tutor either holds them or does not, and the distance from their home to yours is irrelevant to the question.

There is a practical point about marking that follows from the delivery model. Data-analysis questions take longer to mark than theory questions, because the marker has to follow the uncertainty arithmetic and check the graph work line by line. That happens between sessions and nobody travels for it. A tutor who spends ninety minutes a day in Dubai traffic has less of that time, not more, and marking is the first thing to go when an evening overruns.

sections.heading: The 2023 syllabus: what changed, and why old advice is actively misleading
paragraphs: Until the 2023 syllabus, Higher Level physics was assessed through three written papers and an option chosen from a list, with Paper 3 covering the option alongside data analysis. Students chose between relativity, engineering physics, imaging and astrophysics, and a substantial amount of tutoring in this market was built around that choice. The current course has no options and no Paper 3. First examinations on the new structure were sat in May 2025.

The content is now organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Each theme carries a shared core plus additional Higher Level content, which replaces the old core-plus-additional-higher-level-topics arrangement with something more integrated. A theme is taught as one body of work, and the Higher Level extension sits inside it rather than being bolted on at the end of the year.

Assessment is now two papers and the investigation. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and is sat in two parts: Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, a set of data-based and experimental questions drawing on the skills developed in the practical programme. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and runs for two and a half hours at Higher Level, with short-answer and extended-response questions. The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent at both levels.

Why this matters for choosing a tutor: a great deal of material circulating online, including revision sites, second-hand textbooks and the advice of older siblings, still describes the previous structure. A student who spends a term preparing for an options paper is preparing for an examination that will not be set. The first question worth asking any physics tutor in this market is which themes they have taught and how they prepare students for Paper 1B, and a confident answer to the second half of that question is rarer than it should be.
