sections.heading: Paper 1B: the paper nobody prepares for properly
paragraphs: Paper 1B is the component that most reliably separates students in the current syllabus, and it is the one least likely to have been rehearsed. It presents data, often from an experiment the student has not performed, and asks them to work with it: read values from a table or a graph, propagate an uncertainty, determine a gradient and state its units, decide whether a stated conclusion is supported by the evidence, and identify the limitation that matters most.

The marks are lost in a short and highly repeatable list. A gradient calculated correctly and quoted without units. An uncertainty given to three significant figures when the measurement justifies one. A percentage uncertainty added when it should have been combined through a power. An anomalous point noted and then included in the line of best fit anyway. A conclusion that restates the trend instead of evaluating whether the data supports it. Each of these is worth one or two marks, and together they routinely cost a capable student eight or ten.

None of that list is conceptually difficult, which is exactly why it persists. Students who understand physics well assume these are presentational details rather than examined content, and nobody corrects the assumption until a mock paper comes back. The fix is drill: a fortnightly data question marked strictly, with the same errors flagged until they stop appearing. It is unglamorous work and it moves marks faster than any theory teaching available at this stage.

The same skills reappear in the scientific investigation, which is the second reason to treat them as a strand in their own right. A student who can propagate uncertainties properly and evaluate a data set honestly is earning marks in two components worth 56 per cent of the grade between them. We pre-test this in the first fortnight with every new Higher Level physics student, because the result determines the shape of the whole block.

sections.heading: Paper 2 at Higher Level: two and a half hours and 44 per cent
paragraphs: Paper 2 is the largest single component in the course, carrying 44 per cent of the grade over two and a half hours at Higher Level. It mixes short-answer questions with extended responses across all five themes, and it rewards two things that are trainable independently of physics knowledge: reading the command term accurately, and writing the amount the mark allocation implies.

Command terms are not synonyms and the mark scheme does not treat them as such. "State" wants a one-line answer and no justification. "Describe" wants what happens without why. "Explain" requires a causal chain, and a response that describes beautifully without explaining collects none of the explanation marks. "Outline" sits between describe and explain. "Determine" requires working shown. Students who answer the physics they recognise rather than the question that was asked lose marks they had the knowledge to earn, which is the most frustrating category of loss on any script.

The second trainable habit is proportioning. A four-mark question wants four distinct creditable points, not one point written four ways. Students chronically overwrite on the first extended response, run short of time by the final theme, and leave a six-mark question half-attempted. Timing on this paper is not a revision topic; it is a technique that has to be practised against a clock, with the pacing rule written down and applied.

The physics itself still has to be there, and at Higher Level the additional content in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics is where the heaviest losses sit. Gravitational and electric field work with potential and potential energy, magnetic field direction with the right-hand rule applied consistently, and the photoelectric effect read from a graph rather than recalled from a formula sheet: these are the units students most often need rebuilt rather than revised, and they take four to six sessions each.

sections.heading: The five themes, and where Higher Level marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Each theme in the current syllabus carries a shared core and additional Higher Level content, and the losses in each are specific enough to be diagnosed from a marked script. Space, time and motion holds the kinematics and dynamics most students arrive comfortable with, and then adds momentum and impulse with sign conventions that trip up anybody treating velocity as a magnitude. Circular motion free-body diagrams are the other recurring casualty, usually because a centripetal force is drawn as an extra arrow rather than identified among the forces already present.

The particulate nature of matter covers thermal physics, gas laws and energy transfer, where the losses are almost always unit and state conversions rather than concepts. Wave behaviour holds superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference, and its characteristic failure is a path-difference argument asserted without the condition that makes it true. Students who can describe constructive interference frequently cannot state the condition in terms of wavelength, which is the mark-bearing part.

Fields is the single hardest theme for most Higher Level candidates. Gravitational and electric fields are taught in parallel, with potential, potential energy and field strength all defined similarly and all examined separately. Students confuse potential with potential energy, quote a field strength where a potential was asked for, and lose sign conventions moving between attraction and repulsion. This theme repays a full rebuild more than any other, and six sessions on it is usually time well spent.

Nuclear and quantum physics closes the course and is often taught last, under time pressure, which is why so many students meet it badly. Binding energy per nucleon read from a curve, decay calculations handled with the right half-life relationship, and the photoelectric effect interpreted from a stopping-voltage graph are the examined skills. A student who met this theme in a rushed final term rather than taught properly will usually recover several marks from a short, targeted block.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, 24 marks, 3,000 words
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the physics grade at both levels, is marked out of 24, and is limited to 3,000 words. Four criteria carry six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The criteria changed with the 2023 syllabus, which means exemplars and advice written for the previous individual investigation describe a different mark scheme. That is worth knowing before a student models their report on an older example found online.

Research design is where most reports are won or lost, and the decisions are made before any data exists. A research question narrow enough to answer, an independent variable that can actually be varied over a useful range, a dependent variable that can be measured with the equipment available, and controlled variables identified and genuinely controlled. Students routinely choose questions that cannot be answered with a school laboratory's apparatus and then spend two months gathering data that will not support any conclusion.

Data analysis rewards the uncertainty and graph work that Paper 1B also examines: raw data recorded with appropriate precision, uncertainties propagated correctly, a graph with error bars where they belong, and a gradient interpreted in physical terms with its units. Conclusion asks for an answer to the stated research question, supported by the data and placed against accepted physics. Evaluation asks for the weaknesses that actually mattered, ranked, with realistic improvements rather than the standard list of more repeats and better equipment.

The boundaries of legitimate help here are strict and we put them in writing. The investigation must be entirely the student's own work. A tutor may interrogate a research question until it is feasible, discuss whether a method can produce usable data, comment on a submitted draft against each criterion, point out where an uncertainty has been mishandled, and explain what each criterion rewards. A tutor may not supply text, rework paragraphs, generate data or provide analysis for insertion. Providers in this market sell completed coursework outright, and the malpractice consequence falls on the candidate alone.

sections.heading: Practical and laboratory work when the lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the first question most Dubai physics parents ask, and it deserves a direct answer. The laboratory work belongs to the school. The guide sets aside an experimental programme of 60 hours at Higher Level, including the scientific investigation and the collaborative sciences project, and that time is timetabled, supervised and resourced by the school your child attends. No tutor, online or in-person, replaces it, and any provider implying otherwise is misdescribing the course.

What a tutor can do is everything around the laboratory. Planning a method before the session so the laboratory time produces usable data rather than a wasted afternoon. Working through the uncertainty arithmetic afterwards. Checking that a graph has error bars where they belong and that the gradient has been interpreted rather than merely calculated. Rehearsing Paper 1B questions, which present data from experiments the student has never performed and therefore need no apparatus at all.

In practice the online format suits this work better than families expect. A student photographs their raw data table and their graph and sends them; the tutor marks them properly, with the errors annotated, which is more useful than a verbal comment made while looking over a shoulder. Screen sharing a spreadsheet and watching a student propagate an uncertainty step by step is a better diagnostic than watching them write a final answer on paper.

The limits are worth naming honestly. A student who has missed substantial laboratory time cannot recover the experimental hours through tuition, and the right conversation in that case is with the school rather than with a tutor. A student who will not engage without an adult physically present is not helped by better software. And handwritten derivations need a document camera or a graphics tablet, not a laptop webcam pointed at a desk. Each of those should be tested in the free trial rather than discovered in week three.

sections.heading: Rates, availability and the evidence file for Higher Level physics in Dubai
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is among the most expensive subjects to staff in this market, and the reason is supply rather than prestige. Published rates for IB specialists in Dubai run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above, with in-home visits from about AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is priced in. Those figures come from the sources named in the table and are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. We quote after a free trial lesson, when we know which components are in play.

Availability is the constraint worth asking about before price. The tutors who teach the current syllabus confidently and can mark a data-analysis question strictly are a small group, and the hours between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time fill first across the whole emirate. When nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour we say so and name the alternatives: a different hour the same week, a short wait for a named specialist, or a tutor in another time zone whose availability is stated before you decide. No competitor page in our research discloses a coverage limit at all.

What you receive in return is a record. Every fortnight: the marked work annotated in mark-scheme wording, a theme log showing which of the five themes have been pre-tested, taught and post-tested, a separate line for the uncertainty and graph strand because it is examined in two components, and one sentence naming the current working mark and which paper it came from. The investigation drafts sit in the same file in sequence, with the criterion comments attached.

On sizing the commitment, Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run from roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end to AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for examination-year specialist support, and a ninety-minute Higher Level physics session sits at the upper end. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private-school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package, which at least makes a tutoring budget easier to plan against a known school fee.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what a Dubai parent can check for themselves
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than inspection alone.

Private tutoring is governed separately and is permitted rather than unregulated. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the ministry's app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18.

Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted at a parent should be treated with suspicion. There is one more boundary worth knowing: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct to similar effect. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document before relying on it.

All of this is checkable by a parent directly, which is the reason for setting it out. Ask any in-person tutor to show the permit. Read the regulator's own school listing rather than a provider's claim about a school. And treat marketing that attaches a regulator's initials to the word "approved" and then to a tutor as a prompt for harder questions: KHDA licenses schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, and IB Gram holds neither, nor any accreditation from ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

process.title: Tell us the level and which themes are in trouble
process.description: Higher Level physics, the school, the year group, and if you know it, the theme causing difficulty. "Fields" and "nuclear and quantum" route an enquiry differently. Mentioning whether the problem is theory or data analysis is more useful still, because they are separately examined and separately taught.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a named physics specialist
process.description: A working session. The student attempts a question from a theme they find hard, and you see how a wrong answer is handled. It is also where the setup is tested: a document camera or graphics tablet for derivations, and the household connection, so neither becomes a surprise later.

process.title: Pre-test the themes and the data strand
process.description: In the first fortnight each of the five themes gets a short timed test, and the uncertainty and graph strand is tested separately because it is examined in both Paper 1B and the investigation. Scores and dates go into a theme log, which is what the rest of the block runs on.

process.title: Rebuild the lowest theme, drill the data strand weekly
process.description: Teaching concentrates on the weakest theme until a comparable post-test moves, then shifts. The data strand runs every fortnight regardless, because it accounts for a large share of the grade and responds to repetition rather than to explanation. Fields usually needs the longest block.

process.title: Review the log before extending anything
process.description: At the end of a block the pre-test and post-test scores sit side by side with the investigation drafts in sequence. If the themes moved, the next block builds on it. If they did not, we change the tutor, the format or the level and say which. No block is extended on the strength of encouragement.

whyPoints.title: Tutors working from the current syllabus
whyPoints.description: The 2023 restructure removed the options and Paper 3, and a great deal of advice circulating in this market still assumes they exist. Our physics tutors teach the five themes and prepare students for Paper 1B, which is the question worth asking any candidate tutor before you book anything.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty and graph work treated as a strand
whyPoints.description: Paper 1B and the scientific investigation together account for a large share of the grade, and both examine the same experimental skills. We test them separately in the first fortnight and drill them fortnightly thereafter, because a student strong in theory can still be losing ten marks a paper to units and significant figures.

whyPoints.title: Command terms marked strictly
whyPoints.description: "State", "describe", "explain", "outline" and "determine" each carry a different obligation in the mark scheme, and physics students lose marks they had the knowledge to earn by answering the wrong one. Scripts come back marked against the term the question used, which is uncomfortable the first few times and effective after that.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what the school's laboratory does
whyPoints.description: The experimental programme belongs to the school and a tutor does not replace it. What we do is plan the method before the session so the laboratory time produces usable data, then work through the uncertainties afterwards. Any provider suggesting they can substitute for timetabled practical work is misdescribing the course.

whyPoints.title: Firm limits on investigation support
whyPoints.description: The scientific investigation is the student's own work and our tutors comment on it rather than contribute to it. Feedback is keyed to the four criteria with their six-mark allocations stated. Providers in this market sell finished coursework; the malpractice consequence of that falls on the candidate, not on the seller.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE and keeps no office here. Higher Level physics specialists are a small group and early-evening slots fill first, so if your hour is unavailable we say so with the alternatives named rather than filling it with a general science tutor.

faqs.question: Does IB Physics HL still have a Paper 3 and an options topic?
faqs.answer: No. The 2023 physics syllabus removed the options and Paper 3, and first examinations on the new structure were sat in May 2025. The course is now five themes assessed through Paper 1, which carries 36 per cent and splits into a multiple-choice Paper 1A and a data-analysis Paper 1B, Paper 2 at 44 per cent running two and a half hours at Higher Level, and the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. A tutor, textbook or revision site still describing an options paper is describing the previous course.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B and why do good physics students lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: Paper 1B presents data, usually from an experiment the student has not performed, and examines experimental skill in a written paper. The recurring losses are specific: a gradient quoted without units, an uncertainty given to more significant figures than the measurement justifies, percentage uncertainties added when they should have been combined through a power, an anomalous point noted and then included in the line of best fit, and a conclusion that restates a trend instead of evaluating whether the data supports it. Each costs one or two marks and together they add up quickly.

faqs.question: Does the physics tutor come to our home in Dubai, or is this online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address, and in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. Parents search for "home tutor" and this page uses the phrase honestly, but on Higher Level physics the trade is unusually favourable. The people who teach the current syllabus and can mark a data question strictly are few, and restricting the shortlist to those within driving distance usually means accepting a general science tutor instead.

faqs.question: How is practical work handled if my son is tutored over video?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work belongs to his school. The guide sets aside an experimental programme of 60 hours at Higher Level, including the scientific investigation and the collaborative sciences project, and that time is timetabled and resourced by the school. A tutor works around it: planning the method beforehand so the laboratory session produces usable data, then marking the uncertainty arithmetic and the graphs afterwards. Paper 1B questions need no apparatus at all, since they present data from experiments the student has never performed.

faqs.question: Which physics theme causes the most trouble at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Fields, consistently. Gravitational and electric fields are taught in parallel with potential, potential energy and field strength all defined similarly and all examined separately, so students quote a field strength where a potential was asked for and lose sign conventions moving between attraction and repulsion. Magnetic field direction and induction add to it. This theme repays a full rebuild rather than revision, and in one-to-one work that usually takes five or six sessions. Nuclear and quantum physics runs a close second, mostly because it is taught last and rushed.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria for the IB physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks for a total of 24, with the report limited to 3,000 words and the component carrying 20 per cent of the grade. Research design is where most reports are decided, because the question, variables and method are chosen before any data exists. Evaluation is where marks are most often left unclaimed, because students list generic improvements rather than ranking the weaknesses that actually affected the result. These criteria changed with the 2023 syllabus, so older exemplars describe a different mark scheme.

faqs.question: How much does Higher Level physics tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for IB specialists in Dubai run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above, with Unitors advertising IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table reaching past AED 450 for examination-year specialists. In-home visits are quoted from about AED 180 to AED 500 with travel embedded, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions are commonly advertised. Higher Level physics sits at the top of that range because supply is thin. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter understand the physics and still score a 4?
faqs.answer: Usually a combination of command terms and proportioning. "Explain" requires a causal chain and a response that describes without explaining collects none of the explanation marks, however accurate it is. A four-mark question wants four distinct creditable points, not one point written four ways, and students who overwrite the first extended response run out of time before the last theme. Add the Paper 1B losses on units and significant figures and a student with genuinely good physics can sit a long way below their understanding. All three are trainable.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with an investigation draft?
faqs.answer: Interrogate the research question until the method is feasible, discuss whether the apparatus can produce usable data, read a submitted draft and comment against each of the four criteria, point out a mishandled uncertainty, and explain what each criterion rewards. What a tutor must not do is supply text, rework paragraphs, generate data or provide analysis for insertion. The investigation must be entirely the student's own work. Our tutors keep a written note of the advice given, which is useful if the school asks what support was received.

faqs.question: Can my son take Higher Level physics if his school only teaches it to a few students?
faqs.answer: That is the normal situation in Dubai rather than the exception. KHDA recorded 227 private schools in the emirate with the IB at 7 per cent of enrolment, and a single school may enter six or eight Higher Level physics candidates in a year. One teacher, one scheme of work, one laboratory timetable. The course runs perfectly well; what is scarce is individual attention when a theme goes wrong. That is precisely the gap one-to-one work fills, and it is why an online match matters more here than in a larger subject.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics needed for engineering or medicine in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements are set by individual universities and faculties and are revised, so the only reliable source is the admissions page for the named course and the year of entry. The broad pattern is that engineering programmes commonly expect Higher Level physics and mathematics, while medicine more often specifies chemistry and biology with physics optional. No tutoring is required for any admissions process, and any provider implying that a course of lessons is necessary for a university or regulatory outcome is manufacturing urgency about somebody else's decision.

faqs.question: We have twelve weeks before the papers. Where should the hours go?
faqs.answer: In this order. First, two weeks on the data strand, because units, significant figures and uncertainty propagation return marks faster than any theory teaching at that stage. Second, the weakest theme from a pre-test, which for most students is fields. Third, timed Paper 2 practice with a written pacing rule and strict command-term marking. Twelve weeks will not rebuild three themes from nothing, and a plan pretending otherwise wastes the time. A baseline paper in week one shows how many marks are genuinely in reach.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence, and can I verify it?
faqs.answer: Yes and yes. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications through its app, website or e-services. Registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18 may apply. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, so ask to see it.

faqs.question: If no Higher Level physics specialist is free in our slot, what then?
faqs.answer: You are told before paying, which is not standard in this market. Hours between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time fill first across the emirate, so the realistic alternatives are a different hour the same week, often 16:30 or 20:00; a short wait for a named specialist to free a slot; or a tutor in another time zone whose availability is stated plainly so you can judge whether it works for your household. What we will not do is fill the slot with a general science tutor and leave you to find the gap.

faqs.question: Can sessions shift during Ramadan or pause for study leave?
faqs.answer: Both, and online delivery is what makes it simple. Ramadan shortens the school day in Dubai and reshapes the evening, so physics sessions commonly move to post-Iftar slots for that period and then return to the usual time. Study leave and the examination weeks themselves are usually the right moment to pause rather than push, and that is better agreed in advance than cancelled week by week. Family travel is handled the same way, since the lesson follows the student rather than an address.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Physics at Higher Level to Dubai students, working from the themes and tools of the current guide. Each one teaches Paper 1B data technique as a separate discipline, marks extended responses against command terms, and keeps the investigation firmly in the student's own hands.

intro.heading: What Physics HL assesses, component by component
paragraphs: IB Diploma Physics at Higher Level is 240 teaching hours assessed by two examination papers and one internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 lasts two hours and carries 36% of the grade, and it is two different examinations in one booklet: Paper 1A, forty multiple-choice questions across the whole syllabus, and Paper 1B, a set of data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 lasts two and a half hours and carries 44%, in short-answer and extended-response form. The investigation carries the remaining 20%.

That structure is recent enough that a great deal of advice circulating about IB Physics is wrong. The course taught until 2024 had eleven numbered topics and a choice of options; the current one has five themes, lettered A to E, each with its own Higher Level extension, plus a strand of tools and an inquiry process that run through all of them. A tutor describing options, or a student revising from a parent's downloaded topic list, is preparing for an examination that no longer exists.

The five themes are Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; and Nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level does not add a sixth theme. It deepens each of the five, which is why a student cannot drop to Standard Level by simply ignoring part of the syllabus, and why the HL content tends to arrive late in DP2 when time has already run short. Knowing which HL extensions remain untaught in February is the most useful piece of information a Dubai family can have, and it is a question the subject teacher can answer in one email.

Marks in this subject are rarely lost for not knowing physics. They are lost on the data section, where uncertainties, gradients and error bars are treated as an afterthought; on command terms, where a student explains when the question said determine, or states when it asked them to justify; and on the arithmetic of unit prefixes and significant figures. Each of those is a narrow, teachable discipline rather than a gap in understanding, which is why targeted hours work better in Physics than general revision does.

The sections below work through the assessment in order: the components and what each tests, the themes and their HL extensions, Paper 1B in detail, the command terms and what each one owes a mark, the investigation's four criteria, the mathematics the course assumes, and how practical work is handled when lessons are delivered remotely. Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that is a service we provide only in India, and the section on practical work explains exactly what that does and does not mean for a laboratory subject.

Paper 2: two and a half hours, 44%, short-answer and extended-response
Scientific investigation: 24 marks across four criteria, 20% of the grade
Five themes lettered A to E, each with Higher Level extensions
Tools and the inquiry process run through every theme rather than sitting apart

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics HL sits at the end of a sequence, and what a student brings into it determines which part of the assessment hurts. The three stages below describe the preparation each one gives for the components above, and where the predictable shortfall sits.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Higher Level Physics is one of the heavier Diploma subjects by content, and its three assessed components demand different preparation. Paper 1A rewards breadth and speed. Paper 1B rewards a specific set of data-handling routines. Paper 2 rewards structured writing against command terms. A revision plan that treats the subject as one thing, usually by rereading notes, prepares for none of them well, and that is the commonest way a capable student underperforms here.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts are small relative to the emirate's British-curriculum population, with the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent of private school enrolment against 37 per cent for UK curricula. Physics HL groups in a Dubai school are often a handful of students, which has an upside and a downside: teachers know every student, but there is rarely a second specialist to turn to when a theme has not landed and the timetable has moved on.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences assesses against four criteria, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, is the direct ancestor of Paper 1B and of the investigation's data-analysis mark. A student with strong MYP criterion C work arrives in Physics HL already able to handle gradients, anomalies and uncertainty in a basic form. One with strong knowledge marks and weak processing marks will struggle with exactly the components that are hardest to fix late.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB continuum schools run MYP Sciences through to MYP 5 before the Diploma split, and the decision between Physics HL and SL is usually taken then. The useful evidence at that point is a marked criterion C task rather than an overall grade, because it predicts performance on the data section far better than a report comment does.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Physics HL bridge
programmes.description: IGCSE Physics covers much of the same ground as theme A and parts of themes B and C, but at a different level of abstraction and with far less emphasis on uncertainty. The gap into Physics HL is mathematical as much as conceptual: trigonometry in two dimensions, logarithms for decay and intensity, and algebraic rearrangement under time pressure. Students who bridge that in the summer before DP1 report an easier first term.
programmes.countryNote: Most Physics HL students in Dubai arrive from IGCSE, since UK curricula dominate enrolment in the emirate. Cambridge and Pearson both run their International GCSE Physics series in the summer and in November, and a student who sat the November series arrives in DP1 with a shorter gap and fresher practical experience than one whose last physics examination was in June.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics HL is the subject in the URL. The grid below shows it alongside the Diploma subjects Dubai students most often take with it, with each entry written around the component that decides the grade rather than the subject's general reputation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes with Higher Level extensions inside each, assessed by Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data analysis, Paper 2 extended response and a 24-mark investigation. HL adds ninety guide hours of depth rather than a sixth theme, which is why HL content tends to arrive late in DP2.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Built on the same assessment model as Physics: Paper 1A and 1B, Paper 2, and the same four-criterion investigation. The shared skill is quantitative discipline, and a student losing marks on unit prefixes in Physics is usually losing them on moles in Chemistry for the same reason.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Also assessed on the current sciences model, with the heaviest extended-response load of the three. Statistical treatment of data, error bars and correlation overlaps directly with Paper 1B in Physics, so one data session often serves both subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The mathematics Physics HL assumes sits mostly in AA: trigonometric identities, logarithms, calculus notation and algebraic rearrangement at speed. A student weak in AA algebra will lose Physics marks that look like physics errors and are not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI pairs with Physics HL less naturally but workably, with its statistics block supporting data analysis well. The gap to watch is manipulation without technology, since Physics examinations expect algebraic fluency the AI course does not drill as hard.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A common partner subject for Physics HL students heading into engineering. The solution component carries its own development record, and the computational thinking it builds transfers usefully to modelling questions in theme A and theme D.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design cycle produces a heavy internal workload alongside the Physics investigation, which is a scheduling problem more than an academic one. Families taking both should map the two internal deadlines against each other in DP1 rather than in DP2.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Shares energy and systems content with theme B and theme E, and its data questions reward the same treatment of uncertainty. A useful second science for a Physics HL student who does not want a third laboratory subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A frequent third subject for Dubai Physics HL students aiming at engineering or finance routes. The quantitative HL paper benefits from the same graph-reading discipline that Paper 1B demands, and the internal commentaries are a different kind of writing practice.

sections.heading: The three components, and what each one is really testing
paragraphs: Physics HL is assessed by Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%. Paper 1 runs for two hours and contains two distinct sections: 1A, forty multiple-choice questions spread across the whole syllabus, and 1B, data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 runs for two and a half hours of short-answer and extended-response questions. Those three components reward three different kinds of preparation, and the single biggest planning error in this subject is treating them as one.

Paper 1A tests breadth and recall speed. A student with a reliable grasp of every theme but slow recall will run out of time; one with deep knowledge of three themes and gaps in two will lose marks they cannot recover elsewhere, because the questions sample everything. Preparation for 1A is therefore about coverage and pace: short, frequent, mixed-topic sets rather than long sessions on one theme.

Paper 1B tests whether a student can handle data and criticise an experiment. It is the most predictable section on the paper, because the skills repeat: read a table, decide what to plot, draw a line, find a gradient with units, estimate an uncertainty, identify a systematic error, suggest an improvement. Almost every student can learn those routines; most have never been taught them as a set.

Paper 2 tests structured physics writing under time pressure, and the command term in each question is the instruction about how many marks the answer owes. A two-mark state question wants two facts. A four-mark explain question wants a causal chain. A discuss question wants both sides and a judgement. Students who write everything they know, in the same register, for every question, lose marks on long questions while writing far too much on short ones.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level adds inside each one
paragraphs: The current Physics course is organised into five themes rather than numbered topics. Theme A covers space, time and motion: kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, and at Higher Level the rotational and relativistic extensions. Theme B covers the particulate nature of matter: thermal physics, gas laws, current and circuits, with HL depth on thermodynamics. Theme C covers wave behaviour, including simple harmonic motion, which at Higher Level becomes a quantitative treatment rather than a descriptive one.

Theme D covers fields: gravitational, electric and magnetic, with the Higher Level extension handling field potential and orbital motion in quantitative detail. Theme E covers nuclear and quantum physics: structure of the atom, radioactive decay, fission and fusion, and at Higher Level the quantum and particle content that most students meet last. Running through all five are the tools, experimental technique, technology and mathematics, and the inquiry process that the investigation formalises.

The practical consequence of this architecture is a timing problem specific to Higher Level. Because HL depth is distributed across all five themes rather than gathered into a sixth, a school that falls behind in theme A in DP1 carries that debt into every subsequent theme. By February of DP2 it is common to find a student who has met every theme but not the HL extension of two of them, usually in themes D and E. That is a precise, fixable deficit, and naming it is the first job of a diagnostic session.

The table is the document we build first with any new Physics HL student. It is not a revision timetable; it is an audit of what has actually been taught, what has been examined internally, and what remains. Families are often surprised by how much of the subject is secure and how narrow the real gap is, which usually means fewer hours than they expected rather than more.

sections.heading: Paper 1B: the data section almost nobody revises
paragraphs: Paper 1B is a data-based and experimental section inside Paper 1, and it is the most systematically under-prepared part of Physics HL. Students revise content for Paper 1A and essays for Paper 2 and then meet 1B cold, treating it as a quiz about an experiment they have never performed. It is not that. It is a test of a fixed set of routines, and the routines are short enough to list on one page and drill in three sessions.

The routines are these. Read the table and identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables. Decide what to plot to produce a straight line, which often means plotting a square, a reciprocal or a logarithm rather than the raw quantity. Draw the line and extract a gradient with its units, then say what the gradient physically represents. Estimate an absolute and a percentage uncertainty and propagate it through a calculation. Distinguish a random error from a systematic one by looking at the shape of the data rather than guessing.

The last routine is the one that separates grades: suggesting an improvement that is specific enough to be worth a mark. A student who writes repeat the experiment and take an average has written a sentence that applies to every experiment ever conducted and earns nothing. A student who writes that the thermometer should be replaced with a thermocouple because the response time is comparable to the cooling interval has identified something about this experiment. Teaching that distinction is a matter of practising criticism, not of learning more physics.

Significant figures and unit prefixes belong here too, and they are the quietest marks lost in this subject. An answer correct to five figures where the data supports two is penalised; a milli confused with a micro turns a right answer into a wrong one. These are habits of transcription rather than understanding, which means they respond to a checking routine applied under timed conditions rather than to further explanation.
bullets: Identify variables before reading the question stem twice
Linearise: plot the quantity that produces a straight line
Always state the units of a gradient and what it represents physically
Propagate percentage uncertainties rather than quoting them separately
Make every suggested improvement specific to this apparatus

sections.heading: Command terms on Paper 2, and the marks each one owes
paragraphs: Every question on Paper 2 opens with a command term, and that term is an instruction about the shape and length of the answer. The IB groups them by assessment objective: terms like state, outline, list and label sit at the recall end; explain, calculate, determine, compare and distinguish sit in the middle; evaluate, discuss, justify and sketch sit at the analytical end. A student who treats all of them as invitations to write what they know will systematically overwrite short questions and underwrite long ones.

The pattern in marked Dubai scripts is consistent. State questions attract paragraphs where one clause was wanted, costing time that the long questions then lack. Explain questions receive a description of what happens with no causal link, which collects the knowledge mark and loses the reasoning one. Determine questions receive an answer with no working, which forfeits method credit entirely. Discuss questions receive one side of the argument and no judgement, which caps the mark whatever the physics is worth.

Teaching this is quick and measurable. Take a marked script, count the marks lost to command-term mismatch rather than to physics, and the number is usually larger than the family expects. Then practise answers to a stopwatch with the mark allocation visible: two marks, two points, thirty seconds; four marks, a chain of four linked statements, ninety seconds. Within three or four sessions the register changes, and the gain shows up across every topic at once rather than in one theme.

Sketch deserves a specific mention because it is routinely misread as draw. A sketch question wants the correct shape, the correct intercepts and the correct asymptotic behaviour, labelled, without a scale. Students either produce an accurate plotted graph they had no time for, or a vague curve with nothing labelled. Both lose marks that were available to anyone who knew what the term asks for.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks across four criteria
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is the internally assessed component, worth 20% of the Physics HL grade and marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report has a limit of 3,000 words and around ten hours of class time are allocated to it. Those four criteria are the whole of the mark scheme, and a student who knows them by letter writes a different report from one who is working from a general sense of what a lab write-up looks like.

Research design is where most marks are lost, and they are lost before any apparatus is touched. A research question that is too broad produces data that cannot support a conclusion; one with no measurable dependent variable produces no data at all. The fix is a session spent narrowing the question and checking that the method can generate enough points across a wide enough range, with the uncertainty of each measurement estimated in advance rather than discovered afterwards.

Data analysis rewards correct processing and honest treatment of uncertainty, including propagation through to the final result and error bars that mean something. Conclusion rewards an answer to the stated research question, compared against accepted physics with a source. Evaluation rewards identification of real weaknesses in this method and improvements specific to it. A report that evaluates by saying human error affected the results scores poorly, whatever the physics behind it.

The boundary on paid support here is the same across this site and it is worth stating in full. A tutor may teach a technique on a different experiment, ask what a graph shows, question whether a research question is answerable, and point out where a reader cannot follow the method. The student designs the investigation, collects the data, processes it and types the report. Nothing in the submitted file comes from us, and any provider selling a finished investigation is selling a malpractice case that lands on the candidate.

sections.heading: The mathematics Physics HL assumes, and the AA or AI question
paragraphs: Physics HL assumes a working fluency that the mathematics courses deliver at different points. Resolving vectors needs confident trigonometry. Decay and intensity problems need logarithms handled without hesitation. Field and potential questions need algebraic rearrangement of expressions with several variables, done quickly and correctly under time pressure. The Higher Level extensions push further, and a student who is slow at the algebra will read as slow at physics, because the two are indistinguishable from a marked script.

That is the practical core of the AA versus AI question for a Dubai Physics HL student. Analysis and Approaches drills manipulation harder, and its Paper 1 is sat without technology, which builds exactly the fluency Physics rewards. Applications and Interpretation has a much larger statistics block, 36 of 150 guide hours at Standard Level, which supports data analysis well but drills manual algebra less. Neither course disqualifies a student from Physics HL, and plenty do the subject well from AI.

What we will not do is tell you which combination a particular university requires. Entry requirements differ by institution, by faculty and by year, and a tutoring page asserting them would be guessing with somebody's application. Read the published requirements for the specific course, and if your child needs their certificate attested in the UAE afterwards, check the Ministry of Education equivalency conditions through the official channel rather than through any tutoring provider.

Where the mathematics is the real constraint, the honest recommendation is often fewer physics hours and more mathematics ones. A student losing Physics marks to rearrangement errors does not need more physics taught; they need twenty minutes of algebra at the start of each session until the rearrangement stops being the slow step. We say that at the diagnostic rather than after a term of physics teaching that was never the problem.

sections.heading: Practical work when the lessons are delivered online
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen where tutor and student work on the same page, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and no sentence on this site should suggest otherwise to a family in this emirate. For a laboratory subject that raises a fair question, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a reassurance.

The practical work itself belongs to the school and stays there. Your child's apparatus, laboratory access and supervision come from their own teacher, and that is as it should be: the investigation must be their own work carried out under their school's conditions. What an online tutor contributes is everything around the bench. Designing the investigation before the session in the lab. Deciding what to measure and how many times. Processing the data afterwards, which is where most of the 24 marks actually sit.

For Paper 1B, remote delivery is arguably better than the alternative. The section tests the analysis of experimental data rather than the manipulation of equipment, and analysis is exactly what a shared screen supports: the same table of results in front of both people, the same graph being drawn and corrected, the gradient calculated twice because the first attempt dropped a unit. A tutor sitting beside a student on a sofa has no better tool for that than a shared document, and usually a worse one.

The supply argument matters in Physics more than in most subjects. Higher Level Physics groups in Dubai schools are small, and the pool of tutors who have taught the current five-theme guide and marked investigations against the four criteria is smaller still. Requiring a specialist to live within a tolerable drive of your community narrows that pool sharply. If no Physics HL specialist is free in the slot you need, we will say so and offer a different time or a tutor in another time zone, rather than substituting a general science tutor at the same rate.

sections.heading: Dubai schools, inspection bands and what a small HL cohort means
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection outcomes are published on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and those reports are free to read. For a Physics HL family they are context rather than a verdict: a school in a strong band can still have a thin Higher Level Physics cohort and a teacher covering several subjects.

The emirate's scale explains why. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, American at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. A Diploma Physics HL group inside that distribution is often three to eight students. That brings real advantages in teacher attention and a real fragility: when one theme does not land, there is rarely a second specialist in the building to re-teach it.

Supply is also shifting. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following UK curricula and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More IB provision means more Higher Level science cohorts competing for the same specialist teachers, which tends to show up first as scheduling pressure rather than as anything visible in a report.

Two further points belong on any page about tutoring in this emirate. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, so a Physics HL student's week is fuller than a Physics HL timetable suggests. And anyone charging for private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram holds no regulator permit, operates no premises here, and claims no endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board.

faqs.question: What does IB DP Physics HL assess under the syllabus taught now?
faqs.answer: Five themes rather than numbered topics, assessed by three components. Paper 1 runs two hours and carries 36%, split between 1A, forty multiple-choice questions, and 1B, data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 runs two and a half hours for 44% in short-answer and extended-response form. The scientific investigation is internally assessed, marked out of 24 across four criteria, and worth 20%. Advice describing eleven topics and option units refers to the course last examined in 2024 and should be set aside.

faqs.question: How is Physics HL Paper 1 split between multiple choice and data?
faqs.answer: Paper 1A is forty multiple-choice questions sampling the whole syllabus, and Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions. They sit inside the same two-hour paper and together make up 36% of the grade. The two halves need different preparation: 1A rewards coverage and recall speed across all five themes, while 1B rewards a fixed set of data routines. Practising only content revision prepares a student for one of them and leaves the other to chance.

faqs.question: What is the HL-only content in each Physics theme?
faqs.answer: Higher Level does not add a sixth theme; it deepens all five. Theme A gains rotational dynamics and the relativistic treatment. Theme B gains quantitative thermodynamics. Theme C turns a descriptive treatment of oscillation into a quantitative one. Theme D goes further into field potential, orbital motion and induction. Theme E adds quantum and particle content. Because the depth is distributed rather than gathered at the end, a school running late in DP1 carries that debt through every later theme, which is why a theme audit is the first thing worth doing.

faqs.question: Where do Physics HL students lose the most marks on Paper 2?
faqs.answer: On command terms rather than on physics. State questions receive paragraphs where a clause was wanted, which costs the time that longer questions then lack. Explain questions receive descriptions with no causal chain, collecting the knowledge mark and losing the reasoning one. Determine questions receive bare answers with no working, forfeiting method credit. Discuss questions receive one side and no judgement. Counting those losses on a marked script usually produces a bigger number than families expect, and the register is quick to retrain.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Physics scientific investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four marks, split evenly across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It carries 20% of the final grade and the report is limited to 3,000 words, with around ten hours of class time allocated. Most of the marks that go missing are lost in research design, before any apparatus is touched, because a question that is too broad cannot produce data that supports a conclusion. One session narrowing the question is the highest-value hour in the whole process.

faqs.question: Does my child need Maths AA HL to cope with Physics HL?
faqs.answer: No, and plenty of students take Physics HL successfully alongside Applications and Interpretation. What Physics HL does require is fluency: resolving vectors with confident trigonometry, handling logarithms for decay and intensity without hesitation, and rearranging multi-variable expressions quickly under time pressure. Analysis and Approaches drills that manipulation harder, partly because its Paper 1 bans technology. If the mathematics is the slow step, the useful fix is often twenty minutes of algebra inside each physics session rather than a course change.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with Physics practical work?
faqs.answer: With everything except the bench itself, which belongs to the school. Apparatus, laboratory access and supervision come from your child's own teacher, and the investigation has to be their own work under their school's conditions. What a tutor contributes is the design before the lab session and the processing afterwards, which is where most of the 24 marks sit. For Paper 1B, a shared screen with the same table of data in front of both people is a better tool than sitting side by side with one printout.

faqs.question: What do the command terms determine and show that require in Physics?
faqs.answer: Determine asks for a numerical answer reached by visible working, usually with units and an appropriate number of significant figures; an answer with no working forfeits the method marks even when the number is right. Show that asks the student to arrive at a given result, which means every step between the starting point and the stated answer has to appear, since the answer itself is already printed and earns nothing. Both terms reward written working rather than mental arithmetic, and both punish the student who skips lines.

faqs.question: How long is Physics HL Paper 2 and how should the time be split?
faqs.answer: Two and a half hours, carrying 44% of the grade in short-answer and extended-response questions. The workable rule is to spend time in proportion to marks, which sounds obvious and is routinely ignored: students over-invest in early short questions and then rush the extended responses where the most marks sit. Practising with the mark allocation visible and a clock running changes that behaviour faster than any amount of content revision, and it is the single most transferable habit a Paper 2 session can build.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Physics investigation report?
faqs.answer: Three thousand words. That limit is generous for a well-designed investigation and punishing for a badly scoped one, because a student whose research question was too broad ends up describing instead of analysing. The sections that routinely run long are the background theory and the method, neither of which carries many marks; the sections that run short are data analysis and evaluation, which carry twelve marks between them. Reading a draft against the four criteria usually reveals that imbalance immediately.

faqs.question: Which Physics HL theme is usually taught last in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, and often the Higher Level extension of theme D, fields. Both arrive in DP2 when internal deadlines, mocks and the investigation are competing for the same weeks, so they get the least settling time and the least practice. Asking the school where they are in the sequence, rather than assuming the syllabus order, is worth doing in January. A student with two untaught HL extensions has a precise and fixable deficit rather than a general weakness.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL harder than Chemistry HL for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: They are hard differently, and the better question is which one suits your child. Physics HL concentrates difficulty in mathematical manipulation and in multi-step reasoning across unfamiliar contexts. Chemistry HL concentrates it in breadth of content and in precise quantitative chains. Both run on the same assessment model, with Paper 1A and 1B, Paper 2 and a 24-mark investigation. A student strong at algebra and weak at memorising usually finds Physics the better fit, and the reverse holds too.

faqs.question: How much uncertainty and error analysis does Physics HL need?
faqs.answer: More than most students practise and less than they fear. The working set is small: absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through multiplication, division and powers, uncertainty in a gradient, and the distinction between random and systematic error read from the shape of the data. That set appears in Paper 1B and carries six of the investigation's marks under data analysis. Three focused sessions cover it for both components, which makes it one of the highest-return blocks of hours available in this subject.

faqs.question: Can my child drop Physics HL to SL part-way through DP1?
faqs.answer: That is a decision for the school, not for a tutor, and it depends on timetabling, the diploma requirements your child is working to and how far the cohort has travelled. What we can offer is evidence for the conversation: a theme-by-theme audit of what is secure, a marked timed paper, and an honest view of whether the gap is content or mathematics. Schools in Dubai set their own deadlines for level changes, so ask the Diploma coordinator early rather than after the next report.

faqs.question: What should a Physics HL student do with past papers from the old syllabus?
faqs.answer: Use them selectively and with a tutor who knows the difference. Questions on themes that carried over largely unchanged, much of kinematics, circuits and waves, remain good practice. Questions from the retired option units are wasted effort, and the old paper structure does not match the current 1A and 1B split. Marking a pre-2025 paper as though it were the current examination teaches the wrong pacing. We work from your child's own attempts rather than redistributing board material, which is the IB's to publish.

intro.heading: What a Physics HL tutor should be able to show you after a month
paragraphs: Most Dubai parents start looking for an IB DP Physics HL tutor after a report card that says very little. A predicted 5, a comment about needing to show more working, and a parents' evening slot of eight minutes. Nothing in that tells you which theme is costing marks, whether the problem is physics or arithmetic under time pressure, or how much of it is fixable before the May session. A tutor who cannot answer those three questions in writing within a month is not teaching your child; they are keeping them company.

This page is built around evidence, because evidence is the one thing this market almost never produces. A physics session that goes well feels good to everybody in the room. The student nods, the explanation lands, the hour ends warmly, and the next mock comes back as another 5. The sessions that actually move a Higher Level physics grade look different from the outside: a timed question attempted cold, marked against the published criteria, annotated where the marks were lost, and logged so the same loss can be counted again in six weeks.

Higher Level physics is unusually suited to that kind of record keeping. The course is 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra content is concentrated in places that are easy to name: the fields theme, the quantum and nuclear material, the longer derivations, and the data questions in Paper 1B where candidates are asked to handle uncertainty rather than recall a formula. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent of the grade, Paper 2 carries 44 per cent, and the scientific investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent. Every mark your child loses sits inside one of those three boxes, and each box fails in a different way.

The second thing evidence does is tell you when to stop. Dubai parents are rarely short of options; they are short of a way to judge them. If after eight sessions the mark log shows the same category of error repeating at the same rate, the arrangement is not working and no amount of warmth changes that. If the log shows the error rate on unit and uncertainty questions halving while extended-response marks stay flat, you know exactly what the next block of hours should target. That is a decision you can make yourself, from a document, rather than taking a tutor's word for it.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It is not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate, with KHDA, or with any Dubai school named on this page, and tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. What a Dubai family gets instead is a Higher Level physics specialist chosen from a much larger pool than the twenty-minute drive around your own community, and a written record of what each hour produced.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics at Higher Level sits inside a wider Diploma, and the pressures around it change by year group. These are the programmes IB Gram covers for Dubai students, with a note on what each one means for a physics-heavy course load.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Physics HL is 240 taught hours spread over two years, assessed by Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent and the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. The practical scheme adds around 60 hours of laboratory and project work at Higher Level, including the ten-hour collaborative sciences project that is required but not separately graded.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students taking Physics HL usually carry Mathematics at Analysis and Approaches alongside it, and often a second Higher Level science. KHDA's mandatory subjects run in parallel: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. That timetable pressure is why Higher Level physics support in Dubai tends to be booked for a single evening slot rather than spread across the week.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of integrated sciences assessed against four criteria rather than by examination paper. Physics appears as a strand inside MYP Sciences rather than as a separate subject with its own papers, which is why the first weeks of DP1 physics feel abrupt: the command terms get narrower, the mathematics arrives faster, and marks start depending on method rather than on a written explanation of understanding.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the MYP as a continuum into the Diploma, and the handover is where Higher Level physics problems usually begin. A student who scored a 7 on MYP criterion C can still be short of the algebra and the graph-reading that Paper 1B assumes from the first week of DP1. Dubai families often book physics support for the DP1 autumn term purely to close that gap before the fields theme arrives.

programmes.name: IGCSE and O Level
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 are the two routes most Dubai students arrive from. Both are examined in a June and a November series, and both reward recall of defined relationships far more than Diploma physics does. The step up to Higher Level is less about new topics than about being asked to combine two unfamiliar relationships inside one unseen question.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of Dubai students sit IGCSE at 16 and then split between A Level and the Diploma, so Physics HL classes in Dubai often contain students from three or four different IGCSE boards. Knowing which board a student came from matters: a 0625 candidate has met uncertainty informally, while a 4PH1 candidate has usually met more formula recall and less graph analysis.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme and A Level crossover
programmes.description: Some Dubai students move between the Diploma and A Level during DP1, or sit a mixed load. Physics at Higher Level maps reasonably well onto a two-year A Level in content, but the assessment logic is different: no synoptic paper, no option topic since the 2023 syllabus, and a single internally assessed investigation worth 20 per cent instead of a practical endorsement.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is one of the few cities where a family can realistically change curriculum mid-course, because the school density makes a transfer possible. If that is being considered for physics, the decision window in most Dubai schools closes early in DP1, and the conversation needs the school's own Diploma coordinator in it before any tutoring plan is built around it.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics HL is rarely the only subject under pressure, and the subjects a Dubai student pairs it with change what the evidence should track. These are the Diploma subjects IB Gram matches most often alongside Higher Level physics.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data analysis, Paper 2 structured questions and the scientific investigation. At Higher Level the fields theme and the quantum and nuclear material carry the content most often left half-finished, and Paper 2 rewards candidates who state the physics before reaching for algebra.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion to Physics HL. Weak logarithm, trigonometry and calculus fluency shows up as physics marks lost: a correct method abandoned halfway through a rearrangement reads to an examiner as a physics error, and the mark log will record it in the wrong column unless someone separates the two.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Paired with Physics HL less often, and worth checking against university entry lists before DP1 closes. The modelling and statistics content suits data handling in Paper 1B, but the lighter calculus means derivations in the fields theme take longer to build from scratch.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The common second science for medicine and engineering applicants in Dubai. Shares the same assessment architecture as physics, which means a student can carry an identical technique problem into both subjects and lose marks twice for one habit, usually in extended response or in significant figures.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A volume subject rather than a derivation subject, so it competes for revision time in a different way. Students carrying Biology HL and Physics HL together need their weekly hours split deliberately, because the revision method that works for one is close to useless for the other.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A frequent third science in Dubai schools with strong engineering intakes. The logic and algorithmic thinking transfers usefully to physics problem decomposition, though the assessment demands are unrelated and the internal assessment runs on a different timetable.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered in a smaller set of Dubai schools and often chosen alongside physics by students aiming at engineering. The coursework load is heavier and lands in the same DP2 window as the physics investigation, so the two deadlines need mapping together early.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A common sixth subject for physics students, and the one that quietly absorbs DP2 evenings because of its internal assessment commentaries. Worth naming in a tutoring plan so physics revision is not scheduled into weeks that are already committed elsewhere.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The written technique developed here transfers directly to the extended-response marks in Paper 2 physics, where candidates who can structure a short argument out-score candidates who list facts. The reverse is also true: a physics student who writes in fragments loses marks that have nothing to do with physics.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, graded, and the first thing a physics-heavy student drops when time runs short. The TOK essay deadline sits close to the physics investigation deadline in most Dubai schools, which is a scheduling problem rather than an academic one and is solved with a calendar, not with hours.

schoolClusters.note: Diploma cohorts attached to villa communities, where the physics set is often smaller and taught by a single specialist across both years. dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways Dubai families use Higher Level physics support, each producing a different kind of record. The choice is usually dictated by where the student is in the two-year course rather than by preference.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, evidence-led
modes.description: One recurring slot of sixty or ninety minutes, built around a timed question attempted cold, marked against the criteria, and logged. The log drives the following week, so the sequence of topics is decided by the mark loss rather than by the school's scheme of work. This is the format that produces a readable trail across a term.

modes.title: Investigation support block
modes.description: A short block of sessions around the scientific investigation, the internally assessed 20 per cent. Support covers choosing a question that can produce usable data, planning a method that controls what it claims to control, understanding uncertainty treatment, and reading the four criteria as an examiner reads them. The physics and the words stay the student's own throughout.

modes.description: A compressed block in the weeks before mocks or the May session, usually two sessions a week. Every session is a timed paper section under exam conditions, marked and returned, with a short re-teach of whatever the script exposed. This is remedial triage rather than teaching, and the evidence trail is the only way to tell whether the triage is working.

sections.heading: The evidence pack: what should arrive after every Physics HL session
paragraphs: After a Higher Level physics session, a parent should receive three things: the student's own attempt, the marking on it, and a line in a log. That is the whole of the evidence pack, and it takes a tutor about ten minutes to produce. The reason so few Dubai providers produce it is not cost. It is that a written record makes an unproductive arrangement visible after four weeks rather than after a term.

The attempt matters more than the marking. A question the student has already seen, worked through in the session with prompts, tells you almost nothing about what they can do alone in a hall in May. A question attempted cold, in the time the paper allows, is the only artefact with predictive value. For Physics HL that means forty-five to sixty minutes of Paper 1B-style data work or a Paper 2 section, not a worksheet of recall questions with the formulae at the top of the page.

The marking should quote criteria rather than award a grade. Diploma physics marks are allocated against specific statements, and a script annotated with those statements teaches the student where the mark sat. A number out of fifteen teaches nothing. The log is the part parents underuse: one row per attempt, with the error category rather than the score, is what lets you see in week eight that unit and uncertainty errors have halved while extended-response marks have not moved at all.

None of this requires a particular platform or a subscription. It requires a tutor willing to be measured. If a provider will not produce a marked script in the first fortnight, that is the answer to the question you were asking about quality, and it arrives early enough to be useful.
