sections.heading: Reading a marked Higher Level physics script
paragraphs: Dubai parents are often shown a marked paper and told the student is close. Close to what is the question the script can answer. Higher Level physics scripts fail in a small number of recognisable ways, and once a parent can name them, the conversation with a tutor changes completely. You stop asking whether the sessions are going well and start asking which category fell this month.

The first category is arithmetic and unit handling: a correct method carried into a wrong power of ten, a conversion missed, a final answer given to six significant figures when the data had two. These are not physics errors and they cannot be fixed by re-teaching physics. They are fixed by a drill and by a habit, and they respond faster than anything else on the list, which is why they are worth finding first.

The second is the description-explanation gap. The command term asks the candidate to explain and the script describes. In the fields theme this shows up constantly: a student states that the field strength falls with distance and never says why, so the mark for the mechanism is not available to award. The third is the abandoned derivation, where an unfamiliar combination of two relationships stops a confident student dead. The fourth is uncertainty: Paper 1B asks for a treatment of error that many candidates have met only as a laboratory ritual.

A tutor who can place every lost mark into one of those four boxes can also tell you how long each box takes to empty. Unit discipline moves inside a fortnight. The description-explanation gap takes six to eight weeks of marked questions because it is a writing habit as much as a physics one. Abandoned derivations need content re-teaching followed by repetition on unseen combinations, and uncertainty needs a short, deliberate block of its own.

sections.heading: Twenty weeks of DP2 physics, and the evidence at each stage
paragraphs: A Higher Level physics grade does not move in a straight line, and a tutoring arrangement judged week by week will be abandoned exactly when it starts working. What follows is the shape a DP2 block usually takes for a Dubai student starting in the autumn term with a predicted 5 and an ambition of a 7. The dates belong to your school's own calendar; the sequence does not change much.

The first three weeks are diagnosis, and they often feel like the least productive part of the whole arrangement. A cold Paper 2 section, a cold Paper 1B section, and a conversation about the investigation produce a baseline, and baselines are uncomfortable reading. Parents who stop here conclude that the tutor spent three sessions finding out what the school already said. What the school said was a predicted grade; what the baseline gives is a distribution of lost marks across four categories.

Weeks four to ten are content and habit together. The habit work is unit discipline and command-term response, drilled on short questions. The content work follows the mark log, which usually points at fields first and at the quantum and nuclear material second. Through this phase the total score on timed attempts often stays flat while the error mix changes underneath it, and that is the single most misread moment in the whole block. The log is the only thing that shows the change.

From week eleven the investigation competes for every hour, and in most Dubai schools the internal deadline lands in this window. Weeks fifteen to twenty are paper technique under time, with full sections rather than questions, and this is where the score moves visibly. A student whose error mix shifted in week eight typically sees the number follow in weeks sixteen to eighteen. Starting the whole sequence in February rather than September does not compress it; it removes the first half.

sections.heading: Grade movement needs a baseline, and the school report is not one
paragraphs: Every tutoring conversation in Dubai eventually reaches the phrase grade improvement, and it is almost always used without a baseline. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by a teacher using the evidence they hold, which in DP1 is often two class tests and a piece of coursework. It is not a measurement of where a candidate currently stands against Diploma criteria in May conditions, and it moves for reasons that have nothing to do with the student, including a school's own internal moderation.

A usable baseline has three properties. It is a cold attempt, it is marked against the published criteria rather than a school rubric, and it is recorded in a form that can be compared with the next one. Two Paper 2 sections six weeks apart, both unseen, both timed, both marked the same way, tell you something real. A mock sat under different conditions with a different mark scheme and a different question selection tells you much less than the number printed on it suggests.

Grade boundaries make this harder to read than parents expect. The marks required for each Diploma grade are set per session after the papers are sat, so a raw score of sixty does not map to a fixed grade across years. Anyone quoting a precise boundary for a future session is guessing. What can be tracked honestly is raw marks on comparable material and the error categories behind them, which is why the log matters more than any single predicted grade.

This is also why no honest provider can promise a particular outcome. IB Gram publishes no grade guarantee and no success rate, because a success rate without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing number rather than evidence. What can be promised is the record: the attempts, the marking, the log, and a half-term review in which you read it rather than hear about it.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, and where help has to stop
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is 20 per cent of the Higher Level physics grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria, with a word limit of 3,000 words and around ten hours of class time allocated to it. The four criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks. Students lose marks in all four for the same underlying reason: the question they chose cannot produce data good enough to support a conclusion worth drawing.

Legitimate support concentrates on the stage before any data exists. A tutor can ask whether the chosen relationship is actually measurable with the apparatus available, whether the range of the independent variable is wide enough to show a trend, how many repeats the uncertainty budget demands, and what the student intends to do when the graph is not a straight line. Those questions change outcomes more than anything that happens after data collection, and none of them require a tutor to touch the student's work.

The line is specific and the IB enforces it: the work submitted must be the student's own, in the student's own words, and a tutor's contribution must be the kind of guidance a teacher would give. Feedback that arrives as replacement sentences is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. A tutor working through IB Gram gives feedback as questions and criterion references, keeps a dated note of what was discussed at each stage, and says so plainly to the student at the start. If you are offered finished investigation text by any provider in this market, that is the moment to walk away; two providers found in the research for this page sell exactly that.

Practical work raises a reasonable question about online delivery, and it deserves a straight answer. Data collection happens in your child's school laboratory, with their teacher, under the school's practical scheme. What an online session can do is interrogate a method before the laboratory slot, work through uncertainty propagation on the numbers the student brought back, and read a draft conclusion against criterion C. That is where the marks are decided in any case.

sections.heading: What Higher Level physics support costs in Dubai, and what each band includes
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are scarce and inconsistent, so the table below quotes what named providers publish and when it was read, rather than offering an average. The pattern worth understanding is that the band you choose changes the evidence you receive more than it changes the explanation quality in the room. Cheap sessions are rarely bad lessons; they are lessons with no record attached, which means you cannot tell whether they worked.

At the lower end sit university students and generalist science tutors. For a DP1 student who needs company while working through problem sets, that can be reasonable value. For a DP2 Higher Level candidate who needs a Paper 2 section marked to criteria, it usually is not, because marking Diploma physics accurately is a specialist skill and an unmarked hour produces no evidence. The middle band is qualified subject teachers, and the specialist band is where candidates who have taught the 2023 syllabus through a full cycle sit.

In-home visits carry the travel premium, which the market prices at roughly the difference between the online and in-home columns. For a Dubai family that premium buys proximity rather than specialism: the pool narrows to tutors who will drive to your community at the hour you need. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so the comparison here is offered as market information rather than as a service description. Online delivery is what removes the travel cost from the hour and widens the pool to whoever actually teaches Higher Level physics.

IB Gram publishes no price list on these pages. Rates depend on level, session length and the tutor matched, and the honest route is a free first lesson followed by a quoted block. What you should expect in writing before paying for anything: the rate per sixty minutes, whether marking time is inside or outside the hour, the cancellation terms, and what arrives after each session.

sections.heading: KHDA, the permit, and who is actually marking the script
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection reports are published on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and parents reasonably use them when choosing a school. They are much less useful for choosing a tutor, because an inspection judges a school's provision and says nothing about the person marking your child's physics script on a Tuesday evening.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists the application route through its smart app and e-services with a two working day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody.

Two practical consequences follow for a Dubai parent. The first is that you may ask any tutor whether they hold the permit, and a straight answer is reasonable to expect. The second concerns your child's own teachers: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction, so an arrangement with your child's own physics teacher is the wrong place to start regardless of emirate.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the specific authorisation issued to training institutes operating premises in Dubai. Any provider describing its tutors as approved by a regulator should be asked to show the permit number. The regulators named here are described so you can check things yourself, not to borrow their authority.

sections.heading: When the evidence says stop, change tutor, or change strategy
paragraphs: The hardest decision in paid tutoring is when to end it, and families who keep a log find it much easier than families who do not. Three patterns in the record justify three different decisions, and none of them require a difficult conversation about effort or attitude.

The first pattern is a flat error mix across six or more cold attempts. Same categories, same rates, no movement. That is a teaching mismatch rather than a student problem, and the right response is a different specialist, not more hours with the same one. The second pattern is the opposite: the error mix shifts, the raw score lags, and the student reports that papers feel more manageable. That is the normal shape of improvement in Higher Level physics and the worst possible moment to stop paying, because the score usually follows the mix by six to eight weeks.

The third pattern is the useful one nobody markets. The log shows physics errors falling towards zero while marks stay flat for reasons outside physics: time management across a full paper, a reading-speed problem, or mathematics fluency that collapses under exam pressure. In that case the correct decision is to stop buying physics hours and buy mathematics hours or sit a timed full paper with a stopwatch instead. A tutor who tells you that is worth keeping for the subject they do teach.

There is also the honest limit on availability. Higher Level physics specialists who have taught a full cycle of the 2023 syllabus are a small group across any platform, and the 5pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time window is where every Dubai family wants to be. If no specialist is free in your slot, IB Gram will say so rather than placing a general science tutor and calling it physics. The alternatives offered are a different time, a short wait with a named date, or a specialist in another time zone whose evening overlaps a Dubai afternoon.

process.title: Tell us the evidence you already hold
process.description: Year group, school, predicted grade, and whatever marked work exists. A photographed mock script is worth more than a paragraph of description, because it shows the error categories immediately rather than after three sessions of diagnosis.

process.title: Free first lesson with a cold question
process.description: The trial session includes a short unseen question attempted under time, not a conversation about goals. You receive the marked attempt afterwards. If the marking is vague or arrives without criteria quoted, you have learned something useful at no cost.

process.title: Baseline and a written plan
process.description: Across the first two or three sessions the specialist establishes a baseline across Paper 1B, Paper 2 and the investigation, then sets out the sequence of work and what evidence each stage will produce. The plan is a document you keep, not a verbal agreement.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a running log
process.description: Each session returns a marked attempt and adds a log row naming the error category. The log sets the next session's content, so the plan adapts to the evidence rather than to the school's scheme of work or to whatever felt difficult last week.

process.title: Half-term review against the log
process.description: Twice a term you read the record and decide: continue, change specialist, change subject, or stop. Any change of tutor carries the log across, so a new specialist starts from the evidence rather than from another three weeks of diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not general science tutors
whyPoints.description: Higher Level physics marking is a specific skill. A tutor matched for this page teaches the Diploma course at Higher Level and has marked the long structured questions in Paper 2 enough times to annotate against criteria rather than correct arithmetic.

whyPoints.title: A record you can read without us
whyPoints.description: Marked attempts, a mark log and dated investigation notes are yours. They make the arrangement measurable and they transfer: if you change provider, the evidence goes with your child rather than staying in somebody's session notes.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, honestly described
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes, so the pool is chosen for who teaches Physics HL rather than for who lives within a short drive of your community.

whyPoints.description: The AED figures on this page are market rates published by named providers with the date they were read. IB Gram quotes its own rate after the free first lesson, with the marking and cancellation terms stated in writing before anything is paid.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Feedback on the scientific investigation is given as questions and criterion references. Nothing is written for the student, and the boundary is explained to the student directly, because the malpractice consequence falls on them and not on a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated plainly
whyPoints.description: If no Higher Level physics specialist is free in your preferred slot, you are told and offered a dated alternative. A general science tutor is never substituted for a physics specialist on the assumption that nobody will check.

faqs.question: What should an IB DP Physics HL tutor in Dubai hand over after the first month?
faqs.answer: Four marked attempts, each on an unseen question tried under time, with annotation that quotes the assessment criteria. A log naming the error category for each attempt. A short written plan saying which category is being targeted next and why. If the investigation has started, a dated note of what was discussed at each stage. That is around ten minutes of work per session for the tutor and it is the only way you can judge the arrangement at four weeks rather than at the end of term, when the May session is already close.

faqs.question: Why does my son's physics score stay at 5 even though the sessions seem to be working?
faqs.answer: Usually because the error mix is changing before the total does. In Higher Level physics a student often fixes unit discipline and significant figures first, which frees marks that are immediately spent on harder extended-response questions they now attempt instead of leaving blank. The raw score looks flat while the script underneath is quite different. A mark log makes this visible: the unit column falls, the explanation column has not moved yet. The total usually follows six to eight weeks after the mix shifts, which is exactly when families lose patience.

faqs.question: Can a Physics HL tutor mark a Paper 2 section the way an examiner would?
faqs.answer: A specialist who has taught the 2023 syllabus through a full cycle can mark closely to the published criteria and show which statement earned each mark. That is not the same as access to live marking, and no tutor should imply otherwise. What accurate marking gives you is a script annotated with the criterion wording, so the student sees that a description was offered where an explanation was required. Ask to see one marked script before booking a block; the quality of the annotation tells you more than any profile summary.

faqs.question: How much of the Higher Level physics grade actually depends on the investigation?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks. There is a 3,000-word limit and schools typically allocate around ten hours of class time. Because it is internally assessed and then moderated, it is also the one component where early decisions matter most. A question that cannot produce data good enough to support a conclusion costs marks in all four criteria at once, and that choice is made weeks before any data exists.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring physics over video when so much of it is practical?
faqs.answer: Data collection happens in your child's school laboratory with their own teacher, under the school's practical scheme, and that does not change. The marks in the investigation are decided elsewhere: in the choice of question, in the uncertainty treatment, in whether the conclusion claims what the data supports, and in the honesty of the evaluation. All four are better worked through with a screen, a shared document and the student's own numbers in front of both of you than they are standing beside apparatus.

faqs.question: Which part of the Higher Level physics course causes Dubai students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: The fields material, for two reasons. It arrives when DP2 pressure is at its highest in most Dubai school calendars, and it demands explanation of a mechanism rather than recall of a relationship, which is the weakest habit in the average script. The quantum and nuclear material runs it close, usually because it is taught last and revised least. A mark log sorted by theme will tell you which of the two is costing your child more; the general answer is less useful than their own distribution.

faqs.question: Do we pay for the time a Physics HL tutor spends marking a paper?
faqs.answer: Ask before you book, because practice across the Dubai market varies and both answers are legitimate. Some tutors mark inside the hour, which means less teaching time and a script annotated during the session. Others mark between sessions and charge for it, or absorb it into a block rate. What you should not accept is a quote that leaves it ambiguous, because marking a full Paper 2 section carefully takes real time and an arrangement that does not price it tends to stop producing marked scripts after a few weeks.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in DP1. Is it too early for Higher Level physics support?
faqs.answer: DP1 is the cheapest place to fix habits, and unit discipline, graph reading and command-term response are habits. A student who leaves DP1 with those three in place spends DP2 on content and technique rather than on repairing arithmetic under time pressure. The DP1 case for support is weaker if the school's own physics set is small and well taught and the first mock is strong. In that situation a short investigation block later in the year is usually better value than a weekly slot from September.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection rating tell us about tutoring choices?
faqs.answer: Very little. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports, which is genuinely useful when choosing a school. It judges the school's provision as a whole, not the physics set your child sits in and certainly not the tutor you are considering. A school in a high band can still run a Higher Level physics class of twenty-four with one specialist, which is the situation that sends most Dubai families looking for a one-to-one slot in the first place.

faqs.question: Is a tutor advertised as an examiner worth the extra AED per hour for Physics HL?
faqs.answer: Only if the claim can be evidenced and only if it changes what you receive. Current examiner status should never be used to imply access to live mark schemes, boundaries or paper content, and no reputable provider would suggest it does. What matters is whether the person can mark a script accurately against published criteria and explain the gap to a sixteen-year-old. Plenty of tutors in the AED 200 to 450 specialist band do that well. Ask for a marked sample rather than paying for a label.

faqs.question: How long before the May session should a Physics HL student start one-to-one work?
faqs.answer: A full twenty-week block starting in the DP2 autumn term gives room for diagnosis, content repair, the investigation and then timed paper technique in sequence. Starting in February removes the first half of that, so the work becomes triage: find the two biggest error categories, drill them, and leave the rest. Triage still moves marks, but it moves fewer of them and it cannot repair a theme that was never properly taught. Earlier is cheaper per mark gained, which is the honest version of the urgency argument.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics HL and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches together?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it can be efficient because physics marks are frequently lost to mathematics. A tutor comfortable in both can separate a physics error from an algebra error in the same script, which stops the mark log blaming the wrong subject. The risk is dilution: two Higher Level subjects in one weekly hour means neither gets enough timed practice. If both are genuinely weak, two slots are better value than one slot splitting its attention between them.

faqs.question: Does a Physics HL grade matter for Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and it treats curricula differently, so the honest answer is to check the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel rather than trust a tutoring page. For the British track the published rule is five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. No verified IB points threshold was available for this page, so none is published here. Tutoring is not required for equivalency.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level physics specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date. The 5pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most requested across every Dubai community, and specialists who have taught the 2023 syllabus through a full cycle are a limited group on any platform. The options offered are a different time in the same week, a named wait until a slot opens, or a specialist whose own evening overlaps a Dubai afternoon. What is not offered is a general science tutor relabelled as a physics specialist.

faqs.question: Can physics sessions move during Ramadan or study leave?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should. Dubai school hours shorten during Ramadan and families often prefer sessions after Iftar, which moves a physics slot several hours later for a month. During study leave the useful pattern changes too: two shorter sessions a week with timed paper sections in between beats one long session, because the marked script is the thing that drives the next hour. Both are scheduling decisions rather than academic ones, and they are agreed in advance rather than renegotiated each week.

faqs.question: Should we ask for a recording of each physics session?
faqs.answer: Recordings are useful for a derivation the student will want to watch again, and far less useful than a marked script for judging whether the arrangement works. A recording shows what was taught; the script shows what the student can do unaided. If you have to choose, take the script. If a provider offers recordings instead of marking, treat that as a signal about where their time goes, and ask directly what arrives in writing after each session.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step is small: a free lesson in which your child attempts an unseen Higher Level physics question under time, and you receive the marked script afterwards with the criteria quoted on it. That single document tells you more about where the grade is sitting than a term of parents' evenings. If the evidence is worth continuing with, a specialist sets a baseline across Paper 1B, Paper 2 and the investigation, and you get a written plan and a running log. Sessions are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and the first one costs nothing.

intro.heading: What a Physics SL tutor actually costs in Dubai, and why the quotes differ
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai who searches for an IB DP physics SL home tutor is almost never asking about pedagogy. They are asking what this will cost per month, whether the cheap quote is a false economy, and whether the expensive one is buying anything real. The honest answer is that the Dubai market runs from roughly AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 an hour for a named premium tutor, and almost none of that spread is explained by the subject. It is explained by who is teaching, how long the session is, whether anyone is driving, and how close the May session is when you book.

Here is the market as it currently stands, taken from providers' own published pages. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both at the budget online end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with specialist exam-year tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED sits at AED 650. Monthly packages seen across the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices, and each one carries the name of the provider that published it.

Physics at Standard Level sits mid-band rather than at the top. The syllabus is 150 taught hours against 240 at Higher Level, the paper set is shorter, and the scientific investigation is the same single piece of work at both levels. That means a Standard Level brief is genuinely smaller than a Higher Level one, and a tutor pricing honestly will reflect that. A quote that charges Higher Level rates for Standard Level content is worth questioning, and so is one that quotes the same figure for Physics SL as for an English Language A paper, because the preparation load on the tutor is not the same.

What raises a Dubai quote above the band is usually logistics rather than expertise. A tutor crossing the city between Jumeirah and Mirdif at six in the evening is charging for ninety minutes of road as well as sixty minutes of physics, and that cost sits inside the hourly figure whether or not it is itemised. This is the single clearest argument for online delivery, and it is how IB Gram works everywhere in the UAE: lessons are one-to-one over live video, on your child's timetable, with no travel on anyone's invoice. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India.

The rest of this page is built around the number. There is a table of what the Dubai market charges by provider model, a table of the six variables that move a Physics SL quote in this emirate, a breakdown of the paper weightings so you can see what you are buying time against, and a plain account of what a tutor may and may not do with a scientific investigation. Where a figure has a source, the source is named. Where a figure does not exist publicly, the page says so instead of inventing one.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-sl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: This page is about the Diploma Programme, but Dubai families rarely arrive at Physics SL from nowhere. The two programmes below it feed into it, and what a student did in MYP Sciences or IGCSE Physics changes how many paid hours Standard Level will realistically take.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma takes six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Physics sits in the sciences group. At Standard Level it is 150 taught hours across five themes, assessed by two written papers and one internally marked scientific investigation. A student taking Physics SL alongside two or three Higher Levels is usually budgeting their hours, not their ability, and that is a scheduling problem a weekly session solves well.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs the largest Diploma cohort in the UAE by a wide margin, spread across schools under KHDA inspection. Because most Dubai schools follow an August to June year, Diploma Year 2 students sit the May session, and the scientific investigation deadline normally lands in the winter term. That compresses physics revision into a window that also contains Extended Essay deadlines, which is the practical reason Dubai families book paid support in the second term rather than the first.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is marked against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. There are no papers in the IB sense. A student who has only ever been graded on criteria arrives at Physics SL with strong investigation instincts and no experience of a timed written paper, which is a specific and fixable gap rather than a general weakness.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 and then move students straight into the Diploma without an IGCSE year in between. That makes the MYP to Physics SL transition sharper here than in a market where everyone sits IGCSE first. The missing piece is almost always exam technique under time pressure, so the first block of Dubai sessions for an ex-MYP student is usually spent on past-paper discipline rather than new content.

programmes.name: IGCSE and the British route
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum Dubai schools run Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE Physics to Year 11, then split students into A Level or the Diploma. An IGCSE Physics grade of 7 or above usually predicts a comfortable Standard Level start; a grade of 5 or 6 predicts a term of catching up on algebra and graph work rather than on physics concepts. Combined Science rather than separate Physics is a bigger gap and is worth naming early.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, so a large share of the emirate's Physics SL students come from IGCSE rather than MYP. The practical consequence for cost is that an IGCSE-trained student usually needs fewer total hours but a more targeted brief: significant figures, uncertainty propagation and radians, none of which IGCSE required of them.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-sl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Physics SL tutor is rarely booked alone. The subjects below are the ones Dubai Diploma students most often pair with Standard Level Physics, with a note on what each actually assesses so you can tell whether one specialist can sensibly cover two briefs.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics. Two written papers plus a scientific investigation. Marks leak at unit conversion, significant figures, and the difference between stating a relationship and explaining a mechanism.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same five themes with additional depth and a longer paper set across 240 taught hours. Rigid-body mechanics, induction and the quantum material sit heavier here. A Higher Level brief costs more per hour in the Dubai market because the tutor pool that genuinely covers it is smaller.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The natural partner to Physics. Calculus, trigonometry and vectors do most of the work in mechanics and fields. Students who lose physics marks on algebraic rearrangement rather than on concepts are usually having a maths problem wearing a physics costume.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-weighted and modelling-led, with graphical and technology-assisted methods. A Physics SL student on Applications often needs explicit help turning a gradient into a physical quantity, because the course trains them to describe a trend rather than derive a constant.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, organic chemistry. Shares the same paper architecture and the same scientific investigation format as Physics, so a student taking both can be coached on data analysis once and apply it twice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Heavier on command-term precision than on calculation. Pairs with Physics SL for students heading towards engineering-adjacent or health-adjacent courses who want a broad science base.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking, abstract data structures and a solution-development project. Dubai students who enjoy the modelling side of physics often take this instead of a third science, and the logic overlap with mechanics problem-solving is real.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Human factors, resource management, modelling and innovation, with a substantial design project. Shares the experimental-method vocabulary with Physics, which means uncertainty and reliability work done for one course transfers directly to the other.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that satisfies either the sciences or the individuals and societies requirement. Dubai students who want to drop a second laboratory science but keep a quantitative subject often move here, which changes the Physics SL brief to a standalone one.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-sl-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Dubai is wide, and a four o'clock session means something different in each part of it. The notes below describe what the district does to a weekday timetable, because scheduling is the practical constraint on paid tuition here, not distance from a tutor.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: High-rise and heavily expatriate, with schools reached by a bus run that frequently returns after four. A Marina Diploma student realistically starts a Physics session at five, and a lift queue in a tower is part of the arithmetic.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Walkable and dense, with many Diploma families in two-bedroom apartments where a quiet study corner is scarce. Short, focused sessions work better here than a two-hour block, which is a cost consideration as much as a comfort one.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Sits next to several of Dubai's larger school campuses, so the school run is short and a four-thirty start is genuinely possible. Al Barsha families are often the ones who can fit two shorter physics sessions into a week rather than one long one.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: A self-contained community with its own schools and a commute that empties early. Evening sessions here rarely slip, which matters when you are buying a fixed block of hours and cannot afford to waste one on a reschedule.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Villa communities with a long cross-city drive to many of the Diploma campuses. An in-home tutor serving Mirdif from the Jumeirah side is charging for that drive, which is where the AED 180 to 350 in-home band comes from.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Academy timetables and training blocks dominate the week, so a Physics SL schedule here has to flex around fixtures. Families in Sports City are the ones most likely to want sessions moved rather than cancelled, which only works when nobody is driving.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai and the Marina corridor
schoolClusters.note: The cluster where most Marina, JLT and Al Barsha Diploma students study. Several of these campuses run both the Diploma and a British route to A Level, so a Year 11 cohort splits and the Physics SL group can end up small.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and central Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Mirdif, Al Quoz, Deira and Dubai Silicon Oasis families mostly sit here. The mix of Indian, British and IB curricula in this cluster is why a single Dubai physics tutor is often asked about three different syllabuses in one week.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for Physics SL, by provider model
paragraphs: A Physics SL hour in Dubai costs between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 depending entirely on who is at the other end and how they reach your child. That spread is not a mystery and it is not a scam; it is five different products sold under one word. The table below compares the models rather than the brands, with each rate attributed to the provider that published it, because a comparison that quotes an unnamed competitor is not a comparison.

Read it from the bottom up. A university student teaching from their own notes is cheap because their preparation time is near zero and their risk of mis-teaching a topic is high. A subject specialist with Diploma teaching history costs two to four times as much because the hour is planned, the marking is done against the real criteria, and the diagnosis in week one saves hours in week six. An in-home visit costs more again, and the increment is travel, not teaching. A premium named tutor at AED 650 is buying scarcity and reputation, and whether that is worth four times the specialist rate is a judgement no page can make for you.

What matters for a Standard Level brief specifically is that the top of this range is priced for Higher Level scarcity. The pool of tutors who can teach Physics HL induction and quantum material to a confident Year 13 is small, and small pools price upward. Standard Level sits in a broader pool, so the honest place for a Physics SL quote in Dubai is the qualified-specialist band rather than the premium one. If you are being quoted premium rates for Standard Level content, ask what specifically justifies it.

sections.heading: The six things that move a Physics SL quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Two Dubai families can be quoted AED 180 and AED 380 for the same Standard Level syllabus in the same week and both quotes can be fair. The variables below explain almost all of the gap, and five of the six are under your control. Knowing which one is driving your number is the difference between negotiating and guessing.

The largest single factor is who is driving. An in-home rate in Dubai contains the tutor's road time, and across this city that is rarely less than forty minutes each way in the after-school window. The second is session length: a ninety-minute slot almost always costs less per minute than a sixty-minute one, because the tutor's setup and travel overhead is spread across more teaching. The third is when you book. Specialist evening slots between four and eight on Gulf Standard Time are the scarce resource in Dubai, and they are gone by February in an examination year.

The remaining three are level, pairing and format. Standard Level should price below Higher Level. A student who books Physics and Mathematics with the same specialist usually pays less in total than two separate briefs, because the diagnostic work overlaps. And a small group of two or three costs less per student than one-to-one, at the price of a shared pace, which works for syllabus coverage and badly for fixing one student's specific misconception. Online delivery removes the travel line entirely, which is why IB Gram prices a Dubai lesson the same as a Sharjah one.

sections.heading: What you are buying time against: the Physics SL assessment
paragraphs: Before you decide how many hours to buy, it helps to know what those hours have to cover. Under the science guides first assessed in 2025, IB Physics at Standard Level is assessed by two written papers and one internally marked scientific investigation. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 is short-answer and extended-response. The investigation is a single piece of individual research. Confirm the exact structure against the guide your child's school is teaching, because schools transitioned to the current guides on different timetables.

The weightings matter for budgeting because they tell you where an hour is worth most. Paper 1 carries 36% of the final grade and Paper 2 carries 44%, with the investigation at 20%. A family buying six hours of support is usually better served putting four of them into Paper 2 technique and two into the investigation than spreading them evenly, simply because Paper 2 is the largest single block of marks and the one where method marks are won and lost on phrasing.

The data-analysis section of Paper 1 is the part Dubai students most often underprice. It rewards a narrow, teachable skill set: reading a gradient, propagating an uncertainty, choosing a sensible number of significant figures, and saying what a y-intercept physically represents. None of that requires new content knowledge, which makes it unusually cheap to fix. A single well-run session on uncertainty treatment can move more marks than a month of re-reading the kinematics chapter, and that is the kind of calculation a published weighting table lets you make for yourself.

sections.heading: In-home tutoring in Dubai: what it costs and what it is actually for
paragraphs: In-home tuition is a real product with a real market in Dubai, and it is worth understanding properly rather than dismissing. Bestimate's rate table puts an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home blocks of four two-hour sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Against an online specialist band of AED 150 to 300, the premium is somewhere between a fifth and double, depending on which end of each band you compare.

What that premium buys is presence. For a younger child who will not sit still without an adult in the room, presence is worth paying for. For a Diploma student at Standard Level, who is sixteen or seventeen and has a laptop, a screen-shared past paper and an annotated PDF is not a compromise; it is a better record of the lesson than a verbal explanation they will not remember on Friday. The thing presence cannot buy is choice. A Dubai family hiring in-home is choosing from tutors who can reach their district inside the school-run window, which in practice means a handful of people, and the one who teaches Physics SL well may not be among them.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE. Our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses, and no sentence on this site should be read as promising that. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with the specialist chosen for the syllabus rather than for the postcode. Home visits are part of our India service and nothing about them applies here. If physical presence is the thing you need, a local in-home tutor is the right purchase and this is not the right page.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai school fees and the 2026-27 freeze
paragraphs: Tuition is a line in a household budget that already contains a school fee, and Dubai gives you an unusually clear reference point this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning a two-year Diploma, that removes one variable from the forecast.

The scale of the market is worth knowing too. In 2024-25 Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest share of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate a smaller but growing one. For 2026-27 the emirate is adding seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent. More IB places means more Diploma students competing for the same small pool of Physics specialists in the same evening slots, which is a supply story with a price consequence.

Set against that, one weekly Physics SL session at the qualified-specialist band costs roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, which is Bestimate's own mid-band monthly estimate for weekly one-hour sessions. An exam-year specialist on the same basis runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Those are market numbers, published by a market source, and they are the right order of magnitude to plan with. IB Gram quotes after the free trial lesson rather than publishing a fixed list, because the right number depends on how many hours your child actually needs, and nobody can know that before the first session.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: what a paid tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the Physics SL grade comes from one internally marked piece of individual research, and it is the part of the course where paid help goes wrong most often. The rule is simple to state and easy to breach by accident: the work submitted must be the student's own, in the student's own words, and a tutor's contribution must be teaching and feedback. Anything beyond that is malpractice under IB academic-honesty rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor.

In practice, a session on the investigation is spent on the things the student cannot easily do alone. Pressure-testing a research question until it is narrow enough to generate a real relationship rather than a demonstration of something already known. Working out whether the chosen variable range will produce a gradient worth analysing. Reading a draft and saying where the evaluation is thin, where an uncertainty has been stated but not propagated, and where a conclusion has overreached its data. Explaining what each assessment criterion is actually asking for, in plain language, because the criterion wording is written for teachers.

What a session never includes is text. A tutor does not supply sentences for the report, does not rewrite paragraphs into better English, and does not hand over a method to copy. Ask any prospective tutor what they do with a draft; the answer tells you a great deal. Providers in this market do sell finished investigation reports, at prices around AED 3,750, and buying one is an academic-integrity breach that can cost a student their Diploma. There is no version of that transaction that is worth the risk, and no page on this site will offer it.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge for tutoring in Dubai, and how to check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, not informal. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure you see circulating for this should be treated as unverified. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit applies to centres with premises, and no online platform should describe itself as holding it unless it does.

There is one more rule worth knowing, because it affects a request Dubai parents make often. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but do not ask for your child's own classroom teacher as a paid tutor. It puts the teacher's position at risk and it compromises the person who marks the investigation.

sections.heading: What happens if no Physics SL specialist is free in your slot
paragraphs: Every tutoring platform runs out of people sometimes, and most of them conceal it. Between four and eight in the evening Gulf Standard Time, in the term before the May session, Physics specialists are the scarcest resource in this market. The honest version of what happens next is short, and it is worth having before you book rather than after.

First, we tell you the real wait rather than taking a booking and hoping. If a Physics Standard Level specialist is not free in your preferred weekday slot, the options are a different time in the same week, a weekend slot, or a named date when a slot opens. Second, if no UAE-timezone specialist covers the brief at all, we say so and name what we can offer instead: a specialist in another timezone whose schedule overlaps your evenings, with the time difference stated plainly before you decide. Third, if the honest answer is that we cannot staff it well, we say that too. A badly matched tutor costs more than no tutor, because it burns a term and convinces a student that help does not work.

This matters for cost as much as for quality. A family who books a block in April at a premium rate because nothing else is available has paid a scarcity premium that a January booking would have avoided. The practical advice for a Dubai Diploma family is to settle the physics question in the first term, when choice is wide and rates are at the bottom of the band, rather than in the last ten weeks when they are not. The free trial lesson exists so that first decision costs nothing.

faqs.question: What should we budget per month for IB DP Physics SL support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For one weekly sixty-minute session, Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts the budget band at AED 240 to 600 a month, the mid band at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Standard Level Physics usually sits in the mid band rather than the top one, because the syllabus is 150 taught hours against 240 at Higher Level. Market monthly packages of eight online sessions are advertised around AED 799. Those are market figures from published sources, not IB Gram prices; we quote after the free trial lesson, once we know how many hours the brief genuinely needs.

faqs.question: Why is a Physics Standard Level tutor quoted below a Higher Level one?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, and both are legitimate. The syllabus is smaller: 150 taught hours against 240, with less depth in rigid-body mechanics, induction and the quantum material. And the tutor pool is larger, because more people can teach Standard Level confidently than can teach Higher Level, and small pools price upward. The scientific investigation is identical at both levels, so that part of the brief costs the same. If you are quoted premium rates for Standard Level content, ask what specifically justifies the band, because the answer should be about your child's particular gap rather than about the subject name.

faqs.question: Does a ninety-minute Physics session cost proportionally more than a sixty-minute one?
faqs.answer: Usually less, per minute. A tutor's overhead per session is largely fixed: preparing the material, setting up, reviewing last week's work, writing the note afterwards. Spread across ninety minutes rather than sixty, that overhead costs you less per teaching minute. For Physics specifically, ninety minutes also fits a complete past-paper component with marking and review inside one sitting, which sixty rarely does. The trade is concentration. A Diploma student at the end of a Dubai school day may get more from two sixty-minute sessions in a week than from one ninety-minute block, so ask about both patterns before you commit.

faqs.question: Are AED tutoring rates in Dubai higher than in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: For in-home tuition, generally yes, because Dubai has more competition for specialist tutors, longer cross-city drives, and the densest private-school market in the country at 227 schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25. Travel premiums scale with distance and traffic, and Dubai supplies plenty of both. For online tuition the geography largely disappears: a lesson delivered over live video costs the same whether the family is in Mirdif, Sharjah or Fujairah, because nothing is being driven. That is one of the clearer practical arguments for the online format in this market, separate from any question about teaching quality.

faqs.question: Do Physics tutoring rates in Dubai rise as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Effective rates do, even when advertised rates do not. The scarce resource in Dubai is a specialist slot between four and eight in the evening on Gulf Standard Time, and in an examination year those are substantially committed by February. What a late-booking family faces is not usually a higher published figure but a narrower choice: fewer specialists, worse times, and less room to negotiate a block discount. Booking the physics question in the first term, when choice is wide, is the single cheapest decision available. The free trial lesson is free in November and free in April, so there is no cost to settling it early.

faqs.question: Is a tutor charging AED 500 an hour five times better than one at AED 100?
faqs.answer: No, and the market does not work that way. The jump from AED 45 to AED 200 usually buys something real: planning time, marking against the actual assessment criteria, and knowledge of the current subject guide. The jump from AED 300 to AED 650 mostly buys scarcity and reputation, which may matter for a very specific Higher Level brief and rarely matters for Physics Standard Level. Judge the purchase on what the first session produces. A tutor who can name which component your child is losing marks in, and show it on a marked paper, is worth more than a higher number on an invoice.

faqs.question: Do we pay for the time a tutor spends marking a past paper?
faqs.answer: Ask, because providers differ and the answer changes the real hourly cost. Some include marking in the session rate and do it between lessons; some mark live during the session, which uses teaching time you have paid for; some bill it separately. For Physics, marking matters more than in many subjects, because the diagnosis lives in the working rather than the final answer, and a marker who annotates where method marks were lost gives you something to act on. Clarify whether marking is included, how quickly the marked script comes back, and whether it arrives annotated or just scored.

faqs.question: Is in-home Physics SL tuition in Dubai something IB Gram sells?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and our tutors do not travel to Dubai addresses. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared past papers and annotated PDFs you keep. Home visits are a service we run only in India. In-home tuition does exist in Dubai from other providers, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on who you ask, and if physical presence in the room is what your child needs, that is a legitimate purchase from a local tutor rather than from us.

faqs.question: How many hours of Physics SL support does one term usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the first session finds, which is why we diagnose before quoting. A student losing marks on uncertainty treatment and graph interpretation in Paper 1B can see real movement in three or four sessions, because that is a narrow teachable skill rather than missing content. A student who never properly learned Theme A mechanics is looking at a term of weekly work. A student whose physics problem is actually an algebra problem needs the maths addressed first or the physics hours are wasted. Six weeks of weekly sessions is the usual review point: long enough to see movement, short enough that stopping costs little.

faqs.question: What does supporting the scientific investigation add to the bill?
faqs.answer: Typically two to four sessions spread across the drafting period rather than a separate retainer, because the work is bursty: question design early, a mid-point check on whether the data will support analysis, and a draft review. It is twenty per cent of the grade, so the marks-per-hour return is usually good. What it does not include is any writing. A tutor pressure-tests the research question, explains what each criterion rewards, and names where an evaluation is thin. The student writes every word. Providers selling finished reports in this market charge around AED 3,750; that purchase risks the Diploma itself.

faqs.question: Is VAT included in the AED figures Dubai tutors quote?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because practice varies and the published figure is often ambiguous. We cannot state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and no page should. What you can reasonably insist on is clarity about the specific number you are being quoted: whether it is inclusive or exclusive, and what the total monthly charge will be. Any provider who cannot answer that plainly about their own pricing is telling you something useful about how the rest of the arrangement will run.

faqs.question: Our budget stops at AED 250 an hour. What does that buy in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online, which is the band Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 within and where most of the genuinely useful Standard Level teaching in this market sits. It does not buy in-home visits, which start around AED 180 and climb to AED 500 once travel is priced in, and it does not buy a premium named tutor at AED 650. For Physics SL that is a reasonable place to be. The extra money above this band mostly buys scarcity for Higher Level briefs, and the extra below it mostly buys a generalist reading from notes.

faqs.question: Is a group of three cheaper per student than one-to-one for Physics SL?
faqs.answer: Yes, usually substantially, and the trade is pace. In a group the tutor sets one speed, which suits a syllabus sweep before mocks and suits a single student's specific misconception badly. Physics misconceptions are stubborn and individual: one student is mishandling vector components, another is fine with vectors and cannot propagate an uncertainty. A group session cannot chase both. If the brief is broad coverage, a group is good value. If the brief is a diagnosed gap, one-to-one is cheaper in total hours even at a higher rate per hour.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we pause lessons over Eid or the summer?
faqs.answer: On pay-as-you-go nothing happens, because nothing is prepaid. On a term block it depends entirely on the terms, which is why the question belongs in the conversation before you agree one. Ask what notice a pause needs, whether unused sessions expire, and whether the slot is held. Dubai families pause often: Eid, the summer break, travel between terms, and the examination weeks themselves. Sessions can also shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan rather than being cancelled. A provider whose answer to all of this is vague is selling you an open-ended monthly payment.

faqs.question: Why do Dubai quotes for the same Physics syllabus vary so widely between providers?
faqs.answer: Because the word tutor covers five different products. A university student working from their own notes, a planned lesson from a subject specialist, an IB specialist who knows the current guide and the investigation criteria, an in-home visit that includes a driver's time, and a premium named tutor selling scarcity. Those sit at roughly AED 33 to 65, AED 150 to 300, AED 200 to 450, AED 180 to 500 and AED 500 to 650 an hour respectively, each figure published by a provider in this market. The variation is the product differing, not the subject.

faqs.question: Does the tutor's own location in Dubai change what we pay for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Not for the lesson itself. When nothing is being driven, a tutor in Dubai Marina and a tutor two time zones away cost the same to deliver, so the figure reflects their teaching rather than their postcode. What location does affect is scheduling: a specialist whose working day overlaps Gulf Standard Time evenings can hold the four to eight slot that Dubai Diploma families want, and one who cannot will offer you a morning. Where no UAE-timezone specialist covers the brief, we say so and state the time difference plainly before you decide anything.

If the honest answer is that your child does not need paid help, we will tell you that too.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-sl-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Physics at Standard Level to Dubai students. Each starts with a scored diagnostic rather than a syllabus tour, explains every lost mark in writing on returned work, and keeps a dated record of the investigation so the student's authorship is always demonstrable.

intro.heading: The documents that tell you whether Physics SL support is working
paragraphs: IB Diploma Physics at Standard Level runs to 150 teaching hours and is assessed by three components. Paper 1 lasts ninety minutes and carries 36%, divided between 1A, thirty multiple-choice questions across the five themes, and 1B, data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 also lasts ninety minutes and carries 44% in short-answer and extended-response form. The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 and carries the final 20%. Each of those produces a document a parent can read.

Reading them is the point. Confidence is a poor proxy for progress in Physics, because the subject rewards narrow technical habits that feel unremarkable while they are being learned. A student who has been shown how to propagate an uncertainty will not feel different that evening, and a student who has had a comfortable hour of explanation will feel much better while losing exactly the same marks a fortnight later. The documents separate those two situations within a month.

Three documents do most of the work. The first is a scored diagnostic, taken in the opening week, where thirty multiple-choice questions are marked by theme rather than totalled; this turns a vague worry into a list of two or three themes. The second is a marked extended answer, with every lost mark explained in a sentence rather than struck through. The third is the dated version history behind the investigation, which both demonstrates authorship and shows whether the work is running ahead of the school's internal deadline or behind it. None of the three takes a specialist to interpret once you know what each one is for, and all three can be requested in the first fortnight rather than hoped for later.

A fourth, slower document matters as well: the pattern across successive marked scripts. One script is noise. Four scripts over six weeks, with the same losses counted each time, show whether a habit has changed. That pattern is the thing we put on the table at the six-week review, and it is what makes continuing, retargeting or stopping a decision rather than a default. Stopping is a legitimate outcome in this subject, because a Physics SL problem is often one narrow habit rather than a general weakness, and a habit closes in weeks rather than terms.

What follows works through those documents in order, then covers the theme-by-theme error patterns that recur in Dubai Standard Level scripts, what a progress note may and may not claim about a child, and how an online session leaves a better record than a verbal summary at a front door. Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; those are a service we provide only in India.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme

The predicted grade is the document families fixate on and the least informative of the four, because it compresses several different skills into one digit. The mock script is the most informative, since it is usually the only timed, full-length, externally styled evidence a student generates before the examination session itself.

For a Physics SL family the first genuinely comparable evidence therefore tends to arrive in the first term of DP2. Before then, the usable material is whatever the subject teacher has marked, which is why we ask for it in the first message rather than waiting for a mock to exist.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, is the direct ancestor of both Paper 1B and the investigation's data-analysis marks. A marked criterion C task is therefore the single most predictive MYP document for Physics SL. A student with strong knowledge marks and thin processing marks will struggle on precisely the components that are hardest to repair late in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: The IB continuum schools in Al Barsha, Nad Al Sheba and Mirdif run MYP Sciences through to MYP 5, and the Standard or Higher Level decision is usually taken at that point. Asking for a marked criterion C task rather than an overall grade gives a Dubai family a far better basis for that decision than a report comment, and it takes one email to obtain.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Physics SL bridge
programmes.description: IGCSE Physics covers much of theme A and parts of themes B and C, but with far less emphasis on uncertainty and on criticising a method. The bridging document worth collecting is a single marked data question: given a table of results, can the student plot the right quantity, extract a gradient with units and estimate an uncertainty? Those three abilities predict Standard Level performance better than an IGCSE grade does.
programmes.countryNote: UK curricula account for 37 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, so most Physics SL students in the emirate arrive from IGCSE. Cambridge runs its International GCSE series in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel in May/June and November, so a student who sat a November series arrives in the Diploma with fresher practical experience and a shorter gap to close.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-sl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics SL is the subject in the URL. The grid below shows it with the Diploma subjects Dubai families most often support in the same term, with each entry written around the document that subject produces rather than its reputation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: At Standard Level: Paper 1A with thirty multiple-choice questions, Paper 1B on data, Paper 2 extended response, and a 24-mark investigation. The document to ask for first is a theme-scored diagnostic, because a total tells you nothing about which of the five themes failed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Assessed on the same model with the same four-criterion investigation, so the evidence looks structurally identical. A marked calculation chain shows whether marks go on chemistry or on quantitative discipline, and the answer usually applies to the physics too.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Carries the heaviest extended-response load of the three sciences, so marking turnaround governs how much evidence a week can produce. Its statistical treatment of data overlaps directly with Paper 1B, and one data session frequently serves both subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra Physics assumes sits largely here, and AA Paper 1 is sat without technology. A student losing physics marks to rearrangement errors produces scripts that look like physics failures and are not, which a marked AA script settles quickly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics block supports data analysis well, and technology is permitted in both AI papers. The gap to watch is manual manipulation, since Physics examinations expect algebraic fluency that the AI course drills less insistently.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution component leaves a dated development record of its own, which makes it a useful parallel for students learning why dated versions matter. Computational thinking transfers to modelling questions in themes A and D.

subjects.description: Shares energy and systems content with themes B and E, and its data questions reward the same handling of uncertainty. A sensible second science for a Physics SL student who does not want a third laboratory subject.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design cycle produces a large internal workload that competes with the investigation for the same weeks. Families taking both should map the two internal deadlines against each other during DP1 rather than discovering the clash in DP2.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal commentaries give a clear draft history, and graph-reading discipline carries across to Paper 1B. A frequent third subject for Dubai Physics SL students heading towards engineering or business routes.

sections.heading: The thirty-question diagnostic, and what it tells you that a report cannot
paragraphs: Paper 1A at Standard Level is thirty multiple-choice questions sampling all five themes, and that structure makes it an unusually efficient diagnostic. Scored by theme rather than totalled, thirty questions separate a student who is weak in one area from one who is thinly spread across all of them. Those are different problems with different costs: the first is two or three sessions, the second is a term. A school report cannot distinguish them, because it reports one grade.

A theme-scored result also exposes the pattern that worries families most and matters least: a student scoring well on the themes taught in DP1 and badly on whatever was taught last month. That is almost always a settling problem rather than a capability problem, and the remedy is practice rather than re-teaching. The opposite pattern, weakness in the earliest theme taught, usually means a foundation gap carried in from IGCSE, and that needs different work.

Multiple choice has a second use that is rarely exploited. A wrong answer in physics is usually wrong for a recognisable reason, because the distractors are built from common misconceptions: a sign error, a confusion between potential and field, a half-remembered proportionality. Asking a student why they chose a particular wrong option produces more diagnostic information in thirty seconds than a page of working, and it is the fastest way to find a misconception that has been invisible all term.

The table is the format in which we return the result, and it is what a family should expect in the first week rather than at the end of a month. If a provider cannot score a diagnostic by theme and tell you what each wrong answer suggests, they are measuring a total rather than diagnosing a student, and the hours that follow will be planned by guesswork.

sections.heading: Marking a Physics SL extended answer the way an examiner does
paragraphs: The second document is a marked extended answer, and the useful version explains every lost mark in a sentence rather than striking a line through the page. An extended-response physics mark is awarded for a specific statement: a correct equation quoted, a correct substitution, a stated causal link, a unit, a conclusion in context. A student who sees a total of four out of seven learns nothing. A student who sees that three marks went on an unstated causal link, a missing unit and a prefix error learns three separate, fixable things.

Three loss types recur in Dubai Standard Level scripts. The first is the unstated link: a student writes that the current increases and that the resistance falls without saying that one causes the other, which collects the knowledge mark and forfeits the reasoning one. The second is unit and significant-figure discipline: an answer quoted to five figures from two-figure data, or a milli written where a micro was meant. The third is working omitted because the student could do it mentally, which forfeits method credit entirely.

None of those three is a physics problem, which is why they respond so quickly to being named. A student who receives three consecutive scripts with the same three loss types written out usually eliminates two of them inside a month, and the gain appears across every theme at once rather than in whichever topic was being studied. That is what makes marked extended answers a better investment of a session than another explanation of the same content.

The command term governs how much of this an answer owes, and that is worth checking on any returned script. A two-mark state question needs two facts, not a paragraph. A four-mark explain question needs a chain of four linked statements. A determine question needs visible working. Students who write in the same register for every question lose marks on the long ones while wasting time on the short ones, and the pattern is visible on any marked paper within two minutes.
bullets: Every lost mark explained in one sentence on the returned script
Causal links written explicitly, not implied by adjacency
