sections.heading: The data-analysis trail: what a marked Paper 1B question proves
paragraphs: Paper 1B is the data-based and experimental section inside Paper 1, and it is the most testable part of Physics SL. Its skills are a short, fixed list, which means progress on it is unusually easy to evidence: either the student plots the quantity that linearises the relationship or they do not, either they state the units of a gradient or they do not, either their suggested improvement is specific to this apparatus or it is generic. Each of those is a yes or no on a marked script.

Because the list is short, a family can hold the whole of it. Identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables. Choose what to plot to produce a straight line. Draw the line and extract a gradient with units, then say what it physically represents. Estimate absolute and percentage uncertainty and propagate it. Distinguish random from systematic error by the shape of the data. Suggest an improvement that names this apparatus rather than any apparatus.

The last of those is where Standard Level students are separated. Repeat the experiment and take an average is a sentence that applies to every experiment ever performed and earns nothing. Replace the metre rule with a travelling microscope, because the uncertainty in the measurement is comparable to the difference being measured, is an observation about this experiment and earns the mark. Learning to tell those apart is practice in criticism, not additional physics.

Three sessions typically cover the whole list, and the evidence that it has landed is two consecutive marked 1B questions where the routines appear without prompting. That is a short, cheap and verifiable piece of progress, which is why we usually recommend it as the first block of hours a Physics SL family buys rather than the last.

sections.heading: The investigation's paper trail: dated milestones, one author
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20% of the Physics SL grade, is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each, and is capped at 3,000 words. Around ten hours of class time are allocated to it. The evidence worth building alongside it is a dated artefact at each milestone, which does two jobs at once: it keeps the work ahead of the school's internal deadline, and it demonstrates beyond argument that the student produced it.

The milestones are predictable. A research question, written before any data exists. A method with the measurements and their uncertainties listed in advance. A session in the school laboratory, supervised by the school, producing raw data. A processing stage where that data becomes graphs with error bars. A first full draft. A second draft responding to questions. Six dated files, each one visibly building on the last, is a stronger record than any declaration of authenticity.

Dubai schools run their own internal deadlines and their own authenticity conversations, and a student who can walk a coordinator through six dated files is in a different position from one who submits a single polished document. That is worth stating plainly because the essay mills in this market sell completed investigations, and the student who buys one is the person who faces an IB malpractice case rather than the seller.

Our boundary is the same here as everywhere on this site. A tutor may teach a technique on an unrelated experiment, ask whether a research question can be answered with the apparatus available, ask what a graph shows, and point out where a reader cannot follow a method. The student designs the investigation, runs it, processes the data and types the report. Nothing in the submitted file originates with us, and we will say so to a school if ever asked.

sections.heading: Theme-by-theme error patterns in Dubai Standard Level scripts
paragraphs: Across marked Physics SL scripts the same errors recur, and they cluster by theme in ways worth knowing before a diagnostic. Theme A produces sign errors and unresolved vectors, usually because a free-body diagram was never drawn. Theme B produces energy accounting that does not balance and circuit reasoning that treats a changing load as fixed. Theme C produces misread graphs, with displacement and phase confused on a wave diagram that was read too quickly.

Theme D is the most consistent source of lost marks at Standard Level, because field strength and potential are distinct quantities with similar names, related definitions and different units. A student who has not separated them cleanly will answer field questions with potential reasoning and lose marks in a way that looks random and is entirely systematic. One session built around the distinction, with the units written out each time, usually resolves it.

Theme E produces two patterns: decay problems where the logarithm handling is the obstacle rather than the physics, and unit prefix slips in energy values, where a mega and a kilo change places and a correct method yields a wrong answer. The first is a mathematics issue and belongs in a mathematics conversation. The second is transcription discipline and responds to a checking routine applied under timed conditions.

Those patterns are the reason a theme-scored diagnostic is worth an hour. The remedy for each cluster is different in content and in length, from part of a session for a prefix habit to several weeks for a foundation gap carried in from IGCSE. A provider who quotes a term of general revision without knowing which cluster is live is quoting a number rather than a plan, and the evidence to tell them apart takes sixty minutes to produce.

sections.heading: What a progress note says about your child, and what it must never claim
paragraphs: A session note should be short enough to read in thirty seconds: the date, the theme, the component, the marks available, the marks scored, the loss types and the one piece of follow-up work set. That is a record, and it accumulates into something you can audit at six weeks. A note written in assessment vocabulary, or padded to look thorough, gets filed unread, which makes it worse than no note at all.

There are three things such a note will never contain. It will not say that your child is on track for a particular grade, because the grade comes from weighted components compared against boundaries set for that session, and a tutor marking part of one subject cannot know how the rest will score. It will not contain a statistic about our own results, because we cannot show you the sample, the date and the method behind any such figure. It will not promise a timescale for a student nobody has yet assessed.

Records about a child are also personal data, and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs how they are held. What we keep is the enquiry details, the session notes and the marked work. What we do not collect is a photograph, a full school timetable or medical information, because none of those are needed to teach Physics. Ask for deletion and the file goes, and you are told when; we offer copies of the marked scripts first, because a family that paid for a term of marking should keep the output.

The one note that is worth writing at length is the handover. If a tutor changes inside the network, the new tutor should receive the theme diagnostic, the counted loss types and the investigation milestone dates rather than a conversation. That takes one document, it transfers in a day, and it is the difference between restarting and continuing. Families leaving entirely can take the same document with them.

sections.heading: Six weeks of evidence, and the three outcomes of the review
paragraphs: Six weeks of weekly sessions should produce four or five marked scripts, a theme diagnostic from week one, a count of loss types for the first fortnight and the last, and whatever investigation milestones fell inside the period. That is enough to make a decision rather than a renewal. The review is a short meeting with those documents in front of both of us, and it produces one of exactly three outcomes.

The first outcome is to continue with the same target, which is right when the counts are falling but the habit is not yet automatic. The second is to change the target, which is right when the original diagnosis has closed and a different cluster has surfaced; this is common after a theme D intervention, where fixing the field and potential distinction reveals a separate pace problem on Paper 1A. The third is to stop, because the problem was narrow and is now fixed.

Stopping is the outcome this market structurally avoids, and it is the one we most want to be trusted on. A Physics SL difficulty is frequently one habit: a prefix slip, a missing causal link, an unpractised data routine. Those close in weeks, not terms, and a weekly slot that continues afterwards is costing a family money for reassurance. We will say so with the scripts on the table, and families who hear it once tend to come back in DP2 when something genuinely new appears.

Two Dubai-specific items belong in that conversation. Schools here set their own mock windows, so the review should be timed to land after a real script exists rather than at a fixed calendar point. And during Ramadan a session that moves to a post-Iftar slot keeps running, where a session that simply pauses often does not resume; the evidence trail has a gap in it either way, and planning for that beats discovering it.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one in Dubai, and the record a session leaves behind
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen where tutor and student write on the same page, timed to Gulf Standard Time and fitted around a Dubai school day. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and no sentence on this site should suggest otherwise to a family in this emirate.

For a page about evidence the relevant argument is what each arrangement leaves behind. Work exchanged as files exists in two places, can be read by a parent who is travelling, and survives a change of tutor. A shared screen keeps the session's working rather than losing it inside an exercise book. The theme diagnostic, the counted loss types and the investigation milestone dates are documents rather than recollections. A verbal summary at a front door leaves nothing to audit at week six.

The laboratory itself stays with the school, and that is the correct arrangement. Your child's apparatus, access and supervision come from their own teacher, because the investigation has to be their own work under their school's conditions. What a tutor adds is the design before the practical and the processing afterwards, which is where most of the 24 marks sit. For Paper 1B, analysis of data on a shared screen is a better tool than two people sharing one printout.

On availability we would rather be plain than optimistic. Standard Level Physics is reasonably well covered and a match in Dubai usually takes a few days. Where no Physics specialist is free in the slot you need, we will say so and offer a different time or a tutor in another time zone whose evening is your afternoon. What we will not do is seat a general science tutor in a Diploma Physics slot and let the arrangement imply a specialism that is not there.

process.title: Score a diagnostic before planning anything
process.description: The first session produces a theme-scored result across all five themes and one marked extended answer. Thirty questions separate a single weak theme from a thin spread, and those are different problems with different costs. Everything after this is planned from that document rather than from a syllabus.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, free, no card details taken, no obligation afterwards. Your child works with the tutor we actually propose, on their own recent Physics work, and the session ends with a short written note of what it found. You keep that note whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Name the component and the loss types
process.description: Before the second session we put in writing which component the hours target and which loss types we are counting: causal links, units and prefixes, omitted working, or a data routine. Counting something specific is what makes the six-week review a measurement rather than an opinion.

process.title: Produce a marked script every week
process.description: Work set after each session and returned marked before the next, with every lost mark explained in a sentence. Over a Dubai term that is around a dozen dated scripts. Keep them together; the count across them is the evidence, and any single script is noise.

process.title: Review after six weeks and decide
process.description: Continue with the same target, change the target, or stop. We bring the diagnostic, the scripts and the counts, and the decision is yours. Stopping is a real answer in a subject where the problem is often a single habit that closes in a few weeks.

whyPoints.title: A theme-scored diagnostic in week one
whyPoints.description: Thirty multiple-choice questions scored by theme rather than totalled, plus a question about why each wrong option was chosen. That separates a single weak theme from a general pace problem, and the two need different hours and different numbers of them.

whyPoints.title: Every lost mark explained in writing
whyPoints.description: A returned script says which sentence was missing, which unit was dropped and which line of working was skipped. A total of four out of seven teaches nothing. Three named losses teach three fixable things, and two of them usually close inside a month.

whyPoints.title: Loss types counted, not described
whyPoints.description: We count causal links, unit and prefix errors, omitted working and data-routine failures, first fortnight against last. Counts are what a parent can genuinely audit at a review, and they move weeks before a Dubai school report says anything.

whyPoints.title: Six dated investigation files, one author
whyPoints.description: Question, method, raw data, processing, draft, final version. Each one dated and visibly built on the last, which keeps the work ahead of the school deadline and makes authorship a matter of record rather than of assertion.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be shown
whyPoints.description: No predicted grades from a tutor who marks part of one subject, no satisfaction percentage, no proportion-improved figure, no timescale quoted for an unassessed student. Pages in this search publish all of those, sometimes in two contradictory versions.

whyPoints.title: The records are yours
whyPoints.description: Scripts, notes and the diagnostic transfer with the student, inside the network or out of it, under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. Ask for deletion and the file goes, with copies offered first. Student work is not a retention device.

faqs.question: What is the first piece of evidence a Physics SL tutor should produce?
faqs.answer: A theme-scored diagnostic, in the first week, not a syllabus overview. Thirty multiple-choice questions marked by theme rather than totalled will tell you whether your child has one weak theme or a thin spread across five, and those are different problems costing different amounts to fix. Add one marked extended answer with every lost mark explained in a sentence, and you have a document you can plan from. A first session that produces only an impression has produced nothing you can check later.

faqs.question: How do thirty multiple-choice questions diagnose a Physics SL problem?
faqs.answer: Paper 1A samples all five themes, so thirty questions give coverage no class test provides. Scored by theme, the result separates a single weak area from a pace problem spread evenly across the paper. The distractors help too: wrong options in physics are built from common misconceptions, so asking why a particular wrong answer was chosen reveals a sign error, a field-and-potential confusion or a half-remembered proportionality in seconds. That is faster than reading a page of working and usually more informative.

faqs.question: What does a marked Physics SL Paper 2 answer show a parent?
faqs.answer: Which specific statements were missing. Extended-response marks are awarded for a quoted equation, a correct substitution, a stated causal link, a unit, or a conclusion in context. A total of four out of seven conveys nothing, while a script showing that three marks went on an unstated causal link, a missing unit and a prefix slip conveys three fixable things. Those three loss types recur across themes, so naming them produces a gain on every topic rather than only the one studied.

faqs.question: How often should a Physics SL student have work marked?
faqs.answer: Weekly, during any paid arrangement. One marked script per session, returned before the next one, is what turns a term of lessons into a readable record of about a dozen dated documents. Less frequently than that and there is no pattern to read; more frequently and the student is writing rather than learning. The important condition is that marking sits inside the fee, because a tutor charging separately for marking has a quiet reason to set very little of it.

faqs.question: What evidence shows the scientific investigation is on track?
faqs.answer: Dated files at each milestone. A research question written before any data exists. A method listing each measurement and its uncertainty. Raw data from the school laboratory. Processed graphs with error bars and a propagated final uncertainty. A full draft inside the 3,000-word limit. A revision responding to questions. Six dated artefacts, each visibly built on the last, keep the work ahead of the school deadline and settle any question about who produced it far better than a declaration does.

faqs.question: Do significant figures and units really cost Physics SL marks?
faqs.answer: Consistently, and they are the quietest losses in the subject. An answer quoted to five figures from two-figure data is penalised, and a milli written where a micro was meant turns correct physics into a wrong answer by a factor of a thousand. Neither is a knowledge problem, which is why neither responds to further explanation. They respond to a checking routine applied under timed conditions: last line, check the unit, check the prefix, check the figures against the data. Two sessions usually embed it.

faqs.question: What are the three outcomes of a six-week Physics SL review?
faqs.answer: Continue with the same target, change the target, or stop. Continuing is right when the counted losses are falling but the habit is not automatic yet. Changing is right when the original problem has closed and a different cluster has surfaced, which happens often after a theme D intervention. Stopping is right when the problem was narrow and is now fixed, and it is the outcome this market structurally avoids. We will recommend it with the scripts on the table when the counts support it.

faqs.question: How do we compare a Physics SL mock with a real session paper?
faqs.answer: Carefully, because mock papers vary in difficulty between Dubai schools and are sometimes assembled from several past sessions. A mock is the best diagnostic a school produces and the worst predictor. Use it for what it shows: performance on a full-length timed paper against the student's own cohort, including whether the last third of the paper was rushed. Do not read the percentage as a grade, since boundaries are set per examination session and are not published in advance by anyone.

faqs.question: What records does IB Gram keep about a Physics SL student?
faqs.answer: The enquiry details, the session notes, the theme diagnostic and the marked work, held under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. We do not collect a photograph, a full school timetable or medical information, because teaching Physics does not require any of them. Ask for deletion and the file is removed and you are told when, with copies of the marked scripts offered first, since a family who paid for a term of marking should keep what it produced.

faqs.question: Can we see the Physics SL session notes if we change tutors?
faqs.answer: They are yours, and inside our network they move with the student automatically. A handover document should carry the theme diagnostic, the counted loss types and the investigation milestone dates, so a new tutor continues rather than restarts. If you leave entirely, ask and we send the lot. That portability is one practical reason work exchanged as files beats work recorded in an exercise book that stays in a school bag.

faqs.question: Which Physics SL theme produces the most repeated errors?
faqs.answer: Theme D, fields. Field strength and potential are distinct quantities with similar names, related definitions and different units, and a student who has not separated them cleanly answers field questions with potential reasoning. The losses look random across a script and are in fact entirely systematic. One session built around the distinction, with the units written out every time, usually resolves it, and the improvement then appears on questions that seemed unrelated to the original problem.

faqs.question: How soon before the May session is it too late to start Physics SL support?
faqs.answer: It is rarely too late to fix a habit and often too late to rebuild a theme. Six weeks is enough to close a prefix problem, a missing causal link or the Paper 1B routines, all of which pay back across the whole paper. Six weeks is not enough to teach theme D from nothing while also preparing two other subjects. A diagnostic will tell you which situation you are in, and we will say plainly when the honest answer is to prioritise differently.

faqs.question: Does the tutor set Physics SL homework, and who marks it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the tutor marks it, with every lost mark explained in a sentence and returned before the next session. The quantity is deliberately modest: one timed question set or one extended answer, rather than a pile that gets half done. Marking is inside the fee rather than billed separately. Work the school sets stays with the school, and where a school clinic already covers the same ground we will say so, because it is free and we are not.

faqs.question: What should a Physics SL progress note never claim?
faqs.answer: Three things. That your child is on track for a particular grade, since the grade comes from weighted components measured against boundaries set for that session and a tutor marks only part of one subject. Any statistic about our own results, because we cannot show you the sample, the date and the method. And a timescale for a student nobody has assessed yet. A note that avoids all three and reports counted losses instead is more useful than one that reassures.

faqs.question: How do we know our child is doing the Physics SL work themselves?
faqs.answer: The dated trail answers it. Six investigation files, each visibly building on the last, show the development rather than asserting it. Weekly marked scripts in the student's own hand show the same thing for examination work. Our boundary is stated on every page: a tutor teaches technique on other examples, asks questions and points out where a reader cannot follow a method, and the student designs, runs, processes and types their own report. Nothing in the submitted file originates with us.

intro.heading: Physics SL is where mathematical slowness becomes a physics grade
paragraphs: Ask a Dubai Diploma student why they lost marks on a physics paper and the answer is usually about the topic. Look at the script and the cause is often arithmetic. A momentum question rearranged in two steps instead of one, a standard-form exponent dropped between lines, a sine entered in degrees when the calculator sat in radians, a gradient read off a graph without checking the axis scale. The physics was understood. The execution cost three marks, and three marks on a 44 per cent paper moves a grade boundary.

That is the first thing a Physics SL tutorial has to separate. The second is the handling of measurement. IB physics marks uncertainty and significant figures deliberately, not as a courtesy. An answer quoted to six figures from data given to two will lose a mark however correct the method. A percentage uncertainty propagated by adding where it should have been multiplied by a power loses another. Paper 1 now carries a data-analysis section built precisely around these skills, so a student who treats uncertainty as the dull bit at the end of a practical is losing marks in the written examination as well.

The third is the data booklet. Students are given a booklet of formulae in the examination, and a surprising number of Dubai candidates revise by memorising what is already printed while leaving unmemorised the things the booklet does not contain: definitions, the direction conventions, the derivations a question may ask for, unit prefixes, and which quantity in a relationship is held constant. Working out what is in the booklet and what is not is a one-session job that changes how a student revises for the rest of the course.

Around all of this sits the Dubai school year. KHDA oversees the emirate's private schools, which enrolled 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25 with 17 curricula represented, and Diploma students in those schools carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside their six subjects. Add a bus route from Al Quoz to Mirdif and a physics tutorial has to compete for a narrow window of usable concentration. We would rather schedule one protected 90-minute block than three sessions a student sleeps through.

This page sets out what the course assesses, which mathematics it assumes, how uncertainty is marked, what the Higher Level decision actually involves, how practical work is handled when a school's apparatus differs from the one in the question, what the 24-mark investigation rewards, and what weekly support costs in AED in this market. It contains no IB session dates, because those could not be verified from the IB's own site, and no promises about grades. Where a figure appears, it carries either a source or a caveat, and where a date would help a family plan, we point to the school's Diploma coordinator instead of printing something we cannot stand behind.

sections.heading: The arithmetic underneath Physics SL
paragraphs: Most Physics SL marks that look like physics failures are mathematics failures with a physics label on them. The subject assumes a set of manipulations will be automatic: rearranging a formula with the unknown in the denominator, working in standard form without dropping an exponent, taking a square root of a product, converting a unit prefix mid-calculation, resolving a vector into components, reading a gradient from axes with different scales, and knowing when a calculator must be in degrees. None of that is taught in the physics course. All of it is assessed inside it.

A Dubai Diploma student taking Analysis and Approaches usually has these skills from the mathematics classroom. A student taking Applications and Interpretation often does not, because the calculator carries more of the load in AI assessments and the habit of manipulating symbols by hand gets less practice. That is not a criticism of either course; it is a diagnostic shortcut. The first thing a Physics SL tutorial should establish is which mathematics course the student is taking, because it predicts where the marks are going.

The fix is drill with a physics context, not a mathematics worksheet. Twenty rearrangements from real equations in the data booklet, timed. Ten standard-form multiplications where the answer has to be quoted to the right number of significant figures. Five vector resolutions where the angle is given to the vertical rather than the horizontal, which is how examination diagrams are usually drawn. Students find this dull for about two weeks and then notice that extended-response questions have stopped taking them twelve minutes each.

A parent can test for this problem without a tutor. Ask your child to make the acceleration the subject of a kinematic equation on paper, with no calculator, and time it. Under fifteen seconds is fine. Over a minute explains a great deal about a physics report.

sections.heading: Units, significant figures and uncertainties: marks that leave while the physics stays right
paragraphs: IB physics marks measurement discipline as a skill in its own right, and Paper 1 carries a data-analysis section built around it. The rules are small in number and unforgiving in application. An answer is quoted to the precision the data supports, usually matching the least precise measurement. A unit is part of the answer. An uncertainty is absolute, fractional or percentage, and the three are not interchangeable in a propagation.

Propagation is where most Dubai candidates lose marks, and the pattern is predictable. For a sum or difference, absolute uncertainties add. For a product or quotient, percentage uncertainties add. For a quantity raised to a power, the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by that power. Students who learn one of those three rules and apply it everywhere will be right a third of the time. In the investigation, the same error cascades: a wrongly propagated uncertainty makes a conclusion sound either overconfident or impossible to defend, and the evaluation criterion then has nothing to work with.

Graphical uncertainty is the other half. A student who plots points without uncertainty bars has removed their own route to a gradient uncertainty. The expected method is to draw maximum and minimum gradient lines consistent with the bars and quote the gradient as a central value with a range. It takes one tutorial to learn and it earns marks in both the written paper and the investigation, which is an unusually good return.

We practise this on the student's own data where possible. A set of numbers the student measured themselves carries a memory that a textbook table does not, and an evaluation written about one's own untidy results is more honest than one written about a clean dataset that never existed.

sections.heading: The data booklet hands over formulae and quietly assumes the rest
paragraphs: Candidates sit IB physics papers with a data booklet in front of them. It contains relationships, constants and unit information. It does not contain definitions, sign conventions, derivations, the assumptions behind a model, or any guidance on which quantity a question is holding constant. Students who revise by rewriting formulae they will be handed are spending their time on the one part of the subject that has been outsourced for them.

Working out the boundary is a single session. The student opens the booklet, and for each theme we list what is printed and what is not. The not-printed list is the revision plan: the definition of a field, why a particular approximation holds, what happens to the sign of a quantity when direction reverses, which graph shape corresponds to which relationship, the derivation a six-mark question might ask to be shown. That list is short enough to carry on one page and specific enough to test.

There is a second use for the booklet, which is as a question-reading tool. A student who cannot see how to start a problem can scan the relevant page for a relationship containing the quantity the question asked about. That is a legitimate examination technique and it is faster than recall for an anxious candidate. Practising it deliberately, against the clock, turns a blank five minutes into a starting point.

What the booklet will not rescue is a student who does not know what the symbols mean. Every relationship in it is a sentence in physics, and a candidate who reads one as a string of letters will substitute the wrong value into the right formula. We spend tutorial time reading relationships aloud as physics statements, which sounds childish and stops the substitution errors.

sections.heading: Standard Level or Higher Level physics: what the extra 90 hours buys
paragraphs: Physics SL runs to 150 taught hours and Physics HL to 240. The additional 90 hours are not a separate course; they are extensions within the same five themes, with a longer Paper 1 and a longer Paper 2 and the same 24-mark investigation. A Dubai student weighing the two is usually weighing time and mathematics confidence rather than interest in physics.

The honest comparison has four parts. Content: the Higher Level extensions add depth within each theme rather than new themes, which means a student who finds the Standard Level treatment of a topic hard will find the extension harder in the same way. Assessment: the papers are longer at Higher Level, with more questions on Paper 1 and a longer extended-response Paper 2, and the time pressure is real. Internal assessment: identical at both levels, 24 marks and 20 per cent, which is why the investigation is proportionally easier to protect at Higher Level. University requirements: some degrees specify physics at Higher Level, and that is the one part of the decision a tutor cannot soften.

The decision point that matters is the school's change window, usually in DP1. After that, moving down is administratively possible and moving up rarely is. A student stepping down from Higher Level to Standard Level mid-course keeps the work already done on the investigation, which carries over, and loses only the extension content. A student who wanted to move up has to cover 90 hours of extension material in whatever remains of the year.

The advice we give is to make the decision on evidence rather than ambition. Two timed Standard Level papers and one Higher Level paper, all marked, usually settle it in a fortnight. We will say which way the evidence points even where a family would rather hear the other answer.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level answers stop short: a command-term reading
paragraphs: A marked Physics SL script usually shows a student who knew the physics and answered a different question from the one asked. The command terms are the mechanism. State wants a fact with no justification and no credit for extra prose. Describe wants observable features without explanation. Explain wants a causal chain, which means at least two linked statements. Deduce wants a conclusion with reasoning shown from given information. Outline wants a brief account without detail. Discuss wants a balanced consideration. Suggest invites a reasoned proposal where no single answer is expected.

The marks follow the term, not the content. A student who writes four sentences for a two-mark state question has lost time and gained nothing, and the same student will then write one sentence for a four-mark explain question. Over a full paper, that mismatch is routinely worth more than any single topic gap. It is also the fastest thing to fix, because it is a reading habit rather than a knowledge deficit.

The tutorial method is mechanical and effective. The student highlights the command term before reading the rest of the question. For explain questions, they write the causal links as arrows before writing prose. For deduce questions, they state what was given before stating what follows. For discuss questions, they plan two sides in the margin. Three weeks of this converts into visible marks on a mock, which is why we put it early in a plan rather than saving it for revision.

There is a Dubai-specific wrinkle. Many students in the emirate are working in a second or third language, and command-term confusion is easy to mistake for weak physics. Separating the two is worth doing explicitly, because the remedy is different: language-pattern practice in one case, content teaching in the other.

sections.heading: Practical work when your school's apparatus is not the one in the question
paragraphs: Physics SL includes practical work and a 10-hour collaborative sciences project, and an examination question may describe apparatus a student has never handled. Dubai schools are well equipped on the whole, but equipment varies: one school has light gates and data loggers, another runs the same experiment with a ticker tape timer, a third uses a phone application. A question about systematic error in a timing experiment is answerable from any of those starting points, provided the student has been taught to reason about the method rather than recall the particular bench they used.

That is the skill to build. For any described apparatus, a candidate should be able to name the quantity being measured, the instrument's resolution, the most likely systematic error, the most likely random error, and one change that would reduce each. Those five answers cover most practical questions regardless of equipment. They are also exactly what the investigation's research design and evaluation criteria reward, so the work is doing double duty.

Online delivery handles this better than parents expect. A tutor can share a video of an apparatus the school does not own, work through the resolution and error analysis on screen, and set the student to repeat the reasoning on an experiment they can actually run at home with a ruler, a phone timer and a stopwatch application. What a tutorial cannot do is substitute for the school's laboratory time, and we say so: practical hours are the school's responsibility and the collaborative project is run by the school.

Where a student has genuinely missed laboratory sessions, through illness or a mid-year move between Dubai schools, the honest sequence is to tell the school first. A teacher can often arrange catch-up access. A tutor cannot sign off practical hours, and any provider offering to do so is offering something that will not survive contact with the school's own records.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation and the collaborative sciences project: 24 marks and the authorship line
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is the internal assessment for Physics SL. It is worth 20 per cent of the final grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each, and capped at 3,000 words. The four criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The collaborative sciences project runs to about 10 hours, involves students from more than one science subject, and is not externally assessed, though schools use it for reporting.

Reading the criteria as a marker reads them changes what a student does first. Research design rewards a clearly stated research question with defined variables and a method that could be repeated by someone else. Data analysis rewards processing that is appropriate and shown, including uncertainty treatment, not a table of raw numbers followed by a graph. Conclusion rewards an answer to the research question, justified by the processed data and compared against accepted values or theory. Evaluation rewards specific, prioritised weaknesses with realistic improvements, which means naming the instrument and the effect rather than writing about human error.

The authorship boundary is firm and worth stating plainly. The investigation must be the student's own work and the school certifies it on that basis. A tutor may explain how each criterion is read, comment on a draft the student has produced, say that an evaluation is generic, and teach a technique on separate data the student then applies. A tutor may not pick the research question, process the student's data, restructure the document or supply text. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments; an IB candidate who submits one risks a malpractice finding and the Diploma.

We keep a dated record of every draft received and every comment returned. That is partly for honesty and partly practical: if a school ever queries authorship, a timeline of the student's own versions is the only useful evidence anyone can produce.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family pays per week, by study pattern
paragraphs: Hourly rates are a poor way to budget for a two-year course, because what matters is the weekly commitment and whether marking sits inside it. Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 33 to AED 65 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist. Monthly packages in the same market include roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Translate those into patterns and the decision becomes clearer. A single 60-minute session a week with no marking between lessons is the cheapest arrangement and the slowest to produce evidence. A 90-minute session with one marked paper per week costs more per week and generates a mark log, which is what a predicted-grade conversation needs. A fortnightly session plus marking suits a capable student who has drifted on one theme. An exam-term intensive of two or three sessions a week is expensive and short, and it is the pattern families most often regret starting too late rather than too early.

The travel premium is the one Dubai-specific variable in the table. An in-home rate carries the drive, and in a city where a 6pm crossing from Jumeirah to Mirdif can take fifty minutes, that cost is real for the tutor and gets passed on. It also narrows the choice to tutors who live within reach, which for a single named subject at a single level is a poor trade. A Green Community family choosing online picks from every Physics SL specialist whose hours overlap Gulf Standard Time.

On our own fees, the position is that they depend on session length and how much marking is included, and that the first lesson is free with no card details taken. We publish market bands so any quote, ours included, can be judged against something.

sections.heading: Scheduling in Dubai: school finish times, Ramadan, and who may legally be paid to teach
paragraphs: A Dubai Diploma timetable is fuller than the subject count suggests. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit under KHDA guidance. Add a bus route and the usable window for a physics tutorial on a weekday is often ninety minutes wide. We ask for the timetable at booking and fix one protected slot rather than scattering sessions.

Ramadan changes the shape of the week rather than stopping it. School hours shorten, concentration in the afternoon is lower, and many families prefer sessions after Iftar. For a DP2 student whose written papers follow in the spring, the practical approach is to move the slot to the evening for the month, shorten sessions and keep frequency, and use the daytime for lighter review rather than new content. Summer is the opposite case: long blocks are available and most Dubai families travel, so we plan the summer pattern in May rather than in July.

On the legal side, a parent can check more than most providers admit. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any specific amount quoted to you is unverified. An organisation with premises and staff in Dubai additionally needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, so a claim of regulator approval should be accompanied by a permit number.

If no Physics SL specialist is free in the slot you need, we say so. The alternatives offered are the nearest available time, a specialist in another time zone whose hours overlap Gulf Standard Time, or nothing, with nothing charged. Physics at Standard Level is widely taught, so this is uncommon; it is more likely for an unusual recurring slot than for the subject itself.

process.title: Send the theme, the mathematics course and the timetable
process.description: Three facts shape the first session: which theme the class is on, whether the student takes Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and when the school bus actually gets home. All three go on the booking form so the first lesson is useful rather than exploratory.

process.title: Free first lesson on a marked answer
process.description: The student sits one extended-response question under timed conditions beforehand. The free session is spent on that script, separating physics errors from rearrangement errors from command-term errors. The written note afterwards names which of the three is costing most.

process.title: Fix one protected weekly slot
process.description: We set a single recurring time around school periods, mandatory subject lessons and sport, rather than booking ad hoc. A fixed slot survives a busy term; a flexible one quietly disappears by the third week of a DP2 autumn.

process.title: One marked paper between every session
process.description: From week two a timed question or full paper is sat at home and marked before the lesson. Each goes into a log by theme and command word. The log, not an impression of effort, is what a predicted-grade conversation with a school should be based on.

process.title: Six-week review with three honest outcomes
process.description: After around six sessions we compare the log against the first script. The outcomes are continue, change focus, or stop. We write down which and why. Where the log shows no movement, adding sessions is the wrong answer and we say so.

whyPoints.title: Mathematics faults are separated from physics faults
whyPoints.description: A script is read for three different causes before any teaching starts: physics understanding, algebraic execution and command-term reading. The three need different lessons, and treating all three as revision is how a term disappears without the grade moving.

whyPoints.title: Measurement is taught as examinable content
whyPoints.description: Significant figures, propagation rules and gradient uncertainty are marked in Paper 1's data-analysis section and in the investigation. We teach them to the mark scheme rather than as laboratory etiquette, because that is how they are credited.

whyPoints.title: A specialist rather than whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: Delivering online means a family in Green Community or on Palm Jumeirah chooses from every Physics SL specialist whose hours overlap Gulf Standard Time. Choosing by postcode narrows a named single-level subject to whoever can drive there by six.

whyPoints.description: Support on the scientific investigation is criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own drafts, with a dated version history kept. No research question, data processing or prose comes from the tutor, because the student certifies authorship and bears the consequences.

faqs.question: How much maths does IB Physics SL actually need?
faqs.answer: More than the syllabus states and less than a mathematics course. A Physics SL student needs to rearrange formulae quickly, including with the unknown inside a square or a denominator, work in standard form without losing exponents, resolve vectors using trigonometry, read gradients from differently scaled axes, handle unit prefixes mid-calculation and use logarithms for decay work. None of that is taught in the physics course; all of it is assessed within it. Students on Analysis and Approaches usually arrive with these skills. Students on Applications and Interpretation often need two or three weeks of timed rearrangement drill, after which extended-response questions stop consuming twelve minutes each.

faqs.question: Why does my son get the physics right and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Three usual causes, and they look identical on a report card. First, measurement discipline: an answer quoted to more significant figures than the data supports, or a missing unit. Second, uncertainty propagation: absolute uncertainties added where percentages were needed, or a power ignored. Third, command terms: four sentences written for a two-mark state question and one sentence for a four-mark explain question. All three are mechanical and all three are fixable in weeks rather than terms. The way to find out which applies is to have one timed extended-response answer marked against the published scheme and the lost marks sorted by cause rather than by topic.

faqs.question: What is in the physics data booklet and what is not?
faqs.answer: The booklet supplies relationships, constants and unit information for every theme. It does not supply definitions, sign conventions, the assumptions behind a model, derivations a question may ask to be shown, or any indication of which quantity is being held constant. Students frequently revise by rewriting formulae they will be handed while leaving the unsupplied material unlearned. A single session spent listing, theme by theme, what is printed and what is not produces a one-page revision plan that is specific enough to test. The booklet is also a question-reading tool: scanning it for a relationship containing the quantity asked about is faster than recall under pressure.

faqs.question: Should my daughter move from Physics HL to Physics SL?
faqs.answer: Decide it on marked evidence inside the school's change window, usually in DP1. Standard Level is 150 taught hours against 240 at Higher Level, covering the same five themes with less depth, shorter papers and an identical 24-mark investigation. A theme that is hard at Standard Level will be harder at Higher Level in the same way, so the question is workload and mathematics confidence rather than interest. Two timed Standard Level papers and one Higher Level paper, all marked, usually settle it in a fortnight. The constraint to check first is university prerequisites, since some physics and engineering degrees specify Higher Level and no tutor can soften that.

faqs.question: How are uncertainties marked in IB Physics SL?
faqs.answer: As a separate skill with its own marks, in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and across all four criteria of the investigation. The rules are compact. Absolute uncertainties add for a sum or difference. Percentage uncertainties add for a product or quotient. A percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power when a quantity is raised to one. A final answer matches the precision of the least precise measurement. Graphically, uncertainty bars allow maximum and minimum gradient lines, and the gradient is quoted as a central value with a range. Students who learn one rule and apply it everywhere are right about a third of the time, which is the pattern a marked script reveals.

faqs.question: Does Physics SL close the door on an engineering degree?
faqs.answer: At many selective engineering faculties, physics at Higher Level is specified, so Standard Level can be a barrier at those institutions. It is not universal. Some engineering programmes accept physics at Standard Level with mathematics at Higher Level, some require a mathematics level and treat physics as recommended, and several universities inside the UAE publish programme-specific requirements that differ from one another. The practical step is to read the entry requirements on three named degree pages for the current admissions cycle before the DP1 change window closes, then confirm with each admissions office. General statements about the IB, including on tutoring sites, are not a substitute for the programme page.

faqs.question: Can online lessons cover the practical side of Physics SL?
faqs.answer: The reasoning side, yes; the laboratory hours remain the school's. A tutor can share video of apparatus a school does not own, work through resolution, systematic error and random error on screen, and set a student to repeat the reasoning on an experiment they can run at home with a ruler and a phone timer. For examination purposes that is what is assessed: naming the quantity measured, the instrument's resolution, the likeliest systematic and random errors, and one realistic improvement for each. What no tutor can do is sign off practical hours or substitute for the collaborative sciences project, both of which the school records.

faqs.question: What does the collaborative sciences project involve?
faqs.answer: It is about 10 hours of work inside the taught time for every IB science course, bringing together students from more than one science subject on a shared task with a scientific or technological focus. It is not externally assessed and does not carry marks towards the grade, though schools commonly use it in internal reporting and it sits in the same term as other coursework. Because it is organised and recorded by the school, a tutor has no role in it. Where a student has missed the project through illness or a mid-year move between Dubai schools, the first conversation should be with the school rather than with a tutoring provider.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Physics SL support does a DP2 student usually need?
faqs.answer: A useful block is eight to twelve weeks with one 90-minute session a week and a marked timed question before each lesson. That is long enough to produce a mark log showing movement across themes and command words, and short enough for a family to stop without a long commitment. Students rebuilding algebra and measurement skills often need two shorter sessions a week for the first month, then settle to one. In the weeks immediately before the written papers, families commonly move to two or three sessions built entirely around marked full papers. Beyond three a week, the limiting factor is usually sleep rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics SL tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 sit in bands. Budget online providers advertise from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour. Qualified online subject tutors are commonly quoted between AED 150 and AED 300. In-home visits, which include the tutor's travel across the city, run about AED 180 to AED 500. IB specialists sit around AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with premium named tutors advertised as high as AED 650. Monthly packages of about AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in the same market. Those are market figures, not our price list, and the variable that changes value most is whether script marking is included.

faqs.question: Can Physics SL sessions run after school finish times in Dubai?
faqs.answer: That is the normal pattern, and the realistic start time depends on the community rather than the school. Families in Al Quoz and Al Safa can usually manage 4pm. Green Community, Dubai Investments Park and Palm Jumeirah households are rarely settled before 5.45pm because of route length. Motor City and Sports City students on training programmes often need 7.30pm or later. We fix one recurring slot around the school timetable, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education periods and sport, because a fixed weekly time survives a DP2 term and a flexible arrangement quietly stops happening by the third week.

faqs.question: How should Physics SL revision be scheduled around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Shorten the sessions, move them later and keep the frequency. School hours shorten during Ramadan, afternoon concentration drops, and most families prefer lessons after Iftar. For a DP2 student whose written papers follow in the spring, the pattern that works is two shorter evening sessions rather than one long afternoon block, with daytime used for light review of already-taught material rather than new theme content. Timed full papers are better moved to the weekend for the month. We plan the Ramadan schedule a few weeks ahead rather than week by week, because evening slots fill quickly across the whole student group.

faqs.question: What may a paid tutor do with my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Explain how the four criteria are read, comment on a draft the student has already produced, say when an evaluation is generic rather than specific, and teach a technique such as uncertainty propagation on separate data that the student then applies to their own. What a tutor may not do is choose the research question, process the student's data, restructure the document or supply text. The investigation is submitted as the student's own work and the school certifies that. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments; submitting one risks a malpractice finding and the Diploma. We keep a dated record of drafts received and comments returned.

faqs.question: How can a Dubai parent verify a physics tutor's permit?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask for the permit rather than a reassurance. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so treat any quoted fine figure as unverified. An operation with premises in Dubai needs a separate KHDA permit.

faqs.question: What if the only free Physics SL slot clashes with school?
faqs.answer: Then we do not book it. The options we offer are the nearest workable time outside school hours, a weekend block, a specialist in another time zone whose working hours overlap Gulf Standard Time, or nothing at all, with nothing charged. Physics at Standard Level is widely taught across the UAE, so a complete absence of availability is uncommon; the more usual problem is a specific recurring slot, such as 4.30pm twice weekly in term time, which cannot be filled locally. What we will not do is take the booking and allocate a tutor who has not taught this course at this level.

dubai/ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.closingHeading: Book the free session around one marked answer
dubai/ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.closingBody: The quickest way to find out whether an IB DP physics SL tutor in Dubai will help is to have one extended-response answer sat under timed conditions and marked before anyone talks about packages. The free first lesson is spent on that script, sorting lost marks into physics, algebra and command-term causes, and it ends with a written note you can take to the school. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school timetable and mandatory subject periods. If the note says weekly tuition is not what your child needs, it will say that.

Each returns written scores rather than verbal impressions after every session.

intro.heading: Psychology marks are not mysterious. They are allocated by criterion, in writing
paragraphs: The usual trigger for a Psychology enquiry in Dubai is a returned essay with a number on it and no explanation. A student who feels they wrote well receives a 12 out of 22 and cannot see the gap. Parents reasonably conclude that the subject is subjective and that the grade depends on the marker. It does not. The 22-mark essay is scored against five named criteria with published mark allocations, and a tutor who returns a score for each one can show exactly where the twelve came from.

That is the whole method of this page. Psychology is the Diploma subject where a parent can most easily see the evidence, because every component publishes what it rewards. The Paper 1 Section B essay divides its 22 marks across focus on the question, knowledge and understanding, use of research to support the answer, critical thinking, and clarity and organisation. The short-answer questions are marked in bands out of nine. The experimental report is marked across four criteria totalling 22. Confirm the current criteria and mark allocations in the subject guide your child's cohort sits, on ibo.org or through the school.

Once the marks are visible as a set of criteria rather than as a single number, the diagnosis is usually quick and often surprising. A student scoring 12 out of 22 commonly has full or near-full marks for knowledge and understanding, reasonable marks for use of research, and almost nothing for critical thinking. They do not need to learn more psychology. They need to learn to write the paragraph that critical thinking rewards, which is a different and shorter piece of work than another term of content revision.

The second thing a parent can see is named-study recall, and this is where Dubai students most often quietly fail. The subject requires studies to be used in support of an argument, with enough detail to be credible — the researcher, the method, the finding, the limitation. Students who revise by reading notes feel prepared and produce vague references under timed conditions. The test for this is written and immediate: name the study, state the method, state the finding, state one limitation, in two minutes. Weekly, the result of that test is a document a parent can read.

On delivery: tutoring for Dubai families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; sending a tutor to a residence is part of our India service only. For Psychology the practical consequence is that essays and reports move as scored documents that accumulate across the two years, rather than as paper handed back and lost, which is precisely what makes the evidence approach possible.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology is new to almost every student who takes it, since few school systems teach it before 16. Where a student came from still shapes the first month, mostly through their habits of writing and of handling evidence.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology is a group 3 subject at Standard or Higher Level. All candidates study three core approaches to behaviour — biological, cognitive and sociocultural — and at least one option such as abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology or the psychology of human relationships. Higher Level adds extensions within each approach, a second option and approaches to research. All candidates complete an experimental report.
programmes.countryNote: Psychology is a popular group 3 choice at Dubai IB schools and is often taught in large classes, which affects how much individual essay feedback a student receives. A teacher marking thirty 22-mark essays cannot return five criterion scores on each, which is the specific gap a tutor fills in this subject rather than a content gap.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no MYP psychology, so the feeders are Individuals and Societies and Sciences. The useful inheritance is criterion-based marking: MYP students are used to being assessed against descriptors and respond well to being shown a mark allocation. The gap is scientific method, since the experimental report requires a hypothesis, an inferential statistical test and a properly handled sample.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP to the end of Year 11 send students into DP1 Psychology with good extended-writing habits and no experience of designing or analysing an experiment. The first report draft usually reads as an essay about a study rather than as a report of one, and that is a structural correction rather than a knowledge problem.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Psychology sits well in the Career-related Programme alongside career studies in health, education or social care. The DP course is assessed identically to the full Diploma version. The workload consideration is that the reflective project and the experimental report both demand independent written work with citations, and schools usually place their deadlines in the same term.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school offers CP with a health or social-care pathway, students sometimes propose a report topic that overlaps their career study. Each component must be independently produced, so an overlap in subject matter needs the school's explicit guidance before any data is collected.

programmes.name: IGCSE Psychology or arriving new to the subject
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology 0266 exists and gives a genuine head start on research methods and on a handful of classic studies. Most students arrive without it. Those coming from IGCSE Biology or Sociology bring useful habits; those arriving purely from humanities subjects write fluently and under-use evidence, which is the exact behaviour the use-of-research criterion penalises.
programmes.countryNote: With UK-curriculum students at 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, most Psychology students here arrive from an IGCSE programme that did not include the subject. The predictable consequence is a strong first essay on knowledge and a weak one on research support, and it shows in the criterion scores long before it shows in the grade.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is the subject of this page. The remaining entries are what Dubai Diploma students most often take with it, described by the specific habit each one adds or undermines.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The closest science partner, overlapping the biological approach through neurotransmission, hormones, genetics and brain structure. Biology also trains the handling of data and controls that the experimental report needs. The clash is workload, since both subjects require an independently produced investigation in the same academic year.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Directly useful, because the experimental report requires descriptive statistics and an inferential test. A student comfortable with significance, measures of central tendency and dispersion handles the analysis criterion without extra support, which is a real saving in session terms.

subjects.description: Chosen for university prerequisites rather than for Psychology support. Several psychology degrees require a mathematics qualification and some specify a route, so the named programme's own requirement should be checked before DP1 selection closes rather than inferred.

subjects.name: Biology-adjacent: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Overlaps health psychology and the biological approach through physiology, stress and behaviour change. Its own internal investigation shares a method with the Psychology report, which means students doing both often produce a cleaner design but must keep the two pieces of work entirely separate.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The behavioural material in Economics gives a genuine conceptual overlap around rationality and decision-making. The transferable skill is evaluation under a command term. What does not transfer is structure: an Economics 15-mark answer and a Psychology 22-mark essay reward different paragraph shapes.

subjects.description: Shares the sociocultural ground — identity, conformity, group behaviour — from a different direction, and its engagement activity trains the sourcing and defending of evidence on a self-chosen issue. That habit maps closely onto the use-of-research criterion in Psychology essays.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Helps and occasionally hurts. It trains close reading and clear paragraphing, which supports clarity and organisation. The risk is literary habit: a Psychology essay rewards a stated claim supported by a named study, not an elegantly developed argument that arrives at its evidence late.

sections.heading: What this search means, and the four documents that locate a Psychology grade
paragraphs: An IB DP Psychology home tutor in Dubai, in the market's own use of the phrase, is a specialist working one-to-one with a Diploma Psychology student at a time the family chooses. The conventional version is a tutor who travels to a residence. IB Gram teaches the same course one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are part of our India service only and are not sold anywhere in the UAE.

What the family searching that phrase almost always wants is an explanation. A mark came back on an essay and nobody can account for it, or a predicted grade sits a band below what the student and their parents expected. Psychology is unusually well suited to answering that, because the subject publishes its criteria and allocations. The number is reconstructable.

Four documents locate a Psychology grade, and between them they cover almost every case. The first is a criterion-scored essay: five scores rather than one mark, which shows whether the loss is in knowledge, in use of research, in critical thinking or in focus. The second is a timed short-answer attempt, which shows whether the student can produce a usable answer in the time the paper allows. The third is a written study-recall test, which shows whether the evidence base is real or remembered vaguely. The fourth is a report draft scored against its four criteria.

A parent who has those four documents knows what to do next without knowing any psychology. Full marks for knowledge and nothing for critical thinking is one intervention. Good critical thinking with vague study references is a different one. A fluent essay that never addresses the question asked is a third. The sections below set out what each component rewards, so that the four documents can be read against something.
bullets: A criterion-scored essay gives five numbers instead of one
A timed short-answer attempt tests production, not knowledge
A written study-recall test exposes vague evidence immediately
A scored report draft locates the loss inside the coursework

sections.heading: The 22-mark essay, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: This is the single most important thing for a Psychology parent to understand, and it takes one table. The Paper 1 Section B essay is worth 22 marks and those marks are distributed across five named criteria. They are not weighted equally, and the two that students most often neglect are among the largest.

Knowledge and understanding is where able students are usually strong, and it is also where additional revision has the least marginal effect. Use of research to support the answer rewards named studies deployed in support of a claim, with enough detail to be credible — the researcher, the method, the finding. Critical thinking is the criterion that separates a mid-band essay from a strong one, and it is almost always where a 12 out of 22 lost its marks. Focus on the question and clarity and organisation carry fewer marks each and are the cheapest to secure.

What critical thinking rewards specifically is judgement about the psychology: methodological criticism of the studies used, consideration of alternative explanations, discussion of whether findings generalise across cultures or populations, and attention to the limits of what the evidence supports. It is not a concluding paragraph that says the topic is complex. A student who adds one properly reasoned methodological criticism per study typically gains several marks without writing any more content.

The practical method follows directly. One essay a week, written under timed conditions, returned with five criterion scores and written reasons. The next session targets the lowest-scoring criterion rather than reviewing the topic again. Within four weeks a parent can see which criterion is moving. Confirm the current criteria and allocations in the subject guide your cohort sits, since rubric details are revised between syllabus versions.

sections.heading: The nine-mark questions, and why timing beats knowledge
paragraphs: The short-answer questions on Paper 1 Section A are worth nine marks each and are marked in bands rather than by itemised criteria — confirm the current markbands in your cohort's guide. In practice they reward a precise, complete, appropriately short answer that does the one thing the command term asked. They are not miniature essays, and treating them as such is the commonest way to lose both marks and time.

The errors are consistent. A student asked to outline writes an explanation, spending eight minutes to earn what a four-minute answer would have earned. A student asked to describe one study gives two, neither in sufficient detail. A student asked to explain a concept names a study and forgets to explain the concept. Each of these is a reading failure under pressure rather than a knowledge failure, and each is fixable with timed practice and a marked return.

Timing is the hidden constraint. Paper 1 contains three short-answer questions and an essay, and the essay carries more marks than the three short answers combined. A student who overspends in Section A arrives at the essay with insufficient time, which costs more marks than the overspending gained. A plain allocation — a fixed number of minutes per short answer, the rest to the essay — is worth several marks on its own and takes one session to install.

The useful artefact here is a timed attempt with the clock recorded. Not an essay written at leisure, but three short answers under the real allocation, marked and returned with the time taken noted against each. Four of those across a month tell a parent whether the production problem is being solved, and they are a different document from a school mock result because they isolate one behaviour.

sections.heading: The named-study problem, and how to evidence it
paragraphs: Psychology rewards evidence, and the use-of-research criterion is explicit about it. A claim supported by a study the student can name, describe and evaluate earns marks; the same claim supported by a vague reference to research having shown something does not. This is the single most testable thing in the subject and the thing students most reliably over-estimate about themselves.

The reason is the revision method. Reading notes produces recognition, not recall. A student rereading a page about a study feels familiar with it and concludes they know it, then under timed conditions produces the researcher's name and nothing usable about the method. The gap between recognition and recall is invisible until it is tested in writing against a clock, which is why it survives to the mock paper.

The drill is simple and unpleasant, which is why few students do it unprompted: name the study, state the method in one sentence, state the finding in one sentence, state one methodological limitation. Two minutes, written, no notes. Any study that cannot survive that is not available to the student in an examination, whatever their sense of it. The output is a list of unreliable studies that shrinks week by week, and that list is the second document in the evidence file.

How many studies are needed is a question with no single answer, and anyone giving a confident number is guessing. What is defensible is a working minimum per approach and per option topic, built so that every likely essay question can be supported by at least two studies the student can produce reliably. The table below sets out how to structure that coverage and how to test it, rather than prescribing a count.

sections.heading: The experimental report: four criteria, 22 marks, and a word limit
paragraphs: The internal assessment in Psychology is an experimental investigation: the student replicates a simple published study, collects data, analyses it with descriptive statistics and an inferential test, and reports it within a word limit of 2,200 words. It is marked across four criteria — introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation — totalling 22 marks. Confirm the current criteria, allocations and word limit in your cohort's subject guide before planning anything around them.

The design decision made in the first week determines most of the eventual mark, and it is made with the least information. A study chosen because it sounds interesting but cannot be replicated at school scale produces a report that struggles across every criterion: the introduction cannot justify the replication properly, the exploration cannot describe a defensible design, the analysis has too little usable data, and the evaluation becomes a list of everything that went wrong. Testing the choice against practicality before any data collection is the highest-value hour in the whole component.

The analysis criterion is where mathematics meets psychology and where Dubai students most often need help that their Psychology teacher has limited time to give. It requires appropriate descriptive statistics, a justified inferential test, correct application of it, and a statement of what the result means for the hypothesis. Choosing the wrong test, or choosing the right test and then misstating what significance means, costs marks that have nothing to do with psychological understanding.

The evaluation criterion rewards honesty with structure. A report whose results contradict the original study can score full marks on evaluation if the discussion of why is methodologically sound. Students frequently believe a failed replication is a failed report and write defensively, which costs more than the result ever did. The table below sets out the criteria with the first-draft pattern we see most often in this market.
