sections.heading: Ethics in the report: what a Dubai student can and cannot run
paragraphs: Psychology is the only Diploma subject whose internal assessment involves human participants, which gives it a set of constraints no other subject has. Studies must meet the ethical requirements set out for the course: informed consent, the right to withdraw, protection from harm or undue stress, appropriate debriefing, and restrictions on participant age and on deception. Read the current requirements in your cohort's subject guide and follow the school's own ethics approval process exactly — they are not optional, and a study that breaches them cannot be submitted.

This bites in practice far more than students expect. A replication that was straightforward in the original published form may be unusable at school scale because it induced stress, used deception, or involved participants outside the permitted age range. Students who design first and read the ethics rules afterwards lose weeks. The sequence that works is the reverse: read the requirements, then choose a study that can be replicated inside them.

There is a Dubai-specific dimension too. A school-based sample drawn from an international student body is culturally diverse in a way the original study's sample almost certainly was not, which is a genuine strength of these reports if it is discussed rather than ignored. The evaluation criterion rewards exactly that kind of methodological observation, and a Dubai student has a real point to make about the generalisability of a finding across a sample drawn from many nationalities.

A note on data protection, because it applies here. A report involving participants collects personal information about young people, and the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection sits behind how such data is handled. The practical standard is to collect only what the study needs, keep it anonymised, store it securely, and follow whatever the school's own process requires. It is also a useful thing to write about in the exploration section, where handling of data is part of what the criterion rewards.

sections.heading: Critical thinking: the criterion that moves a 4 to a 6
paragraphs: If a Dubai Psychology student is stuck in the middle bands, the odds are strongly that this criterion is why, and it is worth its own section because it is the one most often misunderstood as a personality trait rather than a technique. Critical thinking in a Psychology essay is a set of specific moves, each of which can be taught and practised, and none of which requires being a naturally sceptical person.

The moves are these. Criticise the method of a study you have just used — sample size, sampling method, artificiality of the task, cultural specificity of the sample, researcher effects, measurement validity. Offer an alternative explanation for a finding and say what would distinguish between them. Question whether a finding generalises to a different population or culture. State the limit of what the evidence supports, as opposed to what the theory claims. And where two studies disagree, say which is better evidence and why.

Each of those is a sentence pattern a student can learn. The reason they appear so rarely in first drafts is that students have been taught that an essay should be fluent and consistent, and criticism feels like undermining their own argument. The opposite is true in this subject: the band descriptors reward exactly that undermining, provided it is reasoned. A student who adds one methodological criticism per study typically gains marks immediately, and the gain shows up on the criterion score rather than being lost inside a single total.

The way to evidence improvement is to track the criterion in isolation. A table of critical-thinking scores across six weekly essays is a far better instrument than a sequence of overall marks, because the overall mark moves slowly while a single criterion can move quickly. It is also the clearest thing a parent can look at, and the quickest way to tell whether a tutoring arrangement is working or merely pleasant.
bullets: Criticise the method of each study you use, specifically
Offer an alternative explanation and say what would distinguish them

sections.heading: The evidence file: what a parent should be able to read after four weeks
paragraphs: This section is the practical test to apply to any Psychology tutoring arrangement in Dubai, including ours. Four weeks in, there should be documents. Not a sense that things are going better, not a report that the student seems more confident, but a small folder a parent can read in fifteen minutes and draw a conclusion from.

What should be in it is specific. Four criterion-scored essays, each with five numbers rather than one mark. At least two timed short-answer attempts with the minutes recorded. A study-recall list showing which studies the student can produce reliably and which they cannot, updated weekly so the trend is visible. And, if the report is under way, a scored draft of at least one section against its criterion.

What that folder lets a parent see is which criterion is moving. If critical-thinking scores have gone from 1 to 2 to 3 across four essays, the arrangement is working on the thing that matters. If all five criterion scores are flat and the only change is that the student feels better about the subject, that is worth knowing too, and worth acting on. The point of keeping records is to make a decision possible at four weeks rather than at the mock.

A parent does not need to understand the biological approach to read any of this. Five numbers per essay, four essays, one of the numbers rising. The table below sets out what each week should produce and the one question worth asking about it. We run this review with families at the four-week mark and change the plan or the tutor if the trend is flat.

sections.heading: Which option your school teaches, and why it changes revision
paragraphs: The option is chosen by the school, not by the student, and it determines a substantial share of what is examinable. A tutor who does not know which option a Dubai school teaches cannot plan revision for the option paper, and at Higher Level, where a second option applies, the effect doubles. This is the first factual question to ask any Psychology tutor, and the answer is testable in the trial session.

The options differ in character more than their titles suggest. Abnormal psychology is definition-heavy and demands precision about classification, diagnosis and treatment evidence. Developmental psychology is longitudinal in its logic and rewards understanding of methodological difficulty in studying change over time. Health psychology is applied, with behaviour change models and prevention. The psychology of human relationships is the most socially intuitive and therefore the one students most often answer from common sense rather than from evidence, which the use-of-research criterion punishes.

That last point is worth drawing out, because it is the characteristic failure in the option paper. An option question invites an opinion, and an opinion is exactly what earns no marks. A student writing about relationships or about health behaviour without named studies will produce something readable and mid-band at best. The same student, taught to anchor every claim in a study they can produce, moves up without learning any new concepts.

There is one more practical consequence. Because the option is selected by the department, a student has no say in whether it suits them, and some genuinely do not. A student who reasons well about method and poorly about social nuance will find abnormal or developmental psychology more rewarding than human relationships. That is not changeable, but it is plannable: knowing which option is harder for a particular student determines where the hours go.

sections.heading: What Psychology support costs in Dubai, by what you are buying
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai for 2026 span a wide range: budget online providers advertise from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, Bestimate's rate table puts IB specialists at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED quotes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 in Bestimate's table and up to AED 500 from independent tutors. Those are market figures published by those providers, not IB Gram's prices.

For Psychology the more useful way to think about cost is by brief, because the three main briefs consume very different amounts of a tutor's time per session. Teaching content is the cheapest per hour to deliver. Marking essays to five criteria with written reasons takes substantial time outside the session itself. Supervising an experimental report, including testing a design against the ethics requirements and reviewing a statistical choice, is slower again.

This is why a single headline rate is a poor guide in this subject, and why the question to ask any provider is what the rate includes. A rate quoted for teaching will not include weekly essay marking to criterion level, and families discover that in week two. We quote a plan after a free trial lesson — a brief, a session count and what each session returns — rather than publishing an hourly figure that would mean something different for each of the three briefs.

Some context from the emirate. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Dubai's private sector carried 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate students at 7% of enrolment, and seven new private schools including three IB schools are reported for 2026-27, adding 16,846 places. More Diploma students and the same specialist pool is an argument for booking early.

sections.heading: Online or in the room, and the honest case for each
paragraphs: Psychology is a conversational subject and that genuinely favours presence in some cases. A tutor in the room reads hesitation faster, and for a student who shuts down on a video call that advantage decides the question. IB Gram does not sell that format in the UAE — a tutor travelling to a residence is part of our India operation only — so a family who concludes they need somebody present should hire locally and expect the in-home market band, which absorbs a cross-city journey.

What online delivery contributes to this subject specifically is the document trail, and in an evidence-led approach that is not a minor convenience. Essays arrive as files, come back with five criterion scores and comments, and accumulate in one place from DP1 to study leave. Study-recall lists update in a shared document. Report drafts carry version history, which matters when a school asks what feedback was received and when. None of that survives an arrangement conducted on paper at a kitchen table.

The second contribution is marking volume. The core of the evidence method is one essay a week, marked to five criteria with written reasons. That is work done between sessions, and it is easier to sustain in a format where the essay is already a file. An in-home arrangement tends to drift towards discussion in the hour and less marking outside it, which is pleasant and slower.

Scheduling matters in Dubai too. A 90-minute in-home session booked at 17:00 in Dubai Marina can occupy a tutor for nearly three hours once the journey is counted, and that time is inside the rate whether it is itemised or not. Online, the hour is teaching. The honest summary: if presence is the deciding factor, hire locally; if the deciding factor is criterion-level marking volume and a readable record, the online format is built for it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the specific temptation in Psychology coursework
paragraphs: The experimental report carries a temptation the rest of the subject does not, because data can be invented. A student whose replication produced a messy or non-significant result may be tempted to adjust the numbers, and a student short of time may be tempted to generate a plausible dataset rather than run the study. Both are malpractice, and the sanction falls on the candidate — a Diploma can be withheld. Neither is necessary, because the evaluation criterion rewards methodological discussion of an unexpected result rather than a tidy confirmation.

That point deserves emphasis to any Dubai student panicking in DP2: a failed replication is not a failed report. A report whose findings contradict the original study can score full marks on evaluation if the discussion of why is methodologically sound. The marks are for the quality of the reasoning about the design and the data, not for the data agreeing with a published paper. Understanding that removes the entire incentive.

On the tutoring boundary: a tutor may teach research methods and statistics, explain each criterion, test whether a chosen study can be replicated inside the ethics requirements, review a statistical choice, read a draft the student wrote and score it, and ask why a section asserts something without justifying it. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the report, supply text for insertion, process the student's data for them, or edit a draft to completion. Services selling finished Internal Assessments exist in this market; one was found during research for this project advertising them openly at a fixed price.

The same boundary covers the Extended Essay and TOK, and it covers materials. Published subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB and are referenced and linked to ibo.org rather than reproduced or distributed. Our standard is that feedback is given as criterion scores and questions, and the student does every revision themselves. That is also better teaching: a student who has rewritten their own evaluation section understands the criterion, and one who received a corrected version does not.

process.title: Send one marked essay and the option name
process.description: The two most useful things in a first message are a returned 22-mark essay and the name of the option your school teaches. From the essay the criterion losses can usually be identified before the first session; from the option, a revision plan is possible at all.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a Diploma specialist
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video, free of charge and with no card details taken. The tutor scores a real essay against the five criteria during or after the session and returns the scores in writing, with the lowest criterion named and a specific plan for it.

process.title: A plan that names one criterion
process.description: Not a plan to improve at Psychology. A plan that names the criterion being targeted — usually critical thinking or use of research — the number of essays, and what will be measurable in four weeks. Content revision is added only where the criterion scores show it is needed.

process.title: One essay a week, scored five ways
process.description: A fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time, with an essay written between sessions and returned with five criterion scores and written reasons. The live hour targets the weakest criterion. Study-recall drills run alongside, written and timed, with the unreliable list updated weekly.

process.title: Read the evidence file at four weeks
process.description: Four scored essays, timed attempts with minutes recorded and an updated recall list, read together. If the targeted criterion has moved, continue. If every criterion is flat, the plan changes or the tutor changes. The decision is made from documents rather than from impressions.

whyPoints.title: Five numbers, not one mark
whyPoints.description: Every essay comes back scored against each of the five criteria with written reasons, because a single mark cannot tell a parent whether the problem is knowledge, evidence, criticism or focus. The five numbers make the diagnosis obvious and make a four-week trend readable.

whyPoints.title: Study recall tested, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Written, timed, two minutes per study: researcher, method, finding, limitation. Reading notes produces recognition rather than recall, and the difference is invisible until it is tested. The output is a shrinking list of unreliable studies that a parent can read directly.

whyPoints.title: Critical thinking taught as a technique
whyPoints.description: The criterion that separates mid-band from strong is a set of specific sentence patterns, not a personality trait. We teach the moves — method criticism, alternative explanation, limits of generalisation — and track that one criterion in isolation so the gain is visible.

whyPoints.title: The report handled ethics-first
whyPoints.description: Design choices are tested against the course's ethical requirements and the school's approval process before any data is collected, because a study designed first and checked afterwards loses weeks. Statistical choice is reviewed before the analysis is written, not after.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the option your school teaches
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, the tutor is matched on the specific option your department selected and, at Higher Level, on both. That question is unanswerable for a tutor chosen by driving distance, and the option is a substantial share of the examinable content.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, and gaps admitted
whyPoints.description: AED bands on this page carry the provider and the year that published them. Regulatory statements cite u.ae, KHDA or MoHRE. Where nothing could be sourced — IB session dates, an IB equivalency threshold, a required number of studies — the page says so rather than inventing a figure.

faqs.question: Why did my child's Psychology essay get a mark we cannot explain?
faqs.answer: Because a single number hides the diagnosis. The Paper 1 Section B essay is worth 22 marks distributed across five named criteria: focus on the question, knowledge and understanding, use of research to support the answer, critical thinking, and clarity and organisation. A 12 out of 22 usually means near-full marks on knowledge and almost nothing on critical thinking. Ask for the essay to be scored against each criterion separately and the gap becomes obvious. Confirm the current criteria and allocations in the subject guide your child's cohort sits.

faqs.question: What exactly does the critical thinking criterion want?
faqs.answer: A set of specific moves rather than a sceptical disposition. Criticise the method of each study used — sample size, sampling method, artificiality, cultural specificity, measurement validity. Offer an alternative explanation for a finding and say what would distinguish between them. Question whether a result generalises to another population. State the limit of what the evidence supports. Where two studies disagree, say which is better evidence and why. A student who adds one reasoned methodological criticism per study typically gains marks immediately, without learning any new content.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but still writes mid-band essays. What should change?
faqs.answer: Stop revising content. If knowledge and understanding is already scoring five or six out of six, further revision has almost no marginal effect, and the marks are sitting unclaimed in critical thinking and use of research. The change is a weekly timed essay returned with five criterion scores, with the live session spent on the lowest one. Four essays produce a readable trend on each criterion, which is far more useful than four overall marks, because a single criterion can move quickly while the total moves slowly.

faqs.question: How can we tell whether our child really knows the named studies?
faqs.answer: Test it in writing against a clock. Two minutes per study, no notes: researcher, method in one sentence, finding in one sentence, one methodological limitation. Any study that does not survive that is not available in an examination, whatever the student's sense of it. Reading notes produces recognition rather than recall, and the gap is invisible until it is tested, which is why it usually survives until the mock. The output is a list of unreliable studies that should shrink week by week.

faqs.question: How many studies does a Psychology student need to know?
faqs.answer: Nobody can give a defensible single number, and anyone who does is guessing. What is defensible is a working minimum: at least two studies per major topic in each core approach and per named topic in the school's option, which the student can produce reliably under the two-minute written test, with at least one in each area that can be criticised methodologically. At Higher Level add at least one producible study per extension area, plus a short set usable purely as method examples for research-methods questions.

faqs.question: What is the Psychology internal assessment, and how long is it?
faqs.answer: It is an experimental investigation: the student replicates a simple published study, collects data, analyses it with descriptive statistics and an inferential test, and reports it within a word limit of 2,200 words. It is marked across four criteria — introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation — totalling 22 marks. The design choice made in the first week determines most of the eventual mark, which is why testing that choice for practicality and against the ethics requirements before any data collection is the highest-value hour in the component. Verify current details in your cohort's guide.

faqs.question: What are the ethics rules for the Psychology experiment?
faqs.answer: The course sets requirements that include informed consent, the right to withdraw, protection from harm or undue stress, appropriate debriefing, and restrictions on participant age and on deception, alongside the school's own approval process. Read them in your cohort's subject guide and follow the school process exactly and in writing. The practical consequence is sequencing: a study chosen first and checked against the rules afterwards frequently turns out to be unusable, costing weeks. Choose a study that can be replicated inside the requirements from the start.

faqs.question: Our replication did not produce the expected result. Is the report ruined?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most important thing to tell a worried DP2 student. The evaluation criterion rewards methodological discussion of the design, the findings and their limits — not agreement with the original paper. A report whose results contradict the published study can score full marks on evaluation if the discussion of why is sound. Students who write defensively about an unexpected result lose more marks than the result ever cost. Treat it as a methodological finding to analyse, and the criterion works in your favour.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Psychology experiment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear boundary. A tutor may teach research methods and statistics, explain each criterion, test whether a chosen study can be replicated within the ethics requirements, review whether the statistical test is appropriate, read a draft the student wrote and score it, and ask why a section asserts something without justifying it. A tutor may not write or rewrite any part of the report, supply text, process the student's data, or edit a draft to completion. Inventing or adjusting data is malpractice and the sanction falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Why do the nine-mark questions cost our child so much time?
faqs.answer: Because they are being written as miniature essays. The short-answer questions are marked in bands out of nine and reward a precise, complete, appropriately short answer that does the single thing the command term asked. Outline, describe and explain want different lengths. A student who explains when asked to outline spends eight minutes earning what four would have earned, then reaches the Section B essay short of time — and the essay carries more marks than the three short answers combined. Install a fixed minute allocation and the loss disappears.

faqs.question: Which Psychology option is my child studying, and does it matter who we hire?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal, and the option is chosen by the school rather than by the student. It determines a substantial share of the examinable content, and at Higher Level a second option applies. Ask the department which option or options are taught, then ask any prospective tutor which they have taught and put a question from it to them in the trial session. A tutor strong on the three core approaches but unfamiliar with your school's option is a partial fit, which is better known before paying than after.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to visit our home in Dubai for Psychology lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor travelling to a residence is part of our India service only. Psychology for Dubai families is taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which suits an evidence-led approach because essays move as files, come back with five criterion scores and accumulate in one place across two years. If your child genuinely disengages on a video call, presence matters more than any of that and you should hire a local in-home tutor.

faqs.question: What does Psychology tutoring cost in Dubai, and what should the rate include?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 market figures run from AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online end, through a qualified-tutor band where Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, to an IB specialist band of AED 200-450 and above in Bestimate's rate table, with premium quotes such as BartyED's AED 650. In-home sits at AED 180-350 and up to AED 500 independently. Those are market rates, not ours. The question to ask any provider is what the rate includes: marking an essay to five criteria is substantial work outside the session, and a teaching rate rarely covers it.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see after four weeks of Psychology tutoring?
faqs.answer: A folder you can read in fifteen minutes: four essays each scored against the five criteria, at least two timed short-answer attempts with the minutes recorded, and a study-recall list showing which studies are producible and which are not, updated weekly. If the targeted criterion has risen across those four essays, the arrangement is working on the thing that matters. If every criterion is flat and the only change is that your child feels better about the subject, that is worth knowing and worth acting on.

faqs.question: Can Psychology sessions work around Dubai school timings and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the pattern varies by area. Communities with schools inside them take 16:30 slots; Marina and JLT families with long northbound commutes usually want 18:30 or later, and often prefer the essay to be written between sessions so the live hour targets one criterion. During Ramadan the UAE school day shortens and sessions move to post-Iftar timing rather than pausing. Weekend mornings suit the experimental report, which needs an uninterrupted block for design and analysis.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB DP Psychology home tutor in Dubai, send one marked 22-mark essay and the name of the option your school teaches. Those two things are usually enough to identify which of the five criteria is costing your child marks before the first session begins. Four weeks later you will have a folder to read rather than an impression to trust.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Psychology rather than psychology generally. Each has marked short-answer and extended-response answers against the published criteria, and each can say which of the two is worth buying hours for in a given student's situation.

intro.heading: Buy the marks that are recoverable, not the hours that are available
paragraphs: Psychology is the Diploma subject where tutoring money is most often spent in the wrong place. The subject looks like content: three approaches to behaviour, a set of options, a long list of studies. So families buy content hours, and a tutor re-explains the biological approach to a student who could already have written it out. Meanwhile the marks are going missing in two specific, trainable, technique-shaped places, and those are where an hour of one-to-one teaching has the highest return per dirham spent.

The first place is the short-answer section of the first written paper. Three questions, one on each approach, each worth nine marks, each rewarding a precise shape of answer: the concept named accurately, the research evidence stated with enough detail to be credible, and the link to the question made explicitly rather than left implied. Students lose two or three marks per question for structural reasons, which across three questions is a substantial share of the paper. This is the cheapest improvement in the entire subject and it is reliably achievable in a handful of marked sessions.

The second place is the extended response, where a single essay carries twenty-two marks and the criteria reward critical thinking as much as knowledge. Students who have memorised four studies and describe all four score in the middle bands; students who use two studies and interrogate their methodology, generalisability and alternative explanations score above them. This is harder to teach and takes longer, so it is the expensive purchase, and a family should know that before they commit to a term's hours.

The rest of the spending question is about choices the school has already made. Which option the class studies changes the content load, the availability of good studies and therefore the hours needed. Whether the student is at Standard or Higher Level changes the component weightings and adds a paper that rewards research-methods fluency rather than content recall. And the internally assessed experimental report has its own cost profile, dominated by decisions made at the planning stage rather than by writing time.

Everything numerical on this page carries a source. The AED bands come from named competitor price pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate survey. The regulatory and equivalency material comes from u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE and a sourced report of the Ministry's equivalency requirements. Where a figure could not be verified, including every IB examination and results date, this page says so instead of guessing. Read the weighting table first; it is the one that tells you where the money should go.

One more thing about the spending order, because it is the part families get wrong most often. The cheap work is front-loaded and the expensive work is late, which means a budget spent evenly across two years buys less than the same budget spent deliberately. A short block on short-answer structure in the first term of DP1, a compact study bank built rather than accumulated, and one session testing the experimental design before any data is collected are all inexpensive and all remove work that would otherwise be bought at crisis prices in the final term. Specialist availability tightens as the examination series approaches and rates firm up rather than soften, so the family that plans in October is choosing from a wider pool at a lower point in the band than the family that plans in February.

Extended response: twenty-two marks, rewarding critical evaluation over study count

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology has no direct pre-Diploma equivalent in most Dubai schools, which is unusual and has a cost implication: nearly every student starts from zero in DP1, and the hours that matter most are the early ones spent establishing how the subject is written rather than what it contains.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies and MYP Sciences between them supply the two habits Diploma Psychology needs: constructing an argument from evidence, and designing and evaluating an investigation. Neither supplies the subject content, so an MYP student arrives in DP1 with transferable method and no psychology. That is a cheaper starting position than it sounds.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's continuum schools move students from MYP 5 into DP1 directly, and Psychology is frequently chosen there as a new subject. The early spend that pays is on answer structure, because the content arrives on schedule from the class teacher and the structure does not.

programmes.name: Coming to Psychology from IGCSE sciences
programmes.description: Most Dubai students entering Diploma Psychology come from IGCSE Biology and IGCSE English rather than from any psychology course. Biology supplies useful grounding for the biological approach and for research methods; the IGCSE habit of short factual answers works against the extended response, where description without evaluation caps the mark.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools carry the largest share of Dubai's private enrolment, so this is the commonest entry route in the emirate. For this group the predictable first purchase is extended-response structure, and it is predictable enough to plan and budget for in the first term of DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Psychology
programmes.description: Built on three core approaches to behaviour, biological, cognitive and sociocultural, plus options such as abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and human relationships. Standard Level studies one option and Higher Level two, with additional extension content in each approach and a separate research-methods paper. An experimental report is assessed internally.
programmes.countryNote: Psychology is one of the larger group three cohorts in Dubai's IB schools, so classes are often sizeable and individual marking of extended responses is scarce. That scarcity is precisely what one-to-one hours should be bought to supply, rather than content that the class already covers.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. Psychology appears in health and social care oriented pathways, and the assessment demand for that single Diploma course, experimental report included, is identical to the full Diploma version.
programmes.countryNote: CP runs in a minority of Dubai schools, so a CP student taking Psychology may have a very small class or none. The budget consequence is that work a cohort would otherwise do collectively, particularly collecting experimental data, has to be planned deliberately instead.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: The list below notes what each neighbouring subject assesses and how much marking it generates, because marking volume is the honest driver of a tutoring bill across a two-subject arrangement.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Three approaches to behaviour plus options, assessed through short-answer questions, extended-response essays and an internally assessed experimental report. Higher Level adds extension content and a research-methods paper. Marks are lost to answer structure and to description without evaluation far more than to missing content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Written papers plus a scientific investigation. Overlaps Psychology directly on the biological approach, neurotransmission and hormones, and shares its statistics vocabulary. Students taking both frequently need the two internal deadlines mapped early, because they land in the same DP2 term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Carries the descriptive and inferential statistics that the Psychology experimental report and research-methods questions assume: measures of central tendency, dispersion, correlation and significance. Weak statistics here shows up as lost marks in Psychology rather than in mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra and calculus focused, and the route many psychology and neuroscience degrees prefer at entry. Worth reading against target university requirements before subject choices close, since the mathematics route is more often the admissions blocker than the group three subject is.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, comparative essay and oral components. The transferable asset for Psychology is timed essay construction under pressure, which is exactly what a twenty-two mark extended response requires and what most students have never practised against a clock.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Engagement activity and oral components alongside written papers, built on contested concepts. Shares with Psychology the demand to weigh competing explanations rather than report one, so improvement in one subject tends to show up in the other.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Extended response and data response papers plus short written commentaries. A frequent companion subject in Dubai; the shared discipline is evaluating evidence against stated criteria rather than describing it fluently.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Written papers plus an investigation, overlapping Psychology on health behaviour and physiological measurement. Where a school offers both, students often take one as a lighter companion to the other, and the research-methods work transfers in both directions.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary, assessed through written papers and an investigation. Shares Psychology's demand for evaluating methodology and competing explanations, and its investigation has a similar planning-heavy cost profile.

sections.heading: Where the marks are, and therefore where the money should go
paragraphs: A direct answer first. In Diploma Psychology the highest return per hour of paid tuition is on short-answer technique, because three questions at nine marks each are won or lost on a structure that can be taught in a handful of marked sessions. The second highest is extended-response evaluation, which is worth more marks and takes longer to move. Content re-explanation is the lowest return, because the class teacher already supplies it and a textbook supplies it again for free.

The table sets out the components with their weightings and, in the final column, what an hour of tuition realistically changes in each. That final column is the one families should read twice. An hour spent on short-answer structure changes marks within a fortnight. An hour spent on the research-methods paper changes marks for Higher Level students and does nothing at all for Standard Level students, who do not sit it. An hour spent re-teaching the sociocultural approach to a student who already has the notes changes nothing, and is the commonest way a tutoring budget is quietly wasted.

Component weightings differ between the levels, which changes the arithmetic. At Standard Level the first written paper dominates, carrying roughly half the grade, with the option paper and the internally assessed report taking the remainder. At Higher Level the load spreads across three papers plus the report, which lowers the first paper's share and introduces a research-methods component that rewards a completely different kind of preparation. Confirm the exact current weightings with the school's Diploma coordinator before building a plan around them.

The practical method is to diagnose before buying. One session attempting a short answer, an extended response and, at Higher Level, a stimulus-based methods question, all marked, tells a family which column of the table their money belongs in. Buying a term of weekly hours without that diagnosis is how a family spends AED 3,000 on the wrong component, and no rate card in Dubai warns them about it.

sections.heading: The nine-mark question: the cheapest marks in the subject
paragraphs: Three short-answer questions appear in the first written paper, one drawn from each of the three approaches to behaviour, and each is worth nine marks. Students treat them as warm-up questions and lose two or three marks on each. Across the three that is a material loss, and it is almost entirely structural: the content is usually present and the shape of the answer is not.

What the criteria reward is identifiable. The relevant concept has to be named accurately, in the subject's own vocabulary rather than in a paraphrase. Research evidence has to be supplied in enough detail to be credible, which means the aim, the method in outline and the finding, not a full study report and not a study name floating alone. And the link back to the question has to be made explicitly. Students routinely assume the examiner will infer the link; the mark scheme does not reward inference.

The second recurring loss is length discipline. A nine-mark answer written at essay length consumes time the twenty-two mark essay needs, and it does not score more. Students who have been told to write as much as they can produce exactly this failure. Practising to a deliberate length, against a clock, with the marked script showing where the extra paragraphs earned nothing, corrects it quickly. This is the single clearest example in the subject of a mark loss that is cheap to fix and expensive to ignore.

For a family budgeting, the implication is sequencing. Buy a short block on this first, see the marked attempts improve, and only then decide whether to commit to the longer and more expensive extended-response work. A provider who proposes a term of weekly essay coaching before the short answers are secure is proposing the right work in the wrong order, and it will cost more for less.
bullets: Name the concept in the subject's own vocabulary, not a paraphrase
Supply aim, outline method and finding; not a study name, not a full report

sections.heading: The extended response: twenty-two marks, and why four studies score less than two
paragraphs: The extended response is where the grade is decided and where the expensive hours go. A single essay carries twenty-two marks, and the criteria reward critical thinking as heavily as they reward knowledge. That balance is counter-intuitive for a student who has spent a year accumulating studies, and it produces the most predictable failure in the subject: an essay that describes four studies accurately, demonstrates real effort, and sits in the middle bands.

An essay that scores above that uses fewer studies and does more with them. Two well-chosen pieces of research, each interrogated on method, sample, generalisability, ethical constraints and alternative explanations, generate more creditable critical thinking than four described in sequence. The student also finishes on time, which the four-study essay frequently does not. Teaching this is genuinely harder than teaching short-answer structure, because it requires the student to let go of material they worked to memorise.

There is a second structural problem worth naming. Students often treat evaluation as a final paragraph: three paragraphs of description, then one beginning with a concessive clause. The criteria reward evaluation woven through the argument, so the structure that works integrates the critical point with the study it belongs to. Rebuilding a student's essay plan to that shape, and then practising it under timing until it survives pressure, is the work. It takes a term rather than a fortnight, and a family should budget for a term rather than hope for a fortnight.

The option paper rewards the same skill, which is the one piece of genuinely good news in the cost structure of this subject. Work bought on the extended response transfers directly to the option essays, whether the school studies abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology or human relationships. That means the expensive purchase covers two components rather than one, and families should resist paying separately for option-specific essay coaching when the technique is shared.

sections.heading: How the option and the level change the bill
paragraphs: Two decisions already made by the school and the student determine the content load, and therefore the hours. The first is which option the class studies. Standard Level students study one; Higher Level students study two. The options differ in how much specialist content they carry, how well supplied they are with clear, well-known studies, and how much overlap they have with the core approaches. Overlap is the useful property, because content that appears in both the core and the option is revised once and used twice.

The second decision is the level. Higher Level adds extension content within each approach and a separate research-methods paper built on a supplied piece of research. That paper rewards fluency with method and design rather than recall of content, which means a Higher Level student with weak research-methods understanding has an identifiable, separately buyable problem that a Standard Level student simply does not have. Conversely, a Standard Level student being tutored in research methods beyond what the experimental report needs is paying for a paper they will never sit.

The table maps the options against content load, study availability and overlap with the core. Read it as a budgeting aid rather than as a judgement about difficulty: no option here is easy, and the right one for a student depends on interest as much as on workload. What the table does support is a realistic estimate of how many hours a given school's option choice is likely to require, which is information no competitor page in this market provides at all.

One scheduling consequence follows from the Higher Level structure. Three written papers plus an internally assessed report means the final term is crowded, and the research-methods paper is the component most often left until last because it has the least content to revise. Planning that paper's preparation into the calendar rather than leaving it to the end is a cost saving as well as a sanity measure, because emergency hours in the final fortnight are the most expensive hours in the market.

sections.heading: Studies: how many does a student actually need?
paragraphs: Dubai students arrive at the final term with a document listing forty or fifty studies and a plan to memorise them. It is a reasonable instinct and it is poor value, because the marks do not scale with the number of studies known. A well-chosen core of around a dozen, each understood deeply enough to be evaluated on method, sample and alternative explanation, covers the realistic question space across the approaches and the option more effectively than fifty known superficially.

The selection criteria are practical. A study earns a place if it can serve more than one question, if the student can state its method clearly enough to criticise it, and if it carries an evaluative handle the student actually understands. A famous study the student cannot describe methodologically is worse than useless in an extended response, because naming it invites an examiner to expect what follows and nothing follows. This is the specific piece of work a Psychology tutor should do early, and it reduces the revision load dramatically.

The cost logic is straightforward. Sessions spent building and stress-testing a compact study bank are cheap, front-loaded and reusable. Sessions spent in the final fortnight trying to make fifty half-known studies examinable are expensive, late and largely futile. A family who buys the first and skips the second spends considerably less across the two years, which is the sort of arithmetic no rate card can show them.

There is an honesty point attached. No tutor can predict which studies the paper will reward, and a provider implying otherwise should be treated with real scepticism. The value of a compact bank is coverage and depth, not prediction. The same caution applies to anyone offering model essays to memorise: the question will not match, and a memorised essay reproduced inaccurately scores worse than an honest attempt written to a practised structure.

sections.heading: What Dubai charges, and what the cheapest tier cannot do
paragraphs: The published figures first. A qualified online subject tutor in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB or IGCSE specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, as of October 2026. Budget online tutoring, typically delivered by university students, starts far below that. In-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500, because travel sits inside the rate. Each band in the table traces to a named publisher.

The important column is the last one, which states what each tier cannot deliver. A university-student tutor at the bottom of the band can usefully explain content and quiz a student on studies. What that tier generally cannot do is mark a twenty-two mark extended response against the published criteria with the critical-thinking strand separated from the knowledge strand, because that requires having marked a number of them. Paying the lowest rate for the component that needs the highest skill is the classic false economy in this subject.

The inverse also holds. Paying a specialist rate to be quizzed on content is paying premium prices for commodity work. A sensible two-year plan sometimes mixes tiers deliberately: cheaper hours for content consolidation and recall drilling, specialist hours for essay marking and the experimental report. No provider in this market suggests that, because it does not suit any provider to suggest it, but it is frequently the right answer for a family with a fixed budget.

Two further cost questions are worth asking anyone. Is marking time inside the hourly rate, or is a returned script billed separately? And what happens to a session the family cancels with twenty-four hours' notice? Neither answer appears on any competitor page examined, and both change the real cost per term materially. Local context helps too: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, so a two-year tutoring plan is being budgeted against a flat school fee.

sections.heading: Research ethics and data protection: the part nobody budgets for
paragraphs: The internally assessed component is a replication of a simple experiment, and the ethical requirements around it are not decoration. Participants must give informed consent, must be told they may withdraw, must be debriefed afterwards, and must have their data anonymised. Where participants are under eighteen, which in a school replication they usually are, parental or guardian consent and the school's own approval come into it as well. A study designed without these considerations can be unusable regardless of how good the idea was.

This is where the money is saved or lost in this component. A replication whose design cannot ethically be run, or whose data cannot be analysed with a test the student understands, generates weeks of remedial work. Testing the design against three questions in the first session prevents nearly all of that: can this be run ethically with these participants, can consent and debriefing be documented, and does the design produce data that a specific statistical test can handle. One cheap session at the start removes several expensive ones later.

There is a UAE dimension to the data question. Personal data in the UAE is governed by Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection, and a school replication collecting data about minors should state what is collected, why, and how it will be deleted. This is good practice in a psychology report and a legal consideration in the UAE, and it is the sort of detail that distinguishes a careful report from a careless one in the evaluation section as well.

The academic-honesty boundary applies here in a form specific to empirical work. A tutor may teach design, explain why a test fits a data type, question whether a sample supports a conclusion, and comment on a draft report. A tutor may not collect the data, run the analysis on the student's behalf, or author any part of the submission. Data that has been handled by someone other than the student is not the student's data, and the evaluation section will not survive scrutiny if the student cannot explain how it was gathered.
bullets: Informed consent, right to withdraw, debriefing and anonymity are design requirements, not formalities
Participants under eighteen bring guardian consent and school approval into the plan
State what data is collected, why, and how it will be deleted
The student gathers and analyses their own data; a tutor teaches and questions

sections.heading: Equivalency, attestation and which subjects actually count
paragraphs: Families in Dubai planning for UAE universities ask a question that almost no tutoring page in this market answers: does this subject count towards Ministry of Education equivalency. The honest answer is that equivalency rules are set by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, that they differ by curriculum, and that the published detail for the British track is considerably clearer than for the IB track.

For the British track, the requirements as reported include five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last detail matters because at least one ranking competitor publishes a different subject count, and publishing the correct rule is a straightforward accuracy win.

For the American track, the reported English proficiency requirement is a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT mathematics test. For the IB track, no points threshold appears on this page, because none could be verified on the Ministry's own site. Any figure quoted elsewhere without a moe.gov.ae source should be treated with suspicion.

Two boundaries belong with this. IB Gram does not perform, guarantee or expedite equivalency or attestation, and nothing here should be read as doing so; the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate authority, and families should go to the official channel. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Any provider implying that it is, is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process, which is both dishonest and easy to check.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Psychology online tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures as of October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a Diploma or IGCSE specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IB rates from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate survey covers the specialist band. Those are market rates from the sources named, not a price list for this platform. The more useful question for Psychology is which component the hour is pointed at, because the return per dirham differs sharply between short-answer technique and content re-explanation.

faqs.question: Which Psychology component gives the best return on tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Short-answer technique, clearly. Three questions at nine marks each appear in the first written paper, and students routinely lose two or three marks on each for structural reasons rather than for missing content. That structure is teachable in a handful of marked sessions and the gain repeats three times on the paper. Extended-response evaluation is worth more marks and takes a term rather than a fortnight, so it is the second purchase. Content re-explanation is the weakest use of a paid hour, because the class teacher and the textbook already supply it at no extra cost.

faqs.question: How many marks is a short-answer question worth in the first written paper?
faqs.answer: Nine marks each, with three questions in that section, one drawn from each of the three approaches to behaviour. What the criteria reward is the concept named in the subject's own vocabulary, research evidence supplied in enough detail to be credible, meaning the aim, the method in outline and the finding, and an explicit link back to the question. Students lose marks by naming a study without describing its method, by paraphrasing the concept, and by leaving the link to be inferred. Confirm the current mark allocation with the school's coordinator before building a revision plan on it.

faqs.question: How many studies does my child actually need to memorise?
faqs.answer: Far fewer than they think. A compact bank of around a dozen studies, each understood well enough to be evaluated on method, sample, generalisability and alternative explanation, covers the realistic question space better than fifty known by name. A study earns its place if it can answer more than one question and if the student can state its method clearly enough to criticise it. Naming a famous study and then saying nothing methodological about it scores worse than using a less famous one properly. Building this bank early is cheap; rebuilding it in the final fortnight is not.

faqs.question: Does the option our school chose change how much help my child needs?
faqs.answer: Yes, mainly through overlap with the core approaches. Human relationships and developmental psychology overlap the sociocultural and cognitive approaches substantially, so content revised for one component serves the other and the effective hours needed fall. Health psychology has less overlap and therefore carries more separate content. Abnormal psychology sits in between, with strong conceptual overlap and treatment content that needs its own attention. None of the options is easy, and interest matters more than workload for a two-year course, but the budget implication is real and worth knowing.

faqs.question: Is the Higher Level research-methods paper worth buying separate hours for?
faqs.answer: For a Higher Level student with weak methods understanding, yes, and it is a distinctly separate purchase. That paper is built on a supplied piece of research and rewards fluency with design, sampling, measurement and interpretation rather than recall of content. It also has the least revisable content, which is why it is the component students leave until last and then run out of time for. For a Standard Level student the answer is a flat no, because that paper is not sat at all and hours spent on it are hours bought for nothing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be present while my child collects experimental data?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the design beforehand and discuss what the data shows afterwards, and that is the useful part. Collecting the data is the student's own work, and a report whose data was gathered or processed by someone else is not the student's submission. The honest division is clear: the tutor questions whether the design can run ethically, whether consent and debriefing can be documented, and whether a statistical test the student understands fits the data type. The student then runs it, analyses it, and writes it up, with feedback on their own drafts as observations rather than replacement text.

faqs.question: Who can take part in a Dubai school psychology replication?
faqs.answer: Participants must give informed consent, be told they may withdraw, be debriefed, and have their data anonymised. Where they are under eighteen, which in a school replication they usually are, guardian consent and the school's own approval are part of the plan rather than an afterthought. UAE personal data is governed by Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection, so the report should state what is collected, why, and how it will be deleted. Design around these requirements from the first session; a study that cannot be run ethically consumes far more time than one chosen carefully.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a describe question and a discuss question?
faqs.answer: They sit at different levels of the command-term ladder and reward different things. A describe or outline instruction asks for an accurate account, and additional evaluation earns nothing against it. A discuss, evaluate or to-what-extent instruction asks for a judgement supported by critical examination of the evidence, and an accurate account alone will cap in the middle bands however well written. Students lose marks in both directions: evaluating a describe question wastes time, and describing a discuss question wastes marks. Reading the command term before planning the answer is the cheapest habit in the subject.

faqs.question: Is Psychology an easier Diploma subject than Biology?
faqs.answer: They are difficult in different places, so the comparison rarely helps a decision. Biology carries heavy factual content, precise terminology and a quantitative investigation. Psychology carries less memorisable content and far more weight on written argument, where a twenty-two mark essay rewards critical evaluation that cannot be learnt by rote. Students who write well and dislike memorising usually find Psychology the better fit; students who prefer definite answers often find Biology more comfortable. Choose on the student's habits of work rather than on a reputation, and check target university requirements before either is dropped.

faqs.question: Does a Psychology grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is set by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, not by any tutoring provider, and the published detail differs by curriculum. For the British track the reported requirements include five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the IB track no points threshold appears here, because none could be verified on the Ministry's own site. Check moe.gov.ae directly, and treat any unsourced IB figure with suspicion.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for the final term before the examinations?
faqs.answer: Work from Bestimate's published monthly bands rather than from a single number. Weekly sessions at the mid tier run roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, and specialist exam-year work roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. A final term of weekly specialist essay marking therefore sits at the upper end of that, which is why front-loading cheaper work earlier is the better strategy. Availability also tightens as the series approaches and rates firm up rather than soften, so a family booking in February is choosing from a thinner pool at the top of the band.

faqs.question: Are group revision classes a sensible saving for Psychology?
faqs.answer: For content consolidation and recall drilling, yes, and they are genuinely good value for a student who knows the material and needs pace. For the extended response, no, because group formats almost never include individual marking of a twenty-two mark essay, and individual marking is the mechanism that moves that grade. The sensible answer for a fixed budget is often a mix: cheaper or group provision for content, specialist one-to-one for essay marking and the experimental report. Paying less for a format that cannot deliver the mechanism is not a saving at all.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Psychology and Biology for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The biological approach overlaps Biology directly on neurotransmission, hormones and genetics, and the research-methods and statistics vocabulary is shared across both subjects. A tutor genuinely strong in both reduces cost and keeps the shared material consistent. A tutor strong in one and merely competent in the other will move one grade and leave the other untouched, which costs the same and delivers half. Two specialists beat one generalist at the same combined price where a genuine dual specialist is unavailable.

faqs.question: My child joined Psychology late. Does catching up cost more?
faqs.answer: Usually less than families expect, because Psychology has no pre-Diploma course in most Dubai schools and nearly every student starts from zero in DP1. A student joining a term late is behind on content the class teacher will continue to deliver, and content catch-up is the cheapest kind of work there is: readable, finite and well supplied by the textbook. The expensive gap is technique, and a late joiner is no further behind on that than anyone else. One diagnostic session establishes which gap is real before any block is booked.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Psychology at Standard and Higher Level: the three approaches, the four options, the 22-mark extended response and the experimental report. Matching is by the option your school teaches and the level your child sits, because those two facts decide which hours are worth paying for.

intro.heading: Price the marks, not the hours
paragraphs: Most Dubai families begin this search with a rate in mind and no idea what the rate buys. That is understandable: three of the six pages ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. So the first job of this page is to put honest AED bands on the table, say where each band comes from, and then show which parts of IB Psychology those bands actually fix. Nothing below is an IB Gram price list. Our own figure comes after a free trial lesson and a written plan, because the right number depends on the level, the option and how much marking you want done between sessions.

Psychology is unusual among Diploma subjects in that almost nothing is memorisation-only and almost nothing is calculation. The grade is produced in writing: three short-answer questions of nine marks each in the first section of Paper 1, one 22-mark extended response in the second, option essays in Paper 2, and an experimental report of up to 2,200 words carrying between a fifth and a quarter of the final grade. Every one of those is marked against published criteria. That matters for your budget, because the cheapest tier of tutoring in this market sells lesson hours and nothing else, and a lesson hour on its own cannot mark a 22-mark essay.

The second thing that moves a Dubai quote is geography, in the dull literal sense. A visiting tutor charges for the drive whether the invoice itemises it or not. A 40-kilometre run from Mirdif to Dubai Marina at five on a school night is commonly forty-five minutes to an hour each way, and that time is paid for somewhere. Online delivery removes it, which is why the in-home band in this emirate sits roughly AED 180-500 an hour while the online specialist band sits roughly AED 200-450. The online figure buys more teaching inside the same money, and it widens the pool from whoever lives nearby to whoever actually teaches your child's option.

The third variable is the calendar. Diaries for subject specialists in Dubai tighten from January, through the mock window, and into the final run before the May session. A family that arranges Psychology support in October is negotiating in a loose market; a family that arranges it in March is negotiating in a tight one, and will usually pay at the upper end of whichever band it is in. Costing the two Diploma years in advance, term by term, is the single cheapest thing a parent can do, and the table further down this page does exactly that so you can see where the money clusters.

What follows is deliberately arithmetic rather than reassurance. You will find the market bands and who publishes them, the seven variables that push a quote up or down in Dubai specifically, the assessment weightings you are buying against, a term-by-term plan with indicative monthly figures, the travel maths behind the in-home premium, tutoring set against the school bill under the KHDA fee freeze, a list of things to refuse to pay for, and the permit position that tells you who may legally take your money for private tuition here. If one of those answers your question on its own, take it and leave the rest.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology is a Diploma Programme subject, but the families searching for it in Dubai arrive from three different places: an MYP Individuals and Societies background, an IGCSE background with no psychology at all, or a mid-course switch. Each route has a different starting cost, because each has a different gap to close before essay work can begin.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology sits in Group 3, Individuals and Societies, at Standard or Higher Level. Standard Level is built on the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches plus one option; Higher Level adds the HL extensions, a second option essay in Paper 2 and a separate research-methods paper. The published teaching allocation is 150 hours at Standard Level and 240 at Higher Level, and that 90-hour difference is the honest reason an HL plan costs more than an SL one.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the subject is offered across the emirate's IB World Schools, from Al Barsha to Nad Al Sheba, but the option taught varies school by school. Two students in the same year group at neighbouring schools can be revising entirely different Paper 2 content. Ask the DP coordinator which option is on the timetable before you buy a single hour, because that answer decides how many tutors in the market can usefully teach your child.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies gives a student the habit of using a command term and supporting a claim with evidence, which transfers directly to the nine-mark short-answer questions. What it does not give is the named-study discipline the Diploma expects: a study with a researcher, a year, a method, a result and a limitation, recalled under time pressure. That is the first thing a Year 11 MYP student needs built, and it is cheap to build early.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the full IB continuum, so a student moves from MYP straight into DP Psychology inside the same building. Those students usually need fewer catch-up hours on skills and more on content volume. Families moving in from a non-IB school mid-continuum are the ones who benefit most from a short diagnostic block in the summer before DP1 rather than an open-ended weekly commitment from September.

programmes.name: IGCSE and GCSE entry route
programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE students rarely study psychology before the Diploma, so DP1 begins with no subject vocabulary at all. The advantage is that IGCSE Biology and English Language have already taught experimental control and paragraph discipline. The gap is the research literature. A student arriving this way typically needs six to ten focused sessions in DP1 Term 1 on approach-level content and study recall, then settles into ordinary essay practice.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment at around 37 per cent, and most of them run IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the IB Diploma. That means a large share of Dubai's DP Psychology cohort is meeting the subject for the first time in Year 12. Build the starting cost around that reality rather than assuming prior knowledge nobody has.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines DP courses with a career-related study, so a CP student may take Psychology as one of their DP subjects without sitting the full Diploma. Assessment for that single subject is identical: same papers, same experimental report, same criteria. What changes is the workload around it, which usually makes a shorter, sharper support block more sensible than a two-year weekly arrangement.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by a small number of Dubai schools rather than across the board, so a CP Psychology student often cannot find a classmate doing the same thing. Online one-to-one solves that: the match is made on the subject and level, not on who happens to be teaching in the same postcode.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is rarely the only subject a Dubai Diploma student needs help with, and the second subject is usually the one sharing an essay-writing problem rather than a content problem. The grid below is the Group 3 cluster plus the partners that most often appear on the same timetable.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Three approaches, one option at Standard Level and two at Higher, the 22-mark extended response and a 2,200-word experimental report. Marks are lost on critical thinking and on studies recalled without a method or a limitation, not on enthusiasm for the subject.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A source-based first paper on a prescribed subject, world history topics in the second, and a Higher Level regional option paper of three essays. Shares Psychology's problem of knowing the content and still writing mid-band answers because the question was not addressed directly.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Optional themes, the global change core and a Higher Level extension on global interactions, plus a fieldwork report assessed over six criteria. Data-handling marks are the quickest to recover and the most often left on the table.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Power, sovereignty, human rights, development and peace, assessed through a source-based paper, essays and an internally assessed engagement with a political issue. Students strong in Psychology often struggle here with theory applied to a live case.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theories applied to real organisations, with a written commentary at Standard Level and a research project at Higher. The command-term discipline is close enough to Psychology that one tutor can often cover both.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and a portfolio of commentaries on published news articles. Diagram accuracy and evaluation are where the grade moves, which makes it a marking-heavy subject in the same way Psychology is.

subjects.name: Philosophy
subjects.description: The core theme on being human, optional themes, a prescribed philosophical text and an internal assessment built from non-philosophical material. Useful pairing for a Psychology student who likes argument but needs to stop narrating.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The common science partner for a Psychology student heading towards a health or neuroscience degree. Overlaps the biological approach directly, and the scientific investigation teaches the statistical reasoning the Psychology report needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content here maps onto the Psychology report: measures of central tendency, dispersion, and the inferential test the student must justify rather than simply run. Many report rescues are really maths rescues.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK essay and exhibition sit outside subject grades but draw on Psychology constantly, especially on the reliability of evidence from human participants. Feedback here is about the structure of a claim, never about supplying one.

regions.note: Tower living with building access, visitor parking charges and lift waits that a visiting tutor prices in. Most of the emirate's subject specialists live inland, so an in-home Psychology rate quoted here is usually at the upper end of the market band.

regions.note: Villa communities with an IB continuum school on the doorstep, which keeps local demand high and local availability thin. Families here often pay a premium for a visit that could be a longer online session for the same money.

regions.note: The densest cluster of IB World Schools in Dubai, so the local tutor pool is deep but heavily booked from January onwards. Arranging Psychology support here in October rather than March is worth real money.

regions.note: Well served by schools on the Mirdif and Al Warqa side, but a long run to the Marina or Palm. A tutor living here who takes a Marina booking is charging somebody for ninety minutes of Sheikh Zayed Road.

regions.note: Older established neighbourhoods with a mix of British and IB schools and short internal journeys that lengthen sharply once Al Wasl Road is involved. Good candidate for an essay-marking cycle rather than extra contact hours.

schoolClusters.note: The heaviest concentration of Diploma candidates in the emirate, and the cluster where option choices differ most between neighbouring schools. Students we support from this area are usually balancing Psychology against a Group 4 science and a Higher Level maths course.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and Arabian Ranches
schoolClusters.note: Villa-community catchments with long-established IB provision and strong internal competition for Higher Level places. Psychology here is often a third Higher Level taken alongside Biology, which makes the research-methods paper the pressure point.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and Dubai Festival City
schoolClusters.note: A spread-out cluster with several continuum schools and a long commute to the western districts. Families here are the most likely to tell us that a weekday in-home visit simply cannot start before six, which is what pushes them towards online sessions.
