sections.heading: What an IB DP Psychology tutor in Dubai costs, and what the price is actually for
paragraphs: Market rates for IB Psychology tuition in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 at the premium end. The bands below are compiled from providers' own published rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and they are quoted per 60 minutes unless a provider states otherwise.

The useful question is not which band is cheapest but which band can do the thing Psychology needs. The subject is assessed almost entirely in writing, so the deciding feature of any tier is whether a 22-mark response gets marked against the published criteria by someone who has done it before. A tutor at AED 60 an hour can revise content with a student competently. Marking an extended response and explaining why it sat in the 13-16 band rather than the 17-19 band is a different job, and the market prices it differently.

Read the right-hand column of the table before the rate column. It names what each tier typically cannot do for this subject, which is the information every published rate card in this market leaves out. A family that matches the tier to the task usually spends less in total than a family that buys the cheapest hour and then buys it again because nothing changed.

One note on comparing quotes: ask whether the figure is per hour or per lesson, whether marking between lessons is inside it, and whether the price stated includes VAT. Those three questions explain most of the apparent price differences in this emirate, and any provider who will not answer them in writing has told you something useful.

sections.heading: Seven variables that move a Dubai Psychology quote
paragraphs: Two families in the same building can be quoted AED 180 and AED 420 for what sounds like the same thing. The difference is almost never negotiating skill. It is a handful of specific variables, and each one is checkable before you commit.

Level is the biggest single driver, and it is arithmetic rather than opinion. Standard Level carries a published allocation of 150 teaching hours and three assessed components; Higher Level carries 240 hours, a second option essay in Paper 2 and a separate research-methods paper. A Psychology HL tutor in Dubai is pricing against a syllabus that is half as large again, so an HL plan that costs the same as an SL plan is usually buying fewer weeks rather than cheaper hours.

Marking is the variable that hides best. A rate card that quotes AED 150 an hour with marking billed separately can land higher in total than one quoting AED 260 with marking included, and most families only discover this in February. Session length works the same way: an hour is enough for content recall and not enough for a timed essay plus feedback, so a 60-minute rate and a 90-minute rate are not comparable per hour.

The remaining drivers are the month you book in, the delivery format, which Paper 2 option your school teaches, and who is actually teaching. The option matters more in Dubai than people expect: the four options are not equally taught across the emirate's schools, and a less common one narrows the pool of tutors who can usefully teach it. Narrow pool, longer wait, firmer price.

sections.heading: What you are buying, component by component
paragraphs: Before you buy hours, know where the marks are. The weightings below are those published in the current Psychology subject guide; confirm your child's cohort with the DP coordinator, because the IB revises guides on a cycle and a school can be teaching an outgoing or incoming version in any given year.

Paper 1 is the largest single block at either level, and it contains two very different jobs. Section A is three short-answer questions worth nine marks each, on the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches. These are the cheapest marks in the subject to recover: the content is finite, the structure is repeatable, and a student who is losing marks here is usually mismanaging time rather than missing knowledge. Section B is one extended response worth 22 marks, chosen from three, and at Higher Level the HL extensions are examinable within it.

Paper 2 is the option paper: one essay at Standard Level, two at Higher. Because schools choose their options, this is the component where generic tutoring fails most visibly. Paper 3, sat only at Higher Level, presents an unseen summary of a piece of research and asks about method, sampling, generalisability and ethics. It is a research-literacy test rather than a content test, which is why it rewards short, targeted drilling and punishes general revision.

The experimental report is internally assessed and externally moderated: a replication of a simple published study, a maximum of 2,200 words, and 22 marks across four criteria. It is the only component where a student can bank marks months before the examinations, which makes it the most cost-efficient thing to support in DP1 rather than DP2.

sections.heading: Costing the two Diploma years, term by term
paragraphs: A two-year Diploma Psychology plan is not a flat monthly fee. The work changes shape four or five times, and so should the spend. The table below builds indicative monthly figures from the AED per hour bands earlier on this page at four sessions a month, and sits inside the monthly ranges Bestimate publishes for Dubai: roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist support in an examination year.

The pattern most Dubai families settle into is light in DP1 Term 1, a short intensive block in the summer bridging into DP2 for the experimental report, and a heavier two-session week from the mock window to the final run. Spreading the same total evenly across 22 months costs more and achieves less, because the hours land when there is nothing urgent to fix.

Two Dubai-specific dates belong in the plan. Ramadan shifts the whole evening timetable: sessions move to the post-Iftar window or to earlier afternoon slots, and most families reduce frequency for those weeks rather than cancel. The long summer break pulls families out of the country for six to eight weeks, which is either a hole in the plan or the perfect window for report work, depending on whether you book it. Online delivery is what makes the second option possible, because the timezone follows the student.
Figures below are indicative monthly ranges built from published market bands, not quotations. Your own number depends on level, option, session length and whether marking is inside the rate.

sections.heading: The in-home premium in Dubai is a travel bill, not a teaching bill
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real service in this emirate and plenty of families prefer it. It is worth being precise about what the premium buys. The published in-home band for Dubai runs roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 200-450 for an online subject specialist. The in-home figure covers a teaching hour plus a drive; the online figure covers a teaching hour. At the same spend, one of them contains more teaching.

The table below takes five ordinary Dubai journeys and shows the unpaid time involved, using approximate road distances and the kind of evening timings Google Maps shows at 17:00 on a weekday. The point is not that the drive is unreasonable. The point is that it exists, it is finite, and somebody pays for it. A tutor who absorbs it limits how far they will travel, which is why in-home availability in a given community is narrow and subject-specific.

For Psychology the trade is sharper than for most subjects, because of the option problem. An in-home search is a search within driving distance of your villa. An online search is a search across every tutor who teaches your child's Paper 2 option. If your school teaches a less common option, the second search has candidates and the first may not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script on a shared screen. We would rather state that plainly on the page than let a parent discover it on a phone call.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost next to the Dubai school bill
paragraphs: Context changes how a tutoring figure feels. Dubai's private-school sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent, according to the Dubai Media Office. The Diploma cohort is therefore a minority of a very large market, which is exactly why subject-specific Diploma support is thinner on the ground than general tutoring.

On fees, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family already paying a Diploma-year tuition bill, a frozen fee is the first year in a while where a tutoring line can be added without a fee rise competing for the same money. Setting the KHDA private school fees position next to your tutoring plan is a more honest comparison than looking at the hourly rate alone.

Supply is moving too. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More IB places means more Diploma candidates competing for the same small pool of subject-specific tutors in two years' time, which is an argument for arranging support early rather than a scare tactic.

The practical conclusion for a budget: compare a term of tutoring against the component of the grade it is meant to move, not against the school fee. A report-supervision block that touches a fifth to a quarter of the final Psychology grade is a different purchase from a general revision retainer, even when both are quoted at the same hourly rate.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family should refuse to pay for
paragraphs: Some things sold in this market are worthless, and a few are dangerous. The clearest is any offer to supply completed assessed work. One provider ranking for UAE searches advertises finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules and puts a student's entire Diploma at risk, not just one subject grade. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced; that is the whole of the legitimate service, and it is a real differentiator in this SERP rather than a disclaimer.

Next, refuse to pay for syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as a bundled download. Those materials belong to the IB and the examination boards, and a tutoring provider redistributing them is infringing copyright, not adding value. The legitimate version is a tutor who references the official documents, tells you where to find them, and works with what your child's school has issued.

Then the claims. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university place, and an outcome promise is the surest sign of a provider who has not thought about what they are selling. Treat self-published star ratings with the same scepticism: several providers in this market display ratings they generate themselves, sometimes two different figures on the same page. A rating with no countable, attributable reviews behind it is decoration.

Last, a practical Dubai check. If the conversion path on a UAE page is an overseas phone number, ask directly where the tutor is and in what timezone the lesson will run. A page showing a Dubai address it does not occupy is misrepresenting itself, and a parent is entitled to ask the question before any money moves.
bullets: No completed Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or coursework, at any price
No bundled past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables

sections.heading: Who may legally take your money for private tuition in Dubai
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The MoHRE private tutor permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no published fee.

Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. The useful thing for a parent is not the penalty but the question: ask a prospective private tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tutor permit, and treat an evasive answer as an answer.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. It needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval and then completed within a set window, with annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. That permit is specific to institutes with premises, which is why 'KHDA approval' used loosely in tutoring advertising is so often meaningless. IB Gram does not hold a KHDA institute permit and does not claim one; we are an online matching platform, and we name the regulator here to explain what it governs, not to borrow its authority.

One more rule that catches families by surprise. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit code of conduct carrying a similar restriction. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before relying on it, and in any emirate do not ask a class teacher to tutor your child privately for money.

process.title: Tell us the level and the option
process.description: Two facts decide everything else: Standard or Higher Level, and which Paper 2 option your Dubai school teaches. With those we can say honestly whether a specialist for that combination is available this week, next week, or not at all. Guessing at this stage is what produces a mismatched tutor and a wasted month.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a diagnostic script
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing, needs no card details and carries no minimum term. The student writes a short timed response during or before it, so the tutor's first piece of feedback is about actual writing rather than a conversation about confidence. You get the marked script whether or not you continue.

process.title: A costed plan, not an open-ended retainer
process.description: You receive a written plan: which component the hours are aimed at, session length, whether marking is inside the rate, and what the monthly figure is. It is set against the market bands published on this page so you can see where our figure sits rather than taking it on trust.

process.title: Marking cycle and monthly review
process.description: Timed scripts go out and come back annotated against the criteria, with a band and the reason for it. Once a month you get a short written summary: what has moved, what has not, and whether the plan should change shape. If the hours are not earning their keep, the review is where we say so.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we say so
process.description: Psychology at Higher Level with a less commonly taught option is a narrow match, and sometimes nobody suitable is available in the window you need. We will tell you that and give an honest wait, rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Where a UAE-based tutor is not available, the match may be a specialist elsewhere teaching in your timezone, and we say which.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to published provider rate cards and to Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, and dated. None of them is presented as our price. A number without a source is not information, and in a market where three of six ranking pages publish no price at all, showing the method is the differentiator.

whyPoints.title: Marking in writing, with criterion letters
whyPoints.description: Feedback arrives as an annotated script with a band and the reason for it, not a verbal summary at the end of a lesson. That gives you something to read as a parent and gives the student something to act on. It is also the component most budget tiers in Dubai exclude from the hourly rate.

whyPoints.title: Online, so the match is on the option
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the search is across every tutor who teaches your child's Paper 2 option rather than across the tutors who live within a short drive of your community. For a subject where schools choose different options, that is the difference between a specialist and an approximation.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on coursework
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on drafts the student has produced. Nobody here supplies text for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay, at any price. That boundary protects the student's Diploma, and we would rather state it on the page than leave it implied.

whyPoints.title: No lock-in, and no quiet escalation
whyPoints.description: The first lesson is free with no card details, there is no minimum term, and the plan is reviewed monthly in writing. If the sensible answer is fewer hours, or a finite block instead of a weekly slot, that is what the review will say. Plans that only ever grow are a business model, not a teaching judgement.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the Dubai school year
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit in Gulf Standard Time around the school-run window, move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and can run through the long summer break while a family is travelling. The academic calendar here is not the northern-hemisphere default, and a plan built on that default loses weeks every year.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget each month for IB DP Psychology support?
faqs.answer: Build it from the hourly band rather than guessing a monthly figure. A single 60-minute session a week with a qualified subject teacher sits around AED 600-1,200 a month at published market rates; a 90-minute weekly session with an IB specialist, marking included, lands nearer AED 900-1,800; two sessions a week through the mock window runs AED 1,600-2,800. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions follow the same shape: AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist support in an examination year. These are market figures, not our quotation.

faqs.question: Is the hourly rate for IB Psychology lower than for Chemistry or Maths in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not meaningfully. Published rate cards in this market price by level and tier rather than by subject, so an IB specialist band of roughly AED 200-450 an hour applies whether the subject is Psychology, Chemistry or Mathematics. What does differ is how the hours are used. Psychology is assessed almost entirely in writing, so a sensible plan spends more on marking between lessons and less on worked-example practice than a Maths plan would. Two quotes at the same hourly rate can therefore buy quite different amounts of useful work, which is why the marking question matters more than the subject.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai Psychology quote usually include marking between sessions?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this is the largest hidden variable in the market. Budget tiers almost always sell the lesson hour alone. Mid-market and specialist tiers vary: some include a marked script each week, some bill marking separately at the same hourly rate, and some simply do not offer it. Since the 22-mark extended response and the option essays are where this subject's grade is produced, a plan without marking is paying for revision and hoping writing improves alongside it. Ask for the answer in writing before comparing two figures, because an apparently cheaper rate can total more.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home Psychology rate in Dubai higher than the online rate?
faqs.answer: Because the rate contains a drive. The published in-home band for Dubai is roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 200-450 for an online subject specialist. A 40-kilometre run from Mirdif to Dubai Marina at five in the afternoon is commonly 45 to 60 minutes each way, and that time is paid for whether the invoice itemises it or not. The second cost is narrower choice: an in-home search is limited to tutors willing to drive to your community, while an online search covers everyone who teaches your child's Paper 2 option.

faqs.question: Do Psychology tutoring rates in Dubai rise before the May examination session?
faqs.answer: Rates inside a tier are reasonably stable, but availability is not, and in practice that has the same effect on what you pay. Specialist diaries fill from January, through the mock window, and into the final run before the May session, so a family arranging support in March is choosing from what is left and usually paying at the upper end of the band. Booking in September or October costs the same per hour and gives a genuine choice of tutor. If you are starting late, be specific about the component you want fixed; a narrow brief is easier to place than an open one.

faqs.question: Is a package of ten Psychology sessions better value than paying weekly?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the package contains. A block is the right shape for finite work: experimental report supervision, a Paper 3 clinic at Higher Level, or an intensive run before mocks all have a beginning and an end. A block bought as a general discount on an open-ended arrangement is usually worse value, because it commits money before anyone knows which component needs the hours. Ask whether unused sessions expire, whether marking is inside the block, and whether the block can be paused during the long summer break or Ramadan without losing sessions.

faqs.question: Does VAT apply to the Psychology tutoring price we are quoted in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because the only thing any page should tell you is whether its own quoted figure is inclusive or exclusive. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general rule here: that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance or a tax adviser, and pages that assert it casually are guessing. What you can insist on is a quotation that says clearly whether AED figures include VAT, and a tax registration number where one is being charged.

faqs.question: What does supervision of the Psychology experimental report cost separately?
faqs.answer: It is usually bought as a block rather than an hourly add-on, because the work runs across weeks. Four to six sessions is typical, which at market specialist bands lands roughly AED 1,000-2,000 as a one-off. That covers choosing a replicable published study, scoping it so the results are analysable, the ethics position for a school-age sample, choosing and justifying a statistical test, and feedback on drafts the student has written. It does not include producing text; nobody legitimate offers that. The report carries 20 to 25 per cent of the final grade, which is why this block is the most cost-efficient support in the whole plan.

faqs.question: Can we reduce Psychology costs by sharing sessions with another student?
faqs.answer: Small-group rates in Dubai run roughly AED 90-200 per student per hour, so the saving is real. It works best for content coverage: the three approaches, study recall, revisiting an option. It works badly for essay work, because two students write differently and a 22-mark response needs individual band reasoning rather than general advice. A practical compromise many families use is group sessions for content through DP1 and individual sessions with marking once extended responses start. Check that both students sit the same level and the same Paper 2 option, or the group collapses into two half-lessons.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to prepare for the Higher Level research-methods paper?
faqs.answer: A short clinic rather than a long course. Paper 3 presents an unseen summary of a piece of research and asks about method, sampling, generalisability and ethics; it is a research-literacy skill, not a content load, and it responds quickly to drilling. Three to five focused sessions with unseen summaries done under time, marked, and reviewed will usually move it further than a term of general revision. That is a genuinely cheap intervention against a component carrying 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade, and it is the best-value thing on most HL plans.

faqs.question: How many Psychology sessions does a Dubai student usually need before mocks?
faqs.answer: There is no honest universal number, and anyone who quotes one has not seen the student's writing. What we can describe is the common shape: a diagnostic timed response first, then weekly 90-minute sessions with a marked script each week from about eight to ten weeks before the mock window, moving to two sessions a week for the final three or four weeks if the gap between band and target is large. Fewer, better-aimed hours with marking between them beat more hours without it. The monthly review exists so the frequency can drop when it should.

faqs.question: Will we pay more if our child studies Psychology at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the reason is syllabus size rather than tutor appetite. Standard Level carries a published allocation of 150 teaching hours and three assessed components; Higher Level carries 240 hours, a second option essay in Paper 2 and a separate research-methods paper. Those extra components are extra work to prepare, so an HL plan either runs longer or runs at a higher weekly intensity. The one saving available is targeting: the research-methods paper responds to a short clinic, so the extra HL cost need not be spread evenly across two years.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram charge Dubai families for the first Psychology lesson?
faqs.answer: No. The first lesson is free, with no card details taken and no minimum term afterwards. The condition worth stating plainly is that it is one lesson per student, and it is a real teaching session rather than a sales call: the student writes a short timed response and leaves with it marked against the criteria. You keep that marked script whether or not you continue. If the tutor is not the right match, say so and we will either propose a different specialist or tell you honestly that we do not have one free.

faqs.question: What happens to our Psychology plan during Ramadan and the summer break?
faqs.answer: It changes shape rather than stopping. During Ramadan the evening timetable shifts, so sessions move to post-Iftar slots or earlier afternoon windows, and most families reduce frequency for those weeks instead of cancelling and losing momentum. The long summer break is the opposite opportunity: it is the natural window for experimental report work, and because lessons run over live video they follow a family travelling abroad. Both are budget questions as much as scheduling ones, which is why the term-by-term plan on this page treats them as planned stages rather than interruptions.

faqs.question: Is paying for a Psychology tutor worth it if our school already runs revision clinics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes it is not, and that is a real answer. If the school runs clinics on the extended response and returns marked practice, you may need nothing beyond the report block. Private support earns its place when it supplies something the school structurally cannot: individual band reasoning on every script, a specialist in a Paper 2 option taught by one teacher to a large class, or a Higher Level research-methods clinic. Ask the DP coordinator what marked practice the school provides first, then buy the gap. That is the cheapest advice on this page.

dubai/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the numbers, then decide
dubai/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingBody: You now have the Dubai market bands in AED with their sources, the seven variables that move a quote, the component weightings you are buying against, a term-by-term plan, and the travel arithmetic behind in-home rates. If the sensible next step is a free trial lesson and a written plan priced against those bands, book one and keep the marked script either way. If the sensible next step is a conversation with your child's DP coordinator about which Paper 2 option they teach and what marked practice the school already provides, do that first. We would rather you spend nothing than spend badly.

intro.heading: How you tell a working ab initio tutor from a pleasant one
paragraphs: Beginner language tuition is the easiest kind of tutoring to fake and the hardest kind to judge. A student who starts Spanish ab initio in September knows almost nothing, so anything at all looks like progress. Six months later, a parent is still being told that lessons are going well, the student can order food in Spanish, and the first mock paper comes back at a 3. Nothing dishonest happened. The lessons simply were not pointed at the three things the course assesses.

The fix is an evidence habit, and it is cheap to insist on. Ask for a marked piece of written Spanish every fortnight, annotated with the criterion letter each comment relates to. Ask for a running error log, so the same mistake appearing in October and in February is visible as a pattern rather than as a one-off. Ask for one recorded oral attempt a month. Those three artefacts take a competent tutor almost no extra time to produce and they make the question of whether tuition is working answerable by a parent who does not speak Spanish.

That matters more in ab initio than in any other Group 2 course, because the starting point is zero and the finishing line is an external exam two years later. There is no prior attainment to compare against and no GCSE grade to anchor expectations. The only evidence available is what the student produces, so the quality of the record is the quality of the oversight. A tutor who cannot show you a marked task from last month is asking you to take a two-year course on trust.

Dubai adds its own pressure. Diploma cohorts in the city's IB schools are small, and an ab initio class is often the smallest set in the year group, sometimes six or seven students covering five prescribed themes with one teacher. Individual feedback inside the school day is limited by arithmetic rather than by willingness. That is the real reason families here buy outside help for a beginner language, and it is also why the help needs to produce a written record: it exists to supplement a feedback loop that the school cannot run one-to-one.

A note on the search term. The phrase people type is home tutor, and in Dubai that usually means someone driving to a villa or an apartment for an hour. IB Gram does not do that in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Spanish ab initio support reaches Dubai families as one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is also what makes the evidence habit practical: the marked file, the error log and the recordings all live in one shared folder the parent can open at any point.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Ab initio exists because the Diploma assumes every student takes a second language, including the ones who have never studied one. These are the stages around it, and what evidence each stage leaves behind for the next teacher to read.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Spanish ab initio is the beginner route in Group 2, examined at Standard Level across the two Diploma years. It is built around five prescribed themes with set topics inside each one, and it is assessed through a written task, a paper combining listening and reading, and a recorded Individual Oral. Because the course assumes no prior Spanish, coverage is explicit: the themes and topics define the vocabulary a student is expected to handle, which makes tracking what has actually been learnt unusually straightforward.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students arriving in ab initio are typically either new to the city and short of a language option, or transferring from a British school where a language was dropped after Year 9. Both groups land in DP1 with no reading habit in Spanish, which is the gap that shows up first in the receptive paper and last in the oral.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · Language acquisition phases 1-2 for beginners
programmes.description: A student entering MYP Spanish in phase 1 is doing roughly what ab initio does, at a slower pace and with no external exam. The four MYP criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing separately, which means an MYP report is an unusually useful piece of evidence for predicting ab initio readiness: a low criterion C or D score in MYP5 points at production problems that ab initio will expose quickly.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai continuum schools start a second language late, which leaves students entering the Diploma with phase 1 or 2 Spanish. Reading the MYP criterion breakdown rather than the overall level is the fastest way for a Dubai parent to predict whether ab initio or Spanish B is the honest choice for DP1.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, CAS and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The core does not assess Spanish, but it competes for the same hours. CAS commitments and the Extended Essay deadline both land in the middle of DP1, exactly when a beginner language needs daily contact rather than weekly bursts. Families who plan ab initio support without looking at the core calendar tend to lose the whole of the spring term to deadline collisions, and then try to buy the vocabulary back in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai school calendars put internal Extended Essay checkpoints and CAS reviews close together in the spring, and the long summer break follows. For a beginner, that break is a genuine risk: six weeks with no Spanish costs more at phase one than at any later stage, which is why short summer maintenance sessions matter here.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Group 2 at a Dubai IB school usually runs three or four languages across two or three levels. These are the routes an ab initio student is choosing between or will be compared with, described by what the evidence of competence actually looks like in each.

subjects.name: Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: The beginner course: five prescribed themes with set topics, a written task, a receptive paper covering listening and reading, and a recorded Individual Oral based on a visual stimulus. Evidence of progress is unusually concrete here because the vocabulary expectations are defined by the topic list, so coverage can be ticked off rather than guessed at.

subjects.name: Spanish B Standard Level
subjects.description: The continuing route for students with two or more years of prior Spanish. Same five themes, but texts are longer, the written task expects firmer control of tense and register, and the oral discussion goes further beyond the stimulus. A student placed here with ab initio-level Spanish produces evidence that looks like a plateau, not a climb.

subjects.name: Spanish B Higher Level
subjects.description: Adds two literary works originally written in Spanish, with the Individual Oral built on an extract from one of them. This is not a step up from ab initio; it is a different course for students with years of Spanish behind them. Moving between the two inside the Diploma is a coordinator decision with timetable consequences.

subjects.name: French ab initio
subjects.description: The same structure, the same three components, and in most Dubai IB schools the better-supplied of the two beginner languages. Where a school offers both, the choice often comes down to which teacher has capacity rather than which language suits the student, so ask what the ab initio set size will be before choosing.

subjects.name: Mandarin ab initio
subjects.description: Structurally identical and practically much heavier, because characters have to be learnt alongside everything else. Students who pick it for novelty and then compare workloads with the Spanish ab initio set in February are a recurring pattern in Dubai schools, and a late switch is rarely possible.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Separate from the Arabic that KHDA requires every Dubai private school to teach, and separate from the stream a non-Arab student follows for that requirement. Students carrying both the mandatory school Arabic and a Group 2 beginner language should have the weekly language minutes counted before anything is added.

subjects.name: Spanish A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 course for students whose Spanish is already a first language, and the only Spanish route that contributes towards the bilingual diploma. It is listed here because families sometimes assume ab initio can lead there within the Diploma. It cannot: the two sit at opposite ends of the language provision.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Taken by many Dubai students whose first language is not English, and the course most likely to be competing for the same revision hours as Spanish ab initio. Where both appear on a timetable, the evidence file for each needs to be separate, because the error patterns are entirely different and a single tutor rarely covers both well.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Not a language subject, but the core component most likely to eat the weeks a beginner needs for vocabulary consolidation. It is worth plotting the TOK essay deadline against the ab initio topic schedule in DP1 before agreeing a tuition rhythm, so the two do not collide in the same fortnight.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Families contact us about Spanish ab initio from across Dubai, and the thing that varies by area is not the teaching but the window in which a beginner can realistically sit down and concentrate. These are the patterns we see.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Science Park
regions.note: Several Diploma cohorts within a few kilometres, so ab initio sets here are often shared between schools in extracurricular study groups. Weekday slots at 5pm work; anything earlier collides with bus routes that wind through the community before dropping off.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Long bus journeys into the school clusters further east, which means a DP1 student is frequently home after 4.30pm and flat. Beginner vocabulary work goes better in two short weekday sessions here than in one long evening block.

regions.name: The Greens, Al Sufouh and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Apartment living with siblings in the same room, so a recorded oral attempt needs a planned quiet half hour rather than a spontaneous one. Families here tend to schedule the monthly recording at the weekend and keep weekdays for written work.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah and Dubai Marina
regions.note: Frequent travel in and out of term time, which is the single biggest risk to a beginner language. The evidence habit matters more here than anywhere: a student who misses three weeks in November has a measurable topic gap, and the error log is what finds it.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City and Motor City
regions.note: A wide spread of curricula and a thinner concentration of IB candidates, so ab initio students here are often the only beginner in their friendship group. That isolation shows up as a motivation problem rather than a learning problem, and short frequent sessions hold it better.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Villa communities with easy weekend mornings and heavy weekday evenings, especially in families running multiple school runs. Saturday morning sessions are common here and suit vocabulary consolidation, which benefits from being done when the student is not already tired.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Mixed Indian, British and IB catchments within a short radius, and a high proportion of students carrying the school's mandatory Arabic stream alongside their Group 2 language. Counting total weekly language minutes before adding tuition is particularly worth doing in this part of the city.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South, Dubai Science Park and Jumeirah Village
schoolClusters.note: Diploma cohorts in this belt are large enough to run several Group 2 languages and small enough that the beginner set is often the smallest class in the year. Students we support attend schools across this area, and the evidence request we hear most is simply for something written down between parent evenings.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim, Al Jaddaf and Dubai Festival City
schoolClusters.note: A belt where several schools run the full IB continuum, so a student may have been in the same language programme since primary and still arrive at the Diploma as a beginner because the second language changed along the way. That history is worth reading before any tuition plan is set.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of working cover almost every ab initio request from Dubai, and they are distinguished by what each one leaves behind in the shared file rather than by how long the lesson lasts.

modes.title: Fortnightly diagnostic cycle
modes.description: The default for DP1. The student writes a short task to a topic from the current theme, the tutor marks it against the criterion letters and returns it annotated, and the next session opens on the two weakest comments rather than on new material. Over a term this produces six marked pieces and a visible trend line, which is the evidence a parent can actually read.
bullets: Six marked tasks per term, each annotated by criterion
Error log updated the same evening, with repeat errors flagged
Topic coverage ticked against the prescribed list
Session note naming what moved and what did not

modes.title: Vocabulary build with retrieval records
modes.description: Beginner Spanish fails on volume before it fails on grammar. This mode runs short, frequent sessions built around spaced retrieval, with the tested items and the pass rate recorded rather than described. It is deliberately unglamorous, and it is the format that moves the receptive paper most per hour, because that paper rewards recognition breadth above everything else.
bullets: Two or three short sessions a week rather than one long one
Tested items and scores logged per session
Lists drawn from the prescribed topics, not from a generic textbook
Monthly retest of items first met eight weeks earlier

modes.title: Recorded oral readiness checks
modes.description: One recorded attempt a month from early DP1, against a visual stimulus the student has not seen, timed as the real thing is timed. The recording is compared with the previous month's, and the comparison is the point: a beginner cannot hear their own improvement, and a parent certainly cannot, so the archive does the arguing.
bullets: Unseen stimulus each time, drawn from a different theme
Timed to the format the school will use
Stored so attempt one and attempt six can be played back to back
No scripting, no pre-seen prompts, no rehearsed answers

sections.heading: What ab initio actually means, and who the school will allow into it
paragraphs: Ab initio means from the beginning, and the course is built for students with little or no previous experience of the language. That is an eligibility rule, not a marketing description. Schools are expected to place students appropriately, and a student with several years of Spanish behind them does not belong in the beginner set however convenient the timetable makes it. The decision sits with the school's Diploma coordinator, who is working from the student's language history rather than from a parent's preference.

This matters because families sometimes approach a tutor hoping to engineer a placement. A student who has studied Spanish to Year 9 in a British school and then stopped is a genuinely awkward case, and the honest answer is that the coordinator decides it, not us. What a tutor can usefully do is produce a diagnostic: a short written task and a timed listening set, marked, showing where the student actually sits. That evidence is more use in a conversation with the school than any opinion.

The second thing to know is that ab initio runs at Standard Level only. There is no Higher Level ab initio, and no mechanism for taking it at HL by doing extra work. Families who want a Higher Level language in Group 2 are looking at Spanish B HL, which is a different course with two literary works inside it. Anyone offering to prepare a student for Higher Level ab initio is describing something that does not exist, which is a useful early filter when you are choosing a provider.
bullets: Eligibility is based on prior exposure and decided by the school, not by the tutor
Standard Level is the only level at which the course is offered
A marked diagnostic is the most useful thing to bring to a placement conversation
A provider offering Higher Level ab initio is describing a course that does not exist

sections.heading: The evidence file: what you should see in the first six weeks
paragraphs: Six weeks is long enough for a real pattern to appear and short enough that a bad match can still be corrected cheaply. By the end of it, a parent should be able to open a folder and find three marked written tasks, one recorded oral attempt, an error log with dated entries, and a topic coverage list with items ticked. None of that requires speaking Spanish to interpret. If the folder is empty and the feedback is verbal, that is the finding.

The table below is the schedule we work to, and it is deliberately boring. Week one is diagnostic only, because starting to teach before you know the gap wastes the first month. Weeks two to five alternate production and marking. Week six is a repeat of the week one diagnostic, which is the single most informative artefact in the whole set: the same task, attempted twice, six weeks apart, marked by the same criteria. A parent who reads nothing else should read that pair.

What this does not produce is a predicted grade, and any tutor offering one after six weeks of a beginner course is inventing it. Six weeks of ab initio tells you whether vocabulary is being retained, whether the student can produce a sentence without a model in front of them, and whether the oral is improving in fluency or only in length. Those three findings are enough to decide whether to continue, change the rhythm, or change the tutor.

sections.heading: Three components, one level: where the ab initio marks sit
paragraphs: Spanish ab initio is assessed through three components. A written task carries a quarter of the grade. A receptive skills paper, combining listening and reading, carries half. The Individual Oral, conducted and recorded in school, carries the final quarter. There is no literary element and no second paper of extended writing, which makes the shape of the course simpler than Spanish B and the consequences of neglecting the receptive paper more severe.

Half the grade in one paper changes how tuition should be scoped. Families instinctively buy speaking practice, because speaking is what a beginner visibly cannot do and because conversation feels like a lesson. The paper that carries twice the weight rewards recognition vocabulary breadth and careful question reading, and it improves through volume of exposure and timed practice rather than through chat. If the budget only stretches to one component, the weighting says receptive skills.

Component details, timings and word bands should be confirmed against the current subject guide your school issues, and the component dates against the Diploma coordinator. This page does not publish an IB exam or results date, because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project and an unconfirmed date on a page like this is worse than no date. The weightings below are the stable part; treat the operational detail as something to check in writing.

One more structural point is worth making, because it changes how a tutor should plan. The written task and the oral are both production components, and they improve together: a student who can write three paragraphs on transport can usually talk about transport. The receptive paper is different in kind. It rewards recognising words the student would never produce, which means passive breadth has to be built deliberately rather than picked up as a side effect of speaking practice. Tuition that only ever asks the student to produce language quietly starves the component carrying half the grade, and the deficit does not show up until a timed paper is attempted.

sections.heading: Marking an ab initio written task by criterion letter
paragraphs: The most useful thing a parent can ask for is marking by criterion letter rather than by a general comment. The written task is assessed on language, on message, and on conceptual understanding, with language and message carrying the larger allocations and conceptual understanding the smaller one. Knowing which letter is losing the marks changes what the next six sessions should contain, and it is information the student's own school report rarely gives in that form.

A beginner losing marks on language needs volume: more verbs, more structures, more retrieval. A beginner losing marks on message needs task discipline, because the content is usually there and the task's requirements have been half answered. A beginner losing marks on conceptual understanding has usually written something competent in the wrong register or the wrong text type: a formal letter that reads like a text message, or a blog with no audience awareness. Those are three different tutoring programmes and they are routinely treated as one.

Criterion allocations should be checked against the current guide, and a tutor who cannot name the criteria without looking them up is telling you something. What should not vary is the practice: every marked task returned with the letters attached, every comment tied to one of them, and the error log sorted the same way. After a term, that sorting is what shows whether the problem is shifting or simply being described in new words each month.

sections.heading: The five prescribed themes, and how coverage gets tracked
paragraphs: Ab initio is organised around five prescribed themes, each containing set topics. That structure is a gift for oversight, because it turns a vague question about whether the course is being covered into a list that can be ticked. A student three terms into ab initio should be able to produce language on most topics within at least three of the themes, and the gaps should be known rather than discovered in a mock.

In practice, coverage drifts for ordinary reasons. A school's ab initio set loses lessons to assemblies, examinations and the Diploma core calendar. A tutor following a textbook rather than the topic list covers what the book sequences rather than what the course requires. A student who missed three weeks in November has a specific, nameable hole. None of that is anybody's fault, and all of it is invisible without a coverage list that somebody updates.

The way we handle it is unremarkable: the list lives in the shared file, each topic gets marked as taught, practised, or assessed, and the three states are not the same thing. Taught means it was explained. Practised means the student produced language with it. Assessed means there is a marked piece of work. A list showing twenty topics taught and four assessed is a warning, and it is the kind of warning a parent can see without speaking a word of Spanish.

Coverage also interacts with the oral in a way families rarely anticipate. The recorded assessment uses a stimulus linked to one of the themes, and a student who has strong vocabulary across two themes and thin vocabulary across three is gambling on which one appears. Spreading the work so that no theme is left untouched is worth more in the final term than polishing the themes the student already enjoys, and the coverage list is what makes that trade-off visible rather than a matter of taste.

sections.heading: What progress actually looks like in a beginner language, month by month
paragraphs: Progress in ab initio is not linear and the shape surprises parents. The first two months look spectacular, because going from nothing to a hundred words is a large relative change. Months three to six look like stagnation, because the student is consolidating and the visible performance barely shifts. Months seven to ten is where the second jump happens, as retrieval becomes fast enough for production to stop being effortful. Families who judge tuition in month four frequently cancel it just before it would have worked.

The things that genuinely indicate movement are quiet. Response latency in the oral falls before accuracy rises. Written tasks get longer before they get better, and then shorter and better. Reading comprehension improves on inference questions last, long after vocabulary questions are secure. Listening scores move in steps rather than smoothly, because each step corresponds to a bundle of recognised words crossing a threshold. A tutor who tracks those four indicators can tell you what is happening in month four. A tutor tracking only marks cannot.

This is also why the monthly recording matters so much. A parent listening to a student's attempt from October and from February hears the difference immediately, even with no Spanish, because latency and hesitation are audible in any language. That comparison is the single most persuasive piece of evidence in the file, and it costs one unseen stimulus and five minutes a month to produce. No tutor who is actually working will object to making it.
bullets: Month 1-2: fast visible gains, low durability

sections.heading: Ab initio or Spanish B, and the cost of getting it wrong
paragraphs: The placement decision is the highest-leverage thing in this whole course and it is usually made on a timetable constraint. A student with genuine beginner Spanish placed into Spanish B spends two years producing work that misses the band descriptors for reasons of exposure rather than effort, and the evidence file shows a flat line no amount of tuition bends. A student with four years of Spanish parked in ab initio is bored by November and still has to sit the exam.

There are consequences beyond the grade. Some university courses specify a continuing language rather than a beginner one for certain degree routes, so a student with a specific language-related plan should check the entry requirements of the universities they are considering before settling the level. Neither ab initio nor Spanish B contributes towards the bilingual diploma, which requires two Group 1 languages or a Group 3 or 4 subject studied in a second language. Families frequently assume otherwise, and the assumption is worth correcting early rather than in DP2.

What a tutor contributes to this decision is a marked diagnostic and nothing more. The coordinator decides, the school's placement rules govern it, and the honest role of outside help is to make sure the conversation happens with evidence on the table. Where a family asks us to argue for a placement with a school, we decline; where they ask for a short written diagnostic they can take to the coordinator themselves, that is a reasonable thing to buy.

sections.heading: What the evidence cannot show, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: An evidence file is powerful and it has limits worth naming. It cannot predict a final grade, and nobody should offer one. It cannot tell you how a student will perform in a room on a single morning with an unfamiliar stimulus. It cannot separate tuition from the school's teaching, from maturation, or from the student finally deciding to care. Anyone presenting a folder of marked work as proof that their tuition caused an outcome is overreaching, and we are not going to do that here.

There are also claims this page deliberately does not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and describes itself that way nowhere. No school named on this page is a client or a partner. No statistic appears here without a date and a source, which is why there is no satisfaction figure and no average score. No IB exam or results date appears, because the IB's own site returns an error to automated checks and an unverified date would be a liability on every page in this set.

The boundary on coursework is firm for the same reason. A tutor may explain the criteria, read a draft and say where it is weak, question a choice, and model a text type on a different topic. A tutor may not produce finished work, write into a student's draft, or supply a script for the oral. That is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student. Official guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB and are not ours to distribute; the place to read them is through the school or ibo.org.

sections.heading: Reading a Dubai school report on an ab initio student
paragraphs: Reports on beginner language students are the hardest to interpret in the whole Diploma, because the scale assumes two years of progress and the student has had four months. A 4 in the first DP1 report may be entirely healthy or quietly alarming, and the number alone does not say which. What distinguishes the two is the comment, and specifically whether it names a skill or describes an attitude.

A comment that names a skill is usable. Struggles to produce extended writing without a model points at the language criterion. Answers two of three task requirements points at message. Reads the question too quickly points at the receptive paper. Any of those can be turned into a six-week plan. A comment about enthusiasm, participation or being a pleasure to teach is kind and tells you nothing about the exam, and in a beginner language it is the most common kind of comment there is.

The second thing to read is the gap between the oral mark and the written mark. In ab initio those two separate early and the direction matters. A student stronger orally than on paper usually has a confidence advantage and a vocabulary debt, and responds well to written volume. A student stronger on paper than orally is usually retaining well and avoiding production, and needs the monthly recording habit more urgently than anything else. Both are fixable; they are not fixable with the same plan, which is the whole argument for marking by criterion rather than by impression.
bullets: Read the comment for a named skill, not for a tone

process.description: The week one task is repeated under the same conditions and marked by the same criteria. That pair of documents is the review. Hours go up, down, or get reallocated between the receptive paper and production work, and where the honest reading is that the match is wrong, we change the tutor rather than defend the choice.

process.description: A fresh diagnostic at the start of every term, plotted against the Diploma core calendar so vocabulary consolidation does not land in the same fortnight as the Extended Essay checkpoint. Summer gets short maintenance sessions rather than a break, because six weeks without Spanish costs a beginner more than it costs anyone else.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to take Spanish ab initio in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The course is designed for students with little or no previous experience of Spanish, and placement is decided by the school's Diploma coordinator against that rule rather than by a parent's preference or a tutor's opinion. A student who studied Spanish for several years and then stopped is a genuinely awkward case and the coordinator weighs the history. The most useful thing an outside tutor can contribute is a short marked diagnostic — a written task and a timed listening set — showing where the student actually sits. Take that to the placement conversation; it carries more weight than an assertion from anyone.

faqs.question: Can a Dubai student sit Spanish ab initio at Higher Level if they do extra work?
faqs.answer: No. Ab initio is offered at Standard Level only, and there is no mechanism for sitting it at Higher Level by covering extra material, however much a student does. A candidate who needs a Higher Level language in Group 2 is looking at Spanish B HL, which assumes years of prior Spanish and includes two literary works originally written in the language. Any provider advertising preparation for Higher Level ab initio is describing a course that does not exist, which makes it a quick and useful filter when you are comparing tutors in Dubai.

faqs.question: How will we know a Spanish ab initio tutor is actually working?
faqs.answer: Ask for artefacts rather than assurances. A working arrangement produces a marked written task every fortnight with the criterion letters attached, a dated error log where repeated mistakes are visible as a pattern, one recorded oral attempt a month against an unseen stimulus, and a topic coverage list showing what has been taught, practised and assessed. All four are readable by a parent with no Spanish. If six weeks have passed and the folder is empty while the feedback is warm and verbal, you have your answer without needing to understand a word of the content.

faqs.question: What should a Spanish ab initio beginner be able to do after six weeks?
faqs.answer: Produce a short piece of writing on a familiar topic without a model in front of them, recognise core topic vocabulary reliably under timed conditions, and get through an unseen visual stimulus in a recorded attempt without long silences. None of that is impressive in isolation. What makes it meaningful is the comparison with the week one baseline, repeated under identical conditions and marked against the same criteria. That pair of documents is worth more than any verbal progress report, and it is the thing to ask for at the end of the first six weeks.

faqs.question: How is the Spanish ab initio written task marked?
faqs.answer: Against criteria covering language, message and conceptual understanding, with language and message carrying the larger allocations. Knowing which letter is losing the marks matters because the three imply different work: language means vocabulary and structure volume, message means the task's requirements are being half answered, and conceptual understanding usually means correct Spanish in the wrong register or text type. Confirm the exact allocations against the current subject guide your school issues. A tutor who cannot name the criteria is not marking against them, whatever the comments on the page say.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Spanish B to Spanish ab initio during DP1?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a coordinator decision constrained by the timetable, the set sizes and the school's placement rules. It is far easier in the first weeks of DP1 than after the first reporting cycle, and in many Dubai schools it becomes impossible once internal assessment work has started. If you think the placement is wrong, raise it early and bring evidence: a marked written task and a timed listening score say more than a description of how the student feels about the lessons. We will produce that diagnostic; we will not lobby a school on a family's behalf.

faqs.question: Does Spanish ab initio count towards the IB bilingual diploma?
faqs.answer: No, and neither does Spanish B. The bilingual diploma is awarded on the basis of two Group 1 language and literature subjects, or a Group 3 or Group 4 subject studied and assessed in a language other than the student's Group 1 language, subject to the IB's grade requirements. Group 2 acquisition courses, beginner or continuing, do not qualify. Families in Dubai assume otherwise surprisingly often, usually after reading a summary rather than the regulations, and the assumption is much cheaper to correct in DP1 than in the final term.

faqs.question: Is Spanish ab initio easier than Spanish B?
faqs.answer: It starts easier and it does not stay easy. The vocabulary expectations are defined by the prescribed topics rather than by authentic text, which makes the course trackable and the workload predictable. But it compresses two years of language learning into two years of Diploma, alongside five other subjects and the core, and the receptive paper still carries half the grade. Students who choose it expecting a soft option tend to discover in DP2 that beginner Spanish under exam timing is not soft. It is a fairer course, not a lighter one.

faqs.question: Will a Spanish ab initio grade be accepted for university language requirements?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the course and the institution, and it is worth checking directly rather than inferring. Some degree routes specify a continuing language rather than a beginner one, particularly where the degree itself involves the language. Most courses with no language element treat Group 2 as a Diploma subject like any other. Check the published entry requirements of the universities on your child's list before the level is settled, because the time to discover a specific requirement is DP1 and not the application cycle. Tutoring is not a requirement for any of this.

faqs.question: How much vocabulary does Spanish ab initio actually require?
faqs.answer: Enough to handle the set topics inside all five prescribed themes under timed conditions, which is a larger quantity than the word count of any textbook chapter suggests and smaller than the open-ended demand of Spanish B. The practical implication is that retention beats exposure: a student who has met three thousand words and retrieves eight hundred reliably will outperform one who has met five thousand and retrieves the same eight hundred slowly. That is why retrieval records, with tested items and pass rates logged, are more useful than a list of topics covered.

faqs.question: Does the ab initio written task have to be handwritten in the exam?
faqs.answer: Sit arrangements are set by the school as the examination centre, and most Dubai IB schools still run written components on paper, which makes handwriting speed and accent marks a real variable rather than a detail. Check with your child's Diploma coordinator what format the school uses and whether any access arrangements apply. If the component is handwritten, timed practice on paper rather than on a laptop matters: students who have only ever typed Spanish lose accents, lose legibility and run out of time, and all three are trainable in a few sessions.

faqs.question: What does the Individual Oral involve in Spanish ab initio?
faqs.answer: A recorded assessment conducted in school, built around a visual stimulus linked to one of the prescribed themes: the student presents on the stimulus and then takes part in a discussion with the teacher. It carries a quarter of the grade. Preparation that works is monthly rehearsal against stimuli the student has not seen, recorded and compared with earlier attempts. Preparation that does not work is rehearsing a script, which is also academic malpractice if it is carried into the real assessment. Confirm the exact format and timings with the coordinator before planning around them.

faqs.question: How often should a Spanish ab initio student in Dubai have lessons?
faqs.answer: For a beginner, two or three short sessions a week usually beat one long weekly session at the same total cost, because retention responds to spacing rather than duration. Thirty to forty minutes, three times a week, with retrieval testing logged each time, moves recognition vocabulary faster than ninety minutes on a Saturday. The exception is the oral, which needs a longer uninterrupted slot once a month for the recorded attempt. Dubai school runs make short weekday slots awkward, which is one practical reason online delivery suits this particular course.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit homes in Dubai for Spanish ab initio lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Spanish ab initio support reaches Dubai families as one-to-one teaching over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with marked work and recordings kept in a shared folder the parent can open. For this course that arrangement has a practical advantage beyond the tutor pool: short, frequent sessions three times a week are realistic over video and very difficult to arrange with somebody driving across the city for each one.

faqs.question: What should a Spanish ab initio tutor send us each month?
faqs.answer: Two marked written tasks with criterion letters attached, an updated error log with dates so repeated mistakes are visible, one recorded oral attempt against an unseen stimulus, and the topic coverage list with new items marked as taught, practised or assessed. Plus a short note naming what moved and what did not. That is a fifteen-minute administrative load on a competent tutor and it is the difference between oversight and hope. If a provider treats the request as unusual, it is reasonable to read that as an answer in itself.

intro.heading: Spanish from a standing start, in two school years, with the marking shown
paragraphs: Spanish ab initio is the IB Diploma Programme course for a student who begins with little or no Spanish. It is examined at Standard Level only, it carries the same grade scale of 1 to 7 as every other Diploma subject, and it has to take a Year 12 student from near-zero to a scripted oral and a timed writing paper in roughly twenty months of school terms. That compression is the whole problem. A Dubai student picking it up in September has two Ramadan periods, two sets of mocks, an Internal Assessment in a different subject and an Extended Essay to write before the May session arrives.

Most families searching for an IB DP Spanish ab initio online tutor in Dubai are not looking for conversation practice. They are looking at a report card that says 3 or 4 and cannot tell whether the problem is vocabulary, grammar, exam technique or simply that the student cannot hear fast spoken Spanish. Those four problems need four different kinds of session, and guessing between them wastes the few months that are left. The first thing a tutor should do is produce a marked diagnostic that separates them.

That is what this page is built around. Not a promise about outcomes, which nobody can honestly make, but the evidence a parent is entitled to see each week: which task was set, what it scored against the published assessment criteria, which criterion moved, and which one did not. A student who scores 7 out of 12 on language and 4 out of 12 on message in October, and 8 and 8 in February, has a graph. A student whose tutor reports that lessons are going well has nothing.

Delivery is online. IB Gram matches Dubai families with one-to-one tutors over live video, screen-shared with the student's own past papers and drafts open on the same document. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For a language subject this is less of a compromise than parents expect, because the thing a Spanish ab initio candidate most needs is a specialist in that exact syllabus, and the pool of those within a twenty-minute drive of any one Dubai community is small.

The sections below cover the placement decision between ab initio and Spanish B, the three assessed components and what each is worth, the specific places marks disappear, what a marked evidence file looks like at week four against week twenty, the oral in detail, what the Dubai market charges for language tuition, the two years counted backwards from the May session, and the academic-honesty line that applies when the assessed work is a piece of writing in a second language.
