The gap between those starting points is wide, and a tutor's first job in this city is usually diagnostic: establishing whether the student is short of vocabulary, short of grammar, or simply short of exam technique.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Spanish is organised into phases rather than year groups, and the phase a student reaches by MYP5 largely decides whether Spanish B or Spanish ab initio is the sensible DP choice. Assessment runs on four criteria covering comprehension of spoken and visual text, comprehension of written text, communication in response to both, and the use of language in oral and written form. A student stuck in an early phase at 15 is the single most common reason a Dubai family starts looking for Spanish help.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai IB continuum schools run Spanish from Year 7 with one or two lessons a week, which is enough to build recognition and not enough to build production. Families who see a phase 3 report in MYP5 and a Spanish B SL offer in DP1 are usually looking at a vocabulary debt that takes a term of structured work to clear, not a term of conversation.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP additional language teaching gives a Dubai child early Spanish through transdisciplinary units rather than through formal grammar. There is no external assessment, so nothing here is examinable, but the phonics and the listening habit formed in these years is what later separates a comfortable Spanish B student from a struggling one. Work at this stage is about exposure and confidence, and it is the cheapest Spanish support a family will ever buy.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary timetables are crowded with the KHDA mandatory subjects alongside the licensed curriculum, so additional-language minutes are limited. Parents who want their child to reach DP Spanish B comfortably tend to add a short weekly session from Year 4 rather than a crash programme in Year 10, and the total spend over those years is lower.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Group 2 is the part of the Diploma where Dubai families most often discover their child is in the wrong course. These are the Spanish routes and the neighbouring language options, with what each one actually demands and roughly where it sits in the market.

subjects.name: Spanish B Higher Level
subjects.description: Two literary works in Spanish, a longer Paper 1 response, and an Individual Oral built on a literary extract rather than a photograph. HL is where the price gap opens: the pool of tutors who can discuss a Spanish novel and mark against the band descriptors is far smaller than the pool who can run a conversation class, and specialist bands of AED 200-450 reflect that.

subjects.name: Spanish B Standard Level
subjects.description: Same four assessment components, no literary works, shorter written task, and an oral built on a visual stimulus linked to one of the five themes. SL is the most commonly tutored Group 2 course in Dubai and the one where a qualified online teacher in the AED 150-300 band is usually the right purchase rather than a premium specialist.

subjects.name: Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: The beginner route, restricted to students with little or no prior exposure to Spanish, and available at Standard Level only. Families sometimes ask to move a struggling Spanish B student across. That is a decision for the school's DP coordinator against the eligibility rules, not a tutoring choice, and it has consequences for university language prerequisites.

subjects.name: Spanish A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 course for students whose Spanish is already a first language. It is a literature and textual analysis course, not a language-learning one, and it is the only Spanish route that contributes towards the bilingual diploma. Tutoring here is closer to English Literature support in character and is priced with Group 1 subjects rather than Group 2.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: Structurally identical to Spanish B, same four components, same five themes, and the most widely taught Group 2 language in Dubai IB schools. Supply is better than for Spanish, which keeps French B quotes at the lower end of the qualified-teacher band and makes it a useful benchmark when you are judging whether a Spanish quote is reasonable.

subjects.name: German B
subjects.description: Narrower supply again, and a grammar load that behaves differently from Spanish: case endings and word order cost marks in writing where Spanish students lose them on tense and subjunctive. Dubai families with a German school background often run German B alongside Spanish ab initio, and the combined timetable needs planning rather than two separate bookings.

subjects.name: Mandarin B
subjects.description: The character workload makes this the most front-loaded Group 2 course, and the one where weekly contact matters more than session length. Rates sit at the top of the qualified band in Dubai because the teaching pool is small and much of it is outside the Gulf time zone, which is also why scheduling tends to decide the match.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Distinct from the KHDA mandatory Arabic that every Dubai private school must teach, and examined as a Group 2 acquisition course with the same component structure as Spanish B. Students carrying both the school's mandatory Arabic stream and a Group 2 language have a heavier language week than their timetable suggests.

subjects.name: Hindi B
subjects.description: Common in Dubai's Indian-curriculum IB schools, with a script demand that sits outside anything a Spanish student faces. Where a family runs Spanish B for one child and Hindi B for another, two separate specialists are usually the honest answer rather than one tutor stretched across both.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Spanish B
subjects.description: A 4,000-word essay written in Spanish about the culture of a Spanish-speaking region. It is supervised inside the school, and a tutor's role is strictly process coaching: question framing, source evaluation and feedback on the student's own drafts. Blocks of EE support are usually bought by the hour in short bursts around the school's internal deadlines.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where you live in Dubai changes an in-home Spanish quote and does not change an online one. These are the areas families contact us from most, with the travel reality that the market prices into a home visit.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment living with no spare study room, and a 4pm school run that collides with Sheikh Zayed Road traffic. In-home tutors price the Business Bay drop-off premium into the rate; an online session simply starts at 4.45pm once the child is in the lift.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Tower access, visitor parking and lift waits add fifteen minutes at each end of an in-home visit before any teaching happens. Marina families tend to be the first to switch a language subject online, because the saved travel buys a second weekly session at the same monthly spend.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Villa communities close to several IB and British schools, so the local tutor pool is relatively deep for Maths and Science and still thin for Spanish B HL. This is the area where the gap between what is nearby and what is needed shows up most clearly.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Dubai Hills
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the city, which means Spanish B candidates here are often in the same cohort and chasing the same two or three known tutors before the May session. Booking in September costs less than booking in February for exactly that reason.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Long internal drives inside the community, plus gate access, so an in-home tutor's effective hourly cost climbs further than the published rate suggests. Weekend morning sessions are easier here than weekday evenings, and online slots make Friday mornings usable.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Mixed curriculum catchment with IB, Indian and British schools within a few kilometres, so sibling sets often need two different language courses at once. Running both online removes the problem of a single tutor's travel window deciding both children's timetable.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Furthest from the tutor supply that clusters around Al Barsha and Jumeirah, which is where in-home premiums bite hardest in this city. Families here see the largest difference between an online quote and a visiting-tutor quote for the same qualification.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and the Dubai Hills corridor
schoolClusters.note: This corridor holds the heaviest concentration of Diploma candidates in Dubai, and Group 2 demand here peaks twice a year: once in October when DP1 students meet Paper 2 listening properly, and again in January when DP2 mock results land. Students we support attend schools across this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Al Jaddaf, Dubai Festival City, Mirdif and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: A more curriculum-mixed belt where IB Diploma cohorts are smaller per school, so a Spanish B class of six or seven is normal and individual attention inside the school day is limited. That smaller cohort is the usual trigger for buying outside help in this part of the city.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Spanish B request that reaches us from Dubai, and they differ in price mainly because they differ in how many marked pieces of work come out of each hour.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, criterion-marked
modes.description: A fixed slot each week with a Group 2 teacher, run over live video with a shared screen for the text being worked on. The student produces a Paper 1 task or a reading response between sessions; it comes back annotated against the band descriptors, and the next session starts from the weakest descriptor rather than from the next textbook chapter.

modes.title: Individual Oral rehearsal block
modes.description: A short, intensive run of sessions bought in a block rather than weekly, aimed only at the oral component. The work is recorded practice against unseen stimuli, timing discipline, and the follow-up discussion that most students under-prepare. Blocks are the cheaper way to buy oral readiness because they stop when the student is ready rather than running all year.

modes.description: Listening is the component Dubai students most often write off as untrainable, and it is the one where structured work pays fastest. A clinic hour is spent on audio under exam timing, on the gap between hearing a word and recording it accurately, and on the question types that reward prediction. It is sold as a short course rather than ongoing tuition.

sections.heading: What a Spanish B tutor in Dubai actually costs per hour
paragraphs: A qualified language teacher working online with a Dubai family quotes between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour in this market. An in-home one-to-one visit, with travel priced into the rate, runs from about AED 180 to AED 500. An IB DP subject specialist who can mark against the band descriptors sits between AED 200 and AED 450 and upwards. Those are the three bands that matter for Spanish B, and the table below sets them beside the cheaper and dearer ends of the market so the whole range is visible at once.

Every figure in that table is a market band read in October 2026 from published rate cards and provider pages, labelled by provider model rather than by brand. None of them is an IB Gram price. We do not publish an hourly card on these pages because the honest answer depends on level, component and frequency, and a single number would be wrong for most of the families reading it. What the bands are for is judging whether a quote you have been given is normal, high or implausibly low.

The implausibly low end deserves a sentence of its own. Rates starting near AED 45 an hour exist in Dubai and buy real conversation practice, often from a university student. For a DP2 candidate six months from the May session, that purchase will raise spoken confidence and leave the reading paper exactly where it was, because nobody in that transaction has read the band descriptors. For an MYP3 student building vocabulary, the same purchase can be entirely sensible. The rate is not the problem; the mismatch between the rate and the job is.
bullets: Judge a quote against the band for that provider model, not against the cheapest number you have seen
Ask what comes back marked, and against which criteria
Ask whether the rate is per 60-minute hour or per 45-minute lesson
Ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT, and get the answer in writing

sections.heading: Six variables that move a Spanish B quote in Dubai
paragraphs: The spread between AED 150 and AED 450 for what sounds like the same hour is not arbitrary. Six variables account for most of it, and a parent who knows them can usually move a quote without arguing about the rate. Level is the largest: Higher Level carries two literary works and a longer written response, so the tutor pool shrinks and the price rises with the scarcity rather than with the difficulty.

Timing is the second. A Spanish B specialist booked in September has a timetable with gaps in it. The same specialist in late January, with a DP2 cohort across three Dubai schools already in their diary, is allocating a scarce slot and prices accordingly. Families who book language support early do not get a discount so much as avoid a surcharge, and they also get the slot that fits the school run rather than the one left over.

The remaining four are session length, bundling, the native-speaker request and component scope. Ninety minutes is not 1.5 times the cost of sixty in most quotes, because the fixed preparation and marking time is spread over a longer lesson. Two children in the same house can often share a tutor's preparation if they are at the same level. A request for a native speaker narrows the pool before quality is even discussed, and narrowing a pool raises a price. Asking for everything, every week, costs more than asking for the oral in a block and the listening in a clinic.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home Spanish tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search term is really about, so it deserves a straight answer. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Spanish B teaching for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the text on a shared screen. That is a real constraint and this page is not going to pretend otherwise, so here is the case on its merits.

The merits are mostly about who you can reach. A Dubai family hiring within driving distance is choosing from the Spanish teachers who happen to live near them and have a free weekday evening. A family hiring online is choosing from the Spanish B teachers who are free at that hour anywhere in a compatible time zone. For a subject taught to small cohorts in a minority of the city's schools, that difference is not marginal: it is frequently the difference between a Group 2 specialist and a general Spanish speaker.

There are things the in-room format does better, and the honest list is short. A reluctant twelve-year-old is easier to hold in a chair when an adult is physically present. A student with no quiet space at home may concentrate better with a tutor sitting opposite than with a laptop in a shared living room. Handwriting under exam conditions is simpler to supervise in person. For a sixteen-to-nineteen-year-old working on Spanish B, none of those usually outweighs having the right teacher, which is why the table below compares the formats on the dimensions that actually change a grade.

sections.heading: What you are buying: the Spanish B assessment weightings
paragraphs: Before agreeing any rate, it is worth knowing what the money is pointed at. Spanish B is assessed through three external components and one internal one. Paper 1 is a single written task chosen from three options, responding to a stimulus, and it carries a quarter of the grade. Paper 2 combines a listening section and a reading section and carries half. The Individual Oral, conducted and recorded inside the school, carries the remaining quarter.

The weightings are identical at Standard and Higher Level; what changes is the demand inside each component. HL writing asks for a substantially longer response, HL reading uses denser texts, and the HL Individual Oral is built on an extract from one of the two literary works studied rather than on a visual stimulus. That literary requirement is the single clearest reason HL quotes run above SL quotes in Dubai, because a tutor who has never taught a Spanish novel cannot prepare a student for that conversation.

Read the table as a spending guide. Half the grade sits in Paper 2, which is the component Dubai families least often buy help for, and a quarter sits in an oral that most students prepare for in the fortnight before it happens. If a budget only stretches to one component, the arithmetic says listening and reading, not conversation. Confirm every detail here against the current subject guide your school issues, and check component timings with the DP coordinator before you plan around them.

sections.heading: Costing two Diploma years rather than the next lesson
paragraphs: Families almost always price Spanish B by the hour and then spend across two years, which produces an unpleasant surprise somewhere around February of DP2. The sensible unit is the course, not the lesson. A typical pattern that works is light in DP1, heavy around the internal deadlines, and concentrated in the eight weeks before the May session, with the total hours front-loaded towards skills and back-loaded towards timing.

Set against Dubai school fees, the numbers look different again. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A frozen fee line and an unfrozen tutoring line is the trap: families who budget tuition annually alongside fees tend to overspend less than families who approve each block as it arises.

A worked plan helps. Thirty hours across DP1, spread as a fortnightly session with written work in between, builds the vocabulary and the writing habit at the lower end of the specialist band. Twenty-five hours across DP2, weighted towards the oral block and the listening clinic, handles the components that actually carry the grade. That is fifty-five hours over two years rather than ninety, and the saving comes from scoping rather than from negotiating the rate down. Where a family cannot fund that, the honest advice is fewer hours on the heaviest components rather than cheaper hours on everything.
bullets: Decide the two-year hour budget before the first lesson, then allocate it by component
Put the heavier spend in DP2, not DP1, unless the student is behind on vocabulary
Buy the Individual Oral as a block, not as a year of weekly conversation
Review the plan after the DP1 end-of-year report, when the real gaps are visible

sections.heading: Where Spanish B marks leak, and what each leak costs in hours
paragraphs: Marks in Spanish B do not leak evenly. The pattern across Dubai cohorts is consistent enough to predict: register, text type, tense control, and the second half of the Individual Oral. Register means the slip between formal and informal address inside one piece of writing, which reads to an examiner as a control problem rather than a slip. It is cheap to fix, usually two or three sessions with marked work in between, because the student almost always knows the forms and is simply not monitoring them.

Text type is dearer. Paper 1 offers a choice of task, and each option carries conventions: a blog is not a formal letter, and an article is not a speech. Students who have practised writing in Spanish without practising the conventions lose marks they never see, because the language is fine and the format is wrong. Clearing that reliably takes a term of fortnightly marked tasks, which is around eight to ten hours of tutor time including the marking.

Tense and mood control, particularly the subjunctive, is the long one. It cannot be fixed in a block before the exam, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling. The honest costing is a little work every week for two or three terms, embedded in writing the student is doing anyway, rather than a dedicated grammar course. The oral's second half is the opposite: a short, targeted intervention. Most students prepare the presentation and under-prepare the discussion that follows it, and three rehearsals with recordings usually moves that further than anything else per hour spent.
bullets: Register slips: two to three sessions with marked writing between them
Paper 1 text-type conventions: eight to ten hours across a term
Subjunctive and tense control: continuous low-level work, not a crash block
Individual Oral discussion: three recorded rehearsals, late in the course
Listening accuracy: a short clinic beats a year of incidental exposure

sections.heading: Who may legally take your money for private Spanish lessons in the UAE
paragraphs: This is a question Dubai parents ask less often than they should. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified against a government source and has been left out. If a provider quotes you a penalty figure as a scare tactic, that alone tells you something about the provider.

Two further points matter in practice. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct pointing the same way. Nobody should be marketing your child's own class teacher to you privately. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of any kind and does not describe itself as licensed, endorsed or in partnership with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board.

sections.heading: What a Spanish B tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Group 2 has fewer coursework pitfalls than a science subject with an Internal Assessment, but it has two real ones: the Individual Oral and, where a student chooses it, an Extended Essay written in Spanish. Both are assessed as the student's own work, and both attract offers from providers who should know better. The boundary is simple to state and worth stating plainly, because this part of the Dubai market contains people selling finished coursework.

A tutor may teach the language, explain the criteria, run practice against unseen stimuli, read a draft and say where it is weak, question the argument, point to a source the student has not considered, and model a text type with a different example. A tutor may not produce the finished piece, rewrite a paragraph into the student's draft, supply a script for the oral, or prepare answers to a stimulus the student will meet for the first time in the assessment room. The second list is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not the tutor.

There is one more boundary that is specific to languages. Nobody should be offering to supply recordings of the actual stimuli, extracts from an unreleased paper, or the school's chosen literary works in a reproduced form. Official subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB and are not ours to distribute; reference them, read them through the school, and link to ibo.org for the current documents rather than accepting a folder of files from a tutor.
bullets: Allowed: criteria explained, drafts read and questioned, practice against unseen stimuli
Allowed: a model text written by the tutor on a different topic entirely
Not allowed: a script for the Individual Oral, or a paragraph written into the student's draft
Not allowed: reproduced IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes passed around as files

process.title: Tell us the level, the component and the deadline
process.description: Spanish B SL or HL, which of the four components is weakest, the school's internal dates for the Individual Oral, and the week the family wants to start. Those four facts decide whether this is a weekly match, an oral block or a listening clinic, and they change the quote more than anything else you could send.

process.title: See the match and the rate before you commit
process.description: You get a named Group 2 teacher, their experience with Spanish B at that level, the slot they can hold on Gulf Standard Time, and the rate for that slot in AED. No block booking is required to see any of it, and nothing is charged while you decide.

process.title: Run the 30-minute trial lesson at no charge
process.description: One trial per family, no card details taken, and the student does a short diagnostic task rather than a sales conversation. You will have a written note afterwards saying which band descriptors the work currently misses, which is useful even if you go elsewhere.

process.title: Fix the slot and the marking rhythm
process.description: A standing weekly or fortnightly time, a written task due between sessions, and a session note the same evening. The rhythm matters more than the hour count in Spanish B, because the marked work between lessons is where the writing mark actually moves.

process.title: Re-scope at the DP1 report and again at mocks
process.description: Two review points, both tied to evidence the school produces rather than to a renewal date. Hours go up, down or get reallocated between components, and if the honest answer is fewer hours we say so. A match that is not working is replaced rather than defended.

whyPoints.title: The AED numbers are published, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Most pages in this market quote no price at all, and the ones that do quote dollars. The bands here are in AED, labelled by provider model, read in October 2026, and clearly separated from what IB Gram itself charges, which depends on level and scope. You can use them to judge any quote, including ours.

whyPoints.title: Group 2 specialists, not general Spanish speakers
whyPoints.description: Fluency is the entry requirement, not the qualification. A Spanish B tutor needs to know what a Paper 1 band descriptor rewards, how the Individual Oral discussion is marked, and what two literary works do to an HL course. That is a narrower pool, and online delivery is how a Dubai family reaches it.

whyPoints.title: Marked work, not just talk
whyPoints.description: A written task every fortnight, returned annotated against the criteria, with a running error log the parent can read. Half the Spanish B grade sits in a paper nobody can improve by conversation alone, and the marking record is what makes progress arguable rather than felt.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no regulator approval claimed, no promised grade, no finished coursework, and no statistic on this page without a date and a source. Where a fact could not be verified, such as an IB session date, this page says so and leaves it out.

whyPoints.title: Scoped to components, so hours are not wasted
whyPoints.description: An oral block, a listening clinic and a weekly writing rhythm cost less in total than twelve months of general tuition and move the grade further, because each hour is aimed at a component with a known weighting. Scoping is the only reliable way to cut the two-year cost without cutting quality.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the Dubai school week
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit after the school run and before the evening collapses, on Gulf Standard Time, with Ramadan timings moved to post-Iftar slots by agreement rather than cancelled. Scheduling is the quiet reason most tutoring arrangements fail in this city.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Spanish B home tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market bands read in October 2026 put a qualified language teacher working online at AED 150-300 an hour, an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180-500 with travel inside the rate, and an IB DP Group 2 subject specialist at AED 200-450 and above. Budget platforms start near AED 45 and buy conversation practice rather than criterion marking. None of these is an IB Gram price list; our figure depends on whether the request is Standard or Higher Level and whether it covers all four components or one. Ask any provider what comes back marked, and against which criteria, before comparing rates.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Spanish B tutor to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Spanish B teaching for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with the text being worked on shared on screen. The practical gain is the tutor pool: instead of choosing from Group 2 teachers who live within a short drive and are free on a weekday evening, you choose from the Spanish B specialists available at that hour in a compatible time zone. For Higher Level, where two literary works sit inside the oral, that difference usually decides whether the match is a specialist at all.

faqs.question: Is an in-home Spanish tutor in Dubai worth the extra AED per hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deciding factor is rarely the subject. An in-room adult helps with a young or reluctant learner, and helps when there is no quiet space for a laptop. For a sixteen-to-nineteen-year-old on a two-year Spanish B course, the premium mostly buys a car journey. The money spent on travel is money not spent on a Group 2 specialist, and in Dubai the specialist pool for Spanish B is small enough that proximity and expertise rarely coincide. If you do hire locally, ask directly whether the rate includes travel and what happens to the session when Sheikh Zayed Road is at a standstill.

faqs.question: How many Spanish B sessions a week should we budget for in DP1?
faqs.answer: One a fortnight is usually right in DP1 for a student who is coping, with a written task due in between so the tutor has something to mark. Weekly makes sense where there is a vocabulary debt carried over from MYP or from a two-lessons-a-week GCSE background. The pattern that works best across two years is light in DP1, heavier around the school's internal deadlines, and concentrated in the eight weeks before the May session. Buying a weekly slot from the first month of DP1 and keeping it all year is the most common way Dubai families overspend on this subject.

faqs.question: Do Spanish B Higher Level lessons cost more than Standard Level in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically AED 50-150 an hour more, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. Higher Level requires two literary works originally written in Spanish, and the Individual Oral is built on an extract from one of them rather than on a visual stimulus. A tutor who has taught conversational Spanish for years but never taught a Spanish novel cannot prepare a student for that discussion. The pool of people who can is small, and small pools price upwards. Before paying an HL premium, check with the DP coordinator that the level is actually settled, because changes between SL and HL are common in the first term.

faqs.question: Does Spanish B tuition in Dubai get more expensive closer to the May session?
faqs.answer: Not usually through a published surcharge, but effectively yes. A Group 2 specialist in September has gaps in the week; the same person in late January is holding slots for DP2 candidates across several Dubai schools. What a late booking loses is choice of tutor and choice of time, and the slot left over is often the one that collides with the school run. Families who fix a language slot in the first term are not getting a discount so much as avoiding scarcity. If you are booking late, be flexible on the hour and specific about the component you need.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Spanish B for one child and Spanish ab initio for another?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because both courses share the five prescribed themes and the same component structure, so a Group 2 teacher's preparation overlaps. What should not happen is merging the two children into one lesson: ab initio is a beginner course assessed on different expectations, and a shared hour shortchanges both. Ask whether preparation can be shared while the lessons stay separate, which is where any saving genuinely sits. Where the levels are further apart, such as Spanish B Higher Level alongside ab initio, two tutors is usually the honest answer even though it costs more.

faqs.question: Does a native Spanish speaker charge more than a trained Spanish B teacher?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and the premium does not reliably buy a better grade. Native fluency is the entry requirement for teaching Spanish B, not the qualification: the marks depend on knowing what a Paper 1 band descriptor rewards and how the Individual Oral discussion is assessed. A request for a native speaker also narrows the pool before quality has been discussed, and narrowing a pool pushes a price up. Ask about Group 2 teaching experience, marked work and familiarity with the current guide first. Accent exposure matters for the listening paper, and that is better served by varied audio than by the tutor's own passport.

faqs.question: Do private Spanish tutors in Dubai need a MoHRE work permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service on its app, website or e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no amount. Ask any tutor whether they hold the permit.

faqs.question: Is VAT included in Spanish B tuition quotes in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing, because quotes in this market are inconsistent about it. This page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that depends on the provider's own position and should come from the Federal Tax Authority rather than from a tutoring website. What a parent can insist on is clarity: whether the figure quoted is the figure payable, whether it is per 60-minute hour or per 45-minute lesson, and whether cancellations inside 24 hours are charged. Those three questions remove most of the unpleasant surprises in a tutoring invoice.

faqs.question: Can a Spanish B tutor help with the Individual Oral without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may explain how the oral is assessed, run rehearsals against unseen stimuli, record and replay the attempt, and coach the timing so the discussion is not squeezed by an over-long presentation. A tutor may not write a script, prepare answers to the actual stimulus, or rehearse the specific extract the school will use. The oral is assessed as the student's own performance, and a scripted one is academic malpractice with consequences that land on the student. Any provider offering prepared answers for a live assessment should be declined on that basis alone.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based Spanish B specialist is free at our time?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Group 2 supply in the Gulf time zone is genuinely thin for Spanish at Higher Level, and the options are a different hour with the right specialist, a compatible time zone outside the UAE, or a short wait for a slot to open. All three are offered openly with the rate attached, because an undisclosed substitution is how families end up paying a specialist rate for conversation practice. If none of the three works for your family, we will say that too.

faqs.question: Is there a trial lesson before we pay for Spanish B tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes: one 30-minute trial per family at no charge, with no card details taken and no block booking required. The student does a short diagnostic task rather than a sales call, usually a piece of writing or a timed listening set, and you receive a written note saying which band descriptors the work currently misses. That note is useful even if you decide not to continue, and you are welcome to take it to another provider. Trials are limited to one per family because they cost a tutor an unpaid half hour of preparation and marking.

faqs.question: How do we stop Spanish B tuition costs running away across two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Set the two-year hour budget before the first lesson and allocate it by component rather than by month. A workable shape is around thirty hours in DP1 as fortnightly sessions with marked writing between them, and twenty-five in DP2 weighted towards an Individual Oral block and a listening clinic. That is roughly fifty-five hours rather than ninety, and the saving comes from scoping rather than from negotiating the rate down. Review at the DP1 report and again after mocks, using the school's own evidence, and reallocate hours instead of adding them.

faqs.question: What should we send when asking for a Spanish B tuition quote in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Five things, and a quote that arrives without asking for them is a guess. The level, Standard or Higher. The school and the DP year. The most recent Spanish grade or report comment. The school's internal date for the Individual Oral. And the two or three weekly windows that survive the school run. With those, a provider can tell you whether you need a weekly slot, an oral block or a listening clinic, and price it honestly. Without them, you will be quoted a generic hourly rate for an unspecified amount of work.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-home-tutor.closingHeading: Price the job, then pick the tutor
dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-home-tutor.closingBody: Spanish B is a four-component course with half its marks in a paper most families never buy help for, and the hourly rate matters far less than whether the hour is aimed at the right component. The AED bands on this page are the Dubai market, read in October 2026, so you can judge any quote against them, including ours. Send the level, the school, the last report comment and the Individual Oral date, and you will get a named Group 2 teacher, a slot on Gulf Standard Time, a rate in AED, and a 30-minute trial lesson at no charge before anything is agreed. Lessons run online, one-to-one, with no home visits in the UAE.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Spanish B at Standard and Higher Level. Each marks written work against the published criteria before the lesson that discusses it, records oral practice so improvement can be heard, and keeps a per-criterion record across the term rather than a general impression.

intro.heading: A stuck Spanish B grade is four problems wearing one number
paragraphs: The grade that arrives on a Dubai school report is a single digit covering four different performances. Paper 1 is one piece of writing marked on three criteria. The listening half of Paper 2 is a separate skill from the reading half. The individual oral is a recorded conversation marked on four criteria of its own. A student can be strong in two of those and weak in two, and the report will show a 5 either way. Tutoring that starts from the 5 rather than from the components is guessing, and it is the reason so many families pay for a year of lessons and see the same number in June.

The useful first move is therefore to decompose the grade. That takes one session and some paperwork: the most recent marked Paper 1 with its criterion breakdown, the mock listening and reading scores separately rather than combined, and if the school will release it, a recording or at least the criterion marks from the last oral. Where the school does not provide that level of detail, which is common, a tutor can generate it directly in two sessions by setting a timed task and a recorded oral. Either way, within a fortnight the single number becomes four, and three of the four are usually fine.

Spanish B sits in Group 2 at Standard or Higher Level, framed by the five prescribed themes. Paper 1 is a single writing task worth a quarter, 250 to 400 words at Standard Level and 450 to 600 at Higher. Paper 2, listening followed by reading in one sitting, carries half. The individual oral carries the final quarter: at Standard Level from a visual stimulus linked to a theme, at Higher Level from an extract from one of two literary works studied in Spanish. Those weightings tell you where an hour of work is worth most, which is almost never where the student wants to spend it.

Spanish is the fastest-growing Group 2 choice in a lot of Dubai IB schools, and the cohorts are mixed in a way that complicates teaching. One class can contain a native speaker from a Latin American family, a student who has had Spanish since primary in an IB continuum school, and a student who started in Year 10. All three sit the same paper. The native speaker usually needs register and accuracy work rather than vocabulary; the late starter needs listening volume. Teaching that distinction well is difficult in a class of eighteen and straightforward one to one.

Delivering lessons over live video is what makes the right tutor available. Diploma Spanish B at Higher Level, with a particular pair of literary works chosen by a particular Dubai school, is a narrow requirement. The pool of people who meet it within a twenty-minute drive of one community is thin to the point of chance; online, it is a matter of matching. For a language subject the format itself costs almost nothing, and in two respects, shared annotation of scripts and recorded orals, it is better than a kitchen table.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Spanish runs through the IB continuum in different forms, and a student's Diploma placement usually reflects where they joined it. The notes below set out what each programme assesses and what students bring forward from it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Spanish B is a Group 2 language acquisition course at Standard or Higher Level, examined at the end of Year 13. Paper 1 writing carries 25 per cent, Paper 2 listening and reading carries 50 per cent, and the school-assessed, externally moderated individual oral carries 25 per cent. Higher Level adds two literary works read in Spanish and takes the oral stimulus from an extract of one of them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma classes in Spanish B are often the most mixed language groups in the school, since Spanish attracts both heritage speakers and students who began it recently. For a parent the consequence is that a class average means very little, and a comparison against the class is a poor substitute for a criterion breakdown of your own child's work.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Spanish is taught as language acquisition in phases, with four criteria covering comprehension of spoken and visual text, comprehension of written and visual text, communication in response to text, and use of language in spoken and written form. The exit phase is the most reliable indicator of whether Higher Level Spanish B is a realistic choice, more so than any single report grade.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai families move schools frequently, MYP Spanish records often arrive incomplete or in a different format, and the receiving school rebuilds a placement from a short internal assessment. Students who are strong orally and weak in writing are regularly placed high on that evidence and then struggle with Paper 1 two years later.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Spanish appears as an additional language within transdisciplinary units, with no external assessment and no formal grade. The signal worth watching is whether the child can read unfamiliar text and write connected sentences by Year 6, since oral confidence at that age routinely conceals a reading gap that appears in the MYP.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary pupils already carry mandatory Arabic under KHDA requirements whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, so Spanish in primary is a third language for many children. That is workable, and it does mean the written side of Spanish often receives very little homework time in those years.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: The subject of this page. The decomposition point holds here more than anywhere: students stuck on a 5 are usually losing marks in one or two of the four components while performing adequately in the others, and the report grade conceals which.

subjects.name: Spanish A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 route for students who use Spanish as a school or home academic language. It assesses literary and non-literary analysis rather than acquisition. Heritage speakers placed in Spanish B often belong here, and the misplacement shows as a comfortable 6 rather than as a problem.

subjects.name: Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: The beginners' course, restricted to students with little or no prior Spanish, with much shorter written tasks and a prescribed topic list. A student who studied Spanish through the MYP is normally ineligible, which disappoints a few families every year.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: Often taken alongside Spanish by language-focused Dubai students. The assessment model is identical, so criteria work transfers, but interference between two Romance languages is real and best managed by deliberate contrast rather than by hoping it settles.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Produces regular marked analytical writing, which makes it the easiest subject for a parent to monitor and the hardest for Spanish to compete with for attention. Its work on audience and purpose is directly applicable to the Spanish B conceptual criterion.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Relevant to this page for calendar reasons. The mathematics exploration deadline commonly lands in the same weeks as the school's Spanish B oral recording window, and one of the two has to be pulled forward in any workable plan.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Overlaps usefully with the sharing the planet theme, and its fieldwork and case-study habits give students content to argue from in the oral. Students with content and no structures stall mid-sentence, which costs interactive marks rather than language marks.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Extended writing under time with source work. The transferable element for Spanish B is paragraph architecture: a claim, support for it, and a return to the question. Spanish B scripts frequently supply content with no visible argument, which is a message-criterion loss.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: A popular Dubai option that competes directly for revision hours in Year 13 because of its volume of content. Students taking both should expect Spanish to be the subject quietly dropped from the week, which is the argument for a fixed term-long slot.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A Group 2 Extended Essay written in Spanish is demanding and distinctive. The tutor's role is research method, question narrowing, source discussion and feedback on the student's own drafts, with nothing supplied for submission.

sections.heading: Decomposing the grade before buying any lessons
paragraphs: A Spanish B report grade is a weighted average of four performances, and averages hide exactly the information a parent needs. The single most useful thing a Dubai family can do before booking tuition is to gather the components separately. Ask the subject teacher for the most recent Paper 1 script with its criterion marks rather than its total. Ask for the mock listening score and the mock reading score as two numbers. Ask what criterion marks the last oral attracted. Some Dubai schools provide all of this readily and some provide none of it, which is itself useful information.

Where the school will not break the grade down, a tutor can produce the same picture in two sessions. One timed Paper 1 task under proper conditions, marked by criterion, and one recorded oral with marks against the four oral criteria, gives a profile that is accurate enough to plan from. It will not match the eventual examination exactly, and it does not need to: what it needs to do is identify which one or two components are dragging the grade, because that decides where the next twenty hours go.

The reason this matters commercially as well as educationally is that the components move at very different speeds. Conceptual understanding on Paper 1 responds within weeks, because it is conventions and task response. Listening responds over months and cannot be hurried. The oral's interactive marks respond quickly, because the change required is behavioural rather than linguistic. Lexical range moves slowest of all. A family told which of those they are buying can make a sensible decision about timing; a family sold lessons against a 5 cannot.

sections.heading: Peninsular or Latin American Spanish, and whether it matters
paragraphs: Dubai families ask this more than any other question about Spanish B, usually because a tutor's nationality has come up. The practical answer is that the examination does not require one variety. Written tasks are assessed on language, message and conceptual understanding, and a consistently applied standard variety is acceptable whether it is peninsular or Latin American. What is penalised is inconsistency: a script that mixes voseo with peninsular second-person plural forms, or switches register between paragraphs, reads as uncontrolled rather than as regionally varied.

Listening is where variety genuinely bites. Paper 2 audio draws on speakers from across the Spanish-speaking world, and a student who has only ever heard one accent will lose marks on an unfamiliar one, not through lack of vocabulary but through failure to parse at speed. Caribbean and Río de la Plata speech in particular catches out students trained exclusively on Castilian classroom audio. The remedy is deliberate exposure: listening practice that rotates accents on purpose from early in Year 12, rather than concentrating on whichever variety the class teacher speaks.

For vocabulary the differences are real and mostly harmless at this level, provided the student knows which choices are regional. A tutor from Mexico and a tutor from Spain will both teach the course correctly; the useful thing is for the student to be told when a word is regionally marked rather than discovering it in an examination text. Where variety does matter is at Higher Level, where the two literary works are usually rooted in a particular tradition, and the vocabulary and reference they carry are worth learning as part of the text rather than as general Spanish.

sections.heading: What a grade change actually requires
paragraphs: Families reasonably want to know what is realistic, and the honest answer depends entirely on which component is weak and how long there is. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching. What can be described is the mechanism: what has to change for a particular profile to move, and roughly how long that kind of change has taken for students with that profile. The table below sets out the common Dubai profiles we see in Spanish B and what each one actually needs.

The pattern worth noticing is that the quickest gains are rarely linguistic. A student losing conceptual marks because every task comes out as an essay can fix that with a term of text-type work. A student giving four-word answers in the oral can learn to extend every answer by one sentence inside a month, and the interactive criterion responds immediately. A student whose listening sits well below their reading needs six months of weekly practice, and no amount of intensity in April substitutes for it. Those are different purchases with different timelines.

The slowest change is lexical and syntactic range, which is what most parents assume tuition is for. It moves through reading volume and through writing that is corrected consistently, and it takes a year rather than a term. A student with eighteen months is in a position to improve range. A student with ten weeks should be working on task response, text types, oral interaction and examination timing, which is where the recoverable marks are. Telling a family which situation they are in is more valuable than any lesson plan.

sections.heading: The Higher Level literary works and the oral built on them
paragraphs: Higher Level Spanish B requires two literary works read in Spanish, and the individual oral starts from an extract from one of them. Standard Level has no literature requirement and takes its oral stimulus from an image instead. This is the largest practical difference between the levels and it is the thing students most often fail to factor into the choice, because the Higher Level decision tends to be made on confidence in speaking, which the literature requirement does not test.

The works are chosen school by school and there is no standard pair across Dubai. That means a tutor cannot run meaningful oral preparation without knowing the titles, and it also means a student who moves schools mid-Diploma may face a different pair from the one they started. Families should send both titles at the point of enquiry. The commonest failure is predictable: the works are left until the recording window is announced, read quickly, and then the student is asked to discuss an unseen extract from a text they have skimmed.

Preparation that works treats each work as content. The student needs the shape of the text, its central preoccupations, a handful of passages they know well, and the vocabulary to discuss it without hunting. Practice extracts should come from across the whole of both books rather than from the obvious chapters, because the school's choice of extract is not predictable. And the general conversation phase, which follows the discussion of the extract, still ranges over the prescribed themes, so a candidate who has prepared only the literature runs out of material in the last third of their own oral.

sections.heading: Where Paper 2 marks go in Spanish B
paragraphs: Paper 2 carries half the grade, and it is the component students revise least because it is the hardest to practise alone. The listening section comes first and cannot be controlled: recordings play twice and then they are gone. Most lost marks there are not vocabulary losses. They are parsing losses, where the student recognises every word afterwards and could not process the sentence at speed, and they are note-taking losses, where the first hearing is spent listening passively and the second is spent regretting it.

The technique that changes this is unglamorous. Before the first hearing, read the questions and mark what kind of information each wants. During the first hearing, note only the specific items the questions ask for, in abbreviation, without trying to understand everything. Between hearings, identify what is missing. During the second, target the gaps. Taught explicitly and practised weekly, this lifts listening scores before any improvement in comprehension itself, which is why it is the first thing to teach when listening is the weak component.

The reading section is more tractable and responds to a different habit. The texts are authentic and the questions reward inference, reference and tone rather than word-matching, so the standard student error is to find the matching word and answer from it. Reading the whole text before answering feels slower and scores higher. Beyond technique, the only thing that moves reading substantially is volume: a student who reads Spanish journalism for fifteen minutes a day for a term meets the examination texts at a familiar register, and one who does not meets them cold.
bullets: Most listening losses are parsing and note-taking, not vocabulary

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why a tutor should know
paragraphs: UAE private schools are regulated at emirate level, and the regulator differs depending on where the school sits. In Dubai it is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

This is more than trivia for a family arranging tuition. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate regulator. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Families planning a two-year tuition budget alongside school fees are planning against a known rather than a moving number.

It also matters because of what a tutor must never claim. No private tutoring provider holds KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education or International Baccalaureate approval by virtue of teaching the curriculum, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds none of those and does not claim them. Separately, individuals providing private lessons in the UAE require a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what it does not require
paragraphs: Families planning on a UAE university place ask how a school certificate is recognised here. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process with documentary requirements that vary by curriculum, and it is worth understanding early because the requirements are about subject counts and grades rather than about anything a tutor supplies. For the British track, the Ministry's published requirements include five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

One detail in that rule is widely misreported in this market. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. At least one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and a parent who plans around it may push a child into an unnecessary extra examination. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For International Baccalaureate students specifically, no points threshold should be taken from a tutoring website, including this one. The sourced guidance covering the British and American tracks does not state an IB figure, so the only responsible instruction is to verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channels or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on it. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and no one should be sold lessons on the basis that a university place or an attestation depends on them.

sections.heading: Six weeks out: what is still worth doing
paragraphs: A good share of Dubai Spanish B enquiries arrive with between four and eight weeks until a paper, and the question behind them is whether it is too late. It is not too late, but what is achievable changes completely, and pretending otherwise wastes the time that remains. Lexical range will not move meaningfully in six weeks. Listening will improve a little. What will move, and move quickly, is everything to do with task response, conventions, interaction and timing.

The priority order at that range is specific. First, timing: a student who does not finish loses marks in every written component, and two timed tasks a week fixes it in a fortnight. Second, text types: three or four forms with checklists, which is the fastest conceptual gain available. Third, oral interaction, where extending every answer by one sentence is a behavioural change that the criteria reward immediately. Fourth, listening technique rather than listening ability, which means note-taking method, question reading and targeting the second hearing.

What should be left alone at six weeks is new vocabulary breadth, new grammatical structures, and anything that introduces risk into a script. A student attempting the subjunctive for the first time in May will get it wrong and lose marks they would have kept writing accurate simpler Spanish. The same applies to the oral: this is the point to consolidate what is reliable, not to add. A tutor who takes on a six-week booking and starts teaching new grammar has misunderstood the brief, and the result arrives in July.

process.title: Send the components, not the grade
process.description: Tell us the level, the Dubai school, the Higher Level literary works if applicable, and whatever the school has released: the last Paper 1 with criterion marks, the mock listening and reading as separate scores, the oral criterion marks. If the school releases none of it, say so and we will generate the profile ourselves in the first two sessions.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial that produces a profile
process.description: The trial costs nothing, lasts 45 minutes and takes no card details. It uses a timed writing task and a short recorded oral so the output is a four-component profile rather than an impression. You receive it in writing, including which component is weakest and what the realistic time frame for moving it is, whether or not you book.

process.title: Agree the target component and the measure
process.description: The plan names one or two components to work on and how progress will be evidenced: criterion scores on fortnightly tasks, logged listening results by question type, oral recordings kept in order. Agreeing the measure in advance is what stops a year of lessons ending in the same conversation about confidence.

process.title: Weekly sessions, scripts marked beforehand
process.description: Tasks are set between lessons and marked by criterion before the session that discusses them, with each comment naming its criterion. The error log carries across the course. Oral practice is recorded monthly and kept, so the first recording can be played against the latest rather than remembered.

process.title: Review at half term against the measure
process.description: At half term we look at the recorded numbers rather than at how the lessons felt. If the targeted criterion has moved, the plan continues; if it has not, something changes, which may mean a different approach or a different tutor. A rematch costs nothing and is better made early than endured for a term.

whyPoints.title: The grade is decomposed before anything is sold
whyPoints.description: Four components sit behind one number, and usually three of them are fine. The first fortnight identifies which one or two are dragging the grade, because that determines where the hours go. Buying lessons against a report-card digit is how families pay for a year and see the same number in June.

whyPoints.title: Progress is recorded, not described
whyPoints.description: Criterion scores on every marked task, listening results logged by question type, oral recordings kept in order so October plays against February. The measure is agreed before lessons begin. This is the difference between a tutor reporting that things are going well and a parent being able to check.

whyPoints.title: Honest time frames per component
whyPoints.description: Conceptual marks move in a term, oral interaction in a month, listening over six months and upwards, and lexical range over a year. A family told which of those they are buying can decide sensibly. Nobody here promises a grade, because no honest tutor can and the gate on this subject is the student's own work.

whyPoints.title: Accents rotated deliberately in listening work
whyPoints.description: Paper 2 draws speakers from across the Spanish-speaking world, and a student trained on one variety loses marks on an unfamiliar one through parsing rather than vocabulary. Practice rotates peninsular and Latin American speech on purpose from early in Year 12, and regional lexis is flagged as regional when it is taught.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level orals prepared on the school's own works
whyPoints.description: The two literary works are chosen school by school with no standard pair in Dubai, so preparation happens on the actual titles, with practice extracts drawn from across both books. The general conversation phase is rehearsed separately, since candidates who prepare only the literature stall in the final third.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: On an Extended Essay in Spanish, or any submitted component, the tutor teaches method, questions the argument and gives feedback on drafts the student has written, and supplies no text for submission. IB malpractice consequences fall on the student, which makes that boundary a protection rather than an inconvenience.

faqs.question: My child has been on a 5 in Spanish B for a year. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: By breaking the 5 into its parts. The grade covers four separately assessed performances: Paper 1 writing with three criteria, listening, reading, and an individual oral with four criteria of its own. Students stuck on a mid-band grade are usually losing marks in one or two of those while performing adequately in the rest. Ask the school for the criterion marks rather than the totals, and for listening and reading as separate mock scores. Where the school will not release that, two sessions with a timed task and a recorded oral produce the same profile.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether our Spanish tutor is from Spain or Latin America?
faqs.answer: Not for the examination, which does not require a particular variety. What is assessed is consistency: a script mixing voseo with peninsular plural forms reads as uncontrolled rather than as regionally varied. Where variety does matter is listening, because Paper 2 uses speakers from across the Spanish-speaking world and a student trained on one accent loses marks on an unfamiliar one. The practical requirement is that regional vocabulary is flagged as regional when it is taught, and that listening practice rotates accents deliberately from early in Year 12.

faqs.question: How much can a Spanish B grade realistically move in a term?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which component is weak. Conceptual understanding on Paper 1, which is text type and register, responds within a term. Oral interactive marks can move in four to six weeks, because the change needed is behavioural. Listening takes six months and upwards and cannot be hurried. Lexical and syntactic range takes about a year, through reading volume and consistent correction. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching, but the mechanism and the rough timeline can be described honestly.

faqs.question: What do the two literary works at Spanish B Higher Level involve?
faqs.answer: Two works read in Spanish across the course, with the individual oral starting from an extract from one of them. Standard Level has no literature requirement and uses a visual stimulus instead. Schools in Dubai choose their own pair and there is no standard selection, so a tutor needs the titles before any oral preparation is possible. The usual failure is leaving the reading until the recording window is announced: a student who has skimmed both books cannot place an unseen extract, and that costs message and interactive marks together.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in reading and badly in listening?
faqs.answer: Because they are different skills and the listening section cannot be controlled. Recordings play twice and then they are gone, so parsing speed and note-taking decide the score more than vocabulary does. Most students afterwards recognise every word they missed, which proves the problem was processing rather than knowledge. The fix is technique first: read the questions and mark what kind of information each wants, note only the required items on the first hearing, identify gaps between hearings, and target them on the second.

faqs.question: Should a heritage Spanish speaker be in Spanish B or Spanish A?
faqs.answer: Worth raising with the Diploma coordinator rather than with the Spanish department, because it is a timetable and eligibility decision as well as a language one. Spanish A is the Group 1 language and literature route and assesses literary and non-literary analysis rather than acquisition. A heritage speaker in Spanish B will often reach a comfortable 6 without being stretched, which uses a Group 2 slot another language could have filled. Most Dubai schools set a change deadline early in Year 12, after which a switch means restarting a two-year course.

faqs.question: What should we do with six weeks until the Spanish B papers?
faqs.answer: Work on what moves quickly. Timing first, because unfinished tasks cost marks everywhere, and two timed pieces a week fixes it in a fortnight. Then three or four text types with checklists, which is the fastest conceptual gain available. Then oral interaction, where extending every answer by one sentence is rewarded immediately. Then listening technique rather than listening ability. What to avoid is new vocabulary breadth and new grammar: a first attempt at the subjunctive in May loses marks that accurate simpler Spanish would have kept.

faqs.question: How do we see whether Spanish B tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Agree the measure before the lessons start. Criterion scores on every marked task rather than totals, listening results logged by question type, and oral recordings kept in order so the earliest can be played against the latest. Then review at half term against those records rather than against how the sessions felt. A flat total can conceal a rising language mark and a falling conceptual mark, which is exactly the information a per-criterion record shows and a report grade hides.

faqs.question: Can oral practice be recorded and reviewed in an online lesson?
faqs.answer: It is one of the clearest advantages of the format. Practice runs under the same conditions the school will use, the recording is kept, and the student can hear themselves rather than being told how they sounded. Comparing October with February is the only reliable way to judge whether spoken range has grown or the student has simply relaxed with a familiar tutor. Recordings also let a specific habit be targeted, such as the four-word answer, which is far easier to change once a student has heard it.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees our school, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees, so school calendars can differ. It affects tutoring mainly through honesty: no tutoring provider holds regulator approval by teaching a curriculum, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK rules bar school staff from tutoring their own enrolled students.

faqs.question: Does my child need a permit-holding tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE require a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: How does the Ministry of Education treat an IB Diploma for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The sourced public guidance covers the British and American tracks and does not state an International Baccalaureate points threshold, so no figure should be taken from a tutoring website. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channels or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on it. For the British track the requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both Spanish B and French B to the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. The Group 2 assessment model is identical, so criteria work, text-type teaching and oral technique transfer directly, and a tutor who teaches both can manage interference between the two Romance languages deliberately rather than leaving the student to resolve it. The constraint is genuine Diploma-level competence in both, which is less common than it sounds. Where it does not exist we match two specialists, because a tutor stretched across a language they half-know produces confident wrong corrections.

faqs.question: Is a free trial really free, and what does it include?
faqs.answer: Yes. One trial lesson, 45 minutes, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. It includes a timed writing task and a short recorded oral, because the purpose is to produce a four-component profile rather than to have a pleasant conversation. You receive that profile in writing, naming the weakest component and the realistic time frame for moving it. One trial per student, and if we think a different Group 2 course or a different subject is the real issue, the note will say so.

faqs.question: What if the component that needs work is not one you can fix quickly?
faqs.answer: We say so at the profile stage rather than after a term. If listening is the weak component and the examination is ten weeks away, the honest plan targets technique, timing and the oral while treating listening as a slow secondary gain. If range is the issue and there are eighteen months, range is worth working on. Where the realistic answer is that the available time cannot deliver what a family is hoping for, that belongs in the first written note, not in a June conversation.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-online-tutor.closingHeading: Send the criterion marks and we will tell you what is movable
dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-online-tutor.closingBody: A report grade is four performances averaged into one digit, and the useful work starts once it is pulled apart. Send the level, the Dubai school, the two literary works if your child is at Higher Level, and whatever detail the school has released: criterion marks, separate listening and reading scores, the last oral. The free 45-minute trial adds a timed task and a recorded oral, and you get a written profile naming the weakest component and the realistic time frame for moving it. No card details are taken, and if the honest answer is that the time available will not do what you are hoping for, the note will say that.
