dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB DP Spanish B at Standard and Higher Level. They mark written tasks against the published criteria, run listening practice across more than one variety of Spanish, and at HL work through the two literary works your child's school has actually chosen.

intro.heading: Why two Spanish B students in the same Dubai school get quoted different amounts
paragraphs: Two students at the same Dubai IB school, both taking Spanish B, both with a B grade in MYP, can be quoted monthly figures that differ by AED 900. Nothing about the tutor explains it. One takes Standard Level and one takes Higher Level, and Higher Level is a materially bigger piece of teaching: two works of literature to study and discuss, a Paper 1 task of 450 to 600 words against 250 to 400 at SL, a longer listening paper, and an individual oral built from a literary extract rather than from a photograph. Every one of those costs hours.

Start with the market. In Dubai, a qualified language teacher working online one-to-one is quoted around AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and an IB-experienced language acquisition specialist AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 45 to AED 150. A premium tier quotes AED 500 to AED 650. Those bands come from published provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026, and they are the market rather than an IB Gram price list.

Within those bands, what you are actually buying varies more than the hourly number suggests. A conversation hour, a grammar-repair hour, a Paper 1 text-type hour, an oral rehearsal and an HL literature seminar are five different pieces of work, and only two of them can be done well by a fluent Spanish speaker who has never seen the assessment criteria. Dubai has plenty of fluent Spanish speakers. It has far fewer teachers who can tell you that a task lost marks on the conceptual understanding criterion because the register was wrong for the stated audience.

Geography is the one cost that online delivery removes completely. An in-home visit in this city runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour because forty to ninety minutes of driving sits inside the fee, and the tutor you can reach is whoever is willing to make that drive. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Spanish B for Dubai families is taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the match is made on Spanish B experience rather than on postcode.

What follows is the SL and HL comparison in full, a price breakdown by type of hour rather than by tutor, the literature cost at Higher Level, the two components where Dubai students lose most marks, a term-by-term spending plan, and the questions worth asking before you pay anybody. Every figure is attributed, because a number without a source is no help to a family deciding between one session a week and two.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-tutor.programmesIntro: Spanish B is a two-year course with a long run-up. The notes below describe where each programme hands a student over to the next, because the handover point is what decides whether DP1 is maintenance or rescue.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Spanish B sits in Group 2 and runs at both levels. Students work across five prescribed themes, write one extended task under timed conditions, sit separate listening and reading papers, and complete an internally conducted individual oral. Higher Level adds two literary works, which also become the basis of the HL oral.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools often run a single combined SL and HL Spanish B class because cohort sizes do not justify splitting them. The HL students in that room get less literature time than the course assumes, and that gap is the most common reason a Dubai family looks for an IB DP Spanish B tutor in the first place.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Spanish runs in phases. A student finishing Year 11 in Phase 3 or 4 has the grammar base Spanish B HL assumes; a student finishing in Phase 2 has the vocabulary but not the range, and will meet the Paper 1 word count as a wall rather than a target.
programmes.countryNote: Because families move between Dubai schools mid-MYP, phases do not always transfer cleanly: one school's Phase 3 is another's Phase 2. A diagnostic in the first weeks of DP1 is worth more than the transcript, and it is the cheapest way to decide between SL and HL before the choice hardens.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students meet Spanish through the language development core requirement rather than as an examined Group 2 subject. The work is portfolio-based: evidence of language development recorded over time, with no Paper 1 and no individual oral to prepare.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools offer the CP, so families often reach the language development requirement with no clear sense of what counts as evidence. Support here is short, structured and much cheaper than a two-year Diploma language engagement, and it ends when the portfolio is credible.

programmes.name: The Year 11 summer
programmes.description: The ten weeks between MYP and DP1 are the cheapest hours in the whole course. A short block covering past tenses, the subjunctive in its most common triggers, and reading at length closes most of the gap between Phase 2 and what HL expects from week one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families travel heavily over the summer, so this block usually runs across time zones. Online delivery is what makes it possible at all, and six sessions in August routinely save a term of remedial work in a market where term-time specialist hours cost more.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: Spanish B is rarely the only thing on the list. The grid below covers the language acquisition courses we teach, written around where each one actually leaks marks rather than as a catalogue.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Marks leak in two places: Paper 1 register, where a student writes good Spanish in the wrong voice for the stated audience, and the listening paper, where training on one variety of Spanish leaves a student stranded on another. HL adds literature, where the risk is summarising the work instead of discussing it.

subjects.name: Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: For genuine beginners, SL only, with two short written tasks instead of one long one and no literature. A student who should be in ab initio but sits in Spanish B will meet the Paper 1 word count as an impossible target rather than a stretch, and no amount of vocabulary work fixes that in one year.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The same assessment architecture as Spanish B, a harder listening paper for most learners because of liaison and elision, and a smaller teaching pool in Dubai. Families taking both languages usually need the two sets of sessions sequenced across the week rather than stacked on the same evening.

subjects.name: German B
subjects.description: Written accuracy is the pressure point: case endings and verb-final word order in subordinate clauses produce errors that read as carelessness but are structural. Diagnosing which case a student is guessing at is more useful than another round of vocabulary lists.

subjects.name: Italian B
subjects.description: Thin availability in Dubai and often taught in a combined SL and HL group of a handful of students. Families here typically want literature support at HL specifically, because that is the part a small combined class cannot cover properly.

subjects.name: Mandarin B
subjects.description: Character load means reading speed, not grammar, is the usual constraint on the reading paper. Students who can speak comfortably still run out of time on Paper 2, and the fix is timed reading volume rather than more conversation.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Doubly relevant in Dubai, where KHDA requires Arabic in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. A student taking Arabic B in the Diploma is often also carrying the school's mandatory Arabic stream, and the two have different expectations.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Not a Group 2 subject, but it competes directly with Spanish B for the same DP2 weeks because both carry an internally assessed oral. Families booking support for both should fix the order of the two oral windows before booking either.

subjects.name: Spanish B HL literature support
subjects.description: A distinct piece of work rather than more Spanish: close reading of the two works the school chose, discussion vocabulary, and the ability to speak about a short extract for three to four minutes without reciting plot. This is where the HL premium in a quote actually goes.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment living, short school runs, and parents working nearby. Early evening slots hold well here and sibling pairing is common, because two children often share one desk and one quiet hour between six and eight.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Fast-growing and heavily school-served, which means long activity schedules. Spanish sessions here are most often placed on a weekend morning, and weekend mornings with a language specialist are the first slots to disappear in the DP2 spring.

sections.heading: Standard Level or Higher Level: the decision that sets your bill
paragraphs: Spanish B HL costs more to tutor than Spanish B SL, consistently and for reasons that have nothing to do with tutor greed. HL requires two literary works that SL does not. Its Paper 1 task is 450 to 600 words against 250 to 400. Its listening paper is longer. Its individual oral starts from a literary extract instead of a photograph, which means the student must be able to talk about a text rather than describe an image.

The table sets the two levels side by side with the final column showing what each difference does to tutoring hours, because that is the column families actually need. Read it before DP1 subject choices lock rather than after. A student who takes HL for university reasons and then discovers the literature requirement in March of DP2 is buying the most expensive hours in this market at the worst possible moment.

There is a university dimension that cuts the other way. Some degree routes ask for a language at Higher Level, and a Spanish B HL grade does work that an SL grade cannot. If that applies to your child, the extra hours are not optional spending; they are part of the cost of the application. What is worth avoiding is taking HL on reputation alone, with no admissions requirement behind it, and then paying for literature support to defend a grade nobody asked for.

Confirm the current word ranges, paper durations and literature requirements with your child's IB coordinator. The IB revises its subject guides, and what matters is the document your child's teacher is working from this year, not a figure on a tutoring page.

sections.heading: What Spanish B hours cost in Dubai, by the kind of hour
paragraphs: An hourly rate tells you almost nothing on its own, because a Spanish B engagement is five different jobs. Conversation practice is the cheapest to supply and the easiest to find in a city with a large Spanish-speaking population. Criterion-referenced marking of a Paper 1 task is the scarcest, and HL literature discussion is scarcer again. The table below prices by job rather than by tutor, using the same market bands read in October 2026.

The practical consequence is that a family can buy a cheaper blend rather than a cheaper tutor. Pay specialist rates for the two or three hours a month that genuinely need a specialist, and fill the remaining practice with lower-cost conversation or self-marked listening sprints. That blend lands most Dubai families in the AED 600 to AED 1,200 monthly band that Bestimate's 2026 estimates give for mid-market weekly tutoring, while still getting expert marking where it counts.

The opposite mistake is common and expensive: paying specialist rates for conversation. A student who has six hours a month of pleasant Spanish conversation with a native speaker and no marked written work will arrive at Paper 1 fluent and unprepared, having spent AED 1,500 to find out. Conversation matters, but it is not the component that is failing.

Monthly packages deserve the same scrutiny. Online packages advertised near AED 799 a month for eight sessions work out around AED 100 an hour, which only holds if the sessions are full hours and written work is marked outside them. In-home monthly packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions sit nearer AED 200 an hour with travel absorbed. Ask what is inside the number before comparing it with anything.

sections.heading: The two literary works: the Higher Level cost nobody quotes
paragraphs: Higher Level Spanish B requires the study of two literary works, and the HL individual oral is built on an extract from one of them. That single sentence in the subject guide is responsible for most of the gap between an SL and an HL tutoring bill, and it is almost never mentioned when a family asks for a quote.

The work it generates is real. A student has to read two full works in Spanish, which for many Dubai HL candidates is the first extended reading they have done in the language. They then need a vocabulary for talking about a text rather than about their life: what a character does, what the writer does, how a passage sits in the whole. Then they need to speak about a short extract for three to four minutes without reciting plot, and answer questions about the work and about broader themes afterwards.

Schools choose their own works, so generic support is close to useless here. A tutor working from a different novel than the one your child's class read is teaching a different course. The first question to ask a prospective Spanish B HL tutor is which two works the school has chosen and whether the tutor has read them; if the answer is vague, the HL premium in their rate is not buying what you think.

Sequencing matters as much as cost. The literature block cannot be bolted on in the final month, because the reading has to happen before the discussion can. Dubai families who book literature support in the DP1 summer or in the first term of DP2 pay the ordinary rate and get a choice of tutors. Those who book in the spring are buying in the same scarce window as every oral candidate in the city.

sections.heading: Paper 1: good Spanish in the wrong voice still loses marks
paragraphs: Paper 1 asks for one written task chosen from three options, each specifying a text type, an audience and a purpose. Students lose marks there less for grammar than for voice. A blog entry written as a school essay, a formal letter written in the register of a message to a friend, a speech with no audience address: all of those produce accurate Spanish that answers a question nobody asked.

The task is marked on three criteria in the current guide: language, message and conceptual understanding, carrying twelve, twelve and six marks respectively. Check the exact allocations against your child's subject guide, because the point of knowing them is not trivia. It is that a third of the available marks sit outside grammar and vocabulary, in whether the student understood the audience, context and purpose they were given. That is teachable in a way that fluency is not.

A productive session looks like this. The student writes to a real task brief under timed conditions. The tutor marks it against the three criteria, annotates it, and names one pattern rather than thirty errors. The next task targets that pattern. Three cycles of that will move a student further than ten conversation hours, because each cycle produces evidence of what is actually wrong.

The text-type inventory itself is worth building early. Blog, email, article, brochure, speech, interview, diary, report, set of instructions: each carries conventions a marker expects to see. A student who has written each one once in DP1, with feedback, walks into Paper 1 recognising the format rather than inventing it on the day.

sections.heading: Paper 2 listening: the component that punishes a single accent
paragraphs: Listening and reading together carry half of Spanish B, and listening is where Dubai students most often underperform relative to their classroom confidence. The reason is narrow exposure. Classroom Spanish is spoken slowly and deliberately by one teacher with one accent, while the recordings draw on the range of varieties in which Spanish is actually spoken. A student trained exclusively on peninsular audio stalls on a River Plate speaker, and vice versa.

The fix is volume and variety rather than cleverness, and it is cheap. Short daily exposure to Spanish from different regions, with the transcript checked afterwards, builds processing speed in weeks. What does not work is a long weekly listening session: the skill being trained is real-time comprehension, and it responds to frequency the way fitness does, not to intensity.

Reading has a different failure mode. Students scan for a word they recognise and build an answer around it, which produces confident wrong answers. Timed reading with a required justification for each answer breaks the habit: if the student has to point to the clause that supports the answer, guessing stops being comfortable. Both halves of Paper 2 benefit from an error log kept across sessions, because the pattern is usually two or three recurring traps rather than general weakness.

There is a Dubai-specific advantage here that families underuse. The city has Spanish speakers from many countries, and a student who hears Spanish from more than one region socially is already doing part of the work. Pointing that out is often more useful than selling more hours, and a tutor who says so is worth keeping.

sections.heading: A term-by-term spending plan to the May session
paragraphs: The cost of Spanish B across two years depends far more on shape than on rate. A flat one session a week from September of DP1, rising to two in the DP2 spring, with a separate literature block at HL, costs less in total and produces more than any compressed alternative. The table maps each phase onto an indicative monthly band using Bestimate's 2026 Dubai monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring, scaled by session count.

DP1 is about building something assessable: tense range, reading volume, the text-type inventory, and at HL the first of the two works. It runs at mid-market rates because nothing here is scarce. The DP1 summer is for retention, not teaching, and at HL it is the natural window for the second literary work, because reading can happen in a hotel room in a way that grammar instruction cannot.

DP2 is where the bill rises, and the rise is concentrated in the spring. Two sessions a week from January, one on papers and one on the oral, plus the HL literature block if it has not already run. Mock season pulls every subject into the same evenings, so book Spanish slots before the mock timetable is published rather than after. The oral rehearsal window is the most contested four weeks of the Dubai language year.

One pattern is worth refusing. Families sometimes plan to spend nothing in DP1 and buy an intensive course in DP2. That inverts every cost in the table: more hours, at the scarcity rate, taught by whoever is left, to a student who still has to build a year of vocabulary while sitting mocks. The same total spend placed earlier does more.

sections.heading: Five questions to ask before you pay a Spanish tutor in Dubai, and what we will not do
paragraphs: Ask which level the tutor has taught, not which level they can teach. Ask which two literary works your child's school chose and whether the tutor has read them. Ask whether written-task marking happens inside the hour or outside it, because that single answer can change the effective rate by a third. Ask whether the quoted AED figure includes VAT, and get it in writing. And ask about the private tuition work permit, which MoHRE issues free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, so there is no fee for anybody to have saved by skipping it.

Then ask what the tutor will not do. A Spanish B tutor can set tasks, mark them against the published criteria, annotate the student's own writing, record oral rehearsals, and supply model answers clearly labelled as the tutor's own work for study. A tutor cannot write or rewrite anything your child submits as their own, cannot draft an Extended Essay or TOK essay, and has no business near a recorded individual oral. IB academic honesty rules place the consequence on the student, so a provider who offers help with submitted work is handing your family the risk and keeping the fee.

Be equally wary of the numbers. No tutor can promise a grade in Spanish B, and a provider quoting a success percentage should be asked for the sample size, the dates and the method on the same page as the claim. Self-published star ratings in this market have been found contradicting themselves within a single page. What can be promised is specific: a number of marked tasks, a number of recorded rehearsals, and a written note of where the marks are going.

Our own position, stated plainly: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge endorsement, runs no premises in the UAE, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the Emirates. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the first lesson is free with one per student and no card details taken, and the rate is agreed in writing before the second.

faqs.question: How much more does Spanish B HL tutoring cost than SL in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Expect a similar hourly rate and roughly a third more hours across the two years. The hourly figure moves little, because the same teachers cover both levels, but HL generates work SL does not: two literary works to read and discuss, a Paper 1 task of 450 to 600 words rather than 250 to 400, a longer listening paper, and an oral built from a literary extract. In monthly terms, a Dubai family running one weekly session at mid-market rates sits in the AED 600 to AED 1,200 band for SL, and adds a six to ten session literature block at HL.

faqs.question: Which two literary works will my child need for Spanish B HL?
faqs.answer: Whichever two the school chose, and that is the point. The IB requires the study of two literary works at Higher Level and leaves the selection to the school, so there is no universal list. Ask your child's teacher for the titles in the first term of DP1 and give them to any prospective tutor before agreeing a rate. A tutor who has read the school's chosen works can teach the HL oral; one working from a different novel is teaching a different course at the same price.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on Paper 1 when the Spanish is accurate?
faqs.answer: Because accuracy is only one of the three criteria. In the current guide the task is marked on language, message and conceptual understanding, carrying twelve, twelve and six marks, so roughly a third of the total sits in whether the student wrote the right text type for the stated audience and purpose. A blog written as an essay, or a formal letter in the register of a message to a friend, loses on message and conceptual understanding while the Spanish itself scores well. Confirm the allocations against your child's subject guide, then practise the text types one at a time.

faqs.question: Is conversation practice with a native Spanish speaker worth paying for?
faqs.answer: Worth paying a little for, and not worth paying specialist rates for. Conversation builds fluency and confidence, and in Dubai it is widely available from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour at market rates. What it does not produce is evidence: no marked task, no criterion feedback, no record of what is actually costing marks. Families who buy six conversation hours a month and no marking arrive at Paper 1 fluent and unprepared. The useful blend pays specialist rates for two or three hours of marking and criterion work, and keeps conversation cheap.

faqs.question: How do I stop my child failing the Spanish B listening paper?
faqs.answer: Widen the exposure and shorten the sessions. Listening and reading together carry half the grade, and classroom Spanish is spoken more slowly and in one accent, while the recordings use the range of varieties in which Spanish is actually spoken. Short daily listening from different regions, with the transcript checked afterwards, builds processing speed in weeks. A single long weekly listening session does not, because the skill is real-time comprehension and it responds to frequency rather than intensity. Keep an error log so the two or three recurring traps become visible.

faqs.question: Should my child take Spanish B HL if no university course asks for it?
faqs.answer: Probably not. A Higher Level language is required by some language-related degree routes, and where that applies the extra hours are part of the cost of the application rather than optional spending. Where no course asks for it, HL buys prestige and generates a literature requirement, a longer Paper 1 and a harder oral, all of which have to be defended for two years. Students who take HL on reputation alone and discover the literature requirement in the spring of DP2 end up buying the most expensive hours in this market at the worst moment.

faqs.question: Can a student move from Spanish B HL to SL partway through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It is a school decision rather than a tutoring one, and timing decides whether it is sensible. A move in the first term of DP1 costs a few weeks of adjustment and usually nothing else. A move in DP2 means abandoning literature work already done and re-pitching the oral from an extract to a photograph, which is survivable but wasteful. Ask the school early if the level looks wrong, and ask a tutor for an honest diagnostic rather than a recommendation to buy more hours at the level your child is struggling with.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Spanish B actually need in DP2?
faqs.answer: Two from January to the May session suits most students: one on papers, one on the oral. Before that, one a week through DP1 and the first term of DP2 is enough if it is genuinely weekly. At Higher Level, add a block of six to ten literature sessions, ideally run in the DP1 summer or the first term of DP2 rather than in the spring. Compressing the whole engagement into the final term inverts the cost, because you buy more hours at the scarcity rate from whoever is still free.

faqs.question: Do Spanish tutors in Dubai charge extra for exam-term bookings?
faqs.answer: Yes, and languages more than most subjects, because internally conducted orals are recorded in narrow school windows that cluster across the emirate. Late bookings into that window are commonly quoted AED 20 to AED 60 an hour above the ordinary rate, and the best-matched specialists are often simply unavailable rather than more expensive. Mock season produces a smaller second spike. Booking oral rehearsal in the autumn gets the ordinary rate and a choice of tutors; booking in March gets the scarcity rate and whoever is left.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Spanish B and Spanish ab initio for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: Ab initio is for genuine beginners, runs at Standard Level only, sets two short written tasks instead of one long one, and carries no literature at any level. Spanish B assumes three or more years of prior Spanish and is available at SL and HL. The placement matters financially: a student who belongs in ab initio but sits in Spanish B meets the Paper 1 word count as an impossible target, and a year of vocabulary work will not close that gap. A diagnostic hour covering speech, reading aloud and a short written piece settles the question.

faqs.question: Is a ninety-minute Spanish session better value than two shorter ones?
faqs.answer: For grammar and written work, usually yes. A language session carries fixed overheads, because settling in and warming up into Spanish take the same ten to fifteen minutes regardless of length, so a ninety-minute block spends more of your money on teaching and is typically priced AED 10 to AED 40 an hour below the hourly rate. The exception is listening and reading practice, where two or three short sprints a week beat one long block, because processing speed responds to frequency. Many Dubai families run one long teaching session plus self-managed sprints.

faqs.question: Can my child get Spanish B support during Dubai school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the DP1 summer is the single most useful holiday block in the course, particularly at Higher Level where it is the natural window for reading the second literary work. Online delivery means sessions follow a family that travels, and lessons can be rescheduled around a time-zone shift rather than cancelled. During Ramadan, sessions commonly move to post-Iftar slots or to late mornings at weekends. Holiday retention work is cheap; losing ten weeks of Spanish and re-teaching it in September is not.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Spanish tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Spanish B for Dubai families is taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The market alternative is priced on this page for comparison, at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with forty to ninety minutes of driving inside the fee. The practical gain from teaching online is which tutor you can reach: for HL literature on a specific pair of works, that pool is far larger than the set of tutors willing to drive to your community.

faqs.question: What should a monthly Spanish B progress note contain?
faqs.answer: Artefacts rather than adjectives. Which tasks were set and marked, what the criteria said about each, which single error pattern was targeted, whether it moved, and what the next three weeks will cover. At Higher Level it should also say how much of each literary work has been read and whether the student can yet speak about an extract for three to four minutes. What it should not contain is a predicted grade, because predictions are the school's responsibility, or a percentage improvement figure with no sample size or method behind it.

dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-tutor.closingHeading: Fix the level question first, then the budget
dubai/ib-dp-spanish-b-tutor.closingBody: Almost every Spanish B cost question in Dubai turns out to be a level question wearing a price tag. Standard Level and Higher Level are different amounts of teaching, and the two literary works at HL are the part most quotes quietly leave out. Book the free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, and the tutor will run a diagnostic on tense range, register and reading speed and tell you plainly which level the evidence supports. You will get the blend of hours in writing, a rate to check against the market bands above, and an honest answer about the HL literature block. No tutor can promise a grade, and we will not pretend otherwise.

intro.heading: The price question, answered before the sales pitch
paragraphs: Three of the six strongest competitor pages in this search cluster publish no price at all. One of them has a frequently asked question that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. Of the two that do quote, both quote in US dollars, which is not the currency any Dubai family hands a tutor. That is the state of the market a parent walks into, and it is the reason this page leads with money rather than with adjectives about dedication.

Here is the shape of it. Published rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, run from roughly AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor working online to AED 650 an hour for a premium named practitioner, with qualified subject tutors online clustering between AED 150 and AED 300 and in-home visits between AED 180 and AED 500 because the drive is inside the rate. Sports, Exercise and Health Science sits towards the upper part of whichever band you choose, for one unglamorous reason: it is a small-entry Diploma subject and the number of teachers who have taken it to examination is limited.

What this page then does, which nobody else in the cluster does, is explain what moves the number in Dubai specifically. Session hour matters here more than almost anywhere, because a swimmer training at Hamdan Sports Complex before school and a footballer at an academy in Dubai Sports City after it have almost no free hours in common with a tutor's easiest slots. Format matters, because an in-home visit crossing Al Khail Road at seventeen hundred is paid for by someone. Scarcity matters. Proximity to the May session matters. And whether marking is included matters most of all, because two rates that look identical can be very different products.

On delivery, the position is stated before any figure is discussed. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, with screen-shared past papers and a document the student writes in. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and keeps no UAE office; home visits are available only in India. That is a limit worth knowing before a payment, not after one. It is also why the rate conversation can stay honest: no hour of a tutor's evening is being spent on Sheikh Zayed Road and then billed to you as teaching.

The rest of this page prices a term properly — the hourly bands, a cost-in-context table against Dubai school fees, the extras that quietly change the total, what a legally permitted tutor costs given that the MoHRE permit itself is free, and what happens to the price when no specialist is available at the hour you need. Where a figure belongs to another provider, their name and the month the figure was read are printed next to it.

programmes.description: Every group 4 student produces an internally assessed scientific investigation and takes part in a collaborative sciences project of around ten hours that is not separately graded. subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The widest supply of any group 4 subject in Dubai, so the easiest rate to negotiate. subjects.description: Forces, moments, momentum and projectile motion are the biomechanics content under a different name. Students taking both find biomechanics straightforward; students without physics are the ones who need extra hours on it, which changes a budget.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Overlaps the sports psychology and motor learning material, including arousal, anxiety, goal setting and skill acquisition. Moderate supply in Dubai and moderate rates, and useful to students who find the behavioural half of SEHS easier than the physiological half.

subjects.description: A frequent Diploma pairing for students heading towards sports management or sports marketing. Wide supply, mid-band rates. Shares no content with SEHS, so it is budgeted entirely separately.

subjects.description: Chosen alongside SEHS by students interested in health, population and urban environments. Easy to source in Dubai at mid-band rates, and the fieldwork discipline transfers directly to the scientific investigation.

subjects.name: Scientific investigation support
subjects.description: Bought as a short block rather than a term. Question narrowing, method feasibility, data processing technique and criteria-based feedback on the student's own drafts. Predictable cost because the number of sessions is fixed in advance.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Usually the last thing families buy and often the best value per hour, because a few sessions on argument structure improve essay writing across every subject including the SEHS extended responses.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family is actually paying for, hour by hour
paragraphs: An hour of tutoring is not one product. At the bottom of the market an hour is teaching time only: somebody explains content, the student listens, nothing is set and nothing is marked. At the top of the market an hour is teaching, a task written for that student, the marking of that task against published criteria, and a record of what changed. Both get described as an hourly rate, and the gap between them explains most of the confusion in this market. A rate of AED 150 with no marking and a rate of AED 280 with marking are not two prices for the same thing.

The second thing a family pays for is scarcity, and Sports, Exercise and Health Science is the clearest example of it in the Diploma. It is a small-entry subject. A Dubai family can find biology tutors easily, chemistry tutors easily, and may find nobody at all who has taught SEHS to examination within a reasonable drive. That shortage does not disappear when the delivery moves online, but it shrinks dramatically, because the pool stops being defined by distance from your villa and starts being defined by who is free at a given hour in Gulf Standard Time.

The third thing is travel, and it is paid whether or not it appears on an invoice. Published in-home rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online, and the difference is substantially the drive. A tutor crossing from Mirdif to Dubai Hills at seventeen hundred spends an unpaid hour in traffic and recovers it inside the rate. Nobody is being dishonest about that; it is simply what in-home tutoring costs anywhere with this much congestion.

IB Gram's own answer on price is a quote after a free trial lesson rather than a published rate card, because level, subject scarcity and session length all move it. What is fixed is the inclusion: the session and the marking of the task that follows it are one fee. Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE, so no part of the fee is paying for a car.

sections.heading: The five things that move the number in Dubai
paragraphs: Rate variation in this emirate is not random, and a parent who knows the five drivers can read a quote accurately in about a minute. Level comes first. Diploma work costs more than IGCSE and IGCSE costs more than middle-school support, because the teaching requires subject depth that fewer people have. Within the Diploma, Higher Level firms the rate again, and a small-entry subject firms it a third time. SEHS at Higher Level is therefore close to the top of whatever band a provider operates in, and a quote that looks surprisingly low for it is usually a generalist.

Session hour comes second, and in this subject it dominates. A competitive swimmer training at Hamdan Sports Complex before school and a footballer training in Dubai Sports City afterwards have perhaps two usable evening hours a week. Those are the hours every other family wants too. Early-morning slots before training are easier to get and, online, cost no more; for an in-home tutor a six-thirty start on the other side of the city is a different proposition entirely.

Format, proximity to the exam and inclusion of marking are the remaining three. In-home carries travel. Rates firm in the weeks before the May session as specialist availability tightens. And marking either is or is not inside the fee. The table below sets each driver against its effect and, more usefully, against what a family can actually do about it, because two of the five are entirely within a parent's control.

One driver that does not exist, despite what some pages imply, is the cost of being legally permitted to teach. The MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 is granted free of charge for two years. A tutor cannot justify a higher rate by pointing at permit costs, because there are none. What they can and should do is confirm that they hold one.

sections.heading: Published Dubai rates by level and format
paragraphs: The table below is assembled from other providers' own published figures, read in October 2026, and it is presented as the market rather than as an IB Gram price list. It is laid out by level and format because that is how a family actually shops: a parent is not choosing between brands so much as choosing between an online specialist, an in-home visit and a small group, at a level that is already fixed by their child's year group.

Read it with two cautions. First, the lower bands are usually teaching-only; marked written work is rare below the specialist band, and for a Diploma science that is a significant omission. Second, a single published figure is a starting point rather than a transacted price. Providers quote from a number and then adjust for session length, package size and the hour you want. The ranges here are wide because the market genuinely is wide, not because anybody is being evasive.

For SEHS specifically, expect quotes in the specialist rows rather than the general ones. A provider quoting AED 150 an hour for Higher Level SEHS is either employing somebody whose subject is really biology, or is not including marking, or has not understood the request. Neither is necessarily disqualifying — a strong biology teacher can handle much of the physiology content — but it should be a conscious choice rather than a surprise in week three.

The monthly columns matter more than the hourly ones for budgeting. Published monthly packages in this market sit around AED 799 for roughly eight online sessions and between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context against Dubai school fees
paragraphs: A tutoring rate read on its own tends to look either trivial or outrageous. Read against what a Dubai family already spends on education, it looks like what it is: a marginal addition to a much larger annual number, which is why the right question is not whether it is cheap but whether this particular spend will change anything. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That freeze is the backdrop against which a tutoring decision is now made.

The market itself is large and still growing. Dubai had 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and IB programmes at 7. The 2026-27 intake adds seven more private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment grew by 6 per cent. More IB places means more small Diploma cohorts, which means more families discovering that their child is one of very few taking SEHS.

The table below prices a term and a two-year plan rather than an hour, because that is the decision actually being made. The school-fee row is deliberately left as a band rather than a figure, since fees vary enormously by school and KHDA publishes them school by school; look up the specific school rather than trusting any average. Every tutoring row uses the published market bands from the previous table.

The honest conclusion from the arithmetic is that a bounded, targeted purchase — an investigation block, or eight weeks of twice-weekly work before papers — is a small fraction of an annual fee and has a clear end date. An open-ended weekly commitment across two Diploma years is a different order of spend and deserves a harder test: specifically, whether the marked work is improving. That test is free to apply and most families never apply it.

sections.heading: The extras that change what you actually pay
paragraphs: Hourly rates are compared; totals are paid. The difference between the two is a short list of inclusions and conditions that almost never appear in a headline figure, and a parent who asks about them before booking avoids nearly every unpleasant surprise in this market. The first is marking. If a session is sixty minutes of talking and nothing is set, written or returned, the work of diagnosis has not been bought at all, and a Diploma science is the worst possible subject in which to skip it.

The second is the trial. A free trial is a reasonable offer and a common one, but free with a condition attached is only honest when the condition is stated on the same screen — how long it runs, whether card details are required, whether it commits you to anything. The third is cancellation and rescheduling: a tutor whose rate is ten per cent lower but who charges for any session moved inside twenty-four hours is more expensive for a family whose child competes at weekends, which in this subject is most of them.

The fourth is the replacement policy. If the match is wrong in week two, does a different tutor cost anything, and does the clock start again? The fifth is the exam-term premium: some providers reprice in the spring. The sixth is VAT, where the only responsible answer is to ask whether a quoted figure includes it and to get that in writing; the tax treatment of tuition in the UAE is not something a tutoring page should assert without a Federal Tax Authority citation.

The last item is not a charge but a cost: data. Lead forms collect personal information about a minor, and under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection a family is entitled to know what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted. A provider asking for a child's school, grades and photograph without saying why is taking something from you that is not priced on any rate card.

sections.heading: Why SEHS tutors are scarce, and what the subject actually demands
paragraphs: Scarcity is the main reason this subject prices differently from biology, so it is worth understanding what the subject asks of a teacher. SEHS is a group 4 science. Its content spans exercise physiology and nutrition of the body systems, biomechanics, and sports psychology and motor learning, with additional depth at Higher Level, and it is examined through written papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation. Students also complete a collaborative sciences project of around ten hours, which is not separately graded. Confirm the current structure and weightings with the school's Diploma coordinator, because the guides are revised and the coordinator holds the internal deadlines.

The teaching demand is unusual. A SEHS teacher needs the physiology of a biologist, enough mechanics to handle moments and projectile motion properly, and enough psychology to teach arousal, anxiety and skill acquisition without reducing them to common sense. Very few teacher-training routes produce that combination, which is why schools often staff it from physical education or from biology, and why private tutors with real examination experience in it are rare. That is the whole of the scarcity story, and it is why the rate sits where it does.

For students, the pattern of lost marks is specific. The physiology is usually known and poorly applied: a question gives an unfamiliar sporting scenario and asks the student to explain a physiological response within it, and the answer that comes back is a textbook recital with no scenario in it. Biomechanics loses marks quantitatively, because students who are not taking physics treat force and moment questions as vocabulary rather than calculation. And the psychology section loses marks to vagueness, because named theories and models get replaced by general observations about confidence.

The scientific investigation has its own failure pattern, which is a question that cannot produce usable data. A student wants to investigate whether training improves performance, over a timescale and with a sample that cannot possibly show it. Two sessions spent interrogating the question and the method before any data is collected is the highest-value money in this subject, and it is cheap because the block is bounded. Any support on the investigation is teaching and feedback only; the work submitted must be the student's own throughout.

sections.heading: Heat, training load and when a Dubai session can actually happen
paragraphs: Scheduling is a cost driver in this subject in a way it simply is not in others, because the student's week is set by facilities and coaches rather than by the family. Outdoor training in Dubai moves to the edges of the day for much of the year, and in the hottest months it moves indoors or into the evening entirely. A swimmer may be in the pool before six in the morning. A footballer at an academy may finish at nine at night. Neither of those students is available in the comfortable late-afternoon window that most tutoring is sold in.

That is also, usefully, syllabus content. Thermoregulation, hydration, heat acclimatisation and the physiological limits of exercise in high ambient temperature are on the course, and a student in this city is living the case study. The Dubai Fitness Challenge each autumn produces an entire month of city-wide activity data and participation to think about. Students who connect their own training logs to the physiology they are being taught remember it; students who meet it only as a diagram in a revision guide do not.

For pricing, the practical consequence is simple. Online delivery makes an early-morning or late-evening slot cost exactly the same as a mid-afternoon one, because nobody is driving anywhere. An in-home tutor asked to arrive at six-thirty in the morning in Mirdif, or at nine at night in Dubai Hills, will either decline or load the rate, and both responses are rational. The awkward hours are precisely where the AED gap between formats is widest.

A second consequence is continuity. Competition seasons, training camps and family travel interrupt everything, and a plan that cannot absorb interruption gets abandoned and then restarted, which is the most expensive way to buy tutoring. Sessions that pause and resume with the same tutor, and that shift to post-Iftar slots through Ramadan rather than stopping for a month, cost less over two Diploma years than any discount on an hourly rate will save.

sections.heading: Availability, fallbacks and what each costs
paragraphs: No competitor page in this research set discloses a coverage limit, which is a strange thing to conceal, because every provider has one. For a small-entry subject the limit is real and it is worth publishing. The number of teachers who have taken Sports, Exercise and Health Science to examination and are available in Gulf Standard Time is finite, and at some hours in the exam term there will be nobody free. A family should know that before paying, not during week one.

When it happens, there are three honest options and they have different prices. Waiting for a specialist costs nothing except time, and if the wait is two weeks in October it is usually the right call. Taking a different weekly slot that is covered costs nothing at all and solves most cases. Starting with a closely related specialist — a biology teacher for the physiology, a physics teacher for the biomechanics — covers a large share of the content at that subject's own rate, which is generally lower, and is a reasonable interim rather than a substitute.

What should never happen is a generalist being presented as a subject specialist at a specialist rate. That is the single most common complaint about tutoring agencies anywhere, and it is undetectable for about a month, by which point a term's fees are gone. The protection is simple and free: ask what the tutor's own subject is, ask whether they have taught this specific course to examination, and look at the first marked piece of work critically.

The table sets out what each fallback actually involves. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, so the in-home column exists only to be honest about it: that service is available in India and nowhere in the UAE. If physical presence is a requirement, the in-home rate band earlier on this page is the right place to start shopping, and an emirate-based agency is the right provider.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the cost of using somebody legitimate
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a surprising number of pages in this market either ignore that or imply the rules are optional. They are not. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit is free, it cannot be a cost driver, and any rate justified by reference to licensing costs is being justified by something that does not exist. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you, and a page that confidently prints one is repeating a rumour. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way — so nobody should be offering you your child's own teacher privately.

Schools themselves are regulated by emirate. Dubai's private schools sit with KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, Sharjah with SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. An operation running premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or IB accreditation of any kind.

One more cost that is not on a rate card: the mandatory UAE subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and calculating instructional time in forty-minute units. Those hours occupy the same week as SEHS, which is part of why Diploma students run short of time and why families end up buying support in the first place.

process.title: Say the subject, the level and the hour you need
process.description: SEHS at SL or HL, the school, and the two or three weekly hours that survive the training schedule. The hour is the hardest constraint in this subject, so naming it first prevents a quote for a slot that was never going to work.

process.title: Get the rate before the trial, not after
process.description: A quote based on level, subject and session length, given up front, with marking stated as included. If a provider will not quote before a sales call, that is information. Published market bands on this page give you the range any honest quote should sit inside.

process.title: Use the free trial as a teaching session
process.description: A full session at no cost and with no card details required. Written work gets set and marked inside it, which is the only reliable test of whether the tutor can actually assess this subject. A wrong match at this stage costs nothing to change.

process.title: Bound the purchase
process.description: Agree a block with a number of sessions and an end date — an investigation block, an eight-week exam sprint, or a term. Bounded blocks are easier to budget, easier to evaluate, and far easier to stop than an open-ended weekly arrangement.

process.title: Check the marked work in week four
process.description: Read two marked tasks side by side. If the same errors are being flagged with no movement, change the plan or the tutor rather than the number of hours. Buying more of something that is not working is the commonest way families overspend.

process.title: Reprice at the exam term deliberately
process.description: Demand for specialists tightens before May. Agreeing the exam-term block in advance holds the rate and the slot, and avoids discovering in March that the only availability left is at an hour your child trains.

whyPoints.title: Every number on this page has a source
whyPoints.description: AED figures are other providers' published rates with the month they were read. Regulatory statements are attributed to u.ae, KHDA or MoHRE. No invented satisfaction percentages, no self-awarded ratings, no grade promises, and no IB exam dates restated from secondary sources.

whyPoints.title: Marking is inside the fee
whyPoints.description: A session and the marking of the task that follows it are one charge, not two. That is the single biggest hidden variable in this market, and pricing it in makes an IB Gram rate directly comparable to a cheaper rate that excludes it.

whyPoints.title: Awkward hours cost no more
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a six-thirty start before swim training and a nine o'clock session after academy football are priced identically to a mid-afternoon slot. For a student whose week is set by a coach, that is worth more than a discount.

whyPoints.title: A specialist shortlist instead of a map
whyPoints.description: SEHS is small-entry. Removing distance from the selection means the constraint becomes availability in Gulf Standard Time rather than driving distance from your community, which in this subject changes who is available at all.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free at the hour you want, you are told, with an honest estimate and the realistic alternatives at their own rates. No competitor page in this research set publishes a coverage limit; concealing one only delays the problem.

whyPoints.title: The delivery model stated before payment
whyPoints.description: One-to-one, live video, Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE and holds no UAE office; home visits exist only in India. If a person in the room is the requirement, the in-home bands above show what that market charges.

faqs.question: What should I expect to pay per hour for Higher Level SEHS help in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 put IB specialist teaching between AED 200 and AED 450 or more per hour online, with in-home visits from AED 180 to AED 500 because travel sits inside the rate. Higher Level work in a small-entry subject sits towards the upper part of either band. A quote well below AED 200 usually means either a generalist or an hourly rate with no marking attached. Those are other providers' figures, not an IB Gram price list; a quote here follows a free trial lesson and depends on level and session length.

faqs.question: Why does SEHS cost more than biology tutoring at the same level?
faqs.answer: Supply. Biology is taught in every school and tutored by a large pool in Dubai, so rates are competitive. SEHS is small-entry and needs a teacher who can handle physiology, enough mechanics for biomechanics calculations, and named psychological models. Few training routes produce that combination, and fewer tutors have taken the course to examination. Scarcity firms the rate in every band. The practical response is to buy online, which widens the pool from whoever drives to your community to whoever is free in Gulf Standard Time, and that usually does more for price than negotiating.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package cheaper than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: Usually a little, and the published numbers show the shape. Market monthly packages sit around AED 799 for roughly eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which works out below the equivalent single-session rates. The catch is commitment: a package is only cheaper if every session gets used, and in a subject where competitions and training camps interrupt constantly, unused sessions are pure loss. Ask what happens to a missed session before buying a package, and whether unused hours roll forward or expire at the end of the month.

faqs.question: Does the price change in the weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: Specialist availability tightens every spring and rates firm with it, which is a market reality rather than a tactic. The way around it is to agree the exam-term block before the term starts, which holds both the rate and the slot. Leaving it until March in a small-entry subject often means the only availability left is at an hour that clashes with training. For what it is worth, six to eight weeks of marked timed practice can genuinely move a grade, so a late start is still worth making; it is just more expensive and more constrained.

faqs.question: Can we pay for just the scientific investigation rather than a whole term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many families it is the best value on the list. An investigation block is four to six sessions, priced per session at the level band, with the total known before the first one. The sessions narrow the research question, test whether the method can produce data that supports any conclusion, teach the statistical handling, and read drafts against the published criteria as questions in the margin. The work stays entirely the student's own. Time it to the school's internal deadlines, which the Diploma coordinator holds and which differ between Dubai schools.

faqs.question: How early in the morning can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Early enough to sit before a pool session, which for competitive swimmers in Dubai can mean finishing by six. Because delivery is online and timed to Gulf Standard Time, an early slot costs no more than an afternoon one and no tutor is driving across the city in the dark to reach it. The limit is the student rather than the schedule: a sixty-minute physiology session at five-thirty in the morning is only useful if the student is actually awake. Many families settle on one early slot and one post-training evening slot across the week.

faqs.question: Do cheaper tutors skip marking, and does it matter in a science?
faqs.answer: Below the specialist band, marked written work is frequently not included, and in a group 4 science it matters considerably. The commonest reason a SEHS student underperforms is not missing knowledge but failure to apply physiology to the unfamiliar scenario the question describes, and that failure is invisible in conversation and obvious in a marked script. An hour of explanation with nothing written, set or returned does not diagnose anything. Ask directly whether the session fee covers a task written for your child and the marking of it, because two rates that look alike often are not.

faqs.question: Are small group classes better value for a Diploma science?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes; per outcome, it depends on what is wrong. A group works for a confident student who needs pace, structure and the discipline of a fixed weekly commitment. It cannot find the four recurring errors in one student's writing, because nobody is marking one student's writing. For SEHS specifically, group teaching also struggles with the quantitative biomechanics, where students diverge sharply depending on whether they also take physics. A bounded one-to-one block often costs less in total than a term of group classes that did not address the actual problem.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's MoHRE permit add anything to the price?
faqs.answer: No, because the permit is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. So any rate justified by licensing costs is being justified by a cost that does not exist. What the permit does affect is legitimacy: individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask for confirmation that a tutor holds one, and check mohre.gov.ae for the current requirements rather than any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a premium rate of AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: One Dubai provider publishes that figure for premium named practitioners, and for a narrow purpose it can make sense: a small number of hours on a specific, diagnosed problem close to an exam. As a weekly commitment across two Diploma years it is a very large number, and the published evidence that it outperforms a competent specialist at half the rate does not exist. The more reliable value test is whether marked work improves week to week, which costs nothing to check. Beware of any provider using examiner status to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

faqs.question: What does an in-home tutor in Dubai charge, and what am I paying for?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates run from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home at AED 180 to AED 350, with independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. The difference is largely travel: a tutor crossing Dubai in peak traffic recovers that unpaid hour inside the rate, which is reasonable rather than sharp practice. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. If physical presence is a requirement, an emirate-based agency is the right provider for it.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a SEHS student usually need before papers?
faqs.answer: Families typically buy eight to ten sessions in the final weeks, run as a marking cycle rather than as revision lectures: the student sits a timed section between sessions, the tutor marks it, and the session addresses the three or four errors the marking exposes. That is enough to fix command-term discipline, scenario application and biomechanics calculation, which is where most of the recoverable marks sit. It is not enough to cover a syllabus from a standing start, and no honest provider will tell you otherwise. Coverage gaps need a term, not a sprint.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan without extra charge?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dubai schools run shortened hours through Ramadan, training shifts and late afternoon stops working for many households, so sessions move to post-Iftar evening slots at the same rate. Because lessons are online and timed to Gulf Standard Time, a schedule change is a calendar matter and nobody is driving anywhere at an awkward hour. Families can also drop to a lighter cadence for the month and resume with the same tutor. The expensive option is stopping without a plan, since restarting after a month's silence in DP2 costs more than the sessions saved.

faqs.question: How do I make two SEHS tutoring quotes genuinely comparable?
faqs.answer: Four things, and the same four to each of them: the subject and level written exactly as the school does, the two or three weekly hours that actually work around training, one piece of recent marked work, and the deadline you are working towards. Then ask each provider the same three questions — is marking included, what is the rescheduling window, and what happens if the match is wrong. Quotes become comparable immediately, and the providers who dodge the questions identify themselves. Expect any serious quote to sit inside the published bands on this page.

dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.closingHeading: Get the number, then get the trial
dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.closingBody: If price is the question holding up a decision, the published bands on this page should let you judge any Dubai quote in about a minute: AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online, AED 200 to AED 450 or more for an IB specialist, AED 180 to AED 500 in-home with travel inside the rate. For SEHS, expect the specialist end, because the subject is small-entry. Then ask the three questions that decide the real total — is marking included, what is the rescheduling window, what happens if the match is wrong — and book the free trial lesson. Sessions are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and if no specialist is free at the hour you need, you will be told before any payment.

Availability is checked before a match is offered, because a SEHS specialist is not a tutor you can assume is free in any given fortnight.

intro.heading: What a SEHS hour costs in Dubai, and why it is not priced like a maths hour
paragraphs: Sports, Exercise and Health Science is a Group 4 science, and in Dubai it is taught in far fewer classrooms than Biology or Chemistry. That one fact sets the price. A parent ringing round for a maths tutor is shopping in a crowded market. A parent looking for someone who has actually marked a SEHS scientific investigation is shopping in a thin one. Published market bands for IB subject tutors in Dubai run from roughly AED 150 an hour at the qualified-generalist end to AED 450 and above for genuine subject specialists, and one Dubai provider advertises AED 650 for examiner-level review.

Those AED per hour figures belong to other providers, were published on their own sites, and were collected in October 2026. Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 an hour online. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED advertises AED 650. EdFlik and Tutopiya sit far lower, from AED 45 to 65 and from AED 33 to 52 respectively, which in practice buys general study supervision rather than criterion-level SEHS feedback. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page: the trial lesson is free with no card required, and a quote follows the level, the component and the deadline.

Four things move the number for this subject specifically. Higher Level carries extension content that sits inside both papers, so an HL student needs a tutor who has taught that material rather than one who has read it. A DP2 student in the final two terms is competing for the same specialist hours as every other DP2 student in the emirate. A scientific investigation already collected on the wrong protocol costs more to rescue than one planned properly in DP1. And a mid-year move from SL to HL, which Dubai schools do allow in some cases, creates a catch-up block that nobody budgeted for.

What the money buys is narrower and more useful than general science help. The investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria, and the marks are lost in predictable places: a research question about 'fitness' with no measurable variable, means reported with no measure of spread, a conclusion that restates the data instead of interpreting it, and an evaluation whose only improvement is 'more participants'. On the papers, the losses are command-term losses. A question that says outline does not want the same answer as one that says explain, and data-based questions reward reading a graph rather than remembering a fact.

Delivery is the one thing on this page that is not negotiable. Tuition for Dubai families runs online, one to one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; those are a service we provide only in India. For a subject with this few specialists, that is the advantage rather than the compromise: your child works with someone who has marked SEHS investigations, instead of whoever teaches science within a twenty-minute drive of your community.
