dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.programmesIntro: SEHS only exists at Diploma level, but the route into it starts earlier. These are the stages a Dubai student passes through, and what each one leaves them holding when the Diploma begins.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
programmes.description: A Group 4 experimental science built on exercise physiology and nutrition, biomechanics, and sport psychology and motor learning. Students sit two written papers and complete one independent scientific investigation of around 3,000 words, marked out of 24 against four criteria. Higher Level adds extension content assessed inside the same papers rather than in a separate one, which is why an HL student who was taught by an SL-only teacher often arrives with a visible gap.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, SEHS is offered by a minority of the emirate's IB World Schools, so cohorts are small and a single teacher often carries both levels. That has a direct effect on tutoring: the school may have no second specialist to ask, and an online specialist becomes the only route to a second opinion on an investigation draft.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme: Sciences and Physical and Health Education
programmes.description: MYP Sciences builds the criterion-based habits that the Diploma investigation then tests under pressure: formulating a question, designing a method, processing and presenting data, and evaluating what went wrong. MYP Physical and Health Education supplies the vocabulary of training, performance and health that SEHS later makes quantitative. Students who did well in MYP Sciences criterion B and C usually find the investigation manageable; those who coasted on practical write-ups do not.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts are large and the step to DP1 is where SEHS candidates feel it, because MYP rarely demands uncertainty handling or statistical treatment. A short block in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 is the cheapest SEHS support a Dubai family will ever buy, and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physical Education and Biology as feeders
programmes.description: Most Dubai students arriving in a DP SEHS classroom come from a British-track Year 11 rather than from MYP. IGCSE Physical Education covers anatomy, training principles and components of fitness in descriptive terms; IGCSE Biology covers the systems that SEHS then quantifies. Neither prepares a student for uncertainty, repeatability or a research question with named variables, which is the gap a first tutoring block usually closes.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, and KHDA's own market figures put the UK curriculum at 37% of private-school students. That means the typical Dubai SEHS candidate is an IGCSE student making a one-year jump into criterion-based science, with no MYP grounding to fall back on.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme: sport, health and wellbeing pathways
programmes.description: A small number of UAE schools run the IB Career-related Programme, where a student takes DP courses alongside a career-related study. SEHS appears in sport, fitness and health pathways, and CP students sit the same SEHS papers and complete the same investigation as DP candidates. What differs is the surrounding workload and the reflective project, which competes for the same autumn weeks as the investigation.
programmes.countryNote: CP is rare in Dubai compared with the full Diploma, so a CP student looking for SEHS help is in an even thinner market than a DP one. Scheduling matters more than price here, because the reflective project and the investigation tend to collide in the same term.

dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.subjectsIntro: SEHS is rarely tutored alone. These are the subjects Dubai SEHS students most often pair it with, and what each one actually assesses, so you can decide where a limited budget does the most work.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Two written papers plus one scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade. Marks are lost on command terms, on data-based questions answered from memory, and on investigations whose research question cannot be answered by the data collected. HL extension content sits inside both papers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject most SEHS students sit alongside, and the one most medical and biomedical courses actually specify. Shares the same investigation model and the same four criteria, so one tutor can often carry both. Losses cluster in genetics, physiology detail and extended-response structure.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Frequently required with Biology for medicine and dentistry. Carries the heaviest calculation load in Group 4 and the same 20% investigation. A SEHS student taking Chemistry usually needs separate support, because the skill overlap is smaller than families expect.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Overlaps SEHS on motivation, arousal and skill acquisition, and shares a research-methods vocabulary. Assessed through papers plus an experimental study, so a student already handling a SEHS investigation has transferable habits around hypotheses, variables and ethics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content here is what makes a SEHS investigation defensible: correlation, regression, significance and spread. Students who are weak in AI statistics usually produce weak data-analysis marks in SEHS, so a short AI block often raises two grades at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Dubai schools recommend for engineering and economics destinations. Heavier on algebraic technique and proof than on statistics, so an AA student needs the statistical treatment for a SEHS investigation taught separately rather than assumed.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares the biomechanics ground with SEHS: force, moments, projectile motion and energy. A student taking both can have the mechanics taught once properly and applied twice, which is one of the few genuine efficiencies available in a Group 4 timetable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The extended responses in SEHS Paper 2 are marked on argument, not on prose style, but students who cannot structure a paragraph lose marks in both subjects for the same reason. Support here tends to show up in science grades within a term.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A common pairing for students heading towards sports management rather than sports science. Shares the command-term discipline that SEHS Paper 2 rewards, and the internally assessed work falls in the same autumn window, so the calendar needs planning jointly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: A SEHS-based Extended Essay is popular and risky: the best ones narrow to one measurable question, the worst read as a literature review of training methods. A tutor can question the scope and the sources and give feedback on the student's own drafts, nothing further.

regions.note: Academy training and school fixtures are in the same postcode, so a student can finish a session at the pitch and be online twenty minutes later. Evening slots after 19:30 GST are the ones that survive the training calendar here.

regions.note: Villa communities with long school runs towards Meydan and Al Quoz. Sessions that start before 17:00 GST tend to be missed in term time; a single later weekly slot holds better than two early ones.

regions.note: Dense apartment communities with large Indian and Arab cohorts and a strong maths and science culture. SEHS is often the second science rather than the first, and families here ask about the Biology pairing more than anywhere else.

regions.note: Younger families, longer commutes to Dubai's IB schools, and a lot of DP1 students. Early DP1 support is cheaper and more effective here than crisis help in DP2, which is the pattern the rate table on this page is meant to make visible.

regions.note: Far enough out that an in-home tutor's travel fee is a real part of the price, which is one reason online delivery costs less here in practice than the published in-home band suggests.

regions.note: Villa communities with a strong school-sport culture and several academy swimmers and footballers. Training clashes are the main cause of cancelled sessions, so slots are held on a fixed weekday rather than moved weekly.

regions.note: Walking distance to several IB and British-track schools, so school-run time is short and 16:30 GST slots actually hold. Useful for students who need two shorter sessions a week during an investigation block.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB World Schools where SEHS candidates are concentrated
schoolClusters.note: Not every IB World School in Dubai offers SEHS, and the ones that do often run a single mixed SL and HL class. Students we support attend schools across this group; the list is ecosystem context for a parent working out whether their school has a second specialist to ask.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools running the Diploma alongside a British track
schoolClusters.note: These schools run IGCSE to 16 and then offer the Diploma, A Level or both. A SEHS candidate here has usually come through IGCSE Physical Education or Biology rather than MYP Sciences, which changes what the first tutoring block has to cover.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools with strong sport programmes feeding SEHS interest
schoolClusters.note: Academy and performance pathways push students towards SEHS as a subject choice. The academic consequence is a crowded week, and the practical consequence is that session timing decides whether tutoring works at all.

dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.modesIntro: Three ways Dubai SEHS families actually buy support, each with a different price consequence. The hourly band is the same; the number of hours is what differs, and that is where the real cost sits.

The student collects every data point and writes every word; the tutor questions, marks and explains.

The table below prices the work the way a Dubai family actually buys it: a single diagnostic hour, a weekly slot across a year, a block around the investigation, a paper clinic in the final term. The AED per hour bands are other providers' published figures, collected in October 2026, and the source is named in the last column.

Read the indicative totals rather than the hourly rate. A weekly hour across DP1 at the middle of the specialist band costs more in total than a six-hour investigation block at the top of it, and it buys considerably more. Families who compare only the hourly figure routinely choose the expensive option, because the cheap-looking rate is attached to the stage where the most hours are needed. Nobody ranking for this query publishes totals at all, which is why the comparison is hard to make anywhere else.

One honest caveat about the monthly package row. Advertised Dubai packages at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions work out at roughly AED 100 a session, which is well below the specialist band. That price buys supervision from a generalist, and for a Group 4 subject with a 24-mark investigation that is not the same product. sections.heading: What moves the number in this emirate, driver by driver
paragraphs: Dubai has specific cost drivers that a global rate table misses. Specialist scarcity is the first: SEHS is offered in a minority of the emirate's IB World Schools, so the pool of people who have marked an investigation against the current criteria is small, and small pools price upwards. Deadline proximity is the second, and it is sharper here than in a larger market, because every DP2 cohort in the emirate hits its internal upload deadlines inside the same few weeks.

The third driver is level. Higher Level extension content is assessed inside the same two papers rather than in a separate one, so an HL student cannot simply add revision; they need the extension material taught. The fourth is geography, and it works in your favour. An in-home visit in Remraam or Dubailand Residence Complex prices travel into the hour in a way a session in Al Barsha South does not, which is why the published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 overstates what families in outer communities actually pay for an hour of teaching and understates what they pay for an hour of a tutor's time.

Ramadan and the school calendar move the number in a less obvious way. Compressed school days and post-Iftar session timing shrink the usable evening window, so specialist hours in that period are contested, and a family that books late pays the late price. The practical response is to fix the weekly slot before the term starts and to treat the investigation block as a DP1 purchase rather than a DP2 rescue.

sections.heading: The assessment, component by component, and where the marks go missing
paragraphs: SEHS is assessed through two written papers and one independent scientific investigation. Paper 1 carries a multiple-choice section and a data-based section sat in one sitting. Paper 2 carries short-answer questions and extended responses. The investigation is worth 20% of the grade at both levels, which means a fifth of the result is decided by a document the student controls completely and which almost no Dubai family budgets support for until it is nearly due.

The table below sets out the components with the weightings commonly published for this subject. Confirm them against the current subject guide with your school's IB coordinator before planning around a number: guides are revised, and a tutor who quotes a weighting from an older guide is a tutor who will prioritise the wrong component. The right question to ask at a trial lesson is not 'do you know SEHS' but 'which criterion was my child's last investigation draft weakest on, and why'.

The losses are patterned rather than random. On Paper 1A, students guess on items that test a definition rather than a concept, which is recoverable in a fortnight. On Paper 1B, they describe a trend when the command term asked them to explain it, which is a vocabulary problem dressed as a knowledge problem. On Paper 2, extended responses list facts without an argument. In the investigation, the research question is too broad to answer with the data collected, and every downstream criterion then suffers for a decision made in week one.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, twenty-four marks, one document
paragraphs: A fifth of a SEHS grade sits in one document, and it is the component where tutoring produces the clearest movement, because the criteria are published and the failures are repetitive. The investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A student who understands what each descriptor rewards writes a different document from one who is writing a lab report from memory.

Research design is where most SEHS investigations are decided. A question about whether 'fitness' improves with training has no measurable variable and cannot score well however good the writing is. A question about the effect of a named warm-up protocol on counter-movement jump height in a stated population has named variables, a repeatable method and a realistic data set. Dubai adds a practical constraint here: school facility access and participant availability are limited, and a question that depends on equipment the school does not have fails before it starts.

The other three criteria follow from that first decision. Data analysis rewards processing that suits the data, with spread and uncertainty handled rather than mentioned. The conclusion must answer the stated question and compare the result against published findings, with a citation. Evaluation is marked on specific weaknesses, their effect on the conclusion, and improvements a student could actually implement. The most common single loss in the whole component is an evaluation whose only suggestion is a larger sample.

sections.heading: SEHS or Biology? The question that decides the subject choice
paragraphs: This is the most consequential question on the page and the one no competitor answers. SEHS is a Group 4 experimental science and satisfies the Diploma's science requirement. That does not mean every destination accepts it in place of Biology or Chemistry, and a Dubai family choosing subjects in Year 11 is usually making a decision about university admission without realising it.

The rule of thumb is that courses which name a science usually name Biology or Chemistry, and courses which name a field accept SEHS. Medicine, dentistry and most biomedical sciences specify Chemistry and often Biology. Physiotherapy, sports therapy, sports science and sports management are far more likely to accept or welcome SEHS. The only safe method is to read the entry requirements on the page for the specific course at the specific university, for the year of entry, and to do that before DP1 subject selection rather than in DP2.

For UAE destinations there is a second layer. Ministry of Education equivalency for a secondary certificate is a separate process from university admission, administered by the ministry and the emirate's attestation authority, not by a school or a tutor. The British-track requirements are published and specific; no verified IB points threshold is published in the sources used for this page, so verify the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, and nobody should tell you otherwise.

The timing of the decision matters as much as the decision. Dubai schools confirm Diploma subject blocks in the spring of Year 11, and once the timetable closes a swap from SEHS to Biology may simply be unavailable because the two sit in the same column. A family that reads three course pages in February has more options than one that reads them in DP2. If the destination is genuinely undecided, the safer combination is a named science plus SEHS rather than SEHS alone, and that is a conversation to have with the school's careers lead before the option form goes in.

sections.heading: Where SEHS candidates in Dubai actually lose marks
paragraphs: Command terms cost more marks in this subject than content gaps do. Outline, describe, explain, discuss and evaluate are not synonyms, and each has a mark allocation shaped to it. A student who writes four sentences of accurate description against a question that said explain has written something correct and unmarkable. This is the single cheapest fix available in SEHS, and it is usually worth more than another pass through the theme notes.

Data-based questions are the second pattern. Paper 1B presents data from studies the student has never seen, and the marks go to reading what is in front of them: axes, units, the actual shape of the relationship, the limits of what the data can support. Students trained on revision summaries rather than on unfamiliar data arrive expecting recall and find interpretation. The remedy is practice on studies nobody has pre-digested, which is a thing a tutor can supply and a revision guide cannot.

The third pattern is structural and it shows up in Paper 2 extended responses. Students write everything they know about the topic in the order they learned it. Examiners reward an answer built around the question, with a position, evidence and a limitation. The fourth pattern is biomechanics calculation, where students who are fine on the physiology lose marks on moments, forces and units, usually because the mechanics was taught once and never practised numerically.

A fifth pattern is worth naming because it is specific to this subject. Students who train seriously know a great deal about their own sport, and that knowledge arrives in answers as anecdote rather than as evidence. A question about energy systems wants timescales and substrates, not an account of what a coach says about interval work. The same instinct damages the investigation, where personal conviction about a training method substitutes for a measurable variable. Diagnosing that habit takes one marked script, and correcting it takes a term of being asked, every session, what the question actually requires.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the data comes from human participants
paragraphs: SEHS puts a boundary question in front of students that most Diploma subjects do not, because the data comes from people. Participants have to consent, the protocol has to be approved by the school before anything is measured, and vulnerable participants bring further restrictions. A tutor's role here is to ask whether approval exists before a single data point is collected, because an investigation built on unapproved human data is a problem no amount of good analysis repairs.

The second boundary is authorship, and it is the one worth stating plainly. A tutor teaches, questions, marks against published criteria and explains why a paragraph does not score. A tutor does not supply a research question, hand over a data set, or put sentences into a student's document. Every word and every measurement in an internal assessment must be the student's own. Any provider offering a finished investigation is offering an academic-honesty breach, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the provider.

The third boundary is sources. Comparing a result against published findings is required by the conclusion criterion, and that comparison has to be cited. Reproducing figures or passages from a syllabus document, a textbook or a past paper into an investigation is a copyright and an honesty problem at once. Reference the source, cite the official URL, and link out. That is also the habit that makes the evaluation criterion easier, because a student who has read the published method can see what their own method lacked.

sections.heading: Fitting a SEHS hour into a Dubai training week
paragraphs: SEHS students are disproportionately athletes, and that makes timetabling the deciding factor in whether tutoring works. A session at 16:00 competes with training. A session at 18:00 competes with the drive home from training. In Dubai Sports City the two happen in the same place, so an evening slot after 19:30 Gulf Standard Time usually holds; in Nad Al Sheba or Remraam the commute is the constraint and the later slot is the only one that survives a term.

The practical answer is a fixed weekday rather than a flexible one. Families who agree to 'find a slot each week' lose roughly a third of their sessions to fixtures, and a lost specialist hour near a deadline is not easily replaced in a thin market. Two 45-minute sessions a week often work better than one 90-minute session during an investigation block, because the student has something to do between them and the tutor has something to mark.

The academic calendar adds two fixed pressures. Ramadan compresses school days and moves family routines, and the usable window narrows to post-Iftar session timing for most households; agreeing that shift in advance is better than renegotiating weekly. The second pressure is the autumn of DP2, when internally assessed work across six subjects falls inside a few weeks. A SEHS investigation competing with an Extended Essay and two other internal assessments is the normal situation, not the unlucky one, and planning the block in DP1 is what keeps it out of that pile-up.

sections.heading: How delivery works, and what IB Gram does not do in the UAE
paragraphs: Every lesson for a Dubai family runs online, one to one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. The tutor and the student share a screen, work on the same document or paper, and the student keeps the annotated file afterwards. Written feedback follows each session, naming the criterion or the command term that was addressed, so a parent can see what was worked on without sitting in the room.

IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we offer only in India. That is stated on every UAE page on this site, and for a subject like SEHS it is the stronger offer rather than the weaker one: the question is whether your child can work with someone who has marked investigations against the current criteria, and a twenty-minute driving radius in Dubai is a poor filter for that.

Two further things are worth stating plainly. Anyone providing private tuition inside the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years through the MoHRE smart app and e-services; the official service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. And if no SEHS specialist is genuinely free in the window you need, we say so and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than putting a generalist in the slot and calling it a match.

process.title: Tell us the level, the component and the deadline
process.description: Three facts decide everything that follows: Standard or Higher Level, which component is in trouble, and the date it is due. A DP1 student planning an investigation and a DP2 student eight weeks from the May session need different tutors, different session lengths and different numbers of hours.

process.title: We check who has actually marked a SEHS investigation
process.description: Availability is checked before a match is offered, and the filter is narrow: experience teaching the current themes, and experience marking the investigation against the four published criteria. If nobody who meets that is free in your window, we say so rather than widening the filter quietly.

process.title: A free trial lesson on real work
process.description: The trial runs on your child's own marked paper or current draft, not on a sample exercise, and no card is required to book it. At the end you should know which criterion is weakest and roughly how many hours the fix needs. If the answer is 'fewer than you expected', that is the answer you get.

process.title: A quote in AED against a number of hours
process.description: Pricing follows the plan rather than preceding it: the level, the component, the session length and the number of hours. The published market bands on this page are the context you can check it against, and they are other providers' figures, not ours.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written feedback
process.description: Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time on a fixed weekday, with post-Iftar session timing agreed in advance during Ramadan. Written feedback after each session names what was addressed and what the student should do before the next one, so progress is visible between reports.

process.title: The block ends when the component is done
process.description: An investigation block ends at submission; a paper clinic ends at the May session. There is no rolling commitment, and a family who wants to stop after one lesson stops after one lesson. Most Dubai SEHS families come back for the next component rather than staying on a monthly plan.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED, with the source named
whyPoints.description: Three of the six ranking pages for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote USD. This page publishes AED bands, attributes each one to the provider that published it, and gives the month they were collected, so you can check the figure rather than trust it.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level feedback, not general science help
whyPoints.description: The investigation is marked out of 24 across four published criteria, and feedback that does not name one of them is not feedback a student can act on. Every session note says which criterion or which command term was addressed and what changed as a result.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, marks and explains. No part of an internal assessment is supplied, drafted or edited into shape by us, and the research question is the student's. The boundary is on the page because the alternative is a risk carried by the student.

whyPoints.title: Scarcity handled honestly
whyPoints.description: SEHS runs in a minority of Dubai IB schools and the specialist pool is correspondingly thin. When nobody suitable is free in the fortnight you need, you get told that, with the nearest alternative and the rate that would apply, rather than a generalist presented as a specialist.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the Dubai week
whyPoints.description: Fixed weekday slots that survive fixtures, split sessions during an investigation block, post-Iftar session timing agreed before Ramadan rather than during it, and Gulf Standard Time as the default. Most lost tutoring money in Dubai is lost to cancelled sessions, not to hourly rates.

whyPoints.title: Subject-choice advice that points at the course page
whyPoints.description: Whether SEHS satisfies a university's science requirement is decided by the entry requirements for that course in that year, not by a tutor's opinion. We will tell you where to look and what to look for, and we will not imply that tutoring is required for admission or for equivalency.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Sports, Exercise and Health Science tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands for IB subject tutors in Dubai, collected in October 2026, run from about AED 150 an hour for a qualified online generalist to AED 450 and above for subject specialists, with one Dubai provider advertising AED 650 for examiner-level review. Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 online and TutorChase quotes AED 270. SEHS sits at the upper end of those bands because the subject runs in a minority of Dubai IB schools, so few tutors have marked the investigation. IB Gram publishes no rate card here; the trial lesson is free with no card required, and the quote follows level, component and hours.

faqs.question: Why is a SEHS specialist harder to find in Dubai than a Biology tutor?
faqs.answer: Because supply follows classrooms. Dubai has 227 private schools, and Biology is taught in almost all of the IB ones; SEHS is offered by a minority of them, often as a single mixed Standard and Higher Level class with one teacher. That produces a small local pool of people who have taught the current themes and marked the investigation against the four published criteria. Online delivery is the direct answer to that scarcity: your search is no longer limited to the people who happen to live within driving distance of your community, which is a poor filter for subject expertise in any case.

faqs.question: What exactly is the SEHS scientific investigation, and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It is one independent investigation of around 3,000 words, worth 20% of the grade at both levels, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design decides the rest, because a question with no measurable variable cannot score well however carefully it is written. Data analysis rewards handling spread and uncertainty rather than mentioning them. The conclusion must answer the stated question and compare the result against published findings, with a citation. Evaluation is marked on specific weaknesses and realistic improvements. Confirm the current criteria and limits with your school's IB coordinator.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help design an investigation that uses human participants?
faqs.answer: A tutor can question whether the research question is measurable, whether the method is repeatable, and whether the school has approved the protocol before any data is collected. That approval is not optional, and it comes first: an investigation built on unapproved human data is a problem good analysis cannot repair. What a tutor must not do is supply the research question, hand over a data set, or put sentences into the document. Every measurement and every word belongs to the student. Consent needs documenting, and investigations involving younger or vulnerable participants carry further restrictions that the school, not a tutor, decides.

faqs.question: Is Sports, Exercise and Health Science an easier Group 4 science than Biology?
faqs.answer: It is a different science rather than a lighter one. The content volume is usually smaller than Biology at Higher Level, but SEHS demands biomechanics calculation, statistical treatment of human data, and command-term discipline in extended responses, and those defeat students who chose it expecting coursework about sport. The investigation carries the same 20% and the same 24 marks as the other sciences. Where it genuinely is easier is engagement: students who train seriously find the material intuitive. Where it is harder is the papers, because familiarity with the topic tempts students into writing what they know rather than answering the question.

faqs.question: Does my child need Biology as well as SEHS for a medical degree?
faqs.answer: For medicine and dentistry, assume Chemistry is required and Biology is usually expected, and treat SEHS as a third science rather than a substitute. The decision is made by the entry requirements published for that specific course, at that specific university, for the year of entry, and those pages differ more than families expect. Check them before DP1 subject selection rather than in DP2, when the timetable has closed. Physiotherapy, sports therapy, sports science and sports management are much more likely to accept SEHS. No tutor should tell you a destination accepts it without pointing you at the page that says so.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between SEHS at Standard and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level carries extension content across the themes, and it is assessed inside the same two papers rather than in a separate third paper. That matters practically: an HL student cannot cover the gap by revising harder, because the extension material has to be taught. The investigation is the same component with the same 20% weighting and the same 24 marks at both levels. Students who move from Standard to Higher Level mid-year in a Dubai school almost always need a catch-up block of eight to ten hours, which is a cost nobody budgets for at subject-selection time.

faqs.question: How do the data-based questions in SEHS Paper 1 actually work?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 has a multiple-choice section and a data-based section sat in one sitting. The data-based questions present results from studies the student has never seen, and the marks go to reading what is on the page: axes, units, the shape of the relationship, and the limits of what the data can support. Students who revised from summary notes arrive expecting recall and meet interpretation instead. The fix is practice on unfamiliar studies rather than on pre-digested revision material, and the most common single loss is describing a trend when the command term asked for an explanation.

faqs.question: How many hours of SEHS support does a Dubai DP2 student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which component is in trouble. A scientific investigation block typically runs six to eight hours, spread over the weeks the student is collecting and writing. A Paper 2 extended-response clinic runs four to six. A full final-term consolidation before the May session runs ten to twelve. A weekly slot across a whole Diploma year is 28 to 32 hours, costs more in total than any single block, and buys considerably more, because it front-loads the investigation and avoids the crisis premium that Dubai's bunched DP2 deadlines create.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Dubai for SEHS lessons?
faqs.answer: No. Every lesson for a Dubai family is delivered online, one to one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we provide only in India. For this subject that is the stronger option rather than a compromise, because the pool of tutors who have marked a SEHS investigation is small and a driving radius makes it smaller. Published in-home bands of AED 180 to 500 an hour price travel into the lesson, which is a cost that buys presence rather than subject expertise.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools offer SEHS at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: SEHS is offered by a minority of Dubai's IB World Schools, and whether Higher Level runs in a given year usually depends on how many students opt in. Ask your school's IB coordinator two questions directly: is SEHS running at Higher Level for this cohort, and is the class mixed with Standard Level. A mixed class is common in small cohorts and is the single best predictor that an HL student will need outside support for the extension content. Schools named elsewhere on this page are ecosystem context only; confirm current provision with the school.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover SEHS and Biology for the same Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is one of the few genuine efficiencies in a Group 4 timetable. Both subjects use the same investigation model and the same four criteria, so the research-design conversation transfers directly, and the physiology overlap is real. Chemistry is a different matter and usually needs a separate specialist, because the calculation load and the content have less in common with SEHS than families expect. If a tutor claims to cover SEHS, Biology, Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level, ask which of them they have marked internal assessments in.

faqs.question: Does SEHS count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a ministry process, separate from university admission, and it is administered by the Ministry of Education and the emirate's attestation authority rather than by a school or a tutor. The British-track requirements are published and specific: five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. For the IB, no verified points threshold appears in the sources used for this page, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority. Tutoring is not required for equivalency.

faqs.question: How do sessions fit around school fixtures and academy training in Dubai?
faqs.answer: By fixing the weekday rather than negotiating weekly. Families who agree to find a slot each week lose roughly a third of their sessions to fixtures, and a specialist hour lost near a deadline is hard to replace in a thin market. In Dubai Sports City an evening slot after 19:30 Gulf Standard Time usually survives training; in outer communities such as Remraam or Nad Al Sheba the commute decides it. During an investigation block, two 45-minute sessions a week often work better than one long one, because there is something to do and something to mark between them.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change when a SEHS session can realistically run in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and agreeing it before the month starts is better than renegotiating during it. School days compress, family routines shift, and the usable evening window narrows for every household at once, which means specialist hours in that period are contested. Families who set post-Iftar session timing in advance keep their slot; families who try to rearrange week by week tend to lose sessions at exactly the point in DP2 when internally assessed work across six subjects is landing. The same applies to the autumn pile-up, when the investigation competes with an Extended Essay and other internal assessments.

faqs.question: What happens if no SEHS specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the nearest honest alternative and the rate that would apply, rather than a generalist placed in the slot and described as a specialist. For a subject this thinly staffed in Dubai that conversation happens more often in the weeks before internal upload deadlines than at any other time, which is the practical argument for booking an investigation block in DP1 and a final-term clinic before the winter break. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which does not mean they do not have one.

dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Diploma Sports Exercise and Health Science at both levels for Dubai students: the physiology recall, the data-based question technique, the calculations, the option paper your school has chosen, and the scientific investigation that carries the internal marks.

intro.heading: What SEHS is actually marked on, and where Dubai candidates lose it
paragraphs: Sports Exercise and Health Science is chosen by a lot of Dubai Diploma students who are good at sport and interested in the body, and it punishes them for a reason that has nothing to do with either. It is a science. It is assessed like a science, with precise terminology, data interpretation under time pressure, calculations with units, and an investigation judged on method rather than on enthusiasm. A student who can explain how a muscle works in conversation and cannot write it in the terms an examiner recognises will sit in the middle bands indefinitely, and the gap is almost always technique rather than knowledge.

The four places marks go missing are predictable enough to name. The first is the option paper, which schools choose and students revise last, so it arrives in the examination as the least practised material on the course. The second is the data-based question, where candidates explain the physiology instead of describing what the data shows and then referring to it. The third is precision in the physiology itself: naming a structure correctly, stating a direction of change, giving a mechanism in the right order. The fourth is the investigation, where the marks sit in the design and the processing rather than in the topic.

None of those four is a reading problem. They are all practice problems, which is why they respond quickly to one-to-one work and why a parent should expect visible movement within a handful of sessions rather than within a term. A session that starts from a marked script can usually diagnose which of the four is costing the most marks inside twenty minutes, because each one leaves a distinctive signature on the page.

Confirm the current component structure, option list and weightings with your child's IB coordinator before planning anything against them. The SEHS guide has been revised, different cohorts in Dubai are working from different versions, and no figure from a tutoring page should be treated as authoritative on what your child will actually sit. What does not change with the guide is the examiner's demand for precision, the behaviour of data questions, or the fact that the option paper is the component schools have least time for.

Delivery is online. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around training, fixtures and the school week, which in this subject is a practical requirement rather than a convenience. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. A tutor here teaches, questions and gives written feedback on the student's own work; the investigation, from the research question to the final sentence, belongs to the student.

dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.programmesIntro: The habits SEHS examines are built before the Diploma and reused in the Diploma core. These are the three levels a Dubai family is normally dealing with when they contact us about this subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences and Physical and Health Education
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme splits what SEHS later joins. Its science criteria build the investigation skills, and Physical and Health Education builds the applied understanding. Students who arrive strong in the second and weak in the first are the classic SEHS profile: fluent about training and unpractised at controlling a variable or processing data. That combination predicts a mid-band Diploma grade more reliably than any predicted score does.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs both routes into the Diploma, Middle Years to Year 11 in IB schools and IGCSE in the larger British-curriculum sector. IGCSE Biology and Physical Education students usually arrive with better examination timing and less practice at open investigation design. We test which of the two gaps a student has in the first session rather than assuming.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Sports Exercise and Health Science
programmes.description: SEHS is a Group 4 science assessed through written papers and an internal scientific investigation. The written assessment covers core physiology and applied content plus a paper on an option the school selects. Marks turn on terminological precision, data interpretation and correctly executed calculations. Confirm the current component list, option names and weightings with your school's IB coordinator, because the guide has been revised and cohorts in Dubai are working from different versions.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, SEHS is frequently taught by a biologist or by a physical education specialist who has taken the subject on, and which one it is changes the gap. A biologist-taught class is usually secure on physiology and lighter on applied training theory. A physical-education-taught class is often the reverse. Ask the teacher's background, because it predicts the weakness better than a report grade does.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and the Group 4 project
programmes.description: An Extended Essay in SEHS attracts students who want to research their own sport, and it fails for the same reason the investigation fails: a question that cannot be answered with data a school student can ethically and practically obtain from human participants. The Group 4 project is collaborative and assessed on participation rather than output, and for SEHS students it is often the first sustained work alongside physicists and chemists.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai offers real research material for a SEHS Extended Essay: heat acclimatisation, hydration in high ambient temperatures, training load in a Gulf summer, and the effect of indoor against outdoor training environments. Ethics and participant consent are the constraint rather than the ideas, and the first supervision session is spent on whether the study can lawfully and ethically be run at all.

dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.subjectsIntro: SEHS students in Dubai usually need help with one or two neighbours as well. These are the related Diploma courses our tutors cover for the same families, with the specific demand each makes.

subjects.name: Sports Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Assessed through written papers and a scientific investigation. Marks turn on precise physiological terminology, data-based question technique, correct calculations with units, and an investigation judged on design and processing. The commonest loss is explaining a mechanism when the question asked the candidate to describe data.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Shares the physiology and the laboratory discipline, and demands a heavier recall load across a wider syllabus. Students taking both find the cell and systems material reinforcing, and should expect Biology to set the standard for how precisely a mechanism has to be written.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Where energy systems, respiration and nutrition content actually makes sense. SEHS students who take Chemistry write better answers on metabolic pathways because they understand what a bond and an enzyme are doing, rather than reciting a sequence of names.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Overlaps directly with the sport-psychology material and with research methods. Students taking both have a genuine advantage on study evaluation and on the ethics section of the investigation, because the vocabulary of participants, consent and validity is already theirs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics course that most helps a SEHS investigation. Means, spread, correlation and significance are taught here in the form the investigation criteria assume. Students taking both tend to need fewer hours on the processing section than those who are not.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Relevant to biomechanics, force, levers and energy. A SEHS student who has done any mechanics writes more confidently about movement analysis, and is less likely to describe a lever system in general terms when the question wants named classes and a calculation.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.levels: Both levels, confirm with your school
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary alternative Dubai students sometimes weigh against SEHS. Both involve investigation design, and ESS replaces human participants with environmental data. Worth comparing on assessment style rather than on reputation, because they suit different students.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Often paired with SEHS by students aiming at sports management, marketing or facility operations. The research project in Business Management and the SEHS investigation reward similar planning discipline, so the two can be sequenced to share work habits.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Where the extended-writing habit either exists or does not. SEHS papers include extended responses that need structure as well as content, and students who write well in English A usually need less help organising a six-mark answer than those who do not.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research. In SEHS the risk is a question requiring participant data that cannot ethically be collected by a school student. Supervision is questioning and written feedback on the student's own drafts; the school's registered supervisor signs the work off.

sections.heading: The option paper, and why your school's choice decides the revision plan
paragraphs: The first question we ask a Dubai SEHS family is which option the school teaches, and a surprising number cannot answer it. That is not carelessness; it is a consequence of how the component is scheduled. Schools select an option, teach the core first because it underpins everything, and arrive at the option in the final stretch. Students therefore meet this material when revision has already started, write very few practice answers on it, and sit a paper on the content they have handled least.

It is also the component where tutoring is most obviously efficient, because the fix is question volume rather than teaching. A student who has written twenty marked responses on their option before the mock is in a different position from one who has read the chapter twice, and twenty responses is six to ten sessions of work. Nothing else in this subject converts hours into marks at that rate.

Options are chosen by the school from the list in the current guide, and the list has changed between guide versions. The commonly taught areas are physiological optimisation of performance, the psychology of sport, physical activity and health, and nutrition for sport and exercise. Confirm both the current option list and your school's selection with the IB coordinator before planning revision, because preparing the wrong option is the most wasteful mistake available in this subject and we have seen families make it.

sections.heading: The physiology that has to be known cold, and the precision examiners want
paragraphs: SEHS recall is not enormous, but it is unforgiving about wording. A candidate who writes that the heart pumps harder has said nothing an examiner can credit; one who writes that stroke volume increases and heart rate rises, giving a higher cardiac output, has answered. The difference is not intelligence, it is vocabulary that has been tested aloud until it is automatic. Students who revise by reading always under-perform students who revise by being asked.

The pattern of loss is consistent across the Dubai scripts we read. Structures are named approximately rather than exactly. Directions of change are left implicit, so an examiner cannot tell whether the candidate knows that something rose or fell. Mechanisms are given out of order, which costs the sequencing marks even where every element is present. And comparisons are asserted rather than made, with no reference to the thing being compared against.

The work is therefore oral before it is written. We spend the first part of a recall session asking rather than explaining, which exposes in minutes what a written revision guide would hide for weeks. Then the same material gets written under time, because knowing a mechanism aloud and producing it in six marks under clock pressure are different skills.

sections.heading: Data-based questions: describing before explaining
paragraphs: If a Dubai SEHS student is scoring in the middle bands while their teacher says they understand the subject, the data questions are the first place to look. These items present a graph or a table and ask the candidate to work from it, and the dominant failure is that the candidate ignores the data and explains the physiology they already know. The physiology may be correct. It is not what was asked, so the marks reserved for using the data are never available.

The fix is an order of operations, and it is genuinely mechanical. State what the data shows, with values and units quoted from the figure. Note the deviation from the trend if there is one, because the deviation is frequently where a mark sits. Only then explain, and make the explanation refer back to the numbers just quoted. Students who adopt that order stop losing marks within two or three sessions, which makes this the fastest-moving work on the page.

There is a second habit worth building at the same time: reading the axes, the units and the scale before reading the shape of the line. A surprising share of lost marks comes from a candidate who has interpreted a graph correctly in shape and wrongly in magnitude, because the axis was logarithmic, the units were not what was assumed, or the scale did not start at zero.

sections.heading: Calculations and units: the marks that get dropped rather than lost
paragraphs: SEHS calculations are not mathematically demanding and candidates lose marks on them constantly. The reason is that they are treated as an incidental part of a science subject rather than as a drilled skill, so a student who can do the arithmetic in their head writes it down without units, without the working an examiner needs to see, and without checking whether the answer is physically sensible.

Three habits recover most of this. Write the formula before substituting into it, because a formula on the page frequently earns a mark on its own and always prevents the wrong substitution. Carry units through the calculation rather than attaching them at the end, which is how an impossible answer gets caught. And sanity-check the result against what the body can actually do: a cardiac output or an oxygen consumption that is an order of magnitude out should trigger a second look, and a student who has been taught the normal range will notice while one who has not will not.

The second half of the work is justification. Many calculation items in this subject do not stop at the number; they ask the candidate to use it. A dietary or training recommendation based on a calculated figure needs the figure, the reasoning and the recommendation, and students who stop at the figure leave half the marks on the table. We practise the two halves separately before putting them together, because combining them before either is secure produces answers that are muddled in both directions.

sections.heading: Where Dubai SEHS candidates lose marks, in order of frequency
paragraphs: Across the scripts we read for Dubai students, the losses fall in a consistent order, and the order matters because it tells a family what to buy first. Leading the list is answering a data question with physiology rather than with the data. Second is imprecise terminology, where the candidate knows the mechanism and does not write it in words an examiner can award. Third is the option paper, unpractised rather than unknown. Fourth is calculation presentation, where the arithmetic was right and the page was not. Fifth is extended-response structure, where everything relevant is present and unorganised, so the marks that depend on development are missed.

Only after those five does genuine content ignorance appear, and that ordering is the most useful thing on this page. The default assumption of a worried parent is that their child does not know enough and needs the syllabus taught again. For most mid-band SEHS candidates in this emirate that is the wrong diagnosis and the most expensive possible response, because it buys a term of content delivery to fix a technique problem.

There is a sixth loss worth naming separately because it is specific to this subject's population. Students who train seriously often write about sport from experience rather than from the course, substituting what they know works in their own training for what the syllabus states. Examiners cannot credit that, however true it is. Part of the work with an athlete-student is explicitly separating their practitioner knowledge from the assessed material, and it is usually a relief to them once named.

A session that begins from a marked script can place a student on this list quickly, which is why we ask for one before the trial lesson. The script shows the signature of each failure: data questions answered without quoted values, mechanisms in the wrong order, option answers that are short, calculations with naked numbers, long responses with no paragraph structure.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: design and processing, not topic
paragraphs: SEHS students choose investigation topics they care about, which is a good start and not where the marks are. The marks sit in whether the study was designed so that it could show anything, whether the data was processed in a way that supports the conclusion, and whether the evaluation engages with what actually went wrong rather than listing generic limitations. A beautifully chosen question with two participants and one trial each cannot earn the design or the analysis marks, however interesting it is.

Human participants add a layer this subject's candidates frequently underestimate. Consent has to be obtained and documented, the risk of the protocol has to be considered honestly, and anyone under eighteen involves additional care. A Dubai student planning to test teammates during academy training needs the coach's agreement as well as the participants', and the school's own ethics process governs all of it. These are not obstacles to work around; they are part of what the criteria assess, and a study that ignores them is in trouble before any data exists.

Reliability is the other recurring weakness. A single measurement of anything physiological is close to meaningless, because the body varies between trials and between days. Repeat measures, a stated protocol that a reader could follow exactly, and control of the obvious confounders such as time of day, prior exercise and hydration are what separate a study that analyses cleanly from one that produces noise. In Dubai, ambient temperature is a confounder worth naming explicitly, and a student who controls for it has a genuine methodological point to make in their evaluation.

Our supervision rule is narrow and stated before anyone pays. A tutor may ask any question about the investigation and may not supply any sentence of it. That means the tutor can ask whether the protocol is repeatable, whether the sample will support the processing, whether the evaluation is about this study or about studies in general. It means the tutor does not propose the research question, does not write or rewrite any part of the submission, and does not touch the data.

sections.heading: The student who trains fifteen hours a week
paragraphs: A meaningful share of Dubai SEHS candidates are serious athletes: academy football, competitive swimming, tennis, equestrian, athletics. The subject is often chosen because it connects to their life, and the training load then becomes the main obstacle to studying it. This is a scheduling problem with a known solution, and it is worth setting out because generic advice about weekly routine is useless to these families.

Three adjustments do most of the work. Sessions go where the training is not, which in Dubai frequently means 06:30 before school or after 20:00, and we hold those slots deliberately for this group. Written work is concentrated in the lighter weeks of a fixture calendar rather than spread evenly, so a tournament week carries no marked essay and the fortnight after carries two. And recall testing replaces teaching in the heavy weeks, because being questioned for thirty minutes is sustainable after training in a way that absorbing new material is not.

The second half of the issue is the one named earlier: an athlete's practitioner knowledge competing with the syllabus. A student who has done periodised training for years has strong intuitions about what works, and the examination rewards the course content rather than the intuition. Making that distinction explicit, and treating their experience as a source of examples rather than a source of answers, converts the training background from an obstacle back into the advantage it should be.

Ramadan deserves its own note. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots as standard rather than on request, training loads change, and in the weeks that follow there is often a compressed run-up to internal deadlines. We plan the term with those dates visible instead of discovering them, and we would rather reduce session frequency in a heavy fortnight than hold a slot nobody can use properly.

sections.heading: What one session can actually fix, symptom by symptom
paragraphs: Parents reasonably want to know what a single hour buys, and in this subject the honest answer is specific rather than general. Some SEHS faults are one-session fixes because they are habits of presentation. Others are multi-week because they are gaps in recall or in practice volume. Telling the two apart before spending anything is the most useful thing a family can do.

The habits are quick. Describe-before-explain on data questions, quoting values with units, writing a formula before substituting, naming the lever class, stating direction of change: each of those can be taught, practised and visibly changed inside one session, and they appear on almost every mid-band script we read. A family who buys three sessions and gets those five habits has had good value, and we would rather say that than sell a term.

The gaps are slower and should be priced honestly. An unpractised option paper is six to ten sessions because the fix is question volume. Insecure physiology is four to eight because the fix is repeated oral testing. A weak investigation design caught late may not be fixable at all if the data is collected and the deadline is past, in which case we say so and work on the papers instead.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and how these lessons run
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time via the ministry's app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount is quoted here.

Two further positions should be explicit. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and claims no approval, accreditation, licensing or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way, so no family anywhere in the UAE should arrange for a child to be tutored privately by their own class teacher.

On materials, we do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They belong to the board and are the school's to distribute. We reference them, cite the official source and link out, which is what the examination boards ask of anyone writing about their qualifications. Where this page describes components, options or weightings, treat it as a prompt to check with the coordinator rather than as a source.

Delivery is online: one-to-one over live video, screen-shared, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and moved post-Iftar during Ramadan. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. If no SEHS specialist is free in your slot, we say so and estimate when one will be, rather than assigning a biologist and letting you find out in week three. A free trial lesson comes first in every case, with no card required to book it.

process.description: Every timed response comes back scored with a comment, and the scripts stay in sequence. Reading three consecutive responses tells a parent whether the same loss keeps recurring, which is also how we decide a block has done its job and should end rather than roll on.

faqs.question: Which SEHS option paper has my child's Dubai school chosen?
faqs.answer: Ask the IB coordinator or the SEHS teacher directly, because it is the single most important planning fact in this subject and families often do not know it. Schools select from the option list in the current guide and teach the option last, after the core. If outside help prepares the wrong option, the hours are wasted entirely, which is the most expensive avoidable mistake available here. Get the answer in writing before anyone starts revision, and ask at the same time which guide version the cohort is working from, since the option list has changed between versions.

faqs.question: What does my child actually have to memorise for SEHS?
faqs.answer: Less than for Biology, and with far more precision. Named structures, directions of change, mechanisms in the right order, the three energy systems with their fuels and durations, lever classes, and the distinction between an acute response and a chronic adaptation. The volume is manageable; the standard of wording is not negotiable. A candidate who writes that the heart pumps harder earns nothing, where one who writes that stroke volume and heart rate both rise, increasing cardiac output, earns the mark. We test recall aloud for that reason rather than setting reading.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on questions he says were easy?
faqs.answer: Usually because he answered a different question from the one asked. The classic version is a data item where the candidate explains the physiology they know instead of describing what the graph shows and then referring to it, which leaves the data marks untouched however correct the physiology is. The second version is a command word mismatch: compare answered as describe, evaluate answered as explain. Both are visible in the first line of his answer. Read his last marked script against the opening sentence of each response and the pattern usually appears immediately.

faqs.question: How are the data-based questions in SEHS actually marked?
faqs.answer: In two parts, and candidates usually attempt only one. There are marks for working from the data, which means quoting values with units, stating the direction and magnitude of change, and noting any deviation from the trend. There are separate marks for explanation, which has to refer back to the data rather than float free of it. A strong answer therefore opens with two quoted figures and a direction, then explains. We drill that order until it becomes automatic, and it is the fastest-moving improvement in this subject, typically visible within two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Which SEHS calculations are worth drilling?
faqs.answer: Cardiac output from stroke volume and heart rate, body composition and index measures, energy intake against expenditure, mechanical advantage in a lever system, percentage change between two measurements, and rates read from a graph. None is mathematically hard and all of them lose marks for presentation rather than arithmetic. Three habits recover most of it: write the formula before substituting, carry units through rather than adding them at the end, and sanity-check the answer against physiological plausibility. Confirm with the teacher which formulae your child's cohort must recall and which are provided, as this varies.

faqs.question: What separates a full-mark SEHS answer from a half-mark one?
faqs.answer: Specificity and structure, almost always. The full-mark answer names the structure exactly, states the direction of change, gives the mechanism in sequence, and where a comparison is asked, puts both sides in the same sentence with a comparative term. The half-mark answer contains the same understanding expressed approximately and in no particular order. For longer responses, add development: a point, an elaboration and a consequence, rather than a list of true statements. Students can be taught a default shape for six and eight mark items, and it holds up under exam pressure better than improvisation.

faqs.question: My daughter trains fifteen hours a week. How do sessions fit?
faqs.answer: Around the training, not into it. We hold early slots from around 06:30 and late slots after 20:00 in Gulf Standard Time specifically for athlete schedules, and we concentrate written work in the lighter weeks of a fixture calendar rather than spreading it evenly. In heavy training weeks the session becomes oral recall testing rather than new content, which is sustainable after a session on the pitch or in the pool when absorbing new material is not. During Ramadan slots move post-Iftar as standard rather than on request.

faqs.question: Is SEHS taken seriously as a science by universities?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the course, and the answer should come from the university rather than from a tutoring page. Sports science, physiotherapy, coaching, health and exercise routes generally accept it readily. Medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and the physical sciences usually require Biology, Chemistry or Physics at a stated level, and SEHS does not substitute for them. Read the entry requirements for your child's intended course and entry year on the university's own admissions page. Where a prerequisite science is missing, the right spend is on that subject rather than on additional SEHS hours.

faqs.question: What should a first SEHS session actually cover?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, from the student's own marked work. A useful first hour takes one recent data-based response and rewrites it in the describe-then-explain order, counting the marks before and after, which shows the student rather than tells them. It also establishes which option the school teaches, how secure the core physiology is under oral questioning, and whether the investigation is on track. What a first session should not be is a tour of the syllabus, because that answers a question nobody asked and costs a family an hour of diagnosis.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is content or technique?
faqs.answer: Look at the shape of the loss on a marked script. Technique problems leave partial marks spread across many questions: answers that are broadly right and never quite scoring. Content gaps leave zeros clustered on particular topics while other topics are fine. A quick home test is to ask your child to explain a mechanism aloud. If the explanation is accurate and the written answer scored poorly, it is technique. If the explanation is vague, it is recall. The two need different blocks, and buying the wrong one is the commonest waste in this subject.

faqs.question: What does the SEHS investigation reward that my child may be missing?
faqs.answer: Design and processing rather than topic. Marks sit in whether the study was built so it could show something, whether repeat measures and controls make the data trustworthy, whether the processing supports the conclusion drawn, and whether the evaluation addresses this study's actual weaknesses rather than a generic list. A compelling question with two participants and one trial each cannot earn those marks. In Dubai, naming ambient temperature as a controlled or confounding variable is a real methodological point that very few candidates make and that costs nothing to include.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if the investigation uses teammates as participants?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help with the design, the ethics reasoning and the processing, and must not touch the submission. Using teammates raises specific issues worth resolving early: informed consent from each participant, agreement from the coach where the data is collected during training, additional care where participants are under eighteen, and honest consideration of the protocol's risk. The school's own ethics process governs all of it and the coordinator is the person to ask. A study that collects data before those approvals exist is in difficulty regardless of how good the question was.

faqs.question: How much of the SEHS written assessment is extended writing?
faqs.answer: Enough that structure is worth teaching separately from content, though the exact balance depends on which guide version your child's cohort follows, so confirm it with the coordinator. What is consistent is that longer items reward development rather than coverage: a point made, elaborated and then carried to a consequence will outscore a list of six true statements. Students who learn a default shape for extended responses stop producing answers that contain everything and score in the middle. It is a two or three session fix and it holds under examination pressure.

faqs.question: Does the Higher Level material appear in the option paper too?
faqs.answer: Where a course distinguishes Higher from Standard Level, the additional material typically carries into more than one component, which is why treating it as a separate block rather than as extra weekly content works better. The practical point is that extended material is taught last, revised least and practised almost never, so it behaves exactly like the option paper. Confirm the current structure with your school's IB coordinator before planning, since different Dubai cohorts are working from different guide versions and no tutoring page should be the source for what your child will sit.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover SEHS and Chemistry for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the pairing is genuinely useful. Chemistry is where respiration, energy systems and nutrition content stops being a list of names and starts being a mechanism, so a student doing both tends to write better metabolic answers in SEHS. The caution is scheduling: two subjects in one slot usually means neither gets the written practice it needs, so we would normally run them as separate sessions with one tutor rather than as a combined hour. Tell us both subjects at the consultation and we will say whether one specialist covers them properly.

faqs.question: How late in DP2 can SEHS technique still be fixed?
faqs.answer: Later than in most subjects, because the fastest improvements here are presentation habits rather than knowledge. Describe-then-explain on data questions, quoting values with units, formula before substitution and a default shape for long answers can all be changed in a handful of sessions six weeks out, and they appear on nearly every mid-band script. What cannot be fixed that late is an unpractised option paper, which needs question volume, or an investigation already submitted. Tell us at the consultation which components are still open and we will plan only around those.

dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.closingHeading: Send a marked script and the option name, and we will tell you what it is costing
dubai/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-health-s.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB DP Sports Exercise and Health Science tutor in Dubai, the two things worth sending first are a recent marked paper response and the name of the option your child's school teaches. A specialist will place the losses in order, say which are one-session habits and which need weeks of practice, and tell you honestly if the most useful spend is on a different subject. The first lesson is free, no card is needed to book it, and lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time around training and fixtures.
