sections.heading: Where TOK marks go missing, in the order they go missing
paragraphs: TOK marks are not lost in the places students expect. They are lost in a fairly predictable sequence, and a tutor who has read a lot of scripts can usually name which stage a draft is stuck at within ten minutes. Knowing the order is useful for parents because it tells you whether a problem is structural or cosmetic, and cosmetic problems do not need twelve weeks of tutoring.

The first and most common loss is description instead of argument. The student explains what history is like, what scientists do, what artists intend, and never takes a position that could be disagreed with. The symptom is a draft where no sentence could be answered with "no, because". The fix is slow and it is the main thing weekly sessions buy: every claim gets a question put to it until the student starts anticipating the question themselves.

The second loss is the borrowed example. An essay built on three news stories the student half-remembers reads identically to the two hundred other essays built on the same three news stories. Examples from inside the student's own subjects are harder to find and far stronger: a data-handling problem from a Biology internal assessment, a translation argument from a Language B oral, a proof from Maths AA HL that the student found unconvincing the first time.

The third loss is the unused counter-argument. Students are told to include other perspectives, so they add a paragraph near the end that states a different view and then dismisses it in a sentence. A perspective that does not change the argument has not been weighed. The repair is structural: the counter-argument moves earlier and the subsequent claim is written as a response to it.

The fourth loss is the word ceiling, and it is the most avoidable. A 950-word commentary written by cutting a 1,400-word draft usually loses its justifications and keeps its descriptions, because description is easier to compress. Writing to the ceiling from the start preserves the parts that carry the mark. The fifth and quietest loss is the object itself: a general object cannot be linked to a prompt with any precision, so the commentary has nothing to say and no amount of writing skill saves it.

Examples borrowed from the news rather than owned from the student's own subjects
A counter-argument placed too late to change anything

sections.heading: What TOK and DP core support costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages in this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. Below are the AED bands actually visible in this market as of October 2026, with the provider that published each figure named. These are market rates and not an IB Gram price list. Our own position is a free trial lesson first and a quoted rate after the match, because a TOK specialist and a general subject tutor are not interchangeable and should not carry the same number.

The pattern across the bands is that TOK sits at the specialist end whatever a provider's headline rate says. A tutor charging the budget rate is almost never reading TOK scripts, because the market for TOK readers is small and those people are also marking, teaching or coordinating elsewhere. A family quoted AED 60 an hour for TOK is being quoted a general-essay-help rate, and the work that arrives tends to be general essay help.

Monthly packaging is worth reading carefully. Dubai providers advertise around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For TOK specifically, a short dense block around a deadline usually costs less in total than a year of weekly sessions and achieves more, because the work is deadline-shaped.

Two cautions about rates in this market. First, a premium rate marketed on examiner experience is a claim about a person, and you are entitled to ask what that person currently does and how it was verified. Examiner status does not come with access to marking decisions or grade boundaries, and anyone implying otherwise is selling something that does not exist. Second, ask whether a quoted figure includes VAT before you compare two numbers, because providers in this market are inconsistent about it.

Set the tutoring number against the fee number for context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Against a fee bill that is flat, a deadline-shaped block of TOK support in DP2 is a small and finite line rather than an open-ended commitment.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one versus an in-home TOK tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search phrase implies, so here it is without evasion. An in-home tutor in Dubai is a real option, it costs more per hour than the equivalent online rate because the drive is inside the price, and for some subjects the trade is worth making. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service runs only in India. For TOK the online format is not a second-best substitute, and the reasons are specific rather than general.

Start with the pool. TOK has no textbook and no past-paper bank, so the only thing that separates a useful tutor from a well-meaning one is having read scripts and internalised the instrument. The number of adults in that category who can also reach Dubai Hills Estate or Al Furjan by 4.30pm on a Tuesday is small. Removing the drive widens the search to everyone who does the work, which on a niche DP core component is the whole game.

Then the format itself. A TOK session is two people reading the same paragraph and arguing about it. A shared document with a cursor, live comments and a retained version history is a better instrument for that than a printed draft on a kitchen table, and it produces the evidence trail this page keeps returning to. Nine weeks later you can scroll back and see exactly when the argument changed and who changed it.

Then the calendar. Dubai DP2 students lose weeks to school mocks, to travel, and to Ramadan. Online slots move to post-Iftar timing or to a different time zone when the family travels, and a missed week can be made up on a Saturday morning. A driving tutor's availability is a function of their own commute and their other households, so the same flexibility is not available at any price.

What in-home genuinely does better is worth saying plainly: a younger child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, or a household where screen supervision is difficult. Neither usually describes a sixteen or seventeen year old drafting a prescribed-title essay. If you want someone at the door for a Year 7 student, that is a legitimate need and this is not the service for it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a TOK tutor does not cross
paragraphs: TOK produces two pieces of assessed work that must be the student's own, and the Dubai market for this search contains providers who will sell a finished one. One site found during research offers completed internal assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the provider. So it is worth being exact about where the line sits.

A tutor may teach the course content, explain the assessment instrument, explain what each band of it means, ask questions about a draft, point at a paragraph and say this does not argue anything, suggest that a counter-argument is in the wrong place, and help a student practise the thinking on a title they are not submitting. All of that is teaching, and all of it leaves the authorship with the student.

A tutor may not supply objects for the exhibition, choose the prescribed title on the student's behalf, dictate sentences, rewrite paragraphs into their own prose, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The test we apply is simple: if the finished paragraph contains a sentence the student could not have produced and cannot explain, the line has been crossed, whatever anyone intended. We do not produce assessed work and will not be asked to twice.

The planning and progress forms exist precisely at this boundary. They record the student's interactions with their TOK teacher and the development of their own thinking, and they are the document a school will look at first if authorship is questioned. A student who has worked honestly with a tutor has nothing to fear from them. A student whose draft improved by two bands overnight with no corresponding record has a problem that no tutor can solve for them.

Being explicit about this is also the most useful thing a parent can take from this page. When you interview any tutor for TOK, ask directly what they will and will not do with a draft. The answer tells you more about what you are buying than any rate card.

sections.heading: The TOK year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Almost every DP calendar a family sees runs forwards and is therefore useless by February. TOK deadlines are internal, set by your child's school, and they sit a long way ahead of the exam window because the exhibition has to be marked and moderated and the essay has to be uploaded and marked externally. Planning backwards from the session is the only version that survives contact with a real Dubai school year.

Below is the shape of it in relative terms rather than dates. We publish no IB exam or results dates on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every date in this project would be second-hand, and a wrong date on a page like this costs a family real money. Your DP coordinator holds the authoritative internal deadlines and the IB's published session calendar, and they are the only source to plan against.

The pattern that matters is the collision. The TOK essay's internal deadline tends to land in the same stretch as several subject internal assessments and the Extended Essay final submission, and in a Dubai school year that stretch also contains mocks and, in some years, Ramadan. A student who starts the essay when the titles are released has a comfortable term. A student who starts it when the deadline is announced has three subjects' worth of work in the same fortnight.

Work backwards and the sequencing becomes obvious. The exhibition should be finished in DP1 rather than carried over. The prescribed title should be chosen within a fortnight of release. A first full draft should exist well before the first mock window, so that the mock weeks cost nothing. The final weeks should be spent cutting to the ceiling and strengthening the counter-argument, not writing new material.

One Dubai-specific note on the calendar: during Ramadan, school days shorten and evening energy shifts to after Iftar. Plan the heaviest drafting either side of it rather than through it, and move sessions to post-Iftar slots where the family prefers. This is straightforward to arrange online and much harder to arrange with a tutor who has to drive.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Dubai timetable, and why TOK gets squeezed
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. That band is a useful signal for parents, and it is worth reading alongside the one structural fact that affects TOK directly: the Dubai timetable is fuller than most families realise.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with those requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The guidelines set instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, allow schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advise that no mandatory subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes. Schools must also organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Stack that against six DP subjects, three of them higher level, and the hundred teaching hours TOK is supposed to receive, and something has to give. In practice the thing that gives is often TOK, because it has no exam date visible to students and no weekly homework that a parent will chase. Students arrive in DP2 having had the course delivered in fragments, which is why so much of the tutoring demand in this market is reconstruction rather than extension.

The regulator picture is also worth knowing because it varies by emirate, and Dubai families move. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, so curriculum approval is an emirate-level matter and not only an inspection one.

One thing to be clear about: IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration and no IB authorisation, and nothing here should be read as a regulator endorsing a tutoring service. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, which is a different legal animal from online one-to-one tuition. We name the regulators because parents need to know who sets the rules, not to borrow their authority.

On the tutor side, the rule that does apply is MoHRE's. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, is the official route and lists a two-working-day completion time. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is reported rather than quoted here and worth checking against the current policy document.

process.title: Tell us what the draft actually looks like
process.description: A short form: DP year, school, whether the exhibition is finished, whether a prescribed title is chosen, and what the last reported TOK grade was. One sentence on what worries you most is more useful than a list of subjects. If a draft exists, send it.

process.title: A free trial with the real draft on screen
process.description: Sixty minutes with the student's own work open, not a sample lesson. By the end you should have a written diagnosis naming the band the draft sits in and the two changes that would move it. The trial is free; no card is taken to book it.

process.title: Agree the plan backwards from the school deadline
process.description: We ask for the school's internal TOK deadlines and build the schedule from them, marking the weeks that will be lost to mocks, travel or Ramadan. You see the plan before any payment, and it names how many sessions it assumes.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written note each time
process.description: Each session ends with two or three lines naming what moved and what is next. Drafts come back annotated against the assessment instrument with questions rather than rewrites, in a shared document that keeps every version.

process.title: Review at week four, honestly
process.description: A short written review comparing the current draft against the week-one diagnosis. If nothing has moved, we say so and change the tutor or the approach. If the student no longer needs weekly sessions, we say that too and you stop paying for them.

process.title: Hand back the full record
process.description: At the end of the block you keep everything: the annotated drafts, the session notes, the example list and the plan. That record is also the student's own evidence of how the work developed, which matters if authorship is ever questioned.

whyPoints.title: The evidence is the product
whyPoints.description: Annotated drafts, a written diagnosis, dated session notes and a plan counted backwards from the school deadline. You can read all of it without understanding TOK, and you can compare it month to month. Nothing on this page asks you to take progress on trust.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the instrument, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: TOK readers are scarce. Online delivery means your child is matched with someone who knows how a holistic mark is actually arrived at, rather than with whoever can reach your community before 5pm. For a DP core component that is the difference that moves a letter.

whyPoints.title: Both core grades considered together
whyPoints.description: The points matrix reads TOK and the Extended Essay as a pair, so the first question is which of the two is cheaper to move. Sometimes the answer is that your TOK hours belong to the Extended Essay instead, and we will say so before taking a booking.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated in advance
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. We do not supply objects, choose titles, dictate sentences or produce assessed work, and we say so before the first session rather than after an awkward request.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, with October 2026 as the as-of date. Our own rate is quoted after the free trial, once the match is known, because a DP core specialist and a general essay tutor are not the same purchase.

whyPoints.title: Built for the Dubai school year
whyPoints.description: Sessions on Gulf Standard Time, post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, pauses through mock weeks, and schedules that follow a family that travels. The calendar is the main reason tutoring plans fail here, so it is planned first rather than last.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Theory of Knowledge home tutor in Dubai do in the first session?
faqs.answer: Opens your child's actual draft and reads it on screen. The first session is diagnostic: what the commentary or essay is currently doing, which band that puts it in, and the two specific changes that would move it. You should receive a short written diagnosis afterwards naming those points in plain language. If no draft exists yet, the session instead fixes the IA prompt or shortlists prescribed titles against the student's own strongest areas of knowledge. What it is not is a general introduction to the course. The free trial exists so you can judge the tutor on that first reading before paying anything.

faqs.question: How is the TOK exhibition marked, and how much of the TOK grade does it carry?
faqs.answer: The exhibition is marked inside your child's school and then moderated by the IB, and it carries one third of the TOK grade. The student chooses one prompt from the published IA prompt list and three specific real-world objects, then writes a commentary of up to 950 words in total explaining what each object is and why it connects to that prompt. The mark is a single holistic judgement out of ten rather than a tally against separate criteria. That holistic structure is why vague objects hurt so much: without a specific object there is nothing precise to justify, and the whole piece reads thin.

faqs.question: How long is the TOK essay and who decides the titles?
faqs.answer: The IB releases six prescribed titles for each session, and the student answers one of them in no more than 1,600 words with reference to two areas of knowledge. Neither the school nor a tutor sets the title, and a student may not write their own. The essay is marked externally by an IB examiner, again on a single holistic judgement out of ten, and it carries two thirds of the TOK grade. The word ceiling is firm, which is why writing to length from the outset works better than cutting a long draft: compression tends to remove justification and keep description, and justification is where the mark lives.

faqs.question: Can a tutor pick my child's three exhibition objects for them?
faqs.answer: No, and you should treat an offer to do it as a warning sign. The objects and the justification have to be the student's own work, and the planning and progress form exists to record that they were. What a tutor can legitimately do is test the objects your child has chosen: ask what exactly the object is, whether it is a specific thing or a category, and whether it gives the chosen prompt anything to bite on. That questioning usually produces better objects than any suggestion would, because the student ends up able to explain the choice under pressure.

faqs.question: My son is predicted a C in TOK and a C in the Extended Essay. Is that enough?
faqs.answer: It is one point out of the three available, and it is worth knowing that before offers are accepted. The matrix pairs the two core grades: two A grades return three points, an A with a B also returns three, two B grades return two, and two C grades return one. Moving either component by a single letter in the middle of that grid is often worth a whole point. If one of the two is further from the next band than the other, the hours belong to the one that is closer. Confirm the current grid with your DP coordinator before planning around it.

faqs.question: Is a grade E in Theory of Knowledge really a failing condition for the diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. A grade E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the IB Diploma regardless of how many subject points a student has earned. A candidate on forty points with an E in TOK does not hold a diploma. This is the reason an early and unsentimental diagnosis matters more than a burst of intensity in the final term: a weak exhibition in DP1 is cheap to fix and an E discovered after the essay upload is not fixable at all. Ask your child's TOK teacher directly where the current work sits rather than reading the progress comment.

faqs.question: Which IA prompt should my daughter choose for the exhibition?
faqs.answer: The one that gives her the most to argue about with the objects she can actually find, not the one that sounds the most interesting. A good test is to try writing a single sentence linking a candidate object to the prompt; if the sentence is obvious or unarguable, the pairing will produce description rather than justification. A tutor can run that test with her across several prompts in one session. The choice itself stays hers, because the exhibition has to be her own work and the planning and progress form records how she arrived at it.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Dubai DP student usually book for TOK?
faqs.answer: Two patterns dominate. An exhibition block in DP1 tends to run four to six sessions, because the task is small and deadline-shaped. An essay intensive in DP2 tends to run six to ten, pacing the draft cycle from title choice to the final cut. Families who want steady work through both years book a weekly hour, which accumulates the thinking rather than cramming it. We quote the number the plan assumes before you pay, and the week-four review exists partly so that a block can be shortened when the student no longer needs it.

faqs.question: Can TOK sessions run after Iftar during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for exactly that. School days shorten during Ramadan and useful working energy moves to after Iftar, so sessions shift into post-Iftar slots for the month and the heaviest drafting is planned either side of it rather than through it. Because lessons are delivered online, moving a standing slot by three hours for four weeks is an administrative change rather than a scheduling problem. A tutor who has to drive across Dubai in the hour before Iftar cannot offer the same flexibility at any price.

faqs.question: What does a properly marked TOK draft look like when it comes back?
faqs.answer: It names what each paragraph is currently doing, names what the band above expects, and asks a question the student has to answer themselves. It does not contain rewritten sentences. On a typical first draft you would see comments like: this paragraph describes how historians work but makes no arguable claim, this example is from a news article rather than from your own subjects, this counter-argument arrives too late to change anything. Three specific observations a parent can read are worth more than a page of encouragement, and the comment history in a shared document means you can scroll back and see what changed.

faqs.question: Will my child's school mind us using an outside TOK tutor?
faqs.answer: Schools in Dubai are generally comfortable with it provided the work remains the student's own and the planning and progress form reflects what genuinely happened. Problems arise in one of two ways: a draft that improves by two bands overnight with no corresponding record, or a tutor who supplies material the student cannot explain. We work the other way round, keeping every version so the development of the argument is visible. Tell the TOK teacher that a tutor is reading drafts. In our experience that conversation makes the teacher's own feedback more useful, not less.

faqs.question: How should TOK connect to the Extended Essay subject my child has chosen?
faqs.answer: They are separate pieces of work and must not share content, but they share a skill and they share a points line. A student writing an Extended Essay in History already has a working sense of what counts as evidence for a historian, which is directly usable in the TOK essay as long as the examples themselves differ. The planning benefit is larger: because the matrix reads both grades together, the sensible question each term is which of the two is closer to the next band. That is the arithmetic a tutor should do before recommending any schedule.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay per hour for TOK support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market bands as of October 2026: budget online tutors advertise from AED 45-150, qualified subject tutors online run roughly AED 150-300, in-home visits run AED 180-500 with travel inside the rate, IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 or more, and premium tutors marketed on examiner experience reach AED 650. TOK sits at the specialist end whatever a headline rate suggests, because the pool of people who read it closely is small. Those are published competitor and market figures, not our prices; ours is quoted after the free trial, and ask any provider whether VAT is included before comparing numbers.

faqs.question: We are relocating to Dubai halfway through DP1. Can a tutor catch up the TOK course?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and mid-year transfers are one of the more common reasons families contact us. The practical problem is rarely content; it is that the previous school had begun the exhibition on a different prompt and the new school is further along its own internal calendar. The first session establishes where the new school's TOK sits, what the previous school's work can still be used for, and whether the exhibition needs restarting. The plan is then built backwards from the new school's deadline, which your DP coordinator can confirm in a single email.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Dubai for TOK lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For TOK that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: the session is two people reading the same paragraph in a shared document, the pool of specialist readers is no longer limited to people who can drive to your community, and the version history becomes the evidence trail. If you specifically need an adult physically present, this is not the right service and we would rather say so now.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-home-tut.closingHeading: Start with one marked draft, then decide
dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-home-tut.closingBody: The useful next step is small. Send your child's current exhibition commentary or essay draft and book the free trial lesson. Sixty minutes later you will have a written diagnosis naming the band the draft sits in, the two changes that would move it, and an honest view on whether a tutor is needed at all or whether the student simply needs to rewrite the second half themselves. Some families stop there, which is a fine outcome. If you continue, the plan is built backwards from your school's internal TOK deadline and you will see it before paying anything. Bring the real draft, not a description of it.

Each one works from the published assessment instruments rather than from general advice, scores the student's own writing against them, and keeps the scores so a family can see which strand of the instrument is moving.

intro.heading: Two short pieces of writing, one grade, and no textbook to revise
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge sits in the Diploma core alongside the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, and it is unlike every other course a Dubai student takes. There is no syllabus content to learn, no past paper to work through, and no body of facts that revision can cover. The grade comes from two short pieces of written work: an exhibition of three objects with commentaries totalling no more than 950 words, and an essay of no more than 1,600 words on one of six prescribed titles released for the session.

That structure produces a predictable failure pattern. Because nothing is due for a long time and nothing can be revised, TOK slides to the bottom of every Diploma student's list, behind six subjects with dated deadlines. The student attends lessons, finds the discussions interesting, writes nothing, and then discovers in the spring of Year 13 that the essay is three weeks away and they have never written a paragraph that an examiner would recognise as a TOK paragraph. Nothing about their intelligence caused that; the incentive structure did.

The second thing families underestimate is what the grade is worth. TOK and the Extended Essay together can contribute up to three points to the Diploma total through a published matrix, and a grade of E in either is a failing condition for the Diploma itself. A student sitting on 38 points is not short of a subject; they are often short of the two core points that a term of deliberate TOK work would have produced. Three points is the difference between several university offers.

So this page is built around evidence rather than discussion. Every piece of work a student produces in TOK can be scored against the published assessment instrument for that task, strand by strand, and that score can be recorded with a date. Over a term the pattern of those scores shows whether the student is actually learning to do the thing the instrument rewards, or simply having better conversations. Conversations are enjoyable and they do not produce marks on their own.

Delivery is online. IB Gram matches Dubai families with one-to-one tutors over live video, with the student's own drafts open on a shared screen and annotated as they are discussed. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. TOK is particularly well suited to this, because the work is reading, thinking and writing, and the single most valuable thing a tutor does is read a draft closely and score it honestly against the instrument. Nothing in that depends on being in the same room, and a shared document means both people are looking at the same sentence when a strand of the instrument is named.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-online-t.programmesIntro: TOK belongs to the Diploma core, but the thinking it assesses is built earlier in the IB continuum. Where a Dubai student came from explains a good deal about which part of TOK they find hard.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: TOK runs across both Diploma years as a core requirement rather than as a seventh subject. It is organised around a core theme on knowledge and the knower, optional themes the school selects, and five areas of knowledge. Assessment is the exhibition and the essay, and the final grade runs from A to E.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma timetables carry six subjects, the core and the emirate's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies requirements. TOK typically gets one timetabled lesson a week in that squeeze, which is enough for discussion and rarely enough for supervised writing, and the writing is what carries the grade.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP has no TOK course, but its interdisciplinary units and its emphasis on concepts over content build the habit of asking how a claim is known rather than only what it says. Students arriving in the Diploma from a full MYP usually find TOK's framing familiar even when they find its assessment strange.
programmes.countryNote: Students transferring into a Dubai Diploma from IGCSE or from CBSE have usually never been assessed on anything resembling TOK. That is not a disadvantage in ability, only in orientation, and it means the first few weeks should be spent on what the instrument rewards rather than on the themes themselves.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The other two core elements. The Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece in a chosen subject, and CAS is a non-assessed experiential requirement. The Extended Essay grade combines with the TOK grade in the points matrix, which is why the two are planned together rather than separately.
programmes.countryNote: In most Dubai schools the Extended Essay and TOK deadlines fall within a few weeks of each other in Year 13, and both land near mock examinations. A student who plans one without the other ends up producing both badly in the same fortnight, which is the most common way the core points are lost in this market.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP does not include TOK. It has its own core, including a reflective project and personal and professional skills, which ask related questions about ethics and evidence in a vocational setting rather than across areas of knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of Dubai schools licensed for the Diploma also offer the CP. Families comparing the two should know that the core requirements differ substantially, and that a CP reflective project is not a TOK essay with a different name.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-online-t.subjectsIntro: TOK draws its examples from whatever a student is already studying, which makes the subject combination directly relevant. The list below is how Dubai students most often use their own subjects as TOK material.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an exhibition of three objects with commentaries to 950 words and an essay to 1,600 words on a prescribed title. Marks come from how precisely a student handles knowledge questions, not from how much they know.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The richest source of TOK examples for most students, because evidence, selection and interpretation are explicit in the subject. A History student who already argues about sources has half the equipment the essay instrument rewards.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Useful for questions about method, replication and the status of a model. Students often lean on Biology for the natural sciences area of knowledge and then describe the content rather than examining how the knowledge was established.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Mathematics is the area of knowledge students find hardest to write about, because proof feels like certainty and the interesting TOK questions are about axioms, definitions and applicability. Handled well, it is where the strongest essays distinguish themselves.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A productive human sciences example, with models that are simultaneously useful and unrealistic. The commentaries students write in Economics also build the habit of applying a framework to a specific case, which the essay requires.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Strong material for the arts as an area of knowledge and particularly for object selection in the exhibition, since Visual Arts students are practised at explaining why a particular object carries a particular meaning.

subjects.name: English A: language and literature
subjects.description: The analytical writing closest to TOK in form. Students who write tight English commentaries usually need only the instrument explained; students who write expansively need to learn that 1,600 words punishes digression severely.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Full of methodological questions a TOK essay can use, from replication to the ethics of what may be studied. The risk is importing Psychology essay structure wholesale, which answers a different kind of question.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Widely taken in Dubai cohorts and a reliable source of ethics and decision-making examples. Objects drawn from a family business or a local market work well in the exhibition because the student knows them specifically.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools for students who are not Arab nationals under KHDA rules. It occupies a timetable slot and, usefully, gives students direct experience of how language shapes what can be expressed, which is a live TOK theme.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-online-t.regionsIntro: Matching is on the course rather than on the address, but a TOK plan still has to fit the week a family actually has. The notes below describe when a session and a drafting block can realistically sit.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: Villa communities with moderate commutes and a high proportion of Diploma students at nearby schools. Sessions from 17:00 work well, and the quiet weekend morning hour these households tend to have is the best drafting slot in the week.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Apartment living with very short runs to the surrounding schools, so a 16:00 start is usually feasible. The constraint here is a quiet room for sustained writing rather than travel, which matters more in TOK than in a subject with worksheets.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: Newer towers with longer runs to the established Diploma schools and limited local senior provision. Later sessions after 18:00 hold better across a term, and the essay drafting tends to happen on Fridays.

regions.name: Arjan and Dubailand Residence Complex
regions.note: Growing apartment communities where bus journeys can exceed an hour each way in term time. Short twice-monthly sessions around draft deadlines often serve better here than a weekly slot that keeps being missed.

regions.name: Mira and Reem
regions.note: Suburban villa catchments with heavy co-curricular loading on weekday afternoons. Families generally settle on a single weekday evening, which suits the TOK cycle of writing a section, having it scored, and rewriting it.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and Knowledge Park
regions.note: Short commutes to several long-established international schools and a dense Diploma population. Students here frequently have late free periods, so mid-afternoon sessions are sometimes workable after mock examinations finish.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Spread-out communities on the western edge with long school runs and smaller Diploma cohorts locally. Online matching changes the available choice most here, since a TOK specialist nearby is improbable.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai, from Al Barsha to Al Quoz
schoolClusters.note: The heaviest concentration of Diploma provision in the emirate, where most schools run TOK with one timetabled lesson a week. Students here have company in the subject, which helps with discussion and not at all with the writing.

schoolClusters.city: Southern Dubai and Dubai Investments Park
schoolClusters.note: Newer continuum schools with Diploma cohorts that have grown cohort by cohort. Smaller TOK groups mean a student who is struggling is visible, and also that the teacher has less capacity for individual draft work.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern Dubai, from Mirdif to Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: A mix of IB, American and Indian-curriculum provision, with Diploma students often transferring in from other systems. Those students meet TOK with no prior experience of anything resembling it, which is an orientation problem rather than an ability one.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-online-t.modesIntro: TOK support comes in three shapes depending on where in the two years a family arrives. All three run one-to-one over live video with drafts annotated on a shared screen.

modes.title: Exhibition build, Year 12
modes.description: For students approaching the first assessed task. Sessions start from the chosen IA prompt, test candidate objects against it, and then work each commentary so that it does the three things the instrument asks rather than describing the object. The 950-word limit is treated as a design constraint from the first draft.

modes.title: Essay cycle, Year 13
modes.description: For students working towards the externally assessed essay. The prescribed title is analysed word by word before any planning, the argument is built around knowledge questions rather than topics, and each section is scored against the essay instrument as it is written rather than at the end.

modes.description: For students who have left both tasks late and need a realistic plan rather than reassurance. Sessions triage: what can still be rescued, in what order, with the Extended Essay deadline and mocks mapped alongside. Honest about what is recoverable and what is not.

sections.heading: Why TOK is the subject Dubai families search for last
paragraphs: The pattern is consistent enough to describe in advance. A Dubai Diploma student spends Year 12 with one TOK lesson a week, enjoys the discussions, and writes very little, because nothing in TOK has the dated, visible urgency of a Chemistry internal assessment or an Economics commentary. Their report says they contribute thoughtfully. Then the exhibition deadline arrives, the student produces 950 words in a weekend, and the mark comes back far below what their contributions suggested.

The reason is that TOK assesses a specific kind of writing, and discussion does not teach it. A student can hold an excellent spoken view about whether mathematical knowledge is discovered or invented and still write a commentary that describes an object for 300 words without ever connecting it to the chosen prompt. The instrument rewards the connection, not the view. That is learnable and it is almost never learned by talking.

There is also a diagnosis problem. In most subjects a parent can tell whether work is happening by looking for completed exercises. TOK has no exercises, so the household signal is absent, and a student can go five months without producing a paragraph while appearing to be engaged. By the time the absence becomes visible, the remaining calendar is short and the Extended Essay deadline is sitting in the same fortnight.

Which is why this page argues for scored writing from the start. One short piece every week or two, scored against the published instrument for the relevant task, with the score written down. It produces the signal that TOK structurally lacks, it turns a vague subject into a measurable one, and it means a problem in November is a problem with five months of runway instead of a crisis in April.

Discussion ability and writing ability come apart in this subject

sections.heading: The two tasks, the word limits and where the marks sit
paragraphs: TOK is assessed through two tasks and nothing else. The exhibition asks the student to select three objects, connect them to one of the prescribed internal assessment prompts, and write a commentary on each explaining how it shows TOK manifesting in the world. The total across all three commentaries is capped at 950 words. It is marked inside the school against a single published instrument and then externally moderated by the IB.

The essay is externally assessed. The student writes to a maximum of 1,600 words on one of the six prescribed titles released by the IB for that examination session, and the title must be used exactly as published without alteration. It is marked against a single global instrument rather than against separate criteria, which has a practical consequence: there is no strand to pick up marks in if the central argument does not engage the title.

Both word limits are hard rather than advisory, and they shape the writing more than students expect. At 950 words across three commentaries, a student has roughly 300 words per object, which allows for identification, connection and a specific point and allows for nothing else. At 1,600 words, an essay has room for a clear position, two developed areas of knowledge, genuine counter-argument and a conclusion, and no room for a general introduction about the nature of human curiosity.

The table sets out both tasks with their limits and weightings. The point of reading it early is that the limits are a design brief: the plan has to be built to the word budget, not written freely and then cut, because cutting a finished piece removes the specifics and leaves the generalities, which is the opposite of what both instruments reward.

sections.heading: What a TOK grade is actually worth in the Diploma total
paragraphs: TOK is not a seventh subject and it does not produce a grade out of seven. It produces a letter from A to E, and that letter combines with the Extended Essay letter in a published matrix to award up to three points on top of the twenty-four available from six subjects. Those three points sit at the top of the Diploma total, where university offers are decided, which makes them disproportionately valuable relative to the hours they cost.

The matrix also contains a hard floor. A grade of E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma as a whole, regardless of how strong the six subject grades are. That is the single most important fact on this page for a family whose child has not started either task. A student with excellent subject grades and an unwritten core is not slightly behind; they are at risk of not receiving the Diploma.

Understood properly, the matrix changes how a family allocates the last six months. A student at a B in TOK and a C in the Extended Essay who can move one of those letters gains a point for a few weeks of focused work, which is usually cheaper than moving a subject grade from a 5 to a 6. Core work is the most efficient point in the Diploma, and it is also the one most students have left latest.

The matrix below is widely published and reproduced here to show the shape of the trade-offs. Confirm the current version with your school's IB coordinator before planning around a specific cell, because the IB updates its documentation and the coordinator holds the authoritative version for your child's session.

sections.heading: The prescribed title: six choices and a wording that cannot be touched
paragraphs: The IB releases six prescribed titles for each examination session, and the student chooses one. The title must be used exactly as published, without rewording, narrowing or combining. Students regularly try to improve a title, usually by making it more specific so it feels easier to answer, and the result is an essay that answers a question the examiner was not given. That is the most expensive single error available in this task.

Choosing well matters more than students realise, and the choice should not be made on which title sounds most interesting. The useful test is whether the student can name, within ten minutes, two areas of knowledge they could write about specifically, with real examples they already know from their own subjects. A title that produces enthusiasm and no examples will produce 1,600 words of abstraction. A title that produces two concrete examples immediately will produce an essay.

The analysis that follows the choice is slow and worth doing properly. Each significant term in the title needs unpacking: what it could mean, which readings are defensible, which reading the student will adopt and why. A title containing a word like certainty, or bias, or reliable, is asking for that word to be examined rather than used. Students who skip this step write essays that assume the meaning of the term the title was built around.

Only after that does planning begin, and the plan should name the knowledge question, the position taken, the two areas of knowledge used, the specific examples in each, and where the counter-argument sits. A plan at that level of specificity can be scored against the essay instrument before a paragraph is written, which is the cheapest possible moment to find out that an argument does not engage the title.

sections.heading: The exhibition: three objects, one prompt, 950 words
paragraphs: The exhibition is the first assessed task and the one students approach most casually, usually because it sounds like a display rather than a piece of analytical writing. It is analytical writing. The student picks one of the prescribed internal assessment prompts, selects three objects, and writes a commentary on each that identifies the object, places it in a real-world context, and shows how it connects to the prompt. The instrument rewards that connection and almost nothing else.

Object selection decides most of the mark before any writing happens. The requirement that trips students is specificity: the object must be a particular object with a presence in the world, not a category. A photograph taken at a particular moment, a specific edition of a specific book, a particular item from a family's history. Students who choose a type of thing rather than a thing find there is nothing concrete to say, and then fill the words with general reflection.

The second selection error is choosing three objects that make the same point. Three objects that all illustrate the same aspect of the prompt waste two thirds of the task, because each commentary then repeats the previous one with new scenery. Good sets of three approach the prompt from different directions, which also solves the word budget problem: each commentary has a distinct job and therefore a natural shape at around 300 words.

The word budget should be allocated before writing, not discovered afterwards. Roughly 300 words per object, with identification short, context brief and specific, and the connection to the prompt occupying most of the space. Students who write freely and then cut almost always cut the specifics, because specifics take words, and the result is a commentary that is shorter and vaguer than the draft it came from.

sections.heading: The one permitted draft, and what a tutor may legitimately do
paragraphs: TOK has a rule that shapes how outside support can honestly work. The teacher's written feedback on the essay is limited to a single draft, after which further comment is not permitted. The exact wording and scope of that rule is held by your school's IB coordinator and should be confirmed with them, but the principle matters regardless of the detail: the student gets one round of formal teacher comment, and spending it on a draft that is structurally wrong is a waste of the only round available.

That is where a tutor's role is both legitimate and useful. Work on the title analysis, the knowledge question, the plan and the argument map happens before the draft exists, so the draft that reaches the teacher is a reasonable one rather than a first attempt. A student who arrives at the one permitted draft with a sound structure gets feedback on execution; a student who arrives with a topic-based essay gets feedback on structure and has nothing left to use it on.

What a tutor must not do is the writing. The IB requires that submitted work is the candidate's own, and that applies to a core task as firmly as to a subject internal assessment. No tutor supplies paragraphs for submission, rewrites a section into prose the student could not have built, or hands over an argument to be reproduced. The tutor reads, scores against the instrument, names what the instrument wanted and did not get, and the student writes the next version.

The same boundary applies to machine-generated text, which in this subject is a particular temptation because abstract prose about knowledge is exactly what a language model produces easily. It is also what examiners read all day and recognise quickly: fluent, balanced, and empty of the specific examples the instrument rewards. A student who submits it has not only taken a malpractice risk, they have submitted the weakest kind of TOK essay there is.

sections.heading: Evidence of movement: scoring drafts against the instrument
paragraphs: The angle of this page is evidence, and in TOK that means something specific. Both tasks have a published assessment instrument, and any piece of student writing, including a plan and a single paragraph, can be read against it. A tutor who does that produces a score with a date. A tutor who says the paragraph is a good start produces nothing. The difference over a term is the difference between a measurable project and a pleasant conversation.

What the record looks like in practice is a short list: the date, what the student produced, the score against the instrument, and the one thing to change next. A student whose scores sit flat for three weeks on the same strand has a specific problem, usually that their examples are not doing argumentative work. A student whose scores move after the plan is rebuilt has learned something that will transfer to the essay. Neither of those is visible without the record.

This also addresses a genuine difficulty for parents. TOK is the one Diploma element where a family often cannot tell good work from bad, because the subject's vocabulary is unfamiliar and a confident paragraph about knowledge can be hollow. A score against a published instrument, with the strand named, gives a non-specialist something to hold. It also makes it obvious when a student has stopped producing work, which in TOK is the usual failure.

The table below sets out a workable sequence across the two years. It is indicative rather than a timetable, because school deadlines differ, and the useful property is the order: short scored pieces early, the exhibition banked in Year 12, the title analysed before planning, the plan scored before drafting, and the one permitted teacher draft spent on something worth commenting on.

sections.heading: Fitting TOK into a Dubai Diploma year
paragraphs: TOK competes for time with six subjects that all have dated deadlines, and it loses that competition by default because it has the fewest hard dates. Planning it realistically therefore means planning against the rest of the year rather than in isolation. In most Dubai schools the exhibition sits in Year 12, the essay process runs through the first half of Year 13, and the Extended Essay final deadline lands within a few weeks of the essay, often beside mock examinations.

The Dubai calendar adds its own features. Ramadan shortens the school day and drains the late afternoon, so a student who intends to draft at 17:00 during that month will not, and the realistic move is a post-Iftar slot or a weekend morning. Long winter and spring breaks are where the core work can genuinely be done, provided a specific target is set before the break starts rather than a general intention to catch up.

One honest caution about dates. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session, submission or results date in this project is confirmed, and none is published here. Your school's IB coordinator holds the real internal deadlines for the exhibition, the essay and the Extended Essay, and those internal dates are the ones that govern a student's life. Ask for them in writing at the start of Year 12 and build the plan from them.

The practical shape that works is unexciting. Bank the exhibition in Year 12 so Year 13 holds one task rather than two. Analyse the title before the autumn half term of Year 13. Have a scored plan before December and a scored full draft before the one permitted teacher draft is submitted. Leave the final term for cutting carefully and for the five subjects that have examinations, because by then TOK should be finished.

process.title: Find out which task is live and when it is due
process.description: The first conversation establishes whether the exhibition or the essay is the immediate task, which IA prompt or prescribed title the student is considering, and what the school's internal deadlines are. Those dates govern everything, and most families do not have them written down.

process.title: Free trial with a scored piece of writing
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken. The student brings any TOK writing they have, or produces two short paragraphs in the session, and the tutor scores it against the published instrument for the relevant task. You see a score and a named strand, not an impression.

process.title: Build the plan before the prose
process.description: For the essay, the title is unpacked term by term and an argument map is built naming the knowledge question, the position, the two areas of knowledge and their specific examples. For the exhibition, objects are tested against the prompt. Both are scored before writing begins.

process.title: Short scored pieces, every week or two
process.description: Each piece of writing is read against the instrument and recorded with a date, a score and the one thing to change. That record is the signal TOK structurally lacks, and it makes a flat strand visible in November rather than in April.

process.title: Protect the one permitted teacher draft
process.description: We work so that the draft reaching the teacher is structurally sound, because formal teacher comment is limited and spending it on a misdirected essay wastes it. Confirm the current rule with your IB coordinator; we plan around their answer.

whyPoints.title: Work is scored, not praised
whyPoints.description: Every piece of student writing is read against the published assessment instrument for the task, with the score and the named strand recorded and dated. In a subject with no exercises and no past papers, that record is the only honest signal of progress.

whyPoints.title: The core points are treated as points
whyPoints.description: TOK and the Extended Essay together can add up to three points to a Diploma total, and an E in either is a failing condition. Moving a core letter is usually cheaper than moving a subject grade, and we plan the two together rather than separately.

whyPoints.title: Planning before prose
whyPoints.description: Most lost marks in this subject are decided before a paragraph is written: a title answered as a topic, or three objects that make one point. Scoring a plan against the instrument is the cheapest moment to find that out.

whyPoints.title: The draft rule is respected and used
whyPoints.description: Formal teacher feedback on the essay is limited, so the draft that reaches the teacher should be worth commenting on. We work before that point, and we ask you to confirm the current rule with your school's IB coordinator.

whyPoints.title: Matched on TOK specifically
whyPoints.description: TOK is not a subject any graduate can supervise; it has two instruments and a particular kind of writing. Live video means the match is made on experience of this course rather than on who is available in your community.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed authority, no promised grades
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB. We publish no IB dates we cannot verify, promise no letter grade, and state the line on assessed work before the first session.

faqs.question: What is Theory of Knowledge and why does it have no textbook?
faqs.answer: TOK is part of the Diploma core rather than a seventh subject, and it examines how knowledge is produced and justified across different areas rather than teaching a body of content. That is why there is nothing to revise: the grade comes from two short pieces of written work, an exhibition of three objects with commentaries to 950 words and an essay to 1,600 words on a prescribed title. The practical consequence is that TOK rewards a particular kind of writing, which discussion alone does not teach. Students who produce scored writing regularly from Year 12 do well; students who only talk about ideas generally do not.

faqs.question: How many Diploma points can TOK add to my child's total?
faqs.answer: TOK combines with the Extended Essay in a published matrix that awards up to three points on top of the twenty-four available from six subjects. Those points sit at the top of the total, where university offers are decided, so they carry weight out of proportion to the hours they cost. The matrix also has a floor: a grade of E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma regardless of subject grades. Confirm the current matrix with your school's IB coordinator before planning around a specific combination, since the coordinator holds the authoritative version for the session.

faqs.question: Can the wording of a prescribed title be adjusted to suit my child's interests?
faqs.answer: No. The six prescribed titles are released by the IB for each session and must be used exactly as published, without rewording, narrowing or combining. Students commonly try to make a title more specific so it feels more answerable, and the result is an essay answering a question the examiner never set, which is the most expensive error available in this task. The better approach is to choose the title that produces concrete examples fastest. If a student cannot name two areas of knowledge with specific examples within ten minutes, that title will produce abstraction rather than argument.

faqs.question: How should my child choose the three objects for the exhibition?
faqs.answer: On specificity and distinctness. Each object must be a particular object with a presence in the world rather than a category: a photograph taken at a known moment, a specific edition of a specific book, a particular item with a known history. A type of thing gives a student nothing concrete to say, and the commentary fills with general reflection. The second rule is that the three should approach the prompt from different directions, because three objects making the same point waste two thirds of the task and produce three commentaries that repeat each other with new scenery.

faqs.question: Is 950 words really enough for three commentaries?
faqs.answer: It is enough if the word budget is allocated before writing rather than discovered afterwards. Roughly 300 words per object works out as short identification, brief and specific context, and most of the space given to an explicit argument about how the object shows the prompt operating. Students who write freely and then cut almost always remove the specifics, because specifics cost words, and they end with something shorter and vaguer than the draft. Treating the limit as a design brief from the first outline is the single habit that most improves exhibition marks.

faqs.question: Why did my child get a low TOK mark when they contribute brilliantly in class?
faqs.answer: Because the two assessed tasks reward a kind of writing that discussion does not build. A student can hold a genuinely interesting spoken view and still write a commentary that describes an object for 300 words without connecting it to the prompt, or an essay that discusses a topic the title mentions without engaging the question the title asks. The instrument rewards the connection and the engagement, not the quality of the opinion. The remedy is scored short writing, every week or two, read against the published instrument so the gap between thinking well and writing to the instrument becomes visible early.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or rewrite part of the essay?
faqs.answer: No, and a service offering it is selling a malpractice risk that falls on your child rather than on them. The IB requires submitted work to be the candidate's own. What a tutor legitimately does is read, score against the published instrument, name what the instrument wanted and did not receive, and set the next version for the student to produce. In this subject the ethical line and the effective line coincide: being handed a paragraph teaches nothing, and the examiners who read these essays recognise prose that the student could not have built.

faqs.question: How does the one-draft rule affect using a tutor?
faqs.answer: Formal written teacher feedback on the essay is limited to a single draft, so that round is a scarce resource. The implication is about sequencing rather than permission. Work on title analysis, the knowledge question, the argument map and the specific examples happens before a draft exists, so the draft reaching the teacher is structurally sound and the feedback can address execution. A student who uses that round on a topic-based first attempt receives structural comment with nothing left to apply it to. Confirm the exact current rule with your school's IB coordinator and plan from their answer.

faqs.question: When should my child start the TOK essay?
faqs.answer: The title analysis should be done before the autumn half term of Year 13, with a scored plan by December and a scored full draft before the one permitted teacher draft is submitted. The reason for working that far ahead is the collision: in most Dubai schools the essay deadline sits within a few weeks of the Extended Essay deadline, and mock examinations are usually in the same window. A student who starts in the spring is producing their two most valuable pieces of core work during the worst fortnight of the two years. Ask your coordinator for the internal dates in writing at the start of Year 12.

faqs.question: Do you provide a TOK tutor who visits our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. Theory of Knowledge support for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video, with the student's own drafts open on a shared screen and annotated while they are discussed. TOK suits this arrangement unusually well, because the work is reading, thinking and writing, and the most valuable thing a tutor does is read a draft closely and score it against the instrument, which happens identically on a shared document.

faqs.question: Can a student use artificial intelligence to help with TOK writing?
faqs.answer: Not for producing text that will be submitted, on two grounds. The IB requires submitted work to be the candidate's own, and supplied content is malpractice with consequences that land on the student. The second reason is that it produces bad TOK: fluent, balanced prose about knowledge with no specific examples doing argumentative work, which is exactly what the instruments do not reward and what examiners recognise within a paragraph. Using a tool to find a source to read, or to check a word count, is a different activity from having it generate an argument, and your school will have its own published policy.

faqs.question: What does a scored TOK record actually look like?
faqs.answer: A short list with four columns: the date, what the student produced, the score against the published instrument for that task, and the one thing to change next. Over a term it shows whether a particular strand is moving. A record that sits flat for three weeks on the same strand usually means the student's examples are decorative rather than argumentative, which is a specific, fixable problem. The record also gives a non-specialist parent something to hold in a subject where a confident-sounding paragraph can be hollow, and it makes a student who has quietly stopped writing immediately visible.

faqs.question: Is it too late to improve a TOK grade in the final term of Year 13?
faqs.answer: Something can usually be improved and nobody should promise a letter. What the final term allows is careful cutting, protecting specifics and removing generalities, plus making sure the word count and the title wording are exactly right. What it does not allow is rebuilding an argument that does not engage the title, because that needs a new plan and a new draft. If both core tasks are unstarted in the final term, the honest conversation is about the failing-condition floor rather than about points, and it should involve the IB coordinator immediately rather than a tutor alone.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a licence from the authorities?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services system, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: What if no TOK specialist is available when we get in touch?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a timeframe, rather than placing a general humanities graduate. TOK is not a subject anyone can supervise competently: it has two published instruments, a prescribed-title convention and a particular kind of writing, and a tutor who has not worked with those will produce interesting conversations and no mark movement. The options we would put to a family are a short wait for a named tutor, or a focused block on whichever task is nearest. If the deadline is immediate and nobody suitable is free, the right advice is usually to work with the school's coordinator instead.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-online-t.closingBody: If your child is in a Dubai Diploma and TOK has quietly produced nothing in writing yet, the useful first step is a score rather than a reassurance. Book the free trial lesson, one per family and no card details required. The student brings whatever TOK writing exists, or produces two short paragraphs in the hour, and the tutor reads it against the published instrument for the relevant task and names the strand that is missing. You will see a score, a date and one thing to change, which is the signal this subject structurally lacks and the only honest basis for deciding what to do next.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below coach TOK as an assessed component rather than as a discussion class. Each has marked exhibition commentaries and essays against the IB bands, and works from the prescribed title your child has actually been given.

intro.heading: Why a discussion course ends up being the thing a Dubai Diploma student is stuck on
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is the only part of the Diploma with no syllabus content to revise. There are no topics to cover, no past papers to drill and no formulae. What there is instead is a pair of assessed tasks with narrow technical requirements: an exhibition of three objects with a commentary of no more than 950 words, and an essay of no more than 1,600 words written to one of six prescribed titles issued for the session. Both are marked out of ten. Together they decide a TOK grade from A to E.

That structure catches out the students Dubai schools least expect. Strong science and mathematics students are often the ones who stall, because they have been rewarded for two years for giving the right answer and TOK rewards examining how an answer came to be accepted. Equally, articulate students who enjoy the classroom debate frequently hand in work that reads well and scores in the middle, because enjoying the discussion is not the same as meeting the marking instrument.

The grade matters more than most families assume. TOK and the Extended Essay are combined on a published matrix that awards up to three points towards the 45-point Diploma total, and a grade E in either is a failing condition for the Diploma regardless of how strong the six subject grades are. A student sitting on 38 points with an E in TOK does not have 38 points. That is the single most useful thing to know early in DP1, and it is the reason TOK enquiries from Dubai parents arrive in a hurry in the final term rather than calmly in the first.

What coaching does here is narrow. A tutor cannot teach TOK content because there is none. A tutor can take a prescribed title apart, show what its key terms commit the writer to, check whether a chosen object is specific enough to carry a commentary, press on a claim until the student finds the counter-claim themselves, and mark a draft against the band descriptors so the student can see which band they are writing in. That is a short list, and it is enough to move most students one band.

IB Gram works as a matching platform. Tell us the task, the stage and the deadline — exhibition in DP1 with objects not yet chosen, or essay in DP2 with a title selected and a first draft written — and we propose a TOK specialist and run a free trial lesson, one per family, with no card details taken. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. TOK is a subject where that works well, because the whole lesson is argument, annotation and questioning on a shared screen.
