dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.programmesIntro: The critical-thinking core looks different in each IB programme, and the jump into TOK is sharper for some Dubai students than others. These are the stages we cover and what the core component demands at each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge runs across both Diploma years with a recommended 100 teaching hours. Students complete the exhibition, usually in DP1, and the essay in DP2. The exhibition asks them to show how TOK manifests in the world through three specific objects; the essay asks them to answer a prescribed title using the areas of knowledge. Neither task has a content syllabus to revise.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts are large and TOK classes are often timetabled in a single weekly period shared between two teachers. That arrangement works for the discussion and poorly for individual draft feedback, which is where most of our Dubai TOK enquiries originate rather than from a lack of ideas.

programmes.name: TOK with the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The three core components are assessed differently and compete for the same hours. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word piece of independent research; TOK is two short, technically constrained tasks; CAS is an unassessed completion requirement with its own portfolio. TOK and the EE are the two that carry points, and they are graded on the same A-E scale before being combined.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools tend to stack internal core deadlines between November and February, which means a TOK essay draft, an EE final submission and a CAS interview can land in the same fortnight. Families who book TOK support around that window rather than in April get a better result for fewer hours.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP has no TOK, but it does build the habits TOK assesses: interdisciplinary units, the personal project, and criterion-based marking that rewards justification over recall. Students who learned to write to criteria in MYP usually find the TOK marking instrument legible. Students arriving from content-and-recall systems often meet criterion-based marking for the first time in TOK.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a substantial IB continuum population and an even larger British-curriculum population arriving at Diploma level from IGCSE. The second group is the one that needs the marking instrument explained before the first draft, not after it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The IB Career-related Programme replaces TOK with its own core: personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and the reflective project. The reflective project asks for an ethical dilemma connected to the career-related study, and the thinking it rewards overlaps with TOK closely enough that the same coaching approach applies.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of Dubai schools run the CP alongside the Diploma. Families sometimes approach us for TOK help when the component their child is actually sitting is the reflective project, so the first question we ask is which programme is on the registration.

dubai/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.subjectsIntro: TOK is examined through the areas of knowledge, so a TOK session constantly borrows from the subjects your child is already taking. These are the subjects that come up most in Dubai TOK work, and what each contributes.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The focus of this page. Two tasks, both marked out of ten against a global impression instrument: the exhibition with its 950-word commentary and the essay with its 1,600-word limit. Marks are lost on vagueness, on objects or examples that could be swapped for any other, and on titles answered loosely.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Graded on the same scale and combined with TOK for up to three points. Students who have worked on an EE research question are usually faster at unpacking a TOK prescribed title, because both tasks punish a question answered approximately. The EE criteria reward critical thinking most heavily, as TOK does.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The area of knowledge that gives TOK students the cleanest examples: competing accounts, selection of evidence, the problem of writing about events nobody present agreed on. A history student who can name a specific historiographical disagreement has a TOK essay example that cannot be swapped for a generic one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Useful in TOK for the gap between a model and the thing modelled, and for how a scientific claim becomes accepted. Biology students often need help moving from the method to the knowledge question, because their instinct is to explain the science rather than examine how it came to be trusted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The area of knowledge that makes TOK essays sharper or vaguer than any other. Proof, axioms and the question of whether mathematics is discovered or constructed are genuinely interesting, and also the fastest route to an essay full of borrowed phrases. We insist on a worked example from the student's own course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Human sciences examples travel well in TOK: assumptions built into a model, data that cannot be gathered without changing what is measured, predictions that fail without invalidating the theory. Dubai students taking Economics HL usually have strong material here and underuse it.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The arts as an area of knowledge is where exhibition objects most often come from, and where students are most tempted by an object that is merely interesting. A Visual Arts student can usually justify an object's provenance precisely, which is exactly what the commentary needs.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The subject that most improves TOK writing mechanically. A 1,600-word limit rewards economy, and students who have learned to cut in their Language A essays write tighter TOK prose. The overlap in skill is in handling a claim and its counter-claim without hedging.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Supplies TOK examples about method and interpretation: replication, sampling, the influence of the researcher on the result. Psychology students sometimes import study names as decoration, and the coaching work is making one study earn its place in the argument.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Feeds the optional TOK theme on knowledge and politics directly. Students taking it tend to produce the most specific exhibition objects, because they are already used to treating a document, a statement or an image as a piece of evidence with a context.

sections.heading: What a TOK tutor is allowed to do, and what nobody should offer
paragraphs: This is the right place to start on a TOK page, because the market for this component is the dirtiest in UAE tutoring. The exhibition commentary and the essay are both the student's own work, submitted under the IB's academic honesty rules, and a submission that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter with consequences that reach the Diploma itself. One site ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Treat any offer to supply a TOK essay, to draft a commentary, or to rewrite a draft to completion as a reason to leave.

What a tutor may legitimately do is still substantial. They may take a prescribed title apart and show what each key term commits the writer to. They may question a claim until the student finds the obvious objection to it themselves. They may ask where an example came from and why no other example would do. They may mark a draft against the published band descriptors and name the band it sits in. They may teach how to hold an argument inside 1,600 words. None of that involves writing a sentence that will be submitted.

The practical test we use is simple: at the end of a session, could the student explain every change they are about to make, and why it earns marks? If the answer is no, the session was the tutor's work rather than the student's. We write the boundary into the match, and our tutors return drafts with questions and band judgements rather than with replacement text.

Your child's school is part of this. The TOK teacher sets internal deadlines, marks the exhibition and submits the essay, and they should know a tutor is involved. Nothing about one-to-one coaching needs to be hidden, and a coordinator who knows will usually tell you exactly which stage the student is behind on.
bullets: Both TOK tasks are submitted as the student's own work under IB academic honesty rules

sections.heading: The two TOK tasks, and how each one is marked
paragraphs: TOK is assessed through exactly two pieces of work. The exhibition asks the student to select three objects, link them to one of the prescribed internal assessment prompts, and write a commentary of no more than 950 words explaining how each object manifests TOK in the world. It is marked by the school against a single marking instrument out of ten and then moderated by the IB. The essay asks the student to answer one of six prescribed titles issued for their examination session, in no more than 1,600 words, and it is marked externally out of ten.

The split in weight is two to one in the essay's favour, which is not how most students allocate their effort. The exhibition arrives first, usually in DP1, feels more creative, and absorbs a great deal of time choosing objects. The essay arrives in DP2 in the middle of the heaviest coursework period of the Diploma and is frequently written in a fortnight. Reversing that allocation is one of the cheapest grade improvements available in the whole programme.

Both tasks are marked on a global impression against band descriptors rather than by adding up points for features. That is why a student can produce work that is fluent, well-organised and correctly referenced and still sit in the middle. The instrument asks whether the discussion is clear, coherent, well-evidenced and convincing, and a commentary that describes three objects beautifully without justifying their inclusion does not satisfy it. The fastest route to a better mark is reading the descriptors with the student in front of their own draft.

Word limits are hard limits and examiners are not obliged to reward what falls beyond them. A 1,900-word essay is not a longer essay; it is a 1,600-word essay with its conclusion missing. We treat the limit as a design constraint from the first plan rather than as a problem to solve by cutting adjectives at the end.

sections.heading: The three bonus points, and the grade E that fails a Diploma
paragraphs: TOK and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E, and the two grades are combined on a published matrix that awards up to three points towards the 45-point Diploma total. Those three points are the difference between an offer and a near miss often enough that the matrix deserves to be on the kitchen wall in DP1. Two A grades give three points. An A and a C give two. Two C grades give one. Two D grades give none.

The more important part of the matrix is the column that is not about points at all. A grade E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma. A student with excellent subject grades and an E in TOK does not receive the Diploma, and this is the scenario that produces the most urgent calls we get from Dubai parents — usually in the final term, when the margin for action is small. An E is rare and it is almost always a work-not-done problem rather than a capability problem.

The practical reading for a Dubai family is about sequencing rather than about intensity. A B in TOK and a B in the EE is two points and is achievable by a student who starts both on time and submits complete drafts. Chasing an A in both while two HL subjects are sliding is rarely the right trade. We say that plainly, because the honest advice for many students is to secure the two points and protect the subject grades.

Ask your child's coordinator for the school's internal TOK and EE deadlines in the first month of DP1, and put both on one calendar with the subject internal assessment dates. Nearly every TOK crisis we are called into is a calendar problem that was visible a year earlier.

sections.heading: The exhibition: why most first-choice objects do not work
paragraphs: The exhibition asks for three objects and one prompt, and the commentary has to explain how each object manifests TOK in the world. The requirement that decides the mark is specificity. An object must be a particular thing with a real context — this photograph, taken on this date, by this person — rather than a type of thing. A student who writes about a newspaper has chosen a category. A student who writes about a specific front page from a specific date has chosen an object, and the commentary can then say something that could not be said about any other object.

The second common failure is the prompt. One prompt is chosen for the whole exhibition and all three objects must address it. Students frequently pick a prompt they find interesting and then force objects onto it, or pick three objects they like and attach the prompt afterwards. Both produce a commentary that describes rather than justifies. Testing the prompt against all three candidate objects before any writing starts takes one session and prevents the rewrite.

The third is the balance of the commentary. With roughly 300 words per object, there is no room to explain what the object is at length. The marks are in the justification: why this object, how it shows the prompt operating in the real world, what it reveals about how knowledge is produced or accepted. Students who spend half their words on description are not short of ability; they have misread what the instrument rewards.

Object choice also has a practical dimension in Dubai that is worth using. Students here have access to genuinely interesting local material — regulatory documents, multilingual signage, school inspection reports, family migration records, construction photography — and a well-chosen local object is harder for a marker to have seen before. The criterion is provenance and relevance, not exoticism, and an object the student can account for precisely always beats one borrowed from an example list.

sections.heading: The essay: reading a prescribed title properly before writing a word
paragraphs: Six prescribed titles are issued for each examination session and the student answers one, unchanged. Rewording a title, even slightly, is a route to an essay that answers a question nobody asked. The first job is therefore translation: what does this title actually commit the writer to? A title that asks whether something is ever justified commits the writer to a judgement, not to a survey. A title built around a distinction commits the writer to maintaining that distinction throughout.

The choice between the six is strategic and most students make it too fast. The right title is the one for which the student can produce specific, first-hand examples from the subjects they are actually taking. A student with History HL and Biology HL should pick the title those two areas of knowledge can carry. Picking the most intellectually appealing title and then hunting for examples online produces the commonest middle-band essay: competent, general and unevidenced.

Structure inside 1,600 words is unforgiving. There is room for a precise opening that defines the terms, two developed areas of knowledge, a genuine counter-claim in each, and a conclusion that actually decides something. There is no room for a history of philosophy, a list of definitions from a dictionary, or three areas of knowledge handled thinly. The most reliable improvement we make to a draft is removing the third area of knowledge and deepening the other two.

Counter-claims are where bands separate. A student who states a claim, offers an example, then offers an objection they immediately dismiss in one clause has not engaged with the objection. The habit worth building is treating the counter-claim as if it might win: giving it its own example and its own weight, and then explaining why the original claim survives or is modified. That is a coachable move, and in most drafts it is the single change that lifts a band.
bullets: Answer the title as written; rewording it changes the question
Choose the title your own subjects can evidence, not the most appealing one
Two areas of knowledge developed properly beat three handled thinly
Give the counter-claim a real example, not a dismissive clause

sections.heading: What TOK coaching costs in Dubai, and why it is usually a block
paragraphs: TOK support is priced as specialist work because the people who can mark it against the instrument are subject-core specialists rather than general essay tutors. Published market rates in Dubai give the shape: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase shows AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200-450 or above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those figures belong to those providers and are quoted here with their source so you can check them.

What IB Gram publishes is the model rather than a price list. A free trial lesson comes first, one per family, with no card details taken, and the specific tutor's rate is confirmed in writing before any paid session. For TOK the sensible purchase is a defined block rather than an open weekly commitment: three to five sessions for the exhibition, four to six for the essay, one or two for a draft review. A student who still needs weekly TOK sessions in April has a different problem, and more hours is not the answer to it.

Three things move the number. Turnaround is the main one: a marked draft returned inside 48 hours before an internal deadline is priced differently from a session booked a month out. Stage is the second — a draft review by someone who can name the band is specialist work, while early title discussion is not. The third is the slot, because the 5pm to 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time window is what every Dubai family asks for and the least negotiable thing in the week.

For context on the overall spend: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. Against a Diploma-year fee, a five-session TOK block is a small line. It is still worth buying against a named deadline rather than open-endedly.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home TOK tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: Parents search for a home tutor, so the comparison belongs on the page. An in-home tutor in Dubai costs more per hour than an online one because travel sits inside the rate, and the published bands put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 against AED 150-300 for a qualified online hour. Travel also fixes the schedule: a tutor crossing from Jumeirah to Academic City in evening traffic can take one booking in that window, not two, so cancellations are expensive and reschedules are difficult.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We state it on every UAE page rather than letting a family discover it after booking.

For TOK specifically the online format is the better fit rather than the compromise, because the work is entirely text and argument. The draft sits on a shared screen with the band descriptors open beside it. A title is annotated live, term by term. A commentary's word count is visible to both people as it changes. A recorded session lets a student revisit the reasoning behind a change a week later, which matters when the change was conceptual rather than mechanical.

The deeper advantage is who you can reach. The number of people in any one Dubai community who have marked TOK against the instrument is small, and the number available at 6pm on a Tuesday is smaller. Online, availability is set by the clock rather than by the map, which for a component this specialised is what decides whether real help exists at all.

sections.heading: Fitting TOK into a Dubai school year without a February crisis
paragraphs: The Dubai academic year gives TOK an awkward rhythm. The exhibition usually lands in DP1 when nothing else is urgent, so it drifts. The essay lands in DP2 alongside subject internal assessments, the Extended Essay final submission and university applications, so it compresses. Add the shortened school days of Ramadan and the long summer break between the two Diploma years, and the result is a component with two deadlines and no weekly pressure to keep it moving.

The sequencing that works is simple and almost nobody does it. Finish the exhibition commentary before the DP1 summer break rather than carrying it into DP2. Read all six prescribed titles the week they are released and choose within a fortnight, while the subject examples from DP1 are still fresh. Write the first full essay draft before the internal assessment season starts rather than after it. Each of those moves costs nothing and removes the February pile-up entirely.

Dubai students also carry the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the Diploma. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. That is real timetable space, and it is one reason a Diploma week here has less unallocated time than families assume when planning core work.

Ramadan deserves planning rather than improvisation. School hours shorten, evening routines move around Iftar, and a weekly session at 5.30pm stops working for several weeks. Because sessions are online, a block can shift to later evenings or weekend mornings without travel cost — but it needs agreeing before the month starts, not during it.

process.title: Tell us the task and the date
process.description: The useful first message names the task, the stage and the deadline: exhibition in DP1 with no objects chosen yet, or essay in DP2 with a title picked and a draft half written. TOK support is bought against a date, so that one line decides whether the right answer is five sessions or two.

process.title: Send the work as it stands, however rough
process.description: A partial commentary, a list of candidate objects, or a draft with gaps tells a TOK specialist more than a description of the problem does. If there is nothing written yet, send the prescribed title and your child's six subjects. Which areas of knowledge they can genuinely evidence shapes everything that follows.

process.title: Free trial lesson that produces a band judgement
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken. For a student with a draft, the tutor marks it against the descriptors and names the band it currently sits in. For a student at the start, the tutor tests the prompt or the title. Either way you finish with a concrete position rather than an impression.

process.title: Agree the block, the rate and the turnaround
process.description: Before any paid session we confirm in writing how many sessions the block is, the tutor's rate, the weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, and how fast a draft comes back marked. Turnaround is the part that matters near an internal deadline and the part most often left vague elsewhere.

process.title: Work in drafts the student writes
process.description: Each session ends with the student knowing what to change and why it earns marks. Drafts come back with questions, annotations and a named band, never with replacement text. If your child cannot explain a change, the change does not go in.

process.title: Close the block and hand back to the school
process.description: When the task is submitted the block ends. We do not roll TOK into an open weekly commitment, because there is nothing left to coach once the work is in. If the essay block is still ahead, we schedule it against the school's date rather than continuing out of habit.

whyPoints.description: Every marked draft names the band it currently sits in and quotes the descriptor that puts it there. Most students have never seen their own TOK work placed against the instrument, and seeing it is what makes the next change obvious rather than arbitrary.

whyPoints.title: The student writes every word
whyPoints.description: Our tutors return questions, annotations and band judgements. They do not supply sentences for submission, draft commentaries, or rewrite to completion. In a market where one ranking site sells finished coursework, that boundary is the thing worth checking before you hire anyone.

whyPoints.description: TOK work has two dates and two word limits, so we sell three to six sessions against a named deadline rather than an open weekly slot. A student still having weekly TOK sessions in April has a sequencing problem that more hours will not fix.

whyPoints.title: The matrix explained before it matters
whyPoints.description: Most families meet the TOK and Extended Essay points matrix in the final term. Understanding in DP1 that two Bs are worth two points, and that an E is a failing condition, changes how the two years are planned rather than how the last month is survived.

faqs.question: How is IB Theory of Knowledge assessed in the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Through two tasks and no examination. The TOK exhibition asks for three objects linked to one prescribed internal assessment prompt, with a commentary of no more than 950 words; it is marked by the school out of ten and moderated by the IB, and carries one third of the grade. The TOK essay answers one of six prescribed titles issued for the session, in no more than 1,600 words, is marked externally out of ten, and carries two thirds. The two combine into a grade from A to E. Both are marked on a global impression against band descriptors rather than by adding up points for features.

faqs.question: How many Diploma points can Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add together?
faqs.answer: Up to three, awarded on a published matrix that combines the two A-to-E grades. Two A grades give three points; an A and a C give two; two C grades give one; two D grades give none. Those points count towards the 45-point Diploma total, which is why they regularly decide a university offer. Ask your child's coordinator to confirm the version of the matrix in force for their session. The more consequential part of the matrix is that a grade E in either component is a failing condition for the Diploma, independent of the six subject grades.

faqs.question: Can a grade E in TOK stop my child receiving the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. A grade E in Theory of Knowledge or in the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma, which means strong subject grades do not compensate for it. In practice an E almost always reflects work not completed or submitted far below the requirements rather than a student who cannot do it, so it is also the most preventable outcome in the programme. The protection is sequencing: ask for the school's internal TOK deadlines in the first month of DP1, put them on one calendar with the Extended Essay dates, and treat a missed internal deadline as the warning it is.

faqs.question: What makes a good object for the TOK exhibition?
faqs.answer: Specificity and provenance. The object must be a particular thing the student can account for — this photograph, taken on this date, by this person — rather than a category of thing. A commentary about a newspaper can only say what is true of all newspapers; a commentary about one identified front page can say something no other object would support. Objects should connect to the chosen prompt without being forced onto it, and the strongest choices are usually close to the student's own life, school or city, because provenance is then genuinely known rather than assumed from an example list online.

faqs.question: How long should the TOK exhibition commentary be?
faqs.answer: No more than 950 words in total, covering all three objects. That works out at roughly 300 words each, which is the figure worth planning from, because it makes clear how little room exists for description. The marks sit in justification: why this object, how it shows the prompt operating in the real world, and what it reveals about how knowledge is produced or accepted. Content beyond the limit need not be rewarded, so a commentary trimmed at the end usually loses justification rather than padding. Plan to the limit from the first outline instead of cutting to it afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose my child's TOK prescribed title for them?
faqs.answer: A tutor should not choose it, but helping test the choice is legitimate and useful. Six titles are issued for each session and the student answers one, unchanged. The right choice is the title that the student's own six subjects can evidence specifically — a student with History and Biology at Higher Level should pick the title those areas of knowledge can carry. What a tutor can do is read all six with the student, unpack what each title's key terms commit the writer to, and ask for a concrete example from the student's own courses for each. The decision stays the student's.

faqs.question: Why did my child's TOK essay come back marked as too descriptive?
faqs.answer: Usually because the counter-claims are not doing any work. A common pattern is a claim, an example, then an objection dismissed in half a sentence, repeated three times. The instrument rewards a discussion that is clear, coherent and convincing, and an objection that is raised only to be waved away is not convincing. The fix is to treat each counter-claim as if it might win: give it its own example and its own weight, then explain why the original claim survives or has to be modified. The second common cause is three areas of knowledge handled thinly instead of two developed properly.

faqs.question: How much does TOK tutoring cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give the range rather than a single figure. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour at the budget online end, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase shows AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts specialist IB and IGCSE tuition at AED 200-450 or above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are their figures with their dates. TOK prices at the specialist end because marking against the band descriptors is specialist work, and fast turnaround near a deadline costs more than a session booked a month ahead.

faqs.question: When do Dubai schools usually run the TOK exhibition?
faqs.answer: Most schedule it during DP1, though the date varies by several months between schools because the exhibition is internally assessed and the school sets its own internal deadlines. Some Dubai schools run it early in DP1 as an introduction to the course; others place it late, close to the summer break. Ask the TOK teacher for the internal date in the first month of DP1 and put it on the same calendar as the Extended Essay milestones. The most common pattern we see is an exhibition that drifts across the DP1 summer and then competes with DP2 coursework, which is avoidable.

faqs.question: Is the TOK essay marked by the school or by an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: By an IB examiner, externally, out of ten. The exhibition is the internally assessed task: the school marks it against the instrument and the IB moderates those marks. That difference changes how each task should be handled. For the exhibition, the school's own guidance and internal deadlines carry real weight because the school is the first marker. For the essay, the audience is an examiner with no knowledge of the student, the school or the context, so nothing can be assumed and every example has to be explained on the page.

faqs.question: Can a tutor edit my child's TOK essay before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Not to completion, and this is the boundary worth being careful about. Both TOK tasks are submitted as the student's own work under IB academic honesty rules, and work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter affecting the Diploma. A tutor may mark a draft, name the band it sits in, quote the descriptor, ask questions and identify what is missing. A tutor may not supply replacement sentences, rewrite paragraphs, or hand back a polished version. The practical test: your child should be able to explain every change they make and why it earns marks.

faqs.question: What are the areas of knowledge in TOK and how many should an essay use?
faqs.answer: The areas of knowledge are history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts, and the prescribed titles are answered through them. Inside a 1,600-word limit, two developed areas of knowledge almost always beat three handled thinly: there is room for a precise opening, two areas with real examples and genuine counter-claims, and a conclusion that decides something. The most reliable single improvement we make to a Dubai student's draft is deleting the third area of knowledge and giving its words to the other two. The examples should come from the student's own subjects.

faqs.question: My child is strong in maths and science but lost in TOK. Is that common?
faqs.answer: Very. Two years of being rewarded for producing the correct answer is poor preparation for a course that asks how an answer came to be accepted. The same students often have the best raw material and use it least: a mathematician who can talk about proof and axioms from their own course, or a biologist who can describe how a particular claim became accepted, has examples no example list can supply. The coaching work is mostly translation — moving from explaining the science to examining the knowledge claim — and it tends to click in two or three sessions rather than gradually.

faqs.question: Does TOK coaching actually work over video for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: It suits the component better than most. TOK work is text and argument: the draft sits on a shared screen with the band descriptors open beside it, a prescribed title is annotated term by term, and the word count is visible to both people as it changes. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Dubai school day, which removes the travel that makes an evening in-home booking fragile. It also widens who your child can work with, since the number of people in any one Dubai community who have marked TOK against the instrument is small.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a TOK essay usually take from title to final draft?
faqs.answer: Four to six for most students, spread across six to eight weeks rather than compressed into a fortnight. The first session goes entirely on the title and the subject examples available, which feels slow and saves the most time. The next two build claims and counter-claims from those examples. The remainder are drafting and marking cycles, with the band named each time. A student who already has a complete draft and needs it read properly against the instrument usually needs one or two sessions instead, which is the most common request we get from Dubai families in DP2.

dubai/ib-dp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Programme subjects over live video to Dubai students. Each profile names the subject, level and components taught, which is the level of detail a mark-map conversation needs.

intro.heading: DP stands for Diploma Programme, and the marks are not where parents assume
paragraphs: DP is the IB's shorthand for the Diploma Programme, the two-year course taken at 16 to 19. The abbreviation turns up constantly in Dubai school communications, and families who have arrived from another system often meet it before they meet an explanation. It matters here because searching for a DP tutor rather than an IB tutor usually signals a parent already inside the programme, dealing with a specific component rather than wondering what the Diploma is.

The thing almost nobody is told early is where the marks sit. Parents reasonably assume a subject grade is mostly the final papers, with coursework as a modest extra. In most DP subjects the internally assessed component carries a fifth or more of the subject grade, and at Higher Level a third paper appears that is worth roughly as much as the internal assessment. Add the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, both marked against published criteria with hard word limits, and a substantial share of a candidate's result is decided by work that is not sat in an examination hall.

That has a direct consequence for how tutoring money should be spent. An hour spent narrowing a research question before any writing happens affects a criterion worth several marks and cannot be replicated later. An hour spent on general content revision in April affects whatever the student happens to meet on the paper. Those are not equivalent purchases, and the published rates in this market, roughly AED 150 to 300 for an online qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for an exam-level specialist, apply to both equally.

So this page publishes the map. Component weightings by subject and level, with the honest caveat that subject guides are revised and your child's coordinator holds the authoritative version. Internal assessment criteria named by letter with their mark allocations, which no competing page in this market appears to do at all. Word and page limits in one table, because exceeding them is an avoidable loss. And an estimate of how many hours each common fix takes, converted into AED at published mid-band rates so the comparison is concrete.

IB Gram matches DP students to subject specialists for one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We quote per match after a free first lesson rather than publishing a rate card, and we tell you which band a request sits in before anything is paid. Every market figure on this page belongs to the provider named beside it and was read in October 2026. If a figure on this page differs from the one your coordinator gives you, trust the coordinator.

dubai/ib-dp-tutor.programmesIntro: The Diploma Programme is one of four IB programmes, and the mark structures differ sharply between them. Knowing which one your child is in tells you whether criteria or papers are the thing to work on.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard, each assessed through externally marked papers plus an internally assessed component. The core adds the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Award conditions are set by the IB and confirmed by your school's coordinator rather than by any tutoring page.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP candidates sit the same papers and the same criteria as candidates anywhere, which is worth stating because families sometimes assume a regional variation exists. What is local is the school's internal deadline calendar and its own marking standard before IB moderation, and both differ noticeably between IB World Schools in the emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a letter and number rather than a percentage. There are no papers in the DP sense, so the whole conversation is about descriptors. A student arriving in DP from MYP already reads a rubric fluently and is usually underprepared for the volume of timed written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP reports confuse parents more than DP reports do, because a criterion score of 5 out of 8 is not a percentage and does not translate into a familiar grade. Working out which of the four criteria is holding a subject down is the single most useful thing to establish before buying any hours.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is marked against five criteria totalling 34 marks within a 4,000-word limit, supervised by the school. The Theory of Knowledge essay is written on a prescribed title with a 1,600-word limit, and the exhibition has its own shorter commentary limit. Both are externally assessed and both reward criterion-shaped writing over polish.
programmes.countryNote: Internal deadlines for these components vary by several weeks across Dubai IB schools, and the long summer break between the Diploma years is where Extended Essay progress most often stalls. Hours spent scoping the research question before that break are worth several times the same hours spent after it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two DP courses plus a career-related study, a reflective project and further core elements. The DP subjects inside it are examined identically to the Diploma versions, so the mark map on this page applies directly to those components.
programmes.countryNote: Few UAE schools offer the Career-related Programme, so UAE-based tutor coverage for it is thin and most matches come from our wider pool at a Dubai-friendly hour. The subject depth and the online one-to-one format are unchanged.

dubai/ib-dp-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the note names the component where the largest recoverable marks usually sit for Dubai candidates. Confirm the exact weightings against your child's current subject guide.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level two papers carry 40% each with the exploration at 20%. At Higher Level a third paper appears, typically 20%, alongside two papers at 30% each and the exploration at 20%. Paper 3 is where a Higher Level candidate most often leaves marks unclaimed, because structured investigation is rarely practised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same weighting shape as Analysis and Approaches, with a Higher Level third paper. Interpretation marks are the distinctive recoverable set here: a correct regression or model with no sentence about what it means in the scenario leaves marks on the table every time.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Under the current guide Paper 1 carries 36% of the subject grade, Paper 2 carries 44% and the scientific investigation 20%, at both levels. The investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria, with research design and evaluation the two most commonly underprepared.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same 36, 44 and 20 split as the other sciences under the current guide. Paper 2 extended responses hold the largest recoverable set, because method and reasoning marks are awarded for stated steps rather than for a correct final value.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Also 36, 44 and 20 under the current guide. Extended responses are point-marked against lists of creditable statements, so making five accurate plain points beats writing elegantly about one, and command-term discipline is the dominant recoverable issue.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level commonly runs Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 40% and the internal assessment at 30%, while Higher Level adds a quantitative third paper and reduces the internal assessment share. Diagram marks are individually creditable and routinely half-claimed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Entirely markband-judged. Standard Level typically splits two papers at 35% each with the individual oral at 30%; Higher Level adds a separate essay on a studied work. Paraphrase in place of analysis is the single largest loss across Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Standard Level commonly runs Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 45% and the historical investigation at 25%; Higher Level adds a third paper on a regional option. The investigation is marked out of 25 across three criteria, with the investigation section carrying most of them.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Typically Paper 1 at 35%, Paper 2 at 40% and the internal assessment at 25% at both levels, with Higher Level content extending the case material. Application to the stimulus is separately creditable from tool knowledge, and that is where the grade separates.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Standard Level commonly weights Paper 1 heavily with Paper 2 and the experimental study making up the remainder; Higher Level adds a third paper on research methodology. The experimental study's criteria reward method justification more than results.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay is written on a prescribed title within a 1,600-word limit and is externally assessed against a single global criterion. The exhibition has its own commentary limit. Title choice sets the ceiling, which makes it the cheapest high-value decision in the core.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Marked out of 34 across criteria A to E: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Critical thinking alone carries 12 of the 34, which is why a narrow answerable question matters more than elegant prose.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB World Schools running the Diploma Programme
schoolClusters.note: These schools between them cover most of the emirate's DP cohort. Their internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines differ by several weeks, so the useful planning document is your own school's assessment calendar rather than a generic DP timeline.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools whose students arrive in DP from another system
schoolClusters.note: A significant share of Dubai DP candidates come from IGCSE or an American system. The recognisable pattern is strong content recall and weak extended-response structure, which the weighting table explains: the papers that carry the most marks are the ones rewarding sustained argument.

sections.heading: Component weightings across the common DP subjects
paragraphs: The first thing to establish about any DP subject is how the grade is divided, because that determines which hour of work is worth most. The table below gives the shape for the subjects Dubai families most often ask about. Two cautions apply to every row. Subject guides are revised, and a revision can change the number of papers, the internal assessment task and the weightings. And your child's coordinator holds the authoritative version for their cohort, so a figure here is a starting point for a conversation rather than a fact to plan two years around.

Reading the table, three patterns stand out. First, the internally assessed component is rarely trivial: a fifth of the subject grade is typical and some subjects go higher. Second, Higher Level normally adds a third paper worth roughly as much as the internal assessment, which is a substantial block of marks most families do not discover until a mock result arrives. Third, the paper carrying the largest single share is usually the extended-response paper rather than the short-answer one, which is why technique rather than content coverage tends to be the better purchase.

That third pattern is worth sitting with. If Paper 2 carries 44% of a science grade and rewards reasoning expressed in stated steps, then a student who knows the content and does not write the steps is losing marks in the largest block available. No amount of additional content fixes that, and the fix itself is quick: three or four sessions of writing practice with the criteria visible. The weighting table is how a family works out that this is where to spend.

The same logic applies to the core. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria, and critical thinking alone carries 12 of them. Presentation carries 4. A family that spends its hours on formatting and referencing while the research question remains too broad to answer is optimising a four-mark criterion and ignoring a twelve-mark one. That is an avoidable mistake and the table is the cheapest way to avoid it.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, named by letter with their marks
paragraphs: This is the part of the DP nobody publishes. Across the competitor pages researched for this market, not one names a single internal assessment criterion by letter or states its mark allocation, which is remarkable given that the internal assessment typically carries a fifth or more of a subject grade and is the component a tutor can most legitimately help with.

The letters matter because criteria are judged separately on a best-fit basis. Strength in one does not compensate for a gap in another, so a draft that is excellent on presentation and silent on evaluation loses the evaluation marks entirely. The practical method is mechanical: list the criteria, and for each one ask where in the draft the evidence for it is. If the answer is a vague gesture at several pages, the marker will not find it either.

Take the mathematics exploration, marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation at 6, and reflection and personal engagement carry 3 each. A student who produces impeccable notation and no genuine reflection is leaving a sixth of the component unclaimed, and nothing about that is visible from a general instruction to work harder.

Or take the Extended Essay, marked out of 34: focus and method 6, knowledge and understanding 6, critical thinking 12, presentation 4, engagement 6. Critical thinking is more than a third of the total. That single fact reorders what a sensible support plan looks like, and it is published freely by the IB. A tutor who works from it is doing something different in kind from one who reads a draft and comments on the writing.

sections.heading: Word, page and time limits across the Diploma
paragraphs: Limits are hard edges, not guidance, and exceeding them is the most avoidable loss in the entire programme. The frustrating part is that students who exceed a limit have usually worked harder than those who did not. A 5,000-word Extended Essay represents more effort than a 3,900-word one and will be marked worse, because assessment stops at the stated limit and everything after it is invisible.

The limits also shape what a research question can be. A student who proposes a question requiring four case studies in 2,200 words has designed something that cannot be done, and that is a scoping problem to catch in the first conversation rather than in the fourth draft. The most useful question a tutor can ask early is: can this actually be answered within the limit, with the sources you can reach, in the time available? A no is cheap in September and ruinous in March.

On timed components, the parallel discipline is minutes per mark. A paper's duration divided by its marks gives a rough budget, and students who have never calculated it routinely spend fifteen minutes on a four-mark question and three on a twelve-mark one. Doing that arithmetic once, and practising to it twice, is one of the fastest available gains, and it costs an hour.

A caution before the table: limits and durations are set in the subject guides and can change when a guide is revised. The figures below are the commonly published ones, and your child's coordinator holds the authoritative version for their cohort. We reference and link official sources rather than redistributing board documents, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, an integrity matter as well.

sections.heading: Hours to marks: what each common fix costs at published Dubai rates
paragraphs: This is the cost conversation done properly. Instead of asking what a DP tutor costs per hour, ask what each specific fix costs in total and what it is worth in marks. The hourly figure then becomes a detail rather than the decision. Published rates in this market for an online qualified subject tutor run roughly AED 150 to 300, and for an exam-level specialist roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaching AED 450 and beyond.

Using a mid-band figure for arithmetic, a four-hour fix at a specialist rate is a few hundred dirhams per hour and a low four-figure total, and several of the fixes below take four hours. Compare that with a weekly subject session across a whole DP2 year, which is around twenty-eight sessions, and the difference in total outlay is substantial. Some students genuinely need the latter. Many need two or three of the former and are sold the latter because nobody did the diagnosis.

The marks column below is deliberately framed as what is typically at stake rather than what will be gained. Nobody can promise marks, and any provider who does is making a claim about papers nobody has seen and boundaries set after marking. What can be said honestly is which component a fix affects and how many marks that component carries, which is a different and more useful statement.

One row deserves emphasis because it is the cheapest high-value hour in the programme. Scoping an Extended Essay research question properly takes two to three hours, happens in DP1, and affects criterion C, worth 12 of the essay's 34 marks, plus criterion A at 6. No later intervention recovers a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words. Families who buy nothing else should buy that.

sections.heading: What a raw internal assessment mark becomes, and why boundaries move
paragraphs: Parents are routinely shown a raw internal assessment mark and left to guess what it means. Two conversions sit between that number and a subject grade. First, weighting: a mark out of 20 or 24 is scaled to the component's share of the subject grade, so a four-mark gap on a 20-mark exploration worth a fifth of the grade is not the same as a four-mark gap on a paper worth nearly half. Second, moderation: the school's marking is compared against the IB's standard using a sample, and a whole cohort's marks can be adjusted up or down.

That second step is the one that surprises Dubai families most, because a mark that appeared on a February report can arrive differently in July. It is routine rather than a judgement about an individual student, and nobody can predict it. The only lever available is to make the work unambiguously defensible against each criterion, because a piece sitting clearly inside a band is less exposed to adjustment than one sitting on a boundary.

On grade boundaries, the honest position is that they are set per session after marking and published with results, not before. Anyone telling a student in March exactly what raw mark a 6 will require in the coming session is guessing. What can be said is where this student's marks are currently being lost and which losses are cheapest to recover, which is more actionable than a boundary estimate would be even if one existed.

Two things follow for a family. Treat a school report as a direction of travel rather than a result, and look instead at artefacts: a marked timed paper with the losses mapped, an internal assessment draft at a stage where feedback can still change it, a list of questions scored around half marks. And route questions about a specific moderation outcome or a results enquiry to your school's IB coordinator, who is the only person able to act on either.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, compared properly
paragraphs: Families are usually told that Higher Level is harder, which is true and useless. The differences that matter are structural: more content, an additional paper in most subjects, the same internal assessment in some and a different one in others, and a different expectation about independence. A student choosing between the two, or struggling at Higher Level, needs those differences itemised rather than characterised.

The additional paper is the part most often underestimated. In mathematics it is a structured investigation rewarding the communication of reasoning on an unfamiliar problem, which is unlike anything in Papers 1 and 2. In History it is an essay paper on a regional option with its own content. In Economics and Psychology it is a methodological or quantitative paper. In each case it is a block of marks that cannot be prepared for by doing more of what Papers 1 and 2 require, and it is the component Dubai Higher Level candidates most often meet unprepared in a mock.

The second structural difference is tutoring hours per mark. Higher Level content is broader, so content coverage is genuinely more expensive, while technique work transfers at the same rate across both levels. That argues for a specific sequencing: fix technique first, because it is cheap and applies to every paper, and only then decide whether a content programme is justified. Families who do it the other way round spend more and move less.

The decision itself belongs with the school. If three Higher Levels are producing more extended written work per fortnight than a student can produce at all, that is a timetable matter and only the coordinator can change it, and the window for doing so comfortably is DP1 term one. A tutor's job in that situation is to say so clearly and early rather than to sell eighteen months of symptom management.

sections.heading: Where Dubai DP candidates lose marks, by pattern rather than by topic
paragraphs: Across the marked DP work we see from Dubai schools, losses cluster into a small number of patterns rather than spreading across the syllabus. Naming the pattern is what turns a vague worry into a four-hour plan. Five patterns account for most of it.

The first is command-term substitution: answering evaluate as though it said explain, which caps the top band in every extended response. The second is absent working in mathematics and the quantitative sciences, which forfeits method marks and blocks follow-through credit, so one arithmetic slip costs an entire question instead of one mark. The third is partial statement in point-marked science questions, where a student knows the idea and expresses two-thirds of it and earns nothing.

The fourth is coursework scope: a research question too broad to control, which caps several criteria simultaneously and cannot be fixed after the data is gathered. The fifth is timing, both within a paper, where fifteen minutes goes on a four-mark question, and across the programme, where a component is met for the first time in a mock. Each of these is diagnosable from one marked script and addressable in three or four sessions.

What is usually not the problem: general ability, effort, or a need to restart the syllabus. A DP student who has reached the second year has demonstrated the capacity to do the work. The question is almost always which of these five patterns is costing them marks, and the answer is visible in the marked work they already have at home. That is why the free first lesson is built around a script rather than around a conversation.

sections.heading: Delivery, matching and coverage for Dubai DP families
paragraphs: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 16:30 and 20:30 and typically sixty to ninety minutes. The shared screen matters for mark-map work specifically, because the question, the answer and the criteria can all sit on one screen and the file is saved afterwards for revision.

Matching is on component rather than on subject alone, since the whole argument of this page is that components differ. A tutor strong on Papers 1 and 2 is not automatically the right person for a Higher Level third paper, and a tutor who has supervised a scientific investigation is not automatically right for unseen textual analysis. We say which specialist we are proposing and what they have taught, and we change the match at no cost if the trial shows a mismatch.

Coverage is uneven and we publish it rather than letting you discover it. Common subjects at common levels match within a few days. Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks, and longer between February and May when DP cohorts across the emirate converge on the same specialists. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to format or depth.

What we will not do: produce any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge piece, because everything submitted must be the student's own work and the consequences of crossing that line fall on the candidate; redistribute board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, which we reference and link instead; or promise a mark, a grade or a moderation outcome. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

process.title: Send a marked paper and the component
process.description: The script, the question paper if the school released it, and which component it belongs to. The mark map only becomes useful against real work, and a request that names the component gets matched to a tutor who has taught that component.

process.description: One full lesson at no cost. It ends with a written statement naming the dominant loss pattern, the component it affects, what that component carries in the subject grade and roughly how many hours the fix takes.

process.title: Pick the fix by what it is worth
process.description: We propose the fix affecting the largest block of recoverable marks first, which is often not the subject the family called about. Scoping an Extended Essay question beats general content revision in almost every case.

process.title: Agree hours against a named component
process.description: A capped block aimed at one component, with the criteria and weightings written into the plan. Extending is an explicit decision, which is what stops a four-hour fix becoming an open weekly commitment.

process.title: Track self-marking convergence
process.description: In timed-paper work the measurable indicator is how far the student's own marking has moved towards accurate marking. It is visible well before a grade moves and it is what the session-four review looks at.

process.title: Route the rest to the school
process.description: Weighting confirmation, moderation outcomes, timetable changes and results enquiries belong with your school's IB coordinator. We say which questions are theirs, including when that means you need fewer hours from us.

whyPoints.title: We publish the mark map
whyPoints.description: Component weightings, internal assessment criteria by letter with their allocations, and the word and page limits in one place. No competing page in this market appears to name a single criterion letter, and it is the information a plan should be built on.

whyPoints.title: Fixes priced as totals, not hourly rates
whyPoints.description: We state roughly how many hours a named fix takes and what that comes to at published mid-band rates, so you can compare a four-hour intervention against a year of weekly sessions on the same page.

whyPoints.title: Matched on component
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level third paper, a scientific investigation criterion and an unseen-text paper need different teachers. We name which specialist we are proposing and what they have taught, and change the match at no cost if the trial disagrees.

whyPoints.title: Figures hedged where they should be
whyPoints.description: Every weighting and limit here carries a verify-with-your-coordinator caution, because subject guides are revised. We would rather give you a figure with a caveat than a confident number that is a guide version out of date.

whyPoints.title: No claims about marks or boundaries
whyPoints.description: Boundaries are set per session after marking and published with results. Moderation can adjust a whole cohort. We state what a component carries and where marks are being lost, and we promise neither an outcome nor a boundary.

whyPoints.description: The student writes every submitted word. A tutor lists the criteria, asks where the evidence for each one is, and gives feedback on material the student has already produced. Version history records who made each change.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB and IB DP?
faqs.answer: The International Baccalaureate runs several programmes, and DP is the abbreviation for the Diploma Programme, the two-year course taken at ages 16 to 19. The others are the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Career-related Programme. Dubai school communications use the abbreviations constantly, so a parent may meet DP1 and DP2 before anyone explains them: they are simply the first and second years of the Diploma. If you are searching for a DP tutor rather than an IB tutor, you are almost certainly already inside the programme and dealing with a specific component.

faqs.question: How much is the Higher Level third paper worth in a DP subject?
faqs.answer: Typically around a fifth of the subject grade, though it varies by subject and by guide version. In mathematics at Higher Level the usual shape is two papers at about 30% each, a third paper at about 20% and the exploration at about 20%. In History the third paper carries a larger share. The important point is structural rather than numerical: the third paper tests something the other two do not, whether that is structured investigation, a regional option or research methodology, so it needs its own preparation block. Confirm the exact figures with your child's coordinator.

faqs.question: How much does the internal assessment count towards a DP subject grade?
faqs.answer: Commonly a fifth, and in some subjects more. The mathematics exploration is usually about 20%, the science scientific investigation about 20%, the history historical investigation about 25%, and Economics at Standard Level has carried about 30%. That is far more than most families assume, and it is also the component a tutor can most legitimately help with, since the work is criterion-marked and the criteria are published. Check your child's subject guide through their coordinator, because weightings change when a guide is revised and a figure from an older guide can mislead a whole plan.

faqs.question: What are the criteria for the IB mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Five, marked out of 20 in total: criterion A presentation worth 4, criterion B mathematical communication worth 4, criterion C personal engagement worth 3, criterion D reflection worth 3, and criterion E use of mathematics worth 6. The practical consequence is that use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation while reflection and personal engagement together carry 6, which students routinely treat as a concluding paragraph rather than as a sixth of the component. Listing the criteria and asking where the evidence for each sits in the draft is the method; confirm the current totals with your coordinator.

faqs.question: What is the word limit for a DP internal assessment?
faqs.answer: It differs by subject, and the limits are hard edges rather than guidance. Commonly published figures include about 3,000 words for a science scientific investigation, about 2,200 for a history historical investigation, 1,200 to 1,500 for an English Higher Level essay, and page-count guidance rather than a word limit for the mathematics exploration. Exceeding a limit is the most avoidable loss in the programme, because assessment stops at the stated point and the extra work is simply unread. Check your child's subject guide through the coordinator before planning a piece around any figure.

faqs.question: Are IB grade boundaries the same every year?
faqs.answer: No. Boundaries are set for each examination session after the papers have been marked, and they are published with results rather than in advance. That is why any specific figure quoted to a student in March for the coming session is a guess presented as information. What can be said usefully is where this student's marks are currently being lost, which of those losses is cheapest to recover and what the work would look like if it moved. A tutor who claims to know a future boundary is making a claim nobody in the system is able to make.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level actually add compared with Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Four things, and only one of them is difficulty. More content, because the syllabus adds higher-level material. An additional paper in most subjects, usually worth around a fifth of the grade and testing something the first two papers do not. A greater expectation of independent work. And in some subjects an extended or different internal assessment. For tutoring that means content coverage genuinely costs more hours at Higher Level, while technique work transfers at the same rate across both levels, which argues for fixing technique first and deciding about content afterwards.

faqs.question: Which DP components reward structure more than content knowledge?
faqs.answer: The markband components, which include English papers, History essays, the Theory of Knowledge essay and most criterion-marked coursework. These are judged holistically against level descriptors, so sustained argument, focus and organisation decide the band and additional coverage adds nothing. Point-marked components work the other way: science short questions and mathematics method marks credit each distinct accurate statement or step independently, so breadth of relevant content beats depth on one idea. A student optimising for the wrong model in half their papers is losing marks nobody has explained to them.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Extended Essay worth across its criteria?
faqs.answer: Thirty-four in total, across five criteria: focus and method worth 6, knowledge and understanding worth 6, critical thinking worth 12, presentation worth 4, and engagement worth 6. Critical thinking alone is more than a third of the total, which should reorder how a family spends support hours: a plan focused on referencing and formatting is optimising a four-mark criterion while a twelve-mark one goes unaddressed. The highest-value work happens before writing, on whether the research question can be answered within 4,000 words with sources the student can actually reach.

faqs.question: How long is the Theory of Knowledge essay allowed to be?
faqs.answer: Commonly 1,600 words, written on a prescribed title and externally assessed against a single global criterion, with the exhibition carrying its own shorter commentary limit. Because the essay is judged as a whole against descriptors rather than by collecting points, length discipline and a genuine knowledge question matter more than coverage. The choice of prescribed title effectively sets the ceiling, and a weak choice cannot be recovered by later polishing, which makes title selection the cheapest high-value conversation available in the core. Confirm the current limits with your coordinator.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai DP students lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: In five patterns rather than across the syllabus. Command-term substitution, where evaluate is answered as explain and the top band is capped in every long response. Absent working in mathematics and quantitative sciences, which forfeits method marks and blocks follow-through. Partial statement in point-marked science questions, where two-thirds of an idea earns nothing. Coursework scope, where a research question too broad to control caps several criteria at once. And timing, both within a paper and across the programme, where a component is met for the first time in a mock. Each is visible on one marked script.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to fix a command-term problem?
faqs.answer: Usually three to four sessions, which makes it one of the best-value interventions available because it affects the largest paper in most subjects. The method is mechanical: name the term, name what the examiner requires, write the structure down as a template with the number of elements, practise on six past questions sharing that term, then mix terms so the student has to identify which one they face. At a published mid-band rate of around AED 250 an hour that is roughly AED 750 to 1,000 in total, against a component that commonly carries 40% or more of a subject grade.

faqs.question: Should tutoring hours go on Paper 1 or Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Start from the weighting and from where the marks are actually being lost, not from which paper feels harder. In the sciences under the current guide Paper 2 commonly carries about 44% of the subject grade against Paper 1 at about 36%, and Paper 2 rewards reasoning expressed in stated steps, which is a technique problem rather than a content one. In mathematics the two papers together carry most of the grade, so method discipline serves both. Bring a marked script from each and look at the distribution of losses; that comparison settles the question in ten minutes.

faqs.question: Does going over a word limit cost marks in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, because assessment stops at the stated limit and anything beyond it is not read. The frustrating part is that students who exceed a limit have usually worked harder than those who did not: a 5,000-word Extended Essay represents more effort than a 3,900-word one and is marked worse, because the sections most often cut off are the later ones where evaluation and conclusions live. The fix is structural and happens early, by designing a research question that can genuinely be answered within the limit rather than by trimming a finished draft.

faqs.question: How do I find my child's exact component weightings?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's IB coordinator or the subject teacher for the current subject guide reference and the assessment outline for your child's cohort. That is the authoritative source, because guides are revised and a revision can change the number of papers, the internal assessment task and the weightings themselves. Every figure on this page carries that caution for the same reason. Once you have the real weightings, the planning question becomes straightforward: which component carries the most marks, where is my child losing them, and what is the shortest intervention that addresses that specific loss.

dubai/ib-dp-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the weighting, then buy the hours
dubai/ib-dp-tutor.closingBody: An IB DP tutor in Dubai earns their rate by working from the mark map: which component carries the marks, which criterion has no evidence in the draft, and which of five loss patterns the marked script shows. dubai/ib-dp-visual-arts-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with Diploma Visual Arts students on the parts of the course that are written and curated: comparative analysis, process documentation, selection for exhibition and the curatorial rationale. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, with the student's own screens and images shared.

intro.heading: A making subject that is mostly assessed on how you talk about making
paragraphs: Visual Arts at Diploma level is the subject most often misunderstood by the families paying for it. A student who draws beautifully can finish with a five, and a student with modest technical facility can finish with a seven, because two of the three assessed components are documents. The comparative study is an analytical piece about other people's art. The process portfolio is evidence of how the student's own work developed. Only the exhibition presents finished artwork, and even that is accompanied by a curatorial rationale and by exhibition texts that are themselves assessed.

That is why this page is organised around the components and their requirements rather than around technique. Dubai students rarely need help making art; their schools have studios, materials and specialist teachers, and the emirate has a genuinely serious contemporary art scene within driving distance. What they need help with is analysis that compares rather than describes, documentation that shows thinking rather than progress photographs, selection that produces a coherent body of work rather than a best-of collection, and writing that fits inside a hard word limit without going vague.

The requirements are precise and they are where marks quietly disappear. Each component has a screen count or a word limit, and each differs between Standard and Higher Level. Higher Level students submit more work in every component, including additional screens on how the artists they studied influenced their own practice. Students who discover these specifications late in the second year end up cutting rather than composing, and cut work reads exactly as what it is. Confirm every figure on this page against the current subject guide through your school's Diploma coordinator, because guides are revised and the coordinator holds the internal deadlines.

On delivery, the position is stated before anything else. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, with the student's screens, images and drafts shared and annotated. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. In this subject the limit is clear and worth stating: nobody is going to help a student stretch a canvas or mix a glaze over a video call, and nobody should pretend otherwise. The studio belongs to the school. The analysis, the documentation and the curating are where an outside specialist is useful.

What follows covers the three components and their limits, what the comparative study actually rewards, what counts as process evidence, how an exhibition becomes coherent, where Dubai students lose marks most predictably, what the emirate's galleries and museums offer as primary looking, and the honesty line when the work being assessed is artwork. Every quoted limit is flagged for confirmation, and the one thing this page will not do is restate an IB examination date from a secondary source.
