sections.heading: What you are actually buying when you search for IB exam preparation in Dubai
paragraphs: IB exam preparation in Dubai is one-to-one teaching aimed at a specific externally marked paper, bought in hours, at a market rate of roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour as of October 2026. The thing being bought is not more teaching of the syllabus. A Diploma student in Dubai has already had two years of the syllabus from a subject teacher in a KHDA-inspected school. What they usually have not had is sustained one-to-one feedback on their own written answers against the published assessment criteria, because a class of twenty-two does not permit it.

That distinction is what determines the bill. Content teaching is slow and expensive: covering unlearned HL Chemistry content takes months, and no number of weeks at two sessions a week closes a two-year gap. Technique work is fast and cheap: a student who knows the chemistry but writes answers that earn five of eight marks can move several grade boundaries in a few weeks of marked papers. Before you price anything, work out which of the two you are buying, because they differ by a factor of five in hours.

The honest diagnostic is a marked paper. Have the student sit one full past paper to time, send the script, and have a subject specialist mark it to the criteria and report where the marks went. If the script shows scattered method errors and missing conclusions, you are buying technique and the block is short. If it shows whole topics absent, you are buying content and the realistic target is a grade, not three. We run that diagnostic inside the trial lesson, which is one 45-minute session per student with no card details taken, specifically so the quote that follows is based on evidence rather than on a parent's description of the problem.

One more thing this search is not. It is not a request for someone to produce assessed work. Everything in a Diploma that carries the student's name must be the student's own: the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay. A tutor teaches, questions, and gives feedback on what the student has already put down. The section on academic honesty below sets out exactly where that line sits, because two of the pages competing for this search in Dubai sell the other thing.
bullets: Content gaps: months of work, realistic target is one grade
Technique gaps: weeks of work, realistic target is more

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, by format
paragraphs: Dubai tutoring rates run from roughly AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor online to AED 650 an hour at the premium end, and the single biggest determinant is format rather than subject. The table below is the market, not an IB Gram price list, and every band is attributed to whoever published it. Three of the six pages currently ranking for this search publish no price at all; the two that do quote United States dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays tuition in.

Read the table by eliminating the bands that do not apply to you. A Diploma candidate preparing for externally marked HL papers is not in the budget tier: a first-year undergraduate who took the subject three years ago cannot mark to current criteria, and the saving evaporates the moment the feedback is wrong. Equally, the premium band buys reputation as much as teaching, and the evidence that a named tutor moves marks faster than a careful subject specialist at half the rate is not something anyone in this market publishes.

The in-home line deserves attention because it is where the money quietly goes. The travel premium is real and it is paid by the hour, not once: a tutor crossing from Jumeirah to Mirdif at 5pm is pricing ninety minutes of Dubai traffic into a sixty-minute lesson, every week, for the length of the block. IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Diploma tuition for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, which takes that premium out of the invoice and takes the drive-time radius out of the tutor search at the same time.

Two practical cautions on any quoted figure. Ask whether the rate is per hour or per session, because a ninety-minute session at an hourly rate is not what a parent reading a rate card assumes. And ask whether the figure includes value added tax; we do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as settled fact anywhere on this site, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation, so ask any provider directly whether their number is inclusive.

sections.heading: Six things that move the Dubai number
paragraphs: Once format is fixed, six variables set the total. Each one is decidable, and five of the six are decidable by you rather than by the market. Families who end up paying twice what they expected usually did so because of the second and third rows below: they started late and then bought three subjects at once, which doubles the weekly spend at exactly the moment the student has least capacity to use it.

Lateness is the expensive one. Fourteen weeks out, a block can be paced at one session a week per subject and the student can absorb the work set between sessions. Six weeks out, the same content needs three sessions a week, and the per-week cost triples while the marginal value of each session falls, because there is no time to practise between them. The cheapest version of exam preparation in Dubai is the one that starts in the Gregorian autumn term of DP2, and it is cheaper by more than any discount anybody in this market offers.

Specialism is the second-largest swing and it is the one that most rewards an online format. The band for a careful Standard Level Business Management tutor and for a Higher Level Chemistry specialist who marks to the current criteria differ by over a hundred dirhams an hour, and the latter is scarce in Dubai in absolute terms. Restrict the search to tutors who can drive to Dubai Hills on a Tuesday and the specialist may simply not exist, which is how families end up paying a specialist rate for a generalist. Live video removes that constraint without raising the rate.

The remaining rows are smaller but they compound over a block. Coursework supervision is slower work than paper practice and is usually priced above it. Session length changes the effective hourly figure. Weekend and post-7pm slots are the scarcest in Dubai and carry the least flexibility on price. And a tutor's permit position matters: the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a provider loading a licensing fee into a quote is charging you for something that costs nothing to obtain.

sections.heading: How many hours one subject actually absorbs
paragraphs: This is the table nobody in this market publishes, and it is the one that decides the budget. The five scenarios below are the ones Dubai families present with, in rough order of frequency. The hours are what a subject specialist would plan for, and the indicative spend applies the AED 200 to AED 300 online specialist band from the rates table above rather than any IB Gram figure.

The thing the table makes visible is that total hours are driven by weeks, not by urgency. A student fourteen weeks out at one session a week buys fourteen hours. The same student at six weeks out, needing the same work done, buys eighteen hours at three a week and gets less from each of them, because the practice time between sessions has gone. Urgency does not compress teaching; it just raises the hourly commitment and lowers the return. Every Dubai family that has done this twice books earlier the second time.

Note the last row particularly. A student who has not covered whole HL topics is not a candidate for a revision block at all, and we say so rather than sell one. Thirty-plus hours across a term is a content rebuild, and it needs a weekly slot from the autumn term, work completed between sessions, and a target expressed as one grade rather than three. A provider who quotes you a six-week package for that situation is quoting for a job that cannot be done in six weeks.

Use the table as an upper and lower bound rather than a prediction, and revisit it after the first marked paper. The single most useful number is not in the table at all: it is the gap between the student's mock mark and the mark their script says they should have had. A student losing eight marks a paper to method and presentation is in the top row of the table whatever their grade looks like. A student losing eight marks because they cannot do the question is in the bottom row.

sections.heading: The exam session counted backwards
paragraphs: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session, and the reason families start preparation too late is that they count forwards from today rather than backwards from the paper. Counted backwards, the last ten weeks are already committed: mock results land, predicted grades go to universities, internal coursework deadlines fall, and school revision timetables fill the evenings. The window where a new weekly slot can still be absorbed closes well before most parents start looking.

A caution on dates, stated plainly because it matters more than it looks. The International Baccalaureate's own examination and results dates are not restated on this page. The IB's website returns an automated-access error to the tooling that built this site, so no IB session or results date here has been confirmed from the IB itself, and we will not publish one that has not been. Confirm every IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around it. The Cambridge and Pearson dates referenced below are published by those boards and are cited as such.

What the backwards count does give you, without needing a single confirmed date, is the order of operations and the gaps between them. Coursework deadlines come before mocks. Mocks come before predicted grades. Predicted grades come before the university decisions that make a grade matter. Final entries, for boards that publish their deadlines, sit months before the papers: Cambridge's March 2027 series closes final entries on 27 November 2026 for an examination period that starts on 3 February 2027, which is the clearest worked example in this market of how far ahead the administrative clock runs.

The practical use of the table is to find the week you are in and read the row above it. If you are at the mock-results row, the useful purchase is a marking clinic, not a content block. If you are at the coursework-deadline row, the useful purchase is supervision on the student's own draft. If you are past the entry deadline and the student is sitting the papers regardless, the useful purchase is timed-paper practice and nothing else. Buying the wrong row is the most common way to waste money on exam preparation in this city.

sections.heading: Where marks actually go missing in the final six weeks
paragraphs: In the last six weeks the marks a Dubai Diploma student loses are rarely marks they do not know how to get. They are marks lost in transit between a correct thought and a written answer, and they are diagnosable from a script in about fifteen minutes. This is why a marking clinic is the highest-value purchase late in the year and a content block is the lowest: the student already has the chemistry, and the eight marks are going somewhere specific.

The commonest leak is command-term drift. A question that says evaluate gets an answer that explains; a question that says outline gets three paragraphs where two sentences were wanted and the time is gone for the next question. The second commonest is working: in Maths and Physics, method marks are awarded for shown steps, and a student who computes in their head forfeits marks on an answer that is correct. The third is presentation in data questions, where uncertainties, units and axis labels carry marks that students treat as decoration.

Timing failure is the one that produces the biggest single drop and the one students deny most. A candidate who has never sat a full paper to time will almost always run out of minutes in the last question, which is frequently the highest-mark question on the paper. Three full timed papers in the last month, marked properly, is worth more than twelve hours of topic revision for a student in this position, and it is cheaper.

The last category is specific to the Diploma: students who have budgeted their revision as six equal subjects. The Diploma total is driven by the Higher Level grades and by the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay bonus points, and a student spending equal time on a secure Standard Level language and a shaky Higher Level science is spending their scarcest resource badly. Allocating revision by marginal grade rather than by subject count is free, and it is the single change that most often moves a total.

sections.heading: What mock results are and are not evidence of
paragraphs: Dubai schools run internal mocks in January and families treat the result as a prediction. It is better understood as a measurement with a known bias. Mock papers are frequently set from previous sessions, marked by the class teacher rather than externally, and graded against boundaries the school has chosen, sometimes deliberately harsh to create urgency. A mock 4 is evidence that something is wrong; it is not evidence of what, and it is not a forecast.

The useful information is inside the script, not on the cover sheet. Two students with the same mock 4 can need entirely different work: one lost marks evenly across every question, which indicates a content gap, and the other scored well until question six and then stopped, which indicates timing. The first needs a term; the second needs three timed papers. Ask the school for the marked script rather than the grade, and have it read by someone who marks to the criteria.

Mocks matter for a second reason that is specific to the Diploma: predicted grades follow them, and predicted grades are what universities see. A student whose predicted grade is one below a conditional offer has a narrow and specific job, which is to produce evidence of movement that a subject teacher can act on. That means marked work at the higher standard, in the subject in question, in time for the school to revisit the prediction. Generic effort does not move a predicted grade; a stack of marked papers sometimes does.

We do not publish grade-movement statistics on this site, and neither should anyone else without the underlying data, a sample size and a method. What we can say is what the process produces: a marked script per week, a written record of the errors that repeat, and a visible change or no change in the mark on the next timed paper. If the mark is not moving after four marked papers, that is information, and the honest response is to change the approach rather than to sell more hours.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the Dubai revision calendar
paragraphs: Ramadan falls inside the Diploma revision window, and in Dubai it changes the school day for everyone regardless of whether a family is fasting. Schools shorten hours, after-school activities thin out, and the useful hours in a day move. A revision plan written in October that assumes a 5pm session every week will break in Ramadan, and the families who cope are the ones who planned the shift rather than reacted to it.

The practical adjustment is to move sessions rather than cancel them. For fasting students the hour before Iftar is the worst slot available and the two hours after it are among the best, which in practice means a session at 8:30pm or 9pm that would be unusual at any other time of year. Non-fasting students often find the shortened school day gives them a better afternoon slot than they have all year. Because lessons are delivered over live video, moving a slot costs nothing but a message, which is a genuine operational advantage in this specific month.

Eid is a hard stop and should be treated as one in the plan. Two consecutive weeks with no sessions late in the revision window is a real loss if nothing is set for them, and a real gain if something is. The pattern that works is to set timed papers for the break rather than content, because a paper can be sat at any hour and marked afterwards, whereas a content session needs both people present and alert.

There is a wider calendar point behind this. Dubai's academic year, the Gregorian examination session, the Hijri calendar and the UAE public holiday schedule do not line up, and the Diploma timetable is set internationally with no reference to any of them. Nobody else writing about exam preparation in this city acknowledges that, which is why so many revision plans in Dubai are built on a calendar the student does not actually live in.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch in coursework
paragraphs: Everything in the Diploma that carries the student's name must be the student's own work, and the IB treats breaches as malpractice with consequences that reach the diploma itself. That makes the boundary around Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay a practical matter rather than an ethical flourish, and it is worth stating exactly where the line sits before any money changes hands.

On the permitted side: explaining what a criterion asks for, teaching the subject content the task requires, discussing whether a research question is viable, teaching how to handle uncertainty in a data set, questioning a line of reasoning, pointing at a paragraph that does not support its claim, and teaching referencing. All of that is teaching, and a tutor who does it well changes a mark substantially, because most students lose Internal Assessment marks to criteria they never understood rather than to a lack of ability.

On the prohibited side, stated plainly: a tutor must not supply text for a student to submit, must not rewrite a passage into its final form, must not select the research question for the student, and must not edit a piece to completion. A provider in this market sells finished Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. We will not do it and we say so on every page, because the honest version of this boundary is a differentiator in this particular search result.

There is a related rule specific to the UAE that parents ask about. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also addresses serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK directly if it affects you, but the direction of travel is clear enough that nobody should be marketing a child's own teacher as a private tutor.

sections.heading: After the results: equivalency, retakes and UAE university entry
paragraphs: Exam preparation has a purpose beyond the grade, and in the UAE that purpose runs through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process. A certificate earned in Dubai has to be recognised before it is usable for a UAE university application, and the requirements differ by curriculum. Four of the ten query clusters researched for this site contain no competitor page that mentions equivalency at all, and one publishes the wrong subject count for the British track.

The British-track rules are published and can be stated precisely. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. For the American track, English proficiency requires an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the Diploma itself, there is a gap we will not fill with a guess. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so no IB equivalency figure appears on this page. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate. Equivalency is also not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or assists with as a service: it is a government process, you apply through the official channel, and no amount of tutoring is required for it.

The retake question comes up on results day every year. The Diploma runs a November session as well as a May one, and a student can re-sit specific subjects rather than the whole diploma. The decision is time-sensitive and is better made before results arrive than after, because the preparation window between a May result and a November session is short and the entry administration sits inside it. If a conditional offer is at risk, speak to the Diploma coordinator about the retake route in the week results land, not a month later.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what that costs
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this site discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to a phone number in another country without saying so. The honest position is that availability is finite and it is worst at exactly the moment Dubai families need it, which is the ten weeks before the May session, in Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Maths, in the 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window.

What we do in that situation is say so and give you the options rather than hold a slot you cannot use. The first option is a different time: an early-morning weekend session or a 7:30am weekday slot before school is unpopular and frequently available, and for a motivated DP2 student it works. The second is a different tutor at the same level with a slightly different background, which is usually a better trade than waiting. The third is a wait with a date attached, which is only sensible if the date is inside the useful window.

There is a fourth option that needs stating clearly. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche Higher Level combination, the tutor who does may be based elsewhere, most often in India, teaching the same Diploma syllabus into Gulf Standard Time over live video. That is disclosed before anything is booked, not after. It is the same syllabus, the same criteria and the same marked papers; what differs is the tutor's location, and a family is entitled to know that before deciding rather than discovering it from an accent on the first call.

The commercial consequence is worth being honest about too. A scarce specialism sits at the top of the market band, so a niche Higher Level requirement booked late is the most expensive version of this purchase available. Booked in the autumn term of DP2 it is an ordinary weekly slot at an ordinary rate. That is the whole argument of this page restated: in Dubai, the variable that moves the number most is not the tutor you choose, it is the week you start.

process.title: Tell us the paper, not the subject
process.description: Send the subject, the level, the session the student is sitting, and the specific paper or topic where marks are being lost. A message that says Chemistry HL, May session, Paper 2 organic and energetics gets a specialist and a realistic hours estimate on the first reply. One that says Chemistry gets a question back.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A recent mock paper or a past paper sat to time is worth more than any description of the problem. We read it against the published criteria and tell you whether this is a content job or a technique job, because that distinction changes the number of hours by a factor of five and therefore changes the cost by the same factor.

process.title: Take the trial lesson
process.description: One 45-minute session per student over live video, with no card details taken. The tutor works through part of the script with the student while you watch or not, as you prefer. You come out of it with a named tutor, a view on hours, and the student's own opinion on whether the person was useful, which matters more than ours.

process.title: Fix the slot and the length of the block
process.description: Agree a weekly time in Gulf Standard Time and a block length taken from the hours table above rather than from a package someone wants to sell. Short blocks that are renewed are better than long ones that are abandoned, and a fixed slot survives the January mock period in a way that a flexible one does not.

process.title: Review on marked papers, not on feeling
process.description: Every few weeks, read the marks on the timed papers rather than asking whether the sessions are going well. If the mark is moving, continue. If it is not moving after four marked papers, the approach needs to change, and the honest response to that is a different plan rather than more hours of the same one.

whyPoints.title: Prices on the page, attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here carries the name of whoever published it and the month it was read. Three of the six pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote dollars. A family cannot plan a budget against a sentence that says rates are competitive.

whyPoints.title: Hours, not packages
whyPoints.description: The hours table is built from five realistic starting points and shows the total, not a monthly figure that hides it. A block should be the length the diagnosis says, and when that length is thirty hours across a term rather than six weeks, we say so instead of selling a package that cannot do the job.

whyPoints.title: Online because the specialist matters more than the postcode
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. The gain is not only the removed travel premium, it is that a family in Dubai Hills can work with the right Higher Level specialist rather than the nearest available tutor.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches criteria, content and technique, and gives feedback on work the student has already produced. A tutor does not supply text for submission or edit a piece to completion. That boundary is published here because at least one provider in this market sells the other thing, and the student carries the risk.

whyPoints.title: Regulators named, accreditation not claimed
whyPoints.description: Dubai private schools sit under KHDA; Abu Dhabi under ADEK; Sharjah under SPEA. Individual private tutors need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation and claims none.

whyPoints.title: Dates we have not verified stay off the page
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson timetable dates here come from those boards' own published pages. No International Baccalaureate session or results date is restated, because the IB's site blocks the automated checking this site uses and an unverified date on thousands of pages is thousands of errors.

faqs.question: How much does IB exam preparation in Dubai cost for a full revision block?
faqs.answer: Work from hours rather than from a monthly figure. A qualified subject tutor online trades in a market band of roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and an IB specialist for Higher Level sciences or Maths runs AED 200 to AED 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A typical ten to fourteen week block at one session a week is ten to fourteen hours, so AED 2,000 to AED 4,200 at specialist rates for one subject. Six weeks at three sessions a week is eighteen hours and costs more for less benefit, because there is no practice time between sessions.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai IB student start revising for the May session?
faqs.answer: The useful window opens in the autumn term of DP2 and closes around ten weeks out, when mocks, predicted grades and internal coursework deadlines fill the evenings. A student who starts in the autumn term can take one session a week, absorb work between sessions, and treat the January mock as a checkpoint rather than an emergency. A student starting six weeks out needs three sessions a week to cover the same ground and gets less from each one. Starting earlier is the cheapest decision available in this market, and it costs nothing to make. Confirm your own session dates with the school's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: How many hours of exam preparation does one HL subject need?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the problem is content or technique, and the two differ by about a factor of five. A student who knows the content and loses marks on method, command terms and timing usually needs ten to fourteen hours across ten to fourteen weeks. A student weak across one whole paper needs sixteen to twenty hours at two sessions a week. A student with whole Higher Level topics never covered needs thirty hours or more across a full term, and the realistic target there is one grade rather than three. One marked past paper tells you which case you are in before you spend anything.

faqs.question: Does the price of exam preparation rise as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: The hourly rate does not move much; the weekly commitment does, which is what raises the total. Dubai schools sit the May session almost universally, so demand for the final ten weeks concentrates into the same window and the 5pm to 7pm slots go first. A late start forces two or three sessions a week instead of one, so the monthly spend can triple while the value per session falls. The scarce specialisms, Higher Level Maths and the Higher Level sciences, are also the ones where the top of the band applies, so a niche late booking is the most expensive version of this purchase.

faqs.question: Why do two Dubai tutors quote very different hourly rates for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Four things usually explain the gap. Format: an in-home visit prices travel into every hour, with the market paying AED 180 to AED 500 against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Specialism: a tutor who marks Higher Level work to the current criteria is scarcer than one who covers the subject generally. Scope: coursework supervision is slower work per hour than paper practice. And session length, because a ninety-minute session quoted at an hourly rate is not what a rate card implies. Ask which of the four explains the number before comparing two quotes.

faqs.question: Can we book exam preparation for three subjects without paying three times over?
faqs.answer: Not really, and it is usually the wrong question. Three subjects means three specialists and three rates, because no single tutor marks Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Maths and English A to current criteria. More importantly, a student with three subjects in trouble ten weeks out has a capacity problem rather than a teaching problem: nine sessions a week leaves no time to practise. The better move is to allocate by marginal grade, pick the one or two subjects where hours convert into points, and use marked timed papers rather than teaching for the rest.

faqs.question: What does an exam preparation session look like in Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: Sessions run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, usually 60 or 90 minutes. Most Dubai families take a slot between 4:30pm and 7:30pm on a weekday, with weekend mornings in heavy demand from the villa communities. The student shares the script or the question set on screen, the tutor annotates it live, and the annotated version is saved for the student afterwards. Work is set between sessions and marked at the next one. IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

faqs.question: Are mock results a reliable guide to how much preparation is needed?
faqs.answer: They are a signal, not a forecast. Dubai schools often set mocks from previous sessions, mark them internally, and apply boundaries they choose themselves, sometimes deliberately severe. The grade tells you something is wrong; the script tells you what. Two students on the same mock 4 can need completely different work, one losing marks evenly across every question, which indicates content, and the other scoring well until question six and stopping, which indicates timing. Ask the school for the marked script rather than the grade, and have it read by someone who marks to the published criteria.

faqs.question: Will exam preparation clash with my child's IA and Extended Essay deadlines?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly, because schools in Dubai set internal coursework deadlines ahead of the board's own, and those deadlines land in the same term as mocks. Plan the collision rather than discover it. Supervision on the student's own draft is slower work than paper practice and is usually priced above it, so fit it into the calendar before the revision block rather than alongside it. A tutor may explain criteria, question reasoning and give feedback on what the student has already produced; a tutor may not supply text for submission or edit a piece to its final form.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect an IB revision timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ramadan falls inside the revision window and changes the school day for every family in Dubai, fasting or not. Schools shorten hours, activities thin out, and the useful part of the day moves. For fasting students the hour before Iftar is the worst available slot and the two hours after it are among the best, so a 8:30pm or 9pm session is normal in this month. Non-fasting students often gain a better afternoon slot from the shortened day. Because lessons run over live video, moving a slot costs a message. For Eid, set timed papers rather than cancelling the fortnight.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to prepare for exams in a group class or one to one?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes. The market pays roughly AED 90 to AED 200 per student per hour for a group of two to four, against AED 150 to AED 450 one to one. The saving is real and the condition is strict: it works only when the students share a school, a subject, a level and a similar starting mark. A pair where one needs content and the other needs technique wastes both of their time. Group formats are also unsuitable for coursework supervision, where the work must stay the individual student's own.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legally do with past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: A tutor can reference official material, cite it, link to it and teach from a student's own legitimately obtained copy. A tutor should not reproduce or supply examination board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because that is copyright infringement and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. In practice this makes little difference to a session: the work is on the student's own script and on questions the student has access to through their school, and official timetables and syllabus pages are linked rather than copied.

faqs.question: Does KHDA set or cap what a private tutor in Dubai may charge?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it regulates schools, including their tuition fees; it did not increase private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year. Individual private tutoring sits elsewhere: the route is a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. There is no published cap on a private tutor's hourly rate. A tuition operation with premises and staff is a different matter and needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute.

faqs.question: What happens if my child needs the November retake session?
faqs.answer: The Diploma runs a November session as well as a May one, and a student can re-sit individual subjects rather than the whole diploma. The decision is time-sensitive, because the preparation window between a May result and a November session is short and the entry administration sits inside it. If a conditional offer is at risk, raise the retake route with the Diploma coordinator in the week results arrive rather than a month later. Confirm all session and entry dates with the school or on ibo.org; no International Baccalaureate dates are restated on this page.

faqs.question: Does my child need the IB diploma attested before applying to a UAE university?
faqs.answer: A certificate earned in Dubai generally has to go through the Ministry of Education's equivalency and attestation process before it is usable for a UAE university application, and the requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so check the Diploma requirement on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for a niche HL subject at exam time?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you book rather than after. The tight combination is a Higher Level science or Higher Level Maths in the 5pm to 7pm window in the final ten weeks. The options are an unpopular but available slot, such as a weekend morning or 7:30am before school; a different tutor at the same level; a marking clinic format instead of weekly teaching; or a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same syllabus into Gulf Standard Time over live video. That last one is disclosed up front, because a family deserves to decide rather than discover.

dubai/ib-exam-preparation.closingBody: The useful first step is not a phone call about rates. Send the subject, the level, the session your child is sitting, and one paper sat to time. A subject specialist reads it against the published criteria and tells you whether this is a content job or a technique job, because that single distinction decides whether you are buying fourteen hours or thirty. From there you get a named tutor, an hours estimate taken from the table on this page, and a 45-minute trial lesson with no card details taken. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If the honest answer is that a block cannot do the job in the weeks left, we will tell you that too.

dubai/ib-examiner-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB Diploma and MYP subjects to Dubai students over live video. Where a tutor has examining experience, the profile says which subject and which component, because an unqualified claim of examiner status tells a parent nothing.

intro.heading: The examiner question, answered without the marketing
paragraphs: An IB examiner is a person appointed by the International Baccalaureate to mark candidate work against a markscheme written for that session. The work arrives anonymously. The markscheme is supplied. Marking is sampled and checked by a team leader, and an examiner whose marking drifts from the standard is corrected or stood down. That is the whole of the job. It does not include setting papers, deciding grade boundaries, seeing future question papers, or knowing anything about an individual candidate in Dubai.

This matters because examiner status is the single most heavily marketed credential in this part of the market, and the premium end of Dubai pricing is built on it. One provider in this search advertises AED 650 an hour at the named-tutor and examiner end. Before paying that, it is worth knowing precisely what the status buys. The honest answer: calibration. Someone who has marked two hundred scripts against a markscheme has a very accurate internal model of where marks are actually awarded, as opposed to where a textbook suggests they ought to be. That is genuinely valuable and it is also not magic.

What it does not buy is access. Examiners work under confidentiality conditions. They cannot share live markschemes, cannot discuss specific scripts, and cannot tell your child what is coming. Any tutor implying otherwise is either exaggerating or describing something that would be a breach. In practice the most useful examiner-experienced tutors talk about marking behaviour in general terms, which is exactly what a student needs, and nothing about any particular paper.

IB Gram's position on this is deliberately narrow. We do not describe a tutor as an IB examiner unless that person's examining is specified by subject and component on their profile, and we do not use examining experience to imply any access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because no such access exists to imply. Where a tutor has that experience it is listed as what it is: evidence of calibration in one subject, for one kind of component. A parent reading a profile should be able to tell, in one line, whether the claim is about a specific paper in a specific subject or whether it is a general impression being sold at a higher hourly rate, and we would rather make that distinction for you than leave you to infer it from a biography written to flatter.

The rest of this page is about the thing the examiner search is really reaching for: markscheme literacy. How points-marked and markband-marked components differ, what a best-fit judgement means, why your school's internal assessment mark can move after moderation, and what to practise. All of it is teachable from published criteria by a tutor who has taught the course, examiner or not. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, as home visits are a service we run only in India.

dubai/ib-examiner-tutor.programmesIntro: Marking works differently across the IB programmes, and the examiner question lands differently in each. The Diploma has external examiners; the Middle Years Programme is mostly internally assessed against criteria; the Primary Years Programme has no external marking at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with externally marked papers plus internally assessed components, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. External papers are marked by appointed examiners against session-specific markschemes; internal assessment is marked by the school and then moderated. This is the only programme where the word examiner has its full technical meaning.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP candidates sit the same papers as candidates everywhere, marked by the same pool of examiners, which is worth saying because parents sometimes assume regional adjustment exists. It does not. What is local is the school's internal assessment calendar and its own marking standard before moderation, and those vary noticeably between IB World Schools in the emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, judged on a best-fit basis against descriptors. Teachers mark; there is no external examiner for most of it, although schools may opt into eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. Understanding best-fit judgement is more useful here than anything an external examiner could offer.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP parents often read a criterion score as a percentage and panic unnecessarily, or relax when they should not. A tutor's first job with an MYP report is to translate the descriptors into plain language and identify which criterion is actually holding the grade down, which is usually one of the four rather than all of them.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Both are assessed against published criteria with word limits, and both are externally marked. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words with a reflective process supervised by the school; the Theory of Knowledge essay is written on a prescribed title with its own limit. Criterion structure matters more here than in any paper-based component.
programmes.countryNote: For Dubai students, the practical difficulty with both is calendar rather than content: supervisors set internal deadlines that differ by school, and the summer between DP1 and DP2 is when Extended Essay progress most often stalls while families travel. A tutor can only support process, questioning and feedback; the writing is entirely the student's.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and additional core elements. The DP courses inside it are examined exactly as they are for Diploma candidates, so marking questions for CP students are really questions about those specific subject papers.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of UAE schools run the Career-related Programme, so local tutor coverage is thin and most matches for it come from our wider pool. The lesson format is unchanged: one-to-one over live video at a time that fits a Dubai evening.

dubai/ib-examiner-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below, each subject is paired with the component where marking behaviour matters most. This is the part of the course where knowing how marks are awarded changes the grade more than knowing additional content would.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Extended-response questions are point-marked against specific acceptable statements, so an answer can be chemically correct and still miss the marking points. The scientific investigation is criterion-marked on a best-fit basis, which rewards a tightly controlled question over an ambitious one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Method and reasoning marks are awarded for stated steps, which means a correct final answer with no visible working scores below its potential. Uncertainty treatment in the investigation is where criterion marks concentrate and where most candidates underprepare.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Long answers are marked against a list of creditable points, so breadth of relevant statements beats depth on one. Candidates who write beautifully about one idea routinely score below candidates who make five accurate points in plainer language.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marking separates method from accuracy, and follow-through credit means a single arithmetic slip need not cost the whole question if the method is visible. HL Paper 3 rewards structured investigation and communication of reasoning as much as the final result.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics answers earn marks for interpretation in context, not only for the calculation. A regression quoted without a sentence about what it means in the scenario leaves interpretation marks unclaimed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry discrete marks for correct axes, labels and shifts, each one individually creditable. HL quantitative questions are point-marked with working credited, while essay-style answers are judged against level descriptors where evaluation separates the top band.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Entirely markband-based, judged holistically against descriptors for analysis, focus, organisation and language. There is no list of points to collect, which is why students trained on content-heavy subjects often misjudge what a strong answer looks like here.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source questions are point-marked for specific analytical moves; essays are markband-judged on argument and use of evidence. Narrating events accurately without arguing a position is the most common way to sit in the middle band indefinitely.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus is separately creditable from tool knowledge, so a correctly drawn framework that never mentions the case material forfeits the application and evaluation marks that decide the grade.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed against criteria on a best-fit basis, with the quality of the knowledge question doing most of the work. Choice of prescribed title effectively sets the ceiling, and no amount of later polishing recovers a poor choice.

sections.heading: What an IB examiner tutor in Dubai can honestly offer
paragraphs: Examining is marking. An appointed examiner receives anonymised candidate work and a markscheme produced for that session, applies it, and has their marking sampled and checked by a team leader. Consistency with the standard is the whole of the quality control. An examiner who marks generously or harshly relative to the standard is pulled back into line or removed from the team, which is why examiner calibration is real: it was enforced on them.

The transferable benefit is therefore a reliable internal model of what gets credited. An experienced marker knows that a particular phrasing earns the mark and a near-miss does not, that a method line left out costs more than an arithmetic slip, that an essay with a thin argument and excellent prose sits lower than most students expect. Those judgements are hard to acquire from a textbook and relatively quick to transfer to a student through marking practice.

The things examining does not confer are worth listing, because they are what the advertising implies. An examiner does not write the papers. An examiner does not set or know grade boundaries, which are determined after marking for each session. An examiner has no sight of future question papers. An examiner cannot discuss any individual script, including a script they marked. And examiner appointments are subject-specific and component-specific: marking one paper in one subject says nothing about another.

So the correct version of the examiner question is not whether a tutor has examined, but whether they can mark your child's work accurately against published criteria and explain the decisions. That is a skill plenty of experienced subject teachers have without having examined, and one some examiners are poor at transferring. Ask for a demonstration rather than a title, and the premium question answers itself.

sections.heading: Two marking models, and why students misjudge one of them
paragraphs: IB components are marked in one of two broadly different ways, and the distinction decides how a student should write. Point-marked questions have a list of creditable statements, and each one earns its mark independently. Markband questions are judged holistically against level descriptors, where the examiner decides which band the answer best fits as a whole and then places it within that band.

Students handle point-marked questions badly in a predictable way: they write one idea beautifully. In a question worth five marks against five creditable points, an elegant essay about the first point scores one. The correct behaviour is to make the required number of distinct, accurate, relevant statements, which often means writing in plainer language than a student thinks is appropriate. Science and quantitative subjects are full of these questions, and the fix is almost purely behavioural.

Markband questions fail differently. Here a student who collects points produces a list that no band describes well, because the descriptors reward sustained argument, focus and organisation rather than coverage. English, History essays, Theory of Knowledge and most criterion-marked coursework work this way. A candidate trained on point-marked habits writes something comprehensive and lands mid-band, and no amount of additional content moves it.

The practical consequence for tutoring is that a student needs to know which model they are facing before they start writing, and most can tell from the mark allocation and the command term within a few seconds of practice. Teaching that recognition is quick. Not teaching it leaves a student optimising for the wrong thing in half their papers.

sections.heading: Why your school's internal assessment mark can change
paragraphs: Internal assessment is marked by the school against the published criteria and then moderated by the IB. Moderation compares the school's marking against the standard using a sample, and can adjust the whole cohort's marks up or down. This is routine and it is not a judgement about an individual student. It is also the thing that surprises Dubai parents most, because a mark that appeared on a school report in February can arrive differently in July.

Two consequences follow. First, a school mark is a prediction, not a result, and a family planning around it should treat it as such. Second, the way to protect a mark is to make it unambiguously defensible against the descriptors, because a piece of work that sits clearly inside a band is less exposed to adjustment than one that sits on a boundary. That is a real argument for working on criterion clarity rather than on general polish.

The practical work is unglamorous. Does the research question name the variables? Does the method state what is controlled and how? Is each criterion's evidence actually present and findable, rather than implied across several pages? Does the work stay within the stated limit? A piece that answers yes to all of those is doing what moderation checks for, and a tutor can help a student get there without writing a word of it.

What a tutor cannot do is tell you how your school historically fares in moderation, predict an adjustment, or intervene in it. Those are matters for the school's IB coordinator, who is also the person who would request an enquiry upon results if a grade looked wrong after publication. Any tutor offering to influence a moderated mark is describing something that does not exist.

sections.heading: How to check an examiner claim in one conversation
paragraphs: Verification here is awkward, because the honest answer to the obvious request is no. You cannot ask to see marked scripts, because confidentiality forbids it. You cannot ask for a markscheme, for the same reason. A tutor who produces either should worry you rather than reassure you. So the check has to be about specificity and about demonstration.

Specificity first. Ask which subject, which component, and roughly which period. An honest answer sounds like: Biology Paper 2, for several sessions up to a stated year. A vague answer that avoids naming the component is usually a signal that the status is being borrowed from somewhere, perhaps from an agency's pool rather than from this individual. Ask also whether the appointment is current, because examiner teams change and a lapsed appointment is still useful experience but should not be stated in the present tense.

Then demand a demonstration, which is the part that actually matters. Hand over an unmarked answer of your child's, or a past-paper answer written in the trial lesson, and ask the tutor to mark it and explain each mark. A calibrated marker will be quick, decisive and specific, and will explain why the near-miss phrasing did not earn credit. An uncalibrated one will give generous marks and general praise. You do not need subject knowledge to tell the difference, because the first sounds like a rule being applied and the second sounds like an opinion.

Finally, treat the status as one input rather than the decision. The best outcome for most students is a tutor who has taught the course to examination and can mark accurately against published criteria. Where examining experience sits on top of that, it is a bonus. Where it is offered instead of it, it is a marketing line with a price attached.

sections.heading: What beats examiner status: markscheme literacy the student owns
paragraphs: The deepest version of this advantage is not a tutor who knows how marks are awarded. It is a student who knows. A candidate who can look at a question and predict what the markscheme wants is self-correcting in every piece of work between now and the examination, which no number of paid hours replicates.

Building that takes a specific routine. The student writes an answer under time. The student then marks it against the published criteria, awarding and justifying every mark, before seeing any model answer. The tutor marks the same answer separately. Then the two compare, and every disagreement is examined: why did the student think that sentence earned credit? What was the examiner-style reason it did not? Disagreements are the content of the lesson.

Two things happen over four or five rounds. The student's marking converges towards the tutor's, which is the measurable outcome, and the student's writing changes to produce creditable material, which is the real outcome. Most students start by over-marking their own work substantially. Watching that gap close is one of the clearest leading indicators available, and it is visible long before a school grade moves.

Everything in that routine uses published criteria, past papers in the public domain and the student's own writing. No restricted material is needed, which is why a well-prepared subject specialist can run it. Published syllabus documents, past papers and criteria are referenced and linked from official sources rather than redistributed, since reproducing board material is a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, an integrity problem as well.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, by component
paragraphs: Lost marks are not randomly distributed. Across Dubai DP work we see the same handful of patterns, and they cluster by component type rather than by subject. Short structured questions lose marks to incomplete statements: the student knows the idea and expresses two-thirds of it. Extended responses lose marks to command-term misreads and to argument that is asserted rather than evidenced. Mathematics loses marks to absent working, which forfeits method credit and blocks follow-through.

Coursework loses marks earlier than anyone expects, at the design stage, where a research question too broad to control caps several criteria at once. Oral components lose marks to under-rehearsal of structure rather than to language, since students who have practised the shape of the response handle the unexpected text or prompt far better. And every component loses marks to the word and time limits, which are hard edges rather than guidelines.

The diagnostic value of knowing this is that it turns a vague worry into a short list of checks. Look at a marked script and ask which of these patterns it shows. Usually one dominates, and that one is worth four sessions of attention. Spreading the same four sessions across everything the syllabus contains produces much less movement, which is the central argument for diagnosing before teaching.

A caution on figures: component weightings and limits vary by subject and change when a subject guide is revised. The table below gives the shape of the thing, and your child's own subject guide and the school's assessment calendar are the authorities. Ask the school's IB coordinator if a weighting matters to a decision you are making.

sections.heading: What the premium end of the Dubai market charges, and when it is worth it
paragraphs: Published rates in Dubai put examiner-branded tutoring at the top of the market. BartyED advertises AED 650 an hour at the premium named end. Below that, exam-level IB and IGCSE specialists run around AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 and beyond for specialist exam-year work. Qualified subject tutors online sit roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online provision advertises from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52.

Those figures are other providers' published prices with their names attached, read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's price list, and the spread is the useful information: the premium band is roughly double the specialist band, and the question is what the extra buys. Our honest answer is scarcity and reassurance rather than a different teaching method. The marking calibration an examiner brings is real, and it is also transferable from a specialist who marks accurately against published criteria.

Where the premium is defensible is a narrow case: a candidate already performing near the top of a subject, where the remaining marks are in judgement rather than knowledge, and where the component is one the tutor has specifically marked. Where it is not defensible is the much more common case of a student losing marks to command terms, absent working or a badly scoped internal assessment. Those are mid-band problems with mid-band solutions, and paying premium rates for them buys nothing extra.

In-home tutoring in Dubai sits in its own band of roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, per Bestimate and local home-tutor listings. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so that band is context rather than an option we sell. Monthly packages advertised locally include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

sections.heading: Scheduling, delivery and honest coverage for Dubai families
paragraphs: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time. Marking practice suits this format unusually well, because the answer, the criteria and the marks can all sit on one screen and be saved. After each session a short written note names what was covered and the next target. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India, and we would rather state that than let a page imply otherwise.

On timing, the practical Dubai constraints are the school run, after-school activities and the evening homework window, which is why most of our sessions land between 16:30 and 20:30. During Ramadan many families move sessions to a post-Iftar slot, and that is straightforward to arrange with notice. Gulf Standard Time also sits conveniently between South Asia and Europe, which widens the pool of specialists available at a Dubai-friendly hour.

Coverage is uneven and worth stating. Where a request is for a specific component of a specific subject, and particularly where examining experience in that component is wanted, the pool is small and the match may take one to two weeks. In the February to May window it can take longer, because the whole emirate wants the same thing simultaneously. If we cannot cover it, we say so rather than substituting a general tutor and leaving you to discover the gap.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour. The format and subject depth are unchanged. Where we think the request itself is wrong, for instance a premium examiner match for a student whose marks are being lost to absent working, we will say that too and propose the cheaper thing that will actually help.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: Which paper, which internal assessment, which oral. Marking behaviour differs sharply between components, and a request phrased at subject level gets matched less accurately than one phrased at component level. Include the school and the assessment calendar if you have it.

process.title: We state what the tutor has actually marked
process.description: Where a tutor has examining experience, we name the subject and the component and whether it is current. Where they do not, we say that and describe their teaching history instead. We do not advertise unevidenced examiner status at any price.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson with a marking demonstration
process.description: A full first lesson at no cost. Hand over an unmarked answer and ask the tutor to mark it and justify each mark. That demonstration tells you more about calibration than any biography, and it costs nothing to run.

process.title: Set a marking-practice routine
process.description: The student writes, self-marks against published criteria, then compares with the tutor's marking. Disagreements become the lesson. We agree how often this runs and what else the sessions cover, in writing, before the first paid hour.

process.title: Review the convergence at session four
process.description: The measurable indicator is how far the student's self-marking has moved towards accurate marking. If it has not moved, we change the approach or the tutor. If it has, the writing usually follows, and we set the next target.

process.title: Escalate to the school where that is the right route
process.description: Moderation outcomes, results enquiries and assessment calendars belong to the school's IB coordinator. We will tell you when a question is theirs rather than ours, including when it means you do not need more tutoring.

whyPoints.title: We do not sell unevidenced examiner status
whyPoints.description: A tutor is described as having examining experience only where the subject and component are specified on their profile. We never use examining to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because no such access exists.

whyPoints.title: Calibration taught, not just claimed
whyPoints.description: Marking practice is a format we run deliberately: the student marks their own work against published criteria and compares with the tutor. Convergence is measurable, and it transfers the judgement to the person sitting the paper.

whyPoints.title: Published criteria only
whyPoints.description: Everything we teach from is in the public domain or supplied by the student's own school. We link official syllabus and past-paper sources rather than redistributing board material, and no tutor shares restricted markschemes.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where the premium helps
whyPoints.description: We will tell you when a cheaper specialist match solves the actual problem. A student losing marks to absent working does not need the top of the market, and pretending otherwise would be easy money and bad advice.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, never implied as ours
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is another provider's published rate, named and dated. We do not present market bands as our prices and we publish no statistics about our own results that we cannot evidence.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: Component-specific requests take longer to match, especially between February and May. If we cannot cover it from UAE-based tutors we say so and explain where the match would come from, before you have paid anything.

faqs.question: What does an IB examiner actually do during a marking session?
faqs.answer: They receive anonymised candidate work and a markscheme written for that session, apply it, and have their marking sampled and checked by a team leader. Consistency with the published standard is the entire quality-control mechanism, and an examiner whose marking drifts is corrected or removed from the team. They do not write papers, do not set grade boundaries, and do not see questions in advance. They also cannot discuss any individual script, including ones they marked. Understanding that narrow job description is the fastest way to judge which examiner claims in Dubai advertising are meaningful and which are decoration.

faqs.question: Is an examiner-experienced tutor better than an experienced subject teacher?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Examining builds accurate calibration about where marks are actually awarded, which is genuinely useful and hard to get from a textbook. Teaching the course to examination builds knowledge of how students learn it, where they stall and how to sequence a recovery. The best match usually has both, and plenty of excellent teachers have the second without the first. What settles it is a demonstration: hand over an unmarked answer and ask the tutor to mark it and justify every mark. Decisive, specific marking with reasons beats any title on a profile.

faqs.question: Can an examiner tutor tell my child what is on the next paper?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so should end the conversation. Examiners mark completed scripts; they have no sight of future question papers, and they work under confidentiality conditions that prohibit sharing markschemes or discussing specific scripts. Anyone implying advance knowledge is either exaggerating for effect or describing a breach. The useful version of that help is entirely legitimate and entirely different: teaching your child to predict what a markscheme will reward for a given command term and mark allocation, which is a skill they can apply to any question on any paper.

faqs.question: How do I verify that a tutor has really examined for the IB?
faqs.answer: Ask three narrow questions: which subject, which component, and whether the appointment is current or historical. An honest answer names a specific paper and a period. A vague answer that avoids the component usually means the status is borrowed from an agency's pool rather than held by this individual. Do not ask for scripts or markschemes, because nobody is permitted to show them, and a tutor who produces either is a warning rather than a reassurance. Then ask for a live marking demonstration on your child's work, which is the only check that tests the thing you are actually buying.

faqs.question: Are IB papers marked by collecting points or by overall impression?
faqs.answer: Both, depending on the component, and the distinction changes how a student should write. Point-marked questions have a list of creditable statements, each earning its mark independently, so making five plain accurate points beats writing elegantly about one. Markband components are judged holistically against level descriptors, where sustained argument, focus and organisation decide the band and extra coverage adds nothing. Science short questions and mathematics method marks sit in the first category; English papers, History essays and Theory of Knowledge sit in the second. Many students optimise for the wrong model in half their papers without ever being told.

faqs.question: What is a best-fit judgement in IB marking?
faqs.answer: It is how markband and criterion components are assessed. Rather than adding up points, the marker reads the whole response, decides which level descriptor it best matches overall, and then places it within that band. A response does not have to meet every phrase in a descriptor to sit in that band, and strength in one area does not offset a clear gap in another. The practical consequence for a student is that polish does not move a band; the descriptor's named qualities do. That is why criterion-mapping a piece of coursework before writing is worth more than editing afterwards.

faqs.question: Why did my child's internal assessment mark change after it was submitted?
faqs.answer: Internal assessment is marked by the school against the published criteria and then moderated by the IB, which compares the school's marking against the standard using a sample and can adjust the whole cohort up or down. It is routine and it is not a judgement about one student. The practical lesson is that a school mark is a prediction rather than a result, and that work sitting clearly inside a band is less exposed to adjustment than work on a boundary. Questions about a specific moderation outcome belong with the school's IB coordinator, who is also the person who can request a results enquiry.

faqs.question: Can a tutor show my child an official IB markscheme?
faqs.answer: No. Markschemes are confidential to the marking team for a session, and sharing one would breach the conditions an examiner works under. It is also unnecessary. Published assessment criteria, descriptors and past papers from official sources contain enough to teach marking judgement properly, and that is what our tutors work from. We reference and link official syllabus and past-paper pages rather than redistributing board documents, because reproducing them is a copyright problem and, in the case of unreleased material, an academic-integrity problem for the candidate as well.

faqs.question: Why do two students with similar knowledge get different IB marks?
faqs.answer: Usually because one writes creditable material and the other writes correct material. In point-marked questions a partially stated idea earns nothing, so a student who knows the concept but expresses two-thirds of it loses the mark. In markband components a student who lists accurate content without an argument sits mid-band regardless of how much they know. Mathematics adds a third route: a correct answer with no visible working forfeits method credit and blocks follow-through. None of those gaps is a knowledge gap, which is why they respond quickly to marking practice rather than to more content.

faqs.question: Does examining experience help with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: It can help with criterion judgement, since the Extended Essay is externally assessed against published criteria with a 4,000-word limit. What it cannot change is the boundary around the work. The essay must be the student's own, the school supervisor is formally responsible for the process and its reflective sessions, and a tutor's role is questioning, criterion-based feedback and research-method critique. The most valuable intervention happens before writing, on the research question's scope, and that needs a subject specialist who understands what can be investigated, not necessarily someone who has marked essays.

faqs.question: Should we ask the school for an enquiry upon results if a grade looks wrong?
faqs.answer: That decision sits with the school's IB coordinator, who submits any formal enquiry; a tutor has no role in it and cannot influence an outcome. What a tutor can usefully do beforehand is help you understand whether the result is surprising for defensible reasons, by looking at the marked mock evidence and the pattern of the student's work. Ask the coordinator about the process, the deadline and any cost implication, because those are set by the board and the school rather than negotiable. Treat any tutor who offers to get a grade changed as making a claim they cannot support.

faqs.question: How can my child learn to mark their own work accurately?
faqs.answer: With a routine that takes four or five rounds to bite. The student writes an answer under time, then marks it against the published criteria, awarding and justifying every mark before seeing any model answer. The tutor marks the same answer separately. Then they compare, and every disagreement is examined in detail. Most students over-mark their own work substantially at first, and watching that gap close is one of the clearest progress indicators available, visible well before a school grade moves. The eventual payoff is self-correction in every piece of work between now and the examination.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram advertise tutors as IB examiners?
faqs.answer: Only where the examining is specified by subject and component on that tutor's profile, and never as an implied route to marking, boundaries or paper content. We take that position because the alternative is the most common overstatement in this market and because unverifiable credential claims are a liability for a platform and a false signal for a parent. If examining experience in your child's exact component is what you want and we cannot evidence it, we will say so and propose a specialist who can demonstrate accurate marking instead.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a Dubai student to a tutor for a specific DP component?
faqs.answer: Subject-level requests at common levels are usually matched within a few days. Component-specific requests, particularly where examining experience in that component is wanted, take longer and can run to one or two weeks, with the February to May window the tightest because demand across the emirate peaks at once. If no UAE-based specialist is free we say so before you commit and match from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, keeping the session at a Dubai-friendly hour on Gulf Standard Time. The subject depth and the one-to-one online format do not change.

dubai/ib-examiner-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the marking, not the title
dubai/ib-examiner-tutor.closingBody: If you are considering an IB examiner tutor in Dubai, the useful test takes twenty minutes. Ask which subject and component the tutor has marked and whether that is current. Then hand over an unmarked answer of your child's and ask for the marks with a reason attached to each one. Decisive, specific marking against published criteria is what you are actually paying for, and it is visible immediately. Lessons from IB Gram run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with marking practice built in and a written note after every session. Tell us the subject, the level and the component, and we will tell you honestly what we can evidence.

dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.heroSubtitle: IB holiday tuition in Dubai is worth exactly as much as the window it is bought for. A one-week autumn half-term, a two-week winter break, a spring break three weeks before the May session and a nine-week summer are four different jobs, and most of the disappointment in this market comes from buying the wrong one. This page maps the Dubai private-school year against the Diploma timeline and says what each break can and cannot repair. Lessons run over live video.
