dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.tutorsIntro: Holiday blocks need tutors who are free in the window rather than tutors who are free in term time, and those are different lists. Tell us the break, the subject and the time zone the family will be in, and the list below narrows to people who can hold a daily slot for that fortnight.

intro.heading: Buy the window, not the hours
paragraphs: Dubai families book holiday tuition for a reason that makes sense and then buy it in a shape that does not. The reason is sound: during term, a Diploma student has six subjects, coursework, activities and a school day that ends at three, and there is no room in the week for anything that takes a serious run at a problem. A break removes all of that at once. A fortnight with nothing scheduled is the only time in a Dubai school year when a student can sit down with an absent topic and actually learn it.

The shape usually goes wrong because the window is treated as interchangeable. A one-week autumn half-term, a two-week winter break, a spring break landing a few weeks before the May session and a summer of roughly nine weeks are four different instruments. The autumn half-term is long enough to start an Internal Assessment properly and too short to rebuild a term of Chemistry. The spring break is long enough to drill timed papers and far too late to teach content. The summer is the only window big enough for a genuine rebuild, and it is the one most families leave empty.

The Dubai calendar itself is a planning fact rather than a detail. KHDA publishes a unified academic calendar for private schools, which is why Dubai families across different curricula tend to break at the same time and why holiday tutor availability in this city is lumpier than in most markets. Everyone wants the same fortnight. Schools whose year starts in April run on a different cycle, and the Hijri calendar moves Ramadan and Eid through the Gregorian year, so a plan that worked last year may not map onto this one.

There is a second reason holiday blocks underdeliver, and it is about what happens between the sessions rather than during them. A break session that ends with no work set is a session that has to start again from the beginning three days later. The students who come out of a fortnight visibly further forward are the ones who had something to do on the days in between: a problem set, a timed paper, a draft paragraph of their own, a list of definitions. The block is the scaffolding; the student does the building.

This page therefore goes window by window. It maps the Dubai school year against the Diploma timeline, gives a subject-by-subject bridge for the summer before DP1, deals with the winter break and the January mocks together because they are one problem, explains why the spring break is a technique window and nothing else, works through Ramadan and Eid, and sets out the practical rules for running sessions while a family is travelling. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on whatever time zone the family is in; IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai.

dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.programmesIntro: Holiday work means something different at each point in the Diploma, so the four blocks below are stages rather than programmes. A student entering DP1 in August has a bridge to build; a DP2 student in the spring break has papers to sit; an MYP student has criteria to learn; and the Diploma Core runs across both years with deadlines that always land in a holiday.

programmes.name: The summer before DP1
programmes.ageRange: Ages 15-16 · the break after MYP 5 or Year 11
programmes.description: The most valuable and least used window in the whole two-year Diploma. A student arriving in DP1 with secure algebra, a working method for taking notes from a textbook, and some idea of what a command term is will spend the autumn learning Diploma content rather than remediating Year 11. Nine weeks is enough to close a genuine gap in one or two subjects properly rather than patching it later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai makes this window unusually important because so many students change curriculum at 16. A student moving from IGCSE into the Diploma, or from an Indian-curriculum school into an IB continuum school, meets a different assessment culture rather than harder content: criteria instead of mark schemes, extended writing instead of short answers, and an expectation of independent reading that Year 11 did not require. That transition is teachable in a summer and expensive to leave until October.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: The year where coursework starts and nothing has a deadline that feels urgent yet. Internal Assessment topics are chosen, the Extended Essay research question is settled, and the subject content doubles in depth. Holiday work in DP1 is almost always about getting ahead of a coursework deadline or closing a topic the student quietly did not follow in October, both of which are much cheaper to deal with now than in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: The DP1 autumn half-term and winter break are the two windows Dubai families most often skip, on the reasonable grounds that nothing is on fire. The cost of skipping them surfaces the following January, when a DP2 student is doing mock revision and coursework rewriting in the same fortnight. A single half-term block spent on an Internal Assessment research question in DP1 removes one of the two jobs from that fortnight entirely.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: Mocks in the winter, predicted grades shortly after, internal coursework deadlines through the autumn and spring, and the May session at the end. Holiday work here narrows as the year goes on: a winter block can still teach content, a spring block can only drill technique, and by the final weeks the only useful holiday work is timed papers marked against the published criteria.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session almost without exception, which compresses the whole final-year calendar into the Gregorian second and third terms and makes the spring break the single most contested tutoring window in the city. Slots in that fortnight go early, and the families who get the ones they want booked them in January. We do not restate International Baccalaureate session dates on this page; confirm them with your school's Diploma coordinator.

programmes.name: The Diploma Core: TOK, EE and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service run alongside the six subjects and carry their own deadlines, which schools set well ahead of the board's. The Core is the part of the Diploma most often worked on during holidays, because it needs long uninterrupted stretches rather than weekly hours, and because the bonus points it carries are the cheapest points on the certificate to secure.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically set an Extended Essay first-draft deadline in the DP2 autumn and a Theory of Knowledge essay deadline in the spring, both landing close to a break. A tutor may explain the criteria, question a line of argument and give feedback on a draft the student has already produced. A tutor may not supply text for submission or edit a piece to its final form, and that boundary holds in a holiday block exactly as it does in term time.

dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.subjectsIntro: What a holiday block can realistically achieve differs sharply by subject, because subjects fail differently. In Maths and the sciences a fortnight can close a topic. In the essay subjects a fortnight produces a method rather than content. In the languages it produces vocabulary volume and very little else. These are the ten Dubai families book break blocks for most often.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The best holiday subject there is, because the content is sequential and a fortnight of daily work genuinely closes a topic. Calculus and trigonometric identities are the usual targets. The gain is measurable at the end of the block on a timed question set, which is rarely true of the humanities over the same two weeks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics responds well to a break block because the techniques are discrete and testable: hypothesis tests, regression, distributions, each learnable in a session and checkable the next day. The HL additions of matrices and graph theory are also self-contained enough that a fortnight produces a usable grasp rather than a vague acquaintance.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and energetics are the two topics most often rebuilt over a Dubai winter break, and both reward daily contact. The Internal Assessment is the other common holiday job: a break is long enough for a student to settle a research question and plan a method, which during term competes with five other subjects.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics in DP1 and fields in DP2 are the holiday targets. A fortnight is enough to make a student fluent in one of them, and fluency here is worth more than coverage because the papers recombine the same few ideas. The practical write-up skills that carry Internal Assessment marks also respond well to concentrated work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The one science where a holiday block should not be spent on content. The volume is too large to compress and the marks are in command-term discipline and data handling. Two weeks of marked questions and a vocabulary regime does more than two weeks of topic teaching, which is the opposite of what most families book.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram fluency is buildable in a fortnight and it is where the marks are: a correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns what prose cannot recover. HL Paper 3 calculation practice is similarly suited to a block. The commentary portfolio is the other standard holiday job, worked as feedback on the student's own writing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A break block is best spent on the pre-released case study where one applies, because it rewards reading time that term never offers. Beyond that, the useful work is application discipline: taking a tool and applying it to the named company in the stimulus rather than explaining it in the abstract, which is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Holiday blocks here produce a method, not knowledge. Two weeks of guided analysis on unseen non-literary texts builds a repeatable approach to Paper 1 that a student then applies for the rest of the year. The HL Essay is the other natural break job, as feedback on the student's own drafting rather than on an outline someone else wrote.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work is the right holiday target because it is a transferable skill rather than a body of content: provenance, purpose, value and limitation, practised across unfamiliar sources until the structure is automatic. The HL regional option reading is the other good use of a long break, since it needs stretches of time term time does not contain.

subjects.name: Spanish B, French B and Arabic B
subjects.description: The honest position is that a fortnight raises vocabulary volume and oral confidence and does little to grammar accuracy, which needs months of contact. A break block is well spent on the individual oral format and on building a working bank of themes, and poorly spent trying to repair tense usage that has been shaky for two years.

dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and how they actually use a break
dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.regionsIntro: Holiday patterns differ by community in this city more than term-time patterns do, because travel habits differ. Since lessons run over live video, the only questions an area raises for us are when a family is likely to be in Dubai and what time zone they will be in when they are not.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: A high proportion of families here spend a large part of the summer outside the UAE, often across several countries in one break. Blocks need a time zone agreed per week rather than once, and travel weeks are better used for set work than for live sessions.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer family housing with a strong pattern of staying in Dubai for the shorter breaks and travelling for the summer. Autumn half-term and winter break slots are in heavier demand here than the city average, and the summer is quieter.

regions.name: Jumeirah Islands and Emirates Living
regions.note: Established villa communities where the summer departure is long and the return is late, often days before term restarts. A bridge block for a student entering DP1 needs to be front-loaded into July rather than planned for late August.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Short commutes to several IB schools, and families who tend to stay through the shorter breaks. The winter break here is the most productive window of the year, and the one where daily slots are easiest to hold.

regions.name: Al Barari and Dubailand
regions.note: Spread-out villa communities with long school-bus routes in term time, which means a break removes two hours a day from a student's schedule rather than one. A daily morning slot works unusually well here during a block.

regions.name: Town Square and Serena
regions.note: Younger families, many on their first Diploma cohort, with a high rate of mid-year arrivals into Dubai schools. Transition work over a break is the dominant request: catching up on content a student missed by joining in the second term.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Apartment communities close to IB continuum schools on the creek side of the city. Students here often stay in Dubai for the shorter breaks, which makes the half-term a realistic window for starting an Internal Assessment.

regions.name: Tilal Al Ghaf and Dubai South
regions.note: Newer developments at the edge of the city where term-time evening sessions are constrained by long bus journeys. A break is therefore worth proportionally more here, because the student gets back the time the commute takes.

schoolClusters.city: Al Jaddaf, Dubai Festival City and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: IB continuum schools on the creek side of the city, where many students have been in the programme since the Primary Years. Break work here is usually coursework-led rather than content-led, because the content culture is familiar and the Core deadlines are not.

schoolClusters.city: The Sustainable City, Dubai Investments Park and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: Newer IB provision in the southern corridor, with smaller Diploma cohorts. Where a subject has one teacher, a holiday block with an outside specialist is often the only concentrated subject time a student gets all year.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and Arabian Ranches
schoolClusters.note: Long-established Diploma cohorts with competitive predicted-grade environments and families who travel extensively in the summer. Blocks here are frequently run across two or three time zones in a single break.

dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.modesIntro: Four shapes a break block can take. The difference between them is not the number of hours but the spacing, and spacing is what determines whether a student can use the work between sessions. A fortnight at five sessions a week is a different product from a fortnight at two.

modes.title: Daily intensive over one or two weeks
modes.description: Four or five sessions a week for the length of the break, on one subject or one coursework task. The only format that closes a content topic properly, because each session builds on yesterday's rather than on something from a week ago. Demanding, and best suited to a student who has asked for it rather than one who has been signed up.
bullets: Four or five sessions a week, same time each day
One subject or one task per block, not three
Work set for the day between every pair of sessions
A timed assessment at the end to show what moved

modes.title: Light-touch maintenance through a long break
modes.description: One or two sessions a week across a nine-week summer, designed to stop decay rather than to teach. Cheaper per week than an intensive and far more sustainable. It works best when the sessions are anchored to a weekly piece of produced work, because without that the format turns into a nine-week conversation.
bullets: One or two sessions a week, spread across the break
Each session built on something the student produced
Suits a student who is broadly secure and will drift
Easy to pause for a travel week and resume

modes.title: Transition bridge into DP1
modes.description: A summer block for a student moving from MYP 5, Year 11 or another curriculum into the Diploma. The content is partly subject knowledge and partly the assessment culture: criteria rather than mark schemes, command terms, extended writing, and the reading habit the Diploma assumes. Measured against the first term rather than against a test.

modes.title: Travelling block across time zones
modes.description: Sessions that follow the family rather than the city. A block agreed in Dubai can run from London, Mumbai, Nairobi or Toronto with the slot renegotiated per week. The constraint is a reliable connection and a quiet hour, not a location. Travel weeks with neither are better spent on set work than on a session nobody can concentrate in.

sections.heading: What holiday tuition is for in a Dubai school year
paragraphs: IB holiday tuition in Dubai is concentrated one-to-one work bought for a specific break window, and its value comes from the one thing a break gives that term time cannot: uninterrupted days. During term a Diploma student is carrying six subjects, the Core, activities and a school day that ends in the mid afternoon. Nothing in that week has room for a serious run at a topic the student has not understood since October. A fortnight with nothing scheduled does.

That is the whole argument, and it has a consequence most families miss. Because the value is in the days rather than in the hours, spacing matters more than volume. Ten hours spread over two weeks at five sessions a week closes a Chemistry topic. The same ten hours at one session a week over ten weeks does not, because each session spends its first twenty minutes recovering ground. The break is the only time of year when the daily shape is available, which is why it should be used for the jobs that need it.

It also means the jobs that do not need daily contact are a poor use of a block. Vocabulary drilling, reading, past-paper sitting and note consolidation are all things a student can do alone, and a break is a good time for them. Paying for live sessions to supervise them wastes the window. The useful rule is to spend the block on what requires a teacher in the room and to set everything else for the days between.

Finally, holiday work in Dubai is shaped by a calendar most families only half know. KHDA publishes a unified academic calendar for private schools, which is why a tutor's availability in this city collapses in the same fortnight every year, and schools whose academic year starts in April run a different cycle entirely. Add the Hijri calendar moving Ramadan and Eid through the Gregorian year and the planning rule becomes simple: check the current published calendar rather than repeating last year's plan.

sections.heading: The four Dubai break windows and what each one can repair
paragraphs: A Dubai private-school year contains four usable breaks, and they are not interchangeable. The table below pairs each one with where a Diploma student actually is at that point and with the job that window can realistically complete. The second column is deliberately approximate: confirm the current dates against the KHDA unified calendar and your own school's published year, especially if the school's year starts in April.

The pattern across the table is that the windows get narrower in purpose as the Diploma progresses. In DP1 almost any break can still teach content, because there is time afterwards to consolidate it. By the DP2 spring break, content teaching is no longer a sensible purchase: there is not enough time left to make unfamiliar material secure under examination pressure, and the attempt usually displaces the technique work that would have paid. The same number of hours is worth more or less depending entirely on where it sits on this table.

The autumn half-term is the most under-used window in the Dubai year and the one with the best return per hour in DP1. It is about a week, which is too short for a topic rebuild and exactly right for settling an Internal Assessment research question, planning a method, or building the Extended Essay reading list. Those are jobs that otherwise get done badly in November alongside everything else, and doing them properly in October removes a job from the January fortnight that is already overloaded.

The summer is the opposite case: the largest window and the one most often left entirely empty. Nine weeks is enough for a genuine rebuild in one subject, or a transition bridge for a student entering DP1, or both at a light cadence. Families hesitate because the break feels like a break, which is fair. The compromise that works is two sessions a week for six of the nine weeks, which costs a small part of the holiday and prevents the September restart from being a remediation exercise.

sections.heading: The summer before DP1: a subject-by-subject bridge
paragraphs: The summer between the end of Year 11 or MYP 5 and the start of DP1 is the highest-return tutoring window in the whole Diploma, and Dubai families use it less than any other. The reason it pays is that the Diploma does not start harder; it starts differently. A student who spends the autumn term learning what a criterion is, how a command term behaves and how much independent reading is expected is learning the assessment culture instead of the subject, and the subject does not wait.

The gaps are specific and they are predictable by route. A student coming from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE into Mathematics Analysis and Approaches meets proof, radians and a far heavier algebraic manipulation load than Extended-tier work required. A student from the Middle Years Programme has criteria fluency already and often an algebra deficit, because MYP assessment does not drill procedure the way an IGCSE paper does. A student from an Indian-curriculum school usually has strong procedural mathematics and little experience of extended writing. Each needs a different fortnight.

The sciences divide the same way. The IGCSE-to-Diploma science gap is less about content than about explanation: Diploma papers want mechanism and reasoning where IGCSE accepted a correct statement. The Group 1 and Group 3 subjects need the opposite preparation, which is volume of reading and a method for making notes from a book rather than from a slide deck. Nobody arrives with all of these, and nobody needs all of them: the first session of a bridge block is spent finding out which two matter for this student.

A bridge block is measured against the first term rather than against a test, which makes it harder to sell and no less worth buying. The visible signs that it worked appear in October: the student follows the first Internal Assessment briefing, knows what the criteria are asking, can read a chapter and come out with usable notes, and is not spending evenings relearning Year 11 algebra. The table below sets out the common routes into DP1 from Dubai schools and what each one typically has to close.

sections.heading: The winter break is really about the January mocks
paragraphs: Dubai schools run internal mock examinations for DP2 students in January, and the winter break sits directly in front of them. That single fact determines what the fortnight is worth. A winter block spent on general revision produces a mock result that feels slightly better. A winter block spent on the two papers the student is weakest at, with full papers sat to time, produces a mock result the school can act on when predicted grades are set a few weeks later.

The order that works is narrow and unpopular. Pick one subject, or at most two. Identify the specific paper, not the subject: a student is rarely weak at Physics, but frequently weak at the extended-response paper while competent at the multiple-choice one. Sit a full paper to time in the first days of the break, mark it properly, and spend the remaining sessions on the errors that paper exposed. Sit a second full paper at the end. Two marked papers a fortnight apart is the most informative thing a family can hold going into mocks.

The common alternative, which is to book three subjects for the fortnight, reliably underdelivers. It produces nine or twelve sessions, no daily continuity in any one subject, and a student too tired to work between them. A Diploma total is driven by the Higher Level grades and by the Core bonus points, so a student with limited break hours should spend them where a grade is genuinely marginal rather than distributing them evenly across six subjects for fairness.

There is a coursework complication specific to DP2 and specific to this window. Schools set internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines ahead of the board's, and several of them land near the winter break. If a draft is due in January, the break has two jobs and will do neither well unless they are sequenced deliberately: coursework in the first week, mock papers in the second, with the understanding that a tutor gives feedback on a draft the student has already produced and does not supply text for submission.

sections.heading: The spring break: a technique window, and nothing else
paragraphs: The spring break for a Dubai DP2 student sits a few weeks before the May session, and it is the most contested tutoring fortnight in the city. It is also the window families most often misuse, by buying content teaching in it. At that distance from the papers, unfamiliar content cannot be made secure enough to survive examination pressure, and the hours spent trying displace the work that would actually have moved marks.

What moves marks in that fortnight is paper discipline. A student who has never sat a full Diploma paper to time will lose the final question, which is frequently the highest-mark question on the paper, and will lose it in the real session too. Three full timed papers across a spring break, each marked against the published criteria, with the error list from one feeding the preparation for the next, is the highest-value use of the window. It is also cheap relative to a content block, because it is fewer tutor hours and more student hours.

The errors that come out of that process are consistent enough to predict. Command-term drift, where a question asking for evaluation receives an explanation. Unshown working in Maths and Physics, forfeiting method marks on correct answers. Units, uncertainties and axis labels treated as presentation rather than as marks. And the Higher Level third paper, where it exists, left unpractised because it is unfamiliar and therefore avoided. Each of those is a specific fix with a visible effect on the next paper.

Slots in this window go early, and the booking behaviour in Dubai is predictable: the families who get the fortnight they want booked it in January. If a spring block is part of the plan, agree it when the mock results arrive, which is also the point at which you will know which paper it should be spent on. Confirm the session dates themselves with the school's Diploma coordinator; no International Baccalaureate examination or results date is restated on this page, because the IB's own site blocks the automated checking this site uses.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the moving part of the calendar
paragraphs: Ramadan and the two Eid holidays move through the Gregorian year on the Hijri calendar, which means a Dubai family cannot build a two-year Diploma plan from last year's dates. In some years Ramadan sits squarely in the DP2 revision window; in others it falls earlier and the problem is a DP1 coursework deadline instead. The fixed part is the effect, not the date: school hours shorten, activities thin out, and the productive part of the day moves.

For fasting students the useful adjustment is to move sessions rather than reduce them. The hour before Iftar is the least productive slot available in the whole year, and the two hours after it are among the best. In practice that means a session at 8:30pm or 9pm that would be unusual at any other time, and it works well. Non-fasting students often gain from the shortened school day, which hands them an afternoon slot they cannot get in an ordinary term. Because lessons are delivered over live video, changing a slot costs a message rather than a logistics problem.

Eid should be planned as a hard stop with work attached. Two consecutive weeks with no live sessions late in the year is a real loss if nothing is set for them and a real gain if something is, because a timed paper can be sat at any hour and marked afterwards whereas a teaching session needs both people present and alert. The pattern that works is to set papers and reading for the Eid days and resume the live cadence immediately after.

The wider point is one no competitor page in this market acknowledges. A Dubai Diploma student lives inside four calendars at once: the school's published academic year, the Gregorian examination session set internationally, the Hijri calendar that moves Ramadan and Eid, and the UAE public holiday schedule. None of them is aligned with the others and the Diploma timetable refers to none of them. A revision plan that ignores three of the four is a plan for a student who does not exist.

sections.heading: Running a block while the family travels
paragraphs: Dubai empties in the summer and thins out in every other break, and a block booked in June is frequently delivered across three countries. That is workable and it is the main practical argument for the online format in this specific context: a tutor cannot follow a family to a summer house, and a live video session can. What it needs is agreement about the time zone, the equipment and the weeks where a session is not realistic.

Time zones are the easy part and the part families get wrong anyway. A block agreed as 5pm Gulf Standard Time becomes 2pm in London, 6:30pm in Mumbai, 9am in Toronto and 3pm in Nairobi. Those are not all equally usable: a 9am session on a holiday morning is theoretically fine and practically unattended. Agree the slot per week against where the family will actually be, and agree it in the local time of the student rather than in the time zone of the booking.

Equipment is the part nobody checks until the first session fails. A holiday house rarely has a desk, a second screen, a printer or a reliable connection, and a Diploma session needs a flat surface, paper, a graphical calculator for the Maths and Physics subjects, and enough bandwidth to share a screen. A tablet with a stylus solves most of it and is worth arranging before the block starts rather than during session one.

The honest part is the weeks that will not work. A three-day transit week, a family wedding, a week in a house with eleven relatives and one bathroom: these are not session weeks and pretending otherwise produces a paid hour with a distracted student in it. Set work for those weeks instead, agree the resume date, and keep the block intact. A fortnight of four good sessions and two weeks of completed set work is better value than six sessions of which three were attended properly.

sections.heading: Coursework over a break, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Breaks are when most Diploma coursework actually gets written, because the Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay all need stretches of time that a term week does not contain. That makes the holiday block the point at which the academic-honesty boundary is tested hardest, usually with the best intentions, and it is worth being explicit about where it sits before a block starts rather than during it.

What a tutor can do over a break is substantial. Explain what each criterion asks for and what the mark allocations mean in practice. Teach the subject content the task requires. Discuss whether a research question is viable and narrow enough to answer. Teach how to handle uncertainty in a data set, how to structure an argument, how to reference properly. Read what the student has produced and say where a paragraph fails to support its own claim. Most students lose coursework marks to criteria they never understood rather than to a lack of ability, and all of that is teaching.

What a tutor cannot do, stated plainly: supply text for the student to submit, rewrite a passage into its final form, choose the research question on the student's behalf, or edit a piece to completion. A provider in this market sells finished Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. The student carries the malpractice consequence for that, not the seller, and the consequence reaches the diploma itself. We will not do it, and saying so is a genuine differentiator in this particular search result.

There is a practical sequencing point that follows. Because feedback has to be on work the student has already produced, a coursework block has to be built around the student's own drafting rather than around session hours. The pattern that works over a fortnight is: session one on criteria and plan, two or three days of the student writing, session two on what they wrote, more writing, session three on the revision. Four sessions back to back on consecutive mornings is the wrong shape for coursework, however well it suits a content topic.

sections.heading: How a holiday block is priced and how long it survives
paragraphs: Holiday blocks are quoted in the same market bands as term-time sessions, and the published figures for Dubai are the ones to plan against rather than any price of ours. A qualified subject tutor online trades roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and an IB specialist for Higher Level work runs AED 200 to AED 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Monthly online packages advertised in this market have been seen at around AED 799 for eight sessions.

What is specific to a break is the cadence, and cadence is what actually decides whether the block works. The table below sets out four shapes against the same two-week window. The daily intensive delivers the most teaching and the least independent practice; the alternate-day shape delivers less teaching and more consolidation and is usually the better buy for a content rebuild. A five-session week with no gaps is the format families ask for and the one students most often stop attending properly by day seven.

Attrition is worth naming because nobody selling blocks mentions it. A ten-session fortnight booked in advance commonly delivers seven or eight attended properly, lost to travel, illness and the simple fact that it is a holiday. That is not an argument against booking a block; it is an argument for booking a shape with slack in it, and for agreeing in advance what happens to a session nobody can attend. Ask any provider that question before paying for a package rather than after.

One pricing caution applies to any quote, including a holiday one. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session, because a ninety-minute session quoted at an hourly rate is not what a rate card implies. And ask whether value added tax is included; we do not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition as settled fact anywhere on this site, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation, so the right move is to ask the provider directly for an inclusive number.

sections.heading: What a break cannot fix, and what we say instead
paragraphs: Some requests arrive in a break that a break cannot meet, and the honest response is to say so rather than to sell the fortnight anyway. The clearest case is a DP2 student three weeks from the May session who has never covered two Higher Level topics. A fortnight cannot make that material secure under examination pressure, and the attempt will consume the time that timed-paper work would have used productively. The better plan is to protect the marks that are reachable and be explicit that the target is a grade rather than three.

The second case is a student who has not asked for the block. A holiday intensive requires a student to work four or five mornings in a row during their own holiday, and a student who was signed up without being consulted will attend without engaging. That is a bad use of a fortnight and of a parent's money. Where we can see that pattern in the trial lesson, we say so, and a lighter cadence with the student's agreement will usually produce more than a heavy one without it.

The third case is three subjects in one fortnight. It is the commonest booking request and it is close to the least effective shape available, because it removes the daily continuity that gives a break its value in the first place. The alternative we suggest is one subject taught and two subjects set: a block in the weakest paper, with marked question sets in the other two for the days between. That delivers more measurable movement than nine shallow sessions across three subjects.

The last thing a break cannot do is substitute for availability we do not have. Holiday windows are the tightest point in the year for Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Maths, because every Dubai family wants the same fortnight. Where no specialist is free we say so up front and offer the options: a different cadence, a different slot, a paper-marking format instead of teaching, or a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same syllabus over live video into whatever time zone the family is in. That is disclosed before anything is booked, not after.

process.title: Name the window first
process.description: Tell us which break, how long it is at your child's school, and which weeks the family will be in Dubai. That decides more than the subject does: a one-week half-term and a nine-week summer are different products, and the weeks you are travelling determine whether the block is live sessions, set work or both.

process.title: Pick one job for the block
process.description: One subject, or one coursework task, or one paper. A fortnight that tries to cover three subjects loses the daily continuity that makes a break worth buying. If three subjects genuinely need attention, we will suggest one taught and two set as marked question sets, which delivers more visible movement.

process.title: Send a script or a draft
process.description: For a content or paper block, a past paper sat to time. For a coursework block, the student's own current draft, however rough. Either one lets a subject specialist say what the fortnight should actually do, and whether the honest answer is that it cannot do what you were hoping for.

process.title: Agree the cadence and the time zone
process.description: Daily, alternate days or twice a week, and the slot in the student's local time rather than in Gulf Standard Time if the family will be travelling. Agree in advance what happens to a session nobody can attend, because a fortnight booked in June commonly loses two sessions to travel and illness.

process.title: Finish on a measured outcome
process.description: A timed paper, a marked draft, or a question set completed under conditions, on the last day of the block. Without it, the family has no evidence of what the fortnight produced, and the next decision gets made on impressions. With it, the decision about whether to continue in term time is made on a mark.

whyPoints.title: The window is the product
whyPoints.description: This page prices breaks by what they can repair rather than by the hour. An autumn half-term can settle an Internal Assessment research question; a spring break can drill timed papers; only a summer can rebuild a subject. Buying the wrong window is the commonest way Dubai families waste money on holiday tuition.

whyPoints.title: Work set for the days between
whyPoints.description: A break session that ends with nothing to do until the next one restarts from the beginning. Every block is built with set work for the intervening days, which is also what makes the alternate-day cadence usually better than a daily one for a content rebuild.

whyPoints.title: The block follows the family
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, and a slot agreed in Dubai can be renegotiated weekly against London, Mumbai, Nairobi or Toronto time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; visiting an address is a service we offer only in India, and no tutor can follow a family to a summer house anyway.

whyPoints.title: We say when a break is the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: A fortnight cannot make two uncovered Higher Level topics examination-secure three weeks out, and a student who did not agree to the block will not use it. Both get said before a booking rather than after, with a different plan offered in place of the one that cannot work.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line, in writing
whyPoints.description: Over a break a tutor explains criteria, teaches content, questions reasoning and gives feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor does not supply text for submission or edit a piece to its final form. At least one provider in this market sells the other thing, and the student carries the risk.

whyPoints.title: Dates we cannot verify stay off the page
whyPoints.description: No International Baccalaureate session or results date is restated here, because the IB's own site returns an automated-access error to the checking this site uses. Confirm session dates with your Diploma coordinator and break dates against the KHDA unified private-school calendar.

faqs.question: Which Dubai school holiday is the right one for IB catch-up work?
faqs.answer: It depends on the job. A content rebuild needs daily continuity, so the winter break or the summer. A coursework task needs spacing around the student's own writing, so any break of a week or more works. Timed-paper drilling before the May session needs the spring break. Settling an Internal Assessment research question fits the one-week autumn half-term, which is the most under-used window in the Dubai year. The mistake is treating them as interchangeable: the same ten hours is worth very different amounts depending which fortnight it sits in.

faqs.question: What can realistically be fixed in a two-week winter break block?
faqs.answer: One content topic closed properly, or one coursework draft produced and reviewed, or two full mock papers sat to time and marked. Not three subjects, which is what most families ask for and the shape that reliably underdelivers, because it removes the daily continuity that gives a break its value. For a DP2 student the winter break sits directly in front of January mocks, so the highest-value plan is to pick the weakest paper, sit a full paper in the first days, work on what it exposed, and sit a second paper at the end.

faqs.question: Can holiday lessons continue while we travel out of the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the main practical argument for the online format in a Dubai summer. A slot agreed as 5pm Gulf Standard Time becomes 2pm in London, 6:30pm in Mumbai and 8am in Toronto, so the slot is renegotiated weekly against where the family will actually be and set in the student's local time. Two things to arrange before the block: a flat surface with paper and a graphical calculator, and agreement on which weeks are transit weeks where set work replaces a live session rather than a distracted hour being paid for.

faqs.question: Is the summer between DP1 and DP2 worth spending on tuition?
faqs.answer: It is the largest window in the Diploma and the one most often left empty. Nine weeks is enough for a genuine rebuild in one or two subjects, which no other break can deliver. The shape that works without consuming the holiday is two sessions a week for about six of the nine weeks, anchored to work produced between them. The alternative is a September restart spent remediating DP1 content while DP2 content arrives, which is how a marginal Higher Level grade becomes a fixed one.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week is sensible during a school holiday?
faqs.answer: Three on alternate days is usually the best shape for a content rebuild, because it leaves real practice time between sessions. Five a week delivers the most teaching and the least consolidation, and students commonly stop attending it properly by day seven. Twice a week suits maintenance across a long break or a coursework draft cycle. Expect attrition: a ten-session fortnight booked in advance commonly delivers seven or eight attended properly, so book a shape with slack and agree in advance what happens to a missed session.

faqs.question: Does holiday tuition cost more than term-time tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The hourly bands are the same; what changes is availability. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with IB specialist work at AED 200 to AED 450, TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those are the market's published figures, not ours. The real holiday premium is scarcity: because KHDA publishes a unified private-school calendar, every Dubai family wants the same fortnight, so Higher Level science and Maths slots in a popular break go early.

faqs.question: Should my child work on the Internal Assessment over the holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a break is usually the only time it gets done properly, because it needs uninterrupted stretches a term week does not contain. The sequencing matters: a session on criteria and plan, then two or three days of the student writing, then a session on what they wrote, then revision. A tutor explains what each criterion asks for, teaches the content the task needs, discusses whether a research question is viable and gives feedback on produced work. A tutor does not supply text for submission or edit a piece to its final form.

faqs.question: What happens to lesson timing during Ramadan and Eid?
faqs.answer: Sessions move rather than stop. For fasting students the hour before Iftar is the least productive slot in the year and the two hours after it are among the best, so a session at 8:30pm or 9pm becomes normal for that month. Non-fasting students often gain an afternoon slot from the shortened school day. Because lessons run over live video, changing a slot costs a message. Eid is better treated as a hard stop with papers and reading set for it, since a timed paper can be sat at any hour and marked afterwards.

faqs.question: How do we use the October half-term if mocks are in January?
faqs.answer: Not for mock revision, which is three months premature and will not survive. Use it for the job the January fortnight will not have room for: settling an Internal Assessment research question and method, or building the Extended Essay reading list, or reading the pre-released case study where one applies. A week is too short for a content rebuild and exactly right for one of those. Doing it in October removes an entire job from the winter break, which otherwise has to carry both coursework and mock preparation and does neither well.

faqs.question: My child has just finished IGCSE and starts DP in August. What should the summer cover?
faqs.answer: The assessment culture first and content second. A student coming from IGCSE into Mathematics Analysis and Approaches needs proof, radians and heavier algebraic manipulation; into the sciences, they need explanation and mechanism where IGCSE accepted a correct statement. Across all subjects they need to know what a criterion is, how command terms behave, and how to make usable notes from a textbook rather than a slide deck. Three to five weeks at two sessions a week closes the common gaps. The signs it worked show in October, not in a test.

faqs.question: Can a holiday block replace weekly term-time sessions?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes; for most, no. A block is the right instrument for closing a content topic, moving a coursework draft forward or drilling papers, because those need concentrated days. Sustained grade movement across a year needs the tutor to see the arc: the coursework deadlines, the mock results, the collapse in week six and the recovery in week nine. A reasonable hybrid is a block in each significant break plus a fortnightly term-time session, which costs less than weekly tuition and keeps the thread intact.

faqs.question: Will a tutor set work for the holiday weeks between sessions?
faqs.answer: Always, and it is the part that determines whether the block works. A break session that ends with nothing to do until the next one restarts from the beginning three days later. Work set between sessions is a problem set, a timed paper, a draft paragraph the student writes themselves, or a definition list, chosen so it can be done without supervision. It is also what makes an alternate-day cadence usually better than a daily one, since five consecutive sessions leave no room to use anything that was set.

faqs.question: How far ahead do we need to book a holiday block?
faqs.answer: For the winter and spring breaks in Dubai, several weeks, and for the spring break specifically the families who get the fortnight they want booked it in January when the mock results arrived. Because KHDA publishes a unified academic calendar for private schools, every family in the city breaks at the same time and the demand peak for Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Maths is sharp. Summer is easier at the start and harder at the end, since August blocks compete with every family trying to prepare for September at once.

faqs.question: Does a holiday block work for Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, better than term time does, because the Theory of Knowledge essay needs long uninterrupted thinking rather than weekly hours. The useful work in a block is unpicking the prescribed title, testing whether the student's claim is arguable, finding real examples from their own subjects rather than generic ones, and reading a draft for whether each paragraph supports its own claim. The exhibition is similar. As with every Core task, the writing is the student's; feedback is on what they have already produced.

faqs.question: What should a DP2 student do with the spring break before exams?
faqs.answer: Timed papers, marked against the published criteria, and nothing else. At that distance from the May session, teaching unfamiliar content cannot make it secure under examination pressure and will displace the work that would have moved marks. Three full papers across the fortnight, with the error list from each feeding the next, attacks the real leaks: command-term drift, unshown working, units and uncertainties treated as presentation, and the Higher Level third paper left unpractised because it is unfamiliar. Confirm your own session dates with the school's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share a holiday block?
faqs.answer: Only if they are in the same subject at the same level with similar current marks, which in practice means twins or two students in the same class. The market pays roughly AED 90 to AED 200 per student per hour for small groups against AED 150 to AED 450 one to one, so the saving is real where the fit is real. Siblings two years apart in different subjects cannot share a session usefully. What does work is sharing a window: back-to-back slots from the same desk, which is simple to arrange when lessons run over live video.

dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.closingHeading: Tell us the window and the weeks you are here
dubai/ib-holiday-tuition.closingBody: A useful first message contains three things: which break your child's school is taking and how long it runs, which weeks the family will be in Dubai and where you will be for the rest, and one marked script or current draft. From that a subject specialist can say what the fortnight can realistically repair, propose a cadence that leaves room for work between sessions, and tell you honestly if the honest answer is that this window cannot do the job you were hoping for. The trial lesson is one 45-minute session per student with no card details taken, and sessions run one-to-one over live video in whatever time zone you are in.

intro.heading: The Diploma is mostly coursework, and almost nobody plans for it
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate in Dubai produces, across two years, something close to nine separate pieces of assessed written work before they sit a single examination. Six subject internal assessments, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay. Each has its own criteria, its own word or page limit, and its own school deadline. Together they carry a substantial share of the final result, and they are finished and submitted months before anyone starts revising.

Those deadlines do not arrive evenly. In most Dubai schools they cluster in two bands: a heavy run in the second half of DP1, when the Extended Essay question is fixed and the science investigations are carried out, and a second run in the first term of DP2, when final versions go in. A candidate who treats DP1 as the easy year arrives in DP2 carrying four unfinished components and a mock season, and no amount of exam tuition recovers the marks already banked at a lower level.

The honest reason most families book late is that nobody tells them the numbers. A school will say the internal assessment matters. It rarely says that a Group 4 investigation is marked out of 24 across five criteria and represents roughly a fifth of the subject grade for about ten hours of work, or that the Theory of Knowledge essay has a hard 1,600-word limit and sits in a matrix that can swing three points on a 45-point total. Those are the figures that change a family's priorities, and they are published.

This page therefore does something the ranking pages for this search do not. It sets out the full coursework map with weights, limits and timing; it states exactly where a tutor's permitted role ends, activity by activity, because that boundary is where this market is least honest; and it counts the Dubai school year backwards from the exam session so a parent can see which month belongs to which component.

One point of fact before the tables. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and every session for a Dubai family runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For coursework support that model has a practical advantage beyond the specialist pool: the draft history, the criterion feedback and the worked examples all exist as files, which is exactly the record a candidate needs in the week before a final submission. A candidate in Dubai Hills whose supervisor has eight other essays to read gets a specialist in the subject their essay is actually written in, rather than the nearest available graduate, and the draft history survives the handover.

dubai/ib-home-tuition.programmesIntro: Coursework starts earlier in the continuum than parents expect, and each programme has a flagship independent project that rehearses the next one. Skipping the rehearsal is why the Extended Essay feels impossible to some candidates and routine to others.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP exhibition in the final primary year is a pupil's first piece of extended independent work, and it is a genuine rehearsal for everything above it: choosing a question, gathering evidence, structuring an argument and presenting it. Pupils who are helped to do it themselves rather than rescued by an adult arrive in the Middle Years able to start a piece of work without supervision.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the exhibition sits alongside the mandatory UAE subjects KHDA requires in every private school regardless of curriculum. Pupils handle Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in parallel, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils, and the time cost of that is real and rarely factored into a family's expectations of the primary year.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Personal Project in the final Middle Years year is the direct ancestor of the Extended Essay: a self-directed piece with a process journal, assessed against published criteria. Candidates who learn there that the journal is marked, and that a plan written after the fact reads like one, save themselves a great deal of difficulty two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that switch from MYP to IGCSE at Year 10 cut that rehearsal short, so a cohort arriving in DP1 from an IGCSE route has often never produced a long independent piece. Those candidates need more scaffolding on the Extended Essay process and less on the subject content, which is the opposite of what most families assume.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subject internal assessments plus the three core components, all against published criteria and all finished before the examinations. The single highest-leverage intervention in the two years is interrogating a research question before the school approves it, because a question that cannot be answered with available data caps the mark on a component worth a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sit the May session, which puts most final coursework deadlines in the autumn and winter of DP2 and the investigations themselves in the spring and summer of DP1. Confirm every date, including upload deadlines, with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, because those are set by the IB and revised.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The reflective project is the Career-related Programme's flagship written component, assessed against its own criteria, and it rewards a genuine ethical dilemma arising from the career-related study rather than a general essay on a topic of interest. The DP courses inside the programme carry their usual internal assessments, marked identically to any other Diploma course.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the programme, so candidates often have no peer group and a supervisor covering it for the first time. External process coaching against the published criteria is therefore more valuable here than in the Diploma, where a cohort provides some calibration by itself.

dubai/ib-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Each subject's coursework is a different animal. The entries below name the component, what it is actually marked on, and the failure that costs the most marks in Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The individual investigation, marked out of 24 across five criteria over roughly ten hours. The usual failure is a research question with no controllable independent variable, chosen because the practical looked achievable. A second common failure is data with too few points to support any evaluation, which caps two criteria at once.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same investigation structure, different failure mode. Physics candidates tend to choose questions that produce a straight line and then have nothing to evaluate. Uncertainty handling is where the upper bands are won, and it is the part least often taught explicitly in a Dubai classroom.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Investigations here fail on biological variability rather than on design: insufficient replication makes any conclusion unsupportable. The strongest Biology investigations narrow to one variable with enough repeats to show a pattern, which usually means a less interesting question and a much better mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration, marked out of 20 across five criteria, with personal engagement and reflection the two criteria candidates most often leave empty. Mathematical communication is a criterion in its own right, so notation and clarity carry marks independently of whether the mathematics is correct.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same exploration criteria applied to modelling and data. Candidates have an advantage here if they use genuine data they collected or sourced, because personal engagement becomes easy to evidence. The trap is a statistical test applied without checking its conditions, which costs the mathematics criterion.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A portfolio of three commentaries, each on a different section of the syllabus and each based on a published article within a set age window. Two rules cost most of the lost marks: syllabus coverage across the three, and the word limit per commentary. Diagrams must be referenced in the prose to earn their marks.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A historical investigation with a formal structure, including an evaluation of sources that is marked as its own section. The commonest failure is a question too broad for the word limit, producing narrative instead of argument. Source evaluation must address origin, purpose, value and limitation rather than summarising content.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: An experimental study written up to a published structure and a word limit, marked on the quality of the write-up rather than on whether the hypothesis held. Candidates lose marks on the ethical considerations section and on inferential statistics chosen without justification.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: A fieldwork report, where the single predictor of a good mark is whether the question can be answered with data the candidate can actually collect in Dubai in the time available. Written methodology and presentation of results carry defined marks, and both are commonly thin.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: At Higher Level, a formal essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words on one studied text, developed from a line of inquiry the candidate sets. The usual failure is a line of inquiry too broad to sustain, which produces a general appreciation of the text rather than an argument.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries, plus an essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title released by the IB. Marks come from knowledge claims that are tested against counterclaims, not from explaining the objects or restating the title in different words.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, supervised in school and marked against subject-specific criteria. The research question decides the grade more than the writing does, and a question that is already answered in a textbook cannot reach the upper bands however well it is written.

dubai/ib-home-tuition.regionsIntro: Fieldwork, data collection and supervision access all depend on where a candidate lives and goes to school. These notes concern what is actually practicable in each part of the emirate.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Good material for Geography fieldwork on urban density, microclimate and pedestrian flow, all collectable within walking distance. The constraint is permission: data collection in managed private developments needs asking first, and candidates routinely discover that late.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Central enough that supervisor meetings are easy to attend in person after school, which matters for Extended Essay candidates whose supervisors offer limited slots. Retail and transport data for Business Management and Economics commentaries is readily available here.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Coastal fieldwork sites within reach for Geography and Environmental Systems investigations, including beach profiles and water quality sampling. Candidates should check access rules and seasonal restrictions before building a question around a specific site.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: Villa communities where household energy and water data is obtainable with family cooperation, which supports strong Physics and Environmental Systems investigations. Travel time to a school supervisor is the main friction in the Extended Essay process here.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Dense commercial setting with usable material for Business Management and Economics commentaries, and footfall or transport data for Geography. Apartment living limits the kinds of Group 4 investigation that can be run outside a school laboratory.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University libraries and research facilities nearby, which helps Extended Essay candidates needing sources beyond a school library. Candidates here are also closest to the admissions conversations that make the core points matter.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Established residential areas with good access to community data for social science investigations and questionnaires. Diploma peer groups are smaller here, so candidates have fewer classmates to compare a draft against.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools with newer Extended Essay supervision structures, which means less institutional memory about which questions have worked. External criterion-level questioning fills that gap for candidates in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with long-established core supervision
schoolClusters.note: Several cycles of Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge experience behind them, so candidates arrive with a clear process and need subject-specific interrogation of their question rather than scaffolding.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Newer Diploma cohorts and continuum schools
schoolClusters.note: Core supervision structures are still maturing, and supervisors may be covering the Extended Essay for the first time. These candidates benefit most from early questioning of the research question against the subject criteria.

dubai/ib-home-tuition.modesIntro: Coursework support is a different product from subject teaching, and it should be bought in a different shape. These three cover almost every request that reaches us from Dubai Diploma families.

modes.title: Question-design block
modes.description: Two or three sessions, taken before the school approves a research question, aimed entirely at making the question answerable. The candidate arrives with a topic and leaves with a question narrow enough to control, a data plan and an understanding of which criteria the question has just made easier or harder to satisfy.

modes.title: Criterion review cycle
modes.description: Booked sessions spaced across a drafting period, each reading the candidate's latest version against the published descriptors and naming which band each criterion currently sits in. Nothing is rewritten and no text is supplied; the output is a list of specific weaknesses the candidate then addresses themselves.

modes.title: Core intensive
modes.description: A short run covering the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay together, usually taken in the long gap between DP1 and DP2. Up to three points on the 45-point scale come from these two components, and they are the only part of the Diploma that can be substantially advanced during a holiday.

sections.heading: What IB home tuition in Dubai is usually actually needed for
paragraphs: The phrase suggests exam preparation, and the enquiries say something else. The majority of Diploma requests that reach us from Dubai concern a coursework component rather than a paper: an investigation that has to be submitted in three weeks, an Extended Essay with no usable question, a Theory of Knowledge essay the candidate cannot start. Papers come up later, in the spring, and by then the coursework marks are fixed.

This matters because the two jobs are not interchangeable. Exam support is about technique under time pressure, and it responds to drill. Coursework support is about design, criteria and process, and it responds to questioning. A tutor who is excellent at one may be mediocre at the other, and a family that books a paper specialist in October to solve an investigation problem has bought the wrong service at the right price.

The structural reason coursework dominates is the deadline. Exam dates are months away and feel movable; a school's internal submission date is next Thursday and is not. By the time a family feels urgency about papers, the candidate has already banked six coursework marks at whatever level they managed without help, and those cannot be revisited. The arithmetic strongly favours spending early on components that are about to be locked.

There is one more reason to start with coursework. The skills it demands, framing a question, gathering evidence, evaluating a source or a method, writing to a criterion, are the same skills that produce upper-band answers on an extended-response paper. A candidate who learns to satisfy a criterion in a written investigation has learned something that pays again in the examination hall. The reverse is much less true.

sections.heading: The coursework map: weight, limit and timing
paragraphs: What follows is the map a family should have in September of DP1 and almost never does. Every component, roughly what it carries, the published limit it must fit inside, and the point in the two years when it normally falls in a Dubai school running the May session.

Two warnings about reading it. Limits and weightings are set in the current subject guide for each subject, and they are revised between syllabus cycles, so the only authoritative version is the guide your child's school is teaching from. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the component weightings in writing at the start of DP1; it is a reasonable request and the answer is useful for two years.

The second warning is about the timing column. School deadlines differ, sometimes considerably, and a school that wants final investigations in October is making a defensible choice about DP2 workload rather than being unusually harsh. The column below describes the common pattern, and the only dates that matter are the ones on your school's own coursework calendar.

What the map is for is prioritisation. A candidate carrying a weak Extended Essay question and a weak mathematics exploration topic in the same term should fix the Extended Essay first, because its question constrains 4,000 words of work and the exploration can be re-scoped later with less loss. Decisions like that need the whole map in front of you, not one component at a time as each becomes urgent.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay: the question decides the grade
paragraphs: Four thousand words, one subject, one supervisor and one question. Of those four variables the question does almost all the work, and candidates spend almost all their anxiety on the word count. A question that is already answered in an A Level textbook cannot reach the upper bands however elegantly it is written, because the criteria reward analysis and argument rather than exposition.

The second thing candidates get wrong is treating the Extended Essay as subject-neutral. It is not. The criteria are applied through the lens of the chosen subject, which means a History essay must handle historiography and source evaluation, a Chemistry essay must show experimental or data-based reasoning, and an Economics essay must apply theory to a specific context with diagrams. A good general research paper submitted in History reads as a competent essay in no subject at all.

Choosing the subject badly is the most expensive early mistake. Candidates frequently choose the subject they enjoy rather than the one in which they can access data, and then discover in month three that the question requires primary research they cannot do from Dubai. A question that can be answered with sources a candidate can actually reach, in a subject whose criteria they understand, beats an ambitious question in every case.

The supervisor relationship does the rest, and it is a school relationship. A supervisor has a defined number of meetings, keeps a record of them, and signs off on the authenticity of the work. External support operates inside that structure, not around it: a tutor may teach the criteria, question the research question, point out where an argument fails and comment on a draft the candidate has written. A tutor may not write any part of the essay or supply text for it, and candidates who are offered that are being offered an academic-honesty breach rather than help.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: exhibition and essay, and why candidates freeze
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge produces more blank pages than any other component, and the reason is a category error rather than a difficulty. Candidates approach the prescribed title as a question about the world and try to answer it with content. It is a question about knowledge, and the answer is an argument about how we come to know things, tested against a case where that way of knowing fails.

The exhibition is the easier half and still commonly mishandled. Three objects, each with a commentary linking it to a prompt. Candidates describe their objects, which earns little, instead of using each object to make a point about knowledge that the object specifically demonstrates. The test for a good object is whether swapping it for a different one would change the argument. If it would not, the object is decoration.

The essay runs to 1,600 words on one of the prescribed titles, and the structural requirement is a knowledge claim, a counterclaim and a resolution, worked through examples from at least two areas of knowledge. Candidates who have a stock of specific examples, including from their own subjects, can write it. Candidates who have only abstractions produce 1,600 words that say nothing twice.

Up to three points on the 45-point scale come from the matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades, which is why this component deserves more attention than it gets from both candidates and families. The work is exactly the kind that responds to being asked hard questions by someone outside the class, which is the whole of what support here should consist of. The thinking and the writing stay the candidate's own, and anyone offering more than questions is offering a problem.
bullets: The prescribed title asks about knowledge, not about the world

sections.heading: Where the academic-honesty line sits, activity by activity
paragraphs: This market contains operators who sell finished coursework. One advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Under IB academic-honesty rules that is malpractice, the consequences fall on the candidate rather than the vendor, and the sanction can be the loss of the Diploma. A page offering coursework support owes its readers an exact account of where the line is, rather than a reassuring sentence.

The permitted activities are broad and genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the published criteria and explain what distinguishes band descriptors. A tutor may question a research question until its weaknesses are exposed. A tutor may explain a statistical method, a historiographical approach or a modelling technique. A tutor may read work the candidate has written and say where an argument does not hold, where a criterion is unaddressed, and where the word limit is being wasted.

The prohibited activities are narrower and absolute. No text may be supplied for a submission. No section may be rewritten by anyone other than the candidate. No data may be fabricated or lent from another candidate. No source may be cited that the candidate has not read. And no part of the work may be produced by a tool or a person and presented as the candidate's own, which includes generated text pasted into a draft.

The practical test a family can apply is simple. If the candidate cannot explain, unprompted, why a sentence in their submission says what it says, that sentence is a problem regardless of who typed it. Supervisors in Dubai schools ask exactly that question in meetings, and they are experienced at it. Work that cannot survive the question should not be submitted.

sections.heading: The Dubai school year, counted backwards from the session
paragraphs: Every other page in this market counts forwards from today, which is why families always feel behind. Counting backwards from the examination session produces a calendar a candidate can act on, because it makes visible which month belongs to which component and which months are already spoken for.

The anchor is the May session, which Dubai private schools following the northern academic year sit. Dates for IB sessions, upload deadlines and results are set by the IB and revised, so confirm them with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB itself rather than taking any figure from a tutoring website. What can be stated with confidence is the shape: coursework finishes in the autumn and winter of DP2, mocks follow, and the examined components come last.

For candidates on Cambridge or Pearson qualifications before the Diploma, the equivalent dates are published and sourced, and they illustrate the principle well. Cambridge's March 2027 series has an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due on 27 November 2026, which is to say the entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May or June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is a genuine administrative risk for families in this region, and the only safe practice is to take the timetable from the school's exams officer rather than from the internet.
