sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and when revision actually happens in Dubai
paragraphs: A revision plan built on a European school calendar does not survive contact with the UAE academic year, and no competitor page in this market mentions the problem at all. Dubai schools adjust timings during Ramadan, the working day shortens, and Eid holidays fall on a lunar calendar that moves each year relative to the exam season.

The practical effect on a Diploma candidate is that the weeks available for sustained revision are not evenly distributed, and the densest coursework period can collide with the shortest school days. Families who map the actual term calendar against their coursework deadlines in September find the collisions in advance; families who do not meet them as a crisis in the spring.

Session timing itself is straightforward to adapt when teaching is delivered over live video. Post-Iftar slots work well during Ramadan, and many candidates concentrate better in the evening during that month than in a shortened, tired afternoon. A tutor travelling across the emirate at that hour is a different proposition entirely, which is one of the quieter advantages of the online model in this market.

The planning rule that follows is to treat the calendar as a constraint rather than as background. Count the usable weeks between now and each deadline, subtract the ones the calendar removes, and plan against what is left. A candidate with nine weeks to a deadline who has actually got six will make different and better decisions about what to attempt.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: No competitor page in this cluster addresses this, and it affects every private school pupil in Dubai. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements that schools were to implement by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 applying to schools whose year starts in April.

The rules are specific and worth knowing, because they explain things parents find puzzling. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Language of instruction is specified too. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab pupils, while non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two further points matter for tutoring. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring in these subjects can honestly be described. Support here means working within the school's prescribed material, not supplying an alternative syllabus.

sections.heading: What a session fixes, and what it honestly cannot
paragraphs: Coursework support has a high ceiling early and a low ceiling late, and the difference is the single most useful thing a family can understand before booking. Two sessions spent on a research question before the school approves it can change the band a component ends up in. Two sessions spent on a draft the week before submission can tidy it.

What a session reliably fixes: a question that is too broad, a plan with no controllable variable, a draft that has not addressed one of its criteria at all, a candidate who does not know what a descriptor is asking for, and a word count being spent on description rather than argument. All of those are structural and all are correctable by the candidate once named.

What a session cannot fix: data that was never collected, a question approved six months ago that cannot be changed now, a component already submitted, and a candidate who has not done the reading. It also cannot substitute for the school's supervision structure, which keeps records and signs off authenticity, and should not try to.

The last limit is the important one. If the honest answer is that a component is now going to score where it scores and the better use of the next month is the next component, that is the advice a family should get. An arrangement that bills for polishing a locked-in mark while the following deadline approaches unaddressed is working against the candidate, however busy it looks.

process.description: The assessment criteria from the current subject guide, as the school has issued them. Limits and weightings change between syllabus cycles, and working from a version the school is not teaching produces confident feedback against the wrong standard.

process.description: Each session ends with something the candidate will write before the next one. The tutor supplies questions, criteria and worked examples on other data, never text for the submission. That boundary is stated in writing at the start so there is no ambiguity later.

process.description: School supervision meetings, record-keeping and authenticity sign-off come first, and external support fits around them. Sessions are scheduled between supervisor meetings so the candidate arrives at each one with their own work and their own questions.

whyPoints.description: The research question decides the band on a component worth a fifth of a subject grade. Two sessions spent narrowing it are worth more than ten spent on a draft, and that is where we push families to spend, even though it is the smaller booking.

faqs.question: How many pieces of assessed coursework does an IB Diploma candidate produce?
faqs.answer: Nine in most subject combinations: six subject internal assessments plus the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay. Each carries its own published criteria and limit, and each is finished and submitted before the examination session. Coursework typically accounts for 20 to 25% of a subject grade, and the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades combine in a matrix worth up to three points on the 45-point total. A family that maps all nine in September of the first Diploma year prioritises very differently from one that meets them individually.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai candidate fix their Extended Essay question?
faqs.answer: During the first Diploma year, and earlier than most schools require. The question constrains 4,000 words of work, and a question that cannot be answered with sources the candidate can actually reach from Dubai becomes obvious in month three, when changing it is expensive. The practical test is whether the candidate can name, before the question is approved, the specific sources or data they will use and where those will come from. If they cannot, the question is a topic rather than a question.

faqs.question: Why does the Extended Essay subject matter as much as the topic?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria are applied through the lens of the chosen subject. A History essay is expected to handle historiography and evaluate sources; a Chemistry essay is expected to show experimental or data-based reasoning; an Economics essay is expected to apply a model to a specific context with diagrams. A well-written general research paper submitted in History reads as a competent essay in no subject at all, which is the single most common reason strong writers receive middling Extended Essay grades.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: The essay runs to 1,600 words on one of the prescribed titles released by the IB, and the exhibition consists of three objects with commentaries. The structural requirement in the essay is a knowledge claim, a counterclaim and a resolution, worked through examples from at least two areas of knowledge. Candidates who freeze on this component are usually trying to answer the title as a question about the world rather than about knowledge. Confirm the current limit and format against the subject guide your school is teaching from.

faqs.question: How is a Group 4 individual investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Against five published criteria for a total of 24 marks, over roughly ten hours of allocated work, and it represents approximately a fifth of the subject grade. The research question sets the ceiling: one with no controllable independent variable, or producing too few data points to support an evaluation, caps two criteria regardless of how well the report is written. Biology investigations most often fail on insufficient replication, Physics ones on choosing a question that yields a straight line and nothing to evaluate.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on an internal assessment draft without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the normal, permitted form of support. A tutor may teach the published criteria, explain what separates one band descriptor from the next, question a research question until its weaknesses show, explain a method or statistical test using other data, and read work the candidate has written to say where a criterion is unaddressed. What a tutor may not do is supply sentences, rewrite sections to a finished state, provide data or sources the candidate has not used, or produce any part of a submission.

faqs.question: What happens to a candidate who submits coursework they did not write?
faqs.answer: The consequence falls on the candidate, not on whoever supplied the work, and under IB academic-honesty rules it can extend to losing the Diploma. Supervisors in Dubai schools keep records of meetings and sign off on authenticity, and they are experienced at asking a candidate to explain why a particular sentence says what it says. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price; buying one transfers a serious risk to a sixteen-year-old in exchange for a mark that may never be awarded.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for coursework help in the final week before submission?
faqs.answer: Much less than families assume. In the final week a draft can be tidied, but the band is largely set by decisions made months earlier: the question, the data collected, and whether each criterion was addressed at all. Two sessions spent on question design before school approval change outcomes; two spent on prose the week before submission rarely do. If the honest answer is that this component will score where it scores, the better use of the next month is the next deadline.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan and Eid affect a Diploma revision plan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They redistribute the usable weeks, and no competitor page in this market mentions it. School timings shorten during Ramadan, the working day changes, and Eid holidays fall on a lunar calendar that moves each year relative to the exam season. A candidate with nine calendar weeks to a deadline may have six usable ones. Mapping the school's real term calendar against coursework deadlines at the start of the year surfaces the collisions in advance. Sessions over live video adapt easily, and post-Iftar slots work well for many candidates.

faqs.question: Why does my child study Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with implementation required by the start of the 2025-26 academic year and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The rules are specific: schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

faqs.question: Can we use different material for Arabic or Islamic Education tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and this is a genuine constraint rather than a preference. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited under KHDA guidelines. Support in these subjects therefore means working within the material the school is prescribed, not supplying an alternative syllabus. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential point worth asking about.

faqs.question: How far ahead do exam entry deadlines sit, and who sets them?
faqs.answer: Much further ahead than families expect, and the board sets them. Cambridge's March 2027 series illustrates it: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 while final entries were due on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May or June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. For IB sessions, confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, because those are set by the IB and revised.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge warn about using the wrong exam timetable?
faqs.answer: Because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For families in this region that is a live administrative risk, particularly for private candidates, and the only safe practice is to take the timetable from the school's exams officer in writing rather than from a website or a parents group.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project in the Middle Years help with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and candidates who skipped it notice. The Personal Project is self-directed work with a process journal assessed against published criteria, which rehearses the three habits the Extended Essay depends on: choosing a workable question, keeping a record as you go rather than reconstructing one afterwards, and writing to a criterion rather than to a page count. Dubai schools that move from the Middle Years to IGCSE at Year 10 cut that rehearsal short, so those candidates usually need more process scaffolding and less subject content than their families expect.

faqs.question: Are coursework sessions for Dubai families online or at a home address?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer in-home visiting anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For coursework the online model has a specific advantage: criterion feedback, draft versions and worked examples all persist as files, so in the final week a candidate can see which criterion each revision was meant to address. It also means the specialist is matched on the component and the subject rather than on who can reach your community before 6pm.

intro.heading: The price nobody in this market will print
paragraphs: A parent looking for an IB home tutor in Dubai wants one number and cannot find it. Of the pages competing for this search, one agency's own frequently asked questions ask what tutoring costs and then decline to answer. Another publishes a schema price range that contradicts the figure on the visible page. Two quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. The research behind this page measured the whole cluster: three of six published pages carry no price at all.

That silence is commercially convenient and useless to you, so here is the market in dirhams. Published rates run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 an hour for a named premium provider. Qualified subject teachers working online cluster between AED 150 and AED 300. Diploma, IGCSE and A Level specialists sit between AED 200 and AED 450 or above. Rates quoted for a tutor travelling to a Dubai address run from about AED 180 to AED 500, and that spread is mostly travel, not teaching.

The gap between AED 150 and AED 450 for what looks like the same hour is the question this page exists to answer. Four variables explain almost all of it: whether the tutor teaches that exact subject at that exact level, whether the hour includes travel across the emirate, whether the booking is a single hour or a committed block, and how close the session sits to an exam window. None of those is about the tutor being better as a person. They are about scarcity, time and risk.

Dubai also has a cost context worth putting on the table. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family budgeting a two-year Diploma, that is the first flat fee year in some time, and it is the right moment to decide what tutoring is for rather than to buy hours by default.

One thing to be clear about before the tables start. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any address in the UAE. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and no page on this site will tell a Dubai family otherwise. What is sold here is one-to-one teaching over live video on Gulf Standard Time, priced without a travel component and matched on subject rather than on driving distance. The comparison table further down sets the two models side by side, with the numbers, and you can judge it. The short version is that the in-home band starts roughly where the online specialist band tops out, and the money in between is spent on driving rather than on teaching.

programmes.countryNote: Dubai adds a wrinkle elsewhere absent. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Tutoring for those mandatory subjects is priced separately in this market and is often harder to source than the main curriculum, because the content cannot be varied without prior Ministry of Education permission.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mid-market rates apply, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher online. Criterion-referenced marking out of 8 per criterion is the thing worth paying for: a tutor who can read a criterion strand and show a pupil why a good answer scored 4 earns their rate in two sessions. A generalist who teaches the content and ignores the criteria does not.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP only to Year 9 before switching to IGCSE. Families who discover this late often buy a term of bridging support, and the going rate for that work sits at the upper end of the mid band because it needs a tutor fluent in two assessment cultures at once rather than one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive stage, for a straightforward supply reason. Higher Level teaching in a named subject with current experience of the papers is scarce, and specialist rates of AED 200 to AED 450 or above reflect that. Internal assessment supervision is quoted at the same level, because the work is intensive and sits against immovable school deadlines rather than a flexible weekly slot.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts are often small, which keeps local specialist supply thin and local prices firm, especially between February and April before the May session. Confirm session and upload dates with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, because those dates are set by the IB and revised, and no tutoring page should be your source for them.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Priced like the Diploma for the DP courses inside it, because they are marked identically, and quoted ad hoc for the reflective project and career-related study. Few providers in this market have ever supported a Career-related Programme candidate, so quotes vary wildly and are worth comparing against the Diploma specialist band rather than accepting at face value.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme. A family seeking local support is therefore searching a market of a handful of people, which pushes quotes up for reasons that have nothing to do with the difficulty of the work. Online matching removes that scarcity premium.

dubai/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Some subjects cost more than others, and parents are rarely told why. The driver is the number of people in reach who can teach that subject at that level, not the difficulty of the content. Each entry below notes where the money goes.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Among the most expensive Diploma subjects to tutor in this market, because Higher Level organic mechanisms and the individual investigation both need someone who has marked them. Sessions on Paper 1 stem reading and state symbols in extended response pay back fastest, and they do not need the most expensive tutor in the pool.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: High demand keeps rates firm, especially for Higher Level Paper 3. The calculator-free Paper 1 is where most of the marks are lost, and drilling manual fluency is cheap work that a mid-band tutor can do well. Paper 3 technique is where a specialist rate is genuinely justified.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Slightly easier to staff than Analysis and Approaches, so quotes sit a little lower. The marks are in interpretation: regression and chi-squared output explained in the context of the question rather than left as numbers. A statistics-comfortable tutor at mid-band rates handles this well.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Expensive at Higher Level and genuinely scarce locally. The data-analysis section of Paper 3 is the most coachable component and the least taught in class, which makes it the best value hour in the subject. Explanation structure, not calculation, is where most Dubai candidates lose marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Easier to source than Physics or Chemistry, so rates sit mid-band more often. Content volume makes long-term weekly support tempting, but command-term discipline and data-based question technique are short, cheap interventions that move grades faster than a term of content revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Demand in Dubai is high and Higher Level supply is moderate, so quotes run toward the specialist band. Diagram marks and the three-commentary internal assessment portfolio are the two places money is well spent, because both are rule-bound and therefore fast to correct.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study for Paper 1 means the preparation window is known months ahead, which makes a short block of booked sessions better value than a year-long slot. Candidates pay for tool application to the stimulus, not for definitions of Ansoff and the BCG matrix.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Moderate supply, mid-band rates. Value concentrates in building a bank of studies that each carry a method, a finding and a limitation, which is systematic work rather than inspired teaching. The experimental study in internal assessment is marked on the write-up, so draft feedback is the costly part.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Cheaper to source than the sciences and frequently under-booked by Dubai families until after the first Paper 2 mock. The comparative-essay fix is structural and quick, which makes this one of the highest-return mid-band bookings in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: A genuinely scarce market in Dubai, because KHDA requires schools to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and the content cannot be varied without Ministry of Education permission. Quotes for this work are therefore inconsistent and worth comparing carefully.

dubai/ib-home-tutor.regionsTitle: What the number looks like across Dubai
dubai/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Travel is a real cost in an in-home quote, and it is priced by where you live. These notes describe what a tutor crossing the emirate to a given community is actually absorbing, and what that does to the hour you pay for.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Dense, parking-constrained and expensive to reach by car at the end of the working day. In-home quotes here carry the full travel premium, and a tutor who arrives at 5pm has usually spent 45 unpaid minutes getting there from Deira or Mirdif.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Villa communities where two-hour minimum blocks are the norm, because no tutor will drive that far for sixty minutes. The practical effect is that a family pays for two hours whether the pupil needs two hours or not.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Better served by locally resident tutors, so travel premiums are smaller and budget-band quotes are more realistic. Diploma specialists are correspondingly scarcer, because the local pool skews toward other curricula.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Central and reachable, which keeps travel costs moderate, but demand for evening slots is heavy. Quotes rise for the 5pm to 7pm window because that is the only time most families want, and supply there is finite.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Deira
regions.note: Lower in-home quotes than the newer communities, reflecting a larger resident tutor pool rather than a different standard of teaching. Diploma Higher Level supply is the constraint here, not price.

regions.name: Dubai South and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: The longest drives in the emirate for most tutors, and the point where travel stops being a premium and becomes a refusal. Families in these communities are the ones for whom online delivery is not a compromise but the only reliable option.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Short drives, difficult building access and visitor parking that costs the tutor money. In-home quotes here often fold a parking and access allowance into the hourly figure without naming it.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Central to the emirate's IB provision and reasonably easy to reach, so this is where budget-band in-home quotes are most likely to be genuine rather than a loss-leader a tutor later renegotiates.

schoolClusters.city: Established Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Families from these cohorts tend to buy narrow, expensive help: Paper 3 technique, exploration design, a component clinic. The school teaches the content competently, so what is being bought is the thing class size cannot supply.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Newer and growing Diploma cohorts
schoolClusters.note: Smaller cohorts restrict Higher Level option blocks, so these families more often buy a full subject that the school could not timetable. That is the most expensive kind of tutoring to source locally and the clearest case for an online match.

dubai/ib-home-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named to describe the Dubai Diploma provision families choose between; no affiliation, endorsement or relationship with any named school is implied.
dubai/ib-home-tutor.modesIntro: What you book changes the price more than who you book. These three shapes cover most Dubai Diploma requests, and the cheapest per hour is frequently the most expensive per mark gained.

modes.title: Committed weekly slot
modes.description: A fixed hour each week with the same specialist, usually quoted at a lower hourly figure than ad hoc booking because the tutor can plan around it. It is the right purchase when a content gap genuinely needs rebuilding over a term. It is the wrong purchase when the fault is a single technique problem that three sessions would fix.
bullets: Lowest effective hourly figure of the three shapes

modes.title: Component block
modes.description: Three to six sessions aimed at one assessment component, then it ends. Per hour it costs more than a committed slot. Per mark it is usually the best value purchase available to a Dubai Diploma family, because the diagnosis is already done and the target is specific.
bullets: Scoped to one paper, one criterion or one skill
Best bought immediately after a mock
No open-ended commitment and nothing to cancel

modes.title: Exam-term intensive
modes.description: A short, high-frequency run in the weeks before the exam window. The most expensive shape per hour, because availability is scarce between February and April and every specialist in the market is already booked. Families who plan for it in November pay less than families who discover the need in March.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Dubai costs, in dirhams
paragraphs: Published market rates for Diploma tutoring in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 an hour to AED 650 an hour. A tutor travelling to a Dubai address is quoted from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and a qualified subject teacher working online is quoted from about AED 150 to AED 300. Those are the bands, attributed below to the providers and the cost survey that published them.

The table that follows is not an IB Gram price list and should not be read as one. It is a map of what other people in this market charge, with sources named, so that a quote arriving in your inbox can be placed somewhere on it. A quote of AED 120 an hour for Higher Level Physics tells you something. So does a quote of AED 600 for an SL Biology catch-up.

Two patterns are worth noticing before the numbers. The first is that the in-home band overlaps heavily with the specialist band, which means a family paying AED 350 an hour may be buying either a specialist or a driver, and the quote alone will not tell them which. The second is that the top of the online band and the bottom of the in-home band are the same money, which is the whole decision in one line.

What IB Gram charges is settled after the free trial lesson, in a consultation that depends on the subject, the level, the frequency and the term. Publishing a single figure here would be dishonest, because a weekly SL Biology slot and an exam-term Higher Level Physics intensive are not the same product. What can be published honestly is the market, and it is below.

sections.heading: What the travel actually costs, line by line
paragraphs: The difference between an online quote and an in-home quote is not profit. It is time, and the time is real. A tutor crossing Dubai from Mirdif to the Marina at 4.30pm is absorbing something close to ninety minutes of round-trip driving for a sixty-minute lesson. Nobody can sustain that at the online rate, so either the hourly figure rises or the minimum block does, and usually both.

That is why in-home quotes in this market arrive with conditions attached. A two-hour minimum is standard for the outer communities. A travel surcharge or a zone-based rate is common. Cancellation terms are tighter, because a tutor who has already driven to Jumeirah Golf Estates cannot resell the slot. Parking at a Downtown tower costs the tutor money. None of this is unreasonable, and all of it is paid by the family.

Then there is the invisible cost, which is the one worth the most. A tutor pool limited to people who can reach your community in the window you want is a small pool, and it is selected for geography rather than for subject expertise. A family in Dubai South choosing from locally available tutors for Higher Level Chemistry is choosing from very few people, and may end up with a generalist at a specialist price.

Monthly packages in this market make the same arithmetic visible. Online packages have been advertised at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. In-home packages have been advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions. Both deliver eight hours. The difference is roughly double, and the second one includes a car.

sections.heading: The nine things that move the number in Dubai specifically
paragraphs: Ask two providers for a Higher Level Chemistry quote in the same week and the figures can differ by a factor of three. That is not a market failure; it is nine variables being bundled into one number and never itemised. Knowing which of them applies to you is how a parent judges whether AED 300 an hour is fair.

Subject and level do most of the work. Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the scarcest teaching in this emirate, and scarcity sets the price. Timing does the next largest share: the same tutor is more expensive in March than in October, because every specialist in the market is booked before the May session and nobody is in February. A family that fixes its exam-term slot in November pays November rates.

Then come the structural variables. Session length changes the effective hourly figure, since ninety minutes rarely costs 1.5 times sixty. Commitment changes it, because a tutor who can plan a term discounts against a tutor filling gaps. Delivery format changes it, by the travel arithmetic above. The pupil's starting point changes it, because rebuilding two years of missing foundations is different work from correcting exam technique.

The last three are the ones families forget to ask about. Whether internal assessment supervision is included or billed separately. Whether written session notes and a progress summary are part of the service or an extra. And whether the quote is inclusive of value added tax, which is a question to put directly to any provider rather than to assume, since the treatment of tuition fees is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and not for a tutoring website.

sections.heading: Monthly packages, and how to read one
paragraphs: Packages are how most of this market actually sells, and they are where the hourly comparison gets lost. A monthly figure with a session count attached is easy to agree to and hard to compare. The only way to read one is to divide it back into an effective hourly rate and then check what is inside the hour.

Published examples make the method clear. An online package advertised at AED 799 for eight sessions a month works out near AED 100 an hour if the sessions are sixty minutes. An in-home package at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions works out between AED 200 and AED 225 an hour for the same eight hours of teaching. A cost survey for this market puts monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to AED 600 for budget tutors, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or above for specialist exam-year support.

The second check is what the session count assumes. Eight sessions a month assumes a month with four usable weeks, which Dubai's calendar does not always supply. Half-term, Eid holidays, school trips and the exam weeks themselves all remove sessions, and a package that does not carry unused sessions forward quietly becomes more expensive than its headline.

The third check is the exit. A month is a short commitment and a term is not, and the discount offered for a term is often smaller than the risk of being locked to a tutor who turns out to be the wrong match. For a first booking, the shorter and more cancellable arrangement is worth paying a little more for.

sections.heading: In-home against live online, with the numbers in front of you
paragraphs: This is the comparison the page has been building towards, and it is worth making on the merits rather than by assertion. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits in the UAE, so the table below is not a sales device dressed as a comparison; it is the reason for the model.

On cost, the in-home band starts roughly where the online specialist band tops out. On tutor pool, in-home is restricted to whoever can reach your community in your window, and online is not. On scheduling, in-home sessions are hostage to Dubai's after-school traffic, which is why two-hour blocks exist. On record-keeping, a live video session with a shared whiteboard leaves every annotated paper and worked solution behind as a reviewable file, which a visit to a kitchen table does not.

There are real things on the other side of the ledger, and pretending otherwise would be insulting. A tutor in the room can see a pupil's body language in a way a camera flattens. For younger children, physical presence helps with attention in a way nothing online fully replaces. For a pupil with specific access needs, in-person support can be the right answer, and a family in that position should pay the premium for it without apology.

For a Diploma candidate in Dubai, though, the balance usually lands the other way, because the binding constraint is finding someone who has taught Higher Level Chemistry recently rather than finding someone who can park. A Marina family gets a specialist in the exact subject instead of the best available person within a twenty-minute drive, and keeps the forty-five minutes the tutor would have spent in traffic.

sections.heading: The permit, and why it belongs in a price conversation
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and it is cheaper than most parents assume. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is broad. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school pupils aged 15 to 18 and university students may all apply. That breadth is why the budget end of this market exists at all: a university student tutoring legally at AED 60 an hour is not operating in a grey area, provided they hold the permit.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and press reporting has stated explicitly that the ministry did not specify the amounts, so no figure appears on this page. Any provider quoting you a specific fine is repeating something unverified.

This matters to price in two ways. A permitted tutor has no regulatory risk to price in, which is one reason legitimate rates are not higher than they are. And there is a separate rule families should know: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, and the permit carries its own code of conduct on the same point. Nobody should be selling you your child's own class teacher.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, the freeze and a two-year plan
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little without the budget it sits inside. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, across 17 different curricula. In May 2026 the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion.

For a Diploma family that freeze is the first predictable year in a while, and it changes the planning question. The money that would have absorbed a fee rise is the money most families then spend on tutoring, often without deciding what it is for. The useful discipline is to price the whole two-year Diploma plan once, in advance, rather than approving monthly packages as panic arrives.

A two-year plan priced honestly has three components and two of them are small. One weekly subject slot sustained across DP1 and DP2 is the large number. Internal assessment support, concentrated in two or three blocks when the school deadlines fall, is a moderate number. An exam-term intensive before the May session is a short, expensive burst. Families who plan all three in September spend less than families who buy each one in a crisis.

The last line of the table below is the one nobody mentions. A private candidate sitting exams outside a school pays entry fees directly to the board, and those are set by the board and its local centre, not by a tutor. If that applies to your child, get the figure from the exam centre in writing before building any budget around it.

sections.heading: If the budget is fixed, where the dirhams actually earn marks
paragraphs: Most families do not have an unlimited tutoring budget, and the honest question is not what the cheapest hour costs but which hour buys the most marks. Four years of watching Diploma candidates in this region produces a consistent order, and it is not the order most families buy in.

First purchase: one diagnostic session per weak subject, worked from the most recent marked paper. This is the cheapest high-value hour available, because it tells you whether you need a tutor at all and if so what for. A surprising number of diagnoses conclude that the pupil understands the content and is losing marks to command terms or timing, which is three sessions of work rather than a term.

Second purchase: internal assessment question design, in DP1, before the school approves the topic. A research question too broad to control caps the mark on a component worth a fifth of the subject grade, and no amount of later polishing recovers it. Two sessions spent narrowing a question are worth more than ten spent on a draft.

Third purchase: the single most mechanical technique fix in each subject. Paper 1 stem annotation in the sciences. Calculator-free fluency in Analysis and Approaches. A comparative spine in English Paper 2. Diagram labelling and referencing in Economics. These are rule-bound, drillable and visible in the next marked paper. The committed weekly slot, which is where most families start, belongs fourth, and only where a genuine content gap exists.

Spend on the internal assessment question, not the final draft

process.title: Say the subject, the level and the budget
process.description: Including the budget, which most families withhold and should not. A figure lets us tell you honestly whether a specialist in that subject and level is reachable at that number, or whether a shorter component block is the better use of it. Guessing wastes a fortnight of email.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: The paper with the annotations on it, not the report grade. It shows whether marks are going to content gaps, command terms, conventions or timing. Those four faults cost different amounts to fix, and the paper tells us which one you are buying help with.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the proposed specialist, no cost and no card required. It is run as a diagnosis, so by the end you have a written statement of the fault and the first four weeks of work. If the conclusion is that no tutoring is needed this term, you will be told that.

process.title: Get the quote itemised
process.description: Session length, frequency, whether internal assessment support is inside the figure, whether written session notes are included, what the cancellation terms are, and whether value added tax applies. Any provider unwilling to itemise those six things is worth walking away from.

process.title: Review at four weeks against marked work
process.description: Measured against the next piece of marked school work, not against how the sessions felt. The review names what moved, what did not, and whether to continue, change the match or stop. An arrangement with no scheduled exit is a subscription, not a plan.

whyPoints.title: The numbers are on the page
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure here is attributed to the provider page or cost survey that published it. Three of the six pages ranking for this search publish no price at all and one declines to answer its own question about cost. A parent can only judge a quote against a market they can see.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the rate
whyPoints.description: Delivery is one-to-one over live video, so nobody is charging you for ninety minutes of driving or imposing a two-hour minimum to make the trip worthwhile. The hour you buy is the hour the pupil uses, and sixty minutes is a normal booking rather than an awkward one.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject, not on driving distance
whyPoints.description: The scarce thing in Dubai is a teacher with current experience of a specific Higher Level subject, not a car. Matching from a national online pool means a family in Dubai South chooses from the same specialists as a family in Al Barsha.

whyPoints.title: The permit position stated plainly
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge and valid for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. No fine schedule is published, so no fine figure appears here. Anyone quoting you an amount is repeating something that has not been verified.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the pupil's own
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria, questions a research question and gives feedback on a draft the candidate wrote. No part of a submission is produced for a candidate at any price. One provider in this market advertises finished internal assessments; that is a risk sold to your child.

whyPoints.title: An exit built into the arrangement
whyPoints.description: Four-week reviews against marked school work, with an explicit option to change the match or stop. No grade is promised, because no honest tutor can promise one, and a provider that does is pricing a promise they cannot keep.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published rates for a tutor travelling to a Dubai address run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with a cost survey for this market placing the common band at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500. Higher Level sciences and Higher Level mathematics sit at the top of that range, and outer communities attract a two-hour minimum rather than a higher hourly figure. Online one-to-one teaching with a qualified subject tutor is published at AED 150 to AED 300, and with a Diploma specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 or above.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home rate so much higher than the online rate?
faqs.answer: Travel time, almost entirely. A tutor crossing Dubai in the after-school window absorbs sixty to ninety minutes of unpaid driving for a single sixty-minute lesson, plus fuel, Salik crossings and visitor parking. That is why in-home quotes arrive with two-hour minimums for villa communities and tighter cancellation terms. The teaching itself is not more expensive. The published online packages in this market work out near AED 100 an hour where in-home packages for the same eight hours work out at AED 200 to AED 225, and the difference is a car.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a Dubai address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer in-home visiting anywhere in the UAE; that is a service provided only in India. Teaching for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The practical consequence is a wider choice of specialists rather than a narrower one, because the match is made on the exact subject and level rather than on who can reach your community before 6pm. It also removes the travel component from the price, so a sixty-minute booking is normal rather than uneconomic.

faqs.question: What makes one Diploma subject cost more to tutor than another?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the scarcest teaching in this emirate, because Dubai Diploma cohorts are often small enough that one teacher covers both levels. Scarcity sets the price. English A and Biology are easier to source and quote lower, despite Biology carrying more content than almost anything else. Minority subjects such as Computer Science at Higher Level or Global Politics can be unobtainable locally at any rate, which is a supply problem rather than a pricing one.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the exam session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and predictably. Specialist availability tightens from February through April, before the May session that Dubai private schools sit, and the same tutor who had open slots in October has none in March. Families who fix an exam-term slot in the autumn pay autumn rates for it; families who start looking in March are bidding for what is left. If an exam-term intensive is part of your plan, book the slot early and treat the booking as the purchase, separate from when the sessions happen.

faqs.question: Is the quoted rate per hour or per session, and does it include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask both questions explicitly, in writing, before agreeing anything. Some providers in this market quote per sixty-minute hour and others per session, which may be ninety minutes or two hours, and the two figures are not comparable. On tax, the treatment of tuition fees is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring website, so the only safe question is whether the specific figure you have been quoted is inclusive of value added tax. A provider who will not answer that in writing is telling you something.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget per month for IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: A cost survey for this market estimates monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to AED 600 with a budget tutor, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four in-home sessions of two hours. Divide any package back into an hourly figure before comparing, and check whether unused sessions carry forward across Dubai's half-terms and holidays.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence, and does it cost them anything?
faqs.answer: A permit, and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, whose service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school pupils aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Can I hire my child's own school teacher privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving pupils affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, it is a poor arrangement on its own terms: the person who set the assessment is not the person best placed to show your child how an external examiner reads it. Verify the current policy with the school directly.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai parent ask before accepting a tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Six things, all of which should be answered in writing. Whether the rate is per sixty-minute hour or per session. Whether there is a minimum block. Whether internal assessment support is inside the figure or billed separately. Whether written session notes and a progress summary are included. What the cancellation terms are, including for a session already prepared. And whether the figure includes value added tax. A provider who itemises all six is quoting a service; one who gives a single number is quoting a hope.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor a false economy for Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Frequently, though not always. At the budget end of this market, AED 45 to AED 150 an hour commonly buys a university student or a generalist, which is genuinely good value for primary numeracy, for Middle Years content catch-up and for exam-paper drill under supervision. For a Higher Level science or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level it usually buys someone one step ahead of the pupil, which produces reassurance rather than marks. The better economy is fewer hours with a specialist, aimed at one component, rather than more hours with a generalist.

faqs.question: Does a two-hour in-home block teach twice as much as one hour?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and this is the part of the in-home model families most often overpay for. Two-hour minimums exist because the travel arithmetic requires them, not because a sixteen-year-old concentrates well for two hours after a full school day plus transport. Diagnostic sessions and technique drills are most effective in focused blocks of forty-five to sixty minutes. Where longer sessions genuinely help is sustained drafting work on a piece of coursework, and that is a handful of occasions per subject per year, not a weekly pattern.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee freeze affect what I spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a Diploma family that makes the year's education budget predictable, which is the right moment to price the whole two-year plan once rather than approving monthly packages as deadlines arrive. Families who plan the weekly slot, the internal assessment blocks and the exam-term intensive together in September reliably spend less than those who buy each in a crisis.

faqs.question: What happens to the price if no specialist is available in my child's subject?
faqs.answer: The price stops being the issue. Minority Higher Level subjects are thin in this market because small Dubai Diploma cohorts cannot timetable them either, so there may be nobody to buy at any rate locally. Because teaching is delivered over live video from a national specialist pool, the search is not limited to people who can drive to your community, which widens the field considerably. Where nobody is free even then, the options are a dated waiting position, a related-subject specialist for transferable technique, or a straight no for the term.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be paid to finish an internal assessment before the deadline?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider who offers it is selling your child a serious risk rather than a service. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments for a fee; under IB academic-honesty rules that is malpractice, and the consequences fall on the candidate, up to losing the Diploma. What a tutor may legitimately be paid for is teaching the published criteria, interrogating the research question, and giving feedback on a draft the candidate has written. The candidate writes every word of the submission that carries their name.

dubai/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get the quote itemised before you compare it
dubai/ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are pricing an IB home tutor in Dubai, the market bands on this page are enough to judge any quote you receive. The next step costs nothing: send the subject, the level, the target grade and one recent marked paper, and you will get an honest answer about whether a specialist is reachable, how long a match takes, and what shape of booking that particular fault needs. The trial lesson that follows is a full diagnostic session over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card required. If the diagnosis is three sessions rather than a term, we will say three sessions.

intro.heading: Why two quotes for the same subject can differ by a factor of ten
paragraphs: A Dubai parent who asks three providers for IB tutoring quotes will often get AED 60, AED 250 and AED 650 an hour. Those are not three prices for the same thing. They are three different products with the same label, and the gap between them is made of four things: who the tutor is, how long the session has to be, whether anyone is driving, and what you have committed to in advance. Separate those out and the market becomes legible.

Published market figures make the structure visible. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, typically online and often delivered by undergraduates. Qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Exam-level IB and IGCSE specialists run around AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 and beyond. The premium named end reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home one-to-one visits occupy their own band of roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, per Bestimate and local home-tutor listings.

Those are other providers' published prices, read in October 2026, with their names attached so you can check them yourself. They are not IB Gram's price list, and most competitors in this search publish no figure at all, which is why parents end up comparing by feel. The pattern in the numbers is simple: format sets the floor and demonstrable specialism sets the ceiling. A home visit cannot be cheap in a city where a tutor may drive forty minutes each way, and a Chemistry HL specialist in April cannot be cheap because every family wants the same eight weeks.

This page treats the home-tutoring question straight, because it is the question being asked. Home tuition in Dubai is a real, widely used service, it has a real price, and families choose it for understandable reasons: a younger child who needs an adult physically present, a household with poor connectivity, a parent who wants to overhear the lesson. Those reasons are legitimate and this page does not argue with them. What it does is show you the cost structure behind the quote so you can tell a fair one from an inflated one.

IB Gram's own model is different and worth stating plainly before you read further. We deliver one-to-one tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school week. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The fee consequence of that is straightforward, and it is the main reason the comparison table further down exists: nobody is paying for a car, so the money in the hour goes to teaching, and the tutor is chosen for the subject rather than for the drive.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-fees.programmesIntro: Fees vary by programme because the work does. A PYP session is short and skills-based; a DP2 session is long, paper-based and competes with every other family in the emirate for the same weeks of the year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive band to buy, for sound reasons. Sessions are usually sixty to ninety minutes, demand concentrates into the months before final papers, and the tutor needs current subject-guide accuracy plus the ability to mark against published criteria. Core components add their own hours: Extended Essay process support and Theory of Knowledge feedback are separate asks from subject teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP demand is highly seasonal, which moves prices in practice even when a published rate card does not change. Requests cluster from January to April, and a family booking a specialist in that window is competing with the whole emirate at once. Booking in DP1 term two, rather than waiting for a DP2 mock result, is the single cheapest decision available.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Usually mid-band. Sessions are shorter, the content is less specialised and a single tutor can often cover two related subjects, which reduces the total spend. The useful spend here is on criterion literacy rather than content coverage, because an MYP report in letters and numbers is what most parents cannot act on.
programmes.countryNote: Many Dubai families start tutoring in MYP 4 or 5 because of a transition decision ahead: Diploma or a British sixth form. That makes a short diagnostic block better value than a long commitment, since the question is as much about fit for the next qualification as about recovering a current grade.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The lowest band, and the one where in-home fees look most attractive to parents of young children for reasons that have little to do with teaching. Sessions are typically thirty to forty-five minutes, which matters when a provider's minimum booking is ninety, since you then pay for time a seven-year-old cannot use.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary cohorts include many mid-year arrivals from other systems, so the common request is to close a specific gap rather than to run a long programme. Arabic as an additional language is the most requested primary subject in the emirate, driven by the KHDA requirement that private schools teach it regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, TOK and internal assessment support
programmes.description: Often priced per block rather than per hour, because the work is bursty: heavy at the question-framing stage, light in the middle, heavy again before a supervisor deadline. A fair quote for this is time-based with a stated cap, since open-ended coursework support is how tutoring bills quietly expand.
programmes.countryNote: Internal deadlines for these components differ by several weeks between Dubai IB World Schools, so a block bought against a neighbour's timetable may land in the wrong month. Ask your school's coordinator for the assessment calendar before buying hours, and build the block around the school's dates rather than a provider's package.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Subject scarcity is a real fee driver in Dubai, because DP provision sits in a minority of schools and specialist teachers are correspondingly thin. Below, each subject carries a note on what tends to move its price locally.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in the emirate, which keeps SL supply reasonable and rates mid-band. HL, and particularly Paper 3 investigation work, is scarcer and sits at the specialist end from February onwards.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Growing demand as more Dubai students take the applied route, but fewer teachers have taught both courses. Expect specialist pricing where a tutor can genuinely cover the statistics and modelling content rather than adapting an analysis course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The tightest HL market in Dubai between February and May, which is when most families start looking. Booking the same tutor in DP1 costs the same per hour and gets a better choice of slot.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mid to specialist band. Uncertainty treatment and the practical investigation are the components that need a specialist; mechanics support is widely available and should not attract a premium.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Good supply at SL, tighter at HL. The fee-efficient intervention is command-term and extended-response work, which transfers quickly, rather than a full content sweep across the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Moderate supply. HL quantitative work and internal assessment commentary feedback are the parts worth paying specialist rates for; general theory coverage is not scarce in Dubai.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Widely available, so a premium rate here needs justification. The scarce skill is marking unseen-text analysis against the published descriptors, which is worth asking a tutor to demonstrate before agreeing a rate.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Reasonable supply at SL, thinner at HL. Case-study application work is the high-value hour; framework recall is not something to buy at the top of the market.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The thinnest subject market in the emirate, and the one where UAE-based coverage most often runs out. Expect a longer match time and a match from our wider pool, with no change to the online format.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: High volume across all year groups because Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum. Rates are mid-band, but matching the school's stream matters more than the rate does.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Usually bought as a short block rather than weekly. The highest-value hours are spent on prescribed-title choice and knowledge-question framing, both of which happen before any writing and cost very little.

subjects.name: Extended Essay process support
subjects.description: Price this as a capped block, not open-ended. The scope and method conversation is a few hours; everything after that is the student's own writing, with the school supervisor formally responsible for the process.

sections.heading: IB home tutor fees in Dubai: the published bands, by format
paragraphs: Start with what the market actually publishes, because three of the six most visible competitors in this search publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in. The figures below are AED, attributed, and were read in October 2026. They describe the market, not IB Gram's rates.

In-home one-to-one sits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts the band at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. The spread inside that band is mostly about distance and subject: a maths session for a Year 7 student in a central community is near the bottom, and an HL science session in an outlying villa community in April is near the top. Online qualified subject tutoring sits lower, roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

Above both, exam-level IB and IGCSE specialists run around AED 200 to 450 and above, which overlaps the in-home band and is the fact most parents find useful: a specialist online hour and a generalist in-home hour can cost the same, and one of them contains forty minutes of driving. At the top, BartyED advertises AED 650 for premium named tutoring. At the bottom, EdFlik lists AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, both online and both typically delivered by undergraduate tutors.

Two notes on using these figures. First, an hourly rate is meaningless without the minimum session length, which is covered further down and frequently doubles the real cost of a booking. Second, a provider quoting below the market floor for specialist DP work is telling you something about who will teach the session. That is not automatically wrong, and for homework supervision it may be exactly right, but it should be a conscious choice rather than a surprise.

sections.heading: Taking a quote apart: the line items that are really in there
paragraphs: A home-tutor quote in Dubai is usually presented as one number per hour, and almost never itemised. That is a problem, because the differences between two quotes sit in the items nobody names. Six of them account for most of the variation, and each one can be asked about in a single message before you commit.

Travel is the largest. A tutor crossing the emirate in evening traffic can lose eighty minutes to a sixty-minute lesson, and no sustainable rate ignores that. Minimum session length is the second, and the most commonly underestimated: a ninety or one-hundred-and-twenty-minute minimum exists so the journey is worth making, and it means a parent who needed forty-five minutes of help pays for twice that. Third is subject and level, which is the only item that reflects teaching value.

Fourth is timing in the academic year. Nobody publishes an exam-season surcharge, but availability tightens from January to April and the discount disappears, which has the same effect on what you pay. Fifth is commitment: packages discount the hourly rate in exchange for prepayment and a notice period, which is a real saving and a real risk. Sixth is the admin layer, covering replacement policy, cancellation terms, materials and reporting. Those should cost nothing extra, and a quote that charges for them separately is worth questioning.

One item that should never appear: the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It is granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees. If a quote itemises a licensing or registration cost for an individual tutor, ask what it is for, because the permit itself costs nothing.

sections.heading: Travel is the part of a Dubai in-home fee you pay for twice
paragraphs: The geography of this emirate is the single biggest input into in-home pricing, and it is worth being concrete about why. A tutor living in a central community who takes a 17:00 booking in an outlying villa development is committing roughly two and a half hours to deliver sixty minutes of teaching. They can therefore fit two bookings into an evening, sometimes three if the two families live close together. Everything about the in-home rate follows from that arithmetic.

The first way you pay for it is in the hourly rate, which has to cover the unpaid time in the car. The second way is in the minimum session length, which exists to reduce the number of journeys per paid hour. The third, less visible way is in choice: the tutors who can realistically serve your community are the ones who live within range of it, which is a filter on subject specialism that has nothing to do with teaching quality. A family in an outlying community looking for a Chemistry HL specialist is choosing from a far shorter list than the emirate actually contains.

There is also a reliability cost. Dubai evening traffic is variable rather than merely slow, and a tutor who is twenty minutes late has lost a third of a sixty-minute session. Over a term, that attrition is real, and it is one of the reasons families who have used both formats often report that online sessions start on time in a way in-home sessions do not. A session that begins when it is meant to is worth something.

None of this makes in-home tutoring a bad choice. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present, for a household with unreliable connectivity, or for a parent who wants to overhear the lesson, the premium buys something genuine. The point is to know what the premium is for, so that a family paying it is paying for presence rather than for a tutor's commute.

sections.heading: In-home against online, with the fee difference itemised
paragraphs: Here is the comparison that matters for a Dubai budget. Take a mid-market quote in each format and look at what the money buys. An in-home hour at AED 300 contains teaching, travel and a minimum-length requirement that may mean booking ninety minutes. An online hour at AED 250 contains teaching, chosen from a tutor pool limited only by timezone, in a session as short or long as the student can use.

The second difference is the tutor. In-home selection is geographic first and subject second, because somebody has to drive. Online selection is subject first: a family in an outlying community can have the Chemistry HL specialist rather than the nearest available science teacher. For common subjects at common levels that distinction matters less. For HL sciences, Maths AA HL Paper 3, Computer Science or a narrow internal assessment question, it is the whole decision.

The third is record. An online session leaves annotated past papers, saved whiteboard working and, on request, a recording. A session at a kitchen table leaves a page of handwriting. For a working parent who cannot sit in on a 19:00 lesson, that written trail is the only oversight available, and it is the reason our session notes are deliberately short enough to read in half a minute.

IB Gram's position, stated plainly: we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We would rather publish that than let a page about home tutor fees imply we will send someone. What we sell for Dubai is one-to-one live video tuition on Gulf Standard Time, with the subject specialist chosen for the component your child is actually losing marks on.

sections.heading: Monthly packages: the discount and what it costs you
paragraphs: Packages are how most of this market is actually sold, and reading one properly takes two minutes. Advertised examples in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

The arithmetic is worth doing. Eight sessions at AED 799 is roughly AED 100 a session, which places the tutor firmly in the budget band and tells you something about who is teaching. Four two-hour in-home sessions at AED 1,699 is about AED 212 an hour, which is near the bottom of the published in-home band and implies either short travel or a generalist tutor. Neither is a criticism; both are information the headline figure hides.

The risk in a package is not the price, it is the expiry and the notice period. Unused hours that lapse at month end convert a discount into a loss during a travel month or an exam week. A notice period longer than two weeks means a mismatch costs you a month. And a package that fixes session length at two hours is poor value for a student whose useful attention runs to seventy minutes, which for most DP students it does.

What to ask, in one message: does the rate hold if we pause for a school holiday, do unused hours roll forward and for how long, what notice do you need to stop, and can we change tutor within the package without restarting it? Reasonable answers to those four turn a package into a genuine saving. Evasive answers are the reason to pay per session until the match is proven.

sections.heading: Two years of Diploma support, costed in context
paragraphs: Most families budget tutoring a month at a time and then get a shock at the two-year total. It is worth modelling the whole Diploma up front, because the shape of the spend is not even: DP1 is cheap and DP2 is expensive, and a family that spends nothing in DP1 usually spends more overall.

Useful context for the numbers: Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for roughly a fourteenth of enrolment and UK curricula for well over a third. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For 2026-27 the emirate is also adding seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

Against a frozen school fee, a tutoring budget is the variable part of a family's education spend, and that makes sequencing worth planning. One subject at one session a week through DP1, at mid-band online rates, is a modest annual figure. Two subjects at two sessions a week through the final six months of DP2, at specialist rates, is several times that. Families who start earlier at lower intensity generally pay less in total and get a better choice of tutor, because they are not buying in the February-to-April crush.

sections.heading: Payment terms, receipts and the things worth refusing
paragraphs: Fees are only half of what you agree to. The terms around them decide what a mismatch costs, and in a market where the first tutor is often not the right one, that is the part to read. Four things are worth insisting on and one is worth refusing outright.

Insist on a written rate per hour with the session length stated, because an hourly figure without a minimum is not a price. Insist on a cancellation window you can actually live with, since school events and illness happen in every Dubai term. Insist on a replacement policy at no cost if the subject match is wrong, which is a reasonable ask because the provider chose the tutor. And insist on a receipt that names the service, the hours and the period, which is simply ordinary record-keeping.

Refuse to prepay a long block before a trial lesson has happened. There is no good reason for it and it transfers every risk to the family. A free trial costs a provider one hour and removes the main source of disputes in this market, which is why ours is genuinely free with no card details taken beforehand. The one condition is that it is a single lesson, stated here on the same screen as the word free.

On tax, be careful about what anyone tells you. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and this page does not have one. What you can and should do is ask a provider whether the figure quoted to you is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and get the answer in writing before the first invoice. A quote that becomes five per cent larger at invoice time is the most avoidable surprise in this market.
