sections.heading: Delivery, scheduling and what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time. Most sessions land between 16:30 and 20:30, after the school run and activities. During Ramadan many families move to a post-Iftar slot, which is straightforward with notice. Gulf Standard Time sits between South Asia and Europe, which is why a Dubai evening slot can reach a wide pool of IB subject teachers.

Coverage is honest rather than universal. Common subjects at common levels are usually matched within a few days. Narrow combinations take longer, and between February and May they take longer still, because every family in the emirate is looking for the same specialists in the same eight weeks. Computer Science HL and specific HL science components are the requests most likely to run past a week.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to the format or the subject depth. We say so before you commit rather than after, because a disclosed limit costs a family nothing and a concealed one costs them a fortnight. And where we think the spend is wrong, we say that too: a student losing marks to command terms does not need the top of the market.

One last fee point, because it is the one families thank us for. The cheapest hour in a two-year Diploma plan is the one bought in DP1 to frame an Extended Essay research question properly. It takes a few hours, it is paid at a normal rate, and it prevents the much larger spend that follows a coursework crisis in DP2. Early and small beats late and large, in this market more than most.

faqs.question: How much do IB home tutor fees in Dubai come to per month?
faqs.answer: Published monthly figures give a usable range. Advertised packages in the emirate include around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Convert any package to a cost per hour before comparing, because the implied hourly figure tells you which band of tutor is actually teaching the session.

faqs.question: What is included in a Dubai home tutor's hourly fee?
faqs.answer: Six things, usually unnamed: the teaching itself, the tutor's travel time and fuel, the minimum session length that makes the journey worthwhile, the subject and level premium, the timing in the academic year, and an administrative layer covering replacement and cancellation. Travel is the largest hidden component in a city this spread out, since a sixty-minute lesson in an outlying community can occupy two and a half hours of a tutor's evening. Ask how far the tutor is travelling and what the shortest bookable session is; those two answers explain most of the difference between quotes.

faqs.question: Why do home tutors in Dubai insist on a minimum session length?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is the fixed cost. A tutor who drives thirty to forty minutes each way cannot make a forty-five-minute booking viable, so a ninety or one-hundred-and-twenty-minute minimum reduces the number of journeys per paid hour. The consequence for a family is that the real cost of a short need can double: a student who required forty-five minutes of help pays for twice that. Online sessions have no journey, so length can be set by what the student can actually use, which for most Diploma students is between sixty and ninety minutes of focused work.

faqs.question: Do home tutor fees differ between one Dubai community and another?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, although few providers publish it that way. Distance and evening traffic set how many bookings a tutor can fit into a night, so outlying villa communities attract longer minimum sessions or a higher effective rate than central, well-connected areas. The second, less visible effect is on choice: the specialists willing to travel to your community are a subset of the emirate's tutors, which filters availability by geography rather than by teaching quality. Online delivery removes both effects, which is the main reason families in outlying communities move to it.

faqs.question: Are IB tutor fees in Dubai quoted per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Both are used, and the mismatch is where confusion starts. An hourly rate without a stated minimum is not a usable price, because a quote of AED 250 an hour with a two-hour minimum is a AED 500 booking. Always ask for the figure and the number of minutes together, in writing. Where a provider sells monthly packages, divide the package by the hours included to get the implied hourly cost, then compare that against the published bands. That one calculation reveals more about what you are buying than any description of a tutor's background.

faqs.question: Should I prepay a tutoring package before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: We would advise against it, and not only because we offer a free trial. Prepayment before a lesson has happened transfers every risk of a bad match to the family, and in this market the first tutor is often not the right one. Pay per session until the fourth session, by which point you can see whether technique is moving. If you then want a package, ask four questions first: do unused hours roll forward and for how long, what notice is needed to stop, does the rate hold through school holidays, and can the tutor be changed without restarting the package.

faqs.question: Do IB tutoring fees in Dubai rise before the May examination session?
faqs.answer: Published rate cards rarely change, but the effect is the same. Demand across the emirate concentrates between January and April, so discounts disappear, preferred slots fill, and the specialists who were available in October are not. Families competing for the same eight weeks end up paying the top of a band for a tutor they could have had mid-band six months earlier. The practical response is to book the subject specialist in DP1 or early DP2 at lower intensity, which costs less per hour overall and gives a genuine choice of tutor rather than whoever is left.

faqs.question: Is VAT included in a Dubai tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing before the first invoice. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because stating it responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation that this page does not carry, and a confident wrong answer would be worse than none. What matters practically is whether the figure you were quoted is inclusive or exclusive, since a quote that grows at invoice time is the most avoidable billing surprise in this market. A provider who cannot answer that question clearly is telling you something about their record-keeping.

faqs.question: What does supporting an IB Diploma student in Dubai cost over two years?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on sequencing rather than on rate. One subject weekly through DP1 at online qualified rates of AED 150 to 300, plus a short capped block to frame the Extended Essay question, is a modest annual figure. Two subjects at two sessions a week through the final six months of DP2 at specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 and above is several times larger. Families who start earlier at lower intensity usually spend less in total and get a better choice of tutor, because they are not buying in the February-to-April crush when the whole emirate is looking.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's UAE permit add anything to the fee?
faqs.answer: It should not. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page for it lists no fees and gives a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website and e-services system. So a quote that itemises a licensing or registration charge for an individual tutor deserves a question about what the charge actually covers. Asking to see the permit is reasonable and costs the tutor nothing, since holding it costs them nothing.

faqs.question: What should a tutoring cancellation policy say?
faqs.answer: It should name a notice period you can realistically meet inside a Dubai school term, where concerts, sports fixtures, travel and illness are routine rather than exceptional. Twenty-four hours is common and workable; same-day forfeit with no flexibility is not, and a vague policy is worse than a strict one because it gets interpreted after the dispute. Ask also what happens to a session the tutor cancels, and whether a missed session inside a package is lost or rescheduled. Those two answers tell you whether the terms were written for the family or only for the provider.

faqs.question: Why does online IB tutoring cost less than a home visit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because nobody is driving. The published in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour has to absorb twenty to forty minutes of travel each way plus the fuel, and that is before the minimum session length that exists to make the journey worthwhile. An online hour carries none of that, so a larger share of the fee is teaching. The second effect is on choice: online matching is done on subject and level rather than on who lives within range, which for HL sciences or a narrow component is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available generalist.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one session to reduce the fee?
faqs.answer: It can work, with a caveat worth taking seriously. Where two children are at genuinely similar levels in the same subject, one session split two ways halves the cost per child and the shared work can help both. Where the levels differ, the session becomes two half-lessons and each child gets less than they would from a shorter individual session. Our usual suggestion is to run the siblings separately but back-to-back, which keeps the attention undivided and still solves the scheduling problem that makes families ask in the first place.

faqs.question: What costs tend to appear after the first tutoring invoice?
faqs.answer: Four recur. A VAT line that was not mentioned in the quote. A minimum session length applied to a booking the parent thought was hourly. Materials or reporting charged separately, which should normally be included. And package hours that lapsed at month end during a travel week or a school holiday. All four are avoidable by agreeing five lines in writing beforehand: the AED figure, the number of minutes, the cancellation window, the replacement policy and the VAT position. That takes one message and removes almost every billing dispute we hear about.

faqs.question: How do Dubai school fees compare with a year of IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Tutoring is the variable part of an education budget whose fixed part is currently steady: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Against a frozen fee, a weekly mid-band online session across a school year is a modest addition, while two specialist subjects at two sessions a week through a final exam run is a much larger one. Modelling the whole two years before committing is what prevents the second scenario arriving unplanned.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-fees.closingHeading: Price the hour, then price what is inside it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-fees.closingBody: If you are comparing IB home tutor fees in Dubai, ask every provider for three numbers rather than one: the AED rate, the minimum session length, and what happens to the fee if the match is wrong. Those three reveal more than any description of a tutor's background. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no travel inside the hour, no minimum designed around a journey and no home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Send us the subject, the level and the component, and we will tell you which band the request sits in and why before anything is paid.

intro.heading: The school run is the reason this search exists
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 2 sits between Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Qudra Road, south of the original Arabian Ranches and north of Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3. It is a villa community with a souk at its centre, a British-curriculum primary school inside the gates and no Diploma Programme provision within walking distance of any of it. For a family with a DP1 or DP2 student, that geography sets the shape of the week before anyone discusses tutoring: the child leaves early, returns late, and the first usable academic window opens somewhere after five.

That window is what a search for an IB home tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 is really about. Parents here are not shopping for a venue. They are trying to recover the hour that the drive to Al Barsha South, Dubai Sports City or the Sustainable City removes from the afternoon, and the obvious way to recover it looks like booking somebody who turns up at the gate. That is one answer. In this part of Dubailand it is rarely the quickest one, and the research below shows it is not the cheapest either.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one tuition over live video. We do not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; door-to-door tutoring is a service offered only in India. The reason is not administrative tidiness. A Diploma student taking Chemistry at Higher Level needs a teacher who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level, and the number of those inside a twenty-minute radius of Ranches Souk is small enough that most families settle for a capable generalist who is reading the subject guide on the way over.

Online changes what you are choosing between. Instead of the tutors who happen to live near the Ranches, the choice becomes the tutors who teach your child's exact course: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level rather than maths, Biology Higher Level rather than science, Economics Standard Level with the commentary deadline already in view. Lessons are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, the screen and the working are shared both ways, and the work a student submits stays the student's own. Nothing travels, so nothing is billed for travel, and a five o'clock slot does not require somebody to leave somewhere else at twenty past four.

The rest of this page is written from the clock rather than from a brochure. Which schools this neighbourhood actually feeds, roughly what time each of them finishes, what the return leg does to the afternoon, and where in the evening a sixty- or ninety-minute session can sit without colliding with homework, a swim squad at Dubai Sports City, or a Friday that finishes at lunchtime. Every AED figure quoted is a market rate from a named source, never a price list of ours.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches 2 families arrive at the Diploma by two routes: through the Middle Years Programme at an IB continuum school, or through IGCSE at a British school followed by a switch at sixteen. The three programmes below are the ones that matter for this neighbourhood, each with a note written from a Dubailand villa rather than in general terms.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, and it closes with the Year 6 Exhibition. There is no external examination, which means a parent's only reliable signal is the school's own reporting against learning outcomes. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining a method out loud, because those are what the Middle Years Programme will start grading.
programmes.countryNote: Arabian Ranches 2 children in the PYP are mostly bussing to continuum schools in the Sustainable City or Al Barsha South, so the day is long for an eight-year-old. A thirty-minute online slot twice a week lands better here than a single hour, and it fits after the bus and before dinner without turning the evening into a second school day.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP grades each subject against four criteria, A to D, on an eight-point scale, and converts the total to a 1-7 subject grade using published boundaries. Criterion wording is the thing students misread: a task asking them to analyse is not asking them to describe. Year 11 ends with the Personal Project, which is assessed on its process journal and the student's own reflection as much as on the product.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Arabian Ranches 2 parents most often discover a gap, because MYP reporting looks reassuring until the DP1 maths and sciences start. Families with a child in MYP 4 or 5 are the ones who benefit most from booking a subject-specific review before the DP subject choices are locked, usually in the spring term of Year 11.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment set and marked in school against published criteria and then externally moderated. The Higher Level papers are longer, carry additional content and, in several subjects, add a third paper that Standard Level candidates never sit. UAE schools sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Arabian Ranches 2 are travelling to JESS Arabian Ranches, Fairgreen International School, North London Collegiate School Dubai, Nord Anglia International School Dubai or Dwight School Dubai. That spread is why the evening slot matters so much here: a DP2 student back at 16:15 from Al Barsha South cannot sensibly start Higher Level content before five, and the honest answer is to protect two fixed evenings rather than four scattered ones.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects below are the ones Arabian Ranches 2 families book most often, with a note on what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing. Availability is confirmed before you pay, and where a Higher Level specialist is not free in Gulf Standard Time we say so rather than substitute somebody from a neighbouring subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-proof route, with a no-calculator Paper 1 that catches students who have learned to lean on a graphics calculator. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a two-part extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade. Most lost marks are notation and unjustified steps rather than genuine gaps in method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with a graphics calculator permitted in every paper. Students who chose this expecting an easier course find the Higher Level statistics and the regression work demanding. Marks go in interpretation: a correct value with no sentence saying what it means in context scores less than students expect.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level carries additional content Standard Level candidates never sit, and organic mechanisms plus energetics are where the grade is usually decided. The Internal Assessment is a single scientific investigation of the student's own design, assessed on research design, data analysis and conclusion, which is where most of the avoidable marks sit.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics is taught first and examined last, so DP2 students often arrive at the paper with the oldest topic least secure. Uncertainties and significant figures quietly remove marks in the data-analysis questions. Higher Level fields and the extended topics are what separate a 5 from a 7 in practice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of defined terminology makes this a recall-plus-application subject rather than a reading subject. Command terms matter: outline, explain and evaluate carry different mark allocations for the same content. The investigation needs a measurable, controllable variable, and a poorly chosen one costs more marks than weak writing ever will.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries drawn from published news articles, each tied to a different unit of the course, form the Internal Assessment. Diagrams carry marks on their own: axes labelled, equilibrium shifted, the change explained in the student's own words. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that trip students who treated the subject as essay-only.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under timed conditions, which rewards a repeatable approach far more than wide reading. The Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts and is internally assessed. Higher Level adds the HL Essay, a formal 1,200 to 1,500-word piece on one text studied.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based rather than theory-based: students are expected to apply named frameworks to a real organisation and justify the choice of tool. The Internal Assessment is a research project on a genuine business issue. Marks are lost in evaluation, where answers summarise findings instead of weighing them against the question asked.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition in DP1 and the prescribed-title essay in DP2, graded A to E and contributing to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Students treat it as an opinion piece and lose marks for unexamined claims. Supply of specialist tutors is genuinely thin, and we say so when it is.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: A tutor can help a student narrow a researchable question, test whether the sources exist before the writing starts, and read a draft against the assessment criteria. A tutor cannot draft, rewrite or finish it. That boundary is set by IB academic-honesty rules and it is not negotiable at any price.

The notes below are about session timing, not property.

regions.note: One of the larger clusters, towards the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road side of the community. Families here tend to be on the earlier bus drops coming back from Al Barsha South, so a 16:30 start is often workable for a Standard Level subject.

regions.note: A townhouse and villa cluster whose families mostly use the Al Qudra Road side of Arabian Ranches 2. Secondary students bussing from Dubai Sports City are usually settled by around 16:15, which makes 17:00 the first comfortable Higher Level slot.

regions.name: Palma
regions.note: Close to the central spine and the Ranches Souk end of the community, which is useful for families who stack a tutoring slot after a sports session rather than straight after school. A 19:00 start is common here in DP2.

regions.note: Towards the southern edge, nearest Arabian Ranches 3 and Mudon. The extra minutes on the internal roads at pick-up time are small in isolation but they decide whether 16:30 or 17:00 is the realistic start for a Year 12 student.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.modesIntro: Three formats are realistic for an Arabian Ranches 2 family, and the right one usually depends on the level rather than on the budget. All three are delivered online over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which is what makes the timing in the table further down this page achievable at all.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, fixed slot
modes.description: One tutor, one student, the same evening each week for the length of a term. The fixed slot is the point: it survives the school run, it gets written into the family calendar alongside swimming and football, and it gives the tutor a predictable rhythm for setting work between sessions. Most Diploma families start with two subjects at one session each.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes, chosen to fit after the bus rather than to fill a billing unit

modes.title: Internal Assessment and coursework review
modes.description: Block sessions timed around the school's own internal deadlines rather than the exam calendar. The tutor reads the student's draft against the published assessment criteria and explains which criterion the draft is currently losing marks under. The writing, the data and the conclusions remain the student's own work from first draft to submission.

modes.description: A short, dense block in the weeks before the May session, built around past-paper technique and the specific topics a student's mock paper exposed. This format suits DP2 students who have the content but lose marks to timing and command terms. It is bought by the block rather than open-ended, so the family knows the end date when they start.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 actually gets you
paragraphs: It gets you one-to-one Diploma Programme teaching delivered live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the exact course and level your child sits. It does not get you somebody at the villa door. IB Gram does not operate home visits in the UAE, and saying so on the page is more useful than letting a parent discover it on a phone call.

The phrase itself is worth taking seriously rather than correcting. Families type home tutor because they want the lesson to happen where the child already is, without another car journey at the end of a long day. That requirement is real and it is the one thing online delivery satisfies completely: the lesson happens in the room the child is already sitting in, and the only travel involved is from the kitchen to wherever the laptop lives.

What changes is the pool. A tutor who has to reach Arabian Ranches 2 by road is drawn from whoever lives in Dubailand, Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Al Barsha and has a free evening. A tutor who teaches over live video is drawn from everyone who teaches that subject at that level in a compatible time zone. For Standard Level support in a broad subject the difference is modest. For Chemistry Higher Level, Analysis and Approaches Higher Level or Theory of Knowledge, the difference is the whole decision.

One more practical consequence. Because nobody drives anywhere, a cancelled or moved session costs nothing in wasted travel, which is why rescheduling by notice is straightforward rather than a negotiation. Families in this community reschedule more than they expect to, usually for a sports fixture or a school trip, and a format that absorbs that without a surcharge is worth more over a term than a slightly lower hourly rate.

sections.heading: The Arabian Ranches 2 school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 2 has a primary school inside the community and nothing above it, so almost every secondary student here commutes. The table below sets out the schools this neighbourhood actually feeds, their approximate road distance from Ranches Souk, a typical weekday finish and the earliest hour at which a tutoring session is realistically worth starting. Finish times vary by year group and by term, so treat them as the shape of the day rather than a timetable.

Two features of the Dubai school week matter more than distance. The private-school week runs Monday to Friday with a short Friday, which means Friday afternoon is the single most underused academic slot available to a Diploma student in this community. And the afternoon peak on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Qudra Road overlaps exactly with school dismissal, so the return leg is consistently slower than the same trip at eleven in the morning.

The earliest realistic session column is deliberately conservative. It assumes the child gets through the door, eats something and sits down, which in practice takes longer than parents allow for when they book a slot. A session that starts fifteen minutes late every week loses most of a lesson over a term, so the better move is to book the later slot and keep it than to book the earlier one and apologise for it.

For families running two children on different buses, the arrival spread is usually thirty to forty minutes. Where that is the case, the workable pattern is one fixed evening per child on different days rather than two sessions stacked on the same evening, because the second one always lands in homework time and the student is already done.

sections.heading: Why a quarter past four is the wrong start time for a DP2 student here
paragraphs: Parents book the earliest slot the schedule technically allows, because it leaves the evening free. For a Year 12 or Year 13 student coming off a long commute, that choice reliably produces the worst hour of the week. The student is physically present and cognitively finished, the tutor spends twenty minutes rebuilding attention, and the family concludes that tutoring is not working when the problem was the clock.

The Diploma load makes this sharper than it is at other levels. A DP2 student is carrying six subjects, four of which will have an Internal Assessment deadline inside the same eight-week window, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Their afternoon already contains obligations. Dropping a Higher Level session into the first available gap means it competes with the school's own deadlines rather than supporting them.

The pattern that works in Arabian Ranches 2 is a later start with a protected shape: arrive home, eat, thirty minutes of nothing, then a focused sixty or ninety minutes beginning between five and half past seven depending on the cluster and the sports schedule. Where a family runs co-curriculars at Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches Golf Club two evenings a week, the sensible answer is to accept a seven o'clock slot on the free evenings rather than squeeze a session in before the fixture.

Friday is the exception worth planning around. With a short school day across Dubai private schools, a Friday session sits on a rested student with no commute behind it and nothing scheduled after it. For Higher Level content and for Internal Assessment work, where thinking rather than drilling is required, a single Friday session frequently outperforms two weekday evenings.
bullets: Book the slot the student can concentrate in, not the earliest one the calendar permits
Thirty minutes of decompression after the bus is not wasted time, it is what makes the hour work
Two protected evenings beat four opportunistic ones across a term
Friday mornings and early afternoons are the strongest and least-used slot in the Dubai week

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition compared for a Dubailand villa community
paragraphs: This is the comparison the market avoids publishing. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family pays in. The figures below are AED market rates taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They describe what the market charges, not what IB Gram charges.

Read the travel column first, because in Arabian Ranches 2 it is the column that decides the others. An in-home rate of AED 180-500 an hour includes the tutor's travel, and it is quoted that way because the travel is real: crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road or Al Qudra Road between half past three and half past six is not a fifteen-minute proposition. A tutor who can only fit two visits into an evening prices accordingly.

The second thing the table shows is where specialisation actually costs money. A budget online tutor at AED 45-150 an hour is a reasonable way to supervise homework and keep a Standard Level subject ticking. It is not a way to move a Chemistry Higher Level grade, because the person is usually not a Chemistry Higher Level teacher. The specialist band at AED 200-450 and above buys course-exact teaching, and for one or two subjects in DP2 that is the band most families end up in.

Group classes deserve one honest line. A monthly package advertised in this market at around AED 799 for eight online sessions looks like strong value until you notice it is a group rate and the group is not at your child's level. For topic revision where everyone is sitting the same paper, group teaching works. For a student who is losing marks for a reason specific to them, it does not.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar counted backwards from a villa in Casa or Rosa
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, and the May session is not the deadline that bites first. The deadlines that shape a DP2 student's year are internal: the school's own submission dates for each Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay drafts and the Theory of Knowledge essay. Those sit months before any examination and they are set by the school, not by the IB, which is why two students in the same community can be working to different dates.

Precise IB session and results dates are deliberately not published here. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the school's internal calendar and confirm the external dates with them or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, the published dates further down the IGCSE pages in this set are sourced and usable.

Working backwards is the useful exercise. If an Internal Assessment is due to the school in the second half of DP2 term one, the data collection has to be finished a month earlier, the research question has to be agreed a month before that, and the point at which a tutor can genuinely help is at the question stage, not at the draft stage. Families who book support in the week before a deadline are buying proofreading, which is both the least valuable and the most ethically constrained thing a tutor does.

The same logic applies to the Extended Essay. A 4,000-word piece needs its sources tested for existence before the student commits to the question. Half the Extended Essay problems a tutor sees are not writing problems; they are questions that cannot be answered with the material the student can actually reach from Dubai.
bullets: The school's internal deadlines, not the IB's, are what govern a DP2 autumn
Confirm every IB date with your Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutoring site
Book Internal Assessment support at the question stage, not the week before submission
Test that the Extended Essay sources exist before the question is locked

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an IB tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: A tutor may teach content, model a method, explain what a criterion rewards, read a student's own draft and say which criterion it is currently losing marks under. A tutor may not write, rewrite, draft, edit to completion or supply any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. That boundary is set by the IB's academic-honesty framework and it applies to paid support exactly as it applies to a parent.

This is not a theoretical concern in this market. One site examined during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. A student who submits purchased work faces an academic-misconduct investigation and, where it is upheld, the loss of the qualification. No grade is worth that exposure, and no tutor who offers it is protecting your child.

The practical version of the rule is simple to police as a parent. Ask to see the feedback the tutor gave, not just the improved draft. Criterion-referenced feedback looks like a list of criteria with a note against each; completion looks like prose that suddenly sounds like somebody else. If the draft improves and the student cannot explain why, something has gone wrong regardless of what anybody intended.

We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the boards' copyright. Tutors reference them, cite them and point families to the official source, which is also the only version guaranteed to be current.

sections.heading: What a KHDA inspection band actually tells an Arabian Ranches 2 parent
paragraphs: KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and under the UAE government's own description it is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects private schools annually and publishes an overall judgement on a six-band scale from Outstanding through Very Good, Good, Acceptable and Weak to Very Weak. That report is public and it is the only school-quality signal on this page worth reading.

What the band does not tell you is how your child's specific subject at Higher Level is taught. A school can hold a strong overall judgement while a particular department is thin, usually because of a mid-year staffing change. Conversely a school in a lower band may have an outstanding Physics teacher. Parents in this community occasionally make a tutoring decision on the strength of the inspection headline when the subject-level detail inside the report is the part that matters.

Dubai's private-school sector is large enough that these bands are the practical filter: KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The IB share is small, which is exactly why IB specialist supply is thinner than general tutoring supply.

Two further facts are useful context for a family budgeting a year of support. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the authority valued at AED 1.5 billion. And the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools in Dubai, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Read inspection reports on KHDA's own site, never from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Tutor coverage for this neighbourhood, and what happens when a subject is not covered
paragraphs: No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. The table below is the alternative: what we can usually staff for an Arabian Ranches 2 family, roughly how long a match takes, and what we do when the specialist a student needs is not available in Gulf Standard Time.

The honest position on a thin subject is to say so. Theory of Knowledge is the clearest example: demand concentrates in DP2 when the prescribed-title essay lands, supply is small because few teachers specialise in it, and substituting a subject teacher produces confident advice that does not match the assessment criteria. Where we cannot staff it, the useful answer is a referral back to the school's own Theory of Knowledge lead rather than a booking.

Where a specialist is not UAE-based, we widen the search to tutors teaching in a compatible time zone and tell you before you book. Gulf Standard Time is four hours ahead of UTC, which keeps an early-evening Dubai slot inside the working day for tutors across South Asia and comfortably inside the afternoon for tutors in the United Kingdom. The constraint is not geography but the student's own evening.

Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit in a separate category. KHDA requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects in Dubai schools, and the mandatory content itself may not be varied without prior Ministry of Education permission. For those subjects the first conversation belongs with the school, and we say that rather than taking a booking we should not take.

process.title: Tell us the course, the level and the hour that actually works
process.description: Not the subject but the course: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, Chemistry Standard Level, English A Language and Literature. Then the honest earliest start time given your cluster in Arabian Ranches 2 and your child's school. Those two facts determine whether we can match a specialist, and they take about four minutes to supply.

process.title: We check availability before you commit to anything
process.description: A specialist is either free in your evening slot or is not. We tell you which, name the tutor, state their qualification and board experience, and say if they are outside the UAE. If we cannot cover the subject at the level you need, you hear that instead of being matched with the nearest approximate person.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with no card details taken
process.description: One full lesson at no cost so the student meets the tutor before any money changes hands. The trial is a real lesson on real content, not a sales call: the tutor diagnoses where marks are going and says so at the end. No payment details are required to book it and there is no obligation afterwards.

process.title: Fix the slot and keep it for the term
process.description: The same evening each week with the same tutor, written into the family calendar next to the school run and the sports fixtures. Work is set between sessions and reviewed at the start of the next one. Sessions can be moved by notice without penalty, because nobody has made a journey that cannot be recovered.

process.title: Review against the school's own reporting
process.description: Every half term, compare what the tutor is seeing against the school's reports and the student's own marked work. If the two disagree, that is information worth acting on. If the subject no longer needs support, the sensible outcome is to stop that subject rather than to carry it to the end of the term.

whyPoints.title: The tutor matches the course, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Online delivery removes distance from the selection, so the question becomes who teaches Analysis and Approaches Higher Level rather than who teaches maths and lives near Dubailand. For Standard Level support the difference is modest. For Higher Level sciences and maths in DP2 it is the difference that shows up in the grade.

whyPoints.title: Timing built around the Dubailand school run
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and set after the realistic arrival time for your child's school, not at the first slot the calendar allows. Friday's short school day is treated as the strongest revision window of the week rather than as an afterthought, because for Higher Level content it usually is.

whyPoints.title: No travel, so no travel in the price
whyPoints.description: Market in-home rates of AED 180-500 an hour include the tutor's road time across E311 or Al Qudra Road in the dismissal peak. Nothing travels in an online session, so the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching, and a session moved for a school trip costs nobody a wasted journey.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty boundaries, stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, model and give criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own work. They do not write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, saying where the line sits is the most useful thing a tutoring page can do.

whyPoints.title: Figures and facts with their sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, every regulatory statement to the authority that issued it, and no IB examination date is published because the IB's own site could not be checked automatically. Numbers without a source are not reassurance, they are a liability.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed rather than hidden
whyPoints.description: Where a specialist is not available in Gulf Standard Time, you are told before booking, including whether the tutor is based outside the UAE. Theory of Knowledge and KHDA-approved Arabic and Islamic Education are the two areas we routinely decline, and declining is more useful to a family than an approximate match.

faqs.question: Can I book an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; door-to-door tutoring is a service we offer only in India. What we provide for Arabian Ranches 2 is one-to-one Diploma teaching delivered live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so the lesson still happens in the room your child is already sitting in. The practical gain is the tutor pool: instead of whoever can reach your gate between dismissal and dinner, you get the person who actually teaches your child's course at your child's level. The practical loss is that no adult is physically in the room, which matters more for a nine-year-old than for a DP2 student.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start if my child finishes school at 15:15?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student bussing back to Arabian Ranches 2 from Al Barsha South or the Sustainable City, 17:00 is the first slot that works properly and 17:30 is safer. The return leg overlaps the afternoon peak on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Qudra Road, and the student then needs to eat and decompress. For the schools closest to the community, including JESS Arabian Ranches at roughly three kilometres, 16:30 is usually achievable. Booking the earliest technically possible hour is the most common scheduling mistake families here make: a session that starts fifteen minutes late every week loses most of a lesson across a term.

faqs.question: Which schools do Arabian Ranches 2 children actually attend for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: There is no Diploma Programme provision inside the community, so Diploma students commute. The nearest option is JESS Arabian Ranches, which runs IGCSE and then the IB Diploma about three kilometres away. Beyond that, the cluster most used from here covers Fairgreen International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai in the Sustainable City, and Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Dwight School Dubai and Repton Al Barsha in Al Barsha South. A smaller group travels to Emirates International School Meadows or Sunmarke School. These schools are named as neighbourhood context; no affiliation is implied, and inspection reports should be read on KHDA's own site.

faqs.question: Is Friday actually a usable day for IB tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is the best day of the week for it, and almost nobody uses it. Dubai private schools run a Monday to Friday week with a short Friday, so the student arrives home early, rested and with no commute behind them. For Higher Level content and Internal Assessment work, where the task is thinking rather than drilling, one Friday session frequently achieves more than two tired weekday evenings. Families in Arabian Ranches 2 who protect a Friday slot tend to keep it, because nothing else competes for the hour. The main constraint is family plans, since Friday afternoon is also when weekends start in practice.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor cost per hour for a family in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours. A qualified subject tutor working online is commonly AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table quoting AED 200-450+. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180-500 once travel is included. Budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45-150. Monthly packages around AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in this market, usually as group rates. IB Gram does not publish a rate card here; the free trial and the consultation are where our own pricing is discussed.

faqs.question: Does a 90-minute session work better than two 60-minute ones in DP2?
faqs.answer: For Internal Assessment work and Higher Level problem-solving, yes. Both need a run-up: the student has to reload where they were, and twenty minutes of a sixty-minute session can disappear into that. Ninety minutes gives one proper working block. For content catch-up, vocabulary-heavy subjects or anything that needs repetition, two shorter sessions on different evenings beat one long one, because spacing is doing the work. Most Arabian Ranches 2 families settle on ninety minutes for the subject causing the most trouble and sixty for the second subject. The deciding factor is usually the school run rather than the pedagogy.

faqs.question: My child is at Ranches Primary School — is tutoring sensible this early?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and rarely in the form parents imagine. At primary age the useful targets are reading fluency, number facts and the habit of explaining a method aloud, because those are what the Middle Years Programme will later grade against criteria. What does not help is a sixty-minute evening session after a long bus ride. Two thirty-minute online slots a week, early enough to be before dinner, fit this age group far better. If the school's own reporting is not flagging a gap, the honest advice is usually to wait and spend the money in Year 9 or 10 instead.

faqs.question: How do online lessons handle a maths question that needs working shown?
faqs.answer: Through a shared writing surface rather than a talking head. The tutor and the student both write on the same digital whiteboard, so the tutor sees the working develop line by line and can stop at the line where it goes wrong, which is the only place a maths correction is useful. Students photograph a handwritten page and drop it in when they prefer paper, which many Analysis and Approaches students do for proofs. The session is recorded on request so the student can revisit the method. For a no-calculator Paper 1 technique, this works at least as well as sitting side by side.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics HL and Mathematics AA HL for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because the overlap is real: Higher Level Physics leans on calculus and algebraic manipulation that Analysis and Approaches teaches directly. A tutor comfortable with both can use one subject to reinforce the other. The risk is a tutor who is strong in one and adequate in the other, which produces a reasonable Physics hour and a weak maths hour at the same price. We tell you which subject the tutor's qualification and recent teaching actually sit in, and if the honest answer is that they should only take one of the two, that is what we recommend.

faqs.question: What exactly can an IB tutor do with my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help narrow a research question before the writing starts, check whether the data or sources are actually obtainable, and read the student's own draft and say which criterion it is currently losing marks under. What a tutor must not do is write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of it. One provider examined during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright; a student submitting purchased work risks an academic-misconduct finding and the loss of the qualification. Ask to see the feedback, not just the improved draft.

faqs.question: How does an Arabian Ranches 2 parent check a tutor has a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection band tell me about my child's school?
faqs.answer: KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools annually, publishing an overall judgement on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The band is a reliable summary of the school and a poor guide to one subject at one level, because a single staffing change can leave a strong school with a thin department. Read the subject detail inside the report rather than the headline, and read it on KHDA's own site. No tutoring page, including this one, should be your source for a school's rating.

faqs.question: Can our session move later during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually should. School hours are reduced during Ramadan across the UAE, so the afternoon looks different and the evening is organised around Iftar. The pattern most Arabian Ranches 2 families move to is a later start after Iftar, or a daytime slot on the short school days, with a slightly shorter session length. Because nothing has to travel, moving the slot for the month costs nothing and reverts afterwards. Tell us at the start of the month rather than week by week, so the tutor's whole Ramadan schedule is set once and your slot is not the one that gets squeezed.

faqs.question: We travel over the winter break — can lessons follow the family?
faqs.answer: They can, with one caveat about time zones. An online session needs a stable connection and an agreed hour, both of which usually survive travel. The caveat is that Gulf Standard Time is four hours ahead of UTC, so a Dubai evening slot becomes an inconvenient afternoon or morning slot depending on where you go. The workable approach is to agree the holiday hours before you leave and to reduce frequency rather than attempt the normal pattern from a hotel. Many DP2 families use the break for a short Internal Assessment block instead, which travels better than content teaching does.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not the right fit for my child?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the tutor, which is why the free trial exists before any payment. Fit at Diploma level is rarely about warmth; it is usually about pace and about whether the tutor explains in the register the student thinks in. A mismatch shows up inside two sessions, and the signal to watch for is a student who stops asking questions. When we re-match, the new tutor gets the previous diagnosis, so the term does not restart from zero. If the subject turns out not to need support at all, the useful recommendation is to stop it rather than to carry it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.closingHeading: Start with the hour, then the tutor
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.closingBody: Tell us your child's course and level, which school they travel to, and the earliest evening hour that is honestly workable from your cluster in Arabian Ranches 2. We will say whether a specialist in that exact course is free in that slot, name them, and state their qualification and whether they are UAE-based. Then there is a free trial lesson, with no card details taken, so the student meets the tutor on real content before anything is paid. If we cannot cover the subject at the level you need, you will hear that instead of being matched to the nearest approximate person. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The JBR school run is the real constraint, not the subject
paragraphs: Jumeirah Beach Residence is a strip of roughly forty towers between the beach and King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street, with Bluewaters Island across a short bridge and the Dubai Tram running the length of it. What JBR does not have is a private secondary school inside it. Every Diploma student living in these towers commutes out of the community in the morning and back into it in the afternoon, which is why a parent typing "IB home tutor in JBR" is almost never asking a question about teaching quality. They are asking a question about time.

Work the timings through and the shape of the problem appears. Secondary school days in Dubai mostly finish between 14:30 and 15:15. A school bus from Al Barsha South into JBR in afternoon traffic takes between thirty-five and fifty-five minutes once it has dropped the rest of its route. A car coming north on Sheikh Zayed Road from Umm Suqeim after 15:30 is unpredictable in a way that no tutoring schedule survives. The practical consequence is that a JBR student is rarely at a desk, fed and settled, before 16:00, and in exam term is often not settled before 16:30.

That single fact does more damage to in-home tutoring in this neighbourhood than price does. A tutor driving to a JBR tower has to arrive after the student, find visitor parking in a basement designed for residents, clear a security desk, and share a lift bank at the busiest hour of the building's day. Thirty minutes of billable time can disappear before anyone opens a textbook, and the tutor has to be out again in time to reach their next booking, which is why in-home sessions in this area tend to be sold in two-hour blocks the student is too tired to use well.

IB Gram answers the same search differently. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. There is no home-visit option here: home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. What that buys a JBR family is the thing the commute took away. The session starts at the minute it was booked, because nobody has to arrive. A sixty-minute slot at 16:15 is sixty minutes of teaching. And the tutor is chosen because they teach Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, not because they happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of the Walk.

This page is written around the school run on purpose. It sets out which school clusters JBR children travel to, what time each cluster releases them, when a weekly session can honestly start, how online compares with an in-home visit on cost and on lost time, what the Dubai market charges, and how the Diploma year looks counted backwards from the May examination session. Where a figure appears, its source is named. Where something cannot be verified, the page says so instead of guessing.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: JBR households are mixed: Diploma students in Years 12 and 13, Middle Years students at the same schools, and a steady flow of families arriving mid-cycle from British or American systems. These are the three programmes that come up most on this stretch of coast, with what each one does to a weekday evening.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments in every subject run on school deadlines that cluster in the same two months, which is what turns a manageable DP1 into a difficult DP2. Tutoring here is usually one or two subjects deep rather than broad: the Higher Level that is dragging the predicted total down.
programmes.countryNote: For a JBR family the Diploma's problem is scheduling, not content. Two Higher Level subjects needing weekly support means two fixed slots a week after a commute that already eats ninety minutes. Online slots at 16:30 and 18:00 on different evenings work; two in-home visits in one week rarely survive a month of Dubai traffic.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0-8, with no public examination unless the school enters students for eAssessment. Parents often misread an MYP report because a criterion score is not a percentage. The useful tutoring work in MYP 4 and 5 is criterion literacy plus the algebra and scientific writing that the Diploma will assume from day one.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in JBR finish school earlier than their Diploma siblings and get home with more of the afternoon left, so a 16:00 slot is genuinely available to them. Families with one child in each programme usually stack the MYP session first and the DP session after dinner.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with reading, number fluency and written expression carried underneath. Support at this stage is short and frequent: thirty to forty-five minutes, twice a week, on one specific thing such as number bonds, fraction sense or sentence structure, not a general hour of catch-up.
programmes.countryNote: Several JBR towers have nurseries at ground level, but primary-age children still travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah. Short online sessions suit them because a tired seven-year-old will give a focused thirty minutes at 16:00 and nothing useful at 18:00.

programmes.name: Diploma core: EE, TOK and the IAs
programmes.description: The Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word limit and the Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600 words, both assessed against published criteria rather than against a syllabus. These components fail on process far more often than on knowledge: a research question that cannot be answered in the word count, or a reflection written the night before the deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Process coaching is where this work belongs, and it belongs in writing. A tutor reads what the student has written, points at the criterion the paragraph is missing, and hands it back. IB Gram tutors do not write, draft or complete any part of an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or internal assessment.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Requests from this neighbourhood skew towards the Higher Levels that gate university applications and towards the subjects where a school's teaching group is large. These are the subjects JBR families ask about most, with what the assessment actually rewards and where marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens: students who can get an answer from a graphing screen cannot always reach it by hand. Proof, complex numbers and the algebra of integration are the HL pressure points. The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with six of those marks for the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics, modelling and interpretation carrying the weight. Marks are lost in the words rather than the working: a correct regression with no comment on what the gradient means in context scores poorly. HL adds matrices, graph theory and a far heavier statistical load than most students expect from the easier-sounding route.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The syllabus rewards precision about definitions and about what a graph gradient physically represents. Circular motion, fields and the HL-only sections on induction and quantum phenomena are the reliable trouble spots. Data-analysis questions need uncertainty handled properly, and that skill transfers straight into the internal assessment, which is worth 20 per cent of the grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics separate a 5 from a 7, because both demand that a student explains rather than recalls. Multi-step calculations lose marks on units and significant figures rather than on method. The internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to generate real data in a school laboratory within the time the school allows.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do the work here. "Outline", "explain" and "discuss" ask for different amounts of writing, and students who answer every question at the same length leave marks everywhere. HL depth on nucleic acids, metabolism and plant biology is examinable detail, not background, and the statistical treatment in the internal assessment is marked as carefully as the biology.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest available gain: an axis mislabelled, a shift drawn in the wrong direction, an equilibrium not marked. Paper 2 requires data response written with evaluation attached, and HL Paper 3 is quantitative in a way the textbook chapters do not advertise. The portfolio of commentaries is assessed on published criteria and is the student's own work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and most students lose marks by summarising a text instead of analysing how it works. The Individual Oral requires a global issue linked to two specified extracts, and the HL essay runs to 1,200-1,500 words. Preparation is about building a repeatable analytical move, not about reading more.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as Ansoff, SWOT and break-even analysis are easy to name and hard to apply to an unfamiliar case study, which is exactly what the papers ask for. Higher Level adds the pre-released case study with its own research demands. Quantitative questions on ratios and cash flow are frequently the difference between a 4 and a 6.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under examination conditions is a distinct skill from writing code in an editor, and the paper tests tracing and dry-running as much as design. HL abstract data structures, recursion and the case study carry heavy marks. The solution component is assessed on documented process, so the development record matters as much as the finished program.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Marked on a 1,600-word essay from a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Students who write about knowledge in general score badly; the criteria reward precise argument about a specific claim with real examples. One hour a fortnight from October is usually enough if it starts early rather than in the last fortnight.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in JBR is really asking
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in JBR, in the sense the phrase is normally meant, is a private tutor who drives to a tower in Jumeirah Beach Residence and teaches at the kitchen table. That service exists in Dubai and the market rate for it runs from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour depending on level and on whether travel is priced separately, according to the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and the published from-rates of UAE agencies reviewed in October 2026. IB Gram does not sell it. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

Saying that plainly at the top of the page is more useful than burying it, because the two services solve different halves of the problem. An in-home visit solves supervision: an adult is physically present and a younger child cannot wander off. Online one-to-one solves specialism and time: the tutor is chosen for teaching Chemistry HL rather than for living nearby, and no part of the hour is spent on the drive, the visitor pass or the lift. For a Diploma student with a Higher Level problem and ninety minutes of commute already gone, the second trade is usually the better one.

The rest of this page treats the question seriously in both directions. It gives the honest numbers for what an in-home tutor costs in this area, the honest numbers for what the online market charges, and a side-by-side comparison of the two on the things that actually change a JBR evening. Then it gets specific about the school run, because the single most common reason tutoring stops in this neighbourhood is not price or quality. It is that the slot was set at a time the student was still on a bus.

sections.heading: The JBR school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Dubai secondary school days mostly end between 14:30 and 15:15. What happens next depends entirely on which cluster the school sits in, and the spread is wide enough to make a single recommended session time useless. A student at a school in Al Sufouh can be home in JBR in fifteen to twenty-five minutes. A student on a bus route out of Al Barsha South, with four or five drops before the towers, can take fifty-five. The same child, same school, can be home at 15:35 one day and 16:20 the next, depending on Sheikh Zayed Road.

That variability is the argument for a later fixed start rather than an earlier optimistic one. A session booked for 15:45 is a session that will be fifteen minutes short most weeks and missed entirely some weeks, and after a month of that the family quietly stops. A session booked for 16:30 happens. It is worth asking your school's transport office for the actual drop time for your tower rather than the published arrival window, because the two often differ by twenty minutes once the route is loaded.

sections.heading: Why there is no IB school inside JBR, and what that changes
paragraphs: JBR was built as a residential and retail strip rather than as a master-planned family community with a school plot in the middle of it. There are nurseries at tower level, but no private secondary school stands inside the community, so the schooling map for a JBR teenager is drawn entirely outside it. That is unusual in Dubai, where villa communities such as The Springs or Jumeirah Park typically have a school within a few minutes of the gate, and it is the structural reason the tutoring question here is a logistics question.

It also means a JBR tower holds students from an unusually wide spread of schools and curricula. One lift bank can carry a Diploma student heading to Al Sufouh, a British Year 11 student going to Al Barsha and an American-curriculum student travelling to Jumeirah, which is why neighbour recommendations travel badly in this community. The tutor who was excellent for the child three floors up may teach a different programme at a different level for a different board.

For tutoring, the practical consequence is that matching has to be done on the specific syllabus and level rather than on proximity or reputation. Dubai had 227 private schools serving 387,441 students across seventeen different curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate schools accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment according to the Dubai Media Office. In a neighbourhood with no school of its own, that diversity lands in the same building, and the only reliable filter is the syllabus code and level the student is actually sitting.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home tutor in JBR
paragraphs: The comparison most pages in this market avoid is the one a parent most needs, so here it is on the terms that matter in a tower block. The honest summary: an in-home visit costs more per useful minute in JBR than it does in a villa community, because the building adds friction a villa does not. Basement parking designed for residents, a visitor pass at the desk, and a shared lift at the hour everyone comes home all sit between the tutor arriving and the lesson starting.

The tutor pool is the second difference, and it is larger than most families expect. A tutor willing to drive to JBR for a single sixty-minute booking is drawn from whoever is both free and close, and that pool thins fast at the top of the Diploma. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Chemistry HL and Economics HL specialists are not evenly distributed across Dubai neighbourhoods. Online, distance stops being a filter and the only question left is whether the tutor teaches the level your child is sitting.

None of this makes an in-home tutor a poor choice for every family. A primary-age child who needs an adult in the room, or a household with unreliable connectivity, is better served in person, and IB Gram will say so rather than sell around it. What this page will not do is promise a tutor at a JBR address. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, and the comparison below is offered so the decision is made on evidence rather than on a phrase in a search box.

paragraphs: Three of the six ranking pages in this search publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The bands below are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and they come from published UAE agency from-rates and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, reviewed in October 2026. For what IB Gram itself charges, the trial lesson and the consultation are the route; the rate depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions, so a single published figure would be misleading.

Read the bands alongside the school-fee context, because tutoring is a marginal cost on top of a large fixed one. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second phase of Dubai's economic incentives package. A family whose fees have held flat is usually making the tutoring decision against a known budget rather than a moving one, which is why the cost-per-grade question gets asked more sharply here than elsewhere.

The thing worth paying attention to is what sits inside the rate. A low hourly figure that excludes marking means a student does timed papers that nobody reads carefully, which is the most expensive saving available in DP2. A higher figure that includes marked scripts, written follow-up and contact with the school's deadline calendar is usually cheaper per grade point. Ask what happens between sessions before comparing two numbers that look different.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and the useful way to plan tutoring is backwards from it rather than forwards from today. Working backwards reveals the two pinch points that catch JBR families out every year. The first is the window when internal assessments across several subjects reach final submission within a few weeks of each other, which arrives in DP2 term two. The second is the mock examination period, which is early enough that a student who starts revising afterwards has lost the diagnostic the mocks were for.

One caution on dates, stated here because other pages in this market get it wrong. The International Baccalaureate blocks automated retrieval of its calendar, so no specific IB session or results date is published on this page. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it. Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter and are published by the boards; Cambridge, for example, sets final entries for its March 2027 series on 27 November 2026, months before the February exam window.

The shape below is therefore a rhythm rather than a calendar. It shows what the school is typically doing, what a JBR family should have in place by then, and roughly how many hours a week that implies. The point of publishing it is that no competitor page in this search names a session, a deadline or a results stage at all, and a parent choosing in October needs to know which of these windows they are already inside.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that gets students into real trouble, and it is worth stating precisely because at least one page ranking for these searches sells finished internal assessments outright. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work submitted must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion is asking for, ask the questions that expose a weak research question, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of that work.

In practice the line is easier to hold than it sounds, because the honest version is also the more useful one. If a tutor tells a student that criterion C is thin, the student has to go back into their own reasoning and fix it, and the thinking that produces is exactly what the examiner is marking. If a tutor supplies the paragraph instead, the student learns nothing, the writing does not sound like them, and a supervisor who knows the student's voice will notice.

The consequences are not theoretical. A finding of malpractice can cost a candidate the diploma, and it attaches to the student, not to whoever sold them the text. IB Gram tutors work on the student's own draft and nothing else, and will say no to a request to do otherwise. Separately, no tutor on this platform supplies IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are the boards' copyright and are referenced and linked rather than reproduced.
