sections.heading: Ramadan, Gulf Standard Time and the weeks the schedule changes
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the UAE academic calendar breaks twice a year. During Ramadan, school days shorten and the whole rhythm of a JBR evening moves: a student who was settled at 16:30 in February may be better taught after Iftar in March, and a family fasting through the afternoon will get very little from a 17:00 session. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots for the month and move back afterwards, which is straightforward to arrange online and genuinely difficult to arrange with a tutor driving across Dubai at that hour.

Gulf Standard Time is the second scheduling fact, and it cuts both ways. A tutor based in the UAE shares the student's clock. A tutor in another time zone may be the right specialist for a niche Higher Level subject, and in that case the slot has to be chosen so neither party is teaching or learning at a stupid hour. IB Gram states the tutor's working hours in local time before the trial lesson rather than after the first missed session.

Travel is the third. JBR households travel more than most, between school holidays, summer out of the UAE and family commitments abroad. An online slot follows the student, which means a Diploma student in the submission cluster does not lose three weeks of momentum to a trip. Where a time difference makes the usual slot impossible, the sensible move is a shorter session at a different hour rather than a cancelled block, and that is agreed before the travel rather than during it.

sections.heading: If no specialist is free: the honest version
paragraphs: Availability transparency is missing from every competitor page examined in this cluster, so it belongs here. Some subject and level combinations are genuinely thin. Higher Level Computer Science, Higher Level Economics in the weeks before the session, Arabic as a first language and the less common second languages all run short of specialists at peak. When that happens, there are only three honest answers, and a page that implies otherwise is setting a family up for a bad match.

The first answer is a wait with a date attached: the right tutor has a slot in two weeks and it is worth waiting for. The second is a different format: a shorter session twice a week with a tutor who has fragments of availability rather than one long block that does not exist. The third is a redirect: the student does not need the subject specialist they asked for, they need the Mathematics underneath it, and that is a wider pool. Deciding which of the three applies is what the consultation is for.

What should not happen is a match made on availability alone, which is how a family ends up paying specialist rates for general help. If IB Gram cannot cover a combination to the standard the level needs, the right answer is to say so. A trial lesson exists so the match is tested before any commitment is made, and it takes no card details to book; if the fit is wrong, the honest outcome is a different tutor or no tutor rather than a term of sessions nobody believes in.

process.title: Tell us the school, the subjects and the bus
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the programme year, the two or three subjects causing trouble, and roughly what time your child is actually home in JBR. That last detail decides the slot, and getting it right at the start prevents the most common cause of tutoring quietly stopping in this neighbourhood.

process.title: We match on syllabus and level
process.description: Matching is done against the exact course and level your child is sitting, not against a general subject label. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL and Applications and Interpretation SL are different jobs. Where more than one tutor fits, the tie-breaker is the time slot that works for your commute.

process.title: Trial lesson first, no card required
process.description: The first session is a trial so the match is tested on real work rather than on a profile. It takes no card details to book. Your child brings the current topic or a returned paper, and you get a short written note afterwards on what the tutor found and what they would do over the first month.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot and keep it
process.description: Once the trial works, the slot is set for the same evening each week and held through the year, including exam term. A fixed appointment survives a Dubai term. A session rebooked weekly around other commitments tends to have disappeared by the time mock results arrive.

process.title: Review against the school's own calendar
process.description: Progress is reviewed against the deadlines your child's school actually set, not a generic plan: the internal assessment dates, the mock window, the predicted grade point. If a subject stabilises, the hours move to the one that has not, and if nothing is moving, that gets said rather than billed.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the commute, not to a driving route
whyPoints.description: Every slot on this page is built around when a JBR student is genuinely at a desk, which is later than most schedules assume. Starting at 16:30 with a settled student beats starting at 15:45 with one still on Sheikh Zayed Road, and the difference compounds across a term.

whyPoints.title: Matched on level, not on distance
whyPoints.description: A tutor is chosen for teaching the exact course and level your child sits. Removing distance from the filter is what makes Higher Level specialists available to a tower in JBR, where an in-home search is limited to whoever will drive over for a single booking.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source and a date

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on work the student wrote. No internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is drafted, rewritten or completed for a candidate, and no board material is handed over as a download. That boundary protects the student's diploma.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to my JBR tower?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; home visits are a service offered only in India. Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do sell in-home visits, at market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel usually priced in. In a JBR tower that format loses time to basement parking, the security desk and the lift at the hour everyone arrives home. Online, the hour you book is the hour your child is taught, and the tutor is selected for teaching the level your child sits.

faqs.question: What time should a JBR session start on a school night?
faqs.answer: Between 16:00 and 17:00 for most families, depending on which cluster the school sits in. Children travelling from Al Sufouh are often home by 15:40 and can start at 16:00. Buses from Al Barsha South with several drops can arrive at 16:10, which makes 17:00 the realistic start. Ask your school's transport office for the actual drop time at your tower rather than the published route window, then book twenty minutes after it. A slot set at the optimistic time runs short most weeks and is abandoned by November.

faqs.question: Are there any IB schools inside JBR itself?
faqs.answer: No private secondary school sits inside Jumeirah Beach Residence. There are nurseries at tower level, but every school-age child in these towers commutes out of the community and back, most commonly to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Jumeirah or the villa communities inland. That is why neighbour recommendations travel poorly here: one lift bank can carry students from three different curricula at three different stages. Matching a tutor to the specific course and level a child is sitting matters more in JBR than in a community built around a single school.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student in JBR usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week per struggling subject is the normal starting point, rising to two in the subject under most pressure during the internal assessment submission cluster and the final revision term. Families who start with four hours a week in October rarely sustain it past December, and the sessions that get dropped are not chosen carefully. Starting with one well-placed hour in the subject dragging the predicted total down, then adding only when the first subject stabilises, holds up far better across a Dubai school year.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow my child's own school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the practical difference between useful support and generic tutoring. Internal assessment dates, the mock window and the school's own submission calendar vary between Dubai schools by several weeks, so a plan built on a generic timeline will be wrong for most students. Share the deadline sheet your school issued and the tutoring rhythm is built against it: criterion work before a submission, timed papers before mocks, and recall work rather than new content in the final weeks before the written session.

faqs.question: During Ramadan, does the JBR session time change?
faqs.answer: Yes. School days shorten during Ramadan and a fasting student gets very little from a late-afternoon session, so slots move to post-Iftar for the month and move back afterwards. This is simple to arrange when the lesson is online and genuinely difficult when a tutor has to drive across Dubai at that hour. Agreeing the Ramadan slot a fortnight in advance rather than in the first week avoids the gap that otherwise swallows two or three sessions at a point in the year when coursework deadlines are still moving.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For Diploma-age students, yes, and the reason is specific rather than general. Most of what a DP tutor does is work on a shared document or a marked script: annotating a proof, rebuilding a graph, showing where a command term was answered at the wrong depth. A screen shows that work more clearly than a notebook between two people at a table. The format is weaker for very young children who need an adult physically present, and IB Gram will say so rather than sell an unsuitable fit.

faqs.question: What does IB Gram charge for an hour of IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: The rate depends on the subject, the level and how many sessions you book, so a single published figure would mislead more than it helps; the trial lesson and the consultation are where you get a real number. For context, the Dubai market in October 2026 runs at roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for IB and IGCSE specialists, per published agency rate cards and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table.

faqs.question: Is a MoHRE permit required before a tutor teaches a JBR student?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tutor work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. People tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own service page is the route to verify a permit.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the internal assessment itself?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the content behind it, explain what each criterion is asking for, challenge a research question that cannot be answered within the limits, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, draft, rewrite or complete any part of it. That line comes from IB academic-honesty rules, and crossing it risks the candidate's diploma rather than the tutor's business. Any service offering a finished internal assessment is selling the student a malpractice finding with the text attached.

faqs.question: Which schools do JBR students most often commute to?
faqs.answer: Three clusters cover most of this neighbourhood. Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim hold the closest senior schools and the shortest bus routes. Al Barsha and Dubai Science Park take a large share of JBR Diploma students on longer routes with multiple drops. The inland villa belt around Emirates Hills, Jumeirah Park and the Meadows accounts for the rest. Schools are named on this page only as context for the commute; IB Gram has no affiliation with or endorsement from any of them.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no tutor free for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date. Some combinations are genuinely thin, particularly Higher Level Computer Science, Arabic as a first language and the less common second languages close to the examination session. The three honest options are a short wait for the right tutor, a different format such as two shorter sessions instead of one long block, or a redirect to the underlying skill that is actually the problem. What should not happen is a match made on availability alone at specialist rates.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor covering Mathematics and Physics at the same level removes a slot from a crowded week. Pairings that work are usually within one discipline: the two Mathematics routes, Physics with Mathematics, Chemistry with Biology at Standard Level. Pairings across unrelated Higher Levels usually mean one subject gets a specialist and the other gets a generalist, which is the trade that produces a disappointing term. Two tutors on different evenings is normally the better answer.

faqs.question: How quickly can a JBR family start after the first enquiry?
faqs.answer: Most common subject and level combinations can be matched and trialled within a few days, because the constraint is the slot rather than the search. Niche Higher Levels and less common languages take longer, and in the weeks before the written session everything takes longer because the specialists with the right availability are already booked. If timing matters, the single most useful thing in a first message is the window your child is genuinely free in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: What do you need from us to make the first session useful?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them long. The school and the exact course title with level, so the match is made against the right syllabus. A recent piece of marked work, which tells a tutor more in two minutes than a description does in twenty. And the school's deadline sheet for internal assessments and mocks. With those, the trial lesson starts on real material instead of on introductions, and the written note you get afterwards is about your child rather than about tutoring in general.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma Programme and the Middle Years Programme to students in Jumeirah 3 and along the Jumeirah coast. Matching is done by subject, level and the point you are at in the year: a DP2 student eight weeks from mocks needs a different session plan from a DP1 student opening an Internal Assessment.

intro.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve
paragraphs: Parents in Jumeirah 3 rarely start looking for an IB home tutor in January or in September. The search happens in the weeks after a report, after a mock paper comes back three marks under a predicted grade, or after a DP coordinator uses the phrase "at risk of not meeting the deadline". By then the question is not really about tutoring in the abstract. It is about a fixed calendar: the school's internal deadline for an Internal Assessment draft, the mock window in the new year, and the written papers of the May session, which Dubai Diploma candidates normally sit. Every one of those dates is already set. The only variable left is how the weeks in between are used.

That is how this page is organised. Rather than listing subjects and inviting you to enquire, it counts the IB year backwards from the examination room, so you can see which weeks are load-bearing and which are not. A DP1 student in October has nineteen months and almost no deadline pressure, which is exactly why the Internal Assessment work that gets left until DP2 is the single most common cause of a grade collapsing in the spring. A DP2 student in October has roughly one term before mocks and two before the papers, and in that window the work that moves a grade is narrow and specific: past papers under timing, command-term discipline, and finishing the coursework so that revision is not competing with it.

The phrase you typed matters too. An IB home tutor in Jumeirah 3 is what parents search because that is how home tutoring has worked in this city for twenty years: someone drives along Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road, sits at the dining table for ninety minutes, and leaves. That model has real strengths and one structural weakness, which is that the tutor pool shrinks to whoever can reach your address during the school-run window. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses, and that service exists only in India. What a Jumeirah 3 family gets instead is one-to-one online IB tutoring with a subject specialist, chosen because they teach Physics HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at the level your child sits, not because they happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Umm Suqeim.

The practical consequence is scheduling. A tutor crossing Dubai in the 4pm to 6pm window loses between forty and ninety minutes to traffic, and that cost is either paid in the hourly rate or paid in the start time. Market rates published by Dubai providers in 2026 bear this out: online one-to-one sits roughly in the AED 150 to 300 band for a qualified subject tutor, while in-home one-to-one quotes run from about AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed. Online removes the drive entirely, which is why a 7:30pm or 8:00pm session on Gulf Standard Time is routine for Jumeirah 3 families with two children at different schools and one car.

What follows is the calendar in detail: the Diploma milestones and who sets each one, an eight-week term plan with the evidence a parent should be able to see at each stage, the Ramadan and school-holiday constraints that reshape a schedule every spring, and the academic-honesty boundary that decides what a tutor may legitimately do with an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay. Where a figure appears it is attributed to its source and dated, because an unsourced number on a tutoring page is worth nothing to you.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 3 children sit in three different IB structures depending on their school and year group, and each one has a different relationship with the calendar. The notes below say what each programme assesses and where the term pressure actually falls for a family living on this stretch of the coast.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations, so nothing in it is driven by an exam session. Assessment is continuous and transdisciplinary, built around units of inquiry and finishing with the Year 6 Exhibition. Tutoring at this stage is about securing the mechanics - number fluency, reading stamina, writing structure in English - that the MYP will later assume are already in place.
programmes.countryNote: For a Jumeirah 3 family the PYP question is usually a transition one, because the local school mix means a child may move from a British primary into an IB Middle Years cohort at Year 7. A term of structured number work before that move costs far less time than repairing it in MYP 3.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with the Personal Project in MYP 5 and optional eAssessments at the end. The criteria are published and specific, which makes the MYP unusually diagnosable: a child who scores well on Criterion A and badly on Criterion D has a presentation problem, not a knowledge problem.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 is the year where a Jumeirah 3 timetable gets crowded, because the Personal Project runs alongside the subject criteria and the mandatory Dubai subjects. Families who book a weekly slot in the autumn term of MYP 5 are usually protecting the Personal Project from the February crush.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth a published share of the final grade, and the written papers for most subjects carry the rest. The Diploma is scored out of 45, with three further points available from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the calendar bites hardest in Dubai. A DP2 student in Jumeirah 3 is carrying coursework deadlines set by the school, mocks in the new year, and papers in the May session. Tutoring that ignores the school's own deadline list simply adds a third workstream to a student already running two.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools rather than the mainstream, and the DP subjects inside it are assessed exactly as they are in the full Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Jumeirah 3 student is on the CP, the DP courses inside it still sit to the same session timetable, so the planning in this page applies unchanged to those components. The reflective project has its own school-set deadline, which is the one most often missed.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: Requests from this part of Dubai concentrate on the Group 4 sciences, both mathematics routes and Group 1 English, with Economics and Business Management close behind. The descriptions below name the component where marks are most often lost rather than restating the syllabus heading.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency and proof carry this course. Most lost marks are not conceptual: they come from unjustified steps, dropped working, and answers not given to three significant figures. HL adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper that rewards students who have practised reading an unfamiliar context slowly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. The calculator is assumed throughout, which means marks go missing when students cannot justify the model they chose or interpret a correlation in context. The HL course adds substantially more statistics and matrix work than families expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions and derivations are where the grade is decided. Students who can solve numerical questions often lose Paper 2 marks on explanation questions because they describe what happens rather than why. Uncertainty treatment in the Internal Assessment is a second predictable loss point.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate the most tutoring requests on this coast. The recurring problem is partial answers: a mechanism drawn without curly arrows, or an enthalpy calculation missing a sign. HL extends into additional organic and analytical content that cannot be compressed into a revision fortnight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content masks the real issue, which is command-term precision. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and a student who writes the same paragraph for all four caps out around a 5. Statistical treatment in the Internal Assessment needs separate attention.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis and Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. The Individual Oral is internally assessed and globally moderated. Marks are lost when a student narrates the text instead of analysing how meaning is constructed, and HL adds the written essay on a non-studied body of work.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and real-world application decide the grade. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries built on recent news articles, and most mark loss there is procedural: wrong article date, missing diagram, or evaluation that restates the theory rather than weighing it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based answers reward structure: a student who can deploy an Ansoff matrix or a break-even calculation correctly and then evaluate the limits of the tool scores well. The research project at HL is where time management fails, because data collection is slower than students plan for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode discipline and algorithmic reasoning are examined more tightly than most students assume, and the Internal Assessment requires a documented solution developed for a real client. Sessions usually split between examination technique and keeping the project on the school's deadline.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK produces an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, which together contribute to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. The essay fails when it becomes an argument about the world rather than an argument about knowledge, and that framing is teachable in a handful of sessions.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.regionsIntro: Jumeirah 3 sits between Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road, and the practical difference between it and the communities either side is measured in minutes of school-run traffic rather than in kilometres. The notes below record what that does to a weekday session start.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Villa plots between Al Wasl Road and the beach, with several school gates inside a ten-minute drive. Pick-up traffic clears later here than inland, so a 5pm start is often optimistic and a 7:30pm online slot holds much more reliably through the term.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2
regions.note: Immediately north-east and almost identical in school access. Families here often run two different drop-offs, which is why a fixed online slot in the evening survives the week better than an afternoon appointment that moves whenever a bus is late.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Closer to the City Walk and La Mer side of the coast. Evening traffic on Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road in the DP2 mock season is the main reason parents here end up abandoning in-home arrangements mid-term.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: South along the same coastal strip, with its own cluster of school gates. A tutor driving between Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah 3 in the afternoon is paying for the distance twice, once in time and once in the quoted rate.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Inland of Jumeirah 3 and tightly bound to the same school run. Al Safa families often need a slot after a sports fixture or an after-school club, which is why a schedule agreed in September needs one planned revision by mid-term.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The corridor between Jumeirah and Al Safa. Short distances here disguise long journey times at 4pm, and a session that depends on a car arriving on time is the first thing to break in a week with a mock examination in it.

regions.name: Al Manara
regions.note: A quieter inland pocket with good access to Sheikh Zayed Road. Students here commonly attend schools in Al Barsha and Al Sufouh, which lengthens the afternoon and pushes realistic tutoring to after 7pm.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: Newer coastal addresses with limited school provision inside the community itself. Nearly every family commutes out of the community for school, so a tutoring slot that does not require a second journey is the only one that survives exam term.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah and Al Safa
schoolClusters.note: The school gates closest to Jumeirah 3 are mostly British-curriculum, which is why many students here meet the IB only at Diploma level after IGCSEs. Students we support attend schools across this cluster; we are an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any of them.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The nearest concentration of IB World Schools running the full Diploma sits a short drive inland and south of Jumeirah 3. Diploma students from this coast commonly travel into this cluster each morning, which is what makes their afternoons so short.

schoolClusters.city: Across Dubai, for niche Diploma subjects
schoolClusters.note: Where a subject combination is rare - Higher Level Computer Science with Economics, say - the specialist teaching it may sit outside this part of the city entirely. Online delivery is what makes that irrelevant to a Jumeirah 3 family's schedule.

This is the format that handles coursework deadlines properly, because the tutor sees the draft at the stage the school sees it and can plan backwards from the internal deadline instead of reacting to it.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 3 parent is actually asking in late October
paragraphs: The literal question behind the search is short: can someone experienced in the IB work with my child this term, and how soon. The honest answer for a Jumeirah 3 family is that a specialist can usually be matched within a few working days once the subject, the level and the preferred evening slot are known, and that the first lesson is a free trial with that matched tutor so you can judge the teaching before a schedule is agreed. What a Jumeirah 3 family cannot book through IB Gram is a tutor who drives to the villa, because home visits in the UAE are not a service we sell at all.

That distinction is worth taking seriously rather than treating as a caveat. The reason home tutoring dominated this city for two decades is convenience, not pedagogy, and the price of that convenience is a tutor pool defined by geography. If your child needs Chemistry HL specifically, the question is whether the person teaching it has taught that syllabus to examination, not whether they live within reach of Al Wasl Road at 4:30pm. Dubai's private sector contains 227 schools licensed across 17 curricula, according to figures published by the Dubai Media Office in January 2025, and the Diploma accounts for a small share of that enrolment. The pool of genuine Higher Level specialists in any one subject is therefore thin, and narrowing it by postcode thins it further.

The second half of the question is timing, and that is where the calendar comes in. A family searching in late October is roughly one term from mock examinations and two from the written papers of the May session. That is enough time for a measurable change in a specific component and not enough for a wholesale rebuild of two years of content, which is why the first session is spent deciding what the available weeks will be spent on. The sections that follow set out those weeks explicitly, with the milestones, the people who set them, and the evidence a parent should be able to see at each stage.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar, counted backwards from the examination room
paragraphs: Almost every piece of Diploma pressure a Jumeirah 3 family feels traces back to a date somebody else controls. Some belong to the school: Internal Assessment titles, draft deadlines, mock windows and the internal cut-offs that let teachers mark and moderate before uploading. Some belong to the IB: the submission windows for internally assessed work and the written examination timetable itself. Confusing the two is the most common planning error we see, because a family that treats a school deadline as soft discovers in April that it was the only deadline that mattered.

The table below lays the Diploma out in that order, from the earliest decision to the last paper. Note what is missing from it: specific dates for the IB session. The IB publishes its own examination schedule and results dates, and the only reliable source for them is the IB or your child's Diploma coordinator. Secondary sites circulate versions of these dates that are sometimes a year out of step, so this page names the session - May, which Dubai cohorts normally sit - and sends you to the coordinator for the precise window. Cambridge and Pearson dates, by contrast, are published openly and are quoted on our IGCSE pages with their sources.

Read the table from the bottom upwards if your child is in DP2 and from the top downwards if they are in DP1. The difference in how the two years should be used is stark. A DP1 student has the luxury of fixing the mechanics - working shown properly, command terms understood, a research question chosen with care - at a point where no deadline is pressing. A DP2 student has to triage, which means choosing two or three components where effort converts into marks and deliberately not spending evenings on the rest.

sections.heading: An eight-week term plan that a parent can actually audit
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most Jumeirah 3 families start with, usually because it reaches from a report to a mock or from a mock to a coursework deadline. The value of a fixed block is that it can be audited. An open-ended arrangement that runs for a term without a stated target is how families end up paying for company rather than for teaching, and it is the single most common complaint we hear about previous tutors.

The structure below is what a well-run eight weeks looks like for a DP2 student in one subject. The first fortnight is diagnostic and deliberately slow, because a tutor who starts teaching in lesson one is teaching a guess. Weeks three to six are where content gaps are closed and examination technique is drilled against the published criteria. The last fortnight is almost entirely timed practice, because timing is the skill that collapses first under pressure and the one that recovers fastest with rehearsal.

What matters for a parent is the evidence column. You should not need to take a tutor's word for progress: a marked past paper with a mark breakdown, an error log that shows the same mistake appearing less often, and a session note that names the next target are all checkable without any subject knowledge of your own. Ask for them from the first week. A tutor who cannot produce them after a month is not keeping records, and a block without records cannot be audited at the end of it.

sections.heading: What the Jumeirah 3 school run does to a 4pm session
paragraphs: The hidden variable in every in-home tutoring arrangement on this coast is the car. Jumeirah 3 has school gates within a few minutes in several directions, but many Diploma students travel inland to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or Umm Suqeim, and the return journey lands squarely in the afternoon peak. A tutor booked for 4:30pm is therefore booked against the least reliable hour of the day for both parties, and the usual outcome is a session that starts twenty minutes late and ends on time because the next appointment is somewhere else.

Online delivery removes the journey from the arithmetic on both sides. That is not a marketing point so much as a scheduling one: a 7:30pm or 8:00pm start becomes possible, the lesson begins when it is supposed to, and a cancelled session can be moved to another evening in the same week rather than written off. For families with two children in different year groups it also means two different specialists can teach on the same evening, which no single visiting tutor can do.

The comparison table sets both options out honestly, including the places where a tutor at the table has a genuine advantage. Younger children who need someone physically turning pages are better served in person, and a student who will not keep a camera on is harder to teach remotely than a parent might assume. The AED figures are market figures published by Dubai providers during 2026 and are quoted as a range, not as our price list; IB Gram's own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a published hourly rate.

sections.heading: Ramadan, winter break and the rest of the UAE year
paragraphs: A tutoring schedule agreed in October will meet at least three predictable disruptions before the May papers, and planning for them in advance is the difference between a block that finishes and one that quietly stops. The winter break removes a fortnight at exactly the point where DP2 students most need consolidation before mocks. The spring break lands close to the final coursework and upload period. Ramadan reshapes the whole working day for several weeks, with school hours shortened and family routines moving later into the evening.

Ramadan is the one that most often derails an in-home arrangement and the one online delivery handles most easily. Sessions can move to a post-Iftar slot, run shorter and more frequently, or pause for a fortnight and resume with a revised plan. None of that requires anyone to drive anywhere at a time when the roads around Jumeirah and Al Wasl are at their least predictable. Families who tell us at the start of a block that Ramadan matters to their schedule get a plan that assumes it rather than a plan that is rescued in the middle.

The holidays themselves are a resource rather than an obstacle for a student who is behind. A fortnight with no school timetable is the only period in the DP2 year when a student can work on one subject for several consecutive days, and an intensive block across a break often achieves more than six weeks of single sessions competing with homework. The reverse is also true: a student who is on track should rest, and a tutor who insists on holiday sessions regardless of where the student stands is selling hours rather than teaching.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty boundary, written out plainly
paragraphs: Internally assessed work carries a published share of the Diploma grade, which is exactly why it attracts services that should be avoided. The research for this project found a competitor selling finished Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma entirely. No amount of convenience justifies that risk, and any provider offering it is telling you something important about how it treats the rest of its service.

The legitimate boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word limit, help a student plan a method, read the student's own draft and ask questions about it, point out where an argument is unsupported, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write, rewrite, draft or edit-to-completion any part of the submitted work, may not supply text for the student to adopt, and may not produce the data. Every piece of writing that reaches the school must be the student's own.

In practice that boundary makes feedback more useful rather than less. A returned draft covered in questions - what does this evidence actually show, which criterion does this paragraph serve, why this method and not the obvious alternative - teaches a student to see their own work the way a moderator will. A draft returned already fixed teaches nothing and leaves the student unable to defend it in a supervision meeting. Our tutors work the first way, and your child's school will recognise the difference immediately.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory Dubai subjects and the timetable they occupy
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. For a parent, KHDA matters in two concrete ways: it inspects schools and publishes the outcome on a six-band scale, and it sets requirements that sit on top of whichever international curriculum a school is licensed to teach. Neither of those things gives a tutoring provider any status with the authority, and a company that describes itself as carrying KHDA approval is describing something it almost certainly does not hold.

The requirement most Diploma families underestimate is the mandatory subject set. KHDA's published guidance requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with those requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The guidance also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, states that combined classes for both groups are prohibited, and sets instructional time against a 40-minute lesson unit. It further requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

The practical effect on a Jumeirah 3 Diploma student is timetable arithmetic. Those lessons occupy periods that would otherwise be free, which compresses the school day and pushes private study later. It also means Arabic is a live subject for a student who may have arrived in the UAE recently, and the KHDA guidance is explicit that different or additional content for the mandatory subjects needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education - so any tutoring in those subjects has to work within the school's own scheme rather than a parallel syllabus of its own.

sections.heading: If you are six weeks out, and if nobody is free
paragraphs: Families sometimes arrive at this page with six weeks until a mock or a paper, which prompts the honest version of the question: is it too late. It is not too late to change a grade boundary outcome in one or two components, and it is too late to rebuild two years of content. In six weeks a student can learn to read a structured question properly, show working that earns method marks, finish papers inside the time, and secure two or three topics that have never been solid. That is a realistic and often decisive list. Anything presented as more than that, from any provider, should be treated with real scepticism.

The second honest answer concerns availability. Specialist Higher Level cover in a narrow subject is not infinite, and there are weeks in the year - the fortnight before mocks, the run-up to the May session - when the right tutor for a particular subject and level has no slot left. When that happens we say so and offer the alternatives: a different evening with the same specialist, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, or a later start date with the work resequenced. What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level student and let the family find out in week three.

Starting is deliberately low-commitment for exactly this reason. Tell us the subject, the level, the year group and the evenings that work; we match a specialist and run a free trial lesson with that tutor; you decide afterwards whether to book a block. If the match is wrong, say so and we will change the tutor rather than ask you to persist with it. Six weeks is short enough that a bad match cannot be allowed to consume two of them.

process.title: Tell us the subject, level and year group
process.description: A short message naming the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the year group and which evenings work is enough to start. For a DP2 student, add the school's next internal deadline and the mock window, because those two dates shape the whole session plan.

process.title: We match a subject specialist
process.description: Matching is done on the syllabus your child is actually sitting, not on proximity to Jumeirah 3. For most Diploma subjects a specialist is available within a few working days; for a narrow Higher Level combination it can take longer, and we will tell you if it does.

process.title: A free trial lesson with that tutor
process.description: The first session is a free trial with the matched tutor, taught on a real topic rather than spent on introductions. You and your child hear how they explain something, and you decide afterwards whether to agree a schedule. Nothing is booked before that.

process.title: Agree a block with a stated target
process.description: Sessions are booked as a block with a target written down: a component, a timing problem, a coursework stage. A block with a target can be judged at the end of it. An open-ended weekly arrangement with no stated aim is the thing most likely to drift.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the clock
process.description: At the end of the block you get a summary of what changed, measured against the deadline it was aimed at. If the next milestone needs different work - coursework rather than papers, or timing rather than content - the plan changes accordingly rather than repeating itself.

whyPoints.title: The calendar drives the plan
whyPoints.description: Sessions are sequenced against your school's deadline list and the session your child is entered for, so coursework support happens while a draft can still change and timed practice happens when timing is the binding constraint. Tutoring that ignores those dates becomes a third workstream rather than help.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by subject, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Physics student is matched with someone who has taught that syllabus to examination, wherever they are based. Removing the travel radius widens the pool of genuine specialists considerably, which matters most in the subjects where the local pool is thinnest.

whyPoints.title: Evening slots that survive the term
whyPoints.description: Lessons run on Gulf Standard Time in the evening, which is when a Jumeirah 3 family is actually at home and settled. No part of the arrangement depends on a car reaching Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road at 4:30pm, so the schedule holds from October through to the spring.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you can check yourself
whyPoints.description: Marked past papers with a mark breakdown, an error log, and a session note naming the next target are all readable by a parent with no subject knowledge. You should never have to take progress on trust, and a block without records cannot be reviewed honestly at the end.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on coursework help
whyPoints.description: Our tutors teach criteria, method and referencing, and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write or complete any assessed component, and we say that plainly because this market contains providers that do. The limit protects your child's Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every rate band and school statistic on this page is attributed to a published source and dated. Where a figure could not be verified - the precise IB session dates, for one - we name the session and send you to your Diploma coordinator rather than publishing a number we cannot stand behind.

faqs.question: My child is in DP2 with mocks eight weeks away - is it too late to start tutoring in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: No, but the target has to be narrow. In eight weeks a DP2 student can realistically fix examination timing, learn to show working that earns method marks, rehearse command-term responses, and secure two or three topics that have never been solid. That is often enough to change the outcome of a mock and to make the spring term usable. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of content, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling hours. The first session is diagnostic: a paper sat cold, marked, and used to choose what the remaining weeks actually spend their time on.

faqs.question: Which IB session do Dubai schools enter, and would the November series ever apply to my child?
faqs.answer: Dubai Diploma cohorts normally sit the May session, which is why school calendars here build mocks into January and February. A November series does exist in the IB's schedule, but for a UAE student it is unusual as a first sitting and typically arises for a retake or for a student who has moved between hemispheres. The precise examination and results dates for either session should come from the IB or from your school's Diploma coordinator. Third-party sites publish versions of those dates that are sometimes a year out of step, which is why this page names the session rather than printing a window.

faqs.question: When should a DP1 student in Jumeirah 3 actually begin work on an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect, and the reason is structural rather than motivational. Internal Assessment titles are usually agreed in the spring of DP1 or the first weeks of DP2, and the work that follows needs a research question narrow enough to answer inside the word limit. A question that is too broad is the most common cause of a weak coursework mark, and it is diagnosable in a single session before any writing starts. Students who settle the question in DP1 spend DP2 revising; students who leave it find coursework and revision competing in the same weeks.

faqs.question: During Ramadan, does the weekly Diploma slot move later in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the places where online delivery is simply easier to manage. School hours shorten during Ramadan and family routines move later, so a schedule built for a 5pm start stops working almost immediately. Sessions can shift to a post-Iftar slot, run shorter and more often, or pause for a fortnight and resume on a revised plan. Tell us at the start of a block that Ramadan matters to your timetable and the plan will assume it rather than being patched halfway through. No part of the arrangement depends on anyone driving anywhere at a difficult hour.

faqs.question: How late can a weekday session realistically start for a family on this stretch of the coast?
faqs.answer: Most Jumeirah 3 families settle on 7:30pm or 8:00pm on Gulf Standard Time, and that choice is driven by the school run rather than by preference. Diploma students here often travel inland to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, so the return journey lands in the afternoon peak and an earlier appointment starts late more often than it starts on time. An evening slot begins when it is supposed to, finishes at a predictable hour, and leaves the homework window intact. For younger MYP students a 5pm or 6pm slot usually works better.

faqs.question: What happens to our schedule across the Dubai winter and spring breaks?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the student stands. For a DP2 student who is behind, a break is the only period in the year when several consecutive days can go to one subject, and an intensive block across it often achieves more than six weeks of single sessions competing with homework. For a student on track, rest is the better use of the fortnight and we will say so. The spring break matters more than the winter one, because it sits close to the final coursework and upload period, so plans around it are made with the school's internal deadlines in front of us.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist be matched once we have chosen a subject?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects, usually within a few working days of knowing the subject, the level, the year group and the evenings that work. Narrow Higher Level combinations take longer, and the fortnight before mocks and the weeks before the May session are the tightest periods in the year. If the right specialist has no slot, we tell you rather than filling the gap with a generalist, and we offer the alternatives: a different evening with the same tutor, a specialist based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, or a later start with the work resequenced.

faqs.question: Can we pause lessons during the examination weeks themselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most students that is the right call. Once the papers begin, the useful work is rest, light recall and paper-specific timing rather than new teaching, and some families keep a single short session a week purely to walk through the next paper's structure. Others stop entirely. Because sessions are booked as blocks with a stated target rather than as an open-ended subscription, pausing is a scheduling conversation rather than a contractual one. What we would discourage is introducing a new tutor or a new topic in the final fortnight, which adds load at the point where load is the problem.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson actually involve before we commit to anything?
faqs.answer: It is one lesson with the tutor we have matched to your child's subject and level, taught on a real topic rather than spent on introductions, so you can hear how they explain something and your child can judge whether the pace suits them. Nothing is booked beforehand and no schedule is agreed until after it. If the match is wrong, tell us and we will change the tutor rather than asking you to persist. The point of the trial is to move the risk of a bad match off your family and onto us, which is where it belongs.

faqs.question: Does searching for an IB home tutor in Jumeirah 3 mean somebody comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not with IB Gram. The phrase is how parents in this city have searched for twenty years, so we target it honestly, but our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses and home visits in Dubai are not a service we sell; that service exists only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. What you gain is a tutor chosen for the syllabus your child sits rather than for being within driving distance of Al Wasl Road, and an evening start time that holds through the term instead of competing with afternoon traffic.

faqs.question: How does a tutor work with my child's own school deadlines rather than against them?
faqs.answer: By starting from them. In the first session we ask for the school's deadline list - draft dates, internal cut-offs, the mock window - and sequence the work backwards from the nearest one. That way coursework feedback arrives while the draft can still change, and timed practice happens in the weeks when timing is the binding constraint. Tutoring that ignores the school calendar becomes a third workstream for a student already running two, which is the usual reason a weekly arrangement quietly collapses in February. Your child's teachers set those dates; we plan around them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without crossing the academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific enough to state. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is answerable, teach the subject content behind it, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help plan a method, read the student's own draft and respond with questions, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit any part of the essay to completion, supply text to be adopted, or produce data. Everything submitted must be the student's own work. A draft returned full of questions teaches a student to see it as a moderator will; a draft returned already fixed teaches nothing.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how would a parent verify one?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. The permit route is MoHRE's own service page, and a parent is entitled to ask any individual tutor directly whether they hold one.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Diploma families along the Jumeirah coast usually start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the normal starting point through the term, moving to two or three a week during an intensive block before mocks or papers. More than that is rarely useful for a student still attending school full time, because the limiting factor is the time available to do the work between sessions rather than the teaching itself. Where a family is considering two subjects at once, we would usually suggest starting with the one where the next deadline falls soonest, auditing the result after a month, and adding the second only if the schedule genuinely has room.

intro.heading: The question behind the search, answered plainly
paragraphs: Palm Jumeirah is a residential island with no IB secondary campus of its own. Every Diploma student living on the trunk, the fronds or the Crescent commutes off the island each morning, most often to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or Jumeirah. That single geographic fact shapes the tutoring problem. A family looking for help in Physics HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is not choosing from everyone who teaches that subject in Dubai. They are choosing from the much smaller group willing to cross the trunk, find parking on a frond, and be back out again before the evening traffic on Al Sufouh Road builds up.

The honest answer to "is there an IB home tutor in Palm Jumeirah who knows this syllabus" is that there are certainly tutors who will travel to the island, and that the subset of them who have taught your child's exact course at your child's exact level is small. The deeper you go into the Diploma, the smaller it gets. Plenty of tutors in Dubai teach secondary mathematics. Far fewer have marked a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 or supervised a Chemistry HL internal assessment through to submission. Proximity filters on the wrong variable.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring in a family's own house is a service we run in India only. For Palm Jumeirah the delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working through papers and a recording of the whiteboard where the tutor allows it. We state that first rather than at the bottom of a form, because it is the whole reason we can offer a Diploma specialist rather than a nearby generalist.

What that trade looks like in practice: a Crescent family whose daughter needs Economics HL support is matched on the strength of the tutor's Paper 3 and internal assessment experience, not on whether the tutor lives a twenty-minute drive away. The session starts at the time you choose and ends when it ends, with no travel charge attached to either side of it. Nobody is sitting in a car on the Palm trunk at 6pm, and the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching.

The rest of this page is written for the test you are actually trying to run. It sets out how to check a tutor's syllabus knowledge in a single conversation, what the Dubai market charges by provider model with sources and dates, who is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE and how you can verify it, what a non-specialist typically gets wrong in each Diploma subject group, and where the academic-honesty line sits on an internal assessment or extended essay. Where we cannot cover a subject with a UAE-based tutor, the page says so and says what happens instead.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Palm Jumeirah students sit in schools licensed by KHDA to run their own curricula, so the programme a child is in matters more than the emirate. These are the IB stages we teach to island families, with what each one demands of a student commuting off the Palm every day.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the extended essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria and moderated externally. Final grades run 1 to 7 per subject with up to three points available from the Theory of Knowledge and extended essay combination. The load is cumulative rather than modular, which is why a gap opened in the first term of Year 12 is still costing marks in the second term of Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: For a Palm Jumeirah student the binding constraint is the calendar, not the content. Internal assessment deadlines in several Dubai schools cluster in the same six-week window, and that window overlaps the extended essay's final submission. Students who commute off the island arrive home late, so the realistic tutoring slot sits between 5pm and 8pm on weekdays. We plan around that rather than pretending a 4pm start works.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0 to 8 and reported on a 1 to 7 scale. The criteria reward process: investigating, communicating, thinking critically, applying skills in unfamiliar situations. Students who have been rewarded for presentation and effort through the Middle Years can be surprised by the Diploma's narrower, more technical marking, which is the single most common reason a strong Year 11 report is followed by a shaky Year 12 one.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Palm Jumeirah families run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11 and then split into the Diploma or a Cambridge route. The bridging year is where island families usually first look for a tutor, often because the maths and sciences suddenly require fluency that criterion-based feedback did not test directly. Diagnostic work before Year 12 begins is cheaper in both money and stress than remedial work in the exam year.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led primary framework organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subject syllabuses, with no external examinations. Reporting is against learning outcomes and the approaches to learning skills. The useful tutoring work at this stage is narrow and mechanical: number bonds, written methods, reading fluency and the stamina to write at length, all of which are assumed rather than taught once a student reaches the Middle Years Programme.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families on the Palm often use a short block of weekly sessions to close one specific gap before a transfer, because the island's households move schools more often than the Dubai average when leases and job postings change. Online delivery suits this age group in 30 to 40 minute sessions rather than full hours, and we say so rather than selling the longer slot.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Palm Jumeirah families ask for most, with what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing. A tutor who cannot describe the paper structure of the subject they claim to teach is the first filter you should apply.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. Higher Level adds a third paper that mixes extended problem solving across topics, so students who have drilled topic-by-topic are exposed when a question needs proof technique and calculus in the same answer. Marks go missing on notation, unjustified steps and calculator work shown without method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. The common failure is treating it as the easier maths: Higher Level Applications includes substantial statistical inference and graph theory that punishes a student who chose the course to avoid proof. Interpretation marks need sentences about context, not just correct numbers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium are where Higher Level separates from Standard. The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation, and most of its lost marks sit in the analysis and evaluation criteria rather than in the practical work itself. Data processing with uncertainties is the most teachable high-value skill.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Students lose marks less on the physics than on the explanation: unit errors, unstated assumptions and answers that describe rather than derive. Higher Level content in fields and induction rewards consistent sign conventions. Paper work improves fastest when a student practises writing the argument, not just reaching the number.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of terminology makes this course feel like memorisation, but command terms decide the mark. A question asking a student to evaluate wants a judgement; one asking to outline does not want an essay. Higher Level demands more linking across topics, especially between physiology and biochemistry.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and definitional precision carry early marks; the extended responses need evaluation with real reference points. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a further paper. The internal assessment commentaries fail most often on weak linking between the chosen article and the specific syllabus concept being applied.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper one guided analysis are the two components students most often approach without a method. Marks come from close reading of how a text works, not from what it is about. Higher Level adds an essay on works studied, which needs an argument sustained across a long piece of writing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are easy to name and hard to apply. The marks sit in choosing the right framework for the stimulus and then using the case material, rather than reciting the framework. Higher Level extensions and the case study release reward students who practise under timed conditions with the published assessment criteria beside them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, worth points alongside the extended essay. Students treat it as a general discussion subject and then write an essay with no knowledge question driving it. Support here is structural: choosing a title you can argue, finding real examples, and keeping the claims testable.

subjects.name: Extended essay supervision support
subjects.description: A four-thousand word independent piece in a chosen subject, supervised at school and marked against published criteria. The common collapse is a research question too broad to answer in the word limit. Tutoring here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, never production of the text.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsTitle: Where the island's students go to school, and what that does to the evening
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsIntro: Palm Jumeirah sends its students off the island every morning. These are the neighbourhoods the school run actually reaches, and what each one implies for when a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The first mainland district past the trunk and the closest cluster of large campuses. A frond-to-Al Sufouh run is short in distance and unpredictable in time, so afternoon finishes land home anywhere between 3.30pm and 4.45pm depending on the bus route.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: A longer run inland to several of the biggest international schools serving island families. Students on bus routes here are commonly home after 4.30pm, which puts a sensible session start at 5.30pm or later on weekdays.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Coast-road access from the trunk, which works well off-peak and badly at 7.45am. The practical consequence for tutoring is that Saturday morning slots are often the calmest of the week for families on this route.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: A string of established school campuses along the coast with no single commute pattern. Families here mix car and bus, and siblings in different schools often arrive home forty minutes apart, which is why staggered one-to-one slots beat a shared session.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Inland of the coast road, reached from the Palm via Al Sufouh Road and Sheikh Zayed Road. A reliable route in the morning and a slow one once the schools empty, so evening sessions from 6pm are the norm rather than the exception.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Immediately south of the trunk and a frequent destination for siblings in different schools and for tutoring centres. Close enough that families consider centre-based group classes, which is worth weighing honestly against one-to-one for a diagnosed subject gap.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: Newer coastal developments with growing school and nursery provision nearby. Useful to island families mainly as an alternative route into the Jumeirah campuses when the coast road is congested.

regions.name: Al Manara and Al Quoz
regions.note: Less commonly a school destination and more often where a tuition centre or activity sits. The drive back onto the Palm at the end of a weekday evening is the part families underestimate when they price in-home tutoring.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor search on Palm Jumeirah is really asking
paragraphs: A parent typing "IB home tutor in Palm Jumeirah" into Google is usually three weeks into a problem. A report has come home, or a mock has been marked, or a teacher has used the phrase "not on track". The search is for proximity because proximity feels like the solvable part. What the parent actually needs is somebody who has taught the exact course, at the exact level, and can tell within one session whether the issue is content, technique or confidence.

Those two things pull in opposite directions on an island. Palm Jumeirah has roughly eighty thousand residents on a single connected landmass with one road on and off the trunk. A tutor who comes to the house is accepting a round trip that can swallow an hour of their evening, which means they will do it for a limited number of families, at a limited number of times, and will price the travel in. Every constraint they accept narrows the pool further. The subject-specialist filter is the first one to be dropped, because it is the one the parent cannot easily check.

So the page you are reading answers the question in its honest form. There are tutors who will travel to the Palm. The specialist you want for Physics HL in an exam year may well not be among them. IB Gram's answer is to drop the geography constraint entirely: the tutor is matched on subject, level and assessment experience, and teaches your child one-to-one over live video at a time that fits the commute off the island. That is a real trade, not a workaround, and the next section is about how to test whether it is paying off.

sections.heading: How to tell in twenty minutes whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: You do not need to know the subject to test whether somebody teaches it. You need four questions whose answers are specific, checkable and impossible to bluff. Ask them in the trial lesson, in front of your child, and listen for whether the answer names things or describes feelings about things.

First: what are the assessment components in this course at this level, and what is each one worth? A specialist answers in a sentence with numbers in it. Second: what is the internal assessment in this subject and which criterion carries the most marks? A specialist names the criteria by letter and says where students lose them. Third: what are the command terms in the last paper you worked through, and what does each one require? A generalist talks about exam technique in general; a specialist tells you that "evaluate" needs a judgement and "outline" does not need a paragraph. Fourth: show the tutor one marked piece of your child's work and ask what the next ten marks are. A specialist points at a page.

The reason this matters more on Palm Jumeirah than in a city centre is supply. When a family is choosing among whoever is willing to drive onto a frond at 5.30pm, the temptation is to accept a confident generalist because the alternative is nobody. Asking these four questions costs nothing and removes the guesswork. It is also exactly what the free trial lesson exists for, and why we would rather you spent it interrogating the tutor than watching a sales presentation.

The table below sets out what a Palm Jumeirah family can realistically expect by subject and level, how quickly a match usually happens, and what we do when no UAE-based specialist has a free slot at the time you need. Two patterns repeat. Higher Level sciences and Higher Level mathematics in the exam term are the hardest slots to fill, because the same small group of specialists is in demand across Dubai at the same six-week point in the year. Group 2 languages at Higher Level and the less commonly taken group 3 subjects are harder again, because the pool is small in absolute terms rather than merely busy.

Where no UAE-based tutor covers a subject, we say so and offer a specialist based elsewhere who teaches the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time. That is a disclosure, not a bait and switch: the tutor is named, the location is stated, and the time zone the lessons are held in is yours. If neither option works, we tell you to look elsewhere. A family that books in the dark and discovers the gap in week three has lost three weeks it did not have. The one thing that reliably widens your options is offering two possible evening slots rather than one, because the overlap between your week and a specialist's is what the match actually turns on, far more than the subject itself.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and who published each figure
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this kind of search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars. That is unhelpful to a family budgeting in dirhams. The figures below were read from the providers' own public pages in October 2026 and are attributed to whoever published them. They describe the market, not an IB Gram price list: our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and we quote per student after the diagnostic rather than from a rate card.

The range is wide for a reason. At the bottend sit platforms using university students for school-level work, which can be the right answer for a Year 8 numeracy gap and the wrong one for Physics HL eight weeks from a mock. At the top sit named premium tutors charging several times that. In between is the band most Diploma families actually transact in, and the single largest variable inside it is whether anybody is being paid to travel.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE, and how would you know?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the ministry's own service page for it is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Individuals who offer private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anybody.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents expect. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category is why a confident sixteen-year-old offering IGCSE maths help on a community noticeboard may be entirely within the rules, and also why the permit alone tells you nothing about teaching quality.

A separate thing entirely is an operation with premises and staff. A tuition centre in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which runs through initial approval, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not operate premises in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge. Any service telling you otherwise is making a claim you should ask it to evidence with a permit number.
