sections.heading: What a non-specialist gets wrong, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: The case for specialism is usually made with adjectives. Here it is made with failure modes. In group 4 sciences, a competent generalist teaches the content correctly and then lets a student write up an investigation that scores poorly, because the marks in that component sit in analysis and evaluation rather than in the practical itself. Uncertainties, anomalies and the limitations paragraph are learned behaviours, and a tutor who has not marked against those criteria does not know to drill them.

In group 5 mathematics, the gap shows up in the exploration and in the Higher Level third paper. A generalist can teach differentiation. Fewer can look at a student's chosen exploration topic in week two and say, accurately, that it will not generate enough mathematics to reach the top band of one criterion and that changing it now costs an afternoon rather than a grade. In group 3, economics and business responses lose marks on evaluation and on the use of the stimulus material, not on the diagrams, which is the opposite of where most tutoring time goes.

In group 1 and group 2, the individual oral and the guided analysis are the components students most often meet unprepared, because they are the least like anything in the Middle Years Programme. A specialist knows the structure of the assessment and can rehearse it. A generalist improves the student's general English, which is worth having and will not move that mark. None of this is an argument that generalists are bad teachers. It is an argument that the filter you apply first should be the subject and the level, and geography should come a distant second.
bullets: Group 4: marks lost in analysis and evaluation, not in the practical work
Group 5: exploration scope decided in week two, paid for in the final grade
Group 3: evaluation and stimulus use, not diagram accuracy
Group 1 and 2: oral components rehearsed, or met cold

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line, stated so your child is not the test case
paragraphs: This matters more on a Diploma page than anywhere else, because the internet is full of services offering to supply assessed work. There are operators in this market selling finished internal assessments for four-figure sums. A student who submits one is exposed to a malpractice finding, and a malpractice finding in the Diploma is not a telling-off.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the content, explain the published criteria, discuss method, question a research question, point at a paragraph and say it does not do what the criterion asks, mark a draft against the descriptors and set up practice under timed conditions. The student generates every word, every data set and every line of code that is submitted. If a tutor offers to supply text, restructure a draft into final form, or hand over a worked example that is indistinguishable from the submission, that is the moment to end the engagement, not negotiate it.

We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the boards' copyright material. We reference them, cite the official source, and link to it, and we work from the papers the school has legitimately given the student. On Palm Jumeirah specifically, where several families use the same small set of schools, there is a second reason for care: a tutor working with two students in the same class at the same school has an obligation not to move work between them, and we ask about that at the matching stage.

sections.heading: Starting from Palm Jumeirah, with the limits stated up front
paragraphs: The first step is a short conversation about the subject, the level, the school and what the last marked assessment said. That is enough to know whether the problem is a content gap, an exam-technique gap or a workload-management gap, and those three need different tutors. We ask for the school's name because the scheme of work and the internal deadlines differ, and a session that ignores them is a session spent on the wrong topic.

The second step is a free trial lesson with the proposed specialist. Use it to run the four questions above. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist; a mismatched match is a sunk cost, not a commitment. If the match is right, you choose a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, which for most island families means something between 5pm and 8pm on a weekday, or a Saturday morning when the week has been heavy.

The honest caveats. In the weeks before the May session, Higher Level science and mathematics slots are the scarcest thing we have, and a family that waits until April is choosing from what is left rather than from everyone. During Ramadan, we move sessions later and shorten them where families prefer, and many island households switch to post-Iftar timing for the month. And if no UAE-based specialist covers the subject at the time you need, you will be told before you pay, with a named alternative and their location, or told to look elsewhere.

process.title: Tell us the subject, level and school

process.title: Run the free trial lesson as a test
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, at no cost. Ask the component weightings, the internal assessment criteria, the command terms and the next ten marks on a piece of marked work. Your child should leave the session knowing one thing they did not know. If not, the match is wrong and we change it.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot around the school run
process.description: Most Palm Jumeirah families settle on a weekday slot between 5pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time, or a weekend morning. The slot is fixed so it survives a busy term, and sessions follow the school's own sequence of assessments rather than a generic syllabus order.

process.title: Review at six sessions against the original gap list
process.description: The diagnostic produced a written list of gaps in a teaching order. At six sessions we check it off: what has closed, what has not, and whether the hours should go up, down or stop. Families who use this checkpoint tend to buy fewer total hours, which is the point of having it.

whyPoints.title: The specialist filter is applied before the map
whyPoints.description: Matching starts with the subject and the level, then the assessment experience, then availability at your times. Geography never enters the decision, which is why a Palm Jumeirah family is not choosing from the small group of tutors willing to drive onto a frond at 5.30pm.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are published, not discovered
whyPoints.description: The coverage table on this page names the subjects and levels that are tight, how long a match usually takes and what happens when no UAE-based specialist is free. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all. We would rather lose the booking than conceal it.

whyPoints.title: A mismatch costs you a conversation, not a term
whyPoints.description: If the tutor is not right, the tutor changes. There is no argument about whether to give it four more weeks, because a Diploma student eight weeks from a mock does not have four weeks. The free trial exists so that this decision is made before money moves rather than after.

faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor in Palm Jumeirah who really knows the Diploma syllabus?
faqs.answer: There are tutors who will travel onto the island, and the subset who have taught your child's exact course at your child's exact level is small. The deeper into the Diploma you go, the smaller it becomes. Plenty of people in Dubai teach secondary maths; far fewer have supervised a Higher Level exploration or marked a Paper 3. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes at all. We match on subject, level and assessment experience and teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is how a Palm Jumeirah family reaches a specialist rather than a neighbour.

faqs.question: How can I test whether a tutor actually knows my child's IB subject?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions in the trial lesson. What are the assessment components at this level and what is each worth? What is the internal assessment in this subject and which criterion carries the most marks? What do three command terms from the last paper actually require? And, holding one marked piece of your child's work, where are the next ten marks? A specialist answers with numbers, criterion letters and a finger on the page. A generalist talks about confidence and exam technique in general terms. The difference is audible within twenty minutes and costs you nothing to find out.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level specialist harder to find than a general maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the pool shrinks at every filter. Secondary maths teachers in Dubai are numerous. Those who have taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are fewer. Those who have taken a cohort through the exploration and the third paper are fewer still, and in the term before the May session they are all busy at the same hours. Add a requirement to drive onto a Palm Jumeirah frond at 5.30pm and the list can reach zero. Removing the travel requirement is what puts the specialist back on the list.

faqs.question: Is a permit required before anybody can charge us for private lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified. Eligible applicants include school and government employees, private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see the permit before the first paid session.

faqs.question: What if nobody in the UAE teaches the exact course my child sits?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay. The coverage table on this page names where availability is tight: Higher Level sciences and Higher Level mathematics in the exam term, and the less commonly taken group 2 and group 3 courses year-round. Where no UAE-based specialist has a free slot at your times, we name a specialist based elsewhere who teaches the same syllabus and holds sessions in Gulf Standard Time, and we state where they are. If neither works, we say we cannot cover it. A family that finds this out in week three has lost three weeks.

faqs.question: Can a teacher from my child's own school tutor them in the evening?
faqs.answer: Be careful here. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on it. The practical point for a Dubai family is that "your child's own teacher, privately" is not a service we market or arrange, and a tutor who offers it is worth questioning rather than hiring.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Palm Jumeirah student start sessions?
faqs.answer: Two to four days for most Middle Years subjects and Standard Level Diploma courses, three to seven days for Higher Level sciences and Higher Level mathematics, and a week or more for less commonly taken courses. The free trial lesson sits inside that window rather than after it. The constraint is rarely the matching and almost always the overlap between your available evening slots and a specialist's, which is why families who can offer two possible times start sooner than families fixed on one.

faqs.question: What does the Dubai market charge for an IB specialist per hour?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik for budget online platforms, from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB at Unitors, AED 270 at TutorChase, AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists in the Bestimate Dubai guide, and AED 650 at BartyED at the premium end. In-home visits sit around AED 180 to 350 in that guide and up to AED 500 in listings, because the hour includes a journey. None of these are IB Gram prices; ours follow a free trial and a diagnostic.

faqs.question: Will a tutor drive onto the fronds for an early evening session?
faqs.answer: Some independent tutors in Dubai will, and they price the round trip into the hour or set a two-hour minimum. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service for us, and we would rather state it than let you assume otherwise. For Palm Jumeirah, lessons run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, scheduled at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. Nobody is in a car on the trunk at 6pm, and the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching rather than forty minutes of it.

faqs.question: Which instruction words in an IB question decide the mark?
faqs.answer: Command terms are the instruction verbs in an exam question: outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify. Each one defines how much is wanted and what kind of answer earns the marks. A student who writes a careful paragraph for a question asking them to state has spent time for nothing; one who gives a single sentence where a judgement was wanted has left marks behind. Most students lose more to this than to missing content, and it is among the fastest things to fix, which is why a specialist tests for it in the first session.

faqs.question: Is a general tutor ever the better choice for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, yes. If the gap is foundational arithmetic, written fluency or study organisation, a strong generalist can close it and will usually cost less. If the gap is in an assessed component, a Higher Level topic or exam technique for a specific paper, a generalist improves the subject in general and leaves the mark where it was. The question to ask is whether the problem is below the course or inside it. A diagnostic block of two or three sessions answers that before you commit to a term of anything.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a struggling Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one session a week on one subject, which is enough when the gap is diagnosed and the student does the work between sessions. Two subjects at once usually means two separate slots rather than a longer single one, because attention does not stretch. Short blocks of two or three sessions a week make sense around one assessed component or a mock, then drop back. More hours do not substitute for independent practice, and a tutor who recommends four sessions a week in the first conversation has not diagnosed anything yet.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an internal assessment, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, explain the published criteria letter by letter, question the research question, discuss method, mark a draft against the descriptors and say plainly that a paragraph does not meet the criterion it is aimed at. Off limits is supplying text, restructuring a draft into its final form, providing data, or handing over a worked example close enough to be submitted. The student generates everything that is handed in. Services selling finished coursework exist in this market and a student who uses one risks a malpractice finding, which is a far worse outcome than a low mark.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to teach at a Dubai school to be useful?
faqs.answer: No, and it is a weaker signal than it sounds. What matters is whether the tutor knows the course your child sits and the way it is assessed: the components, the weightings, the criteria and the papers. A teacher at a Dubai school may know your child's school's internal deadlines, which helps, but a specialist who asks for the scheme of work and the assessment calendar gets the same information in one conversation. Ask about subject and level experience first, and about local school knowledge second.

faqs.question: How do I check a claim that a tutor is an examiner?
faqs.answer: Ask which board, which subject, which component and which years, then ask for something that evidences it. Examiner status is not a general badge; it is specific and time-limited. It also does not give anybody access to unreleased papers, mark schemes or grade boundaries, and a tutor who implies otherwise is telling you something that should worry you rather than reassure you. IB Gram does not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners unless the current status can be evidenced, and the useful question is always what the tutor has taught and marked.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-greens.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma subjects at Standard and Higher Level to students in Dubai. Each is matched to one subject at one level, because a Chemistry HL paper and an Economics HL paper fail for completely different reasons. intro.heading: Who in New Dubai actually teaches the Diploma, and how a parent finds out
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor in The Greens is almost never a search about geography. It is a search about competence. The parent typing it has a Diploma student in DP1 or DP2, a mock result that was lower than expected, and a reasonable suspicion that the person who helped with Year 9 maths cannot help with Paper 3. The word 'home' is in the query because that is how tutoring has always been described in this part of the world, not because the family cares where the lesson physically happens.

So answer the real question first. Within a fifteen-minute drive of The Greens there are perhaps a dozen schools, four or five of them running the full IB continuum. The pool of adults nearby who have taught a specific Diploma subject at Higher Level, marked it, and seen what a 5 looks like against a 7 is much smaller than the pool of adults who tutor school maths and science in general. Those two pools get confused constantly, and the confusion costs families a term.

The Greens is a mid-rise apartment community in Emirates Living, bounded by Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Thanya Street, sitting between The Views, Barsha Heights and Emirates Hills. Children here are spread across British, American and IB schools in Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Emirates Hills and The Meadows. One building can hold a Year 11 at Dubai British School Emirates Hills, a DP2 at Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and a Grade 10 at the American School of Dubai. No single local tutor covers that spread well.

IB Gram resolves it by removing distance from the equation entirely. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own past-paper script on screen. That means the Chemistry HL specialist your child gets is chosen because she has taught the 2025 syllabus and knows where candidates lose marks on the data-based question, not because she happens to live near Emirates Golf Club. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; we say so on every UAE page rather than letting a parent find out after booking.

What follows is the detail a parent needs to make that judgement without taking anyone's word for it: how thin the local specialist pool really is subject by subject, six questions that expose a tutor who has not read the current guide, what the Dubai market charges for each format with the source of every figure, and the exact boundary a tutor may not cross on an Internal Assessment. Read the screening questions even if you hire someone else. The Greens sits close enough to several curriculum clusters that two children in one apartment can sit different boards, so the page also covers how a parent checks which board their own school enters before paying for anything.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: IB Gram supports the three IB programmes a child in The Greens is likely to be sitting, plus the IGCSE year that usually precedes the Diploma for British-curriculum pupils in Emirates Living. Each programme is assessed in a different way, so the tutoring looks different too.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1 to 7 per subject with up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Most of the final grade sits in externally marked papers, with an Internal Assessment worth 20 to 25 per cent depending on the subject. The structure punishes a student who is strong in class but has never written under timed conditions against the command terms.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is a minority curriculum in Dubai by enrolment and a crowded one around The Greens. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS Wellington International School and GEMS Dubai American Academy all run DP within a short drive, which is why DP1 and DP2 requests from this postcode outnumber every other level we see in Emirates Living.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0 to 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There are no external papers until the optional eAssessment in MYP 5. The criterion wording is where marks move: a student who can do the mathematics but cannot communicate a justification loses Criterion C regardless of the answer. Tutoring at this level is mostly about teaching a child to read the criterion before starting the task.
programmes.countryNote: Greens families typically meet MYP in Years 7 to 11 at Emirates International School Meadows or Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, then face the MYP-to-DP step at 16. The jump into Maths AA HL from MYP Extended Mathematics is the single most common reason a DP1 parent in Emirates Living contacts us in October.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no formal grades and no external examinations. Reporting is against learner-profile attributes and transdisciplinary themes, which parents new to the IB often find hard to translate into 'is my child behind in maths'. Support at this stage is diagnostic: number fluency, reading age, writing stamina and the specific gaps a report card describes in prose rather than numbers.
programmes.countryNote: Several Emirates Living primary cohorts sit inside IB continuum schools while their neighbours attend Regent International School in The Greens itself on a British curriculum. Parents comparing the two across a stairwell is a weekly conversation here, and it usually ends with a question about what Year 6 readiness looks like in each.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by terminal papers, graded A*-G by Cambridge and 9-1 by Pearson Edexcel. Tiering matters: Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation carry a grade ceiling, so a child entered at the wrong tier cannot reach the grade a Diploma place needs. The syllabus code on the front of the past paper, not the subject name, is what a tutor has to teach to.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum pupils around The Greens sit IGCSE at Regent International School, Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Kings' School Al Barsha and Dubai College, then split at 16 between A Level and the Diploma. A family planning the Diploma route needs the IGCSE subject choices to support it two years early.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Greens families ask for most, with what each one actually assesses. A tutor should be able to name the papers and their weightings before the first session. Where a subject is listed at both levels, the Higher Level course is a different syllabus, not the same syllabus with extra homework.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Five topics, with calculus and proof carrying the HL weight. SL sits Paper 1 and Paper 2 at 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20 per cent; HL adds Paper 3 at 20 per cent. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, which is where fluent-but-calculator-dependent students collapse. Marks go on unjustified steps and on Paper 3's extended problem-solving.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work, with the graphic display calculator allowed in every paper. Easier to pass and harder to score 7 in than parents expect, because the marks sit in interpretation sentences rather than algebra. HL adds financial mathematics, matrices and graph theory, plus the same Paper 3 structure as AA HL.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across two themes, assessed by Paper 1 multiple choice and short response, Paper 2 extended response, and the scientific investigation. Organic mechanisms and the data-based questions are where HL candidates lose most. A tutor who teaches it as A Level chemistry misses the IB's emphasis on uncertainty and on explaining trends rather than reciting them.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and nuclear content, with HL extending into rigid-body and quantum material. Most lost marks are not conceptual: they are missing units, unstated assumptions and graph work that does not use the full range. Dubai students arriving from an American-curriculum Grade 10 often need an algebra-in-physics bridge before the content makes sense.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity across four organising themes, examined by Paper 1 and Paper 2 plus the scientific investigation. The command terms do the damage here: 'outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' want different lengths and different structures, and a student who writes everything they know scores badly on all three.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and the policy toolkit, with HL adding quantitative questions and Paper 3. The internal assessment is three commentaries on recent news articles against a key concept, and it is routinely the easiest marks on the course to lose by picking a weak article in week one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral on a global issue, and an HL essay. The individual oral is where confident speakers under-score, because it is marked on the link between the extract, the work and the global issue rather than on fluency.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with HL adding depth and a longer Paper 2. The internal assessment is a research project on a real organisation, and students with family businesses in Dubai often pick a company they cannot get usable data from, which caps the mark before any analysis happens.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Dubai students sit Arabic across three different routes, and the route matters more than the hours. Arabic A is a literature or language-and-literature course for first-language speakers; Arabic B is language acquisition; ab initio is for beginners. Being entered on the wrong route is the most common Arabic problem we see in Emirates Living.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: TOK is assessed by an exhibition of three objects and a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece. Together they carry up to three bonus points. Support here is process coaching on question framing, scope and argument structure. A tutor reviews and questions the student's own drafting and nothing beyond that.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with HL extending into the options and an experimental study report. Marks hinge on using named studies precisely and on evaluating method rather than summarising findings, which is a writing skill before it is a content one.

subjects.name: Global Politics and Philosophy
subjects.description: Two of the hardest subjects to staff locally and two of the most essay-dependent. Both reward a student who can hold a counter-argument and lose marks fast for description. sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in The Greens is really asking
paragraphs: Answer first: the search means 'find me someone near The Greens who knows my child's Diploma syllabus'. The second half of that sentence is the hard part. There is no shortage of tutors willing to drive to Emirates Living; there is a real shortage of people who have taught a named Diploma subject at Higher Level and can tell you, unprompted, what each paper is worth.

The confusion is structural. Tutoring in Dubai is sold by location because location is what a classified listing can advertise. A listing says 'maths tutor, Emirates Living, available evenings'. It does not say whether the person has taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, whether they have seen a Paper 3 before, or whether they know that Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. A parent cannot tell those tutors apart from the listing, so they pick on price and proximity, and then discover the gap in week three.

Removing distance from the decision is what makes the real criterion visible. Once the lesson happens over live video, the only remaining questions are about the tutor's subject knowledge, their track record with the specific assessment, and whether the time slot works. Those are answerable questions. 'Is there anyone good within twenty minutes of Al Thanya Street' is not, because the answer changes every time a family relocates.

This page is therefore written as a buying guide rather than a brochure. It tells you where the local specialist supply is thin, gives you the questions that expose a bluffer, publishes the market rates with their sources, and sets out the line a tutor must not cross on coursework. Use it even if you end up hiring someone from a WhatsApp group in your own building.

sections.heading: How thin the local specialist pool actually runs, subject by subject
paragraphs: Dubai has a deep teaching market in absolute terms. Dubai's Media Office reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, American at 14 and the IB at 7. That last figure is the one that matters here: the Diploma is a small slice of a very large market, so the number of experienced DP subject teachers in any one neighbourhood is correspondingly small.

Split that small slice by subject and level and it gets smaller again. A school running the Diploma needs one or two Chemistry teachers, not ten. Of those, the ones free to tutor privately are fewer still, because a teacher registered at a school needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit and, under the code of conduct attached to it, should not be tutoring students enrolled at their own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff make the same point explicitly. The practical effect in Emirates Living is that the DP Chemistry teacher two streets away is often precisely the person who cannot take your child.

That leaves three honest options for a Greens family: an experienced local tutor who teaches the subject but not the Diploma specification, a Diploma specialist who happens to be nearby and available, or a Diploma specialist anywhere in the world teaching over video at a Gulf Standard Time slot. The table sets out where each subject sits. Where the nearby pool is thin, we say so rather than pretending otherwise, and we say what we do about it.

The fallback matters more than the headline. If no UAE-based specialist is free for a Higher Level subject, we match the student to a Diploma specialist outside the UAE and run the session at a Gulf Standard Time slot the family chooses. The tutor's location is disclosed before the trial lesson, not after. No competitor page in our research disclosed a coverage limit at all, and several routed UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying where delivery actually happened.

sections.heading: Six questions that tell you in ten minutes whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Credentials are easy to assert and hard to verify from a WhatsApp message. Syllabus knowledge is the opposite: it is almost impossible to fake for ten minutes, because the Diploma's assessment structure is specific and a person who has taught it answers these questions instantly. Ask them on the phone before you book anything, including before you book a free trial with us.

The pattern to listen for is precision. A tutor who has taught the subject names papers, weightings, durations and command terms without being prompted. A tutor who has not talks about confidence, foundations and personalised plans. Neither answer is dishonest, but only one of them tells you the person has sat in front of this specification. The table gives you the question, what a real answer sounds like, what a vague one sounds like, and why the gap matters for your child's grade.

Two further checks are worth making and take a minute each. Ask which year's syllabus the student is on, because the sciences and Mathematics have both been revised in recent cycles and a tutor working from an older guide will teach content that is no longer assessed the same way. And ask the tutor to tell you about a student they could not help. Anyone who has taught for five years has one, and the answer tells you how honestly they diagnose.

Finally, ask about the permit, politely and directly. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: individuals giving private lessons need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the official route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service. A tutor who does not know what you are asking about is telling you something.
bullets: Ask which papers the subject has and what each is worth, before anything else

sections.heading: What an in-home tutor in The Greens costs, and what the drive costs you
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages in our October 2026 research publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. So here are the Dubai market bands in AED, with the source of every figure named and dated. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list: our own commercial answer is a free trial lesson and a quoted plan after it, because the right number depends on subject, level and how many weeks are left.

Read the in-home row carefully, because it hides the real cost. A published AED 180 to 500 per hour for a visit includes travel in the sense that the tutor is not billing it separately. It does not include the constraint travel imposes: a tutor crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at 5pm will take an hour over a twenty-minute journey, which means they can teach three students an evening rather than five, which is why the rate is higher. It also means they will only accept a slot that fits their route, so the family loses control of the timetable.

The second hidden cost is tutor-pool size. Accepting in-home delivery narrows the candidate list to people who will drive to Emirates Living on a Tuesday. For IGCSE maths that is a large enough pool. For Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level it is sometimes a pool of one, and the one is whoever is free rather than whoever is right. Paying AED 350 an hour for a generalist in the room is worse value than paying less for a specialist on screen, and that is the trade the table is really describing.

Monthly packages circulate in this market too. Published examples at the time of writing include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Check what a package includes before comparing it to an hourly rate; the number of contact hours is often the difference.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks are actually lost, and why a generalist misses them
paragraphs: The gap between a 5 and a 7 is rarely a content gap by DP2. The student has met the material; the marks are going somewhere specific and identifiable. A tutor who knows the specification finds that place in one marked script. A tutor who does not teaches the content again, which the student already half-knows, and the mock result moves by a point at most.

In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, the usual leak is procedural rather than conceptual. Students lose marks for unjustified steps, for answers given to the wrong accuracy, and for abandoning a Paper 3 problem after the first unfamiliar sentence. Paper 1 without a calculator exposes anyone who has learned to check every line on a graphic display calculator, and no amount of extra content teaching fixes it. The fix is timed non-calculator practice and a method of showing working that earns the method marks even when the final answer is wrong.

In the sciences, two patterns dominate. The first is the command term: 'explain' wants a mechanism, 'outline' wants brevity, 'evaluate' wants both sides and a judgement, and a student who writes a full paragraph for all three loses marks on two of them. The second is the data-based and practical material, where uncertainties, significant figures and graph ranges carry marks that have nothing to do with chemistry or physics knowledge. In the essay subjects the equivalent failure is description: a Global Politics answer that explains what happened, without an argument, caps itself.

This is why the diagnosis in the first session matters more than the tutor's charm. Bring the most recent marked paper to the trial lesson, including the examiner's or teacher's annotations. A specialist will read it and name the pattern. If the first session is spent on introductions and a generic assessment, you have learned something useful about the tutor, for free.
bullets: Bring the last marked script, not a list of topics the student finds hard
Ask the tutor to name the single recurring error before planning anything
Expect timed practice from week two, not from the final term
Keep an error log the student can revise from without the tutor present

sections.heading: The line a tutor may not cross on an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay
paragraphs: Some providers in this market sell completed coursework. One in our research set advertises finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma. Any Greens parent shopping for Diploma help will encounter these offers, so the boundary is worth stating plainly.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They can teach the skills the task assesses, explain the criteria in plain language, help a student narrow a research question from something unanswerable to something manageable, question an argument until its weaknesses surface, point at a paragraph and say it does not do what the criterion asks, and read a draft and give feedback. They can model an example on a different topic entirely. All of that is teaching.

What a tutor must refuse is equally clear. No supplying text for the student to submit. No rewriting a paragraph into final form. No choosing the research question outright. No sourcing or fabricating data the student has not collected. No editing a draft to the point where the voice and reasoning are no longer the student's. IB Gram tutors are briefed on this boundary and asked to decline the request rather than negotiate it, which occasionally annoys a parent in week one and protects the candidate in May.

There is a practical consequence for scheduling. Because the tutor cannot produce the work, coursework support has to start early enough for the student to do it themselves. A family coming to us six weeks before an internal deadline has a narrower set of honest options than one coming in September, and we will say so rather than take the booking and under-deliver.
bullets: Teaching the criteria, questioning the argument, reading drafts: all fine
Supplying text, rewriting to final form, choosing the question: never
Data must be the student's own, collected or sourced by them

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA inspection report before you blame the tutor
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a rating on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The report is public, it is long, and almost no parent reads past the headline band. The sections that matter for a tutoring decision are buried in the middle.

Look for the subject-level judgements rather than the overall band. A school rated Very Good overall can be Acceptable in Diploma mathematics, and that single line explains more about your child's situation than the headline does. Look also at the attainment-against-progress split: a cohort with high attainment and weaker progress is a cohort that arrived strong and was not stretched, which is a different tutoring problem from one with weak attainment and good progress.

Two pieces of Dubai context are worth holding alongside the report. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second economic incentives package. And Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent. A market adding IB capacity that fast is a market where experienced Diploma teachers are being recruited away from tutoring, which is part of why the specialist pool stays thin.

None of this makes tutoring compulsory, and it is worth saying so. Plenty of Diploma students in Emirates Living get through without any outside help. The report is a diagnostic tool for a parent deciding whether the problem sits with the child, the subject, the teaching or the fit, and that question deserves an answer before anyone spends AED 300 an hour on it.

sections.heading: Scheduling from The Greens: the school run, Ramadan and the honest version of availability
paragraphs: Session timing in this community is decided by two things: when the bus gets back, and when the parent gets home. Secondary school days around Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and Al Sufouh end between 2.45pm and 3.30pm, and a bus route through Barsha Heights or across Al Thanya Street adds thirty to fifty minutes. A child from The Greens is realistically at a desk by 4.15pm at the earliest, and anyone promising a 3.30pm start has not driven the route. The slots that actually hold are 5pm, 6.30pm and 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time.

Ramadan shifts everything. School hours shorten, afternoons are low-energy and the usable study window moves to after Iftar. Families who keep their regular 5pm slot through Ramadan generally lose the sessions; families who move to a post-Iftar slot keep them. We ask about it a few weeks ahead rather than letting four weeks of cancellations happen, and we hold the original slot so the family can move back afterwards.

Then there is the question nobody else in this market answers: what happens when no specialist is free. For common subjects at Standard Level, a UAE-based match in a chosen slot is usually straightforward. For Higher Level Chemistry, Global Politics, Philosophy or a specific Arabic route, there may be no UAE-based specialist available at the hour the family wants. In that case we match a Diploma specialist outside the UAE, run the session at Gulf Standard Time, and say where the tutor is based before the trial lesson. If we cannot cover the subject at all, we say that too rather than substituting a generalist.

The final scheduling truth is about stopping. A good plan has an end: a mock, a session, a specific grade threshold, or a point where the student is running their own revision. Open-ended weekly tutoring that continues because nobody reviewed it is the most common way money gets wasted in this market. Ask for a review date at the start, and hold us to it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IB home tutor to an apartment in The Greens?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India. Diploma tuition for a family in The Greens is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own marked script on screen. We target the phrase because it is what parents search, and then answer it honestly rather than taking a booking we cannot fulfil. If you specifically want a person in the room, hire locally and use the six screening questions on this page before you pay anyone.

faqs.question: Why is a Chemistry HL specialist harder to find near Emirates Living than a GCSE maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Numbers. Dubai's Media Office reported 387,441 private school students in 2024-25, with the IB at around seven per cent of enrolment, so Diploma teaching is a small slice of a large market. A school running the Diploma employs one or two Chemistry teachers, not ten. Of those, the ones registered at a school need the MoHRE private tuition work permit and, under its code of conduct, should not tutor their own enrolled students. GCSE and IGCSE maths, by contrast, is taught in every school in the emirate. The supply difference is structural, not a reflection of Dubai's teaching quality.

faqs.question: How can I check that a tutor has actually taught the current Diploma syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask them to weight the papers in your child's subject at the level they sit, without looking it up. Someone who has taught it will say Paper 1 thirty per cent, Paper 2 thirty, Paper 3 twenty and internal assessment twenty for a Higher Level science, and will tell you unprompted that Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Then ask which syllabus year the student is on and what changed in it. The sciences and Mathematics have both been revised recently, and a tutor working from an older guide will teach content that is no longer assessed the same way.

faqs.question: My child is at Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. Do you support students from that school?
faqs.answer: We support students who attend it, and that is the limit of the relationship. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement from Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills or from any other school named on this page; the schools are listed so you can see which curriculum and which programmes a tutor has to teach to. In practice it matters because the tutor works from your child's own scheme of work, internal deadlines and mock papers rather than a generic course, so knowing the school tells us which assessment calendar the plan has to respect.

faqs.question: What does an in-home Diploma tutor charge per hour around The Greens?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands in October 2026 put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table quotes AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits also circulate. Those are market figures from the providers who publish them, not IB Gram prices. The premium over an online rate is mostly travel: a tutor crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at 5pm teaches fewer students an evening and prices accordingly.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student tutor a false economy for Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it depends on the job. For homework supervision, keeping a Standard Level student on top of weekly content, or rebuilding confidence in a subject that collapsed, a capable undergraduate at the AED 33 to 150 band published by providers like Tutopiya and EdFlik can be good value. For Higher Level paper technique it usually is a false economy, because the marks sit in command-term discipline, timed practice and internal assessment criteria that someone needs to have taught rather than merely passed. The test is simple: ask them to weight the papers.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Maths AA HL and Physics HL for the same child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and we are cautious about it. The overlap in content is real, but the assessment skills differ: Paper 3 problem-solving in Mathematics is a different discipline from the uncertainty and graph work that carries marks in Physics. Where one tutor genuinely has both specialisms we will match them, because continuity helps. More often we match two specialists and coordinate the timetable so the week is not stacked, with notes from both going to the same parent and one contact for rescheduling. Two specialists usually beat one generalist on both subjects.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student in The Greens usually start with?
faqs.answer: Most start with one ninety-minute session a week in one subject. Ninety rather than sixty, because a full Paper 2 question plus review does not fit in an hour at Higher Level. Students with two problem subjects usually run two sessions a week with different specialists, spread across the week rather than stacked on a Saturday. In the final eight to twelve weeks before the papers, families often move to two sessions a week in the weakest subject and then stop entirely during exam leave, which is a deliberate end rather than a drift.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to do with my child's Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain the criteria in plain language, help narrow an unanswerable research question into a manageable one, question the argument until weaknesses surface, point at a paragraph and say it does not satisfy the criterion it is aimed at, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a paragraph into final form, choose the question outright, or source data the student has not collected. IB Gram tutors are briefed to decline those requests rather than negotiate them, because a malpractice finding costs the candidate the Diploma.

faqs.question: Must a tutor teaching a child in The Greens hold a MoHRE permit, and is there a fee for it?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit, and no to the fee. Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The u.ae guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can a family in The Greens book a session after 7pm Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and from this postcode it is a common request. Many parents here work in Dubai Internet City, Media City or Barsha Heights and are not home before 7pm, so 7.30pm and 8pm slots are booked more often from The Greens and The Views than from the villa communities inland. Later slots also suit students whose school bus gets back after 4pm. The practical limit is the student's concentration rather than our availability: a ninety-minute Higher Level session starting at 8.30pm tends to produce less than a sixty-minute one at 7.30pm.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor you match us with turns out to be the wrong fit?
faqs.answer: Tell us after the trial lesson or after any session, and we rematch. The trial exists precisely so that a mismatch costs nothing: one free trial lesson per family, with the tutor you would actually continue with rather than a sales call. When a rematch is needed we ask what specifically did not work, because 'not the right fit' usually resolves into something concrete like pace, accent, pitch or the tutor teaching content when the student needed paper technique. That detail makes the second match better than a blind reshuffle would.

faqs.question: Does my child need a separate quiet room for an online Diploma session?
faqs.answer: A door that shuts helps more than a dedicated room. The Greens is an apartment community, so most of our students here work at a bedroom desk or the dining table with headphones. What genuinely matters is a flat surface big enough for a past paper and a notebook, headphones so the student hears the tutor's annotations, and a camera angle that lets the tutor see written working. Working through a phone makes the session substantially less useful, because the tutor cannot see the mathematics as it is being written.

faqs.question: Should we wait for the mock results before starting Diploma support?
faqs.answer: Usually no, but bring the mock when it arrives. Waiting costs weeks that the student needs, and the diagnosis does not depend on the mock: any recent marked script with teacher annotations shows where the marks are going. What the mock adds is a timed, full-length data point, which is why we ask for it as soon as it comes back and often restructure the plan around it. The one case for waiting is a student two weeks from a mock who would simply lose revision time to a new timetable.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child needs Higher Level stretch or Standard Level consolidation?
faqs.answer: Look at the marked script rather than the grade. A student losing marks on the last part of each question, or abandoning a Paper 3 problem after the first unfamiliar line, needs stretch and timed practice at the top end. A student losing marks spread evenly across every question, including the opening parts, has a content gap that stretch work will not touch. The two need different tutors and different session structures, and the distinction is visible in ten minutes to someone who has marked the specification. It is the first thing a trial lesson should establish.

intro.heading: The school run, not the syllabus, decides when tutoring happens here
paragraphs: The Springs is fifteen gated townhouse clusters off Sheikh Zayed Road, wedged between The Meadows, The Lakes and The Greens, with Springs Souk and Springs Village as the places everybody actually meets. Almost nobody here walks to school. Children board a bus between 06:30 and 07:15, ride it to Emirates Hills, Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim, and come back somewhere between 15:15 and 16:30 depending on the route and the afternoon activity. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a Springs household makes, and it is the reason a search for an IB home tutor in The Springs is really a search for a workable hour.

Work the clock forwards from the bus and you can see the problem. A Year 12 student back at 16:15 needs twenty minutes to eat and change. Diploma homework, Internal Assessment drafting and CAS logging want two hours of their own. Arabic and Islamic Education homework sits on top of the licensed curriculum, because KHDA requires those subjects in every Dubai private school whatever the school teaches otherwise. By 19:30 the useful part of a teenager's day is finished. The window for real teaching is roughly 16:45 to 19:00, four or five evenings a week, and it is contested.

Now put a visiting tutor into that window. The tutor has to leave their own area by about 16:00 to clear Al Khail Road or Hessa Street, find the right cluster and gate, park, and settle. Thirty to fifty minutes of travel each way is normal across New Dubai in term time, and it is the family who pays for it, either in the hourly rate or in a session that starts late and ends in a rush. Worse, the tutor pool shrinks to whoever is willing to make that drive, which is how a child studying Higher Level Chemistry ends up with a general science graduate.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so the only constraint on who teaches your child is whether they know the syllabus. A Springs student taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL gets a tutor who teaches that course and nothing like it, starting at 17:00 on the dot because nobody had to drive anywhere. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service that exists only in our India operation, and pretending otherwise on a Dubai page would waste your time and ours.

What follows is the honest version of this search. What the Dubai home-tutoring market charges, taken from published sources and attributed. Which schools a Springs address actually feeds and what time each of those days ends. How to count backwards from the series your child is entered for. Where the line sits on Internal Assessments. And what we will tell you if no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject in the week you ask.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: Springs children sit in three different IB stages at once in some households, and the stages do not behave alike. A PYP Year 4 pupil needs twenty-five focused minutes; a DP2 student needs ninety and a deadline. Here is what each stage demands of the evening, and what that means for scheduling in Emirates Living.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations, so support here is about literacy and number fluency rather than grades. Transdisciplinary units mean a child may be reading about migration in the morning and measuring volume after break. The exhibition in the final PYP year is the first piece of genuinely independent research a child produces, and it rewards a student who can plan, not one who can memorise. Sessions are short and frequent.
programmes.countryNote: Primary pupils from The Springs ride the earliest buses and are home by around 15:00, which makes them the easiest group to schedule. A 15:30 start works while concentration is still available. Parents here often pair a thirty-minute literacy session with Arabic homework support, because Arabic as an additional language starts in Dubai primary classrooms regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, criterion-referenced marking from A to D in each, and a Personal Project in MYP 5. The marking is what unsettles families moving from a British school: there are no percentages, and a strong piece of work can still score four out of eight because the criterion asked for evaluation rather than description. Tutoring at this stage is largely about teaching a student to read the criterion before writing the answer.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 students in The Springs are the group with the least free evening. They carry the heaviest homework load of any pre-Diploma stage, often with football or swimming at Springs Village afterwards. A 17:30 or 18:00 start twice a week is the realistic pattern, and the Personal Project supervision period in MYP 5 usually needs a third slot for six to eight weeks.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Diploma is a two-year clock, and the Internal Assessment deadlines set inside your child's own school are the ones that bite first, usually months before any external paper. Higher Level papers carry the specialist content and the Paper 3 style questions where most of the marks separate a five from a seven.
programmes.countryNote: DP students from The Springs often get home last, because Diploma timetables run later and CAS activities sit after school. Sessions at 18:00 or 19:00 are common, and in the final two terms families frequently move to a weekend morning as well, since a ninety-minute block on a Saturday does more for Paper 3 technique than a tired hour on a Tuesday.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The least common IB route in Dubai, built around a career-related study, two or more DP courses, and a personal and professional skills core with a reflective project. Students on the CP still sit real DP examinations in their chosen subjects, so the subject tutoring they need is identical to a Diploma student's, even though the surrounding programme looks different.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of Dubai schools offer the CP, so a Springs family on this route is usually travelling further than the Emirates Living cluster for school. Support is nearly always subject-specific: the DP courses inside the CP are tutored exactly as they would be for a full Diploma student, and the reflective project is coached as a process, never drafted for the student.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Springs households ask about most often, and what actually goes wrong in each. A tutor who knows the course knows where the marks leak; a tutor who knows the topic only knows the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the algebra that carries it. Most lost marks at HL sit in Paper 1, where no calculator is allowed and a student who has learned to type into a graphing screen has nowhere to go. The HL Paper 3 extended problems reward students who can carry an unfamiliar definition through several steps rather than recognise a familiar question type.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work. The common failure is treating it as the easy maths: AI HL contains serious statistical inference and matrix work, and the graphical calculator skills are examined rather than optional. Students lose marks by not stating a model's assumptions or by reporting a regression without interpreting it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the distress calls. The HL additional content on entropy, equilibrium constants and acid-base calculations is where a five becomes a seven. Written answers lose marks for describing a mechanism without naming the species, and the internal assessment often fails on uncertainty handling rather than chemistry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circuits and the quantum sections. Students arrive able to use equations and unable to explain them, which Paper 2 punishes immediately. Graph-based questions carry a large share of marks and are frequently answered without reading the axes. HL rotational dynamics and thermodynamics need deliberate practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the enemy here, not difficulty. The course rewards precise terminology, and answers that say cells rather than naming the organelle lose easy marks. Data-based questions in Paper 2 need practised reading of unfamiliar experiments, and HL students routinely underestimate the plant-science and genetics extensions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment commentaries are the most common reason for a disappointing grade, because they fail on diagram accuracy and on using a real news article properly rather than on economic understanding. HL quantitative questions demand working, and Paper 1 essays need evaluation that goes beyond listing two opposing views.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Deceptively friendly. Students who treat it as common sense write unstructured answers and lose the application marks that require named tools used correctly. The HL extension topics and the business research project need planning time, and command terms such as examine and discuss have precise mark implications students rarely learn in class.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen textual analysis is the hardest part for second-language students, and the Individual Oral requires a global issue genuinely traceable through two texts. Grades rise fastest when a student stops summarising and starts writing about how a writer's choices create effect, which is a teachable habit rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Mathematics support across MYP 4 and 5
subjects.description: The bridge year. MYP marking assesses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating and applying mathematics in real-life contexts as four separate criteria, and a student strong at calculation can still score poorly on investigation. This is the stage where Diploma maths route choices are effectively decided.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay are both tightly specified and both routinely left late. The essay must answer one of the prescribed titles using knowledge arguments rather than opinions, and the exhibition needs three real objects with genuine links to a chosen prompt. Coaching here is about structure and argument, and the student writes every word.

sections.heading: What a Springs parent is actually asking when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: The phrase means something precise in Dubai, and it is worth saying out loud. A home tutor is someone who comes to the townhouse, teaches at the dining table for an hour, and leaves. Families want it because it removes a journey, keeps a young child in a familiar room, and lets a parent overhear the lesson. Those are good reasons and they are not imaginary benefits.

The trade-offs are also real and rarely discussed by the agencies selling the service. You are not choosing from the pool of people who teach your child's syllabus; you are choosing from the much smaller pool willing to drive to Emirates Living at five in the afternoon. The rate carries the travel whether or not it is itemised. A cancelled session is harder to recover, because a tutor who has already driven across town will not come back later that evening. And the arrangement quietly caps how specialist your tutor can be, which matters enormously at Higher Level.

IB Gram's answer is to keep the one-to-one part and drop the driving. Your child works with a named subject specialist over live video, screen shared, same tutor each week, at a time chosen around the Springs bus rather than around a commute. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses and we say so before you ask, because the alternative is a conversation that ends in disappointment two emails later. The comparison in the next section is the honest arithmetic, with the market rates attributed to the people who published them.

sections.heading: The Springs school run, hour by hour, and where a lesson fits
paragraphs: Dubai secondary days generally end between 14:30 and 15:30, and primary days a little earlier, but the bell time is not what matters to a Springs family. What matters is the bus. A route that serves Al Sufouh or Umm Suqeim collects from several communities, crosses Sheikh Zayed Road at the worst hour of the afternoon, and deposits children in the Springs clusters anywhere up to an hour after dismissal.

The table below is the typical pattern for the campuses on these routes. It is deliberately a range rather than a claim about any individual school, because bell times and bus contracts change every academic year and only your school's own calendar is authoritative. Use it to work out which column your household sits in, then pick the session start that leaves twenty minutes for food and a change of clothes.

Two patterns show up again and again once families map this properly. First, the earliest realistic start for a secondary student on a second-ring bus is 16:45, and anything advertised at 16:00 will be attended by a child still on Al Khail Road. Second, families who choose a fixed slot and defend it get far more teaching done over a term than families who schedule week by week, because the negotiation itself eats the window. Springs school bus timings are the one variable a tutoring plan cannot argue with, so build the plan around them and treat everything else as adjustable.

There is a quieter benefit to online one-to-one IB tutoring that only shows up after a few weeks. Because no journey has to be absorbed at either end, a session that would have been cancelled can usually be moved by an hour instead. A dentist appointment, a late bus or a school assembly that overruns stops being a lost lesson and becomes a shifted one. Over a Diploma year that difference accumulates into whole weeks of teaching that an in-home arrangement in Emirates Living would simply have forfeited, and it is one of the reasons the fixed-slot habit survives contact with a real family calendar.

sections.heading: Online or a tutor in the car: the Emirates Living arithmetic
paragraphs: Put the two options side by side with real numbers and the decision stops being about preference. The AED figures below are market rates published by named providers and by Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026; they are not IB Gram's price list, and none of them is ours to quote as our own. What they show is that the in-home premium is not a small convenience charge. It is the cost of a car, a driver's hour and a narrowed shortlist.

Read the travel column as the part no price list shows. A tutor crossing New Dubai in term time spends between thirty and fifty minutes each way. Over a two-session week that is up to three and a half hours of unpaid driving, and unpaid time always finds its way into either the rate or the reliability. This is also why in-home arrangements in Emirates Living tend to be built around whoever lives nearby rather than whoever knows Higher Level Chemistry.

The last column is the one that decides most Diploma cases. Online delivery means the shortlist for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is everyone who teaches that course on a compatible timezone, which is a genuinely different pool from everyone who teaches it and is willing to drive to Springs 9. For a subject your child will be examined in for two years, that difference is worth more than the saved minutes.

One warning about how to use Dubai market tutoring rates in AED per hour. A quoted rate is only comparable if you know what sits inside it: session length, whether notes or marked work are included, whether a cancelled lesson is credited, and whether the figure covers travel. The cheapest hourly number on this table can be the most expensive arrangement in practice if half of each session is spent re-explaining last week. Ask providers to price a term rather than an hour, and compare what arrives in writing afterwards. Families comparing IB tutoring in Emirates Living almost always find the gap between providers is in inclusions, not in headline rates.

sections.heading: Why two boards land in one Springs house in the same week
paragraphs: Emirates Living is unusual in how mixed its school choices are. One family will have a child at an IB continuum school in Emirates Hills and another at a British-curriculum school in Al Sufouh sitting Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at sixteen. UK-curriculum schools account for the largest share of Dubai private-school enrolment, around thirty-seven per cent, with Indian curriculum at about twenty-six per cent, American at fourteen per cent and IB programmes at roughly seven per cent, on KHDA's 2024-25 figures. In practice that means IB and IGCSE share a lot of kitchen tables here.

The consequence is a scheduling problem dressed up as a subject problem. The MYP child is being marked against criteria A to D with no percentages; the IGCSE child is being marked against grades nine to one with tiered papers. They are not interchangeable, and a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically useful for the other. Families who try to solve this with a single generalist usually end up with two mediocre arrangements rather than one good one.

The workable pattern is to split by board and share the week. Give the IGCSE child the earlier slot, because their homework load is lighter in Year 10 than a DP student's, and give the Diploma student the later block when the house has gone quiet. Two different specialists, two fixed evenings each, and a shared family calendar. It costs the same as one tutor trying to cover both and produces work that each board's examiners would actually recognise.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same evening
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside whatever international curriculum it is licensed for. This is a federal requirement reflected in KHDA's own mandatory-subjects guidance, which schools were required to implement from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. It is not optional and it does not disappear because a child is in the IB Diploma. For a Springs family it means the evening has a second homework stream nobody mentions in the IB brochure.

The detail matters. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Islamic Education for Arab students and Arabic as a first language are taught in Standard Arabic; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes.

For tutoring, two things follow. First, a non-Arabic-speaking family in The Springs usually needs Arabic as an additional language support rather than first-language support, and the two are different courses with different expectations. Second, the content is tightly controlled: for mandatory subjects, using different or additional material without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so good support means teaching the child to handle the school's own material rather than substituting something livelier. Schools, for their part, must ensure their Arabic and Islamic Education teachers hold the approval KHDA requires.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the series your child is entered for
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a Springs family can do in October is open a calendar and count backwards from the examination series, because every deadline that matters sits months before the papers. Nobody in this market publishes that calendar, which is odd, since it is the part parents consistently get wrong. Entry deadlines are set by the board and administered by the school, and a missed entry is not something a tutor can repair.

For Cambridge International, examinations run in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The March 2027 series is the cleanest worked example of how far ahead the paperwork sits: the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades 27 February 2027, with results released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live PDF on its site rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. For the IB, this page deliberately prints no session or results dates: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so every IB date here would be second-hand. Ask your school's IB coordinator, or read it on ibo.org directly.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: This matters more in the IB than in any other curriculum a Springs family might be in, because the consequences land on the student. The work has to be the student's own, and the IB's academic-honesty rules treat breaches as malpractice with outcomes up to the loss of the Diploma. There is an active market in Dubai selling finished Internal Assessments, including one site publishing a price for them. A family should treat any such offer as a risk to their child's qualification.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and worth spelling out so you know what you are buying. Teaching the underlying content. Explaining what each assessment criterion asks for and what the examiner reads it against. Discussing whether a research question is answerable within the word limit. Reading a draft the student has written and giving feedback at the level of structure, reasoning and clarity. Teaching referencing. Running a mock oral. Helping a student build a timeline they can hold themselves to.

What a tutor may not do is just as clear. No supplying text, no drafting sections, no editing a piece to completion, no providing data the student did not gather, no sourcing a ready-made topic with a ready-made conclusion. If a session ever drifts towards that, the right response is to stop and reset, and a tutor who offers it should be declined. The practical version is a simple test: at the end of a session, could your child explain every line of their own document to a teacher who asked? If yes, the help was legitimate.

Legitimate: referencing, timeline planning, mock orals and viva practice
