sections.heading: What grade movement is realistic, and over what period
paragraphs: Parents are owed a straight answer here and almost never get one. No tutor can promise a grade, and a provider who does is either naive or dishonest. What can be said is what the common fault signatures typically yield when they are correctly identified and cleared, and how long each takes to appear in marked work.

Convention and timing faults are the fast ones. A pupil losing marks to missing units, unlabelled axes or a collapse in the final third of the paper can show measurable change in one to four weeks, because the repair is a checklist rather than knowledge. These are also the faults most likely to be invisible to the family, because nothing about the pupil's understanding is wrong.

Command-term faults take two to four weeks to repair and longer to become habitual under exam pressure. Content gaps take six to ten weeks at one session per week, and that estimate assumes the pupil does the consolidation between sessions. A content gap spanning two years of missing foundations, which happens after a curriculum switch, is a two-term project and should be described as one at the outset.

What none of this supports is a prediction expressed as a number. A pupil who clears a timing fault may gain marks that do not cross a grade boundary, and a pupil who gains fewer marks may cross one. Grade boundaries are set per session by the board and are not published in advance. Any figure attached to a promise about your child's final grade was invented, and the fact that it was offered tells you what else on that page is worth checking.
bullets: Convention and timing faults: visible movement in one to four weeks
Command-term faults: two to four weeks to repair, longer to automate

Post-curriculum-switch gaps: two terms, and worth saying so up front
Grade boundaries are set per session, so no grade can be predicted honestly

sections.heading: What a Dubai school report will not tell you
paragraphs: School reporting in this emirate is generally thorough, and it is built to answer a different question from the one a parent books a tutor to answer. A report tells you where a pupil sits relative to expectation. It rarely tells you which component the marks were lost on, which is the only information that selects an intervention.

Three specific blind spots recur. The first is the aggregated subject grade, which averages a strong internal assessment with weak examined performance, or the reverse, and conceals both. A pupil with a banked upper-band coursework mark and collapsing paper technique looks identical on a report to a pupil with the opposite profile, and they need opposite help.

The second is the predicted grade, which is a professional judgement made for university applications and carries institutional caution in both directions. It is not a measurement, it moves between reporting cycles, and in a newer Diploma cohort it rests on very few historical data points. Treating it as a reading rather than a judgement leads families to relax or to panic at the wrong moments.

The third is the inspection band. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a judgement from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the band is a statement about the school as a whole. It cannot tell you whether this year's Diploma cohort was large enough to timetable Higher Level Economics, or whether one teacher covers both levels of Physics. The subject detail sits inside the full report, and the school's option blocks answer the rest.

sections.heading: Two tutors, one record: keeping a paired plan coherent
paragraphs: Families who book two specialists usually do it for good reasons and then discover a coordination problem nobody warned them about. Two tutors optimising independently will both decide that the fortnight before half-term is the right moment for intensive drafting work, and the pupil will face two coursework deadlines, two sets of feedback and a full school week simultaneously.

The fix is one shared calendar built before either slot is fixed. Every internal assessment deadline across all six subjects goes on it, with the mock window and the co-curricular commitments that actually bind: a CAS project, a sports fixture block, a performance. Then the two slots are placed so that drafting intensity alternates rather than coincides.

The second half of the fix is one record rather than two. A single four-week review covering both subjects lets a parent see something neither tutor can: that the pupil is improving in one subject and flat in the other, which usually means attention is being rationed rather than that one tutor is better. That is a scheduling decision, and it can only be made from a combined view.

This is also where an honest provider says no. Three weekly subject slots plus school plus coursework plus CAS does not fit in a sixteen-year-old's week, and arrangements that do not fit fail quietly, with the pupil absorbing the blame. Two is usually the ceiling for sustained weekly work, with a third subject handled as a short component block when a deadline demands it.

sections.heading: The mock is an instrument, not a verdict
paragraphs: Mock results arrive in Dubai Diploma households in the winter term and cause more poor decisions than any other single document. The grade gets read as a prediction, the household reacts, and the script itself, which is the valuable part, goes into a bag and is never looked at again.

A mock paper is the richest diagnostic a family will see in two years. It is sat under timed conditions, marked against a real scheme, and covers the whole specification. The lost marks on it map directly onto the four fault signatures, and the mapping takes one session. That session is the highest-value hour available in the entire Diploma, and most families spend the equivalent money on general revision instead.

The grade itself deserves much less weight than it gets, for a mechanical reason. Mocks are often marked to boundaries the school chooses, sometimes deliberately harsh to produce urgency. Grade boundaries for the real session are set afterwards by the board and are not published in advance. A mock 4 and a mock 5 can be two marks apart on a script, which means the difference between a household's calm and its panic can be one borderline answer.

The right use of a mock is therefore mechanical. Get the script. Map every lost mark to a fault signature. Rank the faults by how cheaply they can be cleared. Clear the top two before the next assessment, and ignore the grade until something has actually changed. A post-mock block of three to six sessions aimed at exactly that produces more marks than a term of weekly general support started at the same moment.
bullets: Keep the script, not the grade
Map lost marks to fault signatures in one session
Rank faults by repair cost, then clear the cheapest two
Mock boundaries are chosen by the school, not by the board
Three to six post-mock sessions beat a term of general revision

sections.heading: What cannot be evidenced, and how to spot a provider who pretends otherwise
paragraphs: A page about evidence owes the reader the limits of it. Several things parents are routinely told in this market cannot be demonstrated at all, and the willingness of a provider to assert them is itself a useful signal about everything else they say.

No final grade can be promised. Grade boundaries are set per session by the board, a pupil's performance on the day is not controllable, and anybody promising a 7, or an assured jump of a grade, is selling something they cannot deliver. Related claims are equally unfounded: a specific points gain, a top-percentage placement, or a refund tied to an outcome whose terms are nowhere published.

Aggregate statistics about pupil outcomes cannot be published without the underlying data. A satisfaction percentage, a median tutor score or a proportion achieving top grades means nothing without the number of pupils, the date range and the method of collection. Competitor pages in this market carry several such figures, including two different review totals on the same page, and one self-asserted rating attached to a pupil count that does not reconcile. None of those numbers appear here, because the data behind them does not exist in a form that would survive a question.

Regulatory standing cannot be implied either. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here will suggest otherwise. A permit for an individual tutor is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation; a licence for a training institute with premises in Dubai is a separate matter handled by KHDA. Neither is a badge a tutoring platform can borrow, and the phrase to be most sceptical of in this market is any tutor described as approved by a regulator.
bullets: No grade, points gain or improvement can be promised honestly
Any statistic without a pupil count, a date range and a method is unusable

process.title: Send the most recent marked script
process.description: Not the report, the script with the annotations on it. One paper per subject of concern is enough. It is read for the fault signature before anyone proposes a tutor, because the signature determines whether you need a term of teaching or three sessions of technique work.

process.title: Get the fault statement in writing
process.description: Before any teaching, you receive a written statement naming the fault, the evidence for it on the script, and the repair time. If that statement is vague, the diagnosis was vague, and you should say so rather than proceed hoping it resolves itself.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the proposed specialist at no cost and with no card required, run as a diagnosis rather than a demonstration. By the end you should hold a fault list in priority order and a plan for the first four weeks, whether or not you book anything.

process.title: Agree the review instrument now
process.description: Decide at the outset which piece of school-marked work the four-week review will be measured against. Agreeing the instrument before the sessions start is what prevents a review from becoming a conversation about how the sessions felt.

process.title: Review, and use the exit if the evidence says so
process.description: Every four weeks, against the agreed instrument, with a written note of what has not improved. If the pattern of lost marks is unchanged after eight weeks on a non-content fault, the match is wrong and should change. That is the point of measuring.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching, always
whyPoints.description: The first session works from the pupil's own marked script and produces a written fault statement. Four fault signatures cover most Diploma underperformance and each has a different repair time, so teaching before identifying which one is present is an expensive guess.

whyPoints.title: The measurement is the school's, not ours
whyPoints.description: Progress is judged against work the school marked, by someone with no stake in the arrangement, against the scheme an examiner uses. A provider's own progress report is a document about itself. We would rather be judged on a script we never saw in advance.

whyPoints.title: A record that survives the session
whyPoints.description: Live video with a shared whiteboard leaves every worked solution and annotated script behind as a file. Session notes name the component and the criterion addressed. Eight weeks in, that file is a diagnostic history rather than a memory of pleasant afternoons.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level feedback, inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Coursework progress is reported against published criterion descriptors by letter, so movement is visible rather than asserted. Feedback addresses only work the candidate wrote. No text is supplied and no part of a submission is produced for anyone.

whyPoints.title: Reviews that name what failed
whyPoints.description: Every four-week review states what has not improved. An arrangement where nothing is ever reported as unchanged is not being measured, and the family finds out at the mock instead, which is the most expensive possible moment.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated rather than papered over
whyPoints.description: No grade promise, no outcome statistics without the data behind them, and no regulator or board accreditation claimed. Two tutors is the sustainable ceiling for weekly work alongside school and CAS, and we say so instead of selling a third.

faqs.question: How will I know whether IB home tutors are actually improving my child's marks?
faqs.answer: By comparing the pattern of lost marks on school-marked work before and after. Keep the script from before the arrangement started, and the next one the school marks six to eight weeks in. If the losses have moved from the pattern named in the week-one diagnosis, something real changed. If they are in the same places, the arrangement is not working regardless of how the sessions feel. Confidence, attendance and completed homework are not evidence, because a pupil can be diligently consolidating the very method that is costing the marks.

faqs.question: Why should the school mark the work rather than the tutor?
faqs.answer: Independence. A tutor marking their own pupil's practice paper has every incentive, including unconscious ones, to read generously, and their boundaries are not the board's. The school's assessment is produced by someone with no stake in the tutoring arrangement, against the same mark scheme an examiner uses, and under conditions the tutor did not design. That is why the review instrument should be agreed before sessions start: a measurement chosen in advance cannot be selected afterwards to flatter whoever is being measured.

faqs.question: What should a tutor's session note actually say?
faqs.answer: Which component was worked on, which criterion or question type, what the pupil could not do at the start, and what they could do by the end. Four lines is enough. What a session note should not say is the topic covered, because a note reading quadratic equations tells a parent nothing about whether a fault was addressed. Over eight weeks, notes written this way become a diagnostic history that makes a four-week review a judgement on evidence rather than an exchange of impressions about a pleasant hour.

faqs.question: Can progress on an internal assessment draft be measured objectively?
faqs.answer: Yes, more objectively than almost anything else in the Diploma, because the criteria are published with descriptors. A Group 4 investigation is marked out of 24 across five criteria; a mathematics exploration out of 20 across five. Place the draft against the descriptor for each criterion and the band is readable by any careful adult. A draft where the prose improved and every criterion stayed in the same band has not progressed, which is a common and costly outcome of unfocused drafting support.

faqs.question: How long before a technique fix shows up in a marked paper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the fault. Convention faults, such as missing units or unlabelled axes, can show measurable change within one to three weeks, because the repair is a checklist applied to practice answers. Timing faults take two to four weeks. Command-term faults take two to four weeks to repair and longer to hold under exam pressure. A genuine content gap takes six to ten weeks at one session a week, assuming the pupil consolidates between sessions, and a gap left by a curriculum switch can take two terms.

faqs.question: Is a mock grade a reliable prediction of the final result?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a diagnostic rather than a prediction. Mocks are often marked to boundaries the school selects, sometimes deliberately severe to create urgency, while real grade boundaries are set per session by the board afterwards and are not published in advance. A mock 4 and a mock 5 can be two marks apart on the same script. The valuable part of a mock is the script, not the grade: mapping every lost mark to a fault signature takes one session and is the highest-value hour available in the two years.

faqs.question: Why will a tutor not promise my child a 7?
faqs.answer: Because nobody can deliver it and offering it is a straightforward misrepresentation. Grade boundaries are set per session by the board, performance on the day is not controllable, and the same number of extra marks crosses a boundary for one candidate and not another. Any provider promising a final grade, an assured improvement or a refund tied to an outcome has either not thought about it or is relying on the terms never being tested. What can honestly be committed to is a diagnosis, a repair plan, a measurement date and an exit.

faqs.question: What does a four-week review contain if nothing improved?
faqs.answer: A statement that nothing improved, the evidence for it, and a recommendation: change the fault being targeted, change the match, or stop. That is the hardest paragraph in this work and it is the one that makes the rest credible. A review that never reports anything unchanged is not a measurement, and a family relying on one discovers the truth at the mock instead, which is the most expensive possible moment to find out.

faqs.question: Does a predicted grade from a Dubai school tell me how tutoring is going?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made primarily for university applications, and it carries institutional caution in both directions. It moves between reporting cycles for reasons unrelated to the pupil, and in a newer Diploma cohort it rests on very few historical data points. The underlying internal mark history is far more informative, because it separates banked coursework performance from examined performance. Ask for that history rather than for an explanation of the prediction.

faqs.question: Can one record cover two subjects with two different tutors?
faqs.answer: It should. Two specialists reporting separately conceal the one thing a parent most needs to see, which is divergent progress: improvement in one subject and none in the other usually means attention is being rationed rather than that one tutor is weaker. A single four-week review covering both subjects, using the same four fault names, makes that visible and turns it into a scheduling decision. The combined deadline calendar belongs in the same document, built before either weekly slot is fixed.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions can a Dubai Diploma candidate actually sustain?
faqs.answer: Two is the realistic ceiling for sustained weekly work alongside a full school timetable, coursework across six subjects, CAS commitments and transport. A third weekly slot generally displaces the consolidation time that makes the first two effective, and the arrangement then fails quietly with the pupil absorbing the blame. Where a third subject genuinely needs attention, a short component block of three to six sessions timed to a specific deadline works, and it ends. Any provider happy to sell four weekly slots is not thinking about the pupil's week.

faqs.question: What evidence does an online session leave that an in-home visit does not?
faqs.answer: A shared whiteboard retains every worked solution as a reviewable file, annotated scripts exist as documents rather than as paper in a school bag, and the session format invites a written note because there is no doorstep conversation to substitute for one. A visit typically leaves whatever was written on paper plus a verbal summary. IB Gram does not offer in-home visiting in the UAE in any case; teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the audit trail is a by-product of that rather than an added feature.

faqs.question: Why are there no success statistics on this page?
faqs.answer: Because a statistic without a pupil count, a date range and a stated method is not information. Pages competing for this search carry satisfaction percentages, review totals that contradict each other within the same page, and at least one self-asserted rating attached to a pupil figure that does not reconcile. Publishing numbers of that kind would be easy and would tell you nothing about your child. The measurement offered here is specific to one pupil and produced by their own school, which is less impressive and considerably more useful.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved or accredited by KHDA to provide tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody in this market should claim it. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises in Dubai, which is a specific licence for a specific kind of operation. An individual tutor's permit is a different instrument, issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge for two years. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and the phrase to be most sceptical of in this market is a tutor described as regulator-approved.

faqs.question: What should I keep from a tutoring arrangement once it ends?
faqs.answer: The written fault statements, the session notes, the draft history of each coursework component with its criterion feedback, and the marked scripts that were used as review instruments. That file is useful twice. It tells a future tutor in six months exactly what has already been tried and what did not work, which saves two sessions of rediscovery. And it tells the pupil, during the May session revision period, which three faults cost them the most marks and in what order to check for them.

dubai/ib-home-tutors.closingHeading: Send one marked script and see what it says
dubai/ib-home-tutors.closingBody: The useful first step in judging IB home tutors in Dubai costs nothing and requires no commitment. Send the subject, the level and one recent marked script. You will get back a written fault statement naming which of the four signatures the script shows, the evidence for it, and an honest repair estimate in weeks. If the signature is a convention or timing fault, that is three sessions rather than a term, and you will be told so. The trial lesson that follows is a full diagnostic hour over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card required.

dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: Each profile below names the board, the level and the subjects the tutor coaches. Coaching cadence is agreed before the first paid session, because a student eight weeks from a series needs a different rhythm from one starting in September.

intro.heading: Coaching is a rhythm, and the rhythm has to match the Dubai year
paragraphs: Parents searching for IB IGCSE coaching in Dubai are rarely asking for a different subject expert from the one a tutoring search would return. They are asking for something structural: a programme with a shape, a schedule and a report, rather than an open-ended weekly hour that drifts until the exams arrive. That is a reasonable thing to want, and it is also where the word coaching does most of its work in this market, because it is used for formats that share nothing except the label.

At one end, a coaching centre runs a batch of eight to twenty students through a syllabus on a fixed timetable. It is cheap per head, it covers content reliably, and it cannot follow one student's mark pattern, because following fifteen mark patterns at once is not a thing a timetable can do. At the other end, one-to-one coaching is a cycle: diagnose from a timed paper, teach what the paper exposed, drill the question types, re-test under identical conditions, report. The second format costs more per hour and usually fewer hours in total. Neither is wrong; buying one while expecting the other is.

The second thing this page does is put the cycle on the actual Dubai calendar. A school year here runs from late August to late June across three terms, with a winter break, a spring break and Ramadan moving through it year by year. That calendar matters more than any generic revision timetable, because the deadlines that decide a Diploma or IGCSE result are set by the school and sit inside it. Internal coursework deadlines cluster in the middle of Term 2. Mock windows land weeks before entry decisions take effect. Ramadan can arrive in the same six weeks as a Cambridge March series.

The third thing is reporting. A coaching arrangement that reports nothing is indistinguishable from an arrangement that is not working, and parents in this market are routinely offered reassurance in place of evidence. The reporting standard this page describes is modest and specific: a marked artefact after every session, a short written summary after every fourth, and a comparison of two identical timed papers at the ten-week mark. All of it readable by a parent who does not teach the subject.

Delivery, stated once and plainly. IB Gram coaches one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around Dubai school timetables. IB Gram does not run a centre, holds no premises in the UAE, and does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India. No approval, accreditation or partnership is claimed from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and the first session is free and runs as a diagnostic on a real past paper.

dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: Cadence differs by programme more than content does. Below is what each programme demands of a coaching rhythm, and what Dubai schools in particular do with it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses with syllabus codes that determine the papers sat: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0478 Computer Science, 0460 Geography. Most subjects tier into Core and Extended. A coaching rhythm here is weekly through Year 10, rising to two sessions a week in Term 2 of Year 11 as papers replace topics.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June and a November series with March available in some regions, and allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so a Dubai coaching plan takes dates from the school's exams officer rather than from a generic calendar.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology. Some subjects offer a modular route, so units can be sat in different series and banked, which changes a coaching plan fundamentally: the cycle runs to a unit deadline rather than to a single terminal window.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson papers are available in a May/June and a November series each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so a Dubai coaching schedule should be built against the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. Coaching at MYP is usually about criterion literacy rather than content: understanding what the top descriptor band asks for and producing work that satisfies it. The cadence is lighter, often fortnightly, because the assessment points are spread rather than terminal.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai continuum schools run MYP to Year 11, and MYP 5 brings the Personal Project and the ePortfolios into the same term. The coaching risk specific to Dubai is the transfer: a student moving from MYP into IGCSE or the Diploma at a different school arrives with strong criterion habits and no timed-paper stamina, and the rhythm has to change to fix that.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The coaching cadence is governed by the school's internal deadlines rather than by the exam window, and those arrive in waves across Year 12 and the first half of Year 13. Two sessions a week in Term 2 of Year 13 is common.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter candidates for the May session. No IB session or results date is published on this page; the IB's own site is the authoritative source and dates should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator, who also sets the internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines a coaching plan is actually built around.

dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Different subjects need different coaching rhythms, and the difference is usually about how much marking sits between sessions. Here is what each one needs from a plan.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking components, with the writing marks decided by register and task fulfilment rather than vocabulary range. Coaching works best as weekly short pieces marked between sessions, since the gain comes from accumulated feedback rather than from classroom explanation.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger cohorts in Dubai schools and often underestimated, since it borrows calculus and trigonometry conventions from A Level. A fortnightly rhythm with substantial problem sets between sessions suits it better than weekly contact.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and constant graphic display calculator use. Coaching time goes further here when it is split between technique sessions and marked problem sets, because the recoverable marks are in interpretation sentences rather than in the calculations themselves.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory paper plus algorithms and programming, where pseudocode conventions decide marks more often than logic does. A coaching plan should include written pseudocode marked against the mark scheme, not screen time in an editor, because the paper is handwritten.

subjects.name: IB Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper-based theory plus a substantial solution the student develops themselves. Coaching cadence is uneven by design: dense at the design and criteria stage, light during build, dense again for documentation, which has to be timed to the school's internal deadlines.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460
subjects.description: Case-study recall and skills-paper technique, including graph interpretation and map work. The common Dubai pattern is a student who knows the content and loses marks on command terms and on naming a located example, which responds quickly to a short drill block.

subjects.name: IB History
subjects.description: Paper 1 source work, Paper 2 comparative essays, Paper 3 regional depth at Higher Level, plus the historical investigation. Coaching is essay-marking heavy, so a plan should state how many marked essays sit between sessions and who marks them.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Accounting 0452
subjects.description: Highly teachable and consistently under-coached in Dubai. Marks are lost to layout conventions and to arithmetic carried through a ledger, both of which are fixed by repetition rather than explanation, so short frequent sessions beat long occasional ones.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms at Higher Level, plus a data-based paper that punishes loose language about uncertainty. The Internal Assessment needs a narrow measurable research question, and shaping that takes two or three reads spread across weeks rather than one long session.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Information and Communication Technology 0417
subjects.description: Theory plus two practical papers with strict task instructions, where marks go on unfollowed formatting requirements rather than on capability. Coaching works as timed practical tasks marked against the mark scheme, which is unglamorous and reliably effective.

dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.regionsTitle: Where Dubai families sit relative to a coaching centre, and why it stops mattering
dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: Batch coaching is a geography problem: the family travels to the centre, at a fixed time, twice a week, through Dubai traffic. Here is what that looks like from each part of the emirate, and what changes when the coaching runs over video instead.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Al Quoz and Dubai Knowledge Park
regions.note: Where most established coaching centres actually sit, so families nearby have genuine batch choice. The trade is the batch itself: a fixed syllabus pace for eight to twenty students, with no individual diagnostic inside it.

regions.name: Karama, Bur Dubai and Al Nahda
regions.note: Dense centre provision at the lowest per-head rates in the emirate, strongest for IGCSE maths and sciences. Evening batches run late, which works for Year 11 and poorly for Year 9.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Reasonable centre access and good Arabic coverage. The common complaint here is batch pace: a student who misses two sessions in a syllabus-paced batch cannot recover the ground inside it.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills Estate and Motor City
regions.note: Few centres within a realistic weeknight drive, so families either accept a 45-minute each-way journey twice a week or move online. A 6.30pm online start replaces a 5.15pm departure.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and The Greens
regions.note: High-rise living with school buses in by 4pm and limited parking at nearby centres. Coaching at 4.30pm works online and rarely works in a centre, because the journey eats the window entirely.

regions.name: Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and JVT
regions.note: The thinnest centre provision in the emirate relative to the number of school-age children. Two sessions a week here means roughly three hours a week in the car, which is the real cost of batch coaching in this corridor.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis, Nad Al Sheba and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Growing school capacity, with seven new private schools in Dubai's 2026-27 intake across the emirate. Centre supply has not caught up, so online cadence is often the only way to get two sessions a week at a usable time.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Quoz and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: A dense cluster of British and IB schools within a short radius, which is why coaching centres concentrate here. Students we support in this cluster most often ask for Extended-tier sciences and Diploma mathematics.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Nad Al Sheba and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: IB continuum schools sit alongside large British-curriculum schools, so MYP-to-IGCSE and MYP-to-Diploma transfers are routine here and the transition map further down this page is the relevant part.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah Village, Dubai Sports City and Jumeirah Park
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with wide fee spreads and growing Year 10 and Year 11 cohorts, where coaching demand is concentrated on IGCSE tier decisions rather than on catch-up.

sections.heading: What coaching means in this market, and what it should mean
paragraphs: In Dubai the word coaching covers at least four products. A centre batch of eight to twenty students on a fixed syllabus timetable. A small group of three or four. A pair. And one-to-one work with a diagnostic and a marking cycle. The rates differ by a factor of five, the outcomes differ by more than that, and the advertising for all four uses the same vocabulary of structure, discipline and results.

The distinction that matters is not group against individual. It is whether the arrangement can respond to evidence. A batch can deliver content well, hold a student to a schedule, and create the useful social pressure of working alongside peers who are also behind. What it structurally cannot do is notice that your child loses four marks a paper to explain questions answered as describe questions, and change next week's plan accordingly. Fifteen mark patterns do not fit in one timetable, and no amount of good teaching changes that arithmetic.

So the honest way to buy coaching is to decide which problem you have. A student who has not covered the content needs content delivery, and a batch is a rational and cheap way to get it. A student who has covered the content and is still losing marks needs diagnosis, and a batch will not supply it at any price. A student who is both behind on content and leaking technique marks usually needs the cheap format for the first problem and the expensive format for the second, which is a sequence rather than a choice.
The table below sets out the formats with what each can and cannot do, and the per-student rates published in this market, so the trade is visible before you pay for it.

sections.heading: The Dubai school year, term by term, and what coaching should be doing
paragraphs: Generic revision timetables fail in Dubai for a specific reason: they are built around an exam date, and the dates that decide a result here are set by the school and sit much earlier. Internal coursework deadlines, mock windows and the centre's own entry cut-off all land inside the three terms, and a plan that only knows the exam month will miss all three.

The table maps a coaching year onto the real calendar: late August to mid December, the winter break, January to late March, the Ramadan weeks wherever they fall, April to late June, and the results windows in August and January. Each row carries what the coaching should be doing and the mistake families actually make at that point.

Two rows deserve comment. The winter break tempts everyone into an intensive fortnight, which feels productive and reliably underperforms a term of cadence, because nothing is retained from six sessions in ten days. Two or three targeted catch-up sessions are a better buy, with the rest of the break left alone. And Ramadan moves against the Gregorian calendar, which means it can land on top of a Cambridge March series or close to the Diploma May session depending on the year. The practical response is to front-load content teaching before it starts and keep the fasting weeks for paper review and marking discussion, which is lighter cognitive work for a similar mark return.

Dubai's own capacity changes matter here too. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More Diploma cohorts in the same labour market is why Higher Level availability tightens in Term 2 specifically, and why a slot booked in September is worth more than a slot sought in January.

sections.heading: Cadence: why two short sessions beat one long one
paragraphs: The most common structural error in a Dubai coaching plan is a single long session once a week, usually ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes, because it fits the school run and the traffic. It is convenient and it is the wrong shape for most of the work it is asked to do.

Two mechanisms explain why. The first is spacing: material revisited after a gap is retained better than material covered in one sitting, and two sessions three days apart create that gap for free. The second is marking turnaround. A paper sat on Sunday and returned marked before a Wednesday session produces a conversation about specific lost marks while the student still remembers the question. The same paper discussed nine days later produces a general conversation, which is pleasant and much less useful.

There are genuine exceptions. Higher Level mathematics and physics benefit from longer blocks, because re-entering a multi-step problem has a real cost and ninety minutes allows one proper investigation rather than two interrupted ones. Essay subjects with heavy marking between sessions can run fortnightly without loss, provided the writing actually happens. Younger students should be on shorter sessions regardless, since attention rather than content sets their ceiling.

The practical rule that follows is simple enough to apply. Through Term 1, one session a week with one marked piece of work in between. From January for an exam year, two sessions: one on content, one on papers, with the marking moving between them. In the final fortnight, three short sessions and no new content at all. The sprint is where families overspend most, usually by buying hours in a week when the student can no longer absorb them.

sections.heading: The curriculum transition map
paragraphs: Dubai is a transfer city. Families arrive mid-year, schools fill at different rates, and a child can change curriculum twice before Year 11. Each transition has a specific gap, and coaching that treats a transfer as general catch-up wastes most of its first term finding out what the gap was.

The table names the gap for the six transitions most common in this emirate, with a realistic number of weeks of support. The numbers assume one session a week with work in between, and they are ranges because the starting point matters more than the destination.

Two deserve expansion because they are the ones most often misdiagnosed. A student moving from MYP 5 into Diploma Year 12 is usually not behind on content; they are behind on timed-paper discipline, because five years of criterion-marked coursework rewards process and a Diploma paper rewards precision under a clock. Coaching that re-teaches content here is solving the wrong problem. And a student coming from IGCSE Core tier into Diploma Standard Level has a genuine content hole, because the Core syllabus excludes material the Diploma assumes, especially in mathematics and the sciences. That one is long, and it is the transition most likely to need fourteen weeks or more.

The CBSE to IGCSE move, which is frequent in Dubai, is a command-term and extended-writing problem rather than a mathematics problem. Students arrive numerate and lose marks on describe, explain and evaluate, and on the practical-paper technique that has no equivalent in their previous assessment. That responds quickly once it is named.

sections.heading: What a coaching progress report should contain
paragraphs: A coaching arrangement is accountable only if it reports in a form a parent can check. The standard offered across much of this market is a monthly message saying things are going well, which is indistinguishable from the message that would be sent if they were not. The alternative is not elaborate.

Four artefacts do the whole job. A marked script or marked piece of work after each session, annotated against the published mark scheme with marks allocated question by question. A short written summary after every fourth session, naming what was worked on, what moved and what did not. A criterion comment on any coursework draft, giving the criterion letter and the descriptor band the draft currently sits in. And at the ten-week point, two identical timed papers side by side so the comparison is arithmetic rather than opinion.

What makes these useful is that none of them requires subject knowledge to read. A parent who has never seen a chemistry mark scheme can still see that four marks went missing on three explain questions, and can still see whether the same thing happened again six weeks later. That is the whole point of insisting on artefacts instead of reassurance.

The table sets out the reporting rhythm. Anything a provider will not supply from that list is worth a direct question, because each item is a by-product of work that should be happening anyway. A tutor who is marking papers already has the marked papers.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and why it belongs in a coaching plan
paragraphs: Families coaching towards a UAE university place, or towards attestation of a certificate for use here, run into equivalency, and almost no page in this market mentions it. It belongs in a coaching conversation because it sets a floor under subject choices made two years earlier.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last point matters, because at least one ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the source read for this page, so none is published here: an IB family should check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly rather than rely on any tutoring website, including this one.

Two boundaries to state plainly. Equivalency and attestation are processes run by the Ministry and the attestation authorities, not something IB Gram performs, submits or guarantees. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission, or for school progression; anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Exam day, the centre, and the private candidate route
paragraphs: Coaching that stops at the content leaves a predictable gap on the day itself, and the logistics in Dubai have a few local features worth knowing before the week arrives.

The first is the zone timetable. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong one was used. A Dubai family should therefore take the timetable from their school's exams officer, not from a search result, and a coaching plan should be built against that document.

The second is the entry deadline, which sits months ahead of the paper and is the real decision point. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson International GCSE papers run in May/June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The third is the private candidate route, which matters for a student retaking a single subject, sitting a subject their school does not offer, or studying outside a school. Private entries go through an approved exam centre rather than through the board directly, and the centre sets its own earlier deadline and its own fee. A coaching plan for a private candidate should establish the centre before the teaching starts, because the entry window closes long before the student feels ready, and some centres do not accept private entries for every subject or component.

sections.heading: What coaching cannot fix
paragraphs: A useful coaching conversation includes the limits, and three of them are structural rather than a matter of effort.

The first is the tier ceiling. Cambridge Core entries are capped at grade C or 5, and the tier is fixed at entry, months before the paper. No amount of coaching in February converts a Core entry into an A*. If a student is working above the Core ceiling in October, the conversation that matters is with the school about changing the entry before the deadline, not with a tutor about extra hours. That is the single highest-value piece of advice on this page and it costs nothing.

The second is subject choice at Diploma level. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation lead to different university prerequisites, and a student in the wrong route is being coached uphill for two years. The decision point is Year 11, and the right people to involve are the school's Diploma coordinator and the universities on the shortlist, because prerequisites are published by course and change.

The third is the honesty boundary on assessed work. The student is the sole author of their Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay and Personal Project under IB rules. A coach reads the draft, names the criterion and the band, teaches referencing and uncertainty treatment, and reads again after the student has revised it. No tutor at IB Gram supplies sentences, finishes a draft or hands over a model answer to the same research question, and any provider in this market selling a completed Internal Assessment is selling a disciplinary risk that lands on the candidate. Board materials are cited and linked rather than reproduced, because syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB.

sections.heading: Staying on task: how an online coaching session is actually run
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online coaching is attention. A fourteen-year-old in a bedroom with a laptop has more exits than one in a centre with a teacher walking the room, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. What closes most of that gap is the format of the session rather than any monitoring software.

A session that works is almost entirely active. The student writes, on paper or on a shared whiteboard, and the writing is visible to the tutor as it happens. Questions are answered aloud and in writing rather than nodded at. Timed segments are run on a clock the tutor can see. A session built on the student producing work is self-policing in a way that a session built on explanation is not, which is why the marked-artefact rule is a pedagogical choice before it is a reporting one.

The practical arrangements matter too, and they are worth agreeing before the first paid session. The camera stays on. The student has a printed paper and a pen, because almost every assessment they will sit is handwritten and practising on a screen builds the wrong habits. Phones sit out of the room. The session happens somewhere with a door rather than at the kitchen table during dinner. And a parent is within earshot for the first two sessions, which tends to settle the question of engagement quickly for everyone.

What families should expect to hear if it is not working is the truth. If a student is not producing work between sessions, more sessions will not fix it, and the right conversation is about why rather than about frequency. That conversation is more productive at week four than at week fourteen, which is why the written summary arrives every fourth session.

process.title: Decide which problem you are buying for
process.description: Content not covered, or marks leaking despite the content being known. The first is cheap to solve and a group format handles it. The second needs a diagnostic and a marking cycle. Most students have a mix, and the sequence usually runs cheap format first, individual format second.

process.title: Hand over the calendar, not just the subject
process.description: The school's internal coursework deadlines, mock windows, the centre entry cut-off and any planned travel. Those dates set the cadence. A coaching plan built on the exam month alone will miss the deadlines that actually determine a Diploma or IGCSE result.

process.title: Free diagnostic session on a real past paper
process.description: A timed section, marked against the published mark scheme, returned annotated with a written three-session plan. No card is required. You end up holding a baseline that remains useful even if you choose a different provider afterwards.

process.title: Set the rhythm and the reporting standard in writing
process.description: Sessions per week, what gets marked between them, when the written summary arrives, and the date of the week-ten retest. Agreeing the reporting before the teaching starts is what makes the week-ten conversation short.

process.title: Review at week ten against the paired papers
process.description: Two identical timed papers side by side, the summaries, and the criterion comments on any coursework. Then choose: keep the rhythm, change it, change tutor, or stop. All four are legitimate, and all four are better from evidence than from an impression.

whyPoints.title: The plan is built on the Dubai calendar
whyPoints.description: Three terms from late August to late June, the winter and spring breaks, Ramadan wherever it falls, and the school's own internal deadlines. The exam month is the last date to be added, not the first, because it is rarely the one that binds.

whyPoints.title: Format is stated instead of implied
whyPoints.description: One-to-one over live video, with the batch and small-group alternatives described honestly alongside their published per-student rates. You can see what a cheaper format removes before you choose it, which is not how this market usually presents the choice.

whyPoints.title: Reporting is a by-product of the work
whyPoints.description: Marked work after each session, a written summary every fourth, a criterion comment per draft read, and paired timed papers at week ten. Nothing on that list requires extra effort from a tutor who is already marking, which is why it is reasonable to insist on it.

whyPoints.title: The limits are on the page
whyPoints.description: Tier ceilings fixed at entry, Diploma mathematics route choices made in Year 11, and the academic-honesty boundary on assessed work. Naming what coaching cannot do is what makes the rest of the claim credible.

whyPoints.title: Regulatory statements carry their source
whyPoints.description: Equivalency rules from the published July 2026 clarification, mandatory-subject rules from KHDA, the permit position from MoHRE's own guidance, and board dates from Cambridge and Pearson. No IB date appears, because the IB's own site is the only authority for those.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and availability are disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons run online on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram holds no UAE premises, runs no centre and does not make home visits in Dubai, which is an India-only service. Where a Higher Level subject has thin coverage, you are told the realistic match time rather than booked with a generalist.

faqs.question: Is IB IGCSE coaching the same thing as private tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and the word covers four different products here. A centre batch of eight to twenty students on a fixed syllabus timetable, a small group of three or four, a pair, and one-to-one work with a diagnostic and a marking cycle. Published per-student rates differ by roughly a factor of five across those formats. The distinction that matters is whether the arrangement can respond to evidence about your own child. A batch delivers content reliably and cannot follow one student's mark pattern; one-to-one can do the second and cannot spread the cost.

faqs.question: How many students should be in a coaching batch for it to work?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you want from it. Three or four students at the same board and level works genuinely well for diagram technique, command terms and shared content gaps, because those can be taught to several people at once. Eight to twenty works for syllabus delivery at the lowest cost per head. Above three or four, the individual diagnostic disappears, which is the thing that makes a session targeted rather than merely attended. If a batch is sold as personalised above four students, ask how the individual mark pattern is tracked and who does the marking.

faqs.question: How often should coaching run during term time in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Through Term 1, one session a week with one marked piece of work returned between sessions is usually right. From January in an exam year, two sessions a week works better than one longer one: one on content, one on timed papers, with the marking moving between them. In the final fortnight, three short sessions with no new content at all. The mechanism is spacing and marking turnaround rather than total hours. A paper sat on Sunday and returned marked before Wednesday produces a conversation about specific lost marks while the questions are still fresh.

faqs.question: What should a coaching progress report actually contain?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of which requires subject knowledge to read. A marked script after each session, annotated against the published mark scheme with marks shown per question. A short written summary every fourth session naming what moved and what did not. A criterion comment on any coursework draft, giving the criterion letter and the band the draft currently sits in. And at week ten, the week-one and week-ten timed papers side by side on the same question types. Every item on that list is a by-product of work a coach should be doing anyway.

faqs.question: Does coaching help a student moving from MYP into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided it targets the right gap. MYP 5 students arriving in Diploma Year 12 are usually not behind on content. They are behind on timed-paper discipline, because five years of criterion-marked coursework rewards process and research while a Diploma paper rewards precision against a mark scheme under a clock. Coaching that re-teaches content here solves the wrong problem and uses up a term. Eight to twelve weeks of timed sections, marked and discussed, with command-term work alongside, is the shape that usually fixes it before the first serious assessment.

faqs.question: My child is switching from CBSE to IGCSE in Year 10. What is the real gap?
faqs.answer: Almost never mathematics. Students arriving from CBSE are typically numerate and well drilled, and they lose marks on command terms, on extended written answers, and on practical-paper technique that has no equivalent in their previous assessment. Describe, explain and evaluate carry different mark allocations and are answered the same way until someone names the difference. Twelve to sixteen weeks of support is a realistic range, front-loaded on written technique rather than on content. The fastest single gain is usually learning to write an answer sized to the marks available.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a Dubai coaching timetable?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and the usable study window moves late, so weekly sessions shift to after Iftar, often from about 8.30pm, with session length commonly dropping while frequency holds. Because Ramadan moves against the Gregorian calendar, it can land close to a Cambridge March series or near the Diploma May session depending on the year. The practical response is to front-load content teaching into the weeks before it begins and keep the fasting weeks for paper review and marking discussion, which is lighter cognitive work for a similar mark return.

faqs.question: Can coaching fix a Core tier entry that should have been Extended?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most expensive misunderstanding in IGCSE coaching. Cambridge Core entries are capped at grade C or 5, and the tier is fixed when the centre lodges the entry, which for the March 2027 series falls on 27 November 2026. A student working above the Core ceiling in October needs a conversation with the school about changing the entry before that deadline, not extra tutoring hours in February. If the deadline has passed, the honest position is that the ceiling is set and the next decision is about a later series.

faqs.question: What are the UAE equivalency rules for an IGCSE student applying locally?
faqs.answer: The published requirements for the British track are that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no less than E or grade 3, and submits proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Equivalency is run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authorities, not by any tutoring provider, and it is not something a tutor performs or guarantees. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before making subject decisions on it.

faqs.question: Is Arabic counted in the five subjects the Ministry requires?
faqs.answer: No. The published clarification states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. That is worth knowing because at least one page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies remain mandatory in Dubai private schools alongside any licensed curriculum, so a student will study them regardless; they simply do not fill one of the five equivalency slots.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE exams as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Often yes, through an approved exam centre rather than through the board directly, and the practical constraints are worth knowing early. The centre sets its own entry deadline, earlier than the board's, and its own fee. Not every centre accepts private entries for every subject or every component, and practical or coursework components are the usual exclusions. A coaching plan for a private candidate therefore starts by confirming the centre and its deadline, because the entry window closes well before the student feels ready to sit the paper.

faqs.question: How long before an exam series should coaching start?
faqs.answer: For a full programme, the September before the series, which gives three terms and room for a baseline, a content phase, a coursework phase and a paper phase. For a targeted repair, ten to twelve weeks is enough to show measurable movement on the same question types. Under six weeks the plan has to become triage: a timed paper first, the two highest-yield topics, command-term and arithmetic drills throughout, and an explicit decision about what will not be revised. Starting late is worth doing; starting late while pretending otherwise is not.

faqs.question: Do coaching sessions cover Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses together?
faqs.answer: They can, provided the coach knows which one each subject is entered for. Many subject specialists work across both boards, and the difference lies in exam technique rather than in the physics or the algebra: formula provision, tiering, paper structure and command-term habits. Where it needs separate handling is the Pearson modular route in some subjects, which allows units to be sat in different series and banked, and which changes the whole cadence. If a school transfer has split your child across two boards, say so at the start so both timetables are planned together.

faqs.question: What happens if a coaching batch moves faster than my child?
faqs.answer: In a syllabus-paced batch, very little can be done inside it, because the timetable serves the group. That is the structural limit of the format rather than a failure of the teacher. The usual outcomes are that the student falls quietly behind while attending, or the family buys individual sessions alongside the batch and pays twice. The honest way to avoid it is to check before enrolling how a missed session is recovered, whether the batch is set by level, and what the provider does when one student is clearly off the pace.

faqs.question: How is an online coaching session supervised so my child stays on task?
faqs.answer: By the shape of the session rather than by monitoring software. The student writes throughout, on paper, visible to the tutor as it happens; timed segments run on a clock both can see; answers are given aloud and in writing rather than nodded at. A session built on producing work is largely self-policing. The arrangements agreed in advance matter too: camera on, phone out of the room, printed paper and pen, a room with a door, and a parent within earshot for the first two sessions. If work between sessions stops, more sessions are not the fix.

dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Set the rhythm before you buy the hours
dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.closingBody: Decide which problem you are solving: content that has not been covered, or marks leaking from content that has. Hand over the school calendar, including internal coursework deadlines and mock windows, because those are the dates a coaching plan has to hit. Take the free diagnostic session, which runs on a real past paper and leaves you holding a marked script and a written three-session plan. Then agree the cadence and the reporting standard in writing, and review at week ten against two identical papers. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Home tuition in Dubai is three products with one name
paragraphs: A parent typing home tuition into Google in Dubai gets quotes from a visiting tutor at AED 200 to AED 500 an hour, a tuition centre at AED 90 to AED 200 per student in a group, a centre one-to-one room at AED 150 to AED 350, and an online platform anywhere from AED 33 to AED 450 depending on who is teaching. Those are published figures read in October 2026, from Bestimate's Dubai rate table, from Unitors, EdFlik and Tutopiya's own pages, and from centre price lists advertised locally. The adverts use the same vocabulary. The products are not remotely the same.

The confusion costs money in a specific way. Families compare an hourly rate from one model against an hourly rate from another and pick the lower number, then discover the unit is different: a two-hour minimum on the visit, a fixed ten-week term at the centre, a package of eight sessions that expires at the end of the month. By the third invoice the cheaper option has become the more expensive one, and the school year is a term shorter than it was.

So this page costs the thing families actually buy, which is not an hour. It is two years: the start of Year 10 through to the day the results land, with a mock season, an internal assessment or coursework deadline, an entry deadline and an exam window inside it. Laid out that way the decisions change. Frequency matters more than rate, early matters more than intense, and the single biggest controllable cost is how late you start, because specialist availability thins about eight weeks before every exam series and prices firm with it.

The other thing a two-year view reveals is where tuition stops being the right purchase. A student two grades below target in three subjects does not need three tutors; they need a diagnosis and probably a conversation with the school about tier and option choices. A student at grade 7 chasing an 8 in one subject needs marked papers, not more teaching hours. Spending correctly inside the same budget is worth more than increasing it, and nothing on this page is designed to talk you into a larger plan than the evidence supports.

One limit stated plainly before you read further: IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE. Tuition here runs one to one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we offer only in India. Dubai's school fees happen to be flat this year, with KHDA confirming on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for 2026-27 under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, so tuition is the part of the education bill that is genuinely yours to plan.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tuition.programmesIntro: A two-year tuition budget looks different depending on which programme the money is funding, because the deadlines inside each one fall in different places.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear study assessed by terminal papers, with Cambridge offering Core and Extended routes and Pearson reporting across the 9-1 scale. The spending pattern is a slow start, a lift through the mock season in Year 11, and a concentrated block in the eight to ten weeks before the exam window.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai adds an entry-deadline wrinkle worth budgeting for. Where a school uses the Cambridge March series, final entries fall in late November for exams in February, so the decision point is in the autumn term. A family planning to start tuition in January for a March series is arriving after the tier decision has already been locked by the centre.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Internal assessment carries about a fifth of most subject grades. The cost shape is lumpy rather than even: quiet months, then intense weeks around each internal deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma families in Dubai routinely overspend in the first term and underspend in the second, which is the wrong way round. The expensive months are the ones containing an internal assessment deadline and the run-up to the final papers. Budget for short, frequent feedback sessions in those windows rather than a flat weekly hour across two years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, four criteria per subject scored from one to eight, with a personal project in the final year. Tuition at this stage is cheap per hour and the highest-return spending available, because it is buying habits rather than repairing grades.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one stage in Dubai where the lowest published band is often the correct purchase. A Year 8 student who needs routine, supervision and written structure does not need a board specialist at AED 300. Spending at the top of the market here and at the bottom of it in Year 11 is the most common budgeting error families make.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Cost per grade varies by subject because the work varies. Below is what the money buys in each, which is the useful way to decide where a limited tuition budget goes first.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The cheapest grade in the market to move, because most loss is method and exact form rather than knowledge. Expect visible change in three or four sessions, then a slower content phase. This is where a limited budget usually earns the most.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
subjects.description: Procedural topics respond quickly: balanced ionic equations, moles, titration data. Organic pathways take longer. A term of weekly work is the realistic unit here, not a pre-exam block.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Mark recovery sits in units, moments and six-mark causal answers. Technique-heavy, so cost per grade is low if started early and high if left until the final month, when the content gaps are no longer fixable.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and slow to shift, so this is the subject where a late start costs most. Budget a full term minimum, with the money going into data questions and command-term discipline rather than reteaching.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The work happens between sessions: the student writes, the tutor annotates. Pay for marking rather than for teaching hours here, which makes it unusually cheap to support if the provider sells feedback separately.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP SL or HL
subjects.description: Diagram and application drills produce fast, visible gains, so short blocks work. A six-session package aimed only at diagram accuracy is often better value than a term of general teaching.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most expensive subject to support late, because Higher Level assumes fluency from the first weeks. Three hours of audit in the summer before the course is the cheapest intervention available in the whole diploma.

subjects.name: Internal assessment and coursework support
subjects.description: Priced by the session rather than the term, and usually two or three short feedback conversations around a draft the student wrote. Costs little and protects a fifth of a subject grade, which is the best ratio on this page.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools, taught in separate streams under KHDA requirements. Tuition works through the school's own set content, since different or additional material needs prior ministry permission.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tuition.regionsIntro: Where you live changes the price of two of the three products on this page and not the third. The notes below say how, by cluster. All IB Gram sessions run over live video.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: The deepest local tutor pool in Dubai and the shortest drives, so visiting quotes sit mid-band and centre options are plentiful. Families here pay for minimum visit lengths they rarely need rather than for distance.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Serena
regions.note: Villa communities where visiting quotes reach the top of the published band and a tutor fits two bookings into an evening rather than four. The in-home premium across a two-year plan is the largest single avoidable line in the budget here.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Strong centre provision and long bus runs, so group tuition at AED 90 to 200 per student is the default local choice. Worth checking the ratio before signing a ten-week term, because the useful minutes per student change sharply above six.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and JBR
regions.note: Apartment living with good access to both centres and visiting tutors. The budget question here is usually frequency: two short sessions a week beat one long one for a student revising after 7pm.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Meydan
regions.note: Newer communities with growing Year 10 cohorts and fewer resident specialists. Quotes carry a distance element and availability thins first in the exam-term window, so early booking is a price decision.

regions.name: Dubai South, Jebel Ali and Emaar South
regions.note: The outer edge of in-home coverage, where the travel component of a quote is largest and the local pool smallest. A two-year plan built on visits costs materially more here than the same plan delivered over video.

regions.name: Town Square, Dubailand and The Valley
regions.note: Fast-growing families, new schools, few local tutors in scarce subjects. Centre classes fill early in the autumn term, which is when the sensible decision about the whole year gets made.

schoolClusters.city: Established British-curriculum cohorts
schoolClusters.note: Schools with large, tightly set Year 11 groups where a middle-set student aiming two grades up is the standard tuition case. Mock season in these schools sets the family budget for the rest of the year.

schoolClusters.note: Schools running a middle-years programme into a diploma, where tuition spending clusters around internal assessment deadlines rather than spreading evenly across the year. Budget for the lumps.

sections.heading: The three products sold as home tuition, decoded
paragraphs: Read any Dubai tuition advert and ask one question: what is the unit? A rate per hour, a rate per student per session, a monthly package, or a fixed term. The table sets the three real products against each other with the published rates and the unit each one actually bills in, which is where the comparison usually breaks down. A quoted AED 250 with a two-hour minimum costs more per session than a quoted AED 300 with no minimum, and no advert will point that out.

The centre model is the one most Dubai families misjudge. A group class at AED 120 per student is genuinely good value for a child who is behind on content and needs reteaching alongside others at the same point. It is poor value for a student at grade 6 chasing an 8, because the thing that student needs is their own work marked individually, which a fixed scheme of work for eight students cannot deliver. A centre with premises and staff also requires an educational services permit from KHDA, and asking about it is reasonable.

The visiting model bills in two-hour units because the trip has to be justified, and that one structural fact drives most of its cost. Online billing is the only one of the three where thirty minutes is a sensible purchase, which matters more than it sounds: a great deal of useful tuition is a short conversation about a draft or a marked paper, and in the other two models that conversation does not get sold at all.

sections.heading: Two years of tuition, costed stage by stage
paragraphs: Here is the plan families actually buy, laid out as the five stages it really has. The monthly figures are Bestimate's published 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session: AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Read the last column first, because each stage should produce something you can hold, and a stage that produces nothing checkable is a stage to stop paying for.

The shape matters more than the total. Spending evenly across twenty-four months is the most common pattern and not the best one. The high-value months are the first term of Year 10, where habits are set cheaply; the mock season, where the diagnosis is sharpest; and the eight to ten weeks before the exam window, where timed practice converts knowledge into marks. The low-value months are the quiet middles, where a weekly hour often becomes supervised homework at specialist prices.

One line in the table is the one families skip and later regret: the audit in the summer between courses. Three hours with a subject specialist checking what the International GCSE course actually covered against what the next course assumes costs less than a fortnight of catch-up in November. It is also when the honest conversation about whether a subject should be taken at Higher Level can still change something. One further note on the table: the marking-only option in the second row is the least used and best value line in this market. A student in the quiet middle of Year 10 who sends in two papers a fortnight and gets them back annotated keeps the diagnostic running at a fraction of a weekly teaching rate, and arrives at the mock season with a record rather than an impression.
