sections.heading: Packages, minimum terms and the small print that decides the bill
paragraphs: Packages are cheaper per hour and more expensive in practice, for one reason: expiry. A package of eight sessions inside a calendar month assumes eight usable weeks, and a Dubai school year contains half terms, exam weeks, travel, Ramadan and illness. Families routinely pay for sessions they cannot take, which turns an advertised AED 799 for eight into a real AED 799 for five. Ask whether unused sessions roll forward, and get the answer in writing rather than in a conversation.

The second clause worth reading is the cancellation window. Twenty-four hours sounds reasonable until the window falls across a Friday and Saturday, which in practice means notice by Thursday evening. The third is the minimum term: some providers sell ten-week blocks and some require a month's notice to stop, which is a different thing from an hourly rate. The fourth is the rate for a short session, because if thirty minutes is billed as an hour, draft feedback becomes uneconomic exactly when it is most useful.

Then there is tax. Whether tuition fees carry value added tax in the UAE is not something a tutoring page should assert without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and this one will not. What you are entitled to ask any provider is whether the dirham figure quoted is the amount you will be charged, whether a tax registration number applies to the invoice, and whether package prices differ from single-session prices. A provider who cannot answer those three questions in one message is a provider whose invoices will keep surprising you.
bullets: Ask whether unused package sessions roll forward, and for how long
Ask what the cancellation window is in practice across a Dubai weekend

sections.heading: What starting late actually costs
paragraphs: The most expensive decision in this market is not choosing the wrong provider. It is starting in March for a May or June window. Two things happen at once: the work available is narrower, because content gaps can no longer be closed and only technique can be drilled; and the supply of specialists tightens across the whole emirate, because every other family has reached the same conclusion in the same fortnight.

The arithmetic is unkind. One hour a week from September across an academic year is roughly thirty-two hours. An eight-week intensive at two hours a week is sixteen, bought at the specialist end of the band in the busiest month of the year, with no marked history to target it. The intensive costs a similar amount of money for half the teaching and a much narrower set of options, and it is the only route left for a family who waited for mock results before acting.

There is a cheaper version of urgency. If the mocks are three months away and you do not know whether tuition is needed, buy a diagnosis rather than a term: two or three sessions whose only job is to produce a ranked list of mark-loss causes from your child's own work. That costs a fraction of a package, frequently shows that one subject needs help rather than three, and occasionally shows that nothing needs buying at all beyond a conversation with the school about tier.

sections.heading: Group ratios and the price of a useful minute
paragraphs: Group tuition is priced per student, which makes it look like a straightforward discount. The better way to judge it is per minute of individual attention, because that is the ingredient a student at grade 6 needs to reach 8. In a group of two, a sixty-minute lesson gives each student a large share of the teacher's responses. In a group of twelve, the same hour gives each student a few minutes, and the rest is delivery that a recording could provide.

That does not make large groups useless. For reteaching content, a well-run class of eight with a strong scheme of work is excellent value and better than a weak one-to-one hour. What it cannot do is mark your child's script, find the specific errors in it and drill those, which is the work that closes the last two grades. The honest rule is that groups buy content coverage and one-to-one buys error correction, and most Dubai families need the second more than they think.

Ask the centre two questions before signing a term: the actual maximum ratio, not the target, and how many pieces of individually marked work your child will receive across the term. If the answer to the second is none, the class is a course rather than tuition, and it should be priced and judged as one. Centres running premises in Dubai also need an educational services permit from KHDA, obtained in stages with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

sections.heading: The costs that sit beyond tuition
paragraphs: A two-year budget has lines in it that no tuition provider mentions. The first is exam entry where a student sits as a private candidate, which happens more often in Dubai than families expect: a mid-year arrival, an extra subject the school does not offer, or a single-subject resit. Entries go through a centre, the centre sets its own charge per subject per series, and the deadline is the board's rather than the centre's convenience. Neither Pearson nor Cambridge publishes a candidate-facing price.

The second is the resit itself, which is cheaper than it looks for Pearson candidates because there are two series a year. Pearson's November window ran from late October to 19 November in 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a disappointing summer need not cost a school year. Cambridge candidates in Dubai schools using the March series face final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, which puts the decision in the autumn.

The third is equivalency paperwork for families who will need a UAE certificate recognised. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE level at grade E or 3 or better, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. That is a regulatory process run by the authorities, not something a tutoring provider performs, charges for or expedites. Verify your own case through the official channel.

sections.heading: What tuition cannot buy, at any price
paragraphs: Three things are for sale in this market that should not be, and knowing them protects a budget as much as any rate table. The first is a grade. No provider can promise a number, and any page that does is selling confidence rather than teaching. What an honest provider can do is name the three things costing marks after a fortnight and estimate how long each takes to fix, which is a forecast you can check against marked work rather than a promise.

The second is finished coursework. Internal assessment, the extended essay and coursework components must be the student's own work, and one provider in this search result sells completed internal assessments outright. The consequence of that transaction lands on the student as a malpractice finding, not on the seller. Legitimate support means teaching what the criteria reward, modelling technique on other material, and responding to a draft the student wrote in their own words.

The third is a regulatory shortcut. Nobody in this market can accelerate ministry equivalency, influence a grade boundary, obtain unreleased papers, or arrange a school place. We also do not distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link to the boards' own pages. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. Nor will anyone here describe a tutor as a current examiner, because examiner status cannot be evidenced to a parent and would not give a tutor access to anything useful if it could. Where a page in this market leans on that claim to justify a rate, the honest question to ask is what it changes about the hour you are buying.
bullets: No grade promises, no refund tied to an outcome, no score guarantee
No written, redrafted or completed assessed work, at any price
No regulatory shortcuts and no influence over boundaries or entries
No board materials redistributed as files: we cite and link instead

sections.heading: Nine questions to send any Dubai tuition provider
paragraphs: Comparing quotes in this market is hard because providers describe different products in identical language. The fastest way through it is a list of questions sent verbatim to each one, because the answers are short and the differences become obvious immediately. Copy the list below into a message and send it unchanged to three providers, including us. A provider who will not answer in writing has told you something useful at no cost.

Note what the questions are doing. Four of them establish the unit being billed, which is where comparisons usually fail. Three establish what you receive between sessions, which is the difference between teaching and attendance. Two establish compliance: the private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 for an individual tutor, and the educational services permit for any provider running premises in Dubai.

Then apply one test at four weeks, whichever provider you choose. You should be able to name the three things costing your child marks, point at them in marked work, and say which are technique and which are content. If the available evidence is only that the sessions feel positive, the money is buying company at specialist rates. That test costs nothing and it is the only one in this market that has ever predicted a grade change. Send the list to three providers rather than two, and include at least one model you had not considered: a centre class, a marking-only arrangement, an online specialist. The replies tend to cluster, and the one that answers every question in plain sentences with numbers attached is usually the one worth a first lesson.
bullets: What is the unit: per hour, per session, per month, per term?
What is the minimum session length, and the rate for thirty minutes?
Do unused package sessions roll forward, and for how long?
What is the cancellation notice, and how does it fall across the Dubai weekend?
What do I receive between sessions, in writing?
Which exact specification code and level has this tutor taught?
Does your tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit?
Is the quoted dirham figure the final amount on the invoice?
What happens if the match does not work after two sessions?

process.title: Start with the subject that moves cheapest
process.description: Tell us which subjects are short of target and by how much. If the budget only covers one, we will usually point at mathematics or a procedural science first, because those move fastest per hour, and say honestly when a subject needs a term rather than a block.

process.title: A free first lesson before any arrangement
process.description: One full lesson with the proposed tutor at no charge, with no card details taken. Nothing is purchased at that point and no package exists. It is there so the first money you spend follows an hour you have already watched rather than a profile you have read.

process.title: Buy a diagnosis, not a term
process.description: Two or three sessions whose only output is a ranked list of mark-loss causes from your child's own work, with each cause labelled content, method or timing. That list often shows one subject needs help rather than three, which is the cheapest discovery available here.

process.title: Agree a shape, by the session
process.description: With the list in hand we propose a shape: weekly for a term, fortnightly marking only, or a defined block before a deadline. Sessions are billed as they happen, so nothing expires unused and changing tutor costs you no balance.

process.title: Review at mocks and eight weeks out
process.description: The plan changes twice a year whether anyone schedules it or not: after mocks, and eight to ten weeks before an exam window. We raise both, including the version where the answer is fewer hours, and we book the exam-term block early because availability goes first.

whyPoints.title: Billed by the session, not by the month
whyPoints.description: Nothing expires. A Dubai school year has half terms, travel, exam weeks and Ramadan in it, and monthly packages quietly charge for the sessions those weeks remove. Paying as you go is slightly more per hour and usually less in total.

whyPoints.title: Thirty minutes is a real booking
whyPoints.description: Much of the most valuable tuition is short: a marked paper discussed, a draft read against the criteria. The visiting model cannot sell that because of the drive, and the centre model cannot timetable it. Over video it is routine.

whyPoints.title: The whole budget, not the hourly rate
whyPoints.description: We will talk about what two years costs and where the high-value months are, including the months where the right advice is to stop paying. An hourly rate is the least informative number in this market.

whyPoints.title: No package before a lesson
whyPoints.description: The free first lesson comes first, then a diagnosis, then a shape. No minimum term, no commitment ahead of evidence, and no balance to lose if you want a different tutor in week three.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, said plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. We hold no regulator or examination-board accreditation and make no such claim.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you can hold
whyPoints.description: Annotated work keyed to the board's mark-scheme language, plus a short written note after each session. That is what makes the four-week test possible, and the four-week test is the only reliable way to judge whether tuition is worth its price.

faqs.question: What does home tuition cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published monthly figures read in October 2026 put a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, 600 to 1,200 mid-market and 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, on Bestimate's 2026 estimates. Advertised Dubai packages included AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' figures. The important question is not the monthly number but the unit it bills in, because an eight-session month assumes eight usable weeks and a school year rarely offers them.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package cheaper than paying for each session?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, often more expensive in total. The reason is expiry: a package assumes a run of usable weeks, and a Dubai school year contains half terms, exam weeks, travel and Ramadan. Families regularly pay for eight sessions and take five. Before buying one, ask whether unused sessions roll forward and for how long, what the cancellation window is in practice across a Friday and Saturday, and whether there is a minimum term. If the answers are vague, pay by the session until the match and the frequency are both proven.

faqs.question: What is a realistic total tuition budget for Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: Think in stages rather than totals. One weekly hour in one subject from the start of Year 10, using published mid-band monthly estimates of AED 600 to 1,200, plus a heavier two-hour pattern in the eight to ten weeks before the exam window at the specialist band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month, is the common shape. Families who front-load cheaply and spend harder in the exam term get more for the same money than families who spread evenly, because the early hours set habits and the late hours convert knowledge into marks.

faqs.question: Do tuition rates in Dubai rise closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, though usually through availability rather than through a published increase. In the eight weeks before a Pearson or Cambridge window, the specialists are booked, the remaining options sit at the upper end of the band, and families accept a weaker subject match because nothing else is free. The same tutor booked in September costs the published rate and has space to plan. Treat early booking as a price strategy, not just an organisational habit, and book any exam-term block before the mock results arrive.

faqs.question: Can we pause tuition over the school holidays and keep the slot?
faqs.answer: With a session-billed arrangement, yes, and the slot can usually be held for a few weeks by agreement. With a package or a fixed term, often not, which is one of the reasons packages cost more than they appear to. The more useful question is whether you should pause at all. Students who stop entirely in July arrive in September having lost fluency in algebra, and the first three sessions of the new year go on buying it back. One session a fortnight through a long break is cheaper than that.

faqs.question: If a package month ends with three sessions unused, what happens to them?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the provider, and it is the single clause worth reading before signing anything. Some packages roll unused sessions into the next month, some roll them for a fixed window, and some expire them at month end. Centres with fixed terms rarely refund a missed class. Ask for the rule in writing, not in a conversation, and keep the message. With a session-billed arrangement the question does not arise, because nothing is bought before it happens.

faqs.question: Is group tuition worth it at half the price of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends on what your child needs. Groups buy content coverage; one-to-one buys error correction. For a student who is behind and needs reteaching, a well-run class of six at AED 100 to 200 per student is strong value and better than a weak private hour. For a student at grade 6 chasing an 8, what closes the gap is their own script marked and the specific errors drilled, and a group of eight on one scheme of work cannot do that. Ask the centre the actual maximum ratio and how many individually marked pieces your child will get.

faqs.question: How many tuition hours a week is too many?
faqs.answer: Past about three hours a week across all subjects, most students stop converting hours into marks and start losing the time they need to do the work the tutor set. Tuition only pays if there is space between sessions for marked practice. Two hours a week plus an hour of marked work is usually better than four hours of teaching. If a provider's answer to a disappointing mock is more hours rather than a sharper diagnosis, that is a signal about the provider rather than about your child.

faqs.question: Is there an extra charge for coursework or draft feedback?
faqs.answer: Ask, because this is where billing models differ most. Some providers treat draft feedback as a separate service at a separate rate; others include short feedback conversations in the hourly arrangement. With sessions billed by the half hour, a thirty-minute conversation about a draft costs thirty minutes and nothing more. What should never appear on any invoice is writing, restructuring or completing an assessed piece: the work must be the student's own, and the consequence of crossing that line falls on the student.

faqs.question: Who pays the exam entry fee if my child sits as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: You do, and you pay it to the centre rather than to the board. Entries are made by a centre registered to accept external candidates, the centre sets its own charge per subject per series, and the deadline is the board's published one. Neither Pearson nor Cambridge publishes a candidate-facing price list, so collect quotes from more than one centre and ask what the charge includes. Tuition providers do not handle entries, and any provider who implies they can lodge one for you has misunderstood the process.

faqs.question: Is private tuition subject to VAT in the UAE?
faqs.answer: This page will not state the tax treatment of tuition as fact, because doing so without a Federal Tax Authority citation would be irresponsible on a page families use to plan a budget. What you can and should require from any provider is three plain answers: whether the dirham figure quoted is the amount that will appear on the invoice, whether a tax registration number applies, and whether package pricing differs from single-session pricing. Get those in writing before the first payment and the question stops mattering to your budget.

faqs.question: Can we start with one subject and add another later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually the right order. Starting with the subject furthest from target, or the one that moves cheapest, gives you a working relationship and a marked baseline before the budget widens. Mathematics and the procedural parts of chemistry tend to move fastest per hour; content-heavy biology and essay subjects take longer. Adding a second subject after a term also lets you judge the first properly, because by then you are looking at marked work rather than at an impression of how the sessions went.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to move a grade up by one?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis first, then technique, then content, in that order. Two or three sessions to find out where the marks are going usually reveals that one or two habits are costing most of the gap: method not written down, exact form ignored, command terms misread, or a diagram not shifted. Those habits install in a handful of sessions and they cost very little. Content gaps are the expensive part and they take a term. Buying teaching before diagnosis is how families spend a term's budget fixing something that was not the problem.

faqs.question: Is this tuition delivered at our Dubai address or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one to one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen both people write on. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. If your child genuinely needs an adult physically present, this is not the right provider and the question list in the last section is the useful part of the page for you. What online delivery buys is the specialist who teaches your child's exact specification, at an hour that suits a Dubai evening, with no travel in the price.

faqs.question: How do I compare two quotes that look identical?
faqs.answer: Put both on the same unit. Convert each to the real cost of one usable session: add the minimum length, the distance element, the package expiry and the cancellation risk. A quoted AED 250 with a two-hour minimum is AED 500 a session; a quoted AED 300 with no minimum and a thirty-minute option is cheaper in practice. Then compare what arrives between sessions in writing, and whether the tutor has taught your child's exact specification code. Those two columns decide outcomes; the headline rate rarely does.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tuition.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis first, then the plan
dubai/ib-igcse-home-tuition.closingBody: If you read one section of this page twice, make it the two-year table. Tuition is a plan, not an hour, and the families who get most from the same budget are the ones who spend early and cheaply on habits, buy a real diagnosis before committing to a term, and book the exam-term block before everyone else does. Send us the subjects, the year group, the specification codes and what the next assessed piece is. The first lesson is free with no card details taken, sessions are billed as they happen, and everything runs one to one over live video.

intro.heading: The home-tutor question, answered with numbers rather than a sales pitch
paragraphs: Start with the market as it is. Independent home tutors in Dubai advertise AED 200 to AED 500 an hour, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table for the emirate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350. Published online rates for a qualified subject teacher sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 at the student-tutor end and Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Monthly packages advertised here in October 2026 included AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits and AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other people's numbers, dated and attributed, and they are the only honest starting point for this conversation.

The gap between the two columns is not a quality gap. It is a travel gap. A tutor who drives from Al Barsha to Arabian Ranches at six in the evening spends the better part of an hour unpaid, cannot take a booking either side of yours, and prices all of that into the sixty minutes they are actually teaching. Dubai makes this worse than most cities because the good school clusters and the villa communities sit at opposite ends of Al Khail Road, and the hours when a fifteen-year-old can work are exactly the hours the road is full.

So the right question is not whether a home tutor is better. It is what the premium buys. In honest cases it buys three real things: a child who concentrates better with an adult physically present, a parent who can see the session happening, and a household where a laptop and a quiet room are genuinely not available. Those are legitimate reasons and worth paying for. What the premium does not buy is a better subject match, and for International GCSE and Diploma work that is usually the variable that decides the grade.

Here is the limit, stated early because it matters: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tutoring for families here is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. That rules us out for a family who specifically needs an adult in the room, and we would rather you knew that in the first paragraph than in the fourth email. What it buys you instead is reach: a 4PM1 specialist or a Higher Level chemistry teacher is available to a family in Dubai South on the same terms as to a family in Jumeirah, because nobody is driving.

The rest of this page breaks the in-home rate into its components, compares the four realistic ways to buy tutoring in Dubai with the published rate for each, explains why a twenty-minute radius shrinks the tutor pool so sharply for scarce subjects, sets out the permit and safeguarding questions that apply to anyone entering a private home, maps the evening slots against what the city is doing at each hour, and ends with a checklist for hiring a visiting tutor well if that is still the route you want.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Families searching for a home tutor in Dubai are usually buying help with one of three things: the exam course at 16, the diploma that follows it, or the middle-years run-up. The cost pattern differs across all three.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear study ending in terminal papers, with Cambridge splitting many subjects into Core and Extended and Pearson reporting on the 9-1 scale. This is the biggest single block of tutoring demand in Dubai, and the one where published market rates are easiest to compare, because almost every provider quotes a rate for it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai in-home pricing for International GCSE clusters at the lower end of the published band in the dense school corridors and at the upper end for outer communities, because the distance is the variable. The same tutor online costs the same wherever you live, which is why the outer communities are where the online case is strongest rather than weakest.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two years, three at Higher Level, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Internal assessment carries about a fifth of most subject grades, and much of the tutoring value sits in draft feedback between sessions rather than in the session itself.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the in-home model struggles most in Dubai. Diploma support is often a thirty-minute conversation about a draft, two days before a school deadline, at nine at night. Nobody drives across the emirate for thirty minutes, so visiting tutors sell two-hour blocks the student does not need, while a video call that length is routine.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, each subject marked against four criteria scored from one to eight, with a personal project in the final year. Tutoring at this stage is mostly about study habits, written structure and the mathematics that later blocks diploma choices.
programmes.countryNote: Rates for middle-years support in Dubai sit at the lower end of every published band, and this is the one case where a local tutor who lives in your community can be the best-value option: a Year 8 student needs supervision and routine more than specialist knowledge, and a short walk costs nobody anything.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: The other post-16 route in Dubai British-curriculum schools, examined in units across the May/June and October/November series, graded A* to E. Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires at least one Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level.
programmes.countryNote: A Level specialists in minority subjects are the clearest illustration of the pool problem. Further mathematics, physics and economics specialists are thin on the ground in any single Dubai community, and a family insisting on a visitor is choosing from whoever is within range rather than from whoever teaches the subject best.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Dubai families most often want a tutor in the house for, with a note on what the hour is actually spent doing. Where the work is marking and feedback rather than live teaching, the travel premium buys nothing at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-demand subject in the emirate and the one where in-home rates are quoted most often. The hour is worked problems and marked method, both of which happen identically on a shared screen with a graphics tablet. Exact form and visible working are where the marks are.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Diagram work, moments, electrical circuits and six-mark causal explanations. The practical component is Cambridge's separate paper or Pearson's in-paper questions, and both are answer-style problems rather than laboratory problems, so neither needs a tutor in the room.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis, rates and organic pathways. The fastest recoveries are procedural: balanced ionic equations with charges and state symbols, and reading titration data correctly. These respond to repetition with immediate marking, which is what a one-to-one hour is for.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where students plateau at grade 6 by rereading notes. The grade comes back through data questions, describing before explaining, and command-term discipline. Written feedback between sessions matters more here than the session length.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: First Language, Specification A, DP SL and HL
subjects.description: Essay subjects where the real work happens between lessons: the student writes, the tutor annotates, the next session discusses the annotations. A two-hour visit is the wrong unit for this, and it is the clearest case where the visiting model costs more and delivers less.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP SL or HL
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and application to the stimulus material. Marked diagrams returned with corrections drive the grade, and diagram drills work well in a shared document. Dubai students with strong general knowledge lose marks by answering with examples instead of models.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The post-16 step most Dubai families underestimate. Content is familiar from Extended or Higher tier; the mathematical prose style an exploration demands is not. Specialists at Higher Level are scarce in any one community, which is the pool argument in its sharpest form.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside mainstream maths by students heading for a mathematical degree route. Very few tutors in any Dubai community teach it, so insisting on a visitor usually means accepting a general maths tutor instead of a specialist.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum, taught in classes separate from the Arab first-language stream under KHDA requirements. Tutoring works through the school's own set content, since additional or different material needs prior ministry permission for these subjects.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: What changes between Dubai communities on an in-home booking is distance, and distance is the entire premium. The notes below describe how the travel economics work in each cluster. Every IB Gram session runs over live video, so none of this applies to us.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Damac Hills
regions.note: Villa communities a long way from the school corridors where most tutors live. Quoted in-home rates sit at the top of the published band here, and a tutor can usually fit only two visits into an evening instead of three.

regions.name: Dubai South, Jebel Ali and Emaar South
regions.note: The furthest reach of in-home coverage in the emirate. Families here report the fewest options and the highest quotes, which makes this the clearest case in Dubai for buying the subject specialist online instead.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Dense, apartment-based and close to several school clusters, so visiting rates are competitive and availability is good. The thing a visitor cannot fix here is a scarce subject: proximity does not create a further maths teacher.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Eastern Dubai with long bus routes, so students get home late and the usable slots are 6pm onward. A tutor crossing from the western school corridor at that hour is pricing the worst traffic of the day into your invoice.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: The deepest local tutor pool in the emirate and the only cluster where a visiting tutor is routinely a short drive away. In-home quotes here cluster mid-band, and families still pay a minimum visit length they often do not need.

regions.name: Dubailand, Town Square and The Valley
regions.note: Fast-growing communities with new schools and few resident tutors. Quoted rates carry a distance premium, and the subjects most in demand in exam year are exactly the ones nobody local teaches.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown and DIFC
regions.note: Working parents and late evenings. The genuine advantage of a video session here is that a 9pm half hour about a coursework draft is possible at all, which no visiting tutor will sell you.

schoolClusters.city: Western school corridor
schoolClusters.note: Most of Dubai's established British-curriculum schools sit along the Al Sufouh, Umm Suqeim and Barsha band, and most resident tutors live within reach of it. That geography is why in-home quotes rise with every kilometre eastward or southward from this line.

schoolClusters.city: Outer villa and new-town communities
schoolClusters.note: Schools serving Ranches, Dubai Hills, Dubailand and the southern communities draw families who face the widest gap between in-home and online quotes for identical teaching. These are the households this page is really written for.

sections.heading: What you are actually paying for in an in-home hour
paragraphs: An in-home booking bundles at least six separate costs into one number, and most quotes do not break them out. The table below does. The base teaching rate is the part you want; everything under it is logistics. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500, against AED 150 to AED 300 online for a qualified subject teacher.

The component families most underestimate is the minimum visit. Two hours is the standard unit for a Dubai home visit because an hour of teaching does not justify an hour of driving. That turns a quoted AED 250 rate into a real unit cost of AED 500 per session, whether or not your child can concentrate usefully for the second hour. A fifteen-year-old working on exact form in algebra is spent after about fifty minutes; the second hour is frequently homework supervision at specialist prices.

The second is the scarcity premium. A tutor asked to reach Dubai South, Jebel Ali or outer Dubailand prices the trip accordingly, and in practice the family either pays the top of the band or takes whoever is available locally. Both outcomes cost something: one in dirhams, the other in subject match. Online, distance stops being a variable at all, which is why the strongest financial case for video sessions in this emirate is made in exactly the communities furthest from the school corridor.

sections.heading: Four ways to buy tutoring in Dubai, priced side by side
paragraphs: Comparison tables on tutoring sites usually compare the seller against an unnamed competitor. This one compares models, with the published rate for each and the party that published it, so you can check it. Read the last two columns first, because they are the ones that decide outcomes: how large a pool of tutors the model gives you access to, and what the hour actually includes.

The tuition centre group class is the option Dubai parents misjudge most often in both directions. At AED 90 to 200 per student it is genuinely good value for a child who is behind on content and needs reteaching with other students at the same point. It is poor value for a student sitting at grade 6 aiming at 8, because what that student needs is their own work marked, and a group of eight moving at one pace cannot do it. A centre with premises and staff also needs an educational services permit from KHDA, which is a fair thing to ask about.

The pool column is where the real argument sits. An in-home booking draws from tutors who can reach your community in the usable evening window. Online draws from everyone teaching that specification. For mainstream Year 10 maths the difference rarely matters. For further pure mathematics, Higher Level chemistry or a diploma economics draft, it decides whether you get a specialist or a generalist, and that difference shows up in the first marked paper rather than in the conversation.

sections.heading: Why a twenty-minute radius shrinks the tutor pool
paragraphs: This is the part of the in-home decision that nobody prices, because it does not appear on an invoice. When you require a tutor to be physically present, you are not choosing from the tutors who teach your child's subject. You are choosing from the intersection of two sets: people who teach the subject, and people who can be in your community during the two or three hours when a teenager can work. In Dubai, after the school run and before dinner, that intersection is small.

For mainstream subjects it barely matters. Year 10 mathematics, Year 11 biology and GCSE-level English are taught by enough people in this emirate that proximity costs you little. The problem begins at the edges, which is exactly where exam-year families need help: further pure mathematics, Higher Level chemistry, diploma economics with a key-concept evaluation problem, Arabic first language for a student who moved from a non-Arab stream, or a Pearson specification where the school entered a code the local tutor has never taught.

The outcome is predictable and it is why so many Dubai families change tutors in January. A parent hires the best available nearby person in September, the match is adequate for a term, and then the work gets specific and the tutor cannot follow it. Changing tutors mid-year costs four to six weeks of relationship-building during the most expensive weeks of the year. Picking the specialist first and accepting that the specialist is on a screen avoids the whole sequence.

sections.heading: Who is entering your home, and what you should check
paragraphs: If you do hire a visiting tutor, the checks matter more than the rate, and this market does not make them easy. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any page quoting a figure.

There is a specific case worth knowing before you ask a favour of your child's own teacher. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct addressing the same conflict. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so confirm the current position with the school. The convenient arrangement is sometimes the non-compliant one, and the person exposed is the teacher.

The third check is data. A tutoring arrangement collects information about a child: school, year group, marks, sometimes photographs of work. Under the UAE's personal data protection law you are entitled to know what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted, and any provider should be able to answer that in writing. Ask also for identification, for confirmation of the permit, and for a reference you can actually telephone. A tutor who finds those questions unreasonable has answered them.
bullets: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit and matching identification
Check whether the tutor teaches at your child's own school, and what their employer's rules say
Get the cancellation notice period and the minimum visit length in writing
Ask what personal data is kept about your child and how to have it removed

sections.heading: The Dubai evening, slot by slot
paragraphs: Scheduling is the hidden half of this decision. A tutoring plan that ignores what the city is doing at each hour fails in about three weeks, whichever delivery model you choose. The table maps the realistic windows, what is happening across the emirate in each, who each one suits and where it goes wrong. Note that every one of these slots is available for a video session, while a visiting tutor can only sell you the ones they can physically reach.

Two patterns are worth planning around specifically. The after-school slot is the cheapest and calmest, and in apartment communities close to school it is genuinely usable. In eastern Dubai and the outer villa communities, where bus runs are long, a 4pm start means a child who walked in ten minutes earlier and has eaten nothing. The 6pm to 7.30pm band is therefore the most contested in the emirate, which is also why specialist availability in it thins first.

Ramadan deserves explicit planning rather than improvisation. School hours compress, families eat late, and revision moves into the night. Sessions can be rescheduled to post-Iftar timings, and a family that agrees this with a tutor in advance keeps continuity through a month where most tutoring quietly stops. For a Year 11 student with a May or June series ahead, losing four weeks in the spring is the single most expensive scheduling mistake available. The same applies to the long summer: students who stop entirely in July arrive in September having forgotten the algebra they were fluent in, and the first three sessions of the new year are spent buying it back.

sections.heading: Siblings, splitting an hour and where the savings actually are
paragraphs: Families with two or three children in exam years ask about shared sessions more than any other question on cost, and the answer depends on how far apart the children are. Two students in the same subject and the same year can share an hour productively, because the material is identical and one explanation serves both. Two students two years apart cannot: the hour becomes two half-lessons, each with an audience, and both children lose the thing they came for.

In the in-home market the economics push families towards sharing whether or not it suits the children, because the trip has to be justified. A visiting tutor quoted at AED 300 with a two-hour minimum is a strong incentive to put both children in the room. Online, two consecutive single hours cost two single hours, so the decision can be made on what each child needs rather than on what the travel requires. That is a small structural point with a large effect on whether the younger child gets anything out of the year.

The real savings in this market are in frequency and shape, not in sharing. One hour a week sustained from September across Year 10 and 11 costs roughly what an eight-week intensive before the exam costs, and buys far more, because it produces marked evidence the whole way through. Bestimate's monthly figures for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, 600 to 1,200 mid-market and 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, which is the arithmetic to plan against.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost against the rest of the Dubai education bill
paragraphs: Tutoring sits in a household budget that already carries school fees, transport and activities, so the useful comparison is annual rather than hourly. Dubai gives one fixed point to plan against: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are flat this year. Tutoring is the part of the bill that moves.

Set the published monthly figures against that. An advertised Dubai online package ran at AED 799 a month for eight sessions in October 2026; the in-home equivalent advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those two packages contain a similar amount of teaching. The difference is roughly the price of a car on the road four evenings a week, and it is the cleanest single illustration of what the visiting model costs a Dubai family across a school year.

Supply matters too, because Dubai keeps adding schools. KHDA reported seven new private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More Year 10 and Year 11 cohorts each year means more demand on the same pool of specialist tutors in the eight weeks before each exam series. Booking early is a price strategy as much as an organisational one, in whichever model you choose.

sections.heading: If you still want someone in the room, hire well
paragraphs: Plenty of good reasons exist for wanting a tutor physically present, and a page that pretended otherwise would be worth less than this one. A twelve-year-old who will not engage with a screen, a household without a quiet room, a parent who needs to see the lesson happening: these are real, and in those cases the premium is money well spent. IB Gram cannot help you there, because we do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE and we are not going to pretend otherwise to win a booking.

So here is how to buy it well. Ask for the specification code the tutor has taught, not the subject. Ask for one marked piece of a previous student's work with the mark scheme alongside, anonymised. Ask what you receive between sessions, because a visiting tutor who leaves no written record is selling attendance. Fix the cancellation notice, the minimum length and the rate for a short session in writing before the first visit, and agree what happens in Ramadan and over the summer.

Then test the match on output rather than on rapport. Four weeks in, you should be able to name the three things costing your child marks and see them in marked work. If after a month the only evidence is that the sessions feel positive, you are paying specialist rates for company. That test is identical whether the tutor arrives at a Dubai address or appears on a screen, and it is the only one that has ever predicted a grade change.

faqs.question: How much does an in-home IGCSE tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500 depending on subject, level and how far they have to drive. Advertised monthly in-home packages ran at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. For comparison, a qualified subject teacher online is published at AED 150 to AED 300. Those are market figures from other providers, not an IB Gram price list; our rate is agreed per match after a free first lesson.

faqs.question: Why does the same tutor cost more in my house than on a screen?
faqs.answer: Because you are funding the journey as well as the lesson. A tutor driving from the western school corridor to a villa community in the evening loses most of an hour each way, cannot take a booking either side of yours, and pays for fuel, tolls and parking. All of that goes into your hourly figure. There is also an opportunity cost: four online sessions fit into an evening where two visits do. None of this reflects better teaching, which is why the published online and in-home bands overlap at the quality end.

faqs.question: Is the tutor's travel time billed as teaching time?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is the question worth asking before the first visit rather than after the first invoice. Some Dubai tutors quote a flat rate with travel absorbed, some add a distance charge for outer communities, and some apply a two-hour minimum that achieves the same thing. Ask for the rate, the minimum length, the distance supplement if any, and the cancellation notice period in writing. A provider who cannot put those four numbers in one message is a provider whose billing will surprise you in month two.

faqs.question: Can my two children share one tutoring hour to save money?
faqs.answer: It works when both are in the same subject and the same year, because one explanation genuinely serves both and the shared practice helps. It fails when they are two years apart: the hour becomes two half-lessons with an audience, and the younger child usually gets the worse half. In the in-home market the two-hour minimum pushes families towards sharing whether it suits the children or not. Online, two consecutive single hours cost two single hours, so you can decide on what each child needs rather than on what the trip requires.

faqs.question: Which Dubai communities are hardest to get a specialist tutor to?
faqs.answer: The furthest from the established school corridor: Dubai South, Jebel Ali, Emaar South, the outer edges of Dubailand, and the newer southern communities. Families there consistently report fewer options and higher quotes, because a tutor is pricing a long evening drive into a single booking. The pattern is worst for scarce subjects, where the local pool was already thin. That combination is why the clearest financial case for video sessions in this emirate is made in exactly the communities furthest from the schools, not in the central ones.

faqs.question: Can we book a tutor who visits the house instead of teaching online?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Tutoring for families here is delivered one to one over live video, with a shared screen both people write on. If what you need is an adult physically present with a younger or very distractible child, we are the wrong provider and the hiring checklist in the section above is the useful part of this page for you. What online delivery buys instead is access to the specialist who teaches your child's exact specification, wherever in Dubai you live.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre cheaper than a tutor coming over?
faqs.answer: Per hour, usually yes. Dubai centre price lists put group classes at roughly AED 90 to AED 200 per student and centre-based one-to-one at AED 150 to AED 350, against AED 180 to AED 500 for a visit. The trade is that you travel, the timetable is fixed, and in a group of four to twelve the teaching runs at one pace. That suits a student who is behind on content and needs reteaching. It suits a student at grade 6 aiming at 8 much less, because what that student needs is their own work marked individually.

faqs.question: How many sessions a month do Dubai families usually start with?
faqs.answer: Four, which is one hour a week, is the most common starting point and the right one for most cases. Eight a month is normal in an exam year or where a student is two grades short of target. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Start at four, take the diagnostic, and change the number once you have seen three marked pieces of work rather than before.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the weekly tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: School hours compress, meals move late, and most revision shifts into the night, so an afternoon slot stops working almost immediately. Sessions can be rescheduled to post-Iftar timings, which works well over video and is close to impossible for a tutor driving across the emirate at that hour. Agree it in advance rather than week by week, because the late slots fill. For a Year 11 student with a spring exam series, quietly losing four weeks in Ramadan is the most costly scheduling mistake in the whole year.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor who lives nearby a false economy?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it depends entirely on the subject. For Year 8 support, mainstream Year 10 mathematics or general study habits, a competent local tutor at the lower end of the band is good value and the proximity costs you nothing. It becomes a false economy at the edges: further pure mathematics, Higher Level sciences, an unfamiliar Pearson code, or diploma coursework feedback. The usual failure pattern is a match that holds for a term and breaks in January, and changing tutors mid-year costs four to six weeks in the most expensive term there is.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we cancel at short notice?
faqs.answer: Ask before you book, because this is where in-home and online economics differ most. A visiting tutor who has already driven to your community cannot refill the slot, so short-notice cancellations are usually charged in full, and 24-hour notice periods that fall across a weekend catch families out regularly. Online, a freed slot can often be refilled the same evening, so policies tend to be more forgiving. Whichever route you take, get the notice period, what counts as short notice, and the charge in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Do I pay per hour or per month, and is there a minimum commitment?
faqs.answer: Both models exist in Dubai. Hourly is more common with independent tutors; monthly packages are typical with agencies and centres, and advertised examples in October 2026 ran at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Packages are cheaper per hour and less flexible, and some carry minimum terms. With IB Gram the first lesson is free with no card details taken, the rate is agreed per match, and there is no package you have to commit to before you have seen a lesson.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach in a private home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the rule is clearer than most families expect. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years, applied for through the ministry's app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: What should I ask for before letting a tutor into the house?
faqs.answer: Identification and confirmation of the private tuition work permit, first. Then a reference you can actually telephone, and one anonymised marked script with the mark scheme alongside, which tells you more about their teaching than any profile. Ask whether they teach at your child's own school, because professional-ethics rules in some emirates bar staff from paid tutoring of their own students. Finally ask what personal data about your child is kept, why, and how to have it deleted, which you are entitled to know under UAE data protection law.

faqs.question: How will I know within a month whether the money is working?
faqs.answer: By what you are holding, not by how the sessions feel. Four weeks in, you should be able to name the three things costing your child marks, see them identified in marked work, and say which are technique and which are content. Technique habits move in two or three sessions; content gaps take a term. If the only available evidence after a month is that everybody is getting on well, you are paying specialist rates for company, and that is true whether the tutor arrived at a Dubai address or appeared on a screen.

dubai/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Price the teaching, not the drive
dubai/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The honest summary of this page is short. Most of what separates an in-home Dubai rate from an online one is traffic, minimum visit lengths and distance premiums, none of which teach your child anything. If you genuinely need an adult in the room, use the hiring checklist above and spend the premium knowingly. If what you need is the right specialist for a specific specification at a usable hour of the evening, send us the subject, the code and the level, and we will propose a tutor who teaches exactly that. The first lesson is free, no card details are taken, and every session runs one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The question is not whether online works, but how the hour is spent
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai who are sceptical about online tutoring are usually sceptical about something specific, and it is almost never the technology. It is a picture in their head: a teenager nodding at a face on a laptop while nothing is written down. That picture describes a badly run lesson, and badly run lessons happen in kitchens and tuition centres too. The useful question is what the sixty minutes contains, who is writing during it, and what you can inspect afterwards.

A well-structured session for an exam course looks like this. Five minutes on the last piece of marked work, specifically on the errors rather than the score. Twenty minutes of new teaching with the tutor writing on a shared whiteboard the student can also write on. Twenty minutes of the student working problems while the tutor watches the pen move and interrupts at the point of error rather than at the end. Ten minutes setting the next piece of work and noting what the hour fixed. The student talks or writes for more than half of it, or it has failed.

That structure is the whole argument, and it is testable in the free first lesson rather than in a brochure. Watch for three things: whether your child's own work appears on the screen, whether the tutor interrupts mid-error instead of marking at the end, and whether anything is written down that you can still read tomorrow. If all three happen, the delivery format has stopped being the variable that matters and the subject match is what you should be judging instead.

What online does uniquely well is specific. It makes thirty-minute bookings economic, which matters because a great deal of valuable tuition is a short conversation about one marked paper or one coursework draft. It makes a Higher Level chemistry specialist as available to a family in Dubai South as to one in Jumeirah. It makes a 9pm session possible on the night before a deadline. And it produces a written trail by default, because the whiteboard, the annotations and the notes all persist.

What it does badly is also specific, and the page says so below: a young or very distractible child with no adult nearby, a household with no quiet space, and anything requiring physical apparatus in the student's hands. IB Gram delivers one to one over live video for UAE families and does not provide home visits here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. If the honest answer for your child is that they need a person in the room, we would rather tell you that than sell you a lesson that will not work. What follows is the detail: the hour broken into blocks, a component-by-component account of what transfers to a screen and what does not, how handwritten algebra reaches a tutor, how practical-skills questions are taught from real data, what arrives in your inbox in the first four weeks, and the kit and ground rules that make the difference between a session that works and one that drifts.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers, with Cambridge adding a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences and Pearson examining practical skills inside the written papers. Everything assessed here is a written answer under timed conditions, which is why it transfers to video delivery with almost nothing lost.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical question comes up constantly, and the answer depends on the board. Cambridge candidates sit a laboratory paper or its alternative, both of which test written answers about apparatus, variables and error rather than manual skill. Pearson candidates meet the same ideas inside the main papers. School laboratory work still happens at school; the tutoring job is converting that experience into the answer style the mark scheme rewards.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with written papers plus internal assessment worth about a fifth of most subject grades, an extended essay of 4,000 words and a theory of knowledge essay of 1,600. Several subjects carry an oral component assessed on a recording made at school.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Dubai get more from video sessions than anyone else on this page, because the work that decides their grades is produced over weeks and needs short, frequent responses rather than long lessons. A thirty-minute conversation about a draft at nine in the evening, two days before an internal deadline, is a booking the visiting model cannot sell and the centre model cannot timetable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced tasks across eight subject groups, each subject marked against four criteria scored from one to eight, with a personal project in the final year. Assessment is produced over days and weeks rather than in an exam room.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where the honest caution applies. A Year 7 or 8 student who needs an adult beside them to stay on task is not well served by any screen, and families should test that in a free lesson rather than assume it either way. Where it does work, the win is the process journal for the personal project: shared documents make the evidence visible to the tutor week by week.

dubai/ib-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below is what a video session actually does in each subject, as opposed to what the subject contains. The pattern is consistent: anything assessed as a written answer transfers cleanly, and anything requiring apparatus in the student's hands does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tutor writes on a shared board with a stylus and the student works problems live while the pen is watched. Mid-error interruption is the whole value: a student stopped at the moment they drop a negative sign learns more than one who is told at the end.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Circuit diagrams and free-body diagrams are drawn together on the board. Six-mark causal answers are drafted out loud first and then written, because the mark scheme rewards a chain of reasoning that students can usually say before they can write.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
subjects.description: Equation balancing, mole arithmetic and titration data read off a shared screen. Reaction pathways are built as a diagram the student completes, not watches. Practical questions are taught from real past-paper data rather than from a bench.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Diagram labelling and graph description dominate, both of which work well on a shared document. The content load means written work between sessions matters more here than session length: two marked papers a fortnight beats an extra hour of teaching.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: First Language, Specification A, DP SL and HL
subjects.description: The student writes between sessions and the tutor annotates the text itself, which is easier on a screen than on paper because both people see the same annotations. Sessions are spent on the annotations rather than on reading aloud.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP SL or HL
subjects.description: Diagram drills are the fastest-moving work in these subjects and they suit a shared board exactly: five diagrams a session, drawn by the student, marked immediately. Case-study application is taught by annotating the stimulus material together.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level work needs more board space than any other subject, so a tablet or a second screen changes the session materially. Exploration support is mostly short feedback conversations about a draft the student wrote.

subjects.name: Languages with oral components
subjects.description: Speaking practice is one of the things video does best, because the student has to carry the conversation with no one else in the room to defer to. Recordings for practice can be made and reviewed together, with the student's own voice as the evidence.

subjects.name: Internal assessment and coursework support
subjects.description: Short sessions around a draft the student wrote, with feedback given as questions and criterion references. Nothing is written for the student and nothing is redrafted to completion, because the work must be their own.

regions.note: Apartment living, so the quiet-room question is real: bedrooms double as study spaces and siblings share walls. Headphones with a microphone solve most of it, and a 4pm slot is genuinely available here because school is close.

regions.name: Dubai South, Jebel Ali and Emaar South

dubai/ib-igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three session shapes, all over live video, chosen by what the student needs to produce next rather than by a package.

modes.title: Teaching hour with live problem work
modes.description: The standard sixty minutes: a short review of marked work, new teaching on a shared board, then the student working problems while the tutor watches and interrupts at the point of error. The student writes for more than half the hour. This is the shape that moves technique fastest, because the correction lands while the mistake is still warm.

modes.title: Timed paper under conditions
modes.description: The student sits a full paper to time with the camera on, phone away and the tutor available but silent, then the script is photographed and returned annotated against the board's scheme. Run every two or three weeks in the exam term, this is the only reliable way to find out whether a student can convert what they know inside the time allowed.
bullets: Real duration, real conditions, no interruptions
Timing recorded per question as well as the mark
Annotation keyed to mark-scheme wording
A ranked list of the marks that were available and missed

modes.title: Thirty-minute feedback session
modes.description: A short booking about one thing: a marked paper, a coursework draft, a diagram technique problem. Economic only because nobody travels, and the most under-used purchase in this market. Diploma families use it most, typically two days before an internal deadline at an hour no visiting tutor would offer.
bullets: Half-hour bookings, including late evening

sections.heading: Sixty minutes, broken down
paragraphs: The fastest way to judge an online tutor is to time the lesson. Below is the structure a well-run session for an exam course follows, with what each block is for and what it leaves behind. Compare it against what you observe in the free first lesson. If the student is writing or talking for less than half the hour, the format is not the problem and the tutor is.

The block that distinguishes a strong session is the third one. Watching a student work while the tutor says nothing until the pen hesitates is more effective than any amount of explanation, and it is easier on a screen than at a kitchen table because the work is on a shared surface both people can see and annotate at once. The student cannot quietly skip a line and hope, and the tutor cannot miss the moment the error begins.

The last block matters for you rather than for the student. Five to ten minutes spent setting the next piece of work and writing the note is what makes the arrangement inspectable. Across a term those notes become a record you can read before a parents' evening, which changes the conversation from a general worry about confidence to a specific statement about method marks on structured questions. One caveat about the timings: they are a shape rather than a script. A session reviewing a full timed paper spends forty minutes on the script and ten on new work, and a session before a coursework deadline may contain no new teaching at all. What should not vary is the proportion of the hour in which your child is the one producing something.

sections.heading: Teaching each assessed component over video
paragraphs: The honest way to answer whether online tutoring works is component by component, because the assessment is not one thing. The table takes the components a Dubai student actually meets between 14 and 18 and says how each is taught on a screen and what the format cannot do. Read the last column carefully: it is short, but it is real, and no competitor page in this market publishes it at all.

The pattern is simple once it is laid out. Everything assessed as a written answer under timed conditions transfers with nothing lost, because the skill being trained is producing marks on paper and the paper is the same paper. Oral components transfer well and sometimes better, because a one-to-one video conversation gives a student nowhere to defer to a classmate. Anything requiring apparatus in the student's hands does not transfer, and nobody should claim otherwise.

The one row families ask about most is the science practical. For Cambridge candidates the assessed component is a written paper about practical work, either the laboratory test or its alternative, and both reward precise language about variables, repeats, anomalies and sources of error. For Pearson candidates the same ideas appear inside the main papers. School laboratory sessions still do the hands-on part; the tutoring job is the answer style, and that is taught from real data on a shared screen. The second row families query is internal assessment, and the limit there is not technical but ethical: the format makes draft feedback easy and frequent, and the rule is unchanged by that convenience. The student writes; the tutor reads, asks questions and points at criteria. Nothing is written for them and nothing is redrafted to completion, whatever the medium makes possible.

sections.heading: Handwritten working, and how it reaches the tutor
paragraphs: The practical objection to online maths is real and it has a practical answer. Mathematics is written by hand, method marks are awarded for working that appears on the page, and a tutor who cannot see the page cannot award or diagnose anything. So the setup matters more in maths than in any other subject, and it is worth getting right in the first session rather than the fifth.

Three arrangements work. The best is a cheap graphics tablet for the student, which puts their handwriting directly on the shared board and lets the tutor annotate in a second colour as it happens. The second is a phone camera on a stand pointed at the exercise book, so the tutor watches the pen in real time. The third, for timed papers, is simply photographing the script at the end and sending it in, which is how marked work usually travels anyway.

What does not work is a student typing mathematics. Typed notation is slow, it hides the layout that method marks depend on, and it trains a habit the exam will punish. The exam is handwritten, so the practice should be handwritten. Any tutor who is content to watch a student type algebra into a chat window has not thought about what the mark scheme is actually paying for. Settle the arrangement in the first session and keep it. Families who change setup every few weeks lose five minutes at the start of each hour to the same conversation, and five minutes a week across a year is most of a term's worth of teaching spent on cameras and angles rather than on quadratics.
bullets: A graphics tablet of modest cost changes a maths session more than any other purchase

sections.heading: Science practical skills without a laboratory
paragraphs: Dubai parents ask this question more than any other, and the answer depends on which board the school entered. Cambridge candidates in the sciences sit a separate component: either a laboratory test, where apparatus is handled under supervision at the centre, or the alternative-to-practical paper, which is written. Pearson candidates meet practical skills inside the main written papers rather than in a separate test. In both cases the assessed object for most students is a written answer.

What those written answers reward is specific and teachable: naming the independent, dependent and control variables; explaining why repeats matter and how an anomaly is treated; stating a source of error that actually affects the result rather than listing human reaction time out of habit; and reading a results table or graph precisely before explaining it. None of that needs a bench. All of it needs practice against real past-paper data with immediate marking, which is exactly what a shared screen provides.

What a tutor cannot provide is the hands-on experience, and that is fine because the school provides it. Where a student has genuinely missed laboratory time, the honest response is to say so and to work on the written skill while raising the gap with the school, not to pretend a video call substitutes for handling a burette. Where a student has done the practical work and still loses marks, the problem was never the apparatus; it was the sentence structure of the answer.

sections.heading: Speaking, orals and the components people assume fail
paragraphs: Several assessed components involve talking, and they are the ones families assume online delivery handles worst. In practice it handles them well, for a reason that is slightly uncomfortable: in a one-to-one video conversation there is no classmate to defer to, no back row, and no way to let someone else answer. A student who hides in a group room cannot hide for sixty minutes on a screen.

For the Diploma Programme individual oral, and for the language orals, the useful work is rehearsal with recordings. The student speaks, the recording is played back, and the two of them mark it against the criteria together. Hearing their own hesitations is more persuasive than being told about them, and the recording is the student's own evidence rather than a tutor's opinion. The assessed version is still administered and recorded by the school, which is where it belongs.

English speaking endorsements and presentation components work the same way. What improves is structure and timing rather than confidence in the abstract: a student who knows they have four minutes and a three-part shape performs better than one who has been told to relax. For students who find speaking genuinely difficult, short frequent sessions beat long ones, and the camera being on is not negotiable because performing to a blank square trains nothing. There is one genuine limitation worth naming. A student who needs to practise presenting to a room is not practising that here, and if a school component involves an audience, a few rehearsals in front of family members is a sensible supplement. What a tutor can train is the content, the shape and the clock, which is where most of the marks sit anyway.
bullets: One-to-one video gives a reluctant speaker nowhere to defer to
