sections.heading: What arrives between sessions, week by week
paragraphs: The strongest argument for video delivery is not convenience; it is that it produces a written trail by default. Everything happens on surfaces that persist: the shared board, the annotated script, the note. That makes the arrangement inspectable in a way a kitchen-table lesson usually is not, and it gives you a way to judge whether the money is working that does not depend on how the sessions feel.

The table sets out the first month. Note the fourth week specifically: a named list of three mark-loss causes, each labelled content, method or timing. That is the deliverable to demand from any provider in any format, and it is the point at which you should be able to repeat back what is wrong in one sentence. If after four weeks you cannot, something has gone wrong with the arrangement rather than with your child.

After the first month the pattern settles into a rhythm: an hour taught, about thirty minutes of marked work returned, a short note, and a timed paper every two or three weeks in the exam term. Keep the notes. Across two terms they become the document that makes a school conversation specific, and in the eight weeks before an exam window they are what makes revision targeted rather than a second pass through the textbook. Keeping them has one more use that families discover late. If a tutor becomes unavailable, or a subject needs a different specialist in the second year, the notes and annotated scripts hand the next tutor a diagnosis on day one instead of costing you a fortnight of rediscovery. In a market where mid-year changes are common, that record is worth more than the loyalty.

sections.heading: Where online genuinely fails
paragraphs: Three cases, named plainly. The first is a young or highly distractible student with no adult nearby. A nine or ten-year-old, or an older student with significant attention difficulties, often needs a physical presence to stay in the chair, and no amount of good lesson design replaces it. For those families a local visiting tutor is the better purchase, and the hiring questions are the same ones this page recommends anywhere: the specification taught, an anonymised marked script, and what arrives in writing.

The second is the household with nowhere quiet. In a shared Dubai apartment with younger siblings and a television, an hour of concentrated maths is hard to protect. Headphones with a microphone fix a surprising amount of it, and so does moving the slot later. But a family who cannot find sixty quiet minutes should be honest about that before paying for the hour rather than after four interrupted ones.

The third is anything requiring apparatus in the student's hands, which is school laboratory work and nothing else on the assessment list. Beyond those three, the usual objections do not hold up: connectivity in Dubai is rarely the binding constraint, screen fatigue is a function of lesson design rather than of medium, and a student who will not engage with a tutor on a screen very often will not engage with one in the room either. The free first lesson is the cheapest way to find out which case you are in.
bullets: Young or highly distractible students with no adult present: choose local

sections.heading: Setting up the room, the kit and the ground rules
paragraphs: Ten minutes of setup saves a term of friction. The equipment list is short: a laptop or tablet with a screen large enough to show a paper and a board at once, headphones with a microphone, a stable surface, and the exercise book or past paper the session is about. A cheap graphics tablet transforms mathematics sessions and is unnecessary for essay subjects. A printer helps for timed papers but a photograph of a handwritten script does the same job.

The ground rules matter more than the kit. Camera on, phone in another room, door closed, and the student logged in two minutes early with the relevant work already open. Those four conditions account for most of the difference between sessions that work and sessions that drift, and they are worth agreeing with your child once rather than renegotiating weekly. For younger students, a parent within earshot at the start of the arrangement is sensible and usually stops being necessary within a month.

One more thing worth asking any provider about: data. A tutoring arrangement collects information about a child, and where sessions are recorded you are entitled to know who holds the recording, why, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted. Under UAE personal data protection law those are reasonable questions with short answers, and a provider who cannot give them in writing has told you something. Ask also whether recordings are made at all, because many sessions are not recorded and do not need to be.
bullets: Kit: screen, headset with microphone, the work itself, optionally a graphics tablet
Rules: camera on, phone elsewhere, door closed, logged in two minutes early

process.title: Send the work, not just the subject
process.description: The most useful first message is a photograph of a recent marked paper or piece of work, plus the specification code and level. With that a tutor can arrive at the free lesson already knowing where to look, which is the difference between a diagnostic hour and an introduction.

process.title: A free first lesson to test the format
process.description: One full lesson at no charge, with no card details taken. Watch for three things: does your child's own work appear on the screen, does the tutor interrupt at the point of error, and is anything written down that you can read tomorrow. Judge the format on that rather than in principle.

process.title: Fix the setup once
process.description: Before the second session, settle the kit and the rules: headset, camera on, phone out of the room, work open in advance. If mathematics is the subject, decide then whether a graphics tablet or a camera over the exercise book is the arrangement, and stick with it.

process.title: Weekly work with a timed paper in the cycle
process.description: An hour taught, about thirty minutes of marked work between sessions, and a full timed paper every two or three weeks once an exam series is in view. The timed papers are what reveal whether knowledge is converting inside the time allowed, which nothing else does.

process.title: The four-week test
process.description: At four weeks you should be able to name three causes of mark loss, see them in marked work and say which are technique and which are content. If you cannot, we change the tutor or the shape rather than adding hours, and we say which we think it is.

whyPoints.title: The lesson is described, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every claim on this page about how a component is taught over video is written down with what the format cannot do alongside it. That list is short and it is honest, and it is the part competitor pages leave out entirely.

whyPoints.title: The student writes, not watches
whyPoints.description: A shared board both people draw on, mid-error interruption and live problem work mean the student is producing for more than half the hour. Watching a tutor solve problems is the failure mode of online tutoring and it is a design choice, not a property of the medium.

whyPoints.title: Short bookings exist
whyPoints.description: Thirty minutes about one marked paper or one coursework draft is economic here and impossible in the visiting model. For Diploma students working to internal deadlines, that single structural difference is worth more than any rate comparison.

whyPoints.title: Evidence by default
whyPoints.description: Boards, annotated scripts and written notes persist because everything happens on a screen. That is what makes the four-week test possible and what makes a conversation with the school specific rather than general.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. We hold no regulator or board accreditation, we do not call tutors examiners, and we do not promise grades.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty is a boundary, not a slogan
whyPoints.description: Coursework and internal assessment must be the student's own work. Feedback comes as questions and criterion references on a draft they wrote. Nobody here supplies text, redrafts to completion or submits anything on a student's behalf.

faqs.question: What does my child actually need to join a lesson?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet with a screen big enough to show a past paper and a shared board at once, headphones with a microphone, a stable surface and the work the session is about. For mathematics, either a cheap graphics tablet or a phone on a stand pointed at the exercise book, so the tutor can watch handwritten working. A printer is useful for timed papers but not necessary, because a photograph of a handwritten script marks just as well. Nothing else is required, and no software purchase is involved.

faqs.question: How does a tutor show working in maths over video?
faqs.answer: On a shared whiteboard, with a stylus, in a way the student can write on too. The tutor writes a line, the student takes over, and the tutor annotates in a second colour at the moment an error appears. That mid-error interruption is the single biggest advantage of one-to-one work in any format, and a shared digital surface makes it easier than a kitchen table, because both people see the same page and neither can quietly skip a step and hope it works out.

faqs.question: Are sessions recorded, and who can see a recording?
faqs.answer: Many sessions are not recorded at all, and recording should never be assumed either way. Where it happens, you are entitled to know who holds the file, why it exists, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted, and those are short answers any provider should give in writing under UAE personal data protection law. The useful questions to ask before the first session are whether recording happens, whether you can opt out, and what else about your child is stored, such as school, marks and work samples.

faqs.question: Can a student practise a speaking component on a screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, and often better than in a classroom, because a one-to-one video conversation gives a reluctant speaker nobody to defer to. The method that works is rehearse, record, play back, then mark the recording against the criteria together. Hearing their own hesitations persuades a student faster than being told about them. The assessed version is still administered and recorded by the school, as it should be, and what tutoring improves is structure and timing rather than confidence in the abstract.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a session?
faqs.answer: The tutor reconnects, and the time lost is made up either at the end or in the next session. It is worth agreeing that rule once at the start rather than negotiating it in the moment. Connectivity in Dubai is rarely the binding constraint; the more common disruption is a household with several devices streaming at once, which a wired connection or a quieter slot fixes. If a tutor's connection is repeatedly the problem, that is a reason to change tutor rather than format.

faqs.question: How does the tutor see handwritten work if there is no scanner?
faqs.answer: A phone photograph, which is how most marked work travels in this market anyway. For live sessions a phone on a stand over the exercise book lets the tutor watch the pen in real time, which matters because method marks depend on what appears on the page. For timed papers the student photographs the script at the end and sends it, and it comes back annotated against the board's scheme. No scanner, no printer and no app purchase is needed for any of that.

faqs.question: Is a screen as effective for a Year 10 student as for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Diploma students generally get more from it, because their work is produced over weeks and benefits from short frequent responses that the format makes economic. Year 10 students do well provided the session is designed so they produce rather than watch: live problem work, mid-error correction, a question set to follow. The age at which it genuinely struggles is younger than this, and the honest signal is attention rather than year group. Use the free first lesson to watch for it specifically.

faqs.question: How do you stop a student from just sitting there?
faqs.answer: By structure, and you can check it. In a well-run hour the student works problems for about twenty minutes while the tutor watches, writes on the shared board, and attempts an exam-style question under light time pressure. That is more than half the session spent producing. The rules help too: camera on, phone in another room, work open before the session starts. If your child could sit through the hour in silence, the lesson was designed wrongly, and that is a tutor problem rather than a medium problem.

faqs.question: How is a full timed paper run over video?
faqs.answer: The student sits it to the real duration with the camera on and the phone away, and the tutor stays available but silent. At the end the script is photographed and returned annotated, with the time taken per question recorded alongside the marks. That last column is the point: plenty of Dubai students know enough for a grade 8 and produce a 6 because they spend fourteen minutes on a six-mark question. Running one of these every two or three weeks in the exam term is the most informative thing a tutor does.

faqs.question: Which assessed components genuinely cannot be taught this way?
faqs.answer: Hands-on apparatus work, and that is the whole list. For Cambridge sciences the assessed practical component is a written paper, either the laboratory test taken at the centre or its alternative; for Pearson, practical skills are examined inside the main papers. School laboratory sessions provide the physical experience. What tutoring does is train the written answer: variables, repeats, anomalies, sources of error that actually affect the result, and reading a results table precisely before explaining it. That work needs real data on a shared screen, not a bench.

faqs.question: Can I watch the lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a younger student being within earshot for the first few sessions is sensible. It usually stops being necessary within a month, and it is worth stepping back once it does, because a student performing for a parent behaves differently from one working with a tutor. What you should rely on instead is the written output: the annotated work, the note after each session, and the three named causes of mark loss at four weeks. That evidence is more reliable than an impression formed from the doorway.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics tablet, and is it worth the cost?
faqs.answer: For mathematics and the quantitative sciences it is the single purchase that most improves a session, because it puts handwriting directly onto the shared board where the tutor can annotate it live. An inexpensive model is enough; nothing specialist is required. For essay subjects it adds very little, since the work is typed or photographed anyway. If you would rather not buy one, a phone on a stand over the exercise book achieves most of the same thing for nothing.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutor actually marked the work rather than skimmed it?
faqs.answer: Because annotation keyed to mark-scheme wording looks completely different from a tick and a score. You should see marks awarded and withheld at specific points, the scheme's own phrasing quoted, and a note of which marks were available and missed. Over a month the same three errors should be tracked and should either close or be escalated. If what arrives is a percentage and an encouraging sentence, you are buying attendance, and that is as true of a visiting tutor as of a video session.

faqs.question: Can one student work with two different tutors for different subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is common, because subject specialism matters more than continuity of person. A mathematics specialist and a chemistry specialist in the same week is a better arrangement than one generalist covering both, and nothing about video delivery makes it harder to organise: consecutive slots cost two single sessions with no travel gap between them. What you should insist on is that each tutor writes their own note, so progress in two subjects is never averaged into one impression.

faqs.question: We tried online tutoring before and it did not work. Why would this be different?
faqs.answer: Ask what went wrong, because it usually has a name. The most common failures are a lesson where the tutor talked and the student watched, no marked work between sessions, a subject match that was approximate, or a slot in the wrong part of a Dubai evening. All four are fixable and none of them are properties of the format. What to require this time: the student producing for more than half the hour, annotated work keyed to the mark scheme, and three named causes of mark loss by week four.

dubai/ib-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Judge it on one lesson and one marked script
dubai/ib-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: You do not need an opinion about online tutoring. You need one lesson and one piece of marked work. Send a photograph of a recent paper, the specification code and the level, and we will propose a tutor who teaches that paper and knows where its marks hide. The first lesson is free and takes no card details. Watch whether your child writes, whether the tutor interrupts at the point of error, and what arrives afterwards in writing. If all three stand up, the format has stopped being the question. If they do not, we will tell you which of the three cases above you are in.

intro.heading: The assessment is the subject, and most lost marks live in it
paragraphs: The honest case for an IB IGCSE private tutor in Dubai is narrow and strong. A school teacher with twenty-four students, a scheme of work and a reporting cycle is doing a different job from a tutor with one student and a marked script. The teacher is responsible for a cohort reaching a standard; the tutor is responsible for one student's specific pattern of lost marks. Those are both real jobs, and the second one is almost impossible to do at scale, which is why it is worth buying separately.

What a private session should therefore spend its hour on is the assessment. Not the subject in general, which the school already covers properly, but the components your child actually sits and the places marks leave their paper. That is a surprisingly concrete list. Tier caps on Cambridge entries. The additional Higher Level content inside a Diploma subject. Command terms that look like synonyms and are not. Criterion letters with mark allocations attached. Word and page limits. Syllabus codes that change which formula a student is expected to recall.

Almost none of that appears on competitor pages in this market. Across the pages read for this project in October 2026, not one named a single Internal Assessment criterion, and exactly one syllabus code appeared across a whole cluster of area pages. That is not a small omission. The criteria and the codes are the specification the grade is awarded against, and a tutor who cannot talk about them fluently is teaching the subject rather than the assessment.

This page is built as a reference you can use before you hire anyone. The tier table tells you what a Core entry costs in grade ceiling. The level table tells you what the additional ninety published teaching hours of a Higher Level subject actually contain. The command-term table tells you what the mark scheme is paying for. The criterion table gives letters and marks for the Mathematics Exploration, with the shortfall that most often holds a band down. The limits table tells you what counts toward a word count and what to verify with the school.

Delivery, once and plainly: lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around Dubai school timetables. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address and does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India. No approval, accreditation or partnership is claimed from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no board document is reproduced here or supplied to students; syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are cited and linked, and the right route to them is the school's exams officer.

dubai/ib-igcse-private-tutor.programmesIntro: This page is organised by level rather than by programme name, because level is what determines the paper your child sits and the ceiling on what they can score.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: A defined subset of the full syllabus, assessed on the Core paper pair for the subject, with the grade capped at C on the letter scale or 5 on the 9-1 scale. The cap is the defining feature and it is applied at entry rather than at marking, so a Core candidate performing at A standard still receives the capped grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter by tier subject by subject, and a student can sit Core mathematics alongside Extended biology. Because the centre lodges the entry months before the paper, the useful tier conversation happens in October of Year 11 at the latest. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026, which is the date after which the ceiling is fixed.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier, and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: The full syllabus including Extended-only content, assessed on the Extended paper pair and reaching A* or 9. Pearson International GCSE is untiered in several subjects and offers a modular route in some, allowing units to be sat in different series and banked, which changes revision planning rather than content.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families routinely hold both boards at once, because schools choose subject by subject and a transfer can split a child across Cambridge and Pearson mid-course. The practical difference shows up in formula provision and command-term wording, not in the physics, so the first question in any session is which code appears on the statement of entry.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme, Standard Level
programmes.description: The published model allocates 150 teaching hours to a Standard Level subject. Students sit the subject's Standard Level components and produce the same Internal Assessment task as their Higher Level classmates in most subjects, marked against the same criteria. Three of a candidate's six subjects are taken at this level.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level choices in Dubai are often made on timetable pressure rather than on university prerequisites, and that is the decision worth revisiting in Year 11. Several selective courses name a Higher Level subject specifically, so the route should be checked against each university's published prerequisites rather than against a general impression.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme, Higher Level
programmes.description: The published model allocates 240 teaching hours, roughly sixty per cent more than Standard Level, and the additional content is examined. In most subjects an extra or extended component appears. The Internal Assessment task is usually the same as at Standard Level, but it is judged against a stronger cohort and in a more demanding context.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level sciences, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and Economics are the subjects Dubai families most often seek private support for, and they are also the thinnest in local supply. Exact component weightings are published in the current subject guide and should be read with the subject teacher before paper practice is planned.

dubai/ib-igcse-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names what the components actually are and the specific place marks leave the paper. A tutor who cannot name the failure mode in your child's subject is not diagnosing, and the first session should prove they can.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, with marks awarded for selecting and shaping material rather than for retelling it. The common shortfall is a response that summarises the passage accurately and never answers the question's own verb, which is worth several marks on every reading task.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics content assessed as a double award, so breadth matters more than depth and timing pressure is severe. Students lose marks by writing single-science depth on a question worth two marks, which is a pacing problem rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: Multiple choice plus structured data response, where diagram accuracy and the use of case material decide the top band. The frequent error is correct economics stated in general terms when the question asked for application to the extract supplied.

subjects.name: IB Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks: labelled axes, a clear shift and a sentence explaining the movement. Higher Level adds quantitative work with no credit for approximation. The three commentaries require real published articles analysed against named theory, and most lose marks for summarising the article instead of applying the model.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation, with Higher Level adding an extended component that rewards sustained reasoning. Marks go on unjustified steps, on accuracy conventions ignored on the calculator paper, and on final parts of questions that ask the student to deduce rather than compute.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Non-calculator and calculator papers at the entered tier. Method marks are available and routinely forfeited because working is not shown. Bearings, vectors and transformations are taught early, rarely revisited, and reliably cost marks in the final series.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and practical technique account for most of the distance between a 6 and an 8. Apparatus gets described where variables should be controlled, series and parallel rules get confused under time pressure, and units and significant figures leak marks from correct calculations.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Mathematical fluency is the hidden prerequisite, and students who understand the concepts often fail to execute the algebra under time pressure. Uncertainty and error treatment is where the Internal Assessment separates bands, and it is taught in a fortnight if it is taught at all.

subjects.name: IB Spanish B
subjects.description: Productive skills carry the grade, and the assessment rewards range used accurately over range attempted. Dubai students with conversational fluency frequently underperform on the written components because register and text type are marked explicitly and are rarely practised.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools alongside any licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, with Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for that stream, so support must follow the stream the school has placed the child in.

sections.heading: What a private tutor can see that a class of twenty-four cannot
paragraphs: A school teacher in Dubai running four Year 11 sets is managing roughly a hundred students through a scheme of work, a mock cycle and a reporting calendar. They will know which topics their cohort finds hard and which students are drifting. What they cannot realistically do is sit with one student's marked paper and establish that six of the eleven lost marks came from explain questions answered as describe questions, two from working not shown, and three from a single topic taught in Year 10 and never revisited.

That is the private tutor's entire job, and it is worth separating from teaching because it is a different activity. It requires one marked script, the published mark scheme, and the time to read both carefully. It produces a plan that is specific to one student and would be wrong for the next one. And it is measurable, because the same question types can be re-tested six weeks later under identical conditions.

The corollary is that a private session spent re-teaching the syllabus in order is usually poor value. The school is already doing that, competently, with more hours than any tutor will have. A session that covers chapter four because chapter four is next has not used the one advantage the format has. The first session should therefore be a diagnosis, and the parent should be able to see the diagnosis in writing.

What this also means is that a private tutor is a complement to the school rather than a substitute for it, and should behave accordingly: working to the school's syllabus codes, the school's internal deadlines and the school's tier entries, rather than running a parallel curriculum that leaves the student managing two sets of instructions.

sections.heading: Core against Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: The single most consequential academic decision in a Dubai IGCSE year is not how much revision happens. It is which tier the centre enters the student for, because a Cambridge Core entry is capped at grade C on the letter scale or 5 on the 9-1 scale, and the cap is applied regardless of how well the candidate performs on the day.

Entries are lodged months before the paper. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026 against an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. After the entry closes the ceiling is arithmetic rather than ambition, and a revision programme beginning in January is working inside it. This is why a tier review in October is worth more than any amount of catch-up teaching in February, and why it is the first thing a tutor should ask about if the student is anywhere near the boundary.

The decision is not always to push for Extended. A student working securely below the C or 5 boundary may genuinely score better on the Core paper pair, where the questions are accessible and the marks are collectable, than on an Extended paper that defeats them in the second half. The capped grade from a confident Core performance can be more useful than an uncapped grade from a Extended paper the student cannot finish. What makes the call honest is a timed paper at each tier rather than an impression.

Where the tier decision bites hardest is progression. A Core pass is often insufficient for the same subject at A Level or Diploma Standard Level, because the Core syllabus excludes content the next stage assumes. A Core-to-Diploma move therefore needs a content bridge of its own, and that is one of the longest pieces of support described anywhere on this page.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level in the published model
paragraphs: Parents are often told that Higher Level is Standard Level with more content, and students are often told it is Standard Level for people who are good at the subject. Neither is quite right. The published IB model allocates 150 teaching hours to a Standard Level subject and 240 to a Higher Level one, and that additional ninety hours is examined material rather than extra practice on the same syllabus.

The practical consequences are specific. In most subjects an additional or extended component appears at Higher Level, so paper technique has to be practised component by component rather than in general. The additional higher level content tends to sit at the end of the two years, which is exactly when a student under coursework pressure has least capacity for new material. And the Internal Assessment is usually the same task at both levels, judged against the same criteria, which means supervision time is similar while the standard the work is read against is not.

Where this changes a tutoring plan is in sequencing. A Higher Level student who is behind benefits more from protecting the additional higher level topics than from revisiting the core, because the core will be revisited in school anyway and the higher level material frequently will not be revisited at all. A Standard Level student who is behind usually has the opposite problem, and needs core consolidation.

The one thing this page will not do is publish exact component weightings per subject. They are set out in the current subject guide and they change between syllabus cycles, so the right move is to read them with the subject teacher before planning paper practice. A tutor quoting a weighting from memory for a subject whose guide has been revised is a familiar and avoidable error.

sections.heading: Command terms, and what each one is paying for
paragraphs: Command terms are the cheapest marks available in both IGCSE and the Diploma, and they are lost at a steady rate by students who know the content. The terms look like stylistic variation and they are not: each one defines what the mark scheme will credit, and answering one as though it were another forfeits the mark however correct the science or the economics happens to be.

The pattern in a marked script is distinctive once you look for it. A student who writes well and scores below their understanding is usually producing descriptions where explanations were asked for, and judgements that are implied rather than stated. That is three or four marks a paper in most subjects, which is frequently the difference between two grades. It is also fixable in a fortnight, which is why a paper-technique clinic beats more content teaching for this profile.

The table sets out six terms that account for most of the loss, with what the mark scheme is actually paying for, a typical mark allocation and the specific error. The allocations are indicative rather than fixed, because they vary by subject and by paper, and the subject guide is the authority.

Two habits close most of the gap. The first is reading the verb before the content and sizing the answer to the marks available: two marks means two creditable points, not two sentences. The second is writing the judgement explicitly when a question asks for one, because an evaluation that leaves the conclusion for the examiner to infer does not score the conclusion.

sections.heading: The Mathematics Exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes criterion letters with mark allocations attached, which is strange, because the criteria are the specification the Internal Assessment is marked against and they are not secret. For the Mathematics Exploration in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, twenty marks are distributed across five criteria, and the distribution tells a student exactly where to put their effort.

The distribution is counter-intuitive for most students. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation, so the mathematics has to be correct, relevant and at a level commensurate with the course. But presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement and reflection together carry fourteen of the twenty marks, and those are the ones routinely surrendered by a student who produced genuinely good mathematics in a document that reads like a textbook exercise.

The usual shortfall per criterion is predictable. Presentation loses marks to a piece with no clear aim stated at the start and no structure a reader can follow. Mathematical communication loses marks to undefined variables and inconsistent notation. Personal engagement loses marks when the topic is generic, because engagement is evidenced by the choices made rather than asserted in an opening sentence. Reflection loses the most, because students describe what they did instead of discussing what it meant and what its limitations were.

The honesty boundary applies in full here. The student is the sole author of their own Exploration, and a session reads the draft and names the criterion and the band rather than supplying text. Science Internal Assessment criteria differ from these and have been revised between syllabus cycles, so they must be read from the current subject guide with the subject teacher rather than assumed from an older model.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, and what counts toward them
paragraphs: Limits are a quiet source of lost marks, because exceeding one is usually treated as material beyond the limit not being read rather than as a penalty, which means the student loses whatever argument they had put at the end. Students who write long tend to put their conclusion last, so the loss lands exactly where it hurts.

The limits worth knowing cold are few. The Extended Essay has a maximum of 4,000 words. The Theory of Knowledge essay has a maximum of 1,600 words. The Mathematics Exploration is governed by published page guidance rather than a word count, which schools interpret slightly differently, so the school's own statement is the one to work to.

Beyond those, the picture varies by subject and by syllabus cycle, and this page deliberately declines to publish numbers it cannot source for the current guides. The table therefore gives the limits that are stable, and for the rest it names the document to check and the person to check it with. A tutor confidently quoting a science Internal Assessment word limit from an earlier guide is a common way for a student to receive wrong instructions.

The practical habit that protects the marks is simple: write to roughly ninety per cent of the limit, put the conclusion where it will certainly be read, and count before submission rather than after. For the Extended Essay specifically, the structural decisions that keep a piece inside 4,000 words are made at the research-question stage, which is months before the writing, and that is when a session is most useful.

sections.heading: Syllabus codes and where the marks go in each
paragraphs: Exactly one syllabus code appeared across an entire cluster of competitor area pages read for this project. That is a strange omission, because the code is the only unambiguous way to identify what a student is sitting, and it determines formula provision, paper structure and tiering.

A worked example makes the point. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 are both called mathematics and are routinely treated as interchangeable by tutors advertising maths help in Dubai. They differ in what the candidate is expected to recall rather than look up, in how the papers are split between calculator and non-calculator use, and in the phrasing habits of their mark schemes. A student drilled on the wrong board's expectations will arrive well prepared for a different paper.

The table maps six of the codes Dubai families most often hold, with the components sat, the topics carrying most of the marks and the place marks are most often lost. The topic weightings are the broad pattern rather than a published figure, and the authority on any specific weighting is the current syllabus document on the board's own site.

One boundary again, because it matters on a page that discusses papers this much. Syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. This page cites and links them; it does not reproduce them and no tutor supplies them as downloads. The school's exams officer is the correct route, and a provider distributing board material is creating a copyright problem rather than an advantage.

sections.heading: What a single sixty-minute session can actually change
paragraphs: Families reasonably ask what one hour buys, particularly when a provider is suggesting thirty of them. The honest answer depends entirely on what the hour is spent on, and the range is wide.

An hour spent explaining a topic the school has already taught twice usually changes nothing measurable, because the limiting factor was not the explanation. An hour spent on command-term technique with a marked script in front of both people regularly recovers two to four marks a paper, because it addresses a loss the student was repeating without noticing. An hour spent narrowing a research question for an Internal Assessment can save a term of unusable work, since an unmeasurable question cannot be rescued by effort later. And an hour spent on a timed paper at each candidate tier, in October, can change a grade ceiling that no later hour could touch.

That ranking is the argument for diagnosis before purchase. A family buying thirty sessions before anyone has read a marked script is buying attendance and hoping it lands on the right problem. A family buying one diagnostic session first knows what the problem is, and can then decide whether it needs eight sessions or thirty, and in which subject.

It is also the argument for honesty about what will not change. If a student has not covered half the syllabus eight weeks out, no plan recovers it all, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling hours rather than advising. The useful version of that conversation sets out what will be covered, what will deliberately be left, and what grade range that makes realistic, in writing, before the money moves.

sections.heading: Safeguarding, data and the permit question for one-to-one work
paragraphs: One-to-one work with a minor carries obligations that a group class does not, and a private tutoring page should state them rather than leave them to be assumed.

On safeguarding, the arrangements worth agreeing before the first session are practical. Sessions happen in a shared room rather than behind a closed bedroom door. The camera stays on. A parent is within earshot, particularly for the first few sessions and for younger students. Scheduling and messaging go through the parent rather than directly to the child. Any recording happens only with explicit parental consent and a stated purpose, and a family is entitled to decline recording without losing the session.

On data, lead forms and matching conversations collect personal information about a child, and the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the relevant framework. The reasonable standard is to collect only what the match requires: board, syllabus code, level, subjects, year group and availability. A school name helps with timetabling and is optional. Grades, reports and photographs are not needed to arrange a tutor, and a provider asking for a child's photograph before a first lesson should be asked why. A privacy policy should be reachable from the page you are reading.

On permits, private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted. One arrangement to avoid entirely: Abu Dhabi's reported professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported in the same terms, so a child's own class teacher is not the right private tutor for them.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the components
process.description: The statement of entry or school subject list gives the board, the syllabus code and the tier. For a Diploma student, add the level and the subject guide version if the school states it. That is the specification a match is made against, and it takes a photograph rather than a conversation.

process.title: Free diagnostic on a timed paper at the right tier
process.description: A section of a real past paper from the correct tier or level, sat to time and marked against the published mark scheme. You receive the annotated script and a written note naming the question types losing marks. That is the document everything after it is planned from.

process.title: Agree what the sessions will not do
process.description: Written, before the first paid hour: which topics are in scope, which are deliberately out, whether the plan is content or technique, and what grade range that makes realistic. Agreeing the exclusions is what stops a plan drifting into general support.

process.title: Run the block with one artefact per session
process.description: A marked script, a drill sheet with model answers, or a criterion comment naming the letter and the band. One-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, same tutor, same slot, with marking returned between sessions rather than at the end of the block.

process.title: Re-test on the same question types and decide
process.description: An identical timed paper near the end of the block, placed beside the first. Mark movement on the same question types is the measure. From there the choices are extend, change the focus from technique to content, change tutor, or stop, and each is a reasonable outcome.

whyPoints.title: The match is made on the code and the tier
whyPoints.description: Board, syllabus code, tier or level, and the components sat. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different recall expectations, and a tutor who has taught one and not the other will teach the content well and miss the technique.

whyPoints.title: Criterion letters and mark allocations are stated
whyPoints.description: Twenty marks across five Exploration criteria, with the usual shortfall named for each. No competitor page read for this project named a single criterion. The specification is not secret, and a student who knows where the marks sit allocates their effort differently.

whyPoints.title: Tier reviews happen before the entry closes
whyPoints.description: A timed paper at each candidate tier, in October or November, with a written recommendation the family can take to the school. After the centre lodges the entry the ceiling is fixed, and for the Cambridge March 2027 series that date is 27 November 2026.

whyPoints.title: Nothing is quoted that cannot be sourced
whyPoints.description: Teaching hours and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge limits are published and stated. Component weightings and the current science Internal Assessment criteria are not restated here, because they change between syllabus cycles and the subject guide is the authority.

whyPoints.title: Board material is cited, never supplied
whyPoints.description: Syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. Sessions work from them through the school's exams officer and the boards' own sites; no provider should be distributing them, and this one does not.

whyPoints.title: Safeguarding and data practice are on the page
whyPoints.description: Shared room, camera on, parent within earshot, messaging through the parent, recording only by consent. Matching collects the board, code, level, subjects, year group and availability, not a child's grades or photograph.

faqs.question: What does a private tutor see in my child's work that a class teacher misses?
faqs.answer: Not more than the teacher knows about the subject, but more about one student's specific pattern. A Dubai teacher running four Year 11 sets is moving roughly a hundred students through a scheme of work and a mock cycle. A private session can take one marked script and the published mark scheme and establish that six of eleven lost marks came from explain questions answered as describe questions, two from working not shown, and three from a single topic taught in Year 10 and never revisited. That diagnosis is specific to your child and would be wrong for the next student.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Decide it from a timed paper at each tier, not from an impression, and decide it by October of Year 11. A Cambridge Core entry is capped at grade C or 5 and the cap applies however well the candidate performs. Extended reaches A* or 9 but includes Extended-only content and harder second halves. A student working securely below the C boundary can score better on an accessible Core paper than on an Extended paper they cannot finish. The decision becomes final when the centre lodges the entry, which for the March 2027 series is 27 November 2026.

faqs.question: How much of an IB Diploma subject grade comes from Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject and between syllabus cycles, which is precisely why this page does not publish a single figure. The current subject guide states the weighting for each component, and that is the document to read with your child's subject teacher before planning paper practice. What is consistent is that the Internal Assessment is a substantial, teacher-marked, IB-moderated portion of the grade in most subjects, that it is produced across months rather than in an exam hall, and that it is therefore the part of the grade most responsive to planning well in advance.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level just Standard Level with more content?
faqs.answer: Not quite. The published IB model allocates 150 teaching hours to a Standard Level subject and 240 to a Higher Level one, and the additional hours carry examined content rather than extra practice on the same material. In most subjects an extra or extended component appears, so technique has to be rehearsed component by component. The additional higher level content also tends to arrive late in the two years, when coursework pressure is heaviest. For a Higher Level student who is behind, protecting the higher level topics usually beats revisiting core material the school will cover anyway.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain in a mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Describe is paying for what happens, in sequence, without causes. Explain is paying for why it happens, with a mechanism that links cause to effect. A describe answer given to an explain question earns the description marks and loses the mechanism marks, which in a six-mark question is most of them. This is the single most common recoverable loss in both IGCSE and Diploma scripts, it affects students who know the content well, and it is usually fixed inside a fortnight with drills and marked model answers rather than with more teaching.

faqs.question: Which Exploration criterion do students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Reflection, in the experience of marking these, with mathematical communication close behind. The Mathematics Exploration carries twenty marks across five criteria: Presentation four, Mathematical communication four, Personal engagement three, Reflection three, and Use of mathematics six. Reflection asks for critical discussion of process, results and limitations, and students reliably describe what they did instead. Communication loses marks to undefined variables and notation that changes partway through. Together the four non-mathematical criteria carry fourteen of the twenty marks, which surprises most students when they first see the distribution.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay really have to stay under 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: Yes, 4,000 words is the maximum for the main body, and the practical risk is not a penalty but omission: material beyond the limit is generally not read, and students who write long put their conclusion last. The structural decisions that keep an essay inside the limit are made at the research-question stage, months before the writing, which is when a session is most useful. A question that is too broad cannot be answered in 4,000 words however well it is written. Confirm the current subject-specific guidance with your school's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: What happens if my son exceeds a word limit on an assessment?
faqs.answer: The usual consequence is that the work beyond the limit is not read, which costs him whatever he had put there. Since conclusions sit at the end, an over-length piece typically loses the part that was carrying the argument. The habit that protects the marks is writing to about ninety per cent of the limit, placing the conclusion where it will certainly be read, and counting before submission rather than after. The Extended Essay limit is 4,000 words and the Theory of Knowledge essay 1,600; for subject Internal Assessments, check the current guide with the subject teacher.

faqs.question: Which topics carry the most marks in Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625?
faqs.answer: Across the components, electricity, forces and motion, and thermal physics carry the heaviest load, and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper is where the gap between a 6 and an 8 usually opens. The losses are specific rather than general: apparatus described where variables should have been controlled, series and parallel current rules confused under time pressure, and units or significant figures dropped from calculations that were otherwise correct. For any specific weighting, the current 0625 syllabus document on the Cambridge site is the authority, and your school's exams officer is the route to it.

faqs.question: How does Cambridge 0580 differ from Pearson 4MA1 in practice?
faqs.answer: Both are called mathematics and they are not interchangeable. They differ in what a candidate is expected to recall rather than look up, in how papers split between calculator and non-calculator use, in tiering, and in the phrasing habits of their mark schemes. A student drilled on the wrong board's expectations arrives well prepared for a different paper, which is a specific and avoidable way to lose marks. This is why the first question in a session is which code appears on the statement of entry, rather than which subject needs help.

faqs.question: Can one sixty-minute private session really change anything?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the hour is spent on, and the range is wide. An hour re-explaining a topic the school has taught twice usually changes nothing measurable. An hour on command-term technique with a marked script in front of both people often recovers two to four marks a paper. An hour narrowing an Internal Assessment research question can save a term of unusable work. An hour spent on timed papers at each candidate tier in October can change a grade ceiling that no later hour could reach. Diagnose first, then decide how many hours.

faqs.question: Should the first private session be a lesson or a test?
faqs.answer: A test, marked properly, and then the conversation about the marking. A session that begins teaching before anyone has seen a timed script is guessing at the problem, and the most common guess in this market is that the student needs more content. Often they do not; they need technique. Sitting a section of a real past paper to time, marking it against the published mark scheme and reading the pattern together gives both the plan and the baseline for comparison later. That is what the free first session is for, and you keep the script either way.

faqs.question: Is it safe for my daughter to have one-to-one sessions over video?
faqs.answer: It is, with arrangements agreed before the first session rather than assumed. Sessions happen in a shared room rather than behind a closed door, the camera stays on, a parent is within earshot, and scheduling and messaging go through you rather than directly to your daughter. Any recording happens only with your explicit consent and a stated purpose, and you can decline recording without losing the session. These are reasonable things to ask any provider to confirm in writing, and a provider reluctant to confirm them has answered the question.

faqs.question: What personal data do you collect about my child before matching a tutor?
faqs.answer: Only what the match needs: board, syllabus code, level or tier, subjects, year group and availability. A school name helps with timetabling and is optional. Grades, reports and photographs are not required to arrange a tutor, and a provider asking a parent for a child's photograph before a first lesson should be asked what it is for. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the relevant framework, a privacy policy should be reachable from this page, and you can ask for data about your child to be deleted.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher be their private tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is an arrangement to avoid, and in Abu Dhabi it has been reported as prohibited outright. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit's code of conduct has been reported in similar terms. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify it against the current policy, but the practical point holds across the emirates: the conflict of interest is obvious, and IB Gram does not arrange or market that arrangement.

dubai/ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the code on the entry
dubai/ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: Photograph the statement of entry or the school subject list so the board, the syllabus code and the tier are known. Book the free diagnostic, which runs a timed section of a real past paper at the correct tier and returns it marked against the published mark scheme. Read the pattern of lost marks with the tutor, then agree in writing what the block will cover and what it will deliberately leave out. If your child is near a tier or level boundary, do it before the centre lodges the entry. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
